## Main Text (Title Page)

-> **This is the gate of the Lord** <-
<note>original: "Zeh ha-sha'ar l'Adonai." A common biblical citation from Psalm 118:20 used on title pages to signify the holiness of the book.</note>

---

# **The Book of**
# **Leviticus from the Zohar**

---

From the Divine Tanna <term>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</term> <note>A 2nd-century sage traditionally credited with the authorship of the Zohar</note> <term>may his memory be for the life of the world to come</term>, including the <term>Commandments of the Torah</term> <note>original: "Pekudi Oraita," a section of the Zohar explaining the 613 commandments</note> and the <term>Faithful Shepherd</term> <note>original: "Ra'aya Meheimna," a section where Moses, the 'Faithful Shepherd,' discusses the commandments with Rabbi Shimon</note>. Printed and proofread with great care by the young man, the honored Abraham <term>may his Rock protect him and grant him life</term> <note>original: "yod-zayin-vav," a common protective abbreviation for the living</note>, son of the honored Meshullam <term>of blessed memory for the life of the world to come</term> of Modena.

---

# **Here in Mantua**

Under the government of our exalted lord, Duke Guglielmo Gonzaga <term>may his glory be uplifted</term>. In the year **"When I restore your fortunes"** according to the abbreviated era <note>original: "B'shuvi et shevutchem." This is a chronogram from Zephaniah 3:20 where the numerical value of the bolded letters indicates the year 5320, corresponding to 1560 CE.</note>.

By the printer Jacob Cohen of Gazzuolo.

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the third book of the Torah, Leviticus (Vayikra), in the Zohar. It follows the conclusion of the Book of Exodus.</meta>

# ## [Leviticus]

->**And He Called**<-
<note>original: "Vayikra" (ויקרא). This is the first word and title of the Book of Leviticus.</note>

## Main Text (Zohar)

**Rabbi** Elazar opened his discourse with the verse: *“Ask a sign for yourself from the Lord your God; ask it either in the depths or in the heights above.”* <note>Isaiah 7:11</note> I have observed the earlier generations and the later generations—what is the difference between them? The earlier generations knew and observed the <term>Supernal Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Chokhmata Ila’ah"; refers to the divine wisdom or the Sephirah of Chokhmah</note> and knew how to <term>combine the letters</term> <note>original: "Tzerufa Atvan"; the mystical practice of permuting Hebrew letters to affect reality or achieve enlightenment</note> that were given to Moses at Sinai. Even the sinners among them knew how to gaze into the letters of the Supernal Wisdom and knew the secrets hidden within the letters. They established arrangements of wisdom to subdue the workings of this world, because every single letter that was spoken to Moses would be crowned and ascend upon the heads of the <term>Holy Supernal Living Creatures</term> <note>original: "Chayvan Ila’in"; the angelic beings described in Ezekiel's vision of the Divine Chariot</note>. All those Living Creatures were crowned by them and would fly through the air that is described as coming from the subtle, unknown Supernal Spirit. They would ascend and descend, both the great letters and the small, thin letters.

The "great letters" are written as we have learned in the <term>Palace</term> <note>original: "Heikhal"; a reference to the dimensions of the divine realm</note> that is the measure of all things. The "small letters" would descend from that Palace below. Both these and those were handed over to Moses at Sinai. It was revealed to him that these letters are joined in concealment; within every single letter, such as the letter **Aleph (א)**, it is a single letter, yet two others are joined with it in concealment to form the word "Aleph" <note>The letter Aleph (א) is spelled out in Hebrew as Aleph-Lamed-Pe (אלף)</note>, and so it is with all of them. All of this was handed over to Moses at Sinai, and all of it is hidden among the companions.

Regarding the verse *“Ask a sign for yourself from the Lord your God,”* they would take this as the secret of the letters. Similarly, regarding Rahab, what is written? *“And give me a true token”* <note>Joshua 2:12; original: "Ot Emet" (Sign of Truth)</note>. This refers to the letter **Vav (ו)**, for this is called the "Sign of Truth." And if you say the other letters are not truth—they are indeed truth, but this specific letter is called "Truth." *“Ask it in the depths”* refers to the letter **He (ה)**, the final letter of the Holy Name. *“Or in the heights above”* refers to the letter **Yod (י)**, the head of the Holy Name. This is the secret of what is written: *“Ask a sign for yourself from the Lord your God.”* I have heard that the "sign" mentioned here refers to the order of the alphabet... Come and see: when the <term>Cloud</term> <note>original: "Anana"; the Divine Presence or Shekhinah</note> ascended over the <term>Tabernacle</term> <note>original: "Mishkana"</note> and rested upon it, all those Chariots and all those letters **A B C D E F G**... <note>The text lists the first seven letters of the Hebrew alphabet: Aleph, Bet, Gimel, Dalet, He, Vav, Zayin</note>

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Zohar's commentary on the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra). It follows the conclusion of Exodus, transitioning from the physical construction of the Tabernacle to the spiritual mechanics of the Divine Presence dwelling within it.</meta>

# Leviticus (Vayikra)

## Main Text (The Zohar)

These are the kings of the upper Tabernacle <note>The celestial counterpart to the earthly Tabernacle</note>, all of them in this manner. It is written: **"And Moses was not able to enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud rested upon it..."** <note>Exodus 40:35</note> and it is written: **"Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of the Lord filled the Tabernacle..."** <note>Exodus 40:34</note> We learn from this verse that which is written: **"And Moses was not able to enter the Tent of Meeting."** Did Moses then not know [how to enter]? For behold, it is written: **"And Moses went into the midst of the cloud."** <note>Exodus 24:18</note>

At the time he reached the mountain, it was like the time he went out. But on the day the Tabernacle was established, it was not like the Tent of Meeting at Mount Sinai. For at the time that strength and burden came to him from the outside, at times he would reach the mountain and be delayed, reaching a great service, prepared and sheltered, and established with the rectifications of all those holy spirits that are prepared below. For there were two clouds: one that Moses entered, and one cloud that crowned the Tabernacle.

Come and see what is written: **"And the glory of the Lord filled the Tabernacle."** The word is not written except as **"filled,"** <note>original: *malah* (מלא)</note> and the end rises above and below until the Tabernacle below. A hidden arrangement <term>Tikkun: a spiritual rectification or structural arrangement</term> descended below to be established within the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</term>. Four sides of angelic hosts <note>original: *matronin* (מטרונין), referring here to the angelic camps surrounding the Divine Presence</note> were appointed in that first arrangement. One from the side of those four hosts, all of them until the "Head" is established on the right side—in this, Michael [is appointed]. The hosts that are under the authority of Michael and his people were under his hand. And one is appointed to arrange over four, three, four below, because all those hosts are over them when they descend.

And they are appointed from it to arrange on the left side; when they are over them, they do not look upon the worlds. And the one appointed over them in this is Gabriel, standing over them within, and one is appointed over their heads. By the life of the Small YHVH <note>A mystical reference to the angel Metatron or a specific divine name</note>, all these who arrange are nullified to that place of purity and see everything.

From those spirits of the two hosts who stand under the authority of Michael and his people, all those hosts are under his hand. And one appointee stands over them who is called the "Gate of Mercy," to whom twelve appointees are counted, three by three, four times. And the spirit of the second appointee stands over all of them below; a single crown is upon their heads, upon all those hosts. And by the life of the letter *Resh*, when these crowns are nullified, they all belong to that side called "The Gathering." But the letter stands upon its branches, revealing secrets and supporting the head and the nest.

From those is Raphael, the Great Appointee, the Great Host under the authority of Michael, and with him were arranged all those hosts under his hand. They were not permitted to be seen as a covering, so as not to be changed here until [reaching] the "House of Worlds" <note>The Temple in Jerusalem or the afterlife</note>, for there they are all swaddled and the hosts are hidden and nullified.

And what do they resemble here? All those hosts under his hand who were handed over at that hour to that people. And one appointee stands over them, and Chamziel is his name. Twelve appointees crown him on every side, three by three as we have said. And Nofiel, the Great Appointee, stands over all of them so that his name shall not be nicknamed. And each crown is upon the heads of all those hosts. And by the life of the Lord, the letter *Kof*, when this crown is nullified, they all belong to that side called "The Gathering of *Kof*." To them, the letter *Kof* hangs in radiance and covers them three times a day; it rises and descends. Two other [angels] call out to them for the arrangement, who stand in wisdom: one who favors below, and one who strikes, looking toward the Crown <term>Keter: the highest Sephirah or emanation</term>.

From those is Kadumiel, the Great Appointee, the Great Host under the authority of Michael, and with him were arranged all those hosts under his hand. And one appointee stands over them who is called the "Gate," and the spirit of the twelve appointees crowns him, three to each side. And the appointee Kadumiel stands over them so that his name shall never be nicknamed. One crown stands upon their heads, and it is the letter *Resh*.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->And He Called<-

When these colors <note>original: "govanin," referring to the mystical lights of the Sefirot</note> travel, they all gather into the assembly-point of the letter *Qof* <note>original: "kof," the 19th letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note> that we mentioned, which hovers over that Living Creature <note>original: "chayuta," a reference to the angelic beings in Ezekiel's vision</note>. The letter *Resh* <margin>Engravings</margin>
*Resh* hovers over the *Aleph* deep within, in the place where they proclaim "Holy, Holy." A power of understanding, unique and hidden, is in the gathering, and it lived.
The letter *Chet* and the *Vav*, and it lived. The *Chet* and the *Vav* are in the gathering; over all of them are the *Chet* and the *Vav*, and a flow of light emerges from their gathering—those are the *Chet* and the *Vav*.
Then the gathering of the letter *Dalet* and *Yod* strikes the gathering of the letter *Dalet* and *Yod*, and that gathering emerges in the place of the Holy. It strikes within
the gathering of the letter *Dalet* and *Yod*, and then the gathering of the letter *Dalet* and *Yod* strikes within the gathering of the letter *Dalet* and *Qof*. A flow of light was emerging, and the gathering of the letter *Dalet* and *Qof* emerged and struck within the gathering of the letter *Dalet* and *Resh*. All of them emerged as one and were joined within the gathering
of the letter *Dalet* and *Aleph* which stands firm. A flow of light was emerging and striking all those colors of theirs as one: the gathering of the letter *Dalet* and *Vav*
with the *Yod*; the gathering of the *Yod* with the *Qof*; the gathering of the *Qof* with the *Resh*; the gathering of the *Resh* with the *Aleph*. The engravings <note>original: "gilufin"</note> were joined to the gatherings and they emerged
to the Crown <note>original: "Keter," the highest Sefirah</note>. And the Crown, where they are joined according to their colors, brings forth a Voice from their gatherings, and they are joined in this Spirit: **And He called to Moses.** <note>Leviticus 1:1</note> From that [Spirit], he gazed all those days that he did not enter the Crown; for they were sent, the *Chet* and the *Vav* were
revolving like hammers in their carvings, which were handed over as one in the Assembly to Eden. The *Chet* and the *Aleph* were a hand
to Eden, like a hidden image in the place where they proclaim "Holy." And the *Vav* emerged, and it was the memory of the letter *Dalet* and *Aleph*. And the
*Aleph* was joined within the *Vav* that followed it, [forming] a Wall <note>original: "Kir"</note>. And the *Yod* entered between the *Qof* and the *Resh*, and "Wall" <note>original: "Kir"</note> was found. And they were to be engraved and gathered
as before. A flow of light emerged from their gathering and they were joined like the merits of the *Chet* and the *Vav*. They emerged to all and were revealed toward all
those sides that were traveling—those *Chet* and *Vav*. And when the colors of the *Chet* and the *Vav* are joined, a flow of light strikes between them,
the *Chet* and the *Vav* according to their engravings, for all those chariots. He honored, and the flow of Wisdom honored them, and He called between those
chariots to honor... <unclear>koveh mipan ve-chalam mikhtas chipir</unclear>. And this was the portion of Moses, who saw all this.
All this imagery was not established before the eyes of Moses except through the first Spirit, which is called "And He Called." This
is what Moses saw: the voice of "And He called to him, Moses." And in this Spirit below, it was not revealed to him because...
...and it is written: **And He called to the firmament and the heights** and it is written <note>Isaiah 40:26</note> **Mouth to
mouth I speak with him** etc. <note>Numbers 12:8</note> and it is written **Not so is My servant Moses** <note>Numbers 12:7</note> because they do not make known his power...
The *Chet* and the *Vav* ascend to be arranged in all those sides in this manner, like the carving of the *Chet*. Honor and a flow of light
emerge... to the Crown. The *Chet* and the *Vav* were to be received, and they were gathered upon the heads
of all those chariots. They were rubbed together until they were established in their places: the head to the left side, the portion of the Great
Minister, the Great Metatron, over all those who stand at the gate of the Tabernacle under the authority of the lights and with him.
When they are established at that gate, all those sides that are under his hand—and with him is one minister below
at the outer gate, and a scepter is placed and deep... ministers who surround him, three by three on each side, for the four
sides. And the hosts are a covering for the shield of war that turns like... This minister, Chukiel, is appointed
over them above. Within this is a Living Creature, pure ones upon their heads, and the *Chet* and the *Vav* and the *Aleph*. For the profane things do not stand,
nor do they ask, except in this Spirit of life and strength. Because the Left is not nullified except by the Right, and strength
is always nullified to the Left. This is the *Chet* of the gardens, and it emerges from strength. Then they travel to that place where they gather,
that gathering within the crushed... the Great Metatron, who stands within under the authority of the lights and with him
all those sides under his hand. And one minister... to be honored in the Holy Land.
And they surround him, thirty ministers, three by three, thirty times. And... Rastiel stands over all of them so as not
to... The *Chet* is one gathering upon the head of all these sides, and the *Chet* and the *Aleph* of life, the *Vav* and life
below within the strength of the Tabernacle... which began in the Spirit... and it began
like his body.

## Main Text (Zohar)

In the bodies of the letters, the voice calls from within them. When they are crowned upon the heads of all the camps of the appointed angels, then they all travel to the side of that structure. And from this, **Captiel** <note>A presiding angel often associated with the movement of celestial forces</note> is the great chief over all the camps of the appointed angels, and the spirit of the dominion of the Lord <note>original: "ה'"</note> of **Gabriel**; and with him were prepared all those appointed ones under his hand, those who were handed over to him at that hour. And one chief stands over them, **Azza** is his name. And twelve chiefs surround him on every side, three by three, like the hundred we have established. And Captiel the great chief stands over them all. One structure rests upon the heads of all the camps of the appointed angels, and their levity is below, and all of them are bound to the structure of that which is below. This letter hangs in the air over two sides to the windows. And from this, **Samael** <note>In Zoharic thought, the figure representing the "Other Side" or the shadow aspect of the divine system</note> the great chief stands and changes into four sacks of a structure that does not stand like its wings—sometimes to the side of **Michael** and sometimes to the side of Samael. And with him are twelve chiefs who surround him on every side, three by three, like the hundred we have established. And **Ratniel** is the great chief over the twelve forces that are under that chief to surround. And one letter is structured upon their heads above. And this letter is the letter *He* <note>The fifth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often representing the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note>, and this hangs in the air over every side of the letters in that lower place of the courtyards. These two ascended above over every side to the windows, and all are included in that structure that hangs from that letter. This is within the place called the "Holy of Holies," a structure of one letter within the hiddenness of the holy and the sealed piety. This structure is a building over all the letters, and the voice is what emerges from their intention, which are the letters. Then the structure of the host was required, and it nullified two letters for the windows, structures that hang in the air, and they are <margin>God (El)</margin> and the name **God (El)** <note>original: "אל"</note> was awakened, and they all joined to the windows of the right side. And now all of these, and then all of them, returned to their former state as they were at first, and they bend outward. Then they called out: "And He called to Moses."

-> # Leviticus (Vayikra) <-

> **"And the Lord called to Moses, and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying..."** (Leviticus 1:1)

Rabbi Hiyya opened his discourse:
> **"I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk..."** (Song of Songs 5:1)

This verse—its beginning is its end, and its end is not its beginning. It is written, "I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride," and then "with my milk," and after all of them, "eat, friends." One who invites a groom, when he is rejoiced, [the meal] is prepared before him after they have joined together, and the bride stands and provides for the groom. Rather, worthy are the people of Israel, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, took pity on them and desired them more than all other nations, and because of the love He has for them, He raises them above all the accusers of the world. Come and see: the "slaughterhouse" <note>referring to the altar of sacrifice</note> was made below on that day that was prepared to be bound above, as it is written, "the Tabernacle was erected"—simply stated. And that day was the joy of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Once the Tabernacle was perfected, what is written? "And Moses was not able to enter the Tent of Meeting." When the Holy One, Blessed be He, saw this, He said: "What strength!" And this is what reached the preparation and placed him outside. Immediately, "He called to Moses." He said to him: "From the thicket of the cloud, what is in the feast? 'When any man of you brings an offering to the Lord...'"

---

<column-break/>

### [Right Column: Main Text Continued]

"I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride"—they have established this verse regarding all the gardens of my pleasant brothers, which is the **Garden of Eden** above. "My sister, my bride"—this is the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Knesset Israel, the spiritual personification of the Jewish people/Shekhinah</note>, for at that time they are times like a single bride, an arm and a partner, like that Garden of Eden, because they are all blessed from the watering of the river and are tied each one to its fellow. This is what is written: "I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with..."

### [Left Column: Ra'aya Mehemna]

## The Faithful Shepherd

He opened and said: "I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride." This is certainly **Kingship** (*Malchut*) <note>The final Sefirah, representing the manifest presence of God</note>. "I have gathered my myrrh"—this is the level of **Abraham**, of whom it was said:
> **"Go to the mountain of myrrh"** (Song of Songs 4:6)
• "With my spice" • This is **Isaac**, of whom it was said:
> **"The smell of my son is like the smell of a field which the Lord has blessed"** (Genesis 27:27)
• And these are the right arm and the left arm, and the body upon which it is written "In Your right hand is strength." And these are two blessings corresponding to him: the first is "The Shield of Abraham" and the second is "The Fear of Isaac"...

It features a mystical hierarchy of angels and the beginning of a commentary by the 'Faithful Shepherd' on the patriarchal connections to the Sefirot.</summary>

# Leviticus

## Main Text (Zohar)

With the garment of his horses and the radiance of all the kings, they are established and find favor from the flow of the stream. **"Eat, O friends; drink, and be drunk, O beloveds"** <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>—these are all those below. And all the branches are all blessed and nourished when these [above] are blessed on high. And how many are blessed and sweetened, all of them, by the spirit of the sacrifice! Come and see: at the time when the power of the will of the Holy One, Blessed be He, descends to rest in the air <note>original: "avir"</note> upon the half-ice <note>A mystical reference to the firmament separating the realms</note>, it is so that blessings and joy may be found in all worlds, and He is sweetened to bring forth from the daughter of blessings <note>The Shekhinah</note> to all. For when these are blessed, then all the worlds are blessed as one below. **"I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride"** <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>.

Rabbi Isaac said: There is no satisfaction or preparation [of the soul] and the ascent that does not cease. Rabbi Judah said: All the words of the star and the ascent that did not enter, all of them enjoy the Bride. And my mother-in-law for the bride, all of them in that hour, and after them all, they eat and rejoice. Rabbi Abba said: "Eat" refers to those who are called "gracious," of whom it is written: **"The king has brought me into his chambers"** <note>Song of Songs 1:4</note> for everyone. Rabbi Eleazar said: All those below are blessed accordingly. This one said: The Bride is beautiful to every spirit below.

Rabbi Eleazar said to him: Who are those "above" and who are those "below"? He said to him: The merit of this fear is the supernal place where they are like desire and joy that are never separated; they are called "Friends" <term>Re'im: The union of Chochmah (Wisdom) and Binah (Understanding) which is constant</term>. This is what is written: **"And a river went out of Eden"** <note>Genesis 2:10</note>; Eden and that river are never separated and are found forever in a will of joy. "Drink and be drunk, O beloveds"—these are those below who are called "Beloveds" <term>Dodim: The union of the lower Sefirot, which fluctuates based on human action</term> at known times, as we have established.

Come and see: regarding the higher ones, "eating" is written of them, because they receive the blessing from the source of eating. And because the Mother <note>The Sefirah of Binah</note> dwells there, where the "guarded wine" is, "eating" is written of them. But regarding the lower ones who require watering, "drinking" is written of them, for all the hosts require watering from the power of the Deep. Therefore, for the higher ones it is "eating" and for the lower ones it is "drinking"; these are "Friends" and those are "Beloveds."

Rabbi Eleazar said: Come and see, for "Beloveds" implies a love that is seen in those below. These are the ones who share with one another but are not found constantly; they are called "Beloveds." But those who are found constantly, and are neither hidden nor separated from one another, are called "Friends." And regarding these "Beloveds" and these "Friends," these [Friends] are in a will of constant joy, while those [Beloveds] are in repentance at times. And this is the perfection of all, because everything is blessed, and then there is joy in all worlds.

Rabbi Hezekiah applied this verse to the sacrifices, because they are the feast of the King to be brought before Him, and they enjoy His portion, and they are all sweetened, and joy is found for all. Rabbi Yose applied this verse to the time when the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence</note> enters to be found in joy with blessings and gladness in all, and the Shekhinah goes like a bride to the canopy <note>Chuppah</note>, and then Israel below are perfected and rejoice in Her.

<summary>This page provides a mystical interpretation of Song of Songs 5:1, distinguishing between the constant union of the higher divine faculties (Friends) and the intermittent union of the lower faculties (Beloveds) triggered by sacrifices. It explains how the ritual of sacrifice nourishes both realms, bringing the Shekhinah into a state of joyful union like a bride.</summary>

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra) in the Zohar. It establishes the mystical connection between the Tabernacle, the Assembly of Israel, and the Divine Presence.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And He Called**<-

In several verses, it is written: "They shall make for Me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them," and then upon it you shall rest and be sweetened.
**And He called** to Moses. <note>Leviticus 1:1</note> Rabbi Phineas opened his discourse:
> "The blossoms have appeared in the land, the time of pruning has arrived, and the voice of the turtle-dove is heard in our land." <note>Song of Songs 2:12</note>

This verse requires contemplation. Since it is written "appeared in the land," why is it then written "heard in our land"? For they seem to be one and the same. Rather, "the blossoms have appeared in the land" refers to those plants that the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu," the standard rabbinic name for God</note> uprooted and replanted in another place, where they took root. The scripture describes how they all flowered in the land and were blessed by Him as is fitting. And what was it before? A salty and rejected land. "The time of pruning has arrived" refers to the time to uproot the worship of the stars and their nations, and their dominion over Israel, in order to establish the Tabernacle. "And the voice of the turtle-dove is heard in our land"—this is the horn of the future inheritance that Israel received through Joshua. Who is the "voice of the turtle-dove"? This is the Supernal Turtle-dove <note>a mystical reference to a divine masculine force</note> who united with the Perfect Bride in the Sanctuary below. Then the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> was crowned with His crowns like a groom with a bride; then the expansion and breadth of the harp of Zion was like King Solomon, etc. As the Book of Aggadah says: "The voice of the turtle-dove" is the Oral Torah, for the Written Torah is simply called "Torah," but the Oral Torah is called "the Turtle-dove of the Bride." And He called to Moses. "And He called"—this is the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>the Divine Presence, often personified as feminine</note> calling to the Tabernacle. We have established this as it was said, and so it is. Come and see: when the <term>Shekhinah</term> rested upon the Tabernacle, it is written "the bride of Moses" <note>a wordplay on "the completion of Moses"</note>—missing the letter *Vav*—truly the Bride of Moses! And they established for every spirit that she is the Bride of Moses, the Bride of the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>Knesset Yisrael, the mystical community of souls</term>, and "Bride" is a single word. To walk upon her, it is said: once the Tabernacle was established, Moses stood outside and said, "It is not fitting to enter within the canopy." Immediately, "And He called to Moses." Who called? The one of whom it is written "His was that Bride," for the whole canopy was her canopy.

**And the Lord spoke** to him—that which is called "the voice of Moses," that which Moses took hold of.
And He called to Moses. Rabbi Eleazar opened:
> "Why, when I came, was there no man? When I called, was there no answer? Is My hand too short to redeem?" <note>Isaiah 50:2</note>

Worthy are Israel, for in every place they are found, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> is found with them, and the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> is found among them and prides Himself in them, as it is written: "Israel, in whom I will be glorified" <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>. Not only that, but even though Israel is in <term>Exile</term> <note>Galuta</note>, they are like the feet of King Solomon, for they are holy. When Israel is perfect in their deeds, as it were, the Holy Heaven is made perfect. But when Israel is not perfect below, as it were, a blemish is found above. For we have learned: this one rises and that one descends. When Israel rises above, the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> is likewise established below, one from the other. The Holy Heaven remains in total perfection. Because the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> is like a lamp, and the deeds of Israel are like a lamp, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> is found among them. He is required to be holy in the synagogue, and He calls out and returns: "Woe to those who abandon their dwellings and there is no one to take My hand!" Then the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> says: "Why, when I came, was there no man? When I called, was there no answer?" There is strength, but no one to awaken the spirit. Come and see: at that time when the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> finds the holy ones and surrounds them, immediately "And He called to Moses, and the Lord spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying." He spoke to him and informed him that there would be times when Israel would sin before Him and the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> would be drawn away, and the "Appointed Time" <note>Moed</note> would become a time of liability, and it would not be repaired by their hands. As it is written in the portion: "And the Lord spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting." What is missing from the Tent of Meeting? The matters of the Tent of Meeting which are destined to be drawn into the liability of Israel and will not be sustained. Therefore, to the good: "When any man of you brings an offering to the Lord" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>—these are the offerings that come for the Bride. Rabbi Hezekiah was present before Rabbi Shimon...

It emphasizes that the spiritual state of the world above depends on the righteous actions of Israel below.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the sacrificial offerings. It follows the previous discussion on the elevation of the soul and the unification of Divine attributes.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

All of them are called an "offering" <note>Hebrew: *Korban*</note>, which implies "drawing near" <note>Hebrew: *Kiruv*</note>. What is the meaning of an offering? One should know that it is a voice rising toward its Creator. The word "offering" refers to the **Holy Crowns** <note>The *Sefirot* or Divine emanations</note> that draw near to one another and bind together until they all become one in a perfect union, to rectify the **Holy Name** as is fitting. Through this "offering to the Lord," those Holy Crowns are directed toward Him to establish the Holy Name and unify it properly, so that **Mercy** <note>Hebrew: *Rachamim*</note> may be found in all worlds, and the Holy Name below may be crowned and sweetened entirely. All of this is done to awaken Mercy and not to awaken **Judgment** <note>Hebrew: *Din*</note>. For this reason, the text says "to the Lord" <note>The Tetragrammaton, associated with Mercy</note> and not "to God" <note>Elohim, associated with Judgment</note>. It must be "to the Lord" because we need to awaken Mercy; we require Mercy and not Judgment. He said: Happy is the portion of that person who gains these words, for this is the clarification of the matter. Regarding all this, it is written:
> The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise. <note>Psalms 51:19</note>
It is written "sacrifices of God" <note>Elohim</note> and not "sacrifices of the Lord." He said to him: Indeed, it is so. It does not say "an offering of God," but rather "sacrifices of God." For this reason, the slaughtering of the sacrifice takes place in the **North** <note>The direction associated with the attribute of *Gevurah* or Strength/Judgment</note>, because this merit is for the sake of "God"—that side of **Strength** <note>Gevurah</note>—so that it may be subdued and the spirit of Judgment broken. Thus, Judgment is humbled and Mercy prevails over Judgment. Therefore, "sacrifices of God" are intended to break the power and intensity of Judgment, as it says: "a broken spirit"—to break that intense spirit so it does not prevail, and then Mercy replaces its intensity. When one stands at the altar with a broken spirit and repents for his deeds, that intense spirit is broken, all so that Judgment is subdued and Mercy prevails over Judgment.

**"When a man** <note>Hebrew: *Adam*</note> **among you brings an offering to the Lord..."** <note>Leviticus 1:2</note> Rabbi Eleazar said: This verse should have been written as "When a man brings an offering to the Lord." Why does it say "among you"? It is to exclude the **First Man** <note>Adam HaRishon</note>, who brought an offering when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world and established it. Here, "among you" is written to exclude that other Adam, who was not "among you." Rabbi Shimon said to him: You have spoken well, and so it is.

Rabbi Abba opened his discourse:
> A song, a psalm of the sons of Korah. <note>Psalms 48:1</note>
This song is a superior praise above all other praises, which the sons of Korah were privileged to compose. "A song, a psalm" is a praise upon a praise, divided into two praises. The sons of Korah were privileged to present it to the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Knesset Yisrael, the spiritual archetype of the Jewish people and the Shekhinah</note>, and the Assembly of Israel recites it. And what is it? As it is written:
> Great is the Lord and highly praised in the city of our God, His holy mountain. <note>Psalms 48:2</note>
When is the Holy One, Blessed be He, called "Great"? At the time when the Assembly of Israel is found with Him. Then He is "Great in the city of our God." What is the "city of our God"? Rabbi Yehuda said to him: Why is "our God" <note>Eloheinu</note> needed here? Rather, it is certainly so: this "city of our God" is the praise of Israel. What does this imply? It implies that a King without a **Matron** <note>The Queen or Shekhinah</note> is not truly a King, nor is He "Great" or "Praised." Therefore, anyone who is not found as **Male and Female** together, every [holy] name is removed from him; he is not included in the category of "Man" <note>Adam</note>, and he is not worthy of being blessed. It is written:
> And that man was great among all the people of the East. <note>Job 1:3</note>
We have learned in the book of **Rav Hamnuna the Elder** that when a man's mate is fittingly joined with him, he is called "Great." So too here: "Great is the Lord and highly praised." And how great is He? He returns and says: "In the city of our God, His holy mountain." Therefore, this praise is fitting. And if you ask why it does not say "for He is good" as is His name? Because they are destined to be blessed, and the spirit of the King is "It is not good for man to be alone" <note>Genesis 2:18</note>. When He is alone, "good" is not written. Thus, it does not say "for He is good" as His name, but "Great is the Lord and praised," as we have said.
> Fair in situation, the joy of the whole earth... <note>Psalms 48:3</note>
This is the praise of their **Union** <note>Zivug</note>. "Fair in situation" <note>Yofeh Nof</note>—this is the Holy One, Blessed be He; this is the **Righteous One** <note>Tzadik, the Sefirah of Yesod</note>. "The joy of the whole earth"—then there is joy for all, and the Assembly of Israel is blessed.
> God in her palaces is known as a stronghold... <note>Psalms 48:4</note>
These are the Houses of Judgment and the Tent... there...

<summary>This page explains that the purpose of a sacrificial offering (Korban) is to unify the Divine attributes and ensure that Mercy prevails over Judgment. It also emphasizes that the Divine is only called "Great" when in union with the Shekhinah (the Assembly of Israel), mirroring the human requirement of being "male and female" to be complete.</summary>

## Leviticus

For there is the gathering of all blessings, in the likeness of the **Matronita** <note>The Shekhinah or Divine Presence, depicted as a Noble Lady or Queen</note>. From there, they go out above and below. The level above is the **Tzadik** <note>The Righteous One, referring to the Sefirah of Yesod, the foundation and channel of blessing</note>, and from there blessings are gathered into the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Knesset Yisrael, the spiritual archetype of the community, associated with the Sefirah of Malchut</note>, the Holy City, which is blessed from that source. "For behold, the kings assembled" <note>Psalm 48:5</note>—these are all the crowns of the King together, and others are delayed while these ascend.

Come and see: at the time when a person rectifies his deeds through the **sacrifice** <term>Korban: literally "a drawing near"</term>, everything is sweetened, brought close, and bound one to another as one, and everything ascends. This is what is written: *“When any man [Adam] of you brings an offering”* <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. "When he brings an offering" means to bind matters together as is fitting.

Come and see: if one brings an offering to strengthen matters that are not "married" <note>referring to the union of male and female divine aspects</note>, then his sacrifice is not a sacrifice, and blessings are found neither for him, nor above, nor below. What is the meaning of the verse *“When any man [Adam] of you brings an offering”*? It implies that he must be an "Adam" <note>a complete human being</note>, and one who is not "included in Adam" <note>i.e., unmarried or spiritually incomplete</note> has no merit resting upon him. For he must have "Face" <note>spiritual presence/wholeness</note>, and one who possesses a blemish is called "removed," and one with a blemish is distanced from everything—just as a High Priest with a blemish is distanced from the Altar and from offering a sacrifice.

And regarding this, the wisdom of the companions <insert>the circle of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</insert> explains what is written: *“And fire came out from before the Lord and consumed them”* <note>Leviticus 10:2, regarding Nadav and Avihu</note>. In this same manner, it is written: *“When any man [Adam] of you brings an offering to the Lord.”* This is to rectify the **Male and Female** <note>Dechar v'Nukba</note>, for only one who is worthy may bring this sacrifice, and no other.

Rabbi Eleazar said: The companions have learned regarding the standing of **Nadav and Avihu** <note>The sons of Aaron the Priest</note> that it is certainly so. For the incense offering is the highest of all the world's sacrifices, through which those above and below are blessed. This sacrifice is higher than all other sacrifices, and the "Living Creatures" <note>Chayot, high-ranking angels</note> are not permitted to draw near, for they are not included in this sacrifice of the lower beings as long as the higher "Living Beings" are to be blessed through them.

And if you say, *“And fire came out from before the Lord and consumed them,”* let us look at the seal of the matter. It is like a commoner who comes before the **Matronita** to serve her while the King is coming to her house to rejoice with her. If that man who possesses a blemish comes before the King, the King says: "It is not for my honor that this person should enter to the Matronita." For the Matronita has prepared the house for the King. When she saw that the King was ready to come to her, and that this person <note>referring to the unmarried state of Nadav and Avihu</note> caused the King to depart from her, the Matronita then commanded that this man be killed.

So it was with the power of Nadav and Avihu; the incense was in their hands, and the Matronita rejoiced and was prepared to receive the King. When the King saw that these men were "blemished" <note>original: *mecharei de-mumin*; here meaning they were unmarried</note>, the King did not want to dwell with her through them, and He departed from her. When the Matronita saw that because of them the King departed, immediately *“fire came out from before the Lord and consumed them.”* All this is because one who is not married is considered "blemished" before the Holy King; the King departs from him and does not dwell within him. Regarding this, it is written: *“When any man [Adam] of you brings an offering”*—he who is called "Adam" <note>a whole man, i.e., married</note> may sacrifice, but he who is not called "Adam" may not sacrifice.

*“From the cattle”*—this is a general rule. *“From the herd and from the flock”*—this is a specific detail. This is to crown the powers that are permitted to "eat" <note>consume the spiritual essence of the sacrifice</note> and to exclude those foreign powers that are not permitted to eat, so they do not draw near to the holy place, but are pushed to "another side" <note>Sitra Achra, the realm of evil</note>.

*“If his offering is a burnt sacrifice...”* Rabbi Hiyya opened his discourse: *“For My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways My ways”* <note>Isaiah 55:8</note>. *“For My thought [Machshava] is not from your thoughts”*—the word "My thought" is written deficiently, without the letter *Vav*.

Come and see: The **Thought** of the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, is supreme and the head of all. From that Thought, paths and trails spread out to establish the Holy Name and to rectify it in its proper rectifications. From that Thought, the hidden river of Eden emerges to water everything. Upon that Thought, the upper and lower worlds stand. From that Thought, the Written Torah and the Oral Torah are found.

But the thought of a human being is the head of all <insert>his actions</insert>, and from that thought, paths and trails spread out to divert his ways in this world and the world to come. From that thought, the filth of the **Evil Inclination** is created and emerges to make him and everyone else sin. From that thought, small sins, intentional transgressions (God forbid), and arrogance are found. And regarding this: *“For [My thoughts] are not...”*

<summary>This page explains that spiritual wholeness (symbolized by marriage) is required to perform sacrifices, using the death of Nadav and Avihu as a cautionary tale. It also contrasts the Divine Thought, which creates and sustains the universe, with human thought, which can lead to the creation of the Evil Inclination.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), specifically focusing on the laws of the Burnt Offering (Olah). It transitions from the technical requirements of the sacrifice to a profound theological discussion regarding the exile and future redemption of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

"For My thoughts are not your thoughts" <note>Isaiah 55:8</note>. And because of this, the head of the whole matter is written: *If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd* <note>Leviticus 1:3</note>. It does not say "a bull" specifically, but rather "from the herd" <note>original: "min ha-baqar"</note> so that it shall be a male. Rabbi Isaac said: "From the herd" is stated generally, and the decree was issued: *a male without blemish*. A male and not a female, for the male is known Above <note>representing the active, giving force</note> and the female is known Below <note>representing the receptive force</note>. And so too: *from the flock, from the sheep, and from the goats*. All those that come Above must be male and not female, because the Burnt Offering <term>Olah: literally "that which ascends"</term> certainly "ascends upon the heart" <note>a wordplay on the Hebrew 'Olah' and the rising of thoughts</note> and it is known who stands over the heart. Because of this, it ascends Above and all are male; regarding this, the verse opens with the secret of the Burnt Offering more than all other sacrifices, for this is Thought, the head of all.

**Rabbi** Yehuda said: By the Living God! After Thought is aroused Above, it seeks to draw near and manifest Below even more. But he did not have the explanation in his hand. He came before Rabbi Shimon [bar Yochai] and said to him: The head of all is Thought, and the establishment of that Thought is the place where they search the "herd" <note>baqar</note>, and that establishment of the "Body of Wisdom" <note>Guf ha-Chokhmah</note> shows him how to establish it. Thus, from Thought, the male protects the head of all; the establishment of that Thought, when the action is performed, is "in the morning" <note>ba-boqer - a pun on 'herd'</note>. This is what is written: *Woe to those who rise early in the morning... and the work of His hands they do not perceive* <note>Isaiah 5:11-12</note>. For when the morning returns and they occupy themselves with it, it reaches that place where Thought ascends, and the deed certainly draws near to the day of Thought.

Rabbi Chiya was walking on the road and Rabbi Yehuda was with him. As they were walking, Rabbi Yehuda said: That which we have learned regarding the "Virgin of Israel" <note>the Shekhinah/Community of Israel</note>, who is blessed from the Seven <note>the lower seven Sefirot/divine emanations</note> who search "Bathsheba" <note>literally 'Daughter of Seven'</note>, we have established this in several places. And in the Mountain of Mercy, the blessings of the assembly reside. But what of that which is written: *And you, son of man, take up a lamentation for the Virgin of Israel* <note>Ezekiel 27:2 / Amos 5:2</note>? Certainly, this was said concerning the Community of Israel, and this matter is difficult, for it is written: *She has fallen, she shall rise no more, the Virgin of Israel*. Now, I have seen all the companions explain this matter well. But by the life of the Torah, I was seeing it like two waters <note>uncertainly</note>, but in this lamentation, it is said that Wisdom is lacking.

He said to him: It is certainly so, and this word is more difficult to me than all else. We came before Rabbi Shimon with poor and downcast faces. He said to me: From that which is in your heart, it is known what you wish to ask, for your face is pale and your heart is troubled. I said to him: Tell me the meaning of what is written: *She has fallen, she shall rise no more, the Virgin of Israel* <note>Amos 5:2</note>. If a man has anger toward his wife and she leaves him, shall she never return? Heaven forbid! Especially regarding the children who were exiled with her.

He said to me: Is it not enough for you what all the companions have said? I replied: I have heard their words, but they are not settled in my heart. He said: Everything the companions said is all beautiful and appropriate, but woe to the generation when the shepherds are not found and the flock goes astray, not knowing where they are going, neither to eat nor to drink. This verse must be understood, and all is revealed for the times before us.

Come and see: In all the exiles that Israel was exiled, they all had an end and a limit, and in all of them, Israel returned to the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Virgin of Israel returned to her place at the time He decreed for her. But now, in this final exile, it is not so. She will not return as she did in other times. And this verse proves it, for it is written: *She has fallen, she shall rise no more, the Virgin of Israel*. Note that it does not say "He [God] shall no longer raise her up." 

This is like a king who was angry with his Matronita <term>Matronita: The Queen/Divine Presence</term> and cast her out of his palace for a certain time. When that time arrived, immediately the Matronita would return and come before the king. This happened once, twice, and three times. But for the final time, she was distanced from the king's palace, and the king saw her from his palace at a distance. The king said: This time, it is not like the other times where she must come before me. Rather, I will go with all the people of my palace and I will seek her out. When he reaches her house, he will lift her from the dust. What greater honor is there for the Matronita than at that time? <note>The Zohar reinterprets the verse: She will not rise on her own, but God Himself will descend into the exile to raise her up.</note>

<summary>This page discusses the mystical requirements of the Burnt Offering (Olah) as a "male" sacrifice representing pure Thought, before transitioning into a famous Zoharic reinterpretation of Amos 5:2. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai explains that the "Virgin of Israel" (the Shekhinah) will not rise from her final exile by her own power, but rather God Himself will descend to lift her up.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the restoration of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) and the symbolic meaning of the Shofar, following the themes of exile and redemption found in the Zohar's commentary on the book of Leviticus (Vayikra).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Blessed are they and the requests they bring before the King to receive her, until the King shows her his hands <note>A metaphor for divine strength and action</note> and raises her up and returns her to her place, showing her that he shall never be separated from her again; and this shall be established in faith. So it is with the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <term>Kadosh Barukh Hu: the masculine aspect of the Divine</term>. All the times that the **Assembly of Israel** <term>Knesset Yisrael: the mystical community of souls and the Shekhinah</term> is in exile, when the time arrives, she awakens and binds herself before the King. But now, in this exile, it is not so; rather, the **Holy One, Blessed be He** will take her by His hands and raise her up, and be reconciled with her, and return her to her place.

And come and see that it is so, for it is written:
> *The virgin of Israel is fallen, she shall no more rise.* (Amos 5:2)

And regarding this it is written:
> *In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen.* (Amos 9:11)

She herself "shall no more rise" on her own from the time she was destroyed, but *He* shall raise her up. **The fallen Sukkah of David** <term>Sukkat David: a metaphor for the Shekhinah in her state of exile</term>—who is this Sukkah of David? This is the "virgin of Israel" who fell, as it is written, "she is fallen and shall no more rise," referring to the virgin of Israel; and from her wisdom, she did not learn this through her own testimony. **Rabbi Yehuda** said: The trees are for the sake of her choice in praise, and this is the clarity of the matter, and these things are like a word that exists in the expansiveness of the Lord. For we have learned that **Rabbi Yossi** said: The **Holy One, Blessed be He** is destined to make a proclamation concerning the **Assembly of Israel** and will say:
> *Shake thyself from the dust; arise, and sit down, O Jerusalem.* (Isaiah 52:2)

Like one who takes the hand of his friend and says, "Shake yourself off and arise," so the **Holy One, Blessed be He** will speak to her and say, "Shake yourself off and arise." **Rabbi Abba** said to him: And so all those members of the King's palace open the order with this melody:
> *Arise, shine; for thy light is come.* (Isaiah 60:1)

The King is here, and there is great honor and joy for all when the King is reconciled with her. It is written, "And Bathsheba went in unto the king into the chamber"; in this manner, in all those times, she came to the King and stood before him, as in "she came before the King and stood before the King." But in this time <note>the final redemption</note>, it is not so; rather, the King will come to her and be reconciled with her and come to receive her. This is what is written:
> *Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion... behold, thy King cometh unto thee.* (Zechariah 9:9)

Certainly, she does not go to Him. Blessed is she that He comes to appease you, "comes to you" to prepare you, "shall be to you" to provide for you; all of them shall be for you, to elevate you, to sustain you, and for joy with you for all eternity. Then "I will betroth thee unto Me in faithfulness." While they were walking, **Rabbi Yitzhak** met them. They said: Behold, the path of the **Shekhinah** <term>The Divine Presence</term> comes to receive the faces of the Shekhinah. When they drew near as one, the light of the lamp shone and was established correctly. He opened and said:
> *And the voice of the shofar waxed louder and louder.* (Exodus 19:19)

The "voice of the shofar" is mentioned here; our ancient books and all of them are established in one word. "The voice of the shofar" implies two voices: one of the shofar, making two. And one who is precise notes that it does not say "And the shofar waxed louder," but rather "the *voice* of the shofar"—the voice that emerges from the shofar. Truly, it is called **Shofar** as in "He shall blow with a **Great Shofar**" <term>Shofar Gadol: the horn of the Jubilee, symbolizing ultimate liberation</term>. And which is the shofar through which servants go out to eternal **Freedom** <term>Herut</term>? This has been established. And one who is precise notes that all is one, as it is written "the voice of the shofar," the voice that is called "shofar." And from here we know it is called "voice" from what is written:
> *...a great voice, and it was not heard again.* (Deuteronomy 5:19)

And this voice is called "shofar," and regarding this, "the voice of the shofar *goes*" is written. "Goes"—this refers to the living word at Mount Sinai, which was for Israel and all that was needed. Rather, the **Torah** <term>Oraita: the divine Law/Wisdom</term> is found in it, and this was awakened, for all other rectifications are seen through these words. Regarding the ancients, these words were hinted at, and this is the spirit of the matter as it is written:
> *Graven upon the tables.* (Exodus 32:16)

Do not read it as *charut* (graven), but as *cherut* (**freedom**); literal freedom, for all freedom depends upon it. And come and see, there is no other matter like this. In freedom, everything does not go to one place and one seeking, to cover and shield all; "all the rivers run into the sea," and it is written, "all go unto one place." "And waxed very strong"—as we have learned, "a vessel that holds blessing" is the **Secret of the Lord** <term>Sod Hashem</term>. "And waxed very strong"—for you have no word of the Torah that does not have the power to break, for every word is established and you will find it as strong as a hammer that shatters rocks. And its voice is as they established it, as it is written:
> *For it is not a vain thing for you.* (Deuteronomy 32:47)

And if it is "vain," it is "from you" <note>meaning any perceived emptiness in the Torah is due to the reader's lack of understanding</note>. And regarding this, "and waxed very strong" is written.

It also explores the symbolism of the "Voice of the Shofar" at Sinai as a source of eternal freedom and the inherent strength of the Torah.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the book of Leviticus (Vayikra). It transitions from discussing the unique nature of Moses's prophecy to a symbolic interpretation of the soul using the laws of the priesthood.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Leviticus** <-

It is written: *Moses would speak, and God would answer him with a voice* <note>Exodus 19:19</note>. All of these [other prophets] were not included in this manner, for it is established that "Moses would speak," and it is also written, "And God remembered" <note>original: *v'yizkor v'dechar Elohim*</note>. And so it is written, *Moses would speak*. However, some say it is because it is written: *And they said to Moses, "You speak with us and we will hear, but let not God speak with us"* <note>Exodus 20:15</note>. Because of this, *Moses would speak and God would answer him*, for not a single word in the Torah is found to come from the mouth of Moses alone. And this is what they established: "The curses in the Torah <note>specifically those in Deuteronomy</note> Moses spoke from his own mouth." From this we learn they were spoken from his own mouth. These [in Leviticus] were from the mouth of the **Might** <note>original: *Gevurah* - a term for God's attribute of Strength/Severity</note> and those [in Deuteronomy] were from his own mouth—from that **Voice** to which he was attached, which is called by this name, and the matter is well-explained. And in the Book of Aggadah of the School of Rav, they said: even though the entire Torah was stated from the mouth of the **Might**, it was likewise stated from the mouth of Moses himself. And what is this? For example, the curses in the Torah, which were later included in the **Might**. This is the meaning of *Moses would speak and God would answer him with a voice*. *Moses would speak*—this is the voice of Moses. *And God would answer him with a voice*—this is the **Might** which joined with that voice so that He would answer him with a voice like the voice of Moses. And he opened with words that began like the words of the Torah, therefore all were happy with him. They said: it is written, and the words he opened with shall be given to the day.

**Rabbi Abba opened** and said: It is written, *And if a priest’s daughter is a widow or divorced and has no offspring...* <note>Leviticus 22:13</note>. Worthy is the portion of Israel above all the nations who worship stars and constellations, for the Holy One, blessed be He, when He created the world, only created it for the sake of Israel so that they would receive the Torah at Mount Sinai and increase like the whole [creation] and be found righteous before Him. Come and see: when this world is perfected through Israel in the **likeness of that which is above**, and that path which they tread in their level reaches its height up to the Throne, like the essence of the sacrifice, the Holy One, blessed be He, agrees to draw the **Holy Name** from above to below so that it may be joined and bound together. For the Holy One, blessed be He, created [man], as it is written: *And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground...* <note>Genesis 2:7</note> to be a bond of one with the other, so that the world would be found in the **likeness of that which is above**. And if he prepares and rectifies himself thus, just as He created him **male and female** to be complete. And he is called "complete" <note>original: *chumta*</note> when they are whole in the **likeness of that which is above**. Just as the reason for pairing with one's mate is according to the law... in desire, to produce strength and dedication, so too is the **priest's daughter**. When they are complete in the **likeness of that which is above**, he inherits below in the likeness of the **Holy Name** upon him, and then the **Holy Name** is called upon him. But a man who does not wish to be completed in the **Holy Name** below, it would be better for him had he not been created, for he has no portion at all in the **Holy Name**. And when his soul departs from him, it is not found in him at all, for he lacks the image of his Master until he is bound, and there is no remedy for anything. This is the meaning of: *And if a priest’s daughter is a widow or divorced*. The **priest's daughter** is the **Holy Soul**, which is called the daughter of the King. For the wisdom of the **Holy Soul** emerges from the union of the **King and the Matronit**. Because of this, just as the body below is from **male and female**, so too is the soul above. *If she becomes a widow*—this is the body that went to the secular realm in its days. *And divorced*—that she was cast out from that portion of the **Holy Name**. And why all this? Because *she has no offspring*—to be found in the **likeness of that which is above** and to be bound to the **Holy Name**. *And she returns to her father’s house*—who is "she returns"? She returns to be rectified as she was at first, and then *she returns to her father’s house*, for the Holy One, blessed be He, is *as in her youth*, as in the beginning. *Of her father’s bread she shall eat*—to delight in the delight of the King. From here on: *but no stranger shall eat of the holy thing*. These are the "strangers"—the one who did not establish the **Holy Name** below and has no portion in it. *He shall not eat of the holy thing*—he has no portion in the delight of above which belongs to everyone, as it is written: *Eat, friends; drink, and be drunk with love* <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>. Above is the delight of the holy.

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of sacrifices and the unification of Divine attributes. It transitions into an exegesis of Psalm 133 to explain the relationship between the Holy One and the Community of Israel.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Leviticus<-

The smoke ascended, and this matter rests after all the spirit of the sacrifice rises up. And come and see the reason that faith is found below, as the vision above proves. It is like a King who prepared a feast for himself but did not prepare it for his servants. When he came to his servants, he ate from his own feast and they ate from theirs. This is what is written <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note> **"I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey"**—this is the feast of the King. **"Eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved"**—this is their feast from the leftovers of the sacrifice. Because of this, it is called "a sweet savor unto the Lord." "Savor" for His servants, "Sweet" for the Lord. This is from the mystery of the Ancient One <note>term: Atika (The Ancient One) - the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note> that is found. And for this reason, the King’s feast is delayed for the sake of the feast of His servants. Because of this, Israel provides sustenance for their Father in Heaven through the daily offerings. And from the King’s feast, everyone is nourished. Portions of strength are distributed to the righteous.

Furthermore, he opened his discourse and said <note>Psalm 133:1</note> **"Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity."** Worthy are the people of Israel, for at all times the Holy One, blessed be He, desires them to be at ease, and His Presence rests upon them more abundantly. He holds onto their existence; first He called them "servants" before the Holy One, as it is written <note>Leviticus 25:55</note> **"For unto Me the children of Israel are servants; they are My servants."** Afterwards, He called them "children," as it is said <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note> **"Ye are the children of the Lord your God."** Afterwards, He called them "brothers," as it is written <note>Psalm 122:8</note> **"For my brethren and companions' sakes."** And because He called them brothers, He desired to settle His dwelling place among them and never depart from them. Then it is written: "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity."

And the Holy Scripture says this: "Behold, how good and how pleasant" is the general rule, and "a man shall not rise up against his sister"—this refers to the Community of Israel <note>term: Knesset Yisrael - the mystical personification of the people of Israel, often identified with the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> who is called the "sister" of the Holy One, blessed be He. It lacks "rising up for his sister"—why is this? It lacks *Hesed* <note>term: Hesed - the Divine attribute of Loving-kindness</note>, the Kindness of Abraham. They have established this, and regarding this: "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity"—this refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel. The word "also" <note>original: "gam" (גם)</note> comes to include Israel below, when they are refined in that hour when the Community of Israel is as one. The Community of Israel below dwells as one, and we have learned that they "also" cling to the Holy One, blessed be He, and therefore "also in unity" is written.

And like a flower to the Great One, as it is called here "also in unity" to include the Righteous One <note>note: likely referring to the Sefirah of Yesod</note> toward this Community of Israel. They are one preparation and everything is one matter. And we have learned in the section of "Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One" <note>The Shema prayer</note>: What is "One"? This is the Community of Israel which is united with the Holy One, blessed be He. For Rabbi Shimon said: The union of male and female is called "One." After the female rests [with the male], He is called "One." What is the reason? Because a male without a female is called "half a body," and a half is not "one." When they are joined as one, two halves become one body, and then it is called "One." But now [in exile], the Holy One, blessed be He, is not called "One" [in the lower worlds].

And the secret of the matter: The Community of Israel is like a garden, and the Holy One, blessed be He, ascends higher and higher, and goes to spread out. This holy flow is *Hesed* (Kindness), which is complete, and below it is not called [One]. But it will be called "One" at the time when the Matronita <note>term: Matronita - The Noble Lady/Queen, a title for the Shekhinah</note> is found with the King and they are coupled as one. This is what is written <note>Obadiah 1:21</note> **"And the kingdom shall be the Lord's."** See, "Kingdom" is the Community of Israel, through which the King is established. Then <note>Zechariah 14:9</note> **"In that day shall the Lord be one, and His name one."** And regarding this: "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity."

And it is written <note>Psalm 133:2</note> **"It is like the precious oil upon the head."** See, "the precious oil" is the Kindness (*Hesed*) of the holy softness that flows and emerges from the Holy Ancient One, which is found in that Supernal Crown (*Keter*), the Holy Beard <note>term: Dikna Kadisha - the "Holy Beard," a Kabbalistic metaphor for the channels of Divine mercy flowing from the highest source</note> that is prepared to kindle the lamps. And that Kindness flows onto the head of the King, and from its mystery to the glory of the Holy Beard, and from there it flows to all those garments of glory of the King which are perfected by them. This is what is written: "that ran down upon the beard." "Upon the beard"—this is Kindness, and these are the crowns of the King of the holy heavens that are found in them. Come and see: all the treasures and all the joy of the worlds do not come to be blessed except through those holy crowns, through those [emanations] of the Holy King. And thus: "that ran down upon the beard." "The beard" certainly—everything is according to Aaron <note>note: Aaron the High Priest represents the attribute of Hesed/Kindness</note>, and so it shall be, according to the measures that weaken and flow to all the worlds, so that blessings are found for all. And come and see, this precious oil...

It describes how Divine Kindness (Hesed) flows from the highest crown down to the lower worlds, likened to the anointing oil on Aaron's beard.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the sacrificial system and the necessity of joy in divine service. It connects the concept of the "Sacrifice" (Korban) to the restoration of cosmic unity.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Vayikra (And He Called)**<-

It is good for her <note>referring to the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> at the times when the service below ascends and they meet one another. Behold, "Oil and incense rejoice the heart" <note>Proverbs 27:9</note>; incense is prepared above and incense below, and then there is joy for all. Rabbi Chasdai and Rabbi Yose lifted their hands and gave thanks to Rabbi Chasdai. Rabbi Chasdai opened his discourse: "And a dream came... and he dreamed a dream" <note>referring to the dreams of Joseph or general dream phenomena</note>. It is written: "And God said to him in a dream, 'I also knew that you did this in the integrity of your heart...'" <note>Genesis 20:6</note>. By my life! "And God came to Abimelech in a dream of the night"—what is the praise here regarding the dreams of the world? "And God came to Abimelech in a dream of the night" contains a secret regarding the dreams of others.

You should know that because the Holy One, blessed be He, is high and exalted, dwelling forever and Holy is His Name, He is King over all. When He descends, His holy palace is prepared in restraint below. Within it are seventy crowns, and from here seventy ministers are appointed over the seventy nations of the world, to see that each one rules over his nation and his land. They receive and guard the spirit of impurity in their studies. But the Voice <note>the Divine Word</note> rules over Israel and Jerusalem, for "Your name is called upon Your city and upon Your people" <note>Daniel 9:19</note>.

No other nation has a portion in the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written: "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you" <note>Deuteronomy 28:10</note>. And it is written: "For all peoples walk each in the name of his god, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God" <note>Micah 4:5</note>. And it is written: "For the Lord's portion is His people..." <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>. Rather, we have learned: every mention of "God" <term>Elohim - a name associated with judgment and universal governance</term> here refers to that great power appointed over them. Similarly, "And God came to Balaam at night"—this refers to the power appointed over him. And if you say, "And God said in a dream of the night," it is so. By my life! "I also knew"—the word "also" <note>Hebrew: *gam*</note> comes to include something more. Even though it is known from the power above, "I also knew." "And I also withheld you"—the "also" includes you. However, the word for "sinning against Me" <note>Hebrew: *me-chato*</note> is written without the letter *Aleph*. What does this say? Because he placed them in the standing powers.

Rather, this is the exchange: just as the people below cause a blemish above, so the people below can remove their ministers above from their dominion. "And I also withheld you"—after the matter depends on the one above, "I also" includes Himself. "From sinning against Me" <note>original: *me-chato li*</note>—because they were not found barking <note>like dogs</note> at this time. For if you cause me to sin through your guilt, it would remove me from my dominion and my seniority, as it is said: "And I will be zealous..." In these matters, we learn that through the sins of human beings, they create a blemish within the inner realms above, and it strikes the bosom of all. In simplicity, it ascends to heat and cover.

And for this reason, a **Sacrifice** <term>Korban - from the root 'to draw near'</term> is offered. Why is it called a *Korban*? It is as we said: after simplicity forgives the violence that caused a separation within, the *Korban* brings the upper world near to the lower world, and everything is made one.

Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Judah taught, and they waited for Rabbi Isaac. Rabbi Judah opened: "Serve the Lord with gladness..." <note>Psalms 100:2</note> and "Serve the Lord with fear" <note>Psalms 2:11</note>. The service that a person must perform for the Holy One, blessed be He, must be with gladness and joy, with the will of the heart, so that his service is found in perfection. And if you say: the service of the sacrifice—is it not a loss? For that man who transgressed the commandment of his Master, the commandment of the Torah, and returns before his Master like one who is ashamed—surely he stands before Him with a broken spirit and a sad spirit! Where then is the joy and the song?

However, we have learned there: that man who stands before his Master and transgressed His commandments and sinned, brings a sacrifice to repair himself with a broken spirit and a sad spirit. But the joy and the song are found in the service of the Priests and the Levites. For they complete the joy and the song on our behalf. **Joy** is in the **Priest** <term>Kohen</term> to prepare, because he is always far from Judgment <term>Din</term>, and he must always be found with a shining countenance and more joy than all the people, for his crown is light. **Song** <note>or "ringing cry"</note> is in the **Levites**, and so it is, for the Levites are found in song forever, as they have established. And the hosts stand over it.

<summary>This page explains that while a sinner brings a sacrifice with a broken heart, the Priests and Levites provide the necessary joy and song to complete the ritual, drawing the upper and lower worlds together into unity.</summary>
