<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), focusing on the spiritual mechanics of prayer and sacrifice as a means of unifying the Divine Name.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Divine service and prayer are a service to the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: HaKadosh Baruch Hu</note>, consisting of praise for Him and the directing of words with joy and will, to arrange the holy praise as is fitting and to unify the Name. Thus it is written:
> Know that the Lord, He is God <note>Psalm 100:3</note>

For this is the essence of the sacrifice <note>term: Korban (sacrifice/offering), from the root meaning "to draw near"</note>: to bring Mercy near to Judgment so that everything becomes sweetened. He opened his discourse saying: A sacrifice is not found except from one who has sinned before his Master and returns to Him, breaking the bitterness of the soul, as it is written:
> The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit <note>Psalm 51:19</note>

To establish the Name and the connection, for these were not found with him previously. Rather, they established it thus: that those who are dependent and shining in their sickness, and the binding of their illness, do not possess joy or clarity. And we have learned: "One should not stand [to pray] from a state of sadness" <note>Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 31a</note>, for a person should not stand before his Master in sadness, as he cannot then establish his proper state. Rather, the matter is that he must always be prepared... <note>The OCR contains several corrupted or phonetic strings here: "kham adam se'or sheki pitchis," likely reflecting difficult manuscript shorthand or damaged text</note>... all of this hints at what King David said: Your mercies are the dwelling and the foundation of life within the inner secrets of the levels of Kindness <note>term: Chesed</note> and Fear <note>term: Pachad/Gevurah</note>, which are the openings of the world. Therefore, a person must intend in his devotion to face the Holy of Holies, which are the holy supports and all the exiles. And like these twenty-two crowns and the devotion that is taught here, this "Joy" is the **Assembly of Israel** <note>term: Knesset Yisrael, a mystical personification of the Jewish people and the Divine Presence/Shekhinah</note>. And they established Joy for her, as it is written:
> For with joy you shall go out... <note>Isaiah 55:12</note>

And Israel is destined to go out from exile through this Joy. And what is she? She is the **Assembly of Israel**. And regarding this:
> Serve the Lord with joy <note>Psalm 100:2</note>

As it is written:
> Come before Him with singing <note>Psalm 100:2</note>

For his perfection is not complete without Joy, and the binding... was a greater perfection. And the perfection of this Joy is recognized and becomes known, and this is the preparation of a person before his Master. Then "Know that the Lord, He is God" becomes as one word; the transgression is removed to the Crown <note>Keter</note> to unify the Holy Name as is fitting, and to bind this to that so that all becomes one. This is the service of the Holy One, Blessed be He. They said to him: Rabbi Chama, is it not written so? Blessed is the portion of the righteous who labor in the Torah and know the ways of the Holy One, Blessed be He. They rose and went on their way... Rabbi Abba opened and said: "As a cherub covering..." <note>referring to the golden figures on the Ark</note> thus they established it, that a person should not be covered when entering the synagogue, but if your fear is as it was at first... for you have established the exile before the Holy One, Blessed be He... This refers to the Throne. "Join toward Your holy Temple"—this refers to Isaac, and he needs to include them in the Throne and enter the synagogue and reveal his exile. Then it is written:
> And He said to me, "You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified." <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

---

**If** his offering is a burnt offering from the herd <note>Leviticus 1:3</note>. Rabbi Yose said: What is the difference between "from the herd," "from the flock," and "from the birds"? If all is one, why are they distinguished from one another, since from all of them one thing is accomplished? Rather, whoever has the means brings from the herd. And if he cannot, then from the flock. And if he cannot, then from the birds. For it is written: "And if for the Lord..." for the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not burden a person more than he is able. Rabbi Eleazar said: According to the sin, so he offers. There are times when a wealthy man must offer a bull because his sin was greater in sinning before his Master. Another offers from the flock because his will was not so great in sinning. A poor man, whose means are not great and whose will is like yours, offers that which is lighter than all... and their offerings are recognized, each one individually, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, sees the pressure of each one according to the weight of his heart. Rabbi Eleazar went to the house of Maon as a guest. He said to him: We have learned that because of three things famine comes to the world, and yet we find only the wealthy [suffering?], for their hearts... and they are not found like the poor...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Leviticus<-

The Holy One, Blessed be He, <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note> kills the poor and revives the wealthy, for from their sins and their ceasing to sin before Him, there is no moment or end to His wisdom. His companions said: when the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to punish the wicked and grant goodness to them in the world, He then gives them peace and tranquility in everything. Come and see that all the people of the world are not found to be close to the Supernal King; they are all darkened because their sins are upon them. And who are those [who are close]? Those with a broken and crushed spirit, as it is written: **and with him that is of a contrite and humble spirit** <note>Isaiah 57:15</note>. These are the vessels of the King. And when lack is found in the world and famine strengthens against the poor, then they all cry out before the King, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, draws them closer than anyone else. This is what is written: **For He hath not despised nor abhorred the lowliness of the poor** <note>Psalms 22:25</note>. And then the Holy One, Blessed be He, remembers the world and brings down sustenance to the world and feeds the hunger of the world. Woe to those guilty ones who cause this! For if the King is awakened to gaze upon the world by the voice of the poor who cry out to be saved from their pain and their oppression, then it is written: **I will surely hear his cry** <note>Exodus 22:22</note>. "Surely hear" <note>original: *shamoa eshma* - a double expression in Hebrew</note> implies two merits: one to gaze upon their voice, and one to take vengeance from those who caused this for them. This is what is written: **and I will hear, for I am gracious... and My wrath shall wax hot** <note>Exodus 22:23-24</note>. And because of this, this is the claim of the open-eyed that is found in the world: woe to those wealthy sinners, for the cries of the poor are before the Holy One, Blessed be He.

Come and see that the sacrifice of the poor man is lighter than all others, because his heart is broken, and it is not a disgrace that he brings a sacrifice for the sin he committed, for his poverty and his shame are enough for him. And because of this, every single sacrifice is recognized individually by the priest. There is the praise of that wealthy man who brought [a sacrifice] before the priest twice; when he sinned, the priest said to him: "This sacrifice is not your way." He went to his house and was sad. They said to him: "Why are you sad?" He said to them: "Because the priest did not perform the service for my sacrifice." They said to him: "And what sin did you commit?" He said to them: "Two kinds." They said to him: "But look at the poor man who is not like you, for it is written: **When a soul sins** <note>Leviticus 2:1</note>—'a soul' etc.—and he does not bring a sacrifice." He said to them: "From his obligation." They said to him: "One ox." He said to them: "And is the sin so grave that the sin is according to the way that you did not spare your merit from the saving of sins?" From then on, what did he do? Every day he busied himself with trade, and it was a disgrace... when he was awakened, he would call to his brother and they would change his garments to white, and he would labor until he ascended and was wiped clean. For the sake of laboring in the Torah, whiteness does not require luxuries or trade, but rather to be filled with the cup and the brain. Because of this, they killed the memory of his whiteness. This is what is written: "And when you give a nest, the staff..." <unclear>textual corruption</unclear>. And you performed kindness with all the Children of Israel. Because the King... the staff like his house. And we have learned: because he changed his portion one extra time in joy and performed kindness with Israel, and his words... all this matter is like the war of Amalek. Rather, the "haven" <note>original: *mahoz*</note>—when all of Israel went out from Egypt, from all the other nations of the world, there was no one to push Israel or to prosecute them except for Amalek. And he made a "nest" <note>original: *ken*</note> for Israel and waged war against them, and you preceded them with peace and performed kindness with them, and thus there is no... then to be... And not only that, but what is written concerning Jethro? **And Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took a burnt-offering and sacrifices for God** <note>Exodus 18:12</note>. For he came to bring a sacrifice to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and to see that we have learned the sin-offering speaks of the sacrifice...

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of sacrifices and the structure of the cosmos. ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Leviticus**<-

It is carved before the Holy One, blessed be He, and because it is beloved when one brings an offering to the Holy One, blessed be He, it is written: <note>Exodus 18:12</note> *And Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law before God.* "Before God" is stated precisely. From all this we learn that whoever brings an offering with a willing heart <note>term: "re'uta de-libba" — the mystical intention or "will of the heart" that elevates a physical act</note>, the Holy One, blessed be He, is present before him. Come and see: the offering of a poor man is carved before the Holy One, blessed be He, for he actually brings two offerings before Him. One is his own fat and blood <note>meaning his physical exertion and the hunger he suffers to afford the sacrifice</note>, and the other is the actual sacrifice he brings, for he has nothing to eat, and that sacrifice is his very life. The lightest offering of them all is two turtledoves or two young pigeons, and if not even that, a little flour, and he is atoned through it. At that moment, heralds go forth and say: <note>Psalms 22:25</note> *For He has not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the poor.* Why all this? Because the offering of the poor is superior to all, for he grinds himself down to be part of the "moistness" <note>the divine flow of life</note>. Therefore, I have commanded concerning all the property of the poor, for they have caused Me all this. Just as the poor man prepares his fat and blood, so that flour is prepared with five types of kneading. And so we have learned, that even if any person brings this meal-offering upon the Altar, it is refined; for just as the "engraver" <note>the divine attribute of Judgment</note> cuts into his fat and blood through the sin of evil judgment, and all the edges of Mercy [are blunted] by sin, so this offering acts like the "swords" that draw down [grace] from below. The essence of the sin offering brought before the Holy One, blessed be He, is the will of his heart, his spirit, and his longing—this is more beloved than anything else before Him. Happy is the portion of the righteous, for they bring this offering before the Holy One, blessed be He, every single day. And what is it? It is their very bodies and their longings that they offer before Him. This is how we must truly bring this offering, and this is what the Holy One, blessed be He, desires. Above all, the offering of the "All" <note>the collective community</note> is superior so that all the worlds may be blessed. Furthermore, he opened and said: <note>Psalms 135:21</note> *Blessed be the Lord out of Zion, who dwells in Jerusalem. Hallelujah.* How many times is He "Blessed"? This flows from the deep, supernal spring—He is Blessed. Rather, "Blessed be the Lord" refers to when the Moon <note>the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> is illuminated by the light of the Sun <note>the Holy One</note> and they draw near to one another, so that one light does not destroy the other. Sometimes, in its clarity, it is called by the Name of the King, as it is written: <note>Genesis 19:24</note> *And the Lord rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the Lord out of heaven.* Not only this, but even a single messenger from them is called by the Name of the King. To the Lord: "Blessed be the Lord out of Zion"—from which place is the Holy One, blessed be He, known? He is Blessed, and then [known] "from Zion"; from the place of Zion it is known that He is Blessed. What is the reason? Because it is written: <note>Psalms 133:3</note> *For there the Lord commanded the blessing, even life for evermore.* Rabbi Isaac returned to him: Happy is the portion of the righteous who are alive and vigorous, those who labor in the Torah; for whoever labors in the Torah is entirely grasped by the Holy One, blessed be He. This is what is written: <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note> *But you who did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day.*

---

**If** his offering be a sacrifice of peace offering <note>Leviticus 3:1</note>. Rabbi Judah opened: <note>Genesis 1:6</note> *And God said: "Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters..."* Come and see: according to the pattern by which the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He created seven firmaments above, He created seven lands below, seven seas, seven rivers, seven times, seven weeks, seven years, seven cycles, and the thousands of years that the world exists—the Holy One, blessed be He, is the seventh of them all. He ascended on high, and in each and every one are stars, constellations, and ministers who minister in each and every firmament. All of them drive chariots <note>term: "ratikhin" — celestial vehicles or angelic assemblies</note>, one above the other, to receive upon themselves the yoke of the kingdom of their Master. In all the firmaments, there are chariots and ministers differing from one another, one above the other. Some have twenty-six wings, and some have twenty-four wings. Some have four faces, and some have two faces. Some are made of consuming fire, some of water, and some of the spirit that is occupied [in service]. Some hold spears [standing] from one side to the other. All these firmaments are one above the other like the layers of an onion, these below and those above. Each and every firmament moves and trembles from the awe of their Master; by His word they all stand. The eye of the Holy One, blessed be He, is over all of them, sustaining them all with His strength and power. In this same manner, there are seven lands below, and all of them are a covering, except that these are in fear...

## Main Text (Zohar)

This firmament makes peace between them, and the worlds are only sustained through peace. Come and see <note>original: "Ta chazi"</note>: the Holy One, Blessed be He, is called "Peace," His name is "Peace," and everything is bound together in peace. Rabbi Abba said: I have seen that this supreme Holy Brain <note>The "Holy Brain" refers to the highest cognitive levels of the Divine, often associated with the Sefirah of Chokhmah (Wisdom) or the hidden Crown</note> is entirely peace and entirely one. Yet they spread out to this side and to that side, and all of them, from the side of the Holy Brain, are bound together in three knots. This is because there is one Master above, one Master below, and one in the middle. For three knots are found in Him: one Master above, who is the highest of all heights, appearing as the Supreme Crown <note>Keter</note>, which is the Head of all Heads, and He stands over all. One Master is in the middle, which is another Head, for there are three Heads, and each one is a Head on its own. And one Master in the middle—this is another Head of which it is written "the source from above," and it is the Head for all other Heads to establish the holy side, and this is the Head that is the most hidden of all. The other lower Head is a Head to look toward, and it is the fountain of water from which all drops are watered. And this is the letter *Yod* <note>The first letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing the point of Wisdom</note> with its three knots. And the letter *Ayin* <note>Numerical value 70</note> is called "perfection"; in this perfection, everything is bound together and everything is one. Thirdly, **in the Book of Enoch**, at the time when they showed him the supreme levels of wisdom, he saw the tree of the Garden of Eden and they showed him Wisdom in a supreme mystery. He saw that all the worlds were bound one to another. He asked them: "Upon what do they stand?" They said to him: "All seventy <note>The 70 nations or 70 names of God</note> stand, and from Him they are found and perfected." And he saw that they all tremble from the fear of the Matron <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note>, and all of them are called by the seventy names.

**And in the Book** of King Solomon, he said: We have seen the *Katpora* <note>A technical term for a divine structure or "cluster"</note> below which are included in the clusters of the body itself. One vision showed that they are all hidden measures, one like a deep pitcher. Afterward, he specified on its own to change the house in its completion, and this is like the way the whole is one hidden measure and one deep Crown for all the hidden things of the Holy Brain, the Head of all, the Father of all. And so the fear <note>or "sand"</note> goes out from it, and from it is found the letter *Dalet*, the daughter of her Master, in whose hand all judgments are found, hidden in all the worlds. Because of this, the upper and lower beings went out from her. The seal of this is the letter *Yod*, the perfection of all. The Holy One is destined to look into it, and it is found hidden within the Crown. The *Yod* brings everything out and curls everything in a single bond; this is the whole. And this is the precious, holy Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>, and it brings out that river of which it is written:
> And a river went out of Eden to water the garden <note>Genesis 2:10</note>
In its colors, this is the letter *Kaf*, the spirit of Understanding <note>Binah</note>, and it is the supreme life. From this river go out two children, as has been said, and from it they are nourished. Afterward, two sons and a daughter go out and are nourished from there; this is the *Vav* and the *He*. The Priest, the King of Solomon—all is his. And afterward, the *He* is found to be nourished from the *Vav*. And this Wisdom is found to be the *Yod*, the root and the source and the perfection of all. Thus, <term>by wisdom a house is built</term> <note>Proverbs 24:3; a reference to Chokhmah building the "house" of Binah or the world</note>. We have learned: at the time they were completed and went out from this *Yod*, which is the sheaf of life, He perfected them all. And the holy river, when it conceives and guards its hiddenness, all are hidden as one, and all are hidden in the *Yod*. He includes them and brings them out. And this is the Father of all, the Father of Wisdom; from Him they go out and in Him they dwell. They rise to the Crown according to the count of the seal: *Yod* includes *Nun* and *Lamed* <margin>(Folio 11a)</margin>, the perfection of all. And the *Lamed* is male and female; we call them "two" <note>original: "du"</note>, and because of this, they were made into "two faces" <note>original: "du-partzuphin"; the concept that the original human/divine form was male and female joined back-to-back</note>. And those faces, male and female, were like the pattern above. And the *Lamed* is from the world below to the *Vav*, and the *Vav* is to the world above, and the whole thing is one matter. Twelve measures hang from it, and until the *Yod* includes the *Lamed* as was said. And this is Wisdom, and the *Tav* and *Vav*—from this they are toward it. **And in the Book** of the Father of the Present, the Elder, the Child, they prepare two levels corresponding to two firmaments, and they benefit from this Crown, and she shall taste and understand it and her oath. The first is *Yah* <note>The first two letters of the Name of God</note>, because the *Yod* includes the *He*, and the *He* goes out from the *Yod*. Like the "G-B" <note>Gevurah-Binah</note>, Wisdom is called *Yah* secondarily, and the generation is called *Elohim* because that river is mercy. And because judgments are awakened from it and go out to show mercy, it is written "with the voice of peace," as it is written:
> The Lord will give strength to His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace. <note>Psalms 29:11</note>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the sacrificial offerings and the incense. ## Leviticus

Thirteen transformations of the Great Army. The weakening of the Judgments <note>Hebrew: *Dinim*</note> is stirred within it, and a soft voice becomes powerful. He strikes with the hand of the whole in the perfection of Faith <note>Aramaic: *Meheimanuta*, referring to the unified system of the Sefirot</note>, and this is the Mercy <note>Hebrew: *Rachamim*</note> of them all. We call this the "Hiddenness of the Thickening of Moisture." The perfection of the living whole is like a golden plate over the forehead of the Lord <note>original: *Y-H-V-H*</note>, a seal upon the grave of our life. And this gazes out, for all life emerges from there, and they investigate the Foundation <note>Hebrew: *Yesod*</note> of all, "The Lord is Righteous" <note>Psalm 11:7</note>. This is the small letter *Yod* of the Holy Name. Because of this, the letter *Vav* and the *Vav-Yod-Nun* are two perfections, and this is the Holy Kingdom <note>Hebrew: *Malchut*</note> from which Judgments go out into the world; this is the gateway to all the Names. It is the joy of the whole and the hiddenness of the first, and this is the Supernal Solution, the goodness of all movements. His Name is hidden and not revealed, yet it is sealed. In the Book of Aggadah <note>Legendary/Homiletic traditions</note>, the crowns of the Names are written in another way, but we have not learned it so.

**Rabbi Abba** opened his discourse: **"Awake, O north wind, and come, O south; blow upon my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden and eat his choicest fruits."** <note>Song of Songs 4:16</note>
"Awake, O north wind"—these are the Burnt Offerings <note>Hebrew: *Olot*</note> which are slaughtered in the north of the Altar, because they come to atone for the thoughts of the heart that stray. Since thought is found included in the time of Judgment, it is found in the North. The North Wind awakens at midnight when the pious ones <note>Hebrew: *Chasidim*</note> arise and the harp of David plays of its own accord, and all the pure ones are awakened. "And come, O south"—these are the Peace Offerings <note>Hebrew: *Shelamim*</note> which are slaughtered in the South, because they are the "perfection" <note>a wordplay on *Shelamim* and *Shleimut* (perfection/wholeness)</note> of all. They are the peace of the upper world and the lower world, and these are the peace of the sides of the world. They are the peace of all from the side of Faith. Peace offerings are so called because they bring wholeness to all in the world; they mend and prepare the flaws, for there is peace for Him and for the whole world in a single degree.

The Sin Offerings <note>Hebrew: *Chataot*</note> and Guilt Offerings <note>Hebrew: *Ashamot*</note> belong entirely to the Priests <note>Hebrew: *Kohanim*</note>, because they are prepared to atone for the people and to remove their sins. But of all sacrifices, none are as beloved before the Holy One, Blessed be He, as the Peace Offerings, because peace is found through them above and below. And the Incense <note>Hebrew: *Ketoret*</note> rises above them, for it binds peace together. It does not come for sin, nor for guilt, nor for iniquity, but only for joy, as it is written: "Oil and incense rejoice the heart" <note>Proverbs 27:9</note>, and this is Wisdom <note>Hebrew: *Chokhmah*</note>. Therefore, the incense is only offered at the time when the oil is offered, as it says: **"Every morning when he dresses the lamps, he shall burn it."** <note>Exodus 30:7</note> And it is written: **"And when Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight, he shall burn it,"** <note>Exodus 30:8</note> so that oil and incense are found as one. Come and see: the Peace Offerings are the peace of all, but the Incense is not stirred in the world except as a "binding" <note>Aramaic: *Katura*, a pun on *Ketoret*</note>, the binding of Faith.

**Rabbi Eleazar said:**
All the crowns of the Names are written, and we have learned the first one, which is the Supernal Hiddenness. It is like one who says "Wait" <note>Aramaic: *Chaka*</note>—one who waits and it is not known who he is. And the Crown <note>Keter</note>, Kindness <note>Chesed</note>, and Splendor <note>Hadar</note>—this is what is destined to be revealed through the wisdom of other crowns. For at first it is hidden, and later it begins to be revealed until it reaches the revelation of the Holy Name in its perfection. Thus it is written: "Like a rod of iron." At first, the hiddenness of all is a "waiting"—who is it that waits? The Crown, Kindness, and Splendor are waiting to be revealed. The Crown and Kindness are at the gateway, and this is when the action is seen but still remains hidden, yet destined for revelation, as it is written: **"Go and gather the elders of Israel and say to them: The Lord, the God of your fathers..."** <note>Exodus 3:16</note> This is the perfection of all. Here is the revelation and the binding of the Holy Name. Therefore, the first of all is sharp.

The "Perfected Yah" <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton</note> is because Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note> brings forth the letter *He* and is hidden within it, never separating from it. This is the Wisdom of which it is written: **"A river goes out from Eden"** <note>Genesis 2:10</note>. In this manner, the letter *Yod* is the exchange. As it was said regarding the Crown of *Yah*, they never separate; the *Yod* brings forth the *He*. In this way, the *He* is called *Yod*, and that river goes out from it, and your seal is from it. Below there are two, because they emerge from them from the side of the "waiting." A "Son" <note>Hebrew: *Ben*</note> emerges, for he is joined to the *He*, and he is as desirable as that river. And from the side below, a "Daughter" <note>Hebrew: *Bat*</note> emerges from the strength of the lower river. And so is your seal for the Crown, and he bows from his place and the tip...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), specifically focusing on the Divine Name and the Sefirotic emanations. It follows the previous discussion on the nature of sacrifice and the elevation of the soul.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->And He Called<-
<note>original: "Vayikra" - the opening word of Leviticus</note>

And at this time, when it is found that the **Faith** <note>Aramaic: *Meheimanuta*; refers here to the unified structure of the Divine Sefirot</note> of all is bound together and covered below as is fitting, it is the source and the foundation, which is the **Hand of the Lord** <note>original: *Yad-YHVH*</note>. And regarding this, one who wishes to write the **Holy Name** <note>The Tetragrammaton, Y-H-V-H</note> must first write the letter *Yod* (י) with one point above, one point in the middle, and one point below, as has been stated. Afterward, the letters *Yod* and *Heh* (יה) are written, which are never separated from one another, in this manner, so that both are found as one; for this is all one and is written in this way: **YH**. Behold, you have the entire **Image of Faith**.

Afterward, the Faith spreads out and two "children" emerge, included together as one; these are the "Son" and the "Daughter" from both of them. This is the letter *Vav* (ו) of the Holy Name. The "Daughter" emerges from the "Mother" <note>The Sefirah of Binah/Understanding</note>, and she is the final *Heh* (ה) of the Holy Name. She is not completed except with the *Vav*, because she is nourished by it. Therefore, one must write the *Vav* and then the *Heh* in this manner: **VH**. Behold, the *Vav* represents the expansion that emerges from the hidden place, like a **river that flows** out from the *Yod*, because the *Heh* is nourished by it.

And these matters are laws for the wise, as has been stated. When one reaches these words, one should say them, for such is the command of wisdom. A person must be careful with the Holy Name, to write the Holy Name in this manner, for this is what is fitting; it is the **Mystery of Faith** and is called the **Holy Name** and the **Divine Countenance**. One who blemishes the Holy Name, it would have been better for him had he not been created.

The third aspect is the **Hand of the Lord** <note>Yad-YHVH</note> which is called "the worlds," as it is said, it is **Mercy** <note>Aramaic: *Rachamei*</note>, yet from it emerges **Judgment** <note>Aramaic: *Dina*</note>. This is that **flowing river** that flows out from Eden. The fourth is **God the Great** <note>El Gedolah</note>, which has been discussed; this "Greatness" <note>Chesed/Lovingkindness</note> is divided into the worlds, and in every place it is **Might** <note>Gevurah</note>. The fifth is the **Hand of the Lord**, the Mercy that is the **Image of All**, the root of all, the bond of Faith, the male aspect of all sides; this is the **Beauty of Israel** <note>Tiferet Yisrael</note>. The seventh and eighth are **Victory** <note>Netzach</note> and **Splendor** <note>Hod</note>. Therefore, the "Hand of the Lord" is near to everything and holds all sides. Sometimes the *Yod* is for the worlds, for the "Beauty" is near to "Victory" and "Might." Sometimes the Name is for the powers, for "Beauty" is near to the prophets, and "Splendor" is the companion of "Victory."

And it has been stated that they are recognized from the hidden place before their locations. All the prophets said, "Thus says the Lord" <note>Koh Amar YHVH</note> for the worlds, and when they said "Thus says the Lord," it referred to Victory and Splendor, and they knew from which place these words came. The ninth is **Shaddai** <note>Almighty</note>, who said to the world "Enough!" <note>Dai</note>, for he is the end, and the end of the lower world comes from the **Righteous One** <note>Tzadik</note>, who is the **Foundation of the World** <note>Yesod Olam</note>, who said to the world "Enough!" The tenth is the **Kingdom** <note>Malchut</note>, for it is the head of the Kingdom, which is certainly Judgment. This is to set the battles of the King in the world, and this is the **Lower Might**, which is **Justice** <note>Tzedek</note>.

And these are the **Ten Names** by which the "Ends" are called; they are tied to one another in a perfect unity. These are the **Holy Crowns** of the King by which He is known. They are the Heavens, and they are meritorious, and all are tied together as one through the scent of the **Incense** <note>Ketoret</note>. Then it is called "Incense" because of the "Binding" <note>Katura</note>, for they are bound together as one. Happy is the portion of the righteous who know the path of the Torah and know how to recognize the glory of their Master. Concerning them it is written: *“And they shall see and declare My glory”* (Isaiah 66).

**And if** his offering is a **sacrifice of peace offerings** <note>Zevach Shelamim</note> (Leviticus 3). It is written: *“Ten, ten is the weight of the spoon, by the shekel of the sanctuary”* (Numbers 7). Why "ten, ten"? This corresponds to the **Ten Utterances of Creation** <note>Ma'aseh Bereshit</note> and the **Ten Commandments of the Torah** <note>Matan Torah</note>. There were ten utterances in the Work of Creation and ten utterances in the Giving of the Torah. All of them are connected because the world was only created for the sake of the Torah. As long as the righteous of Israel occupy themselves with the Torah, the world is sustained. But if the righteous of Israel cease from the Torah, what is written? *“If My covenant be not with day and night, I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth”* (Jeremiah 33). Come and see: Ten utterances for the Work of Creation, as we have learned: "By ten utterances the world was created." Ten utterances for the Giving of the Torah, as it is written... and it is written regarding the Work of Creation, "Let there be light." This is the **Faith of the Holy One, Blessed be He**.

It concludes by linking the Ten Utterances of Creation to the Ten Commandments, emphasizing that the world's existence depends on Torah study.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the book of Leviticus (Vayikra), specifically focusing on the structural and spiritual correspondence between the Ten Utterances of Creation in Genesis and the Ten Commandments in Exodus. The text uses Aramaic and Hebrew interchangeably.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The scripture says, as it is written: *Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven* etc. <note>Genesis 1:14</note> and it is written: *You shall have no other gods before Me* <note>Exodus 20:3</note>. And it is written regarding the Work of Creation: *Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters* etc. <note>Genesis 1:6</note>. *Let there be a firmament*—and Israel are not able to [be harmed by] the scourge <note>Aramaic: mulka</note> because they cling to that place called "Heaven." And this is the spirit that the Holy One, blessed be He, prepared. Joseph looked at Rabbi Eleazar and said: "These things are beautiful." The Holy One, blessed be He, set them for their blessings, appointing them as rulers over Israel in the place He gave them. Regarding this it is said: *And God set them in the firmament of the heaven* <note>Genesis 1:17</note> and He forgave and pardoned him. It is written: *The water between the dwellings of His Torah.* *And let it divide between the waters and the waters* <note>Genesis 1:6</note>—between the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called "Living Waters," and between Idolatry <term>Avodah Zarah: literally "foreign service"</term> which is called "broken cisterns" etc. <note>Jeremiah 2:13</note> for they are foul waters, murky waters, and because of this, the holy Israel separate between water and water. It is written: *You shall not bow down to them nor serve them* <note>Exodus 20:5</note> at the end, and it is written regarding the Work of Creation: *Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place* <note>Genesis 1:9</note>. Come and see: all those who are in this holy seal are called "separated" from the place above. And through two holy ones, these are established in their places; but a whisperer separates a close friend <note>Proverbs 16:28</note>. And this "Friend" <note>Hebrew: Aluf, also meaning Chief or Master</note> is the Holy One, blessed be He. And it is written: *Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place*—do not cause a separation, because this gathering is called "unto one place" as is fitting, in the place of Truth, and not in another place that is [so] called. And what is it called? It is that they go from the water to another place that is not its living source.

It is written: *Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy* <note>Exodus 20:8</note> and it is written regarding the Work of Creation: *Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree* <note>Genesis 1:11</note>—this is the holiness of the Land, to be crowned with the crown of beauty on the Sabbath day, for then the Bride is united with the King to bring forth sustenance and blessings to the world.

It is written: *Honor your father and your mother* <note>Exodus 20:12</note>. And it is written regarding the Work of Creation: *Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven* <note>Genesis 1:14</note>. What is this speaking of? Rather, these "lights" are your Father and your Mother. Your Father is the Sun. Your Mother is the Moon. And they are the Sun of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written: *For the Lord God is a sun and shield* <note>Psalms 84:12</note>, and the Moon is none other than the Assembly of Israel <term>Knesset Yisrael: the mystical personification of the Jewish people</term> as it is written... this is all one.

It is written: *You shall not murder* <note>Exodus 20:13</note> and it is written regarding the Work of Creation: *Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures* <note>Aramaic/Hebrew: Nefesh Chaya; Genesis 1:20</note>. This means you shall not kill a human being who is called by this name, as it is written: *And man became a living soul* <note>Genesis 2:7</note>. And do not be like those fish where the big ones swallow the small ones.

It is written: *You shall not commit adultery* <note>Exodus 20:14</note> and it is written regarding the Work of Creation: *Let the earth bring forth the living creature after its kind* <note>Genesis 1:24</note>. There should be no exchange [of partners] and a man should not be false to his fellow's [wife] who is not his own "living creature" and mate. And regarding this it is written: *Let the earth bring forth the living creature*—that a woman should not give birth except from her own kind, and the mating of the "living creature" should be with its own kind; this is the [proper] union.

It is written: *You shall not steal* <note>Exodus 20:15</note> and it is written regarding the Work of Creation: *And God said: Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed* <note>Genesis 1:29</note>. That which I have commanded for you and designated for you shall be yours, and you shall not steal that which belongs to another.

It is written: *You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor* <note>Exodus 20:16</note> and it is written regarding the Work of Creation: *And God said: Let us make man in our image* <note>Genesis 1:26</note>. One who is in the image of the King—do not testify falsely against him. For one who testifies falsely is as if he declares that all is void above.

It is written: *You shall not covet your neighbor's wife* <note>Exodus 20:17</note> and it is written regarding the Work of Creation: *It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a helper fit for him* <note>Genesis 2:18</note>. And because of this, "You shall not covet your neighbor's wife." And this is the [parallel of] the ten [utterances] of the end of the Work of Creation and the Ten Utterances of the giving of the Torah. And these are "ten, ten"—the "ten of the spoon" <note>referring to the offerings in Numbers 7</note> by the shekel of the sanctuary, established as a single attachment. And because of this, the world stands and peace is found within it. And regarding this: *And if his sacrifice be a peace offering* <note>Leviticus 3:1</note>—to establish the world in peace. And not only that, but it atones for the sin of the [scape]goat and for that "negative commandment" in order to cast peace over all. It is written: *Dominion and fear are with Him; He makes peace in His high places* <note>Job 25:2</note>. Thus the colleagues have established it.

## Leviticus (Vayikra)

Abraham is the one of whom it is written that he was "trusting" <note>original: *batuach*</note> to knead the dough below according to its proper measure. And it is written, "And Abraham shall surely become..." <note>Genesis 18:18; the text links Abraham to the attribute of Lovingkindness/Chesed</note>. And "Fear" <note>original: *Pachad*</note> refers to Isaac, as it is written: -> "The Fear of Isaac was with me" <- <note>Genesis 31:42</note>. Alternatively: -> "Dominion and Fear are His" <- <note>Job 25:2</note>, and this atonement is the attribute of Might <note>term: *Gevurah* - the left-hand attribute of judgment and strength</note>. This one has its foundation in life, and that one has its foundation from above, and Solomon <note>referring here to the King of Peace/The Holy One</note> made a connection between them, as it is written: -> "He makes peace in His heights" <- <note>Job 25:2</note>.

This "He who makes peace in His heights" refers to Jacob, as it is written: -> "You give Truth to Jacob" <- <note>Micah 7:20</note>. It is also written: -> "Love Truth and Peace" <- <note>Zechariah 8:19</note>, for Truth and Peace are bound one to the other. Because of this, he represents the perfection of all, and Peace is the perfection and the wholeness of everything. Whoever brings "Peace Offerings" <note>term: *Shelamim* - from the root *Shalom* (Peace) or *Shalem* (Whole)</note> brings peace into the world. Jacob is the one who makes peace, as we have said, because he takes hold of this side <note>Chesed/Abraham</note> and that side <note>Gevurah/Isaac</note>. The Peace Offerings are like the branches of the attributes, and in the strikes <note>judgments</note> you shall not engage, neither on this side nor on that side; therefore they are called Peace Offerings. He is the "Spirit of the King," as it is written: -> "And Jacob was a simple man" <- <note>Genesis 25:27; the word *Tam* (simple/innocent) also means "complete" or "perfect"</note>. A complete man: complete above and complete below.

Rabbi Hezekiah said: It is written, "If he offers it for a thanksgiving, then he shall offer with the thanksgiving sacrifice..." <note>Leviticus 7:12</note>. What is the meaning of "upon the thanksgiving" <note>original: *al todah*</note>? It specifically means "above it," and because of this, "unleavened cakes..." <note>Leviticus 7:12</note>. The "unleavened cakes" <note>term: *Matzot*</note> stand to establish that which is to come. The word for "cakes of matzot" is written deficiently <note>note: missing a letter in the Hebrew spelling, often interpreted mystically as a lack or a need for filling</note> because it reached "above it."

Come and see, Rabbi Hiyya said: It is written, "with the sacrifice of his thanksgiving peace offerings" <note>Leviticus 7:13</note>. This "peace offerings" <note>plural</note> implies two: Thanksgiving and Peace Offerings. You should know that this is what Rabbi Judah meant: "Thanksgiving" is known, but what is "his peace offerings" in the plural? He said to him: They are two, which is the meaning of "his peace offerings"—the peace of all. One is Isaac; the "thanksgiving of his peace offerings" goes toward the peace of all and awakens mercy upon all worlds.

Rabbi Yose said: That which Rabbi Hiyya said is good, for the Assembly of Israel <note>term: *Knesset Yisrael* - the mystical personification of the nation, associated with the Sefirah of *Malkhut*</note> is blessed from those two places, the peace of all. Rabbi Yose said: It is known to us, and it has been stated, that just as the Tabernacle was set up, so was the offering brought—in that exact manner. "Cakes of matzot" is written deficiently as we said. The cakes correspond to the number, and "unleavened wafers anointed with oil." To what do the "unleavened wafers" <note>original: *rekikei matzot*</note> hint? He said to him: These refer to "the flaming sword which turned every way" <note>Genesis 3:24</note>, because they all lean upon the mercies of human beings—upon those who transgress the commandments of the Torah. Therefore, the cakes are all of a kind to be found as a vessel of greatness <note>or "anointing"</note> that ascended below, so that all should be blessed as one from that holy oil of greatness.

And this is the "wine for the libation," and we have established it as a "fourth of a hin." Afterward, wine and oil are hung together for the libation. We have established that water <unclear>...</unclear> they were crowned, and all those are laden. Therefore there is "water and there is water." There is wine from a place that is good, and there is wine from a place of punishment <note>original: *ducha*</note>. Regarding this, the cakes are like wine. Wine in dreams: for some it is good, and for some it is a trial. If he is a Torah scholar, it is written: -> "And wine gladdens the heart of man" <- <note>Psalms 104:15</note>. And it is written: -> "For your love is better than wine" <- <note>Song of Songs 1:2</note>. This is the "preserved wine" that is a joy to all. But if not: "Give strong drink to him who is perishing, and wine to the bitter in soul" <note>Proverbs 31:6</note>. There is another wine which is a trial/punishment. Therefore it is proper to bring these things in the sacrifice so that the punishment may be removed and mercy awakened. I have passed over the wine and seen the wine, and so it is with everything.

The oil shall never be removed from the sacrifice, except for the "Meal Offering of Jealousies" <note>the offering of the *Sotah*, the woman suspected of adultery</note>, of which it is written: "He shall pour no oil upon it" <note>Numbers 5:15</note>. For here, mercy is not desired, as the whole matter is a trial/punishment, as it is written: "It is a meal offering of memorial, bringing iniquity to remembrance" <note>Numbers 5:15</note>. And it is written <unclear>...</unclear>. And regarding this: "And the cake of the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings. If he offers it for a thanksgiving."

Rabbi Hezekiah was sitting before Rabbi Isaac. They rose at midnight to labor in the Torah. Rabbi Isaac opened and said: -> "Behold, bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord, who stand in the house of the Lord by night" <- <note>Psalms 134:1</note>. The companions have already established this verse, and it has been said regarding all those who rise in this night. For what is faith <note>original: *meimanuta*</note>? And who are the "children of faith"? They are those who exert themselves in the Torah and know how to unify the Holy Name <note>term: *Shema Kadisha*</note> as is fitting. We have found that the "children of faith" are those who rise at midnight to labor in the Torah.

<meta>This page continues the discussion from the end of the previous section regarding the mystical rewards for those who rise at midnight to study Torah, specifically focusing on the flow of blessings from the celestial realms of 'Holiness' and 'Zion'.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

In the Torah, and they cleave to it like the soul of Israel, so that the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note>, may be found through the words of the Torah. **Come and see:** at the hour when a person rises at midnight to labor in the Torah, and the North Wind awakens at midnight, that "Doe" <note>The *Shekhinah*, the Divine Presence, often symbolized as a doe in the Zohar</note> stands and is found by the Holy One, Blessed be He. And at the hour she stands, many hosts and many chariots stand with her, her holy ones, and they all go to be found by the Holy King. Happy is the portion of one who merits and rises at midnight to labor in the Torah; the Holy One, Blessed be He, weaves for him [a thread of grace], as we have established, for it is written:

> "You who dwell in the gardens, the companions listen for your voice; let me hear it." (Song of Songs 8:13)

And all those celestial hosts and all the "sons of praise" who sing to their Master, they all fall silent for the sake of the praise of those who labor in the Torah, and they proclaim and say:

> "Behold, bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord, who stand in the house of the Lord by night." (Psalms 134:1)

You are the ones worthy of the Holy King; you crown Him. And that Doe is crowned by him when that person stands before the King and says: "See with what a son I have come before You, with what a son I have appeared before You," and He sees those who are all hers <note>The students of Torah who support the Shekhinah</note> before the King. He returns and says: "Who stand in the house of the Lord by night." These are called "servants of the Lord"; these are fit to bless the King, and their blessing is a true blessing:

> "Lift up your hands in holiness <note>original: *Kodesh*</note> and bless the Lord..." (Psalms 134:2)

You are fit for the Holy King to be blessed by your hands, and the blessing by your hands is a true blessing. **Lift up your hands in holiness.** What is "holiness"? It is the supernal place from which the spring of the deep river emerges, as it is written:

> "And a river went out of Eden to water [the garden]" (Genesis 2:10)

And Eden is what is called "Supernal Holiness" <note>Refers to the Sephirah of *Chokhmah* (Wisdom), the source of divine flow</note>; because of this, "lift up your hands in holiness." And when a person does this and merits this, they engrave and proclaim over him and bless him: **"The Lord bless you from Zion."** You shall bless the Holy One, Blessed be He, from the place called Supernal Holiness, and He will bless you from the place called Zion <note>Refers to the Sephirah of *Yesod*, the channel of procreation and blessing</note>, for from there the King and the Matron <note>The *Shekhinah*</note> are blessed together, just as their union was as one to be found by the King. So from that place that is blessed, from that very place, blessings are given to you. **This is what is written:**

> "The Lord bless you from Zion; and may you see the good of Jerusalem." (Psalms 128:5)

See what is the "good of Jerusalem"? These are the blessings that go out to her from the King by way of that holy grade of the "Righteous One" <note>The *Tzadik*, another name for the Sephirah *Yesod*</note>, and regarding this, "The Lord bless you from Zion," and it is all one fullness. And not only that, but:

> "And see children to your children... and see children to your children is good." (Psalms 128:6)

What is "Peace upon Israel"? One might ask why "upon Israel" is needed here. Rather, it is because he increases peace above, for when he [studies], he establishes peace for all, above and below. "Peace upon Israel" is stated generally, and peace is found, for the upper and lower worlds find the secret of all worlds. And the words of Torah oversee peace in the world, as it is written:

> "The Lord will give strength to His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace." (Psalms 29:11)

---
-> **SOUL** <-

"If a soul shall sin..." Rabbi Yose opened:

> "Until the day breathes and the shadows flee..." (Song of Songs 2:17)

How much must human beings be careful of their sins, so they do not sin before their Master! For every single day a herald goes out and calls: "Awaken, children of the world! Purify yourselves before the Holy King! Awaken to be careful of your sins! Awaken for the holy soul <note>original: *Nishmata*</note> that He placed within you from a supernal holy place!" For at the hour when the Holy One, Blessed be He, sends out a soul to enter into human beings, He adjures her with many warnings and many commands to keep His commandments. And not only that, but He passes her through the power and wonders of all the worlds to delight in them and to see the glory of those who strive in the Torah. She goes out and stands before the King in a garment of glory, crowned in the very image of this world. In that supernal form, she gazes at the glory of the King every day and tastes of many crowns. At the hour when the time arrives to descend to the world, she makes her dwelling in the Garden of Eden for thirty days to see the glory of the Matron, ascending to this place and crowning...

It then transitions into a discourse on the soul's purity and its celestial journey before descending into the physical body.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Zohar's mystical commentary on the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), specifically addressing the soul's journey and the consequences of sin. It connects the observance of the Covenant (Circumcision) with the study of the Torah.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The <term>Holy King</term> <note>original: "Malka Kadisha," referring to God</note> said to her [the soul]: "Pass through seven crowns until the lower world." And she enters into the body of a human being to be in this world and to labor in the service of the <term>Torah</term> <note>original: "Oraita"</note>. There shall be a protection over her. And what is all this honor and all this perfection that shall be for the assembly of the King? It is so that she may have a portion before Him. **"When a soul sins"** (Leviticus 4:2)—what is the nature of this sin? Rabbi Yose said: "Now, 'when she sins,' it is to be purified before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> until the end of the day. What is the counsel for this soul to be purified? It is prepared and settled to be purified until the end of the day, until the shadows flee and the days of this world breathe their last, and the witnesses come and the Mighty One is ready to demand the soul when the King desires her to depart from this world." And "the kings came"—this is the secret of the creation of the Holy One, Blessed be He, at the time when a person's time arrives to depart from the world. All of a person's [limbs] are removed from him, everything until the end of the day, until the time is longed for to depart from this world. And "the kings came" so that all should be removed and return before their Master. Rabbi Eleazar said: "A person has two [spirits] all his life in his existence, one tender and one small. And they are found as one; then a person is in his existence. And regarding this, 'the kings came' is written. Then a person needs to labor in his deeds and to prepare them before his Master and to be careful of them, because the Holy One, Blessed be He, searches the heart and sees, and receives at times those who repent before Him. And this is 'until the end of the day' and 'the kings came,' for once they see that their [days] are passing from them, and one sees the fear of the Holy One, Blessed be He, everything helps this ascent... <note>The text here contains several difficult Aramaic contractions and archaic forms related to the soul's preparation for the afterlife.</note> ...Remember your Covenant as in the days of your youth, until the days of my affliction are finished. And regarding this, 'until the end of the day,' for now a person must prepare his deeds, so that when his days arrive to depart from the world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, shall have mercy upon him. **"When a soul sins"**—this is a great voice to her. And what is prepared for her in sin? For she did not look or arrange herself when she descended to the world... surely wisdom is prepared to be arranged in her after His commandments. Therefore, when he sits before the King... look and see, know clearly that one who transgresses the command of his Master, woe to him! How shall he rejoice? Woe to him! What is written when he departs from this world? 'And he shall bear his iniquity.' And when he bears his iniquity, how will they open the gate for him? And how shall he stand before his Master? And regarding this, it is written: **"When a soul sins."**

---

->**"When a soul sins"** (Leviticus 4:2)<-

Rabbi Isaac opened:
->**"All this has come upon us, yet we have not forgotten You, nor have we been false to Your covenant."** (Psalms 44:18)<-

"All this has come upon us"—all these [suffering] have been exhausted upon us, from pains and illnesses; all the judgments from above came upon us, "yet we have not forgotten You." We did not neglect our study. From here we learn: anyone who turns away from the sages who labor in the <term>Torah</term> and does not wish to know it, it is as if he forgets the Holy One, Blessed be He, for the Torah is entirely the <term>Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Shema de-Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>. "Nor have we been false to Your covenant"—that one should not be false to this <term>sign of the Holy Covenant</term> <note>original: "Ot Brit Kadisha," referring to circumcision</note> which is sealed in him. For anyone who is false to it, it is as if he is false to the Name of the King, because the Name of the King is sealed in him... and the verse calls out further regarding this, as it is written: "If we have forgotten the name of our God, or spread forth our hands to a strange god" (Psalms 44:21). "If we have forgotten the name of our God"—this refers to the Torah, which is the Name of our God. "Or spread forth our hands to a strange god"—this is when we are false to the Covenant. And it is all one matter. What does "false" mean here? It is one who spreads his hands to another authority and is false to this Covenant. And regarding this, the Torah is tied to this: for anyone who guards this Covenant, it is as if he guards the entire Torah. And one who is false to this, it is as if he is false to the entire Torah. Come and see: before Abraham was circumcised, he was not considered to have guarded the Torah. Once he was circumcised, what is written? "Because that Abraham obeyed My voice, and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws" (Genesis 26:5). And all this because he was circumcised and the holy mark was recorded in him, and he guarded it as is fitting; it was accounted to him as if he guarded the entire Torah. Isaac...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the mystical significance of the Covenant (Brit) and the sacrificial offerings. It transitions from the general laws of Leviticus (Vayikra) into a deep kabbalistic exploration of how the Covenant links the earthly realm to the Divine Sefirot (attributes), specifically focusing on the figures of Joseph, Abraham, and the concept of "Day and Night."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

So too it is written: *And my covenant I will establish with Isaac* <note>Genesis 17:21</note>, and because of this the Torah is called "Covenant." And Joseph also [is associated with it] because he guarded this covenant <note>referring to his resistance of Potiphar's wife</note> and did not wish to draw near to [sin]. Thus, he merited the glory of this world and the glory of the world to come. Not only that, but he acquired the side of beauty, as it is written: *He ordained it in Joseph for a testimony* <note>Psalms 81:6; original: "Edut bi-Yehosef shemo"</note>, and through this, he was found in this world and for the inheritance of the world to come. Rabbi Isaac said: It is written, *His firstling bullock, majesty is his...* <note>Deuteronomy 33:17</note>. Joseph merited the "bull," for they are the first of the sacrifices. Rabbi Judah said: If so, why is he found associated with the word of the impure serpent on the right <unclear>side</unclear>? For behold, it is written: *and the face of a bull on the left side* <note>Ezekiel 1:10</note>, because judgments rest upon the thighs of Jeroboam <note>a descendant of Joseph who led Israel into idolatry</note>.

Rabbi Yose said: There is a reversal in this verse, for since Joseph guarded this covenant, this covenant takes hold of two levels, and those two levels above are called "the gatherers." And there is a reversal regarding the Red Heifer, for this heifer is of a certain level, and the radiance of the heifer is called "bull." And this is [the meaning of]: *His firstling bullock, majesty is his, and his horns are like the horns of a wild ox* <note>Deuteronomy 33:17</note>. The secret of this verse is in the "Bull of the World," but the companions have established that the "horn" rose above all others, and because of this, "He shall conquer my angry people" <note>interpretive reading of the power of the tribe of Joseph</note>.

Rabbi Abba said: This implies that anyone who guards this sign of the holy imprint <note>the Brit Milah/Circumcision</note>, those two supernal levels are bound to him to guard him in everything and to crown him with supernal glory. And because of this, [Joseph] merited two portions—one half here and one half there. And when King Solomon was found <unclear>in error</unclear>, Ahijah the Shilonite announced the kingdom to Jeroboam, and because of this, the "Covenant of Achziv" was cut off from everything.

Because of this, [Rabbi] Simeon said: This man who fathers a son is bound to the *Shekhinah* <note>the Divine Presence</note>, which is the "Opening of all Openings" above, the opening that is bound to the Holy Brain. For Simeon said: That fluid which comes from the brain is pure and guarded before the Holy One, blessed be He. And at the hour when judgments are awakened in the world, it protects like that blood and the radiance of the world. And because of this, it is written: *And so on the eighth day... and you shall circumcise every male...* <note>Genesis 17:12</note> and it is written: *And if by strength* <note>original: "be-gevurot"</note> *eighty years* <note>Psalms 90:10</note>, and all rises in one scale. We have learned: Like that blood, the world merits to be sweetened with *Chesed* <note>Loving-kindness</note> and the sustainers of all worlds, as it is written: *If not for My covenant day and night, I would not have appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth* <note>Jeremiah 33:25</note>.

"If not for My covenant" is understood, but why "day and night"? It means those two crowns are united as one, and they are the opening for all other crowns. One side is Judgment and one is Mercy, and they are sweetened one with the other as male and female. From the side of the male, he exerts effort before Him; from the side of the female, the place is prepared. And because of this, one is white and one is red, so they may be sweetened together; therefore they are bound as one. And this Covenant takes hold of them in "day and night," in Judgment and Loving-kindness. In the first likeness, he later exerts himself in Loving-kindness and is found in everything. And this is the Covenant called "Day and Night" which takes hold of both.

Because of this, Abraham was called "old," as it is written: *Walk before Me and be whole* <note>Genesis 17:1</note>, and she <note>the Shekhinah</note> is called "Elohim" when he merited both day and night, as it is written: *By day the Lord commands His loving-kindness, and in the night His song is with me* <note>Psalms 42:9</note>. Abraham inherited both of these, to establish in him Loving-kindness as a lasting peace until he was circumcised. Once he was circumcised, he was perfected and merited both, and they are called "Peace," as we have learned, for it is written: *And he sat at the door of the tent in the heat of the day* <note>Genesis 18:1</note>. "The door of the tent" is the supernal crown of the King, which is the opening to the entire Holy Tabernacle that surrounds the crowns. And King David called the "opening" as it is written: *Open for me the gates of righteousness* <note>Psalms 118:19</note>, and it is written: *This is the gate of the Lord* <note>Psalms 118:20</note>. "In the heat of the day" refers to when the light of *Chesed* (Loving-kindness) shines as his portion, like one who sits in that heat to be established in all those lights. Because of this, the Covenant is called "Day and Night."

We have learned: It is written and paused, *And He will pass over the door* <note>Exodus 12:23</note>. What is "And the Lord will pass over the door"? That Loving-kindness exerted itself over this opening to be sweetened, and because of this, *He will not allow the Destroyer [to enter]* etc. Rabbi Eleazar said: We have learned this—when a convert is circumcised and enters under the wings of the *Shekhinah*, he is called a "Righteous Convert" (*Ger Tzedek*), and certainly a "Righteous Convert" merits to see that crown...

It explains how figures like Joseph and Abraham achieved spiritual perfection by "guarding the covenant," thereby uniting the divine attributes of "Day and Night."</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), specifically focusing on the spiritual status of Israel and the role of the righteous leader in averting divine judgment.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->And He Called<-

Through righteousness to justice, and this is the desire that arose and flowed to merit them both. Come and see, Rabbi Elazar his son said: one who comes from the side of holiness and from the root of truth is not comparable to one who comes from an evil root and from the side of Esau <note>original: "Esau," often used here as a metonym for foreign nations</note>, powerful strangers. Regarding Israel, it is written of them:
> "Yet I had planted you a noble vine, wholly a seed of truth" (Jeremiah 2:21)
Regarding the idolatrous nations, it is written:
> "Whose flesh is as the flesh of donkeys, and whose issue is like the issue of horses" (Ezekiel 23:20)
And because of this, the holy Israel, the seed of truth, were made to be used in the seal of the Name <note>The Divine Name</note> and below it, and they are all sweetened and all enter into the holy existence of day and night to be complete as a whole. But among the idolatrous nations, that which is mixed in brings impurity and they pass away through the generations. And because of this, a "righteous convert" <term>Ger Tzedek: a sincere convert to Judaism who takes on all commandments</term> is certainly so. For Rav Hamnuna the Elder saw five heathens before they were circumcised; they resembled the lower crowns that are not holy, and a spirit of impurity rested upon them. Once they were circumcised, they resembled the holy crowns upon the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine immanence of God</term> which rests upon the other lower crowns, and a holy spirit rests upon them. But the holy Israel, children of holy ones from roots and foundations, are found in the faith of the Holy Mother <note>A reference to the Sephirah of Binah/Understanding</note> at the time she comes to dwell, all as one, as it is written: "And this is the blessing..." and for her, all life is the conclusion.

**And it shall be** when he sins and is guilty, that he shall restore that which he took violently... (Leviticus 5:23). Rabbi Yose opened:
> "For this is as the waters of Noah unto Me; for as I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth..." (Isaiah 54:9)
And it is written:
> "Neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the waters of a flood" (Genesis 9:11)
It is written "waters of a flood" and not "waters of Noah." But here it is written "For this is as the waters of Noah unto Me." He questioned: why is the fault hung upon him <insert>Noah</insert>? Come and see: when the righteous are numerous in the world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, rejoices and is found among them. For we have learned: when the righteous dwell in the world and are found in it, He, as it were, casts peace into the world, and the whole world is blessed because of him, and they are complete in the heavenly retinue. From where do we know this? As it is written:
> "Or let him take hold of My strength, that he may make peace with Me; and he shall make peace with Me" (Isaiah 27:5)
There are two "peaces" for one who takes hold of this. Rabbi Yose said: "He shall make peace with Me" refers to the arrangement of the male and female <note>The balancing of divine attributes</note>. "He shall make peace with Me" refers to the blessing of the lower worlds. What is the difference between them? Rabbi Yose said: when the lower worlds are blessed, "He shall make peace with Me" means the whole world is sustained, and because of this, peace is holy. "He shall make peace with Me"—why was "peace" not placed first here? Rather, because the spirit that labors in the female is found first, and then the male comes to dwell in his hole <note>his place/receptacle</note>, and because of this "He shall make" precedes "peace." Come and see: at a time when the righteous are lacking in the world, judgments are not awakened and do not rule in the world because that righteous man was in the world, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires his honor, and the world is sustained because of him. Rabbi Yose opened: at a time when the people of the world are found guilty before the Holy One, Blessed be He, that righteous one who is found in the world—the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to speak with him, like a shepherd who has mercy on the world and is appeased by his arrangements. What does the Holy One, Blessed be He, do? He speaks with him about the sins of the world. He says to him <insert>not</insert> to benefit him alone but to protect them. What did you say? That a man should be commanded and everything rises to his hand, and then the Holy One, Blessed be He, is appeased by his arrangements. From where do we know this? From Moses. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:
> "Let Me alone, that I may destroy them" (Deuteronomy 9:14)
> "They have turned aside quickly out of the way... they have made them a molten calf, and have worshipped it" (Exodus 32:8)
Moses said: If my precious children, Israel, are to be destroyed from the world, death is better for me, so they shall not say that I was meritorious before the Living One of the world while my precious children were destroyed. Immediately:
> "And Moses besought the Lord his God" (Exodus 32:11)
And he gave his soul over to death in several places for the sake of Israel, as it is written:
> "Yet now, if Thou wilt forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray Thee, out of Thy book" (Exodus 32:32)
And so on. And Moses did not move from there until the Holy One, Blessed be He, forgave Israel. This is what is written:
> "And the Lord repented of the evil which He thought to do unto His people" (Exodus 32:14)
And it is written:
> "And the Lord said, I have pardoned according to thy word" (Numbers 14:20)
But regarding Noah, He said "peace" to him <note>meaning, He spoke only of Noah's own safety</note>:
> "The end of all flesh is come before Me" (Genesis 6:13)

<summary>This text contrasts the spiritual lineage of Israel with other nations and explains how a convert's soul is transformed. It further critiques Noah for failing to intercede for his generation, contrasting him with Moses, who risked his own life and spiritual standing to save Israel from divine wrath.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the spiritual responsibilities of the righteous (Tzadikim) toward their generation. It specifically contrasts Noah, who failed to pray for his contemporaries, with Moses and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who actively intervened to nullify divine decrees.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Before etc. He said to him: "What are you doing?" <term>Heaven forbid</term> <note>original: ח"ל - chas lei</note>, for a covenant exists with you and so forth: "Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood" (Genesis 6:14). But Noah did not seek mercy for the world, and because he sought only rest and merit for his own household, the flood is called "the waters of Noah" (Isaiah 54:9) <note>The Zohar suggests the flood is named after Noah as a subtle rebuke for his silence.</note>. Furthermore, Noah certainly had merits to rely upon, yet he did not seek mercy for the world. From here, <term>Rabbi Yose</term> said: What is the meaning of that which is written, "And Noah, a man of the earth, began" (Genesis 9:20)? "He began" <note>Hebrew: Vayachel</note> is as the phrase "He shall not profane <note>Hebrew: yachel</note> his word" (Numbers 30:3); he made himself profane. He is called "man of the earth" because for his sake the inhabitants of the world were found <note>preserved</note>, yet he did not seek mercy for them. He is "man of the earth" because through him the earth was sustained after the first ones were destroyed, as it is written:
> I will never again curse the ground because of man... (Genesis 8:21).

Come and see: they call the waters of Noah a "flood" <note>original: גליס - likely a corruption of 'galis' or 'tophan'</note> because of his name. <term>Rabbi Yosa</term> said to him: "Does he not have a sin being discussed here?" Rather, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> said: "The waters of Noah caused them to fear, but not the world," as it is written:
> And it came to pass after seven days... (Genesis 7:10).

And come see the covenant etc. "I have set my bow in the cloud" (Genesis 9:13). That is to say, there are none among them who merit to be called by My Name, to be included in "This" <note>Zoharic term for the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note>, and some call this "the waters of Noah." From here we see a sign for the transmission of merit, that it should not be revealed, and the world should not need this "Sign" <note>the rainbow</note>. And who is he? He who seeks mercy for the world and is found to protect it, such as one in whose days the world does not need this sign of the covenant, for the sign is only a reminder that a decree should never again be enacted upon the world to destroy it. And this is what is written: "A ruler among men" (2 Samuel 23:3). Just as a ruler among men, so too—who rules over the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>? As it were, the **Righteous One** <note>Tzadik</note>; for the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> decrees, and the Righteous One nullifies it. Such a one was <term>Bar Yochai</term> <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note>.

One day he was sitting at the entrance of the gate of Lod. He lifted his eyes and saw the sun shining, then it became darkened three times. He remembered that such darkness [is a sign], and he focused his mind through the depth of wisdom and saw <note>a vision</note>. He said to <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> his son: "Follow me, my son, and let us see, for surely a decree has been enacted above, and the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> wants to inform me. For surely times are suspended, and a matter is about to be decreed upon the world, and the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> does nothing until He reveals it to the righteous," as it is written:
> For the Lord God does nothing without revealing His secret to His servants the prophets (Amos 3:7).

While they were walking, they hid in a certain field. They saw a serpent coming with its mouth open, flaming like a coal in the dust, seeking to satisfy itself with blood. [Rabbi Shimon] struck his hands together <note>a gesture of power or prayer</note> and the serpent's mouth was struck and its scales moved away. He said: "Serpent, serpent! Go and see that serpent <note>the spiritual force of judgment</note>, for the spirit of judgment is aroused in the world." He made it put its head into a hole in the dust. He said: "I decree that just as the lower one returns to the hole in the dust, so shall it be." It returned to the hole beneath it. <term>The Chariot</term> <note>original: רכ"ז - likely referring to the celestial arrangement</note> of the firmament revolved. While they were walking, they heard a voice: "Sentinels of the heights, enter your places! The accusers of your districts need not labor in the world, for <term>Rabbi Bar Yochai</term> has nullified them!" Worthy is the Rabbi who protects the foundation of the children of the world, as it is written:
> And Moses besought... (Exodus 32:11)

Which implies that he pulled back the curtain <note>the barrier of judgment</note> and did not let it descend. And the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> establishes [the decree], but the Righteous One nullifies it. He then saw the sun shining and that [dark] wisdom passed away. <term>Rabbi Shimon</term> said: "Surely the world is established upon its foundation," and he expounded:
> For the Lord is righteous, He loves righteous deeds; the upright shall behold His face (Psalms 11:7).

Why "For the Lord is righteous, He loves righteous deeds"? Because "the upright shall behold His face." What is "His face"? The faces of the children of the world, to seek mercy for them for all that they need. <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> said to him: "Blessed be the Living One!" Thus, "the upright shall behold His face" means they behold the light and the decree is seen [and averted]. He said to him: "The Supernal Spirit of your life, which precedes the <term>Ancient Holy One</term> <note>Atika Kadisha</note>, the Hidden of all Hidden, and the world of the <term>Small Face</term> <note>Zeir Anpin</note>, they are called 'His face' <note>original: פנימו - Panimo, literally 'His faces'</note>... they behold with joy more than what is needed to be seen."

Come and see: at the time when the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> is revealed in the world and sees that the deeds of mankind are proper, the gaze of the <term>Ancient Holy One</term> falls upon the <term>Small Face</term>, and all those faces look into the Hidden Faces, and they are all blessed. And they are blessed because they look at one another in joy... not turning to the right or the left... the upright...
