<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), focusing on the mechanics of the divine realms and the process of Repentance. It connects the imagery of Daniel’s vision to the internal workings of the Sephirot (divine emanations).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Leviticus<-

And the secret of His name is internal, and they are all blessed and gaze upon one another until all worlds are found as one; then He is called "The Lord is one and His name is one." When the joy and radiance of the world—the faces of the Hidden Holy Ancient One <note>Hebrew: *Atika Kadisha*, the highest, most hidden aspect of God</note> which are not revealed—are covered and concealed, then judgments are awakened in the world. And they were all "cast down" <note>referring to the thrones in Daniel 7:9</note> while the Ancient of Days <note>Hebrew: *Atik Yomin*</note>, who is hidden and unrevealed, was watching until "thrones were cast down and the Ancient of Days sat." <note>Daniel 7:9</note> Regarding the "thrones were cast down," these are the supreme crowns <note>The Sephirot</note> that raise all others to establish them in their existence. And who are they? For behold, the Ancient of Days sits and is not revealed. At that time, the wicked of the world turn Mercy into Judgment <note>Hebrew: *Rachamim* into *Din*</note>, coming from the side of those bent, suppressed, and engraved powers. They speak with the rods of Severity <note>Hebrew: *Gevurah*</note>, ruling over Mercy, as it is said: "Those who strive with the Lord shall be shattered." Then the worlds are found lacking and without connection, for they do not ascend, and strife is awakened among them all.

But when the inhabitants of the world improve their deeds below, the judgments are suppressed and pass away, and Mercy is awakened and rules over that "cup" <note>a metaphor for a vessel of divine influence</note> which was awakened from the initial judgment. When Mercy is awakened, joy and comforts are found from the cup that rules over that [other] cup, for "The Lord relented of the evil" <note>Exodus 32:14</note> and He comforted, because they ruled over the evil which was found to be a harsh judgment. Mercy then rules, just as when judgments are suppressed and Mercy governs, every single crown is established and they are all blessed as one.

When each one returns to its place and they are all blessed by the Master, the heat of the engraved "locks" is suppressed and they return to their side. Then it is called "Complete Repentance" <note>Hebrew: *Teshuvah Shelemah*</note>, and the world is transformed, for behold, it sits in perfect joy. As it is written: "He brought in joy," and then it is called the Day of Atonement <note>Hebrew: *Yom HaKippurim*</note>, of which it is written: "To cleanse you from all your sins." <note>Leviticus 16:30</note> And the twenty gates of the engraved sides are opened.

It is written: "If he shall sin..." What is "if he shall sin" and finally "and he sinned"? Rather, "if he shall sin" refers to the brain/mind that searches out sin, as it is written: "From all the sins of man." "And he sinned" is as one says, "He shall purify the altar for the Lord" <note>referring to the word *ve-chitte*, which can mean to sin or to de-sin/purify</note>; he shall purify and repair. That is to say, he shall repair his deeds and "restore the spark which he robbed." This implies the days of the year, as it is written: "And he shall restore," and it is not written "and he shall turn away," but specifically "he shall restore and improve."

We have learned: when the lower powers are strong, the Voice is cut off and judgments are awakened, and Repentance depends on whether things are repaired. When judgments are awakened, a voice goes out and the four corners of the world are smitten. A herald cries out, but there is no one to listen or awaken. At such times, if they would return, He would sit and live; but if the Voice is cut off, judgments are executed. Then it is called "and he passed over" <note>referring to the divine anger passing through</note>.

We have learned: from the day the Holy Temple was destroyed, there is no day in which "evil wrath" is not found. Why? Because Rabbi Yudai said in the name of Rabbi Isaac: The Holy One, blessed be He, swore that He would not enter the Upper Jerusalem until Israel enters the Lower Jerusalem. Because of this, wrath is found in the world.

Rabbi Yose said: It is written, "The nakedness of your father and the nakedness of your mother you shall not uncover." <note>Leviticus 18:7</note> And it is written, "She is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness." "She is your mother" certainly! Behold, if one uncovers her nakedness, to whom does he wish to reveal it? Certainly to the "Strong Heat" <note>a personification of harsh judgment</note> that reveals it, as it is written: "When evil increases, it has already covered her face." Rather, these are the "Nakednesses" <note>Hebrew: *Arayot*, forbidden unions</note>, and all the kindnesses are seized by that nakedness. It is written "you shall not uncover" so that the lower realm may be repaired to counter that which was revealed. This is called Repentance.

Rabbi Isaac said: All the hidden things of the world are linked to one another until the "Heat" is revealed because of them. When the "Breasts" are revealed, all those suppressed things are revealed. And it is written: "You shall not take the mother with the young." <note>Deuteronomy 22:6</note> When the world below is repaired, everything is repaired until the repair reaches the Holy One below, and they are repaired and the "Heat" is covered so that it is not revealed. Because of this, it is written: "Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered." <note>Psalms 32:1</note> Then it is certainly called Repentance, and then it is called the Day of Atonement, as it is written: "From all your sins before the Lord you shall be cleansed." Rabbi Judah said...

## Leviticus

Its glory and its desire are called **Repentance** <note>Hebrew: *Teshuvah*, literally meaning "Return"</note> when those below gather and stand in joy. For it is written: "He who gathers is spared." Joy, ornaments, and words—all that was closed off returns to its place. Each and every thing is repaired and each one is blessed. Then it is called *Teshuvah* after the name of the "Hidden Repentance" <note>A reference to the higher Sephirah of Binah (Understanding), the source of cosmic return</note> which provides life to everything. **Rabbi Isaac** said: When the whole world is bound together as one, it is written:
> For Your kindness is great above the heavens <note>Psalm 108:5</note>
"Above the heavens" specifically, for it rises higher than the place called "Heaven." **Rabbi Yehuda** said: It is written "Above the heavens" precisely. "Upon the heavens" would imply the place where it stands, but since it says "Above the heavens," it implies that place which stands higher and higher. And what is it? It is the life and support called *Teshuvah* which they grasped at that time when the deeds below are gathered in joy. Then **The Holy Ancient One** <term>Atika Kadisha: The highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</term> is revealed and gives light to **The Small Face** <term>Ze’ir Anpin: The emotive attributes of God, often associated with the Tetragrammaton</term>. Then everything is in joy, everything is in perfection, everything is found in blessings, mercy, and life, and all the worlds are in joy. This is what is written: "And the Merciful One will wash away our iniquities" <note>Micah 7:19</note>. Who is "The Good"? It is **The Holy Ancient One** becoming revealed within **The Small Face**. When He is revealed within him, it is written as it was at first, and the whole is called **Repentance**. **Rabbi Yehuda** said: Everything is included within the whole. And it is written:
> So that the Lord may turn from His fierce anger and grant you mercy <note>Deuteronomy 13:18</note>
**Rabbi Isaac** said: It is all one. <note>The text here transitions into a technical legal-mystical discussion regarding the soul and restitution</note>. We have established these words before **Rabbi Isaac**. Why is it written:
> He shall restore the stolen object <note>Leviticus 5:23</note>
And no more? Rather, we have established that this is because the upper values are like the lower values. And regarding that which is higher, what is written?
> If a soul shall sin <note>Leviticus 4:2</note>
As we have said elsewhere. They returned to the verse "If a soul shall sin..." and it is written:
> If a soul commits a trespass <note>Leviticus 5:15</note>
And so on. **Rabbi Isaac** said: "Soul" <term>Nefesh: The lowest level of the soul, associated with action</term> is written, and not **Spirit** <term>Ruach: The middle level of the soul, associated with emotions</term> or **Breath/Super-soul** <term>Neshamah: The highest level of the soul, associated with intellect</term>. <margin>Page 241</margin> And regarding the "Soul" it is written: "And it shall be when he sins and is guilty, he shall restore the stolen object." One who wishes to rectify his deeds, as we have said—what is the meaning of "and is guilty"? It is like one who repairs his deeds, as if he returns from his rest to his place to rise up from error. For he was previously occupied with his sins, which prevented him from that rest. Therefore, "he shall restore the stolen object" as has been stated. **Rabbi Abba** was sitting before Rabbi Elai. **Rabbi Eleazar**, his son, said: Rabbi, it is written:
> The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree <note>Psalm 108:5</note>
Why "like a palm tree"? For of all the trees in the world, none takes as long to blossom as the palm, which takes seventy years. <note>The Zohar links the 70 years of the palm's growth to the 70 years of the Babylonian Exile</note>. Just as the palm rises after seventy years, so too the **Divine Presence** <term>Shekhinah: The feminine immanence of God</term> did not return to her place until the end of seventy years. This is what is written regarding the exile to Babylon. This is "The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree," rising as male and female after seventy years. **The Righteous One** <term>Tzadik: A title for the Sephirah of Yesod, or God Himself</term> refers to **The Holy One, Blessed be He**, for "He loves righteousness," and it is written "The Lord is Righteous" and "Say of the Righteous One that He is good." He shall flourish like a cedar in Lebanon. What is this "Lebanon"? It is **The Holy One, Blessed be He** sitting on the Throne of Judgment. He shall flourish in Lebanon—this is **Eden** <term>Gan Eden: Paradise</term>, of which it is written:
> No eye has seen, O God, besides You <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>
And this "Lebanon" is the supernal height where He flourishes. This is even in the time of exile, for He does not delay in rising. And from there the spring goes forth, and the "Priest of the Waters" does not rest. This "Lebanon" is powerful, as it is written "Like a burning light rising in the House of the Lord" for the time of the **King Messiah** <term>Mashiacha: The promised redeemer</term>. Like divided rivers, its fruits are in perfection. At that time, the world will be found full and lush, and they shall be as a crown. So too the heavens are renewed and the earth is new, and then "The Lord shall rejoice in His works" is written. And why all this?

## Main Text (Zohar)

Why [does it say] "before her"? This means etc. and "behold His form," and no iniquity was found in Him. Furthermore, he opened [his discourse] and said:
> A perverse man sows strife, and a slanderer separates the Chief. (Proverbs 16:28)

"A perverse man sows strife," as we have said, they cause a **union** <note>original: *mizvaga*</note> to be made inwardly above; "and a slanderer separates the Chief," he separates the Chief of the world. And this is the Holy One, blessed be He. Another explanation: "A perverse man sows strife." What is "sows" <note>literally "sends"</note>? He sends forth those drops of strife that draw nourishment from the side of wrath. "And a slanderer separates the Chief," as we have said, they cause a **union** to be made inwardly above. He causes a separation so that the Holy One, blessed be He, withdraws Himself; he separates the Matron <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Feminine</note> from the King, and the King from the Matron. Because of this, He is not called "One," for "One" is only used when they are in a single union. Woe to those scoffers who cause a separation above! Happy are the righteous who maintain the supernal establishment, and happy are the Masters of Repentance <note>term: *Ba'alei Teshuva* — those who return to God after sinning</note> who return everything to its proper place. Regarding this we have learned: In the place where the Masters of Repentance stand, the perfectly righteous cannot stand. Why? Because they are established in a higher place, a power that establishes the Garden of Eden.

---

### [Right Column - Continuation of Main Text]

From there the spirit of the righteous goes forth; therefore they are called Masters of Repentance, and they are established in another place called **Righteous** <note>term: *Tzadik* — referring to the Sephirah of Yesod</note>. Therefore, these dwell in a higher place and those dwell in a lower place; for these return the strength to its place from the supernal abyss of the **Crown** <note>term: *Keter* — the highest Sephirah</note> deep unto the end, the place called **Righteous**. And the perfectly righteous are moved from the place where they dwell in this world, and therefore these are above and those are below. Happy is the portion of the Masters of Repentance, and happy is the portion of the righteous, for because of them the world is sustained. "If a soul sins and commits a trespass..." (Leviticus 5:21). What is written above? Grace is lacking, and it is written of her etc. who spoke, because of this the Holy One, blessed be He, withdrew from everything. As it were, the Holy One, blessed be He, is not found in His established state, for the **Assembly of Israel** <note>term: *Knesset Yisrael* — the spiritual personification of the Jewish people/Shekhinah</note> has been separated from her place. This is what is written: "Faith is lost" (Jeremiah 7:28). What is **Faith** <note>term: *Emunah*</note>? This is the Assembly of Israel, as it is said: "And Your faithfulness in the nights" (Psalms 92:3). The kindness of Faith is all upon which the land was destroyed, and all is one. And we have established "kindness" and not "as kindness" nor "Your kindness." In this manner the Prophet said: "Remember the grace," it is not written "as the kindness" but "kindness." Witness the kindness of Faith, because of this it is followed by "the exile of grace with the kindness" etc.

### [Left Column - Raya Mehemna]

## The Faithful Shepherd

The Faithful Shepherd said: It is written that there are those among them who whisper <note>or "murmur"</note> regarding the secrets of the Sabbaths in the chapters, and they were not in repentance regarding even one of them, such as Elul <note>The month of repentance</note>. And they are upon them... thus sometimes there is among them a summons for the calf, nakedness, and for those who fill the flaw after he forgives the folly, and for those who suffer... for the place, and for those who suffer with their belly... grace and merit, grace of the handmaid. And thus to pass over the book of "Thou shalt not do" for every debt, there are those among them who are meritorious and [the burden] rests upon him. And he requires an extra payment for himself along with all his sins and his place and his dwelling. And he who returns in repentance before Him, for your transgression you shall be comforted, their bandage to the place... who purifies and merits, and there are no sins whispered above nor below. And there are no whisperings below nor above. And there are those whispered below and above. They shall be comforted below, thus they are comforted above after he returns in repentance and he fears them from the worlds, they are comforted, and he bears his iniquities engraved upon his bones. The righteous man whose iniquities are engraved upon his bones <note>A warning that unrepented sins leave a physical/spiritual mark</note>... because he places bandages between the debtors to be recognized by them, and a voice goes out concerning him: "See the wicked man," and they shall seize his iniquities among them. And we have established: the transgressions of the wicked are the laws in the world, and their spirit was established over them by the Masters of the Mishnah...

## Commentary / Conclusion

The soles of the feet of the righteous and the masters of repentance are all toward the Throne that was carved therein, the **Throne of Understanding** <note>term: *Binah* — the Sephirah of Divine Intellect/Motherhood</note>, whose throne's wheels are a burning fire, and it scatters... from before Him at the time when the righteous eat and are purified... and to be built... silver... and they also consume... lacking her cutting, Lilith <note>A demonic figure representing the "Other Side"</note> of the sword, and I have stood.

And this is the secret of the arrangement. After they are all nourished, each according to its specific form, they are healed. If one committed one transgression, another penalty is assigned to him. Immediately, the Divine has compassion on the person and honors those who are elevated, the generous and the redeemed, the pious of the world who are destined and equal. For the sake of this purification, the secret is to strengthen them with the openings of the tongue. To be sanctified, the will gathers upon them, and the merits of Israel are nourished, which rise from the earth to the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine indwelling presence of God</term>. Just as the living creatures draw near, performing their service to cover the deceivers who hide in the depths of the sea, so too the foundation of the world draws near. Because of this, the offering is for the Unique One, for no one can bring the hosts and the high ones to wisdom unless they slaughter the wonder of the blood to bring it near; for if you have not done it for Me, do not bring the spirit to the dust. Just as these are for the waters and the foundations, they are called "holy things" because there are no destroyers among them.

Furthermore, this ascends to the two crowns that conclude the prayer for the affliction of the soul in all existences, which include all six sides of the body, the six <term>Sefirot: Divine emanations or attributes</term>. And the secret of the world is sealed above and below for the good of the priests who inherit and live in humility through their self-affliction. In the treasury and secret of the day, in the <term>Yesod: the Sefirah of Foundation</term>, the King is satisfied, including all in the "Beauty" <note>Tiferet</note>, the tree of luscious fruit. Because of this, the place of attachment is there, the Name <note>YHVH</note>, and thus the soul follows the Name in the completion of the peace-offerings for Him and for all the existences that are seen within it. There the Foundation <note>Yesod</note> exists with the Name of David, and the "Koph" with the Name of the Child. Thus, the living and warm breaths are for the preparation of the six sides included in the garments, living worlds. With the lower Name, the man and the spirit of the world are like a booth... for the sacrifice. Two by two for the moment, seven by seven for the firmament, ten is the Name to complete it, and the Righteous One <note>the Tzadik, associated with Yesod</note> is included in the ranks. Because of this, the world was established and mixed with three completions, like three redemptions that were strengthened. And he is the "Vav" <note>the letter representing the six Sefirot</note> of the rest of Jacob, including six anointed ones, a support for the head of the lower Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note>, which is the lower "He" <note>the final letter of the Tetragrammaton</note>. The Crown <note>Keter</note> is the tip of the "Yod" above the letters. Until here.

<meta>This page continues the Zoharic commentary on the spiritual dynamics of exile and the sacrificial laws in Leviticus. It focuses on the mystical interpretation of the "Anointed Priest" and the merit of children.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

When [the Community of Israel] went out into exile, she said before Him: *Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where do you feed your flock?* <note>Song of Songs 1:7</note> Where is that "feeding" <note>original: *re'ita*</note>, that "where" <note>original: *eichah*</note> toward which all the desire of my soul is directed? How will you lead them through the deep places <note>or "the silent places"</note> of darkness that never cease? How will you lead them from the brightness of Eden above? *Where do you make your flock rest at noon?* How will you provide for all those who are parched, to give them drink from your constant flow? For the sealed fountain rises from you every day, opening and giving drink to all those below. And the lily <note>a symbol for the Community of Israel</note> is closed, for the sun is harsh. *Why should I be like one who veils herself?* How shall I be wrapped in a cloak without blessings, when your children need blessings and they are not found in my hand? *Beside the flocks of your companions*—how shall I stand over them and not raise up favor for them, nor grant merit to them? The "flocks of your companions" are the people of Israel, who are the children of the Patriarchs, who are the Holy Chariot above.

The Holy One, blessed be He, returned to her the sum of that "where" <note>*eichah*</note>, for the Beloved's word is a hidden matter for the future: *If you do not know, O fairest among women* <note>Song of Songs 1:8</note>—if you do not know how to provide for yourself, here is the counsel for you, "fairest among women," as it is said: *Behold, you are fair, my love.* *Go your way by the footsteps of the flock*—these are the righteous who examine the "heels" <note>the end of days or the lowest levels</note> and their breaths. And it is good for you to sustain the world through all this. *And feed your kids beside the shepherds' tents*—these are the **school children** <term>school children: *tinokot shel beit raban*, literally "infants of the house of our teacher," whose pure study is said to sustain the universe</term>, for the world is sustained because of them, and they give strength to the Synagogue. *The shepherds' tents*—these are the schoolhouses and the place of the House of Study, where the Torah is found constantly.

*If you do not know, O fairest among women...* Come and see: when the righteous are found, and these school children are found and labor in the Torah, everything is established with them in the world. And the "face of the sun" <note>the Divine light</note> cannot, as it were, be withheld from them. If they are worthy, they are found in their original strength, and they are the pillars upon which the world is sustained. But if, Heaven forbid, they are removed from the world, it is so that no guilt shall be found in them. This is like a physician who keeps sickness far from his beloved. And they are drawn into exile...

# **IF**
**If the anointed priest shall sin, bringing guilt on the people** <note>Leviticus 4:3</note>. The sin of the people is because of the debt they owe. If the "Anointed Priest" sins, he diminishes the goodness and pushes away the bounty from everything. This is the secret that rises from the depths. "The Anointed Priest" refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, as we have established; if He "sins" <note>metaphorically: if the flow of grace is interrupted</note>, He withholds from above and does not grant the outpouring of blessings. And this "sin" is certainly because of the guilt of His people. *The Anointed Priest shall sin.*

Rabbi Isaac opened: *Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, Your servants* <note>Exodus 32:13</note>. This verse is difficult; it should have written "to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Israel" <note>repeating the preposition "to"</note>. Why is it omitted for Isaac? However, we have learned that in every place, the Left <note>Isaac/Severity</note> is included in the Right <note>Abraham/Mercy</note>. It is within the inclusion of the Right that it is written: *Your right hand, O Lord, is glorious in power* <note>Exodus 15:6</note>—to eternally include the Left within it. Therefore, he did not separate [Isaac], in order to include him. For this reason, "to Abraham" and "to Isaac" are specifically joined as a general principle of Mercy <note>*Chesed*</note> for all. And "to Israel" <note>Jacob</note> refers to both of them together, for he stands alone in his height <margin>(variant: on his shoulders)</margin> and he balances everything.

The Holy One, blessed be He, said to the Priest above <note>the Archangel Michael or the Divine attribute of Mercy</note>... as it is written: *I have said, "Mercy shall be built forever"*... The Holy One, blessed be He, said this to the Priest once and twice... for my soul said it was His will... and what will you say... for the world, the world above... and you are established above... it is for the sin of the people. Rabbi Isaac said: *If the anointed priest shall sin*—this refers to the priest below who is found in the Temple service. If sin is found in him, it brings guilt upon the people, and woe to those who rely upon him.

All open their mouths and bless, seeking to be blessed through his hands. For we have learned that at the hour the Priest spreads his hands, words and blessings and sacrifices are offered upon him; all are found in blessings and joy. The witnesses are stirred to awaken **Mercy** <note>original: *Rachamim*</note> so that it may be included in the "Right Side" <note>the mystical attribute of Lovingkindness or *Chesed*</note>, and all are unified and bound one to another, and all are blessed as one. Thus, it is found that through the hand of the Priest, the upper and lower realms are blessed. This has been established. For this reason, he must offer a sacrifice for himself, so that his own debt may be atoned.

Rabbi Yose said: We have learned that through the hand of the Priest, a person’s debt is atoned when he offers a sacrifice. But now that he himself has sinned, who shall offer for him, and who shall atone for him? If you say he offers for himself—behold, we see he is impaired, and he is not worthy for the upper and lower realms to be blessed through him, let alone for himself to be blessed.

Rabbi Yehuda said: **Come and see** <note>original: *Ta Chazi*</note>, it is written: "And he shall atone for himself and for his house" <note>Leviticus 16:6</note>. Regarding his sin, he confesses it upon himself because he has sinned, and he atones for himself, as it is written, "and he shall atone for himself." Rabbi Hiyya said: I know a new matter regarding the binding of the High Priest and all the places where the other Priest is bound. Because of this, another offers his sacrifice and raises it to that place where he is bound. Once the crown of the Priest rises to that place, they do not hinder him from ascending to his place and atoning for his debt; therefore, another offers the sacrifice for him. Since another was offering it, and they were not satisfied solely by his own hands, they are all blessed to atone for his debt, and the Holy Witness is found through them. This is like the rule: "One who prays and makes an error, another shall stand in his place."

Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Hama were sitting. Rabbi Eleazar said: I have seen in my days that on **Rosh Hashanah** <note>The Jewish New Year</note> and Yom Kippur, one should not listen to the prayer of just any man, unless he has prepared himself for thirty days prior. **Another interpretation** <note>original: *Davar Acher*</note>: Just as the wine dregs are at the bottom, so the sins of a righteous man are cleansed to atone for the world. This is especially true regarding the sounding of the Shofar; one should not accept the sounding of a man who is not wise enough to blow according to the secret of the sounding <note>the mystical intentions or *kavanot* of the Shofar</note>. For we have learned that Rabbi Yose the Elder said: The soundings must be in their proper order. The first includes everything. The second is one in order, with a "Great Order" between them. The third has one here and one there, with **Strength** <note>original: *Gevurah*</note> between them. The sound rises from the lower depths, one strong and one soft, as has been established. We have learned: Ten worthy ones planted one, and all of them shall weep. And how is Isaac crowned? And how does the sound cry out to embrace us? On this day it is written "remembered" <note>God "remembered" Sarah</note> because of sins. And how was Isaac bound? The Binding of All, and the crown wails <note>marginal variant: *howls*</note>, and the voice of the Shofar is strong. Worthy is the portion of one who passes through his days and is saved from the gathering.

Rabbi Hama said: For this reason, we read the section of the Binding of Isaac on this day, for on this day Isaac was bound below to be bound to that which is Above. And he was destined to be bound at the hour it is written: "And he bound Isaac his son..." <note>Genesis 22:9</note>. Rabbi Eleazar said: On this day, Isaac is crowned to be rebuked, as it is written: "And God tested Abraham" <note>Genesis 22:1</note>. What is "tested" (*nissa*)? It is like the phrase "Lift up a banner (*nes*) for the nations." It is hidden. "And he called the name of the Lord..." is hidden. What is the **Holy One's** <note>original: *Kudsha Leh*</note> purpose? To include the Right Side and to be uplifted. Then he renews it according to the law of rebuke. He arranges it exactly, and this is the "Fear of Isaac." For behold, it is written: "For God is the Judge; He humbles one and exalts another" <note>Psalms 75:8</note>. For God is the Judge, and we see that judgment is stirred in the place of Jacob... Woe to the world when it is summoned to judgment, for the secret of the matter is that through Him, the Lord judges, and this is the secret of the world's foundations. And since the crown of Jacob entered, Jacob took hold...

# Leviticus

->**Leviticus**<-

At that time, fire is sharpened and coals are found on every side, for He is harnessed and girded with weapons. A herald goes forth to slay all those [accusers]. A wise one stands at the entrance and desires it; the left side <note>The side of Judgment/Din</note> does not turn away from me, and the power of slaughter is gazed upon among the children of men. They sigh while they strengthen one another and desire one another, and His anger is prepared against those who go out to kill. He goes out to rebuke where the foolishness of anger and the strength of judgment reside. This man’s wrath is harsh, and thus the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: "My children, do not fear! Behold, I stand at the entrance; return in repentance on this day and take for Me a word." And with what? With the Shofar. For when the sound of the Shofar is found to be as it should be, and they direct their hearts through it to open [the gates], that voice ascends, and through it the Patriarchs <note>Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, representing the Sefirot of Mercy, Strength, and Beauty</note> are crowned and stand in the dwelling place of Jacob. Therefore, one must be careful with the Shofar, to know this sound and to direct the heart through it. There is no sound of the Shofar that does not ascend to a certain firmament, and all the hosts of that firmament give place to that sound. Concerning this it is said: *And the Lord uttered His voice before His army...* <note>Joel 2:11</note>. And that voice is praised in that firmament until another voice comes to be prepared <margin>Another version: to be removed</margin> together, and they ascend with intention to another firmament. Regarding this we have learned: there is a voice that ascends and strikes another voice. Let that sound of the Shofar blasts of Israel be below, and once all those sounds from below join together and ascend to that supernal firmament of the Holy King, they surround Him and are all crowned before the King. Then the thrones are raised, and the other throne of Jacob stands and is prepared. Because of this, the level of Enoch the Elder <note>Metatron</note> is found in the Shofar... <note>The text here uses dense mystical metaphors regarding the "womb" of the Shofar</note> for that voice which issues from the inner breath and from the soul is found in the Shofar. Through this, one merits to lead the music on high. On that day, accusers stand and are found above, but when that sound of the Shofar ascends, they are all pushed away from before it and cannot remain. Happy is the portion of the righteous who know how to direct their will before their Master and know how to repair the world on this day through the sound of the Shofar. Regarding this it is written:
> **Happy is the people that knows the joyful shout (Teruah)** <note>Psalms 89:16</note>

It says "knows," not just "blows." On this day, the people must look for a man who is greater than all, who knows the secrets <term>Harmoni: likely a corruption of the Greek 'Harmonia' or 'Hermeneia', referring to the hidden arrangements or interpretations</term> of the Holy King, who knows the glory of the King, so that he may request a prayer for them with his life and soul, and to produce the sound of the Shofar for all the worlds with the intention of the heart, with wisdom, and with the will of all, so that judgment may be removed from the world through his hand. Woe to those whose ascent is not found to be as it should be, for the sins of the world are remembered... <note>The text here is somewhat fragmented, discussing the weight of the world's debt</note>. Happy are the people when all the judgments are removed from their places through him. How much more so the Priest (Kohen), through whom those above and below are blessed. One is Eleazar... and the Levite, until he ascends to the service, they crown him, and they know the secrets and his works; if not, he does not ascend to the service. So too in the Sanhedrin to judge a case... and thus the gravity of the Sanctuary is upon him. If he is not [fit], he does not ascend to the service. This is what is written: *And to Your holy one...* He returned and asked: Why did Aaron merit the Urim and Thummim <note>The oracular breastplate of the High Priest</note> and to perform the service? Because of the measure of Kindness (Chesed) that was in him, etc. *Who said of his father and mother, "I have not seen them"...* <note>Deuteronomy 33:9</note>. And once all these levels are found, then *They shall teach Your ordinances to Jacob... they shall put incense before You...* to quiet the anger and to purify the world, *and whole burnt offerings on Your altar*, so that all may be sweetened and blessings may be found in all worlds. Then, *Bless, O Lord, his substance...* <note>Deuteronomy 33:11</note>.
**And if** the whole congregation of Israel shall err... <note>Leviticus 4:13</note>. Rabbi Shimon opened: "How much must a man look into the glory of his Master, so that a herald may be found before the Holy One, blessed be He. For when the Holy One, blessed be He, created man..."

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the creation of humanity from the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra. ## Main Text (Zohar)

He created everything for him, as it is said <note>Genesis 2:3</note> **which God created to make** and so on. "The" <note>The Hebrew particle 'Et'</note> Adam, male and female. And the female was included within the male, and then it is written further on how they calculated many reckonings. Come and see: when the supernal mystery was established, a single female was given, the soul-mother of all spirits, whom we have established is named Lilith, and she was found initially with Adam. And at the time Adam was created and his body was formed, a thousand spirits from the "Left Side" <note>The side of judgment and impurity</note> gathered over that body; they sought to enter him but were not permitted, and they could not until the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> rebuked them. He [Adam] stood around the body without a spirit, and his face was somewhat green, and all those spirits surrounded him. At that moment, a cloud struck and cast away all those spirits. And at this time it is written <note>Genesis 1:26</note> **And God said, Let us make man** in our image, after our likeness, which we have established: for the female was conceived from the male, from that soul of Adam, and she brought forth that spirit to enter into Adam, comprised of two sides as is fitting, for it says <note>Genesis 2:7</note> **And He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.** Truly a "living soul." And for one who has a doubt about this because he does not know if this "living [soul]" refers to the <term>Lower Chayah</term> <note>The lower vital soul or the Shekhinah</note> or the <term>Upper Chayah</term> <note>The higher celestial life-force</note>—and the male side is only found through her—it is not written "to the living soul" <note>with the definite article 'ha'</note> but simply "to a living soul," which implies the inclusion of everything. And when Adam stood up, his female was attached to his side. And that holy soul within him would incline to this side and to that side, and provide for this one and that one, because she was thus included. Afterward, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <term>sawed</term> <note>original: "nesar" - referring to the mystical separation of the joined male and female</note> Adam and prepared his female, as it is written <note>Genesis 2:22</note> **And the Lord God built the rib** etc. "The rib"—this we have established as the "side" and not a literal bone. And the female of Adam, in her adornments, was like a bride to the wedding canopy. Once Lilith saw this, she fled, and she is attached [to the world] and from then until now she is ready to harm the children of the world. And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, is ready to settle the worlds, He subdues this <term>Lilith</term> and banishes her to the ruins, for she is the ruin of the world. This is the "toss of the headband" <note>An idiom for seductive distraction</note> toward harlotry, and he charms her away from the house. And the ancient books say that she fled from Adam long ago, but we have not learned it thus, for this female [Eve] was found with him. But before the "Living One" <note>Eve</note> stood properly with Adam, he would couple with her [Lilith], and when he saw that [Eve] was properly prepared with him, [Lilith] fled to the sea and intended to harm the children of the world. Heaven forbid! At that time when a man couples with his wife, he should direct his heart to the holiness of the matter. And at the time she is wrapped in the veil that is prepared, [the spirits] circle around; do not enter and do not bend to her, for your portion is sufficient. Otherwise, he will be weakened... <note>The text here uses protective incantations and instructions for marital purity to ward off Lilith</note> ...holiness is grasped by the holiness of the King, and you are wrapped. And do not let his spirit be puffed up until a certain time, and so at all times until three days of conception, for if she does not conceive within three days, she will not conceive again. And in the Book of Enoch we find that the King said thirty days... and after the deed is finished, let frozen waters surround the bed, and the protection of all. Afterward, one who nurses... should not couple with a man except at the time the firmament is covered, and afterward do not bend to him until one hour... and all because of the rebuke of the firmament... and when he saw, the blow was changed for the better. Happy are the righteous who sanctify these deep mysteries above and below, and all for the sake of the Torah. For the Torah—whoever strives in it is crowned with the crown of the Holy Name, for the Torah is the Holy Name. And whoever strives in it is spread out and crowned with the Holy Name, and then he knows hidden paths and deep mysteries above and below, and he shall never be afraid. Come and see...

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Leviticus** <-

At that time when they were appointed over a sin and transgressed a commandment for which they were liable. And because below was the first sin, that sin descended upon it. It is written, "He forgives and pardons" <note>original: *וסלח ומחל*</note> thus from all of them, and to forgive at all times when they are recognized and established as penitents before the Holy One, Blessed be He. Behold, we have established that these are a covering above, at times to forgive them from the side of harsh judgment <note>term: *Din Kasya* - the restrictive, punishing aspect of the Divine</note>, for this is what is written: *As for My people, a babe is their master, and women rule over them.* <note>Isaiah 3:12</note> When a master rules over him, it is certainly so. And all of them are called "the flame of the turning sword" <note>Genesis 3:24</note> to see visions; the turning sword is entirely gathered from that sword which is called "a sword that executes the vengeance of the covenant" <note>Leviticus 26:25</note> and "the sword of the Lord is filled with blood." <note>Isaiah 34:6</note> And that flame of the turning sword is at times male <note>term: *Dukhra*</note> and at times female <note>term: *Nukva*</note>, and behold, we have established this. Woe to the world when those women rule in the world! When the sins of Israel increased, they crooked their paths and were found in guilt before those to whom they were liable; then it says "covering," and to be covered—how are you appointed, how do you sit, so as not to be mixed into the world before Him? And after the sin, we established for it a "horn," and behold, the companions have established this. Regarding all this, it is said that everything is found in the male, as it is written: *And he judged Israel at that time.* <note>Judges 4:4</note> And regarding this we have learned: Woe to the man whose wife stands up to say the blessing for him to fulfill his obligation. So too the male [aspect], yet "she judged Israel at that time"—woe to the generation in which there is found no one to judge the people except for one female. Come and see: there are two types found in the world who said praise to the Holy One, Blessed be He, such that all the males in the world could not say the same. And who are they? The male and the female [aspects]. Hannah said: *There is none holy as the Lord, for there is none beside Thee* <note>1 Samuel 2:2</note> and all those verses. For she opened the gate of faith to the world, such as: *He raises up the poor out of the dust, and lifts up the needy from the dunghill*—behold the gate of faith—*to make them sit with princes*—behold the faith of above. After they are found dwelling, who are these "princes"? These are the Patriarchs, as it is written: *The princes of the peoples are gathered.* <note>Psalms 47:10</note> *To make them sit with princes*—all of them for the sake of His name; He is destined to be sanctified with Moses and Aaron, as it is written: *Moses and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among them that call upon His name.* <note>Psalms 99:6</note> *And He makes them inherit the throne of glory.* This is the kingship of Samuel, who shared the honor of kingship with two kings. This and that, *and He makes them inherit the throne of glory*—this is the Holy One, Blessed be He, who is their portion, His own throne for His servants; this is what is written: *And He makes them inherit the throne of glory.* *And He shall give strength to His king.* <note>1 Samuel 2:10</note> "His king" <note>original: *מלכו*</note> is written without the letter *Vav* <note>note: This orthographic detail is used to distinguish between the earthly king and the Divine King</note>. It speaks only of "His king"—we have learned this refers to the Holy King. And the spirit of wisdom is below here; at the time when judgment is awakened and rules, it rules over mercy, and mercy is suppressed. But at the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, is awakened from the grace of the stream, then mercy prevails and judgments are suppressed. This is what is written: *And He shall give strength to His king, and He shall exalt...* with the *Vav* upon him in life, *He shall thunder.* What is "upon him"? At the time when the dew of the Holy Ancient One <note>term: *Atika Kadisha* - the highest, most merciful level of Divinity</note> spreads over him and the Head descends into the assembly called "Heaven," then *He shall thunder*—their power and the strength of the harsh judgments shall be broken. *And He shall give strength to His king*—this is the Holy One, Blessed be He. *And exalt the horn of His anointed*—this is what is called the "Horn of the Jubilee" <note>note: A reference to the Sephirah of Binah, the source of liberation</note> as we have established. "His anointed" <note>original: *Meshiho*</note> as in another matter: *The anointed of the God of Jacob.* <note>2 Samuel 23:1</note> Because of this, "the horn of His anointed" is said. The male below in relation to the Shekhinah <note>term: *Shekhinah* - the Divine Presence, the feminine aspect</note> of the Holy King. *The Lord, His adversaries shall be broken in pieces; against them shall He thunder in heaven.* This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, was destined to offer the Torah to all other nations, but they did not want it. Was it not revealed before Him that they would not want it? Rather, it was so they would have no opening of the mouth [to complain]; for the Ancient One, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave them the Torah, but they dismissed it. And all those verses that Deborah said are all within the secret of wisdom, until that hour of danger caused... etc., *until I, Deborah, arose.* <note>Judges 5:7</note> "I arose" <note>original: *שקמתי*</note> is written without the letter *Yod*, for they have established that the Holy Spirit was below her, and because of this: *Awake, awake, Deborah; awake, awake, utter a song.* <note>Judges 5:12</note> And regarding this, when males are found in sin and are not worthy, the Holy Spirit certainly rests upon them [the women], and if...

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the laws of sacrifices from the Book of Leviticus, specifically focusing on the communal sin offering for the Sanhedrin (the High Court) and the spiritual mechanics of confession and repentance.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

**And if** the whole congregation of Israel shall err, etc. <note>Leviticus 4:13</note>. As it is said, "the whole congregation of Israel shall err"—it should have simply said "all Israel shall err." Why "the whole *congregation* of Israel"? This refers to those who are found in Jerusalem, for from there the Torah goes forth to all the people. And if those who were there erred, it is as if all Israel erred. We have learned that because they erred there, the whole nation is considered to have erred, because everyone follows after them. This is as it is said: "from the eyes of the assembly" <note>Numbers 15:24</note>—the "eyes of the assembly" are the Sanhedrin <note>The High Court of 71 sages</note>, those who are appointed over Israel.

**Rabbi** Hiyya and Rabbi Yose were walking on the road. As they were walking, Rabbi Yose said to Rabbi Hiyya: "I see that the pillars of the Torah are like the Priests of the Ancient of Days" <note>A reference to the highest, most hidden level of Divinity</note>. Rabbi Hiyya opened his discourse and said:
> "I acknowledged my sin to You, and my iniquity I did not hide; I said, 'I will confess my transgressions to the Lord,' and You forgave the iniquity of my sin. Selah." <note>Psalms 32:5</note>

From here we learn that any person who hides his sins and does not reveal them before the Holy King to seek mercy, they do not open for him the "Opening of Repentance," because he has hidden it from Him. But if he reveals them before the Holy One, Blessed be He, the Holy One has pity on him and mercy prevails over judgment. This is especially true if he weeps, for then even when all gates are closed, the Gate of Tears is open and his prayer is accepted. Therefore, the spreading out of one's sins is an honor to the King, to awaken mercy over judgment. And regarding this it is written:
> "He who offers a sacrifice of confession honors Me." <note>Psalms 50:23; original: *Zoveach todah yechabdaneni*</note>

What is the meaning of "honors Me" <note>original: *yechabdaneni*, which has a double 'n' in Hebrew</note>? These are two honors: one above and one below; one in this world and one in the World to Come. The verse moves quickly like burning coals, speaking of many transgressions at once. Why does it say "I acknowledged my sin to You and my iniquity I did not hide" and then "I will confess my transgressions to the Lord"? And furthermore, why "to the Lord"? It should have said "to You." However, David said all his words through the Holy Spirit, and he spoke to the Kingdom of Heaven <note>The Shekhinah</note>, as one who worships from below to above and from above to below. One who seeks the King must first make it known to the Matron <note>The Queen/Shekhinah</note>, and therefore: "I acknowledged my sin to You and my iniquity I did not hide" refers to the Foundation of the World. "I said, 'I will confess my transgressions to the Lord'"—this refers to the Holy King who forgives all judgment and pardons the person who seeks to enter before Him. For God is approached through confession, as it is written: "upon the sacrifice of his peace-offering confession." "And You forgave the iniquity of my sin, Selah"—for this reaches to the highest of the high, the place where the Holy Ancient One spreads His light. Therefore, the verse is concise, for a person who seeks for his iniquity before the King must unify the Holy Name with his will and bind everything as one. When the binding is complete, his will is found. These are the lights of the day; the wise person knows how to seek his will before the King, for he knocks at the King's gate. Rabbi Hiyya turned to him and said: "Certainly, it is so. The lamp of the Torah teaches us the secrets of the King."

## Commentary (The Faithful Shepherd)

This commandment is to bring an offering for the Great Sanhedrin that erred in a ruling. There are times when they sin, and they are the "Great" ones, and the "Tail" follows them—the Small Sanhedrin of twenty-three. <margin>Another explanation</margin> The Kingdom is called the "Small Sanhedrin" and is prepared with twenty-three gates. The Sanhedrin of seventy corresponds to the seventy languages of the world and the seventy faces of the Torah. The Matron <note>The Shekhinah</note> of the Kingdom possesses these seventy languages... everything is explained through the secret of the exchange of atonement. The Levite who sings in his service knows all the languages, even the language of separation. The seventy faces of the Torah are in one language, and the Law <note>Halakha</note> does not deviate, but is Wisdom. The secret of the seventy languages is established in the secret of the Foundation <note>Yesod</note>, the secret of the Chariot with seventy thrones. Regarding them it is said: "Anyone who occupies himself for the sake of Heaven, the Great Name blesses him with all His strength, and they tear up his sentence." Seventy years, one language, every measure of Wisdom... the secret of the seventy-two names. Until here.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar regarding the destruction of the Temple and the exile of the Divine Presence. It focuses on the personification of the Shekhinah as Rachel weeping for her children.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...of the Holy King, in order to know the "Right Hand" <note>The attribute of Mercy/Chesed</note> for their crowns, and all the others depend on these, etc. **Rabbi Yose** opened his discourse and said:
> "Thus says the Lord: A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping..." (Jeremiah 31:15).

"Thus says the Lord"—this has already been established: in every place where a prophet begins to speak, his words were meant to be identified [with a specific level of prophecy], but here regarding this "Thus says the Lord," it is difficult. And what is this "voice heard in Ramah"? Thus we have learned: at that time when the Holy Temple below was destroyed and [Israel] was driven out and went into exile, which was destined for their light and their hands. And at the time when the destruction approached and the <term>Knesset Yisrael</term> <note>The Assembly of Israel, a title for the Shekhinah, the feminine aspect of God</note> was banished from the King’s house to go after them in the error [of exile]. Previously, she had hovered over the Altar and over the Ramp and over everything; but when she saw that the destruction was near, and how the blood of the pious was snatched away into hiding, and the holy Ark and the company of strength were hidden, then she raised a voice. The upper and lower worlds were shaken, and the voice reached on high to the place where the King dwells. The King then desired to return the world to "tohu and bohu" <note>Chaos and void (Genesis 1:2)</note> until he saw many hosts and many camps [of angels] meeting her, yet she would not receive comfort from them. This is what is written:
> "A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping; Rachel weeping for her children; she refuses to be comforted for her children, because he is not" (Jeremiah 31:15).

That she did not receive comfort from them "because he is not"—because the Holy King had ascended higher and higher and was no longer found in the hidden chamber. This is why it is written "because **he** is not" <note>original: *ki einennu*</note> and it is not written "because **they** are not" <note>original: *ki einam*</note>. **Rabbi Hiyya** said to him: What is "Rachel weeping for her children"? Rather, it is the portion of the <term>Knesset Yisrael</term>, and this is the wisdom of Jacob and Rachel, as it is written:
> "And Jacob loved Rachel" (Genesis 29:18).

And it is written, "But Rachel was barren" (Genesis 29:31). And it is written there:
> "He settles the barren woman of the house as a joyful mother of children" (Psalms 113:9).

This "because he is not" is as we have said: "Where is He?" <note>original: *heikhano* - a play on the word *einennu*</note> is a great matter because of [the exile]. "Where is He?"—for He has ascended on high and distanced Himself from all. In this manner, "Where is He?" is to be looked for from the "Great Waters." **Rabbi Hiyya** said: From what place was she banished and distanced? He said to him: From the Holy Temple she was banished, and afterward she sought out all the portions of Israel. Afterward, when she went out from the Land, she stood upon the Altar and sat there for three days, speaking to all her hosts and camps, and she was estranged from the King's house and called out over herself:
> "How does the city sit solitary..." (Lamentations 1:1).

Already **Rabbi Hiyya** and **Rabbi Yose** said: Israel was exiled from the Land, and the Holy Temple will not be rebuilt until all of Israel is found in [proper] intention, and until they remember the world as it was at first... for once my people are stirred like this, all the people will be found [restored] to their crowns. **Rabbi Hiyya** said from the verse: "And spare all the congregation of Israel," and it stands as a vision... if the eyes of the community are hidden, then my people will be stirred and all the people will be settled in their crowns.

He said: While they were walking, they saw a place where the Altar was like smoke, and a spark flew from it that was moving within it. They sat until, while they were sitting, a bird flew and ran before them. **Rabbi Hiyya** said: Let us look out so that we may be facing the mountains where they are found. They stood and went until they arranged their movements and saw the place... A canopy was prepared for them, and they found before them a mountain-crag and a cave within it, and they entered there and sat all that day and all night.

**Rabbi Hiyya** opened his discourse and said:
> "But you, do not fear, My servant Jacob... for behold, I will save you from afar" (Jeremiah 30:10; 46:27).

"From afar"? It should have said "from near"! But they have already established this verse: "From afar"—all of them merit from the "Deep." "From afar" is like that which is written:
> "From afar the Lord appeared to me" (Jeremiah 31:2).

And it is written:
> "She brings her food from afar" (Proverbs 31:14).

And these are all the depths of the River, the place of that River that flows and goes forth <note>Referring to Binah, the divine source of emanation</note>. This is Jacob, for since it is written "Do not fear, My servant Jacob," what is "And Jacob shall return"? It is as we have said: "For behold, I will save you from afar," for the foundation ascended higher and higher, as it is written:
> "Why, O Lord, do You stand far off?" (Psalms 10:1).

And the "far place" bears witness: "I will save you," and "Jacob shall return" to descend to his throne in joy like the Assembly of Israel, "and shall be quiet and at ease," and they will laugh at the rains of his sorrow... and all of them will honor Isaac from the "great trembling."

## Leviticus

And concerning this, it is written: **"Then you shall see and be radiant, and your heart shall thrill and tremble"** <note>Isaiah 60:5</note>. That "trembling" occurs when the *Yesod* <note>The foundational emanation of the Divine, often associated with the channel of blessing</note> awakens to depart to another place, and everything becomes constricted. Like a bird or a shadow that flits away, the Holy One, blessed be He, prepares for us a distant and hidden place in quietness and security, removed from all disturbance. For when the Holy One, blessed be He, performs a miracle, He performs it completely.

Rabbi Yossi opened his discourse: **"And Moses said to the Lord: See, You say to me..."** <note>Exodus 33:12</note>. What is being discussed here? Master Barak asked: Since the Holy Spirit rests upon you, the stars have come to teach, yet they do not guard me according to the law. And just as Barak relied on a woman <note>Deborah</note> to be found there because of her, so the Torah is with you, for she is the Name of the Holy King upon him.

They sat inside that cave all that day. When evening fell, the cave was illuminated by a great glory. Two merchants passed by, their donkeys laden with wine and various goods. They stopped at another cave nearby. The Holy One, blessed be He, provided for them, saying: "Here is food for us to eat, drink, and rejoice." They saw the light of this [first] cave. One said to his companion: "Before you say anything, I will ask about this verse." He replied: "What is it?" He said: "One matter that is written: **'Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good; for His mercy endures forever'** <note>Psalm 136:1</note>. Why does it say **'for He is good'** and not simply 'His mercy'? It says **'for He is good'** in relation to His pious ones <note>Chassidim</note>. But for others, is He not also good?" He sighed and said: "Woe to the merchant who is found to be the possession of the Holy One, blessed be He!"

Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Yossi, who were sitting in the cave, rejoiced. Rabbi Chiya said to Rabbi Yossi: "Did I not tell you that when the Holy One, blessed be He, performs a miracle, He performs it completely?" They went out to meet them. Rabbi Chiya stepped forward and opened with: **"Peace, peace to him that is far off and to him that is near"** <note>Isaiah 57:19</note>. He said: "Here is one for the 'far off' and one for the 'near,' yet all is one. 'To the far off' refers to one who was distant but has been made near. Furthermore, 'to the far off' refers to the path of Repentance <note>Teshuvah</note>; previously he was far, and now he is near. Furthermore, 'far' is when a person distances himself from the Torah, he is far from the Holy One, blessed be He; but those who draw near to the Torah are drawn directly to the Holy One, blessed be He. And now that you have drawn near to us, enter the cave!"

The merchants came and were found before them. They unloaded their burdens and prepared food. They all went to the mouth of the cave. One of the merchants said: "Let the masters of the Torah tell us about this verse: **'Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good...'** Why is it written **'for He is good'**? It is written **'for He is good'** in relation to His pious ones—is He not good to others?"

Rabbi Chiya said: "**'For He is good'** is certainly a second level. It is 'forever' because of the wonders of the world that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed and established. Even if a person sins against the Holy One, blessed be He, every day, the verse still concludes **'for He is good'** in relation to His pious ones. This is certainly so: it refers to those righteous ones who fear the Holy One, blessed be He, and not to the wicked who provoke Him every day and do not labor in the Torah."

The merchant said to him: "It is fitting for every vessel that is delayed from the crown of the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence</note> to yearn for the light." Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Yossi said to him: "Certainly your words of Torah belong to a single source."

He said to them: "Once I was traveling to Lod and entered the city. I found myself by a certain wall. For a long time, I stayed in that house and heard a profound explanation of this verse: **'Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good.'** They said that the Holy One, blessed be He, refers to the 'Lower World' <note>Malkhut</note>, which King David held onto, and thus inherited his kingdom. And the verse concludes **'for He is good'** because the Holy One, blessed be He, is the Foundation <note>Yesod</note> of this world, which is called 'Good.' And sometimes He is called 'Good' in relation to His pious ones. Are there not many pious ones? Rather, there is 'Mercy' (*Chesed*) and there is 'Mercy.' These are called **'the sure mercies of David'** <note>Isaiah 55:3; original: *Chasdei David HaNe'emanim*</note>. And when these 'mercies of David' are filled from the hidden dew of the Holy Ancient One <note>Atika Kadisha; the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note>, then they are called the 'Good Foundation' (*Yesod Tov*). Then 'Good' is found for them, for when it is found in the abundance that flows into it, it writes [blessing] for this lower world, and everything is found in blessing. Therefore, David waits for this level to illuminate this world which he held onto."

"These words helped us, and all this I know." Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Yossi came and kissed him in blessing. Rabbi Chiya said...

## Main Text (Zohar)

**Leviticus**

Hiyya, Hiyya! Cover your eyes with the dust <note>A metaphor for humility or the physical state of the deceased</note>, for you are not like the righteous who are in the place where you shepherd the upper mountains. I cover the birds that support [the world], and they all rejoice in your words. Woe to the world when it goes astray when you depart from it! He opened [the discourse] further and said: That man, regarding this matter we have spoken of, I heard that at the hour when he departs from the house, as it is written: <note>Daniel 9:17</note> > "Now therefore, O our God, hearken unto the prayer of Thy servant, and to his supplications... for the Lord's sake." 

He said this: If this support raises the word, it is well, for so they say, "Do it for the sake of the King." But this medicine <note>original: *sama*</note> knows that the voice of the Law is like the Judgment from which the spirit goes out to the world. See, just as they say to a king, "Do it for the sake of your servant," or for the sake of a small matter from you; rather, it was necessary that this medicine prepare the House of the King and the Palace of the Sanctuary below. And this is held as one, in order to repair this as one. 

And when the Sanctuary below stands in its established state, then the Name above stands in its established state. And this is as he said, that the King weeps for this House and this Temple because the **Matronita** <note>The Divine Queen/Shekhinah</note> is not found there, as she sits outside the Temple. "Spare, O Lord, and cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate sanctuary, for the Lord's sake." What is the reason for "for the Lord's sake"? Because He is not found outside of His dwelling place. Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose arose and rejoiced in that night more than all of them. The traveling companion opened and said: Let me say one word before you that I have observed. I stand by this verse which is written: <note>Psalm 63:1</note> > "A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah." 

David uttered a song when he was fleeing from him <note>King Saul</note>, and what did he say? <note>Psalm 63:2</note> > "O God, Thou art my God, earnestly will I seek Thee; my soul thirsteth for Thee..." "O God, Thou art my God"—this is because he was constantly held by the attribute of Power <note>Gevurah</note>. And how could David say this to the Holy One, blessed be He, in a distant land and an impure place where the Shekhinah does not dwell? Rather, even though your sister <note>The Shekhinah</note> is from there, his [connection] did not cease. He said to the Holy One, blessed be He: I have seen and heard that you said <term>I have beheld Thee</term> <note>original: *chaziticha*</note> in the way that I observed before You; when I was unable to do so, I was hidden, except for coming outside the place where the Shekhinah dwells. In the matter of "my soul thirsts for Thee," for the soul longs, and your son and my body [long] to be seen before You, but I cannot because I am "in a dry and weary land, where no water is." For a "dry and weary land" is what the place outside where the Shekhinah dwells is called, because the Living Waters are not found here. And we see that these Living Waters are the Shekhinah, as it is written of her: "A well of living waters." And regarding this, "in a dry and weary land, where no water is" is written. 

Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose said: Certainly the way is prepared before us. They entered a cave and slept at midnight. They heard the voice of the beasts in the desert that were awakening. Rabbi Hiyya said: This is the time of Eden, to assist the Community of Israel <note>Knesset Yisrael</note> so that she may be found to eat. They said: Let each and every one say a word from what he has heard and knows of the ways. They all sat. Rabbi Hiyya opened and said: <note>Psalm 22:1</note> > "For the Leader; upon the hind of the dawn. A Psalm of David." 

**The Hind of the Dawn** <note>original: *Ayelet HaShachar*</note>—this is the Community of Israel, who is called "a lovely hind and a graceful doe." And why "the hind of the dawn" and not "of the day"? Behold, the hind is from that place called "Dawn," then it is hidden like a *mezuzah*. And King David said this concerning the Community of Israel, for he did not say "the Community of Israel" [explicitly], but this is implied by what is written: "upon the hind of the dawn." Come and see: at the time when evening falls, the gates of the worlds are closed and the lower ones are covered <margin>variant: hidden</margin>. And all those "distant ones" <note>impure spirits</note> awaken and go and roam the whole world, and they arrange themselves over the bodies of human beings and force them to their mountains and their beds. And the image of the Holy King descends, and it is defiled by this, for they have strengthened themselves in their beds like one who is holy-impure. And He weeps without their souls; each one ascends as is fitting for it. And they have established it: the power of the portion of the righteous is that their souls ascend above and are not delayed in a place where they should not be, until midnight. Then [the world] stands in stern judgment, and a herald calls, and the gates are opened. Then a certain wind from the North side <note>Sitra Tzafon/Gevurah</note> awakens and strikes 

like a harp...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra). It focuses on the spiritual mechanics of the midnight study of Torah and the symbolic relationship between the Divine King and the Shekhinah (the Divine Presence), personified here as the Community of Israel.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Leviticus<-

The harp of David plays of its own accord, and praise rises to the King, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, delights with the righteous ones <note>original: *tzaddikaya*</note> in the Garden of Eden. Blessed is the portion of whoever awakens at that time to look into the Torah. Anyone who stands up at that time is called a "companion" of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the Community of Israel <note>The *Shekhinah*, the feminine aspect of the Divine</note>. Not only that, but they are called "brothers and friends" to Him, as it is written <note>Psalms 122:8</note>: **"For the sake of my brothers and friends, I will now say, 'Peace be within you.'"** And they are called "companions," as it is written <note>Song of Songs 8:13</note>: **"Companions listen for your voice."**

When the day comes, they all stand and proclaim, and the gates of the South side <note>The side of *Chessed* or Lovingkindness</note> are opened, and they are crowned with many splendors. The crowns of mercy are opened, and the King sits and receives praises. Then the Community of Israel and all those companions take hold of His wings, and their words come and rest in the lap of the King. Then the King commands that all those members of the Palace be written in the book, and a thread of lovingkindness <note>original: *chuta de-chesed*</note> is drawn over them. By that thread, a person is crowned like the crown of a King, and the fear and awe of them is upon those below. Even in times when others are under judgment, he may enter all the gates of the King, and there is no one to stop him. Those others <note>the accusing angels</note> do not pass judgment upon him because he is marked with the mark of the King, and it is known that he belongs to the King's Palace; therefore, they do not judge him.

Blessed is the portion of the righteous who labor in the Torah. When the King's priest comes to the world of the Torah—come and see—a word does not stand for the Community of Israel before the King except through the Torah. For as long as Israel labors in the Torah, the Community of Israel dwells with them. When they are found to be neglecting the Torah, she cannot remain with them for even a single hour, as it were. So, at the hour when the Community of Israel awakens toward the King, her strength is fortified, and the Holy King rejoices to receive them. But whenever the Community of Israel comes before the King and the Torah is not found with her, her strength is weakened, as it were—the strength of those who gather the supernal power. Therefore, blessed are those who labor in the Torah, for at that hour when the Community of Israel needs it, a voice cries out concerning them: "You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified."

Rabbi Yose opened and said <note>Isaiah 21:11</note>: **"The burden of Dumah. One calls to me from Seir: 'Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?'"** The companions have established the meaning of this verse in several places. But "The burden of Dumah" <note>Dumah literally means "silence," often associated with the angel of death or the grave</note> refers to all the time that Israel is found in exile; their time is known, as is the length and the voice of that exile. But the end of the exile of Edom <note>Seir/Edom is traditionally identified with Rome or the final long exile</note> is a "burden of silence" (*Dumah*), for it is not revealed or known like the other beasts <note>the previous three empires/exiles</note>. 

The voice says: "One calls to me from Seir"—the voice of those suffering in the exile of Seir, who are crushed into the dust, crying out and saying: "Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?" They want to know about the Matronita <note>The Queen/Shekhinah</note>: "What have You done with my Matronita?" Then the voice, as it were, turns to them and says: "Arise, My beloved ones, who sleep in exile and forget their own pain to ask Me about the Matronita." They say: "Watchman, come and search; Watchman, wait for our protection." As it is written: "What of the night?" (*mah mi-leilah*)—what have You done with the night? How have You guarded her? "What of the night?" (*mah mi-leil*). For sometimes it is called *Leilah* and sometimes it is called *Leil*. What is the difference? It is written <note>Exodus 12:42</note>: **"It is a night of watching"** (*leil shimurim*), and it is written: **"That is the night"** (*ha-laylah ha-zeh*). 

Then the voice answers them: "Behold, My guarding is found, for they are ready to receive and to be found as one." This is what is written: "The watchman said"—He who guards the company below—"The morning comes, and also the night." For as before, she rises higher and higher, ascending to that place (the King) where they are always united. That "morning" is below. Behold, they are ready to be joined as "night." "And also the night"—this day is for all your gatherings to be delayed... [the text continues regarding repentance] ...ask this: "Why are you delayed? Return, come!" through repentance. Then you shall come to Me. Everything depends on the *Mazal* <note>The supreme source of divine influence/destiny</note>, and all is written to be reconciled together. And the righteous one rejoices in your preparation...

It also provides a mystical interpretation of the prophecy in Isaiah regarding the exile of Edom, framing the exile as a period where the "Watchman" (God) is questioned about the fate of the Divine Presence (the Matronita).</summary>
