## Leviticus

-> **Vayikra** <-
<note>original: "Vayikra" - And He Called</note>

Also "good" and "good," twice "good" is written here. Rather, one is for the Assembly of Israel <note>the Shekhinah</note> and one is for the Holy One, Blessed be He. "The Lord your God will turn your captivity and have compassion <note>literally: 'do good'</note> upon you" and "bless you more than all the peoples." That merchant opened his discourse and said: *“When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy”* <note>Job 38:7</note>. Come and see: the Holy One, Blessed be He, comes to delight with the righteous in the Garden of Eden. All those above and below (folio 85b) <note>reference to another edition</note> appear before Him, and all those who walk in the Garden of Eden open with praise before Him. Come and see: "Then shall the trees of the forest sing for joy before the Lord, for He comes..." and these birds of the earth all chirp praise before Him. Then the rooster strikes its wings and calls out and praises the Holy King, and calls to the Assembly <note>of Israel</note> to begin engaging in the Torah, and to the praise of the Matronit <term>Matronit: A title for the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence, depicted as a Queen or Mother</term>, and according to the mouth of merit. Merit is the portion of those who rise from their beds to engage in the Torah. When the morning comes, the gates of the South open, which are the gates and portals of Loving-kindness <term>Chesed: The divine attribute of expansive love and grace</term> that go out into the world. The East wind awakens and mercy is found, and all those stars that are appointed under the dominion of this "Morning" all open in praise and sing to the Supreme King. This is what is written: *“When the morning stars sang together...”* What do the "sons of God" want here, that they prepare a "shout" <note>teruah</note> in this morning? For behold, all Judgments <term>Din: The divine attribute of strict justice and restriction</term> are passed away at the time when Loving-kindness awakens in the world. Rather, *“and all the sons of God shouted for joy”* is in order to break the strength of the harsh Judgments, to break their power. Then "the earth is utterly broken." And all this is because this Morning has awakened in the world. And a companion who awakened and came to strike... <note>The text here uses obscure Aramaic idioms regarding nature and medicinal plants</note> ...and it is written: "And he called... medicine..." unto the Eternal God.

The companions of the merchant opened and said: *“The morning was light, and the men were sent away...”* <note>Genesis 44:3</note>. What is "The morning was light"? Thus we have learned: What is "Morning"? It is the time when the light comes and the Judgments pass away and Loving-kindness seeks to awaken. All those who come from this side are called to be satisfied, and blessings are prepared for the world. And that is "The morning was light," for mercy is poured into the world and Loving-kindness stands in its place; then it is "Morning Light." And it is written: "And God saw the light, that it was good." Come and see, these are known levels: "Night" is a known level. "Morning Light" is a known level. And it is for the "feet" of the world to look upon it always. It comes when the sun is bright. The "Sun" is a known level and it is for the "feet" of the world to taste everything... for the Lord God is a sun and a shield. And "Morning Light" stands like a mountain from the sun and does not shine for the night. Because of this, everything depends on one another. And this Morning Light, when it awakens, all those below are in freedom and joy, and they are found as this people. And this opening shines... it is the will of the King in His way.

Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yossi wept for them and kissed them on their heads. Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yossi arranged their words: "Blessed is the Merciful One who prepared our way before us!" By the life of the Holy One, Blessed be He, He arranged for us merits—those who engage in the Torah and do not turn away from it for even one moment. Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yossi went out and traveled on their way. Rabbi Hiyya said: "Certainly the love of my heart is tied to these merchants!" And Rabbi Hiyya said: "I am not surprised by this, for in the days of Rav Hamnuna the Elder, we saw merchants of wisdom, for they are full of Loving-kindness, known above and below."

Rabbi Hiyya opened and said: *“And the Lord said to Moses: Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers...”* <note>Deuteronomy 31:16</note>. Come and see: all the time that Moses was alive in the world, he stayed the hands of Israel so they would not sin... before the Holy One, Blessed be He. And because Moses was found among them, he did not give permission... until the generation when the King Messiah shall come... <note>The text becomes highly elliptical and symbolic here, referencing the "eyes" of the generation and the Sanhedrin</note> ...and all the supreme hidden things. Moses, the faithful one, is higher than all. And now these merchants, travelers, bring forth such wisdom! ...wisdom for those who stand before Him, not to change, but to increase every day.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), specifically focusing on the sacrificial laws for leaders and the community. It follows the previous themes of spiritual leadership and the consequences of the departure of great sages.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Rabbi Yose said: This is certainly a voice that rises above all. After the death of Moses, what is written? *“And this people will rise up and go astray...”* <note>Deuteronomy 31:16</note> So it is woe to the world when Rabbi Shimon <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the central figure of the Zohar</note> shall depart from it. Wisdom shall be forgotten and withdrawn from the world, and a person will seek a word of wisdom and will not find anyone to say it. The whole world will err in the Torah because there will be no one found among them who can awaken wisdom. Regarding that time, it is written:
> “And if the whole congregation of Israel shall err, and the matter be hidden from the eyes of the assembly...” (Leviticus 4:13)

The liability of all is because the matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly, for there will not be found one who knows how to reveal the depths of the Torah and its paths. Woe to the guilty generations that are found then in the world. Rabbi Yehuda said: The Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to reveal the deep secrets of the Torah in the time of the King Messiah, because *“the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.”* <note>Isaiah 11:9</note> And it is written:
> “And they shall teach no more every man his neighbor, and every man his brother, saying: ‘Know the Lord’; for they shall all know Me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them.” (Jeremiah 31:33)
And all is joined together.

**When** a ruler <term>Nasi: a prince or tribal leader</term> sins, and does one [of the commandments] etc. <note>Leviticus 4:22</note> as a deputy who has sinned. Rabbi Isaac taught: Wherever it is written "And if" <note>Hebrew: *Ve-im*</note>, such as "If the anointed priest shall sin" or "And if the whole congregation of Israel shall err," the word "sins" <note>Hebrew: *Vechata*</note> is written in a diminished form <note>original: "חסר" (chaser) - referring to a missing letter in the Hebrew spelling</note>. But here, it does not say "And if," it says "When" <note>Hebrew: *Asher*</note> a ruler sins—what does this imply? Even these priests are not found to be frequent in error, for the priest guards himself constantly because the celestial influence <term>Mazal: destiny or constellation</term> rests upon him every day, and the influence of all Israel watches over each one for the rectification of their lives when he sins; therefore it says "And if." Likewise, "And if the whole congregation of Israel shall err," the feminine form is diminished, for they are all found in a single sin—if these sin, those do not sin—and in such a manner "sins" is written. But here, **When a ruler sins**, it is a certainty, because his heart is haughty within him and the people depend upon him and his rectifications. And for this reason, "sins" is written in a diminished form. For example, if he transgresses a negative commandment and performs one of them intentionally, for this reason it does not say "and he sins," for the matter does not depart much [from his nature]. Rabbi Yehuda opened:
> “But when the flocks were feeble, he put them not in; so the feebler were Laban's, and the stronger Jacob's.” (Genesis 30:42)

<margin>The priests and kings search and strengthen.</margin>
How these words are investigated as a plastering, and no man has said them. And this is written: "All that my heart is able, the heave-offering of the Lord." And it is written: "They clothed in ceremony and clothed the King to search and strengthen." Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: even though everything depends on the voice, in purity these stones ascended to the rulers <note>The Nesi'im brought the precious stones for the Ephod and Breastplate</note>. What is the reason? Because they were found upon the heart of the priest. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Let them come in their being, even the priest, and let him give these stones, for the guilty are found upon the heart, and it shall be atoned for them from the movements of the heart. And it is written:
> “And they shall be upon Aaron’s heart, when he goeth in before the Lord.” (Exodus 28:30)
And until they brought them: "And they brought the onyx stones, and the stones to be set, for the ephod, and for the breastplate." And for this reason, "sins" is certainly written in a diminished form. **And does one of all the commandments of the Lord which should not be done**—as they have established, that he transgressed a negative commandment. **Or if his sin be known to him**—because his heart was haughty, he did not consider it a sin at first, but afterward it became known to him and he performed repentance <term>Teshuvah: returning to God</term>. Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yose were sitting one night and toiling in the Torah. Rabbi Yehuda said: Rabbi Yose, I see that the clarity of the Torah in exile is greater at night than by day. He said to him: Because the clarity of the Torah is a danger; the Oral Torah and the Written Torah rule at night and are crowned more than by day, and at the time when it rises, then the life-breath of the Torah dies.

Rabbi Minyumi <note>Likely Rabbi Minyumi</note> opened and did not say to him: "Flower, do here," and they said it is a bride. It comes at the hour when the north wind stirs and the night is divided. Behold, they have established that the Divinity emerges and rages beneath the wings of the rooster, and it strikes its wings and calls out. And the prayers call out at the time when it reaches the pleasantness and awakens toward it. It is written therein: "And we made known," and it calls and strengthens me and is stirred for the sake of the glory of the flame to do His will. And it calls to us for the cup, and for this, it calls out in a groan. And it calls "stranger" because it awakens like the foreign prayer...

...of the male.

## Main Text (Zohar)

For the light, like the rain of **Strength** <note>original: *Gevurah*; the Sefirah of Judgment and Power</note>, comes to awaken the world. Then the children of faith arise and give strength to the **Community of Israel** <note>original: *Knesset Yisrael*; the mystical personification of the Jewish people and the Shekhinah</note>, and then it is called the "Greatness of the Torah." Because of this, David inherited the **Kingdom** <note>original: *Malkhuta*</note>, and he shall subdue the nations and choose them. And when the **rooster** <note>original: *tarnagola*; symbolizes the midnight call to spiritual awakening</note> crows, etc., as in the days of the beds, and they do not awaken. The rooster crows afterward, and as it is said, they later established it with "six wings." Woe to that person, a body of fear, whose spirit is not awakened and who does not gaze upon the glory of his Master. When the day shines, a herald calls out concerning him, and about this it says: "The beast of the forest wraps itself in a garment," etc. All of them are for his house, like your deeds, and they melt away entirely like a sword from the dread of his deeds that provoke Him. What is "wraps"? Even in the error of the male when he slumbers at midnight and the path of the Torah is extended; for the path of Torah is only called such at night. And all those who occupy themselves with the Torah—when the day shines, the **Holy One, Blessed be He** and the **Community of Israel** prepare for him a single "thread of loving-kindness" to be drawn from all of them, to arrange him between the upper and lower worlds. Rabbi Judah said: I heard that Rabbi Isaac said, this is the meaning of the verse: "The beast of the forest wraps itself," it seeks from me the secret of the wrapping. Come and see: as you said, in the error of the law at midnight, he extends himself in the Torah. When the day shines, Abraham awakens in the commerce of the night, as it is written: "From the morning until the blessing of the Master," etc. And the Holy One, Blessed be He and the Community of Israel prepare him and act for him as every day. Then the holiness arranges the light of the wrapping, and they spoke of its laws—Heaven forbid—and specifically Heaven forbid for Abraham, as it is written: "The voice of the Great Shofar," etc. This is the Holy One, Blessed be He; "the" is the Community of Israel, and he did not speak of God. And thus they act for him outside the cup and prepare him as every day. And in this manner it is written: "wraps" when the day shines, Israel at the fifth hour of the day, and thus he speaks, and it is all one matter.

**Or** if his sin which he has committed is made known to him. Rabbi Judah opened and said:
> **"Or if his sin which he has committed is made known to him..."** (Leviticus 4:23)

It provokes him: what is "is made known to him"? Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, commanded the Community of Israel to make known to a person that debt of the sin he committed. And once it is made known to him, then all of them come to protect the sin of his iniquity, and they stand up for him. "Is made known to him" implies it was commanded to another <note>i.e., the Shekhinah informs the sinner</note>. For we have learned: in the error of the male, when he sins before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and does not look into the sin to be purified through **repentance** <note>original: *tiyuvta*</note> before his Master, his sins follow after him. When his soul ascends and testifies before the Holy One, Blessed be He, then the King commands the Community of Israel and says: "Go, make known to him his sin which he has committed"—a sin that he is capable of overcoming—and make known to him his debt. Then, "Make known to Jerusalem her abominations." After they reach him, it purifies him and his spirit is awakened to arrange himself in repentance before his Master. He humbles himself and brings an offering... even if he sinned and was covered in filth and did not gaze upon it, the King desires to accept him and commands to make known to him that debt so that he will not be forgotten by his Master. Rabbi Yose said: This is the voice, and I derive from here that since he committed that act with Bathsheba, He did not look at him <note>with favor</note>. Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, sent to make known to him the debt; I have remembered you immediately. What is written? "Thus says the Lord: You are the man." <note>referring to the prophet Nathan rebuking King David</note>. He came to the place where he did not remember him, to the place where he made it known to him, and how much was made known to him through the spirit of prophecy! So too here, the Holy One, Blessed be He, says: "Let it be made known to him his sin which he has committed," and the matter is well-explained. And so it is, for it is not written "or it became known to him" <note>passive</note>, as it is written "or it became known that the ox was a gorer." Rather, for one who rises at night to labor in the Torah, another <note>the Shekhinah</note> makes known to him his sins. And not in a harsh way, but like a mother who makes known to a person in a soft manner, and he speaks and does not sin further, and returns in repentance before his Master. And if you say: David, who arose at midnight, was he not awakened by the spirit of wisdom? David, who committed that act, was he not purified? And just as he committed it, he was judged. It was a sin against the Holy Kingdom and against the Holy Jerusalem below; from Jerusalem and the Kingdom he was cast out until he was restored.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on the Torah portion Emor (Leviticus). The previous page likely discussed themes of divine judgment and the rectification of the soul. ## Main Text (Zohar)

->Leviticus 24<-

...that they were prepared as is fitting and wrapped. Rabbi Yehuda said: What is the meaning of that which was said, that He [God] acted against David by means of his son, as it is written: *Behold, I will raise up evil against you from your own house* <note>2 Samuel 12:11</note>? Rabbi Yose said: We have established it thus: so that no one would rise against him when he sinned greatly, He would not have mercy on him. He said: And all wisdom sought to kill his enemies with many afflictions of man upon him. He said: I have not heard this. He said: This is what I heard: David sinned with Bathsheba <note>The original text uses "plainly" or "without specification"</note>, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: Let a son come who is not a "strange god" <note>original: *el nechar*</note> and exact punishment and words, and this is the wisdom of what is written: *and the worm breathed shame from within her.* From here we learn: whoever is nullified below, this is within her, and he dies in the end; from her issues a *stubborn and rebellious son* <note>Deuteronomy 21:18</note>. Because until now the filth <note>original: *zuhama*, referring to spiritual impurity</note> had not ceased from her, as they have established.

Rabbi Yose opened and said: *With the rod of the Lord in its kind, and with the arm of strength...* they established it. For every Torah scholar, whenever a man sins before the Holy One, blessed be He, there is a level <term>darga: a spiritual degree or rank</term> that is known above corresponding to him, and it says: "Extend [the rod] to judge this man," and to look (here: and to look) upon him. If he returns in complete repentance before his Master, the debt is delayed, and anger does not rule over him and does not cause him to sin. If he does not return to his place, which is the extension of thieves, that level adds to the sin against another level, and they go toward him to look at the first judgment. Then he requires greater repentance. And if he does not return, level is added upon level until the levels are lowered. Once the "Right Side" <note>The side of Mercy/Chesed</note> is prepared toward him to look upon him, Samael <note>The figure representing the Accuser or the "Left Side"</note> is ready to strike at the Right and to be included within it. Once Samael looks at the Right, then it no longer depends on repentance, as they have established. And then all are found against him in judgment, and anger rests upon him.

And when their judgment is to hang him and spread over the man, then to fulfill and prepare the five fingers like the five ready in Samael to strike him, for they are all found against him like that night, and his hand is crowned to strike him. The whole matter depends on the intention of the man; if he does not intend it, it is written: *Your right hand, O Lord, is glorious in power; Your right hand, O Lord, shatters the enemy* <note>Exodus 15:6</note>—to include Samael in the Right so that judgment is not revealed, and then it is the preservation of all. And therefore, when the Voice sought to preserve all, it is written: *With the rod of the Lord in its kind and with the arm of strength etc.*

Rabbi Yehuda opened: It is written, *The fruit of a beautiful tree, branches of palm trees* <note>Leviticus 23:40, referring to the Etrog and Lulav</note>. *The fruit of a beautiful tree*—who possesses this? The Etrog <note>The citron fruit</note>. And as for the Etrog, who is "beautiful" <note>original: *hadar*</note>? The Voice, and in it are many thorns surrounding it from all sides, yet it possesses the *fruit of a beautiful tree*. He said: The secret of the matter is as it is written: *And the Lord God acquired...* He took Kindness <term>Chesed</term> from Kindness for Kindness, and built the Kindness. And it is written: *A branch from its branches and flesh from its flesh*, and this is the Voice, the *fruit of a beautiful tree*. From here it is said: it is called "Tree," as it is written: *For man is a tree of the field* <note>Deuteronomy 20:19</note>. *Branches of palm trees* <note>original: *kappot temarim*</note>—which rises to seventy years, and in it seventy years are to be included. And this is Wisdom, and it shall be tied above and below. And therefore it is called *Kappot* <note>meaning "bound" or "palms"</note>, for the Bride <note>The Shekhinah</note> is like our palms which are gathered here and there... for all that is in Heaven and Earth.

Rabbi Yose was precise in saying: *The fruit of a beautiful tree*—this is a vision to pass the *Prosbul* <note>A legal mechanism, here used mystically</note> prepared for all sides. For what reason? Because all faces look to it for a portion and to be surrounded by all of them. What is it speaking of? Because whoever reaches the Altar <term>Mizbe'ach</term> with all sins, for which his soul was to be killed, the binding <note>original: *kefit*</note> is above, and therefore this is to be tied to that. *The fruit of a beautiful tree, branches of palm trees*—is it not written *and* branches of palm trees? It is written, and it does not imply Aaron, but implies the sons. Here it speaks of the space, and not the poverty of the Altar which is strengthened, and not the lack, as it is written: *And he shall desolated the Altar of burnt offering and all its vessels.* And this "desolation" is like that which is divided to be used, to be softened, to be surrounded, and to be included. The Priest covers the Altar at this time every day, and seven times after. Here it speaks of the space for the King who invites guests <term>ushpizin</term> and busies himself with them. And the King has a precious daughter; the Master of the King praises him because of the guests, not to look upon her. He said immediately: The precious daughter, before she ascends to you every day, who dwells in weariness...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Vayikra (And He Called)**<-

Thus, every single day, Israel sanctifies the Master of the world. The Altar said to the Holy King <note>The Altar is personified here as a feminine aspect of the Divine, the Shekhinah</note> that for all of them, new portions are found, and so on. Just as on the Sabbath and Festivals, etc. He said to her: Thus every single day, I intend for you seven times for blessing, and for you, seven portions are added every day. Rabbi Yose said: Seventy portions every day, corresponding to the seventy bulls that are offered on the Festival <note>The 70 bulls offered during Sukkot, traditionally representing the 70 nations of the world</note>. Rabbi Yehuda said: Seven every day, because she is blessed from the place where all are found, and eventually she is blessed seven times from the place where the spirit is found. And after seven times, corresponding to all those seven times, in order to establish for her the blessing from the source of the stream <note>original: "mabua de-nachla"</note> that flows constantly and never ceases. It is found that she is blessed constantly every single day seventy times, being blessed from the source of the stream. And so at another time, seven times as we said, and the blessings are established afterward from the supernal place of the source that emerges and does not cease, as we have said. Every day it is proclaimed concerning her: "Until the barren has borne seven, and she who has many children is forlorn" <note>1 Samuel 2:5</note>. "Until the barren has borne seven"—this is the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah</note> who is blessed by seven every day, and the calculation rises upon her. "And she who has many children is forlorn"—these are the idolatrous nations who initially rise to a great number in their buildings, but afterward they diminish and pass away every single day. And the Altar makes atonement for the sins of Israel; the Altar remembers them and distributes blessings to them from above to below. "The branch of a thick tree" <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>—this is the Holy King who takes hold of two sides, and therefore the Myrtle has three branches, becoming the "branch of a thick tree" that takes hold of every side. "Willows of the brook"—these are the two supports from which all emerge to the "branches of palm trees." The "branches of palm trees" <note>The Lulav</note> take hold above and take hold below. And of it, it is said: "two palms" <note>original: "kaf," meaning palm or spoon</note>, they bring joy to people. So it is with the branch of the palm tree; it also takes hold of them, and for all that emerges from the world, it is a "palm," and from here they come. Rabbi Yose opened: "And her sister to the Altar..." <unclear>illegible</unclear>. What is the Altar of God? This is the Altar above, the Altar of God, and this is the Mountain of Isaac. And your dwelling is the Altar <note>original: "mizbe'ach"</note>, the sum of 160 <note>Gematria/numerical value of Mizbe'ach: Mem(40)+Zayin(7)+Bet(2)+Het(8) = 57; the text likely refers to a different mystical calculation</note> before the Altar of the Lord, and they shall inherit the worlds from here...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the soul's ascent. It follows the previous discussion regarding the hierarchy of the soul and its purification. The text is primarily in Aramaic, the language of the Zohar, which I have translated into English while preserving the original structure.</meta>

## Leviticus

[Line 1] ...the body, and the Spirit <term>Ruach: the middle level of the soul associated with emotion and moral movement</term> is to the Soul <term>Neshamah: the highest level of the soul, the divine spark of intellect</term>, and the Soul is to the Holy One, Blessed be He. And all of them ascend; whoever is worthy inherits this inheritance. Woe
[Line 2] to those who assist their souls <note>original: "nefashon," the lowest level of the soul</note> to be unworthy in this world, and certainly in the world to come. Concerning them it is written:
[Line 3] *And the soul of your enemies He shall sling out as from the hollow of a sling* <note>1 Samuel 25:29</note>. They wander through the world and find no place
[Line 4] to be gathered into, and they are found among the "sides of impurity" <note>the Sitra Achra or demonic realms</note>. And this is the secret of what is said: *If a soul commits a trespass*
[Line 5] *against the Lord* <note>Leviticus 5:15</note>. From the sanctuary of the Lord, which is holiness, it does not enter and is not included; and these are the "damagers of the world" <note>destructive spirits</note> because
[Line 6] they cleave to them and are defiled. Rabbi Isaac said: We have established that when the soul is crowned in the holy
[Line 7] King, it is crowned and called the "Bundle of Life" <note>Tzeror ha-Chayim</note> because there everything is bound together. Rabbi Eleazar said: Happy is the soul
[Line 8] when it is crowned with wisdom. Come and see: *And the angel of God, which went before...* <note>Exodus 14:19</note>. Rabbi Abba said: Everything
[Line 9] is made into one crown, because it is crowned with peace. And that which is holy was not seen among them <insert>at that time</insert>
[Line 10] at that hour. It is written: *As an apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons* <note>Song of Songs 2:3</note>. And they were like those of Israel; the radiance
[Line 11] of the supernal glory moved before them. And this is what is written: *And He made you ride on the high places of the earth, that you might eat the increase of the fields* <note>Deuteronomy 32:13</note>.
[Line 12] And because of this, it says: *Behold, He comes leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills* <note>Song of Songs 2:8</note>, and there is no one but the good. And happy is
[Line 13] the portion of Israel. Come and see: A person brings a sacrifice to heal <note>or "to the Lord"</note>, and there it says: *If any man of you brings an offering...* <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. Why does it say "of you"? To exclude from
[Line 14] Heaven any "evil side" <note>impure force</note>. And an evil person who brings a sacrifice—it is not so. For it says: If he does not desire to draw near to the Lord,
[Line 15] but an "unclean spirit" passes over him or he occupies himself with it, then his sacrifice is in that "shell" <term>Kelipah: a mystical 'husk' or 'shell' that conceals the divine light</term> which
[Line 16] they see in him. And it says: We have learned that whoever is worthy of the *Neshamah* <note>the highest soul</note>, he is worthy of the awakening
[Line 17] of the Spirit <note>Ruach</note>. Whoever is not worthy has only the *Nefesh* <note>the lowest soul</note>. Woe to him who is not worthy of more and does not strive more, for he remains attached
[Line 18] to that "unclean side." And all those evil sides come and attach themselves to him and inform
[Line 19] him in dreams of worldly matters—some are lies and some are truth. And sometimes they mock him and show him
[Line 20] false things and distress him in his dreams. And regarding this, we have learned that most of what they see in their dreams are false things,
[Line 21] because of that "side" they are attached to. And all their words are close to being lies. Come and see: In visions and evil spirits there are
[Line 22] six levels, one above the other. The highest level of them is like that which hangs in the air. The lowest level of them are those
[Line 23] who mock human beings and distress them in their dreams, because they are all mockers. And there is a higher level
[Line 24] over them, who are the "masters of wailing" <note>spirits of lamentation</note>, and they inform him of things—some are lies and some
[Line 25] are truth. And those words of truth are all close at hand. And there is a level of those who hang in the white light <note>or "purity"</note>,
[Line 26] who are more exalted. And he who is not worthy of more than the *Nefesh*, that *Nefesh* must strengthen itself
[Line 27] to receive the Spirit <note>Ruach</note>. Until that Spirit comes to him, it goes out from that *Nefesh* and spreads through the world, and seeks
[Line 28] to ascend, but it cannot until it meets those "messengers." And they inform him of things— some near
[Line 29] and some further away. And that level returns and is not bound in his dreams until he acquires the Spirit <note>Ruach</note>. When he acquires
[Line 30] the Spirit, that Spirit goes out, breaking through mountains and hills, ascending and spreading, and wanders among the angels of the
[Line 31] holy world. And there it knows what it knows, and gathers words, and returns to its place. Then he is bound to everything
[Line 32] in holiness, until he is worthy of the *Neshamah*. And when he has acquired the *Neshamah*, she ascends to the Upper World, and the gatekeepers
[Line 33] open for her; they do not hinder her. And she returns and spreads among those sparks that are included in the "Bundle of Life."
[Line 34] And there she sees the delight of the King and is nourished by the supernal radiance. And when the holy soul <note>Neshamah</note> awakens in the body,
[Line 35] it is as if she is in a dream. And she has acquired this, and she passes through a strong wind in the white light until she reaches the place
[Line 36] and returns. In that holy soul, she stands before the King to receive a "thread of grace" <note>Chut shel Chesed</note> and life.

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> Leviticus <-

This is the "String of Abraham" <note>original: *chuta d'Avraham*; a mystical reference to Abraham's merit or a specific spiritual lineage</note> which stands before Him, as it is written: *Your eye shall not pity* <note>Deuteronomy 19:13</note>. He took a "good eye" <note>generosity/spiritual clarity</note> so as not to benefit from the [impure] side at all. The sign of this is "pity" from "sparing" <note>a wordplay on the Hebrew roots *chus* and *machos*</note>, and so it is regarding the "string." This is called the "String of Abraham," and all who hold fast to the truth are strengthened. Then the people are crowned before the King. David spoke of gathering over the "dough-offering of the bread" <note>original: *challat ha-pat*</note>; this refers to the Assembly of Israel. The "dough-offering of the bread" is the song of the Assembly of Israel which they sing in exile: *My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?* etc. <note>Psalm 22:2</note>.

Rabbi Shimon said: Blessed are the masters of the soul, the masters of **freedom** <note>original: *cheruta*</note>, through the service of the Holy King. Woe to those guilty ones who do not merit to cleave to their Master and do not merit freedom. For anyone who does not merit freedom does not merit either the spirit <note>Ruach</note> or the soul <note>Neshamah</note>. Their attachment is to that side of "evil sales" <note>metaphor for the forces of impurity</note>, and the sign is that he has no portion in the Holy King, no portion in holiness. Woe to him when he departs from this world, for he is recognized by those "evil sales," the masters of insolence, strong as dogs, who strip the male... who have no mercy upon them.

Come and see the difference between Israel and the idol-worshipping nations: Even if an Israelite has not merited [perfection], when he humbles his soul <note>literally "slaughters the vinegar/sourness in the soul"</note> through a difficult level, he seeks to acquire a spirit, and through labor he seeks to acquire a soul. But the idol-worshipping nations never acquire the spirits of the "furnace," for they acquire a soul under many other [impure] sides. And the side that stands at a higher level—it is alive, yet he does not seek to merit more, and his deeds are many. Woe to that guilty one who violates the **commandments of freedom** and does not strive for freedom to merit his Master. Concerning him it is written: *Let sinners be consumed from the earth* <note>Psalm 104:35</note>.

And come and see how many cups <note>or "coverings"</note> are attached to this side because of that soul that did not merit more. And when that spirit of impurity passes over them, they are diminished and cleave to it. Then, if a man swerves toward the side of sin, it is from the side of that spirit of impurity. His sacrifice is a sacrifice that does not [ascend?], because it is the "beast" that sinned from side to side to atone for his guilt.

Rabbi Elazar said to him: It is blessed! It is written: *His body shall not remain overnight upon the tree... that you do not defile your land* <note>Deuteronomy 21:23</note>, because the land is holy. And the "bride" of the Master of Violence <note>a cryptic reference to the forces of judgment</note> is not found like the Holy Land. And this is the power: since it is the "beast" that sinned, the spirit of impurity enters and sins from the side... they bring it near to the side of Holiness.

To every wise student, it is written: *For the Lord your God is a consuming fire* <note>Deuteronomy 4:24</note>. There is a fire for every fire. The fire of the Holy One, blessed be He, [consumes] all other fire. And come and see the angels who say song before the Holy One, blessed be He; they are nullified when they stand in that song in the sorrow that comes to all. Below, the Holy One, blessed be He, prepared the fire of the altar, and that fire consumes and destroys that entire [impure] side. That side is nullified through that service of the sin-offering, and nothing of it remains in the world. And that man who brings his sacrifice stands over it, and through that ascending aroma, the side of the spirit of impurity that rested upon him is removed from him, and he is atoned for through repentance. Thus everything is nullified and increased, and there is no one who approaches the consuming fire.

Rabbi Isaac was walking on the road, and Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose met as one. Rabbi Isaac came and pushed/rejoiced <note>unclear reading</note> three times to receive the face of the **Divine Presence** <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note>. They joined together and walked. He said: Let each and every one of us say a word of the holiness of the Torah as we go.

Rabbi Hiyya opened and said: *Drop down, O heavens, from above* <note>Isaiah 45:8</note>. This verse is the spirit of wisdom that we learned from the Holy Assembly. *Drop down, O heavens, from above*—if they all dropped down, they would meet like the rain of my teaching. And concerning the side of the rain of that "doorpost" <note>mezuzah</note> of all, it is said: and because of this, all the eyes of the world look from here to the Holy One, blessed be He, because He is the sustenance of all. And furthermore, you might say that after this, which is called "Heavens," the matter depends [on merit]. But we have learned that the matter does not depend on merit <note>original: *zekhuta*</note>. And "merit"—they have established it as the Targum translates it: "righteousness" and "merit" and "heavens" are one thing. And here it says *Drop down, O heavens*. And if you say it depends on it, it is written *from above*. "From above" certainly means it comes from the **Holy Ancient One** <note>original: *Atika Kadisha*; the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note>.

## Main Text (Zohar) - End of Parashat Vayikra

They are nourished and fed from that place called "the heavens" and "righteousness," and this is precisely the "shoe" <note>The "shoe" is a kabbalistic metaphor for the lowest level of the divine world that touches the physical realm.</note>. And in the place where they flow like fine dust, for when the heavens bestow upon the "shoe" from that supernal place that surrounds it, then the skies pour down like fine dust. What are the "skies"? The place where they grind manna for the righteous. And who are they? *Netzach* and *Hod* <note>Victory and Splendor: the two divine emanations associated with prophecy and the "grinding" of divine energy into digestible forms.</note>, and they certainly grind manna for the righteous. For that place called "the Righteous One" <term>Tzadik: the foundation or Yesod</term>, they grind for him that manna which comes from above. All that goodness is gathered in their vessels to be given to the level of the Righteous One so that he may be blessed by all of them. Therefore, they grind manna for the "righteous ones." Who are these "righteous ones"? This refers to *Tzadik* and *Tzedek* <note>Righteousness and Justice</note>, Joseph and Rachel <note>Representing the male and female divine principles</note>. When they are joined as one, like fine dust they search and see, certainly grinding manna for the righteous. Regarding this, it is written: *And the skies shall pour down righteousness.* Then *the earth shall open and bring forth salvation* for the sake of the world, and it shall be humbled together. All mercy and all the goodness of the world come from them and their union. When they are found in the world, then joy upon joy is added and all nations are blessed. Rabbi Abba said: "If I had only come to hear this, it would have been enough for me!"

Rabbi Yose opened and said: *"To the governors of Israel, the volunteers among the people, bless the Lord."* Come and see: all the will and all the heart of a person should be directed to pour blessings from above to below, to unify the Holy Name, and to cleave in his thoughts to the Holy One, blessed be He. As it is written: *Out of the depths I have called to You, O Lord.* For there is the depth of all, in the supernal depths which are the beginning of all, and all sustenance follows everything. *To the governors of Israel*—who are the governors of Israel? These are the "engravings of Israel" <note>A wordplay on 'Chokek' (governor/engraver)</note>. These are the governors, the fathers who are the engravers... <unclear>illegible</unclear>... *The volunteers among the people*—these are the righteous who join together. Then the people gather with the princes of the company. Then *bless the Lord* to draw from Him blessings below, so that blessings may be found in the whole world. For when blessings are found here from above, everything is in joy, everything stands in peace. Happy is the portion of Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, pours blessings upon them and redeems their exile. Of them it is written: *He has turned to the prayer of the destitute and has not despised their prayer.*

## Main Text (Zohar)

And they are commanded and the spirit is bound as one, which is hidden, concealed, and secret; and they direct their intention as has been stated. Because of this, the **burnt offering** <note>Hebrew: *Olah*, literally "that which ascends"</note> is **Holy of Holies**. Other sacrifices are brought to make peace in the world from various sides. Those that are destined to be removed and bound through the will of **Wisdom** <note>Aramaic: *Chokhmah*, the second Sefirah</note> are called "lesser holy offerings" because they are not crowned in the highest heights of the Holy of Holies. And because they are lesser holy offerings, they may be slaughtered in any place, as we have established. But the burnt offering is the spirit of the Holy of Holies, which is the essence of the sacrifice of the entire ritual. To what end is it holy? As it is written <note>Leviticus 6:3</note>: **"And the priest shall put on his linen garment."** These are garments designated for holiness when the unification is weighed for the holy. And it is written <note>Leviticus 16:4</note>: **"They are holy garments; therefore shall he wash his flesh in water, and so put them on."** This "garment" <note>original: *mido*</note> is holy; it is the spirit regarding the holy things which are the Holy of Holies, to elevate everything and to be crowned in the Holy of Holies with the **holy incense**. It is chosen before Him, and a spirit passes from the sanctuary to remove all impurity so that it does not deviate or approach the sanctuary, and it shall be removed from every side of holiness so that all may be joined, holiness within holiness, in a single unification. And this is what was stated in the verse <note>Psalms 36:7</note>: **"O Lord, thou preservest man and beast."** Thus the spirit of **man** ascends from the side of the Priest, and because of this it is written <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>: **"When any man of you brings an offering."** "Man" certainly, for this is a sacrifice on high to bind the knot, and afterwards "from the cattle," etc. This is on another level. For the beast, which possesses no [human] spirit, is needed for the sacrifice of "man and beast" as we have said. And come and see: when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He acted thus. And it is a wonder, for it is written <note>Genesis 1:20</note>: **"And let fowl fly above the earth."** For from them, they bring a sacrifice, and the burnt offering is a sin offering, as it is written <note>Leviticus 1:14</note>: **"And if the burnt sacrifice for his offering to the Lord be of fowls."** Come and see: of all those birds, they only offer turtledoves or young pigeons. Rather, this is because there is no defect found in them, so that one shall not sin, and this is the support. And it is all one: "fowl that fly above the earth"—these are the living beings <note>Chayyot/Angels</note> that possess the lower spirit, and through them the Holy Spirit is prepared to be taken up on high. For they are two: one to the right and one to the left. The bird to the right is <term>Michael</term> <note>The archangel of mercy</note>. And the bird to the left is <term>Gabriel</term> <note>The archangel of strength/judgment</note>. This one is to the right and that one is to the left, and because of this, these two are offered to elevate the Holy Spirit. And the support crowns and arms that crown below, which is decided. And the right joins to the right and is bound below in the wing that shows as one. And everything ascends and is bound as one, above and below, and the Holy One, blessed be He, ascends alone and is strengthened. And in the ancient books, the poor man does not give a portion to another, but only to the One on high, to bind everything together on high. Each one is bound to its side as is fitting, and this we have established.

Rabbi Eleazar asked Rabbi Chiya: Since the incense is for everything to be smoked in the Holy of Holies to illuminate, and the cleaving of the will of the Priests, Levites, and Israelites is toward the heights—how far does it ascend? He said to him: We have established it is until the <term>Infinite</term> <note>Hebrew: *Ein Sof*, the unknowable Godhead</note>. For every bond, unification, and perfection is to be hidden in that pure state which cannot be grasped or known, for the "will of all wills" is in His hand. It does not stand as one, nor does it pass the "End," nor does it pass the "Whisper" <note>original: *rachash*, a subtle movement or sound</note>. For the ancients did not produce a whisper or an end. What is the "Whisper"? This is the **Higher Point** <note>Nekuda Ila'ah</note>, which is the secret of all that is hidden, standing within the Thought. And it makes an "End" to be called the "End of all," and after that is the Infinite. There are no wills, no lights, and no lamps in that Infinite. All these lights and lamps depend on them for their existence, but they do not exist to be grasped. Who knows and does not know them? It is only the Higher Will, hidden beyond all hidden things. It and the Higher Point are hidden. When it comes to ascend, none know except the spirit, like a vision of fear, a spirit that is strengthened. And this does not stand, for it is written: "He did not deliver in a spirit of comfort," for the spirit is like heat. The spirit of the will of all these wills, and the prayer, and the will of the incense, and the will of the Priest—all of them are the spirit of one. Then they all become one will, and this is a "pleasing aroma" <note>Hebrew: *Reiach Nichoach*</note>, a "will" as the Targum translates it. Then everything is bound and illuminated as one, as is fitting, as we have said. And because of this, it is a "satisfaction of spirit" <note>Aramaic: *Nachat Ruach*</note> before the Master of all...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Book of Leviticus, specifically the portion of 'Tzav' (Command). It transitions from the general laws of sacrifice to the deeper spiritual mechanics of the Burnt Offering (Olah) and the battle between holy and impure forces.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

"Command Aaron and his sons, saying..." <note>Leviticus 6:2</note>: The secret of this matter, as we have established, is that we have nothing other than the "Tree" <note>referring to the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil</note>, and "This shall be" <note>a reference to the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note>. It is through her that the "evil mixture" <note>the Sitra Achra or 'Other Side'</note> is burned and removed from within the Holy One, Blessed be He, through the will that ascends on high. In this way, she is prepared and purified so that all their thrones <note>the powers of judgment or impurity</note> are removed from before the Holy One, Blessed be He. All the time that they perform the will of the "absolute ones" <note>the forces of impurity</note>, they are unable to rule over them. A voice ascends, and everything is sealed to show the spirit of the King, to crown Him with the Holy Spirit above, and to separate the spirit of impurity from Him, casting it down below. This is according to the will and the completion we mentioned, which is not like a common deed before the Holy One, Blessed be He. A voice ascends and testifies concerning them, as it is written: **"Command Aaron and his sons, saying."** For this "Tree" is the spirit of impurity, "saying"—this refers to the lower realm that they investigate. And "the fear of the Lord" is written here as "saying," and it is written there as "saying." These ascend to Him as his sin-offering, as they have established. Because of this, everything is sealed and all stands to be rectified through the spirit of man and his submission. Blessed is the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come, for they know the paths of the Torah and walk in the path of truth. Concerning them it is written: **"O Lord, by these things men live"** <note>Isaiah 38:16</note>. What is "by these" <note>Hebrew: *aleichem*, literally 'upon you'</note>? These are the paths of the Torah, and through them, they shall exist in this world and the world to come. Come and see, it is written: **"This is the law of the burnt offering."** Rabbi Hiyya said: "The burnt offering" <note>Hebrew: *Olah*, literally 'that which ascends'</note>—we have established this in relation to "This is the law," which is the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>The Shekhinah</note>. "The burnt offering" is that which ascends and is crowned higher and higher to be bound properly until the place called the Holy of Holies. Another explanation: "This is the law"—this is the <term>Assembly of Israel</term>. "The burnt offering"—this is the "evil mixture" that ascends upon the will of a person to lead him astray from the path of truth. And this "burnt offering" which ascends and causes a person to deviate must be burned in fire so that it is not given a place to lead astray. Because of this: **"on its firewood on the altar all night."** What is "night"? This is the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> who comes to purify a person from that [evil] will. "On its firewood"—because in that place, all those who do not maintain their existence are burned, for they are brought into that flaming fire and their dominion is removed from the world. And so that this "side" <note>the side of impurity</note> shall not rule, it is "on the firewood on the altar all night," and it is suppressed and does not rule. Therefore, when this side is suppressed, the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> ascends to establish the Holy Spirit that ascends and is crowned above. For her ascent occurs when this "other power" is suppressed and separated from her. Because of this, we require the spirit of the sacrifice to separate this side from the Holy Spirit and to give it its portion, so that the Holy Spirit may ascend on high.

## Main Text (Zohar)

**[Right Column]**

Come and see: The Holy One, blessed be He, sent a spirit <margin>4th L.</margin> of impurity, and they are invited to recognize the sacrifices below from the side of the "Other Side" <note>Sitra Achra, the realm of evil</note>. It sought to draw near to the altar like a female, yet that spirit of impurity was neither changed nor nullified. Thus, a companion, etc. And so, from that lower side, it leaves; likewise, all those on the altar, from that fat <note>Hebrew: Chelev, the sacrificial fat offered to God</note>, the spirit of impurity is consumed, and the wicked of the world are purified. The Priest then intends to arrange the fat so that the wicked of the world are consumed. Therefore, they desired that they should never be known, and the matter should not be seen. The rectification of the coupling is to break the power of the Serpent, for the evil fat is removed from the world. Regarding this, it is written, "It shall not go out" <note>Leviticus 6:6, referring to the altar fire</note>, and the Priest shall arrange the fat upon it "morning by morning" <note>Leviticus 6:5</note>, in the manner that the side of the coupling rises and is awakened in the world, like a soul to the world. Then the judgments are subdued and are not awakened in the world. Concerning this, we have learned: Life is fat, fat, fat, fat from above; fat, fat, fat, fat of the altar; fat, fat, fat. Therefore, the fat shall not be extinguished forever, and the Priest arranges it as is fitting for it.

**[Left Column]**

Time, each kind to its kind. The Torah is the milk <note>Hebrew: Chalav, a play on Chelev/Fat</note> of the Bride, and she eats for the living. And those who flow are the unleavened bread of the Torah for life, like one who is dry and becomes saturated with whiteness, like one who is supple. And this milk then eats for the living and those who flow. Furthermore, it eats to melt all the sacrifices that were offered in the exile on account of the Ten <note>The Ten Commandments</note>, and all the sacrifices offered in exile suckle on account of the "Prohibitions" <note>Negative commandments</note>. And with this milk, the prey is stoned like the fear of Isaac on account of the Prohibitions. The sacrifices of the support of the exile are sweetened by the commandments of the Ten and the Prohibitions. Corresponding to the five [fingers] of the mistress, these were established in the secret of the exile in the days of the rains; and corresponding to the crown, they will be the days of wandering, sixty corresponding to the generation of the Lord, five matters corresponding to the secret of the Crown <note>Keter</note>.

-> **The Commandment** <-
<note>Raya Mehemna section marker: The Faithful Shepherd (Moses) speaks</note>

After this, to perform the leavened vengeance, the scale of the waters and the traditions. For we have learned that the business of the holy burnt offering is a rectification for its side, to greatly seek out His daughter, so that she may be the Law <note>Halakha</note>. These are the husks <note>Kelipot</note> of the Mixed Multitude <note>Erev Rav</note>, which are difficult and evil; they have no resolution and no redemption. Concerning them, it is said:
> That which is crooked cannot be made straight, and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.
<note>Ecclesiastes 1:15</note>
It is said of the void: "Teyku" <note>A Talmudic term for an unresolved legal problem</note>. Let them stand in their "Teyku," and every "Teyku" that is for stringency shall be for stringency. They shall be established as a deficiency, for there is no rectification for the deficiency once the world below has been spared. For a "Teyku" is an ornament from below, a "Teika" <note>A case or sheath</note>, as if to say: a rectification. Thus it rose in the Thought.

## Commentary / Raya Mehemna Continuation

And these difficulties are like heat to the evils of the Law <note>Halakha</note>, which are called "poverty." And this is the secret of the matter:
> The King’s daughter is all glorious within; her clothing is of wrought gold.
<note>Psalms 45:14</note>
And you cut them into many sections and resolve them with many solutions. And if a horse is missing, a section from your time, as we have established, is missing from the molten image. **A fire** shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out. Rabbi Hiyya opened: "And a fire said to its companion, 'Smite me, wound me'" <note>Song of Songs 5:7</note>. -> "Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven" <note>Genesis 1:14</note> <-

"And he said" Edom and a line of the firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide between water and water.

...with severity. The worlds are established upon them. For example, the "Ox" has its yoke, and the "Donkey" has its burden. During the weekdays, the worlds are established, and the children of man have the labor of occupying themselves with the Torah and the commandments; they have the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven to signify the letter *He* <note>ה</note> in the "Expansion of the Kingdom of Heaven," which is called the "Yoke of the Commandment." He gives the "Additional Soul" <note>Neshama Yeterah</note> upon the letter *He* in the Kingdom of Heaven, and it is a commandment upon the Tablets.

For the children of the "Egyptians" and "Pharaoh," it is pressed upon them against their will. Regarding the Egyptians, it is taught that they have a burden, as it is said of the Egyptians that they are "dark and blackened." We have learned in our Mishnah <note>The Zohar often refers to its own esoteric teachings as "our Mishnah"</note> that all spiritual hearings are heard through the word *Skhanz* <note>original: סכנז. On **Festivals** <note>Yom Tov</note> they have no dominion of their own, for they are like the King's servants who act as secular vessels for themselves in this world and the world to come, to branch them out with all kinds of food and drink and to honor them with beautiful garments, in the manner of the Sabbath where it is stirred: "Honor it with clean clothing." Whatever a person does for the Sabbath and Festivals should not be done for those [forces], for one who profanes them is liable for stoning. So too, one who makes personal use of the "Crown" <note>the Torah</note> passes away. This applies to one who uses the one who has completed the Laws to fix his own Torah, and certainly one who despises him—it is as if he despises the **Divine Presence**, the Festivals, and the appointed times. Those who carry their sacks: anyone who despises the Festivals is as if he denies the Essence. Just as all the Kings of the Holy Temple were called "Holy," so all those who serve the Disciples of the Sages shall be called "Holy." And the disciples of the Rav, who correspond to the "Sages of the Bodies," shall be called "Holy of Holies."

And the spirit that goes takes their secrets and divides the **Veil** for you between the Holy and the Holy of Holies. My arrangement and your arrangement need to bring a holy sacrifice every night, to take upon oneself the **Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven**. This is the acceptance of the suffering of poverty below, to cleanse the sin of the "body of the beasts" <note>the animal soul</note> which feeds its portion, for a pairing of the beastly, the spirit, and the soul of "dogs" is prepared. The Priest, the Levite, and the Israelite: the Priest is **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note>, the Levite is the **Levite** <note>Understanding/Binah</note>, and the Israelite is **Knowledge** <note>Da'at</note>. This is the letter *Vav*. The "bosom" is the extra *Samekh* of your Crown... as it is written:
> This is the law of a human <note>Numbers 19:14</note>
And this includes the symbol of the Explicit Name: *Yod-He-Vav-He*. The voice of the "bosom" is the portion that feeds the strength in its four wings. The merit of the "beasts" is in the meal, the wine, and the arrangement of the skins of the fruits. "God has made one opposite the other" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14</note>. Therefore, every person at night is a sacrifice of atonement and spirit, like the taste of the "beasts" before the seven, and the burning of the fat... the sacrifice is holy to the Lord to remove the "dog" and the "donkey" from before the Holy. He distresses his spirit to bring it out from the veins of the heart, like the secret of **Remember** and the slaughtering and the message that were guarded before the Caesar... This is the Sabbath. Three things cause death: the gall, the jaundice, and the blackness <note>the three humors/husks</note>, which are like the liver, the gall, and the spleen. These are the three "husks" of the damager. First, one should prepare the altar for the "lambs" and intend to remove the "dust" of the "gall" that rules the wings of the lungs. These are the "Kingdom of Fears," the "beasts" are appeased there... and they shall be food, for the beasts and the clean birds are to be brought near to the Lord to smell the heavens upon them. Through this, the "lower rungs" will be sustained... and they shall be as chariots to ride upon, as it says: "That You ride upon Your horses, Your chariots of salvation."

Come and see <note>Aramaic: Ta Chazi</note>: the "bosom" is the weight of all the beginnings of the Torah. Thus one must intend to remove the "bones" from the portion of the "beast" and the "fat" for the body. One must remove the bones for all the people of the world... A person should always see himself as if he is entirely without a garment... and intend in his spirit to make sacrifices for all the people of the world. And the poor man who has a good thought... the Lord shall save. The small ones are like the "thin ones" and the "salted ones" for the Prophet... all of them in the voice of the Faithful Shepherd <note>Moses</note>... to do all this to merit the "stoning" of all Israel. May the Holy One, Blessed be He, forgive you in His mercy. Until here.

**This**—The Rabbis taught:
> This is the law of the burnt offering <note>Leviticus 6:2</note>
Rabbi Hiyya said: The masters of the treasury established this verse. "**This is the law**" refers to the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Knesset Yisrael/Malchut</note>. "**The burnt offering**" <note>Olah - literally "that which ascends"</note> refers to that which ascends in thought to appease the Will, to provide the satisfaction of the human will so that the **King of Truth** <note>God</note> will be reconciled with him. It stands in the world; a voice, a voice that ascends to the King... it is better for a person to honor Him in everything.

Just as it is, so that its purity shall not be increased for entry; and because of this, it shall remain **on the hearth upon the altar all night** <note>Leviticus 6:2</note>. Who is this? And so to the four sides, to the four watches, and they are all covered at the time the Priest ascends the Altar.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Command Aaron<-

Through which the inner and thin incense is brought near. This is the bond of faith as one, for through it, everything is bound together—this incense with the incense of faith. This is called the **Golden Altar**, and from here the bond of faith is smoked and tied into a single knot. And there is one altar that is outside <note>The Outer Altar</note> and it is called the **Bronze Altar**. This one is on the outside <insert>another version: to bring blessing to the world</insert>, and Michael the Great Prince offers upon it a sacrifice of pleasing aroma to the Holy One, blessed be He. The **Golden Altar** <term>Mizbeach ha-Zahav: The inner altar used for incense, representing the hidden, spiritual realms</term> and the **Bronze Altar** act as one incense, and all are kings and rulers. Regarding this it is written:
> Oil and incense rejoice the heart (Proverbs 27:9) 

And it is not written that "oil, galbanum, and rulers" rejoice. For even though there is a sweetening of anger and judgment in them at all times, the incense is the joy of them all and does not come from the side of anger and judgment. This is the inner altar of compassion and the incense <insert>another version: for they are the inner aspect of the incense</insert> which is thin and pure, the bond of faith. It is called the "still small voice" <note>referencing Elijah's revelation in 1 Kings 19:12</note> because of the pressing of the inner altar which is tied in the bond of faith. The altar that is outside is called the **Bronze Altar** <term>Mizbeach ha-Chitzon: The outer altar used for animal sacrifices, representing the physical world and the rectification of lower forces</term>. And the inner one is called the "Altar of the Lord." The place for offering on the Bronze Altar—the whole Bronze Altar which was before the Lord was "too small to contain" etc. (1 Kings 8:64). Rabbi Yose said: from here we see it is included upon "Your altar" (plural), yet it is written "upon My altar (singular) for acceptance" (Isaiah 60:7). Rabbi Abba said it is written:
> And Moses built an altar and called its name 'The Lord is my Miracle' (Exodus 17:15)

This corresponds to that inner aspect, the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah</note>, and therefore it is called "The Lord is my Miracle" <note>Hebrew: Adonai Nissi</note> because the letter *Nun* <note>the first letter of Nissi/Miracle</note> stands to remove the writing of Amalek below, for this holy hint subdues it. For this altar stands to humble the "Strong One" who is the "shackle" below. Therefore, it is called "a sword that executes the vengeance of the covenant," and this is to strengthen Israel through a holy hint. And the Staff <note>of Moses</note> corresponds to this altar and is called "The Lord is my Miracle." This is the inner altar, the still small voice. And regarding this: "A permanent fire shall burn on the altar... it shall not go out" (Leviticus 6:6). It is constant, and the fire of Isaac <note>representing the attribute of Gevurah/Judgment</note> strikes it. Then it is heard as pure. When the Priest arranges the fragrance upon it with the Name, we call it by the Name of Mercy <note>YHVH</note>, and sometimes we call it by the Name of "No" <note>referring to the hidden aspect</note>, and sometimes it stands in joy. Rabbi Shimon said: There were two, and the inner one stands over the outer one, and from it, the outer one is illuminated; this is the secret of the sacrifice for Aaron.

Rabbi Hezekiah opened:
> The Lord is righteous in all His ways and pious in all His works (Psalms 145:17)

**This** means "The Lord is righteous in all His ways." We have learned how much human beings must look into the glory of their Master and not stray from their paths to the outside. For at all times and every day, **Judgment** <term>Dina: The divine attribute of justice and law</term> hangs over the world, because the world was created and stands upon judgment. Therefore, people must guard themselves from their sins, for one does not know when the time of judgment will rest upon them. If he sits in his house, judgment rests upon him; if he goes out of his house to the street, judgment rests upon him, and he does not know if he will return to his house or not. He bows to the path before you, for then judgment goes out before that **Righteous One** <term>Tzadik: The foundation of the world, often referring to the sephira of Yesod</term> who commands him to go. Because of this, one must precede with a plea for Mercy before the King, so that he may be saved from the side of judgment that dwells in the world. For every single day, judgment dwells in the world, as it says: "God is indignant every day" (Psalms 7:12). Now it must be said: we have learned "And God is *not* indignant every day"—how can this be? Everything follows Kindness <note>Chesed</note>, as it says "The Great God," and this is the light of the supernal **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah: The first flash of divine intellect</term>. And it is said "And God is indignant every day" surrounding the verse "at all times," and "pious" in this—if so, the words do not stand! Furthermore, it is written "The Great, Mighty God"—Kindness <note>Chesed</note> is linked to Him, Judgment <note>Din</note> is not linked to Him, only **Mercy** <term>Rachamim: The balance between kindness and judgment</term>. Rather, this is what I heard: the equivalence of turning Mercy into Judgment. For you have no crowns among the supernal crowns of the Holy King that are not all tied together as one. Therefore, the "Living Creatures" <note>the Chayyot of the Chariot</note> turn Mercy into Judgment. Rabbi Yehuda said to him: It is well explained by that which is written "Mighty God" and "God is indignant every day." What does this mean? That every single day He stands [in judgment], whether the people of the world are meritorious or not. It was not in his power to be profaned. To this he said to them: Certainly "God is indignant every day," and the colleagues established that sometimes there is Judgment and sometimes there is Mercy.

Mercy is his. Worthy are the children of the world, for the world could not stand, nor could it endure, nor would it be honored by judgment. And the portion of this God awakened in the world—the world could not endure even a single hour before the powerful judgments that awaken in the world every day. Because of this, the Priest completes the offering and brings the union near, and all is their portion in this world and the world to come.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Command Aaron**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, Leviticus 6:1</note>

And to be holy, etc. One who sanctifies himself from below <note>term: *it'aruta de-leta'ta* — the concept that human initiative on earth triggers a corresponding divine response</note> is sanctified from above. One who sanctifies himself from below is granted additional holiness from above. This holiness, which he is obligated to seek, rests upon him. Conversely, for one who defiles himself, the impulse comes from above <unclear>to match his intent</unclear>... his thoughts dwell above. Rabbi Hiyya said: This is what we have learned: according to the action below, an action is aroused above. If the action is one of holiness, it arouses holiness above, which then comes and rests upon him, and he is sanctified by it. But if he intends to be defiled below, he arouses a spirit of impurity <note>original: *ruach mesachvuta*</note> from above, which comes and rests upon him, and he is defiled by it; for the matter depends entirely upon the action. For you have nothing—good or evil, holiness or impurity—that does not have a root and a source above. And according to the action below, the action above is aroused.

What we have learned regarding action: as the action is below, so it is aroused above and an act is performed. And what we have learned regarding words: as the words are below, so it is aroused above. And if you say a word <note>a prayer or incantation</note> that arouses a secular or profane thing, so it is written: **"and refrain from speaking [idle] words"** <note>Isaiah 58:13</note>. That word arouses another word above, and it is called "the word." **"The word of the Lord which came..."** **"And the word of the Lord was precious"** <note>1 Samuel 3:1</note>. As it is written: **"By the word of the Lord the heavens were made"** <note>Psalm 33:6</note>. For we have learned that this word ascends and pierces the firmaments until it rises (even a word intended for defilement). As it is written, that which is aroused below is aroused above; if good, then good; if evil, then evil. As it is written: **"You shall keep yourself from every evil thing [word]"** <note>Deuteronomy 23:10</note>.

The four species <note>The Lulav, Etrog, Hadas, and Arava used on Sukkot</note> are all-inclusive, and they are seven <note>referring to the seven symbolic branches/leaves</note>. And if you say there are seven species, it is not so; rather, they are four, but they branch out below. Through their ritual action, seven others are aroused above to bring goodness to the world from several sides, such as Kindness, Strength, and Beauty <note>The Sefirot: *Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet*</note>, for the whole is blessed by all of them, and they are six <note>the six directions/eminations</note>. And from the power of the "Deep" <note>the hidden source of Wisdom</note> which is the rest of all, whose waters never cease, they nourish the "Heart." Because this power is given to the upper and lower worlds to be blessed by all of them, this entire arousal occurs. For at the moment it is blessed by all of them, the entire world is blessed, down to the foundation under the Altar, just as it is below.

Furthermore, through this arousal, all six [extremities] are blessed so as to be satisfied, and they are all found to flow from the source of the "Deep Brain" of all, to descend to the world. Thus, they are all moist and not dry, so that blessing may be found in the world. For these [the species] are always moist and do not wither; they are found constantly. The time of their joy is this current time <note>Sukkot</note>, as we have learned in the Book of Rav Hamnuna the Elder. For that matter which is entrusted to each one of these [species] provides them with a dew of blessings of joy from above. Only at the time when their joy is above, is their joy below. And all of them flow over the waters and are watered as if from a river, as it says: **"And a river went out of Eden to water the garden"** <note>Genesis 2:10</note>. We require the physical taking [of the willow] and not just the word, because at this time the entire year is blessed. The seventh day of the festival <note>Hoshana Rabbah</note> is the conclusion of the judgment of the world. The gates are opened, exiting from the King's palace, and the "Strengths" <note>*Gevurot*</note> are aroused and concluded on this day. The willows of the brook <note>*Arvei Nachal*</note> depend on them. We need the "Strengths" to arouse the waters and to bless the four species for the benefit of all. When it is filled, all the upper realms are blessed by it. We take [the willow] and fulfill the "Strengths" needed for the water, to establish it afterwards. For in this...

## Main Text (Zohar)

On this day, the **judgments** <note>original: "dinin" — the spiritual forces of strict justice</note> are finalized, and therefore we need to beat them against the ground and diminish them so they are no longer found. For this day is both an **awakening** and a conclusion. It is an awakening and a conclusion just as we perform on the eve of Atonement. Rabbi Hiyya said: Is it not so? It is well-explained that the "willow of the brook" <note>the arava branch used on Hoshana Rabbah</note> comes from the side of the serpent, bent and guarded. On this day, they are awakened and finalized. Regarding this day it is written: "He sat and rested and went around to the end of the waters." <note>A mystical interpretation of the conclusion of the festival season</note> It is written: "He searched, and turned, and sat." The first day of the month was the beginning of judgment for the whole world. The Mercy <note>The Divine attribute</note> stands upon the throne to judge the world on this day, to turn and comfort, to awaken judgments and to end judgments. "He goes around the end of the waters" to distribute the **Severities** <note>original: "Gevuran" — the harsh spiritual energies</note> to the **Assembly of Israel** <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael" — the spiritual archetype of the Jewish people</note>. These "waters," as mentioned, are the fear of the world. And because they are Severities, they only descend through distress. On a day of distress, one does not have the strength to spare the world, except because the world needs them. See the reason: because the world was created with Judgment, and everything requires this. Therefore, everything depends on action. One needs an action and a rectification below; an action performed below awakens the higher realms to be rectified, and they are rectified through his hands.

Rabbi Yosei said: We have learned that the willow branch resembles **lips** <note>The shape of the willow leaf is traditionally compared to the human mouth/lips</note>. What is its significance on this day? Rabbi Hiyya said: It refers to a specific branch or level. Indeed, on this day, everything depends on the "lips" <note>prayer and speech</note>. On this day, the King commands that the "notes" <note>the divine decrees or "pitkin"</note> be written for the invalidation or finalization of judgments. Evil speech in the world has its beginning and end on this day, as has been stated. Come and see: on this day, the mouths are finished and completed upon their thrones, and they grant forgiveness. Then, on this day, their judgments are finished and removed, and they are dismissed with a blessing. From here on, one should not be enslaved to anything other than the King. For every opening and every priest, a single type is not found in the King... he asks for whatever he desires and it is given to him. One must remove the offense, and for this the nations conclude. It is written: *I will provide for them a plantation of renown...* <note>Ezekiel 34:29</note>. If you say that support was given to Esau <note>representing Rome/foreign empires</note> as a merchant in the kingdom with high palaces, ruling over the world... so it is. Once the **Holy King** has decreed a decree, the decree is prepared according to his "note"... to have mercy on that which was enslaved. And regarding this it is written... according to the notes of the **Levites**, and likewise all those good things that were decreed upon Israel...

->**This** is the law of the sin offering; this is the law of the meal offering; this is the law of the sacrifice of the peace offering; and this<-
->is the law of the guilt offering.<-

Rabbi Yitzhak said: They have already established that "This" <note>The word "Zot" in Hebrew, often referring to the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> refers to the lower realm which is within everything. It is the life of the world. Whoever exerts himself in the Torah does not need to bring a sacrifice for his portion in everything, above or below, in all sides. Rabbi Yitzhak opened his discourse:
> The priests did not say, "Where is the Lord?" and those who handle the Torah did not know Me; the shepherds also transgressed against Me. <note>Jeremiah 2:8</note>
"The priests"—these are those who serve in the **High Priesthood** and bring holy matters near to the lower realms, uniting the **Unification** <note>original: "Yichuda" — the mystical balancing of Divine attributes</note> each one as is fitting. "Those who handle the Torah"—these are the **Levites** who handle the Torah. Is a Priest not also one who handles the Torah? Rather, these are the Levites who handle the harps, which come from the side of the Torah, for the Torah was given from their side <note>The attribute of Gevurah/Strength associated with Levites</note>. And we see from here the rebuke of the Holy King to Israel, to the tribe of Judah... "The shepherds transgressed against Me"—these are the leaders of the people, who are shepherds to the nation like a shepherd in the desert. And these are the three levels that must always be found at the **sacrifice** <note>original: "karbana"</note> to find **favor** <note>original: "re'ua"</note> above and below, and so that blessings may be found in all worlds. The Priest brings the sacrifice near and intends to unite the **Holy Name** as is fitting, and to awaken the side of the Levite... to be included...
