## Main Text (Zohar)

And it ascended on the left side, and Israel below were found by all of them, and the will of desire ascended and joined before the Holy King. Because of this, everything was in agreement, joy increased, and gladness was found above and below.
**Rabbi Yehuda** opened <note>Psalm 104:3</note> > Who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters, etc. <
When the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, created the world, He brought it forth from the midst of the waters and established it upon the waters. What did He do? He divided the waters into two halves: a half below and a half above. He made a structure built from below; this He made and prepared as the lower world, establishing it upon the half of the waters, and He established for it a foundation above <note>Psalm 24:2</note> > For He founded it upon the seas <. And the other half ascended above and is called their upper roof, as it is written: "Who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters." And He made a firmament between their two halves, which are the secret of the foundation: "Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters" <note>Genesis 1:6</note>. Upon them, holy beings were established and arranged from the dripping drops, like the spirit below and like the body, as it is written <note>Nehemiah 9:8</note> > And You made a covenant with him <. All of them were established, and He arranged the "brain" and its increase like the days. All the drops of water were mixed, and these are the troops of the "Watchers" <note>term: "Irin" - a class of angels</note> who all sing a song like the day.
And you shall sacrifice like the morning, and they sing as it is. When they reach the night, all the songs of above cease. The troops of below gather, standing in the likeness of the lower world, and they raise one to another—for all is one—that which is outside of both of them. In this group, there is no silence; eight levels ascend one above the other. At times, the depths of above and below are opened, and all of them proceed from the heads of the spirits from the side of the Holy Spirit. Within the side of the lower abyss, sparks of fire are struck like pipes, appointed over the "sides of the world" to investigate the guilty, like the streams that flow from the Mountain of Fire. All of these are below, and their appearance is flaming; they stand between above and below.
When the smoke of the altar <note>original: "Madbecha"</note> ascends, they are awakened and ascend from that level where they stand to prostrate and to give thanks. And there is a power like a crown <note>original: "Keter"</note> of fire that burns strongly, and because of this, it returns to its place. All of them are nourished by the enjoyment of the altar in order to be prepared before the Supernal Kings. For this reason, they prepare here, and they draw near to here, and the smoke ascends purely to establish for each and every one the "will of all" that ascends to His Name, so that it may be like a spirit before the Holy King.
From that seal, when the smoke of the altar ascends, its light is seen like the image of a powerful lion <note>note: The lion represents the attribute of Mercy and divine acceptance</note> crouching over its prey. The Priests and Israel would see this and rejoice, for they knew that the offering was accepted with favor before the Holy King. From that place of the holy upper light, it hastens to receive this lower offering. Then, a person should be known before his Master and return in complete repentance to the King for whom they prepared a gift. It is as if the King says to his servants: "Go and take this gift that he brought to me." So says the Holy One, blessed be He, and He receives the gift that His children offer. Oh, how much joy is found in all! How much radiance is found! All of them accompany the one who brings the offering <note>original: "Korban"</note> when he intends to offer the sacrifice as is proper. <note>Psalm 76:2</note> > In Judah God is known <.
Come and see: regarding the drawing near of the lower offering, the light does not cease until it reaches the altar to receive the gift. It appears like a great lion crouching over the sacrifice. But when the people rebel and merits are not found, and the one bringing the sacrifice does not offer it as is proper, his sacrifice is not accepted. They would see that the smoke did not ascend in a straight line, and a certain spirit would come from the side of the North to the altar. They would then see the image of an impudent dog <note>note: The dog represents the "Other Side" or external forces of judgment and rejection</note> crouching over the sacrifice. Then they knew that the sacrifice was not accepted with favor by the King for whom they prepared the gift. It was as if the King said: "Look at this flawed gift; give it to the dog!" Because it was not worthy to be brought before Him, it was handed over to the external forces. For this reason, they would see the image of a dog.

## Main Text (Continued)

...and the blue thread <note>The *Tekhelet* used in the Tzitzit/fringes</note>. This corresponds to the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings. ## Main Text (Zohar)

One who has no blemish within him shall have no dwelling <note>original: *madur*</note> there. And because of this, for those who did not grow fat and did not turn back from their error, He increased [His grace] to bring us back from error, so that one may be called "learned in the Torah and fearful of sin." And if he is a son of that place, there is no sin in him. And whoever merits the service of the Lord, Heaven forbid [that he should sin], for one who fears sin inherits the dignity of the Lord. This is argued *a fortiori* <note>original: *kal va-chomer*</note> from King Noah, who performed the King's commandments, and since he merited and grew old, etc., for at that time it was spread forth that he should be called "Man" <note>original: *Adam*</note>. He is a partner to the animalistic soul and the animalistic spirit, for in the animalistic soul of the whole world, the speaking spirit <note>original: *ruach memalla*</note> is in these worlds. 

Silver is in her, all the musings and thoughts of the world's enemies. In the lower exile, through her, God who opens shall open for him. "And my companion, my beloved"—and "beloved" is nothing other than the veil through which kings are prepared to draw near to the King. Holy children with many kinds of nourishment; in the animal, for the free man, of whom it is said: "Let us eat of our bread and our food," and with their wine, and he was able to be sent to the free man. How many sacrifices for the ascent! The kings of the Mishnah established it in the flesh that comes out from Heaven; deep ones are healed from Heaven, a circle for the prevention, regarding which it is said: "And the flesh of my guards," and not the holy flesh that is divided into many services from the side of the perplexed one, in the love of her husband, to be called in the awe of the one who receives. In the love of the unification, for her *night and day it shall not be extinguished* <note>Leviticus 6:6</note>. And the friends, in your lives, *give Him no rest until He establishes* <note>Isaiah 62:7</note> to fulfill for them in the elevations of the love of His unification, which stands within it: *A perpetual fire shall be kept burning on the altar; it shall not go out* <note>Leviticus 6:6</note>. Thus far his words.

Furthermore, they did not cover themselves and were blemished, for they died; there is no prevention. Was that not made a connection before the blood to be armed? ...that it should not be written as "blemished," for he is not <note>referring to the integrity of the priest</note>, and "it shall consume them and they shall die." **"This is the anointing of Aaron and the anointing of his sons"** <note>Leviticus 7:35</note>. It ascended higher and higher and flows down to him below. From that place, blessings flow like veins upon it, and as it flows to those below, it stands. <margin>This is to be mixed</margin> Let "This" be like "This": "This is the anointing of Aaron and the anointing of his sons." And it is written: **"Like the good oil upon the head..."** <note>Psalms 133:2</note>.

"With You"—it dwells with You and is never separated from You. "In Your light"—this is the light hidden for the righteous in the time to come, as it is written: "And he went to the day of light, for it was good." And from that light, Israel is destined to look upon the world.

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Zohar on the Torah portion "Tzav" (Leviticus 6:1). It focuses on the relationship between the earthly priesthood and the celestial realms, specifically the concept of the "Source of Life."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Command Aaron** <-

...to the World to Come, for it is written: <term>For with You is the source of life</term> <note>original: "Ki imcha mekor chayim"; Psalms 36:10</note> and so on. This refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He, who is the World to Come that descends and takes hold of all sides. Why? Because that Source of Life takes hold of Him and crowns Him with supreme crowns all around. Because He is the one who crowns everyone, He binds everything together and reaches out to the furthest extent...

And because of this, <term>For with You is the source of life</term>, and therefore <term>in Your light we see light</term> <note>Psalms 36:10</note>. <term>Rabbi Isaac</term> said: "For with You is the source of life" refers to the <term>High Priest</term> <note>Kohen Gadol</note>, who goes toward Him. The High Priest below exists because of the honor of the Priesthood in general—the supreme holy greatness above. He kindles the <term>lamps</term> <note>original: "butzinin"; refers to the mystical lights or emanations</note> above. The High Priest ascends through the lamps of supreme radiance to be crowned over all.

Corresponding to this are the seven <term>days of ordination</term> <note>original: "yemei miluim"; the seven days of consecrating the Tabernacle</note> for the priest below, to rectify everything in the likeness of that which is above. These days of ordination are called "days of completion" because the priest is completed through the side of the other days to achieve perfection... as it is said, the seven days of ordination are so named because the other sides are completed all around. What does this teach? That when the priest is awakened, everything around him is awakened with him. Therefore it is written: <term>And from the entrance of the Tent of Meeting [you shall not go out...] until the day of completion</term> <note>Leviticus 8:33</note> and so on. At these times, the priest below is certainly crowned in everything in the likeness of that which is above, because when the priest below is awakened, everything is awakened, and through him, the upper worlds are awakened, and blessings are found above and below.

<term>Rabbi Abba</term> said: What is the meaning of the staff that was cast down to purify? This is because he [the priest] surrounds the Holy One, Blessed be He, the Source of Life. And it is written that he adds to the right, the arm of His glory, and the staff encompasses all those seven days of ordination to crown the Bride with him...

<term>Rabbi Hezekiah</term> was sitting before <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> and said to him: How many "lights" were found before the world was created? Eight, seven, six... and these are: the Light of the Torah, the Light of Gehenna <note>Hell/Purgatory</note>, the Light of the Garden of Eden, the Light of the Throne of Glory, the Light of the Holy Temple, the Light of Repentance, and the Light of the Messiah. These seven were found before the world was created, and the "lights" corresponding to them were found within it, and this is what kindles the lamps from above to below.

<term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> opened with the verse: <term>All was from the dust</term> <note>Ecclesiastes 3:20</note>. Even the "all" [the universe] was made of dust. And if you say "All was from the dust" according to the cycle of things, from what dust? From that which is refined beneath the Throne of Glory. In the book of Rav Yosef, it is explained: "All was from the dust"—the place that gathers everything. This teaches that the "swords" [forces] are bound on this side and that side, and they gather to be called "dust," which is scattered in every direction. And regarding this: "All was from the dust and all returns to the dust." This is certainly from the dust of the Holy Sanctuary, refined from the supreme dust... "and it has dust of gold" <note>Job 28:6</note>. Just as the action is found below, so it was above in this likeness. And we have established: "Dust, dust"—the purity of the Sanctuary of this world was not found [otherwise]. And therefore even the "circle of water," as it is said: "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created" <note>Genesis 2:4</note>—He created them with the letter *He*.

And because of this, "All was from the dust." Which dust? That which is hidden beneath the Throne of Glory. It is written: <term>You are all beautiful, my love, and there is no flaw in you</term> <note>Song of Songs 4:7</note>. "You are all beautiful, my love" refers to the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>Knesset Yisrael; the mystical personification of the Jewish people/the Shekhinah</note>, and "there is no flaw in you" refers to the Sanhedrin <note>The high court of 71 sages</note>, who correspond to the seventy-two pillars, the seventy souls who descended with Jacob, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, is over them all. From here, the righteous ones of the Sanhedrin and above... We have learned it is written: <term>And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation</term> <note>Exodus 19:6</note>. What is a "kingdom of priests"? Everything is drawn from the source... for when the Assembly of Israel is blessed and the priests are [consecrated], then it is called, based on the Holy One, a "kingdom of priests." This means it is not just called a kingdom, but a kingdom of priests, making her the Mistress over all. It is not called a "kingdom of priests" in a mundane sense, but the Kingdom of Heaven certainly. And she is a "kingdom" as it is written, for the priests bless her, and then she is a kingdom over all, a kingdom over all the radiances of the King.

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Command Aaron** <-

From the King of the upper and lower realms, the kingdom over all worlds. Rabbi Yose says: It is written, *“And He has founded His vault <note>original: 'agudato' - His bunch or vault</note> upon the earth.”* <note>Amos 9:6</note> "And He has founded" refers to when the King unites to receive all those holy sides in one gathering; then it is written "And He has founded." Rabbi Isaac said: "And He has founded" is like the phrase *“And you shall take a bunch of hyssop.”* <note>Exodus 12:22</note> What is he speaking of? That when they are joined as one and are blessed by them, then He rules over all and shines above and below. Everything follows the pattern of the Priest’s service: he offers sacrifices and burns incense, intending his words to bring everything together as one. Then it is written, *“And He has founded His vault upon the earth.”* Rabbi Yose said: When the dew descends, everyone partakes of it until the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> is blessed, and the upper and lower beings are blessed. Then it is written: *“Blessed be the Lord from Zion, who dwells in Jerusalem. Hallelujah.”* <note>Psalms 135:21</note> And *“Blessed be His glorious name forever; and let the whole earth be filled with His glory. Amen and Amen.”* <note>Psalms 72:19</note>

Rabbi Eleazar was traveling from Cappadocia to Lod, and with him were Rabbi Yissa and Rabbi Hezekiah. Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse and said: *“And I have put My words in your mouth, and have covered you in the shadow of My hand...”* <note>Isaiah 51:16</note> We have learned: any person who busies himself with the words of the Torah, and whose lips murmur the Torah, the Holy One, Blessed be He, spreads His presence over him, and the Soul spreads its canopy over him. This is what is written: *“And I have put My words in your mouth, and have covered you in the shadow of My hand.”* Not only that, but he sustains the world, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, rejoices with him as if on that day He planted the heavens and the earth. This is what is written: *“...to plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth, and to say to Zion: You are My people.”* From here we learn that Israel is called the "Assembly of Zion," as it is written: *“And to say to Zion: You are My people.”* We see that the Assembly of Israel is called the Assembly of Zion, as it is written: *“Zion shall be redeemed with justice, and they that return to her with righteousness.”* <note>Isaiah 1:27</note>

He opened another discourse and said: *“A perpetual fire shall be kept burning on the altar; it shall not go out.”* <note>Leviticus 6:6</note> This is the testimony of the generation, as it is written: *“And My testimony <note>original: 'eduti'</note> that I shall teach them.”* <note>Psalms 132:12</note> The "perpetual fire" is the bond joined as one, like the smoke of the incense tied together in holiness. *“Bind up the testimony, seal the Torah among my disciples.”* <note>Isaiah 8:16</note> The "testimony of the Torah" is the seal of the Torah, and all the hidden things and secrets stored from above are all sealed within it, among "my disciples." For there the secret and the key are gathered between the two pillars <note>referring to the Sefirot of Netzach and Hod</note>, for there dwells the gathering place of every secret and every key from above, to reveal it at the mouth of the "Amah" <note>a measure/conduit</note> and to lead it into this testimony. And because of this, everything is tied in one bond of faith.

Come and see the difference between the wise who busy themselves with the Torah for its glory: those who sustain the worlds by busying themselves with the Torah are superior to prophets at all times. What is the reason? Because they stand at a higher level <term>grade: 'dargha' - a spiritual rank</term> than the prophets. Those who busy themselves with the Torah stand above in the place called "Torah" <note>The Sefirah of Tiferet</note>, which is the sustenance of all faith, while the prophets stand below in the place called "Endurance" and "Splendor" <note>The Sefirot of Netzach and Hod</note>. Therefore, the wise who busy themselves with the Torah are superior to prophets and rise higher than them, for these stand above and those stand below. And those who speak words through the Holy Spirit stand lower than all of them. Therefore, happy are those who busy themselves with the Torah, for they are at a higher level than all. Because of this, a wise man who toils in the Torah does not need sacrifices or burnt offerings, for the Torah is superior to everything and is the bond of faith for all. Thus it is written: *“Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace.”* <note>Proverbs 3:17</note> And it is written: *“Great peace have they who love Your Torah, and there is no stumbling block for them.”* <note>Psalms 119:165</note>

While they were walking, they met a man who was coming with three branches of myrtle in his hand. They approached him and said: "Why do you have these?" He said: "To bring fragrance to the journey." Rabbi Eleazar said: "You have spoken well. But why these three?" He said to him: "One for Abraham, one for Isaac, and one for Jacob. And I bind them together and smell them because it is written: *'Because of the savor of your good ointments, your name is as ointment poured forth.'*" <note>Song of Songs 1:3</note> And because through this scent, the weakness of the soul is sustained in this faith, to be established and to awaken blessings from above and below. Rabbi Eleazar said: "Happy is your portion, <margin>O Israel</margin>."

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Command Aaron**<-

A remembrance in this world and in the world to come. Come and see: the world is only sustained by the scent <note>original: "reicha"</note> and the spirit. Through this, another pure spirit is recognized. At the moment it departs, the "bundle is unraveled" and the soul ascends further. The levels of the soul—the <term>Nefesh</term> (vitality), <term>Ruach</term> (spirit), and <term>Neshamah</term> (higher soul)—separate, yet they are made below to correspond to this spirit. They draw near to one another and rejoice. Because of this, one spirit seeks after another to receive it; once this spirit is balanced, they draw together as one and rejoice. In this same manner, the spirit of the sacrifice, as it ascends, causes all things to draw together as one, and the <term>lamps</term> <note>original: "butzini" - referring to the divine emanations or lights</note> are kindled and rejoice.

Come and see: there are two stars, one above and one below. The lower star shines when it receives the <term>smoke</term> <note>original: "tnana" - the vapor or smoke of the offering</note> that ascends to the higher star. Thus, the smoke of the sacrifice is the vapor that ascends to the higher stars, and they are kindled together and all draw near as one, like this spirit. For this reason, it is called "a pleasing aroma to the Lord." Below is the end of <term>Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Chokhmah"</note>, and upon the scent of the sacrifice everything stands—the preservation of the whole and the preservation of the world. The sacrifice is performed by the hand of the Priest <note>Kohen</note> who brings everything near. Because of this, there are times when "bread" is found within it, as they are all crumbled into a pleasing aroma, and joys and blessings are found above and below. It is written:
> "O Lord, You are my God; I will exalt You..." <note>Isaiah 25:1</note>
The masters have established this verse. However, below, a person must give thanks to the Holy Name and praise Him for everything. From what place does his praise arise? As they have established, it is from the depths of all, as it is written:
> "...for You have done a wonder" <note>Isaiah 25:1</note>
"Wonder" <note>Pele</note> is as it is written, "And his name shall be called Wonder," and this is the "Wonder" below. "Counsels from afar" are certainly everything. "From afar," as it is written:
> "From afar the Lord appeared to me" <note>Jeremiah 31:2</note>
And it is written:
> "She brings her food from afar" <note>Proverbs 31:14</note>
"Faithfulness and truth" <note>original: "Emunah omen"</note>. Everything is directed toward Wisdom and Life, as they have established. "Faithfulness in the night." Everything is found in its completeness, and it is written:
> "They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness" <note>Lamentations 3:23</note>
And the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to purify Israel from their sins, as it is written:
> "I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean; from all your uncleanness and from all your idols I will cleanse you." <note>Ezekiel 36:25</note>
Blessed be the Lord forever.

->**Portion of "And it came to pass on the eighth day"**<-

**And it came to pass** on the eighth day, etc. Rabbi Isaac opened his discourse:
> "When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy" <note>Job 38:7</note>
Happy are Israel, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave them the holy Torah, the joy of all the joys of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Torah, as it is written:
> "And I was His delight day by day" <note>Proverbs 8:30</note>
And in whose joy? In the Holy One, Blessed be He. And through the Torah the world was found, as it is written:
> "Then I was beside Him as a nursling [Amon]" <note>Proverbs 8:30</note>
Do not read it as *Amon* (nursling), but as *Oman* (architect/artisan). Through the Torah, a person is saved from this world and inherits the world to come. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to the Torah: "I wish to create Man." She replied: "This man is destined to sin before You; if You do not extend Your anger toward him, how will he stand in the world?" He said to her: "I and My strength are in the world, for not in vain am I called 'Slow to Anger.'" Rabbi Hiyya said: The Written Torah and the Oral Torah established man in the world, for it says, "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness." Rabbi Yose said: From here:
> "...that which has already been done" <note>Ecclesiastes 2:12</note>
"Done" <note>plural in Hebrew: 'Asuhu'</note> certainly, and this is the whole, resembling the whole—the male likeness and the female likeness. Because of this, the <term>beginning</term> <note>original: "shiruta"</note> of the Torah starts with the letter *Bet* [ב], as they have established. Rabbi Isaac said: From here we see that the *Bet* is open on one side and closed on the other; it is like the moment when a person comes to be joined...

## Main Text (Zohar)

To be joined in its way, it is open to receive him and to be found in holiness. And regarding the taste of all good that is hidden from it and given to another—that "other" <note>The *Sitra Achra* or "Other Side," representing the forces of impurity</note> is closed from the other side and does not provide an opening until it is given to be joined with it in its way, to subdue it. And beneath it, another opening shall flow before the sons of men, and a companion, and it calls to them: "to you, to be defiled..." and it is written: *As a sheep before her shearers is dumb* <note>Isaiah 53:7</note>. We say in the Talmud regarding the gates in the city: Rabbi Judah said, there are two treasuries and one that is alone for them. What is he speaking of? Rather, one is to the left and one is to the right, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, is unique and received them. 

Rabbi Elazar said: Two cups <note>original: *kassayin*</note>—these are the holy upper ones, for awe and for vision and for merit, the sum of the Torah. And these open an opening to all openings, an opening to faith. And these are the "House" <note>Hebrew: *Bayit*</note> of everything, and because of this, it is called "House," for these merit the House. And for this reason, the beginning of the Torah is with the letter *Bet* <note>The first letter of the first word *Bereshit*, which also means "House"</note>, for it is the second and the perfection of the world. 

And because of this, regarding the matter of one who strives in the Torah, they all strive in several holy ways. And it has been said that the Torah is entirely the High Holy Name. And because it is the Holy Name, it opened with a *Bet*, which is the Holy Name in the three bonds of faith. 

Come and see: at the time when they strive in the Torah, they are mended by it before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and are crowned with the crowns of the Torah, to be sanctified above and below. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, extends His right hand to them when those who strive in the Torah are as one. And it is established that they are partners with the Divine Presence <note>Hebrew: *Shekhinah*</note> and are joined as one. And when one comes who serves the Holy One, Blessed be He, He crowns them as one holy [crown] of Loving-kindness <note>Hebrew: *Chesed*</note>, to be recognized among the upper and lower beings. And all those stars of the soul in the branches of the Assembly of Israel, and all those above in the Torah, are seen to appear before the King; they all sing as one: *Holy, Holy, Holy... When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy* <note>Job 38:7</note>. 

What is "shouted for joy"? They all sound the blast of the *Teruah* <note>The broken, sobbing sound of the Shofar</note> for those who are broken, and they were all broken before the morning. When the morning awakens in the world, they all arrange their praise like the morning and are shaken, and all the sons of God shout for joy. 

Rabbi Elazar was traveling on the road to visit Rabbi Phinehas ben Yair, who was his father-in-law. Rabbi Phinehas said: "Surely I heard a voice of joy." Once he emerged from the cover of the mountain branches, Rabbi Elazar appeared before him. He said: "Surely the commandment of the journey has departed." Rabbi Elazar descended toward him and kissed him. He said to him: "If the pattern of the way is before you, stay here and let us be joined as one." He said to them: "Take the path and go on my way toward you to accompany you." Once they were found together, they walked and were joined as one. 

Rabbi Phinehas opened and said: *The Lord bless thee out of Zion; and see thou the good [of Jerusalem]* <note>Psalm 128:5</note>. "The Lord bless thee out of Zion"—see the reason for this, because from there blessings are found. This is what is written: *For there the Lord commanded the blessing, even life for evermore* <note>Psalm 133:3</note>. And because of this, "The Lord bless thee out of Zion," for from there blessings go out to all. "And see the good of Jerusalem"—because of this it is blessed, for once Zion is filled with blessings, then Jerusalem is blessed, and mercy is found in it. And when Jerusalem is blessed, all the people are blessed. "All the days of thy life"—that they shall not see distress in your days as in the past. And regarding this: "And see the good of Jerusalem all the days of thy life. And see thy children's children"—for what is the portion of the holy pious ones? Then, "Peace be upon Israel." What is "Peace be upon Israel"? It is like one who says "Peace be upon the head of the King," that his glory shall not be diminished. So too, "Peace be upon Israel," when the righteous dwell in the world. 

Rabbi Elazar opened and said: *Children's children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers* <note>Proverbs 17:6</note>. This verse is stronger than the other. "Children's children"—these surround the crowns of the King. "And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord" <note>Isaiah 54:13</note>. And it is written "Children's children" who are precious. "And the glory of children are their fathers"—children are not crowned except through their fathers. From what exchange? That children are not crowned and do not establish the priestly preparations except through their fathers, from whom they are crowned and blessed. This is what is written—

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on the Torah portion Shemini. It follows the journey of Rabbi Phineas ben Yair and Rabbi Eleazar, using a miraculous encounter with a snake to explain the cosmic mechanics of reward, punishment, and the balance between Divine Mercy and Judgment.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Shemini<-

And Beauty <note>Tiferet, the central Divine attribute</note> gathers into its house. While they were walking, the time for the afternoon prayer arrived. As they were walking, a knot <note>original: *kaptor*; some versions read *kapta*, a binding</note> stood at the feet of Rabbi Phineas’s donkey, and it brayed twice. 

After they finished their prayer, Rabbi Phineas said: "Surely this is a braying for the animal! The judges of the righteous have judged this day for me beforehand. Its color is a vision of whiteness, yet it passed me through a place of filth, torn and closed off from passing." They stood up and saw a snake knotted around the donkey's legs. Rabbi Phineas said: "Snake, snake! Go and hide <note>another version: and conceal</note> your knot in the white cleft. Let darkness be knotted, snake, with all its twisted knots." 

Rabbi Eleazar said: "Why is the Holy One, Blessed be He <term>The Holy One, Blessed be He: The standard rabbinic title for God, often abbreviated as Ha-Kadosh Baruch Hu</term>, so exacting with those He loves?" He replied: "Surely the Holy One, Blessed be He, is exacting with them because of His love; He watches over them and desires to add holiness upon their holiness. And now, I say that because I did not guard my own holiness, I was guarded [by this omen]. This snake smelled the scent, for the serpent has many paths, and all of them perform His mission." Even in the vision of the spirit, it is written: *And You shall pardon my iniquity, for it is great* <note>Psalm 25:11</note>; it was not before Him, and everything was to be covered. And even among the nations, it is written: *The Lord will bring a nation against you from afar* <note>Deuteronomy 28:49</note> from the end of the earth. 

Rabbi Eleazar said: "Does one of Israel perform His mission? Heaven forbid! Not like a wicked person, for this is a righteous man. But a wicked person of Israel is like any other wicked person. He does not perform a mission except at a time when he does not intend it." It is possible that we did not tread, and behold, Jews are in our hands, and it is forbidden—we specifically did not tread so as not to kill him surely, as it says: *But God caused it to come to his hand* <note>Exodus 21:13</note> in order to punish both of them. 

Rabbi Eleazar said: "How does the Holy One, Blessed be He, perform a mission through the hands of these? Is it like a Gentile, heaven forbid?" And he said to him: "His love for us tells you to speak to Him before they go." He opened and said: "Be silent and still, rise and tremble and rest." And it is still at the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives a command, and there is much outside. Who is the Mercy to clothe him and to make an accusation <note>original: *kategor*</note> against him? He hides His face and chastises us. And at the time when He has hidden His eyes from watching over you, who is the Judgment over him to guard him and to make him a binding and a ban? Thus is the Holy One, Blessed be He, over a nation and over a man alike, whether for the whole world, for one nation, or for a single individual. 

Come and see: At the time when human beings' deeds are proper below, the Right <term>The Right: The side of Chesed (Loving-kindness) and Mercy in the Sefirotic system</term> of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is awakened toward them above. Then many mercies are awakened, many guardians of the world, many guardians of man from the right and from the left. Then the Left <term>The Left: The side of Gevurah (Strength) and Din (Judgment)</term> is subdued and cannot rule. 

But at the time when human beings' deeds are not proper below, the Left is awakened, and all those who come from the side of the Left are awakened. They all become numerous against human beings, for those who transgress the words of the Torah are all marked in their faces and are recognized by those who are awakened from the side of the Left. Because of this, the snake <term>Snake: Symbolizing the Primordial Serpent or the Sitra Achra (the Other Side/Evil)</term> and the [Evil] Eye and all those who come from the side of the Left are all called "gods" <note>in the sense of powers</note> toward those marked ones who are awakened before them. 

And Israel, even though their deeds are not proper, they all come from the side of the Right. But because the Right is subdued by their deeds, the Left rules over them, along with all those who come from the side of the Left. And He performs a mission through the hand of the snake and all that resemble them, which are from the side of the Left. It is not so for a righteous Israelite—may the Merciful One save us—who comes from the side of the Right. Yet Israel is grasped in everything, like that other altar, at a time when he did not intend it, so that both should be punished and receive punishment to purify them. 

Rabbi Eleazar said: "From the beginning, they are on the Right and should not cleave to the Left, nor be arranged with it forever, until another time they are removed." Rabbi Eleazar said: "From where do we know this?" He said to him: "Come and see from the Concubine at Gibeah <term>Concubine at Gibeah: A biblical narrative from Judges 19-21 involving a civil war in Israel</term>. Even though they were guilty, the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not want snakes and seraphs to awaken against them for your sake. Because of this, many of Israel died during those times until all the guilty ones who were awakened against them died. Then they were atoned for and preserved for those meritorious ones <note>original: *zakkayin*</note>."

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Torah portion "Shemini" (The Eighth). It continues the mystical exploration of the Tabernacle's inauguration, focusing on the transition from the seven days of ordination to the eighth day of revelation.</meta>

## The Portion of Shemini

Fortunate are those who arrange their words in the way of truth. Even though they are righteous, a matter is not firmly established until it is settled through merits. When the world ascends as one—the lower world reflecting the pattern of the upper world—at that time, the worlds are not found lacking. Because of this, the wicked of Israel are held responsible by the righteous, for the righteous are guarantors for them. The righteous are not considered fully meritorious if they do not distance themselves from the side of impurity <note>The "Other Side" or Sitra Achra</note> regarding the sins committed against the King. Then Samael <note>The primary archangel of judgment and the accuser</note> is aroused against them to seize them and to find the sins they committed against the King. He stands as an accuser with a document in his hand and mixes among them. When Samael lifts his eyes and sees a person, he rejoices and seeks to collect the debt of the sins committed against the King. It is as if one says: "First, stone him and kill him."

Thus, Israel comes from the Side of the Right <note>The attribute of Hesed or Lovingkindness</note>. When they cause themselves to be found on the right through their actions, Samael and all those who come from his side are aroused. A living being from the side of darkness stands and mixes with them to identify them. They say to him: "They have the merit of protection because they come from the Side of the Right." Even if they have stumbled in sin, they have the merit of the King's protection. Who gave you the right to collect from them? It is found that the King forgives them first, and the King dwells before them and says: "It is a time of kindness; I forgive all at once." This is because the King's forgiveness precedes their life, and this comes from that side.

Rabbi Eleazar said: It is certainly so, for we have learned that the freedom and life of Samael are bound in Mercy and Judgment. The nations of the world perform actions for the Right, and the nations perform actions for Samael. But Israel—even though the wicked among them are subdued—they are rooted in the Right and never cleave to Samael, nor are they ever mixed together.

And because of this, it is written: **"Save with Your right hand, and answer me"** <note>Psalm 60:7</note>. For when the Right Hand is raised, Israel, who cleave to it, are raised and crowned with it. Then Samael and all who come from his side are subdued. The Right Hand returns and prepares the way for life.

Rabbi Eleazar opened and said: **"And it came to pass on the eighth day, that Moses called..."** <note>Leviticus 9:1</note>. What is this "Eighth Day"? It is written: **"And from the door of the Tent of Meeting [you shall not go out]... for seven days shall he consecrate you"** <note>Leviticus 8:33</note>. It should have said "for a period of seven days." Why does it say **"for seven days"** <note>original: "Ki shevat yamim"</note>? 

Fortunate are the priests <term>Kohanim: the hereditary ministers of the Temple</term> who are crowned with the crowns of the Holy King and are seen in the Great Holy Kindness <note>Hesed</note>. For the Supernal Kindness is aroused, which sweetens all seven [lower emanations]. They are sweetened by that holy greatness, and from it, all **seven stars** <note>The seven lower Sefirot or spiritual dimensions</note> are kindled. It bathes in the goodness of the flow that includes all seven, and all are included in it.

We have learned: there are six, and all are included in this one, and this is the sum of them all. And because of the "seven days of consecration," for they are doubled in this, it is called "for [Ki] the seven." When these seven were completed for the priests, and they were crowned and anointed with all of them, and they reached the stage of life-sustenance, Aaron was commanded to offer a **calf** <note>original: "Egla"</note>. This was because the calf-sin <note>The Golden Calf</note> had to be hovered over and atoned for—that sin which Aaron had a hand in. 

Just as with the Red Heifer, which comes from a deep place to purify the impurity of Israel, so here everything was perfected. He was clothed in garments of glory, perfected in all crowns, perfected above and perfected below. When the work began below, it was done in this way so that it would be aroused similarly above, and everything would be found in a single pattern. Then all the worlds are blessed, and the blessings of the Priest are found. Here the Priest is perfected in everything as is fitting. This is why it is written: **"Take for yourself a young calf for a sin offering"** <note>Leviticus 9:2</note>, because it was the sin he committed previously. And **"a ram for a burnt offering"** <note>Leviticus 9:2</note>. Why a ram? Because of the strength of Isaac <note>referring to the ram substituted for Isaac at the Binding</note>, which is a "perfect burnt offering." It descends below to complete everything. The place from the side of Isaac is perfected, and he takes strength because the strength of Isaac approaches as a burnt offering, for a burnt offering <note>Olah</note> ascends on high. Because of this, he crowns it in its ladder: a calf and a ram. A calf for the reason we stated, and a ram to complete it...

## Main Text (Zohar)

The perfection that emerges as it should, and the power of the **Other Side** <note>The "Other Side" (Sitra Achra) refers to the realm of evil or spiritual impurity in Kabbalah.</note> dwells within this offering in this manner. As it is written: *Strength and gladness are before Him* <note>1 Chronicles 16:27</note>, to find merit before the Lord. Even though they came, not one revealed to this place the peace that emerges. What is written regarding it? *A young bull for a sin offering* etc. It is written regarding Israel, *an ox for a sin offering*, but Israel did not receive the initial punishment. Because they received punishment in several places for this, the Holy One, blessed be He, did not wish to mention their sins as before. Therefore, it is not written here "for a sin offering" but rather "for merit," to show that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not act toward Israel in this manner. And there was a deficiency, for he did not receive punishment in the exile that arrived, as it is written: *And with deficiency the Lord weakened* etc., and it is written: *He grew strong against the Master of deficiency at that time*. Until now, the proof was hanging. It is written: *A young bull for a sin offering*—certainly for a sin offering.

And there was strength for peace so that his sin would be atoned for, and they would be purified and become complete in everything. On that day, the upper and lower worlds were completed, and peace was found in all of them, like the joy of above and below. Had it not been for the confusion caused by the sons of Aaron on that day, which removed joy from the world, there would have been no lack of joy above and below. On that day, the **Other Side** was meant to be removed from the world, and all the righteous would have been found clinging in joy all that day. All the accusing sins above would have been removed; they were seeing and hearing in the surroundings of Israel, and they were not found on that side until their reason shone, and they all stood up and caused destruction.

And they caused (variant: and they mixed) confusion in the joy of everyone, and anger was found in the world. This is what is written: *And the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people* <note>Leviticus 9:23</note>. Immediately: *And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, each took his censer* etc. <note>Leviticus 10:1</note>. We have learned: on that day, the joy of the House was meant to be bound in the **incense of faith** <note>The incense (Ketoret) represents the highest form of mystical union and prayer.</note>, where all holy connections are bound together as one. For this reason, it is called *Ketoret* <note>The word Ketoret is linked to the Aramaic root K-T-R, meaning "to bind" or "knot."</note>. But they sinned and brought all the sins of deficiency together, and they cast it <note>the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> outside, for they did not bind it with them. They offered something else, and therefore it returned to them. For this reason, it was merited as it is written: *With this shall Aaron come into the holy place* <note>Leviticus 16:3</note>. In several ways, they confused the joy of the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Knesset Yisrael, a term for the Shekhinah, the feminine aspect of God.</note> until they were not found or seen as fit to draw near and to bless the worlds through them. One reason was that the intent was not as it should be; another was that they pressed the hour; and another was that they did not emerge from a pure source like their own. *And they offered strange fire before the Lord* etc. <note>Leviticus 10:1</note>. And we have seen that they strove to offer incense when they were not permitted. Rabbi Phinehas said: Do not let this be a joke to you; they cast it outside even though it was not offered by their hands. For in every place, **Male and Female** <note>The union of masculine and feminine divine energies is essential for holiness in Kabbalah.</note> are not found unless the Divine Presence dwells between them. Therefore, it returns to this, as it is written: *With this shall Aaron come into the holy place*, so that Male and Female may be found. For this reason, a priest does not enter the sanctuary until he is married, so that he may be found in the proper "binding." Since he [Nadab/Abihu] was not married, he caused a defect "outside," and he was not found in the proper union. Because of this, confusion was found on that day for their prophets.

->**And it was** on the eighth day. Rabbi Yose opened and said:<-

> As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants for You, O God. <note>Psalms 42:2</note>

This refers to the **Assembly of Israel**, who desires and thirsts for the Holy One, blessed be He. And the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, is toward her, to be found within her. Therefore, whoever is wise must fear the Holy One, blessed be He, and appear before Him, for the "repair" <note>Tikkun</note> of all things requires showing action. Just as we see that when a man clings to a single union, his "repair" is set toward her. When he comes to serve before the Holy King, he is more [complete], and there is another union, for the Holy One, blessed be He, desires his love to be found in him. Whoever awakens a holy word, the Holy One, blessed be He, blesses him. And when He blesses him, this is what is said. Therefore, the Assembly of Israel thirsts for Him in that distress, like this deer that thirsts for water and rises above all. Thus, because she rises and is crowned...

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), specifically the beginning of the Torah portion "Shemini." The text explores the spiritual mechanics of the sacrifices brought by Aaron the High Priest to inaugurate the Tabernacle and atone for the Sin of the Golden Calf.</meta>

## Section: Shemini (The Eighth Day)

The Ancient One <note>original: *Saba de-chi*, referring to the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note> is invited over all of them, and this is very good. When he saw and they were illuminated, when he saw that the Ancient One appeared over all of them. Furthermore, when they are blessed through the Priests, Israel is blessed; and through the Priests, the Priests themselves are blessed by the Supernal Priest, the hidden Ancient One. **"And they shall put My name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them"** (Numbers 6:27). It is written: **"Remember, O Lord, Your tender mercies and Your lovingkindnesses, for they are from of old"** (Psalms 25:6). "Your tender mercies" refers to Jacob, and "Your lovingkindnesses" refers to Abraham. "For they are from of old"—the Holy One, blessed be He, took them from the beginning and raised them up on high, making of them a Holy Chariot <note>term: *Merkavah* (Chariot), a mystical structure of Divine attributes</note> to illuminate the world. Because they were "from of old," He remembers them to bring light and mercy to the world. In this same manner, He gathers the righteous from the world and raises them up to illuminate the world from above... to prevent the execution of punishment for the sins committed by His children. This is the meaning of **"Stir up Your might"** (Psalms 80:3) and it is written: **"And the Lord passed before his face and proclaimed"** (Exodus 34:6). The Holy One, blessed be He, etc. This is the comfort that rises from here.

Rabbi Hiyya said: "Remember Your tender mercies and Your lovingkindnesses"—these are Jacob and Abraham, whom we need to illuminate us at all times. To perform a sacrifice that stands and gathers, we need this prophecy. "For they are from of old"—when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He created it with Isaac <note>representing *Gevurah* or Judgment</note>, but He saw the world could not stand alone. He took Abraham <note>representing *Chesed* or Lovingkindness</note> and established the world with him. This is the meaning of: **"These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created"** (Genesis 2:4). Do not read it as "when they were created" (*be-hibare'am*), but rather "through Abraham" (*be-Abraham*). He saw they needed further establishment, so He took Jacob and joined him with Isaac, and the world was established. This is: **"In the day that the Lord God made earth and heaven"** (Genesis 2:4). Thus, through Abraham and Jacob, the world is sustained, and therefore "they are from of old."

Rabbi Yehuda opened: **"And it came to pass on the eighth day"** (Leviticus 9:1). This was to distinguish them from the seven days of inauguration. Perfection was crowned on this day, seeking to be distinguished from the seven through the Priest. Therefore, the service of perfection is crowned from the seven, to rectify the Priest for that which he sinned previously. This is why he said to Aaron: **"Take for yourself a young calf"** (Leviticus 9:2). This was surely to atone for the [Golden] Calf, as it is written: **"And they made a molten calf"** (Exodus 32:4). "A son of the herd"—what is a "son of the herd"? This is the son of a cow. But surely it needed to be rectified in relation to the "Cow" <note>referring to the Red Heifer, which atones for the Golden Calf</note>. It is not fitting to bring a gift to a King from the King's own property. Have you seen it written that one takes from the King and gives to the King? Rather, the gift you prepare for the King should come from another source, not from the King's own. Rabbi Yossi said: From his own to his own is not fitting. Rabbi Yehuda said: Therefore, it is "a son of the herd" specifically, and not a "son of a cow," for a sin offering, to purify that sin which he committed.

"And a ram for a burnt offering, without blemish." "Without blemish" (*temimim*, plural)—you might say this refers to both the ram and the calf, but both do not ascend as a burnt offering, for it is written "the calf for a sin offering." What then is "without blemish" (plural)? And it is written "a ram." Rather, these are the rams of Isaac, to be brought near to the "Cow." For the verse says: **"And Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, behind him a ram caught in a thicket by its horns"** (Genesis 22:13). And further: **"And Abraham went and took the ram."** This makes two. **"And offered it up for a burnt offering."** Thus, "a ram for a burnt offering, without blemish" refers to two. From here we learn of the "Mights" (*Gevurot*), and from them many others branch out.

**"And to the children of Israel you shall speak, saying: Take a kid of the goats for a sin offering, and a calf..."** (Leviticus 9:3). This is similar to the Priest's requirement, but for Israel, they received punishment. Regarding the calf for Israel, it does not say "a calf for a sin offering" but rather "for a burnt offering." For all those who sinned with it received their punishment, whether by plague, by the sword, or by the service [of the Levites]. But those who did not act wickedly, even if they elevated it in their hearts' desire to worship it—do not do so, as it is written "the sin of the children of Israel." But all those who elevated it in their desire, not to worship it, but who elevated it in the "will of wills"—through this, all are blessed and bring it as a burnt offering.

## Main Text (Zohar)

...above and not below. But they stood with a **goat for a sin offering** <note>Leviticus 9:3</note> to fulfill it. This was because they first brought [offerings] to appease the inner powers over the mountains of darkness, and this is the "sin offering." Because of this, he was found free from that sin, and furthermore, the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity in Kabbalah</term> was subdued.

---

**And an ox** and a ram for peace offerings <note>Leviticus 9:4</note>. An ox and a ram—a bull—because the ox represents a living force, to show peace; this is for the "peace offerings." Rabbi Yose said: The ox and the ram come from the Left Side <term>the attribute of Judgment/Gevurah</term>. The ox is from the Left Side, as it is written:
> And the face of an ox on the left side (Ezekiel 1:10)

The ram corresponds to the Ram of Isaac <note>the ram sacrificed in place of Isaac at the Akedah</note>, and they ascend as peace offerings to bring completion to the heart. Regarding "an ox and a ram for peace offerings," Rabbi Yehuda said: All of this is so that the Assembly of Israel <term>Knesset Yisrael: the spiritual personification of the Jewish people, often identified with the Shekhinah</term> may be crowned and blessed through the Priest, as is established. On that day, the joy of all was the joy of the Assembly of Israel in the **Holy One, Blessed be He**—a joy of the upper and lower worlds. It was like a wedding day. When the Priest below was perfected, as it were, the High Priest Above <term>the archangel Michael or the sefirah of Chesed</term> was perfected, except for the rebuke that was stirred up among the stars between the levels and the King. Because of this:
> And fire came out from before the Lord and consumed them... (Leviticus 10:2) <note>Referring to the death of Nadav and Avihu</note>

---

**And Moses said** to Eleazar and Ithamar: "Do not let your hair go untrimmed... for the Lord’s anointing oil is upon you" (Leviticus 10:6-7). Rabbi Abba said: We have learned that through actions below, actions are awakened above. An action below must appear in the likeness of the action above. Come and see: the joy above depends on that holy oil <note>the flow of divine emanation</note> from which joy and blessings go out to all the lamps. The High Priest is crowned by it according to the law of the rain. Therefore, the Priest who is great with anointing oil must have it move upon him; he must appear holy and precious in the likeness of the Above, more so than anyone else. No deficiency should be seen in his head or his garments, but rather he should remain entirely complete in the likeness of the Above. No blemish should be seen in him at all, so that he does not cause a blemish in another place <note>the spiritual realms</note>. Come and see: if, Heaven forbid, Eleazar and Ithamar had been seen with blemishes at that time in their garments or their heads, they would not have survived that hour, for that hour was set for the execution of Judgment. Regarding this we have learned: in a time when a plague occurs in the world, a wise man should not involve himself in worldly matters so that they [the judgments] are not stirred up against him—except for one who stirs himself for good and can press the hour. For the power and taste of Judgment stands in the world; whoever encounters it is seized by it and removed from the world. Because of this, it is written: **"that you do not die."** "But your brothers, the whole house of Israel, may weep for the burning" (Leviticus 10:6), because they do not come from the side of the Priesthood and were not prepared [in that same way].

Rabbi Eleazar opened:
> And Aaron took Elisheva, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Nahshon, as his wife (Exodus 6:23)

"And Aaron took." Everything was as it should be, a bride in the likeness of the Above. Come and see: "And he took" refers to the Six <term>the six emotional sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</term>. Bathsheba was destined for David from the day the world was created. So too, Elisheva was fitting for Aaron from the day the world was created. What is the difference between these [couples]? They are all one. But there <note>David and Bathsheba</note> it was for Judgment, and here <note>Aaron and Elisheva</note> it was for Mercy. When they are joined as one, the mercies approach to unify the waters. Here, a Priest came to mate with a Priestess <note>Elisheva's name contains "El," God</note> to subdue that which was found. Therefore she is called thus. There, Bathsheba is seen as "Seven" <note>Sheva</note> to be joined in Kindness <term>Chesed</term>. Come, Bathsheba is for Judgment, for the moon, for the Kingdom <term>Malchut</term>, and for strength. Rabbi Shimon said: That which we learned, as it is written, **the sound of the Shofar** (Exodus 19:19), is beautiful. This is Jacob, who ascended in Thought to Wisdom <term>Chokhmah</term>, and they emerged as one from within the Shofar. For the Shofar brings out water, fire, and spirit as one, and from them, a voice is made. So the **Supernal Mother** <term>Imma Ila'ah: the sefirah of Binah, symbolized by the Shofar</term> brings out Wisdom in one voice, and from Thought they ascend together as one voice. That voice is called "the sound of the Shofar," and this is Jacob <term>Tiferet</term> who includes Wisdom as one. They are called "Voice" more than all other voices, for from the Voice, a voice emerges, and every single voice is called "the sound of the Shofar." From here, the rest of the voices emerge from within the sound of the Shofar in the manner of approaching...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Eighth<-
<note>Hebrew: Shemini. The name of the Torah portion covering Leviticus 9:1–11:47.</note>

...of Thought and the seven voices that emerge from the union of Thought like a shofar <note>a ram's horn trumpet</note>; and this shofar prepares them and casts them to the wise first, and later to the many, and every word is wisdom. Come and see: *And Aaron took Elisheba* <note>Exodus 6:23</note> for the Assembly of Israel, to cause her to dwell in the wilderness. This was not like a king whose union is divided; rather, blessings are found for all the worlds through the hand of Aaron. Because of this, the Priest must be found with a radiance of countenance <note>term: Nehiro de-Anpin; a state of joy and divine favor</note> and in joy, just like the pattern above, so that through his hands blessings and joys are found. Therefore, no judgment, anger, or sadness should be seen from him, so that the keys of permission do not turn away from the attachment of the Body. And regarding this:

> *And let all the house of Israel bewail the burning which the Lord has kindled.* <note>Leviticus 10:6</note>

Concerning them it is written: "When the Lord remembered the labor and the work of His hands, they shall sing," etc.

> *Drink no wine nor strong drink, you nor your sons with you...* <note>Leviticus 10:9</note>

Rabbi Yehuda opened this discourse: I have heard from all the sages hidden secrets regarding this—why this one is blocked and acquired and blocked. Rabbi Chiya opened:

> *And wine that makes glad the heart of man...* <note>Psalms 104:15</note>

Behold, the Priest must rejoice and be found with a radiance of countenance more than anyone else; he should have wine to gladden him, for behold, joy is found in it and the radiance of countenance is found in it. However, the beginning of wine is joy, but its end is sadness. Furthermore, wine comes from the side of the Levite <note>the "Left Side" of the Sefirotic tree, associated with Gevurah/Judgment</note>, for this wine is red. For behold, whiteness <note>associated with the Priest/Chesed</note> and red wine—red wine is from the side of Severity <note>Gevurah</note>. And the side of the Priest is entirely disqualified from wine. Rabbi Yossi said: Each one is seen according to its measure, and everything is included one in the other. Red wine is a measure because everything comes from the water to the Crown, to the return, and the Ancient One <note>Atika</note> is hidden, and therein sits Judgment. But the Priest is the beginning and the end; he requires joy and radiance of countenance. Rabbi Abba said: From this one path, they add pure water, and the King is water, and the sign of everything is like this:

> *Like the precious oil...* <note>Psalms 133:2</note>

...more than anything. For the pressure of joy is the beginning and the end, as it is written: *Like the precious oil upon the head, running down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron.* And wine is for rejoicing, bread is the voice, to gladden and not to be silent; for behold, wine is never silent, and the sign is like one who whispers and speaks constantly. What is the difference between this and that? Rather, the sign of the Levite is like a whisper, speaking constantly from the side of Thought, which is found in them as a constant speaking that is not heard, speaking in a whisper, and therefore he is on the right. But wine is pressed to renew the voice; it is never silent and comes from the side of Mercy <note>Chesed</note> and they inherit it to the left side, and they stand to renew the voice and stand in Judgment. Because of this, it is written:

> *And by their word shall every strife and every plague be tried.* <note>Deuteronomy 21:5</note>

Therefore, when the Priest enters the Sanctuary to perform the service, it is forbidden for him to drink wine, for behold, his works are in a whisper <note>silence</note>, and they and the Priest are directed and intended just as the union is intended for the one who unites, drawing down blessings to all the worlds, and everything is in a whisper. Furthermore, all his works are in mystery and darkness <note>hiddenness</note> from the revelation of secrets, for all his works are a voice of praise. Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yitzchak were walking on the road from Meron to Sepphoris, and a young man was walking before them with wine in a traveler's flask. Rabbi Yehuda said: How great is the matter of whiteness and everything. Rabbi Yitzchak opened and said:

> *And your palate like the best wine, that goes down smoothly for my beloved...* <note>Song of Songs 7:10</note>

"And your palate like the best wine"—this is the red wine of the Levite which is good, for behold, it can go to my beloved in a good mercy, and the red wine is for everyone. It is good for this world and good for the world to come, and this is what is proven to be received more than anything. And they merit these words that hint at the life of the whites <note>the righteous</note> that will be awakened in the world to come, and he will prove it to the living when the Holy One, blessed be He, grants merit to the righteous. Rabbi Yehuda said:

> *...causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.* <note>Song of Songs 7:10</note>

Behold, this establishes that even in that world, they will merit to labor in the Torah, as it says, "causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak." That young man said: It is written "And your palate like the best wine." I say this: it is written "like the best wine" and not from wine that defiles the vessel. Rabbi Yehuda said: My son, may you live, for you have spoken well; the wine of the palate that I heard is the fear of those who labor in the Torah, and it is refined here and there, and it is a matter of whiteness... <unclear>not to be burdened like a plague</unclear>.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on Parashat Shemini, focusing on the hidden mechanics of creation and the symbolic meaning of the "Great Sea Monsters."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

In a whisper <note>original: *be-lachishu*</note>, a voice is hidden; a voice that is held within. Thus it is necessary to raise the voice, as it is written: *At the head of the noisy streets* <note>Proverbs 1:21</note> *she calls out.* One must raise the voice of that which is held, and not in a whisper. Since "Good" was said of it, it is not silent, and it is destined to raise its voice. As it is written: *Flowing smoothly for my beloved, stirring the lips of those who sleep* <note>Song of Songs 7:10</note>. For it is known that even in that world, their lips murmur the Torah. Furthermore, we have learned: "The Good Wine"—this is the voice of the Assembly of Israel <note>The Sefirah of Malkhut</note> as it is said in the *Tosefta*. If so, who is it that leads it in a whisper? If it is difficult, what is the meaning of *flowing for my beloved*? It should have said "flowing to me."

Rather, certainly, the Holy One <note>original: *Kudsha Berich Hu*</note> leads it to the Assembly of Israel, just as He leads it there, as it is written: *His palate is sweetness* <note>Song of Songs 5:16</note>. So too, the Holy One leads it to the Assembly of Israel, as it is written: *And your palate is like the good wine* <note>Song of Songs 7:10</note>. And "good wine" is that which speaks from within. *Flowing for my beloved*—this is Isaac <note>representing the attribute of Gevurah/Judgment</note>, for he is called "Beloved" <note>original: *Yedid*</note> from the side of the Father, to lead the Bride there. She is prepared to be led, to include the Left within the Right. And this was the leading: because of the fragrance of that good oil, the Left was included in the Right, and they were all sweetened. *Stirring the lips of those who sleep*—for they all ascend through their fragrances and their speech, and all the worlds are found in joy and ascend to be crowned with blessings below.

Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Isaac came and kissed his hands and traveled with him. They said: "What is your name?" He said: "Yishai." They said: "May Rabbi Yossei be comforted." And they further asked: "Is there another Yishai in the world?" <note>referring to the father of King David</note>. He said: "From the word *Yishai* <note>meaning 'existence' or 'wealth'</note>, which is a blessing to be removed from poverty." They said to him: "From whom did you learn to depart from the world?" He was a sharp man and a master of the lodging-place of the Torah, and he possessed three matters of wisdom and Haggadah. And they received words of learning from him. And now, he dwells among every person and ascends to me from the Torah, and he goes every day to his work, and every day I review those words of learning from him. They said: "Does that man know the Torah?" He said to them: "That Yishai was wise, but he did not know how to bless the Holy One, and he has a son, but they were not like the sons of a Great Master."

"If the image is established, it was because I was cast toward that child to speak with you." He opened and said: "It is beautiful for us to see his wings." He said: "Go with us." They said to him: "Who was he?" He said: "Rabbi Zeira of the village of Samin." Rabbi Yehuda heard and wept. He said: "Merit is the portion of his house! I have learned from him three matters in the secret of the blessing, and I have learned from him two matters in the Work of Creation." Rabbi Isaac said: "And what of the whisper? And in it, I have learned the secret of the beginning. From him, I saw this." They returned and held his hands until he turned and sat there. He said to him: "Tell us one thing from what he taught you regarding the Work of Creation."

He opened and said: *And God created the great sea monsters...* <note>Genesis 1:21</note>. *And God created*—every place requires the name *Elohim* <note>the name associated with Judgment</note>. And that upper place from which they emerge is also called by this name. And even though it is Mercy, from it emerge Judgments, and they depend upon it. *The great sea monsters*—these are the Leviathans, for they were established at the beginning and they rule over all. And there is *every living soul that creeps*. And there is *every living soul*—this is the soul of that Upper Tree <note>the Sefirotic structure</note> that turns from that upper life-force over all, as it is written: *Let the earth bring forth a living soul* <note>Genesis 1:24</note>. This is the soul of the Primordial Man <note>Adam Kadmon</note> who is drawn in color. *That creeps*—this is the living beast that moves through all the mountains <margin>meaning: sides</margin> above and below. *Which the waters brought forth*—this is the upper water that flows and emerges from Eden and waters that tree to be completed in its roots over all, and to find within it sustenance for all. This is *that creeps*—this is King David, of whom it is written: *My soul thirsts for the living God* <note>Psalms 42:3</note>. *And every winged bird according to its kind*—these are all those holy angels who are found to sanctify the name of their Master every single day, as it is written of them: *Each had six wings, six wings* <note>Isaiah 6:2</note>. And they are the messengers in the world to do the will of their Master, each one as is fitting. Rabbi Yehuda said: "Certainly, all the secrets of the heart were not revealed here, for how much is hidden within it, so that the Upper Secret may ascend." Rabbi Isaac said: "Certainly..."

It frames these teachings through a narrative encounter between Sages and a mysterious traveler named Yishai.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of spiritual purity and the mystical significance of wine, following the themes of Parashat Shemini (the eighth day of the Tabernacle's consecration). It focuses on the correspondence between earthly actions and the celestial realms.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And this, see the distinction: this is indeed the world above all, for the other is called the "Holy Land" here, as it is written: **"And let the birds multiply in the land"** <note>Genesis 1:22</note>. And "in the land" certainly, and not like that river which flows and goes out and waters everything <note>referring to the divine flow from Eden</note>—the explanation is until that place called "Land," and from there it is written: **"and from there it parted..."** <note>Genesis 2:10</note>. And the "birds"—the birds of this Land depend on it and are sustained by it, and this is what is written: **"And let the birds multiply in the land"** before Him and the mundane. Rabbi Judah said: When you are at the table of the Master <note>referring to a meal or a gathering of scholars</note>, each and every one should say a word of Torah. Rabbi Judah opened and said: **"Stay me with dainties, refresh me with apples..."** <note>Song of Songs 2:5</note>. This verse has already been explained and permitted to all, for it refers to the Congregation of Israel <note>the *Shekhinah* or Divine Presence</note>. What is "stay me" (*samkhuni*)? Rather, one who falls needs to be supported (*le-asmakha*), as it is written: **"The Lord upholds all who fall..."** <note>Psalms 145:14</note>. And because of this, regarding her <note>the *Shekhinah*</note> it is written: **"She has fallen, she shall rise no more"** <note>Amos 5:2</note>—she needs to be supported and aided by another. "Stay me"—for whom? For Israel, for the Congregation of Israel who are with her. And how "with apples"? These are the Patriarchs <note>Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, representing the divine attributes of Mercy, Strength, and Beauty</note> who were filled first from that good fruit which is blessed. And whoever knows how to unify the Holy Name, even if the strength is not found in the world, he supports and assists the Congregation of Israel. "Refresh me with apples"—it is all one, as we have said: to every spirit that takes hold and enters, he says "apple," he brings out wine and directs his will, and regarding this: "closed" and "apples." "Closed" for the expansion of speech; "apples" to direct the will so that the word is not harmed. And all this why? **"For I am lovesick."** And one who says the Holy Name must unify it so that he is a son of the "water" <note>purity/mercy</note> and to empower them as is fitting, to be sweetened and strengthened as is proper, and this supports the Congregation of Israel.

Rabbi Isaac opened and said: "Milk and like it we shall hope for, times of wine..." <note>referring to the different grades of spiritual light</note>. Fortunate are Israel for they are holy, and everything requires them to be sanctified. Come and see: Holy Israel, all the life of the worlds is their inheritance; everything depends on that "World to Come" <note><term>World to Come</term>: In the Zohar, this often refers to the Sephirah of *Binah* (Understanding), the source of life and liberation</note>, because the life of everything above and below is spared there. And from that place of the **guarded wine** <note><term>Guarded Wine</term>: *Yayin ha-Meshumar*, the primordial wine kept in its grapes since the six days of Creation, representing deep mystical secrets and divine joy</note> which is called "Wine," from there life and holiness go out to all. And the wine of Israel is like the wine of the "other side" <note>the side of impurity</note>, and all this depends on it, for Israel above is like the shadow of life. And because of this, it is called the "Tree of Life"—a tree from that place called "Life," and the face of life. And for this reason, we bless the Holy One, Blessed be He, over wine, and the wine of the "other side" below is in this manner. Those who look upon it, and whoever comes close to it, will find all honor like the wine of Israel—this is found and lacking when that wine is made.

And do not say that this is alone, but rather everything that Israel does below is all in the likeness of the pattern above. The wine that is poured is like the upper place, the pattern of the **guarded wine**. Because of this, Israel drinks the wine of Israel which is prepared as is fitting in holiness, in the likeness of Israel above who are hidden and rooted and blessed by that supernal holy wine. And this is the "hidden wine" that is prepared in Thought <note><term>Thought</term>: *Machshavah*, the highest level of divine consciousness</note> and the guard of Thought, for the cup is the secret of the spirit of Thought. And this is the side of Israel; but one who goes with "them" <note>the side of impurity</note>, his spirit is defiled and his soul is dragged down, and he has no portion in the World to Come. For that World to Come is the **guarded wine**, and therefore the holy people must guard this above all, so that they may be bound to the place of the World to Come.

And because of this, since the Holy One, Blessed be He, blessed more than the whole, because He rejoices in the side of fullness, and His joy is to be included in the "Right Side" <note>the side of Mercy/Chessed</note>. And when everything is prepared, the Right Side is then happy, the Holy One rejoices in joy, and blessings are found in all worlds. And the son below must awaken the action above. Therefore, we dilute wine against wine <note>mixing wine with water to temper judgment with mercy</note>. And because it is "guarded" above, one must guard it below. And all his guarding is holiness for Israel. And one who blemishes it below, on the side of impurity, he will be found in this world but will have no portion in the World to Come, the place where that **guarded wine** dwells. If he did not guard it here, he will not be guarded for the World to Come.

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Shemini from the Zohar, Volume III.
