## Eighth (Shemini)

->Eighth<-

He considered that they should support him in that world; this gave him a portion in that supernal wine that comes <note>original: "יין דלעילא" - referring to the mystical wine of the world to come, often associated with the Sefirah of Binah</note>. Righteous are the people of Israel who crown the One who crowns them and sanctifies the King with these supernal crowns. They are meritorious in this world and in the world to come. That youth opened his discourse and said: *“A king by justice establishes the land...”* <note>Proverbs 29:4</note>. This “King” is the Holy One, blessed be He. “By justice” <note>original: "במשפט" - Mishpat</note> refers to Jacob, who is the synthesis of the Patriarchs. *“...but a man of gifts [terumot] overthrows it.”* It is written “Gifts” <note>Terumot</note>, as in *“And this is the offering [terumah]”* <note>Exodus 25:3</note>. “A man of gifts” refers to Esau, who inquires about offerings and tithes every day but does nothing. Their “man of gifts” is judgment, for the offering <note>Terumah/Malchut</note> is removed from mercy; therefore, it does not come through justice properly, and the secret of the matter is “without justice.” On this account, “a man of gifts overthrows it.” And if you say that King David possessed this “offering,” it was only through mercy. Furthermore, it is written: *“The sure mercies of David”* <note>Isaiah 55:3</note>; just as he cleaved to this, he cleaved to that. Come and see: every day King David strove so that the “offering” would be bound to “justice” <note>Mishpat</note> and they would be joined as one, so that the world would be sustained through a single desire. He joined them as one, and it stood called “in kindness,” and death was stayed by his will. Then Zedekiah came and separated them, and the land was found without justice; the moon <note>symbolizing Malchut</note> was diminished and the land was embittered. Then, “a man of gifts overthrows it.”

Come and see: oil is for the Priests and wine is for the Levites. This is because they require this from the wine that crowns it, to prepare their connection toward the Whole, so that all the worlds should not be found [lacking], but rather right and left included in one another. Thus, the love of all and the mercy of the faithful is found. For one whose desire cleaves to this, he is complete in this and in that, and in all those things to come. All his days he shall be determined to cleave to Repentance <note>Teshuvah</note> after judgment and time are found. Then he will not be left behind this world, neither for its wealth nor for its shame. King Solomon was a shadow <note>perhaps meaning a reflection of supernal wisdom</note> and said to him: May the Holy One grant that this time shall crown him, for wealth and wine shall be prepared for him to have a portion in it, and to have a portion in the world to come, after judgment and time dwell in this world and the world to come. And one who runs to this place does not desire wealth nor pursue it. Praised are the righteous who strive for this supernal wealth, the day of which it is written: *“Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor can it be exchanged for vessels of fine gold”* <note>Job 28:17</note>. He who merits this supernal [wisdom] will merit to enter this sea and its light to rest.

He opened [the discourse] and said: *“And the Lord said to Moses, ‘Come up to Me on the mountain...’”* <note>Exodus 24:12</note>. *“...and the Torah”*—this is the Written Torah. *“...and the commandment”*—this is the Oral Torah. For there it is written deficiently <note>referring to a spelling variation</note>, as it says, “and to the glory of my beams.” Here one must look: to whom was the instruction given? If you say the instruction was for Israel, it would be so; but Israel did not go into this [division]. Rather, it is the instruction of the Torah and the commandments. And what is this? It is the wine that crowns, for every writing of the Supernal Book dwells there, and from there the Torah emerges. Therefore, we call it the “Written Torah.” And is it not “which I have written to teach them”? “To teach them” <note>le-horotam</note> certainly includes everything, and it does not lack the “beams” of the Oral Torah—another Torah that stands upon the “mouth” <note>Pe/Oral</note>. Who is this “Mouth”? This is Knowledge <note>Da’at</note>, which is the mouth of the Book and the Writing. And this Torah is another Torah to investigate, the Oral Torah which stands upon the “Mouth,” which is the mouth of the Written Torah. Because of this, the staff is raised above all, lacking like the faithful ones, as it is written: *“And it shall be given to you”*—specifically “to you.” It is written: *“Get you wise men, and understanding, and known among your tribes, and I will make them heads over you”* <note>Deuteronomy 1:13</note>, all of them.

Come and see the claim of the enemies: the wicked are liable in the world when they assist the Holy King to be established in judgment and to be found <margin>what is "and be found"</margin> according to His law, and the worlds would be burned. And like the error of those who are drunk, the wicked [are removed] from the world; then they shall be established in kindness—in all of them, in kindness and not in judgment. Come and see: the appointed times of error, for the cause of the Torah depends on the Supernal World, and the Supernal World [acts] according to the ways of the lower world. And they shall all be established in kindness.

<meta>This page begins the commentary on Parashat Shemini (Leviticus 11), focusing on the spiritual implications of dietary laws. It follows the previous discussions on the priesthood and transitions into the distinction between the pure and the impure.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

In His name. He who desires to bless Him in a place where it is not written. Why "defiles, defiles"? For when he enters from his house to the Holy Temple, his judgment is as one who is at rest; he shall not enter with wine, which is **Severity** <note>original: *Gevurah*; the divine attribute of judgment and restraint</note>. He should enter with water <note>representing Mercy</note> and not enter with wine. Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Isaac taught: regarding the "Head" <note>a title for a great scholar</note> who startles the day, he was distinguished in the house of Rabbi Yehuda. When he would enter the House of Study, Rabbi Yehuda would stand before him and say: "I have learned a word from him: 'And this is the blessing' <note>Deuteronomy 33:1</note> when it is precious." Afterward, he departed from among the companions, and they called him Rabbi Yossi, "The Head of the Hammer" <note>Aramaic: *Reisha de-Patisha*</note> who breaks rocks and brings forth sparks to every side. Rabbi Eleazar applied this verse to him: "As a beloved mountain, like my children and your mind."

---

->**And He Spoke**<-
The Lord to Moses and to Aaron, saying to them: "These are the living things which you may eat..."
<note>Leviticus 11:1-2</note>

Why is Aaron mentioned here? It is because he stands constantly to separate between the impure <note>original: *mesava*</note> and the pure <note>original: *dachya*</note>, as it is written: "To distinguish between the unclean and the clean." Rabbi Abba opened his discourse and said:
> "Who is the man who desires life... Guard your tongue from evil... Turn away from evil..."
<note>Psalms 34:13-15</note>
And it is written:
> "He who guards his mouth and his tongue..."
<note>Proverbs 21:23</note>

"Who is the man who desires life?" What is this "life"? This refers to the life engraved in the World to Come, where life dwells. Concerning this, we have learned: "It is a **Tree of Life**" <note>Proverbs 3:18</note>; these are the lives of the Tree that is planted by those waters. Therefore, it is written: "Who is the man who desires life?" "Who loves days, that he may see good"—which days are these? This is the Name of the Holy King, which takes hold of those Supernal Days called "the days of heaven upon the earth." Furthermore, it is certainly "upon the earth." One who desires the life above must acquire a portion in them. And one who desires days to be sweetened by them and to walk in them must guard his mouth from everything; he must guard his mouth from food and drink that defiles the soul <note>original: *nefsha*</note>. Such things distance a person from those lives and those days. He must guard his mouth from evil words so that he is not defiled by them, and he should be distanced from them and have no portion in them. Come and see: a "foreign place" <note>the side of impurity</note> enters him in this way, and therefore he should not bring a "guest" into his mouth <note>referring to forbidden food</note>, and certainly not defile his soul and his body, for he then finds himself in the "other world" <note>the realm of the Sitra Achra</note> and stands there.

**"These are the living things which you may eat from among all the beasts..."**
This "taking hold" is a secret; this mouth and the "clinging" of the head. "These are the living things" comes first, and afterward "from among all the beasts." Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: "At all times that Israel guards their souls and their bodies from eating these [forbidden things], then certainly 'these are the living things which you may eat'—they shall be pure in holiness to cleave to My Name." Through the clarity of that which is clear for you to eat, you will not be defiled by them and you will cleave to My Name. But whenever they do not guard their souls and bodies from [impure] food and drink, they cleave to the "Other Side," the impure, to be defiled by them. Because of this, it is written: "These are the living things which you may eat from all." "From all" <note>original: *mi-kol*</note> is certainly the secret of the Holy Name to cleave to it. "From all the beasts that are upon the earth"—because this food comes from a pure place and does not defile the heart, you shall have a portion in My Name to cleave to it. Furthermore: "These are the living things which you may eat." Regarding Pharaoh, it is written:
> "By this <note>original: *be-zot*</note> you shall know that I am the Lord."
<note>Exodus 7:17</note>
Behold, "this" <note>the attribute of Justice</note> stands against you to take vengeance upon you. So too here: "This <note>zot</note> is the living thing which you may eat..." Behold, "this" stands against you to take vengeance from you if you become defiled, and in shame it will be, for the soul comes from it. If you become defiled, that which belongs to "Her" <note>the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note>, this "This" (*Zot*), stands against you to establish a covenant against you. But the righteous stand in their prophecy. Rabbi Eleazar said: "These are the living things which you may eat from all the beasts"—from all those that take hold from this side <note>the side of holiness</note>, it is permitted for you to eat. But all those that do not come from this side...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the spiritual laws of kashrut (dietary laws) from the previous section, focusing on the ontological difference between "pure" and "impure" sources of life and their impact on the human soul.</meta>

->Shemini<-
<note>The name of the Torah portion, meaning "Eighth"</note>

## Main Text (Zohar)

From the side that is not forbidden for you to eat, for there are animals below from this side, and there are those below from the other, impure side <note>original: *sitra achra*, the "other side" or realm of evil</note>, and their food [is likewise]. As it is written: *Every animal that has a parted hoof and is cloven-footed...* <note>Leviticus 11:3</note> they are similar, and all of them are according to the pattern of the verses. And thus, anyone who eats from those that come from this impure side becomes defiled by them and defiles his soul, for they come from the side of this [impure] throne. It says that the whole is included because there are ten crowns of faith above <note>The ten *Sefirot* or divine emanations of the holy realm</note>, and likewise there are ten crowns of impure sorcery below. Everything that is on the earth is nourished either from this side or from that side. 

And if you say: this goat or bee, or the fruit and the bear—is it that the impure life-force dwells within them, making it forbidden for us to eat? Even though they act for their sake and are given over to them, their [impure] spirit does not rest upon all of them in the same way. Rather, another spirit passes over them and they are separated from them. Therefore, they are given over to them and they are prosecuted because of them, but they do not rule over them like the leopards, and because of this, it is permitted to eat [certain species]. 

Come and see: since they come to curse through them, and an evil spirit passes and fixes the eyes and shows signs to them, they are separated from them below. It is not forbidden for us to eat, whether among cattle, wild beasts, birds, or fish of the sea; they are all seen and proven through Mercy and Judgment. Everything that comes from the side of the Right <note>The side of *Chesed* or Lovingkindness</note>, from the side of Mercy, is permitted for us to eat. But all those that come from the side of Samael <note>The primary archangel of the "Other Side"</note>, from the side of [harsh] Judgment, are all forbidden for us to eat. This is because their cause is entirely impurity, and they are all destroyers, and an impure spirit rests upon their children and dwells within them. 

For this reason, the Holy Spirit of Israel shall not be mixed with them and shall not be defiled by them, so that they may be found holy and be supported above and below. Fortunate is the portion of Israel, whom the Holy King desired and wished to purify and sanctify above all, because they take hold of Him. Come and see, it is written:
> *And you shall sanctify yourselves, and you shall be holy; for I am holy* <note>Leviticus 11:44</note>
In this side—in the side of those who come to be defiled and entangled in the impure side—concerning this it is written: *And you shall sanctify yourselves, and you shall be holy; for I am holy, and you shall not defile your souls...* One who dwells in the image of the King should not separate himself from the King's portion. Because of this, the Holy One, blessed be He, loves Israel. All those who come from the side of Life [are for Israel], and all those who come from the Other Side are cast away from the portion of Israel, as it is written of them:
> *Every moving thing that lives shall be food for you; as the green herb I have given you all things* <note>Genesis 9:3; the Zohar notes this was the decree for the sons of Noah, but Israel is held to a higher standard of holiness</note>
Water • In You, O Lord, are all of them. And come and see: anyone who eats of those forbidden foods clings to the Other Side and becomes flawed and deceptive, and an impure spirit rests upon him. He shows that his body has no portion in the Supreme God, and he does not come from His side and does not cling to Him. If he departs from the world, all those who take hold of the side of impurity grab him and defile him, judging him like a person who sinned against his Master. He is punished in this world and punished in the World to Come. 

Regarding this it is written: *And you shall be defiled by them* <note>Leviticus 11:43; the Hebrew word *ve-nitmetem* is written without the letter Aleph, which the Zohar interprets as "you shall be blocked/dulled"</note>—without an Aleph—meaning there is no remedy to cleanse him, and he never leaves his impurity. Woe to them, woe to their souls, for they shall not cling to the Bond of Life <note>term: *Tzeror ha-Chayyim* — the collective treasury of holy souls in the afterlife</note> forever, for they have been defiled. Woe to their bodies, for of them it is written:
> *For their worm shall not die... and they shall be an abhorrence to all flesh* <note>Isaiah 66:24</note>
What caused this for them? May the Merciful One protect us. 
That side to which Israel clings is the side of the Right; they are "Living" and cling to the Side of Life. They are internal to themselves and internal to their souls, just as they are internal in this world and internal in the World to Come. Anyone who clings to the side of impurity is separate from all, not according to the law. And it is written:
> *For you are a holy people to the Lord your God...* <note>Deuteronomy 7:6</note>

Rabbi Yose opened and said:
> *All the labor of man is for his mouth...* <note>Ecclesiastes 6:7</note>
I have looked at this verse. The King and all of them take hold of the Supreme Wisdom <note>term: *Chokhmah Ila'ah* — the second Sefirah, representing the flash of divine intuition</note>. *All the labor of man is for his mouth*—this verse is according to the knowledge of those who judge him...

It contrasts the "Side of Life" belonging to Israel with the "Side of Death" and impurity that leads to punishment in both worlds.</summary>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on Parashat Shemini (Leviticus 9-11), which focuses on dietary laws and ritual purity, and transitions into Parashat Tazria (Leviticus 12-13), concerning childbirth and skin afflictions. ## Main Text (Zohar - End of Parashat Shemini)

For a person in this world, it is written that the entire "Torah of the Serpent" <note>The mystical influence of evil or the "Other Side"</note> and all those who surround the world and take from it, [do so] because of the mouth of the world. Because one does not guard their mouth, it drags their soul down and they do not cleave to the Side of Life, the side of the Living God. And it is written: **"The serpent you shall not eat"** <note>original: *v'et hanachash lo tochelu*</note>, meaning you shall not inherit them or be repaid by them forever and ever. This "you shall not eat" means you shall not join with the "External Forces" <note>The *Sitra Achra* or "Other Side"</note> to be connected to them forever, because they turn away from the Presence and cling to the other side. Rabbi Isaac said: All those who participate in these [forbidden foods] are like bread for the "Impure Beast" of the Lord, and it is written: **"You shall not eat any abomination."** <note>Deuteronomy 14:3</note> Those who serve foreign gods and leave the Side of Life depart from the Holy Domain and enter the Other Domain. So too, those who participate in these [forbidden] foods depart from the Side of Life and the Holy Domain and enter the Other Domain. Furthermore, those who participate in them in this world and the world to come, it is written of them: **"And you shall be defiled by them"** <note>Leviticus 11:43</note>, written without the letter *Aleph* <note>The Zohar notes the Hebrew word *v'nitmetem* is spelled defectively, implying a "blockage" or "dulling" of the heart/soul</note>. And it is written: **"You shall not defile your souls with any animal or bird or anything that creeps on the ground, which I have set apart for you as unclean."** One brings uncleanness upon uncleanness. Therefore, make for yourselves a sign: if they are meritorious, they come from the side of the Holy Angel, and each one clings to its place.

Rabbi Eleazar was sitting before Rabbi Hiyya and said to him: We have learned that in the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will purify Israel. With what? He replied: As it is written: **"I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean..."** <note>Ezekiel 36:25</note> Once they are purified, they become sanctified, and through the purity with which the Holy One, Blessed be He, purifies them, they are called "Holy." As it is written: **"Israel is holy to the Lord, the firstfruits of His harvest."** <note>Jeremiah 2:3</note> And it is written: **"And you shall be holy people to Me."** <note>Exodus 22:30</note> All these are Israel, whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, called "Supreme," saying: **"You shall be holy, for I the Lord am holy,"** because it is written: **"And to Him you shall cleave."** And it is written: **"He has not done so for any other nation; and as for His ordinances, they have not known them. Hallelujah."** <note>Psalms 147:20</note>

---

-> **The Faithful Shepherd** <-
<note>The *Raya Mehemna* is a later layer of the Zohar where Moses, the "Faithful Shepherd," reveals secrets to the rabbis.</note>

**Fish** and locusts do not require ritual slaughter <note>Hebrew: *shechitah*</note>, rather their gathering is their death. So too, the "Masters of the Academy" <note>Aramaic: *Marei Metivta* - great scholars</note> do not require slaughter, but rather their preparation is through knowledge <note>term: *Da'at* - mystical knowledge/connection</note>. They are considered like the fish of the sea; in the "Day of Light" <note>The era of redemption</note>, these Masters of the Academy—their deaths are their standing in the Torah, and they do not depart from it into the profane. Those of perfect knowledge are increased through them... they know the "taste" of the secrets. They are like the "Great Fish" <note>The Leviathan</note> mentioned by the Prophet Ezekiel, dwelling in the midst of the rivers. Among the children of the Academy, there is no dispute, for they all draw from the same source.

---

-> # Parashat Tazria <-

**And the Lord spoke** to Moses, saying: **"If a woman conceives and bears a male child..."** <note>Leviticus 12:1-2</note> Rabbi Eleazar opened [the discussion] with the verse: **"Upon my bed at night I sought him whom my soul loves..."** <note>Song of Songs 3:1</note> He asked: It should have said "In my bed" <note>Aramaic: *be-mishkavi*</note>, why does it say **"Upon my bed"** <note>Aramaic: *al mishkavi*</note>? It is because the Assembly of Israel <note>The *Shekhinah* or Divine Presence</note> speaks before the Holy One, Blessed be He, regarding the Exile. Because she dwells among the other nations with her assembly, lowered to the dust, and because she lies in a defiled foreign land, she says "Upon my bed," like one who is impoverished and in exile. And because of this, **"I sought him whom my soul loves"**—to seek Him out of the strength of longing, yet **"I sought him but I found him not,"** for it was not the time for the [divine] union.

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on the Torah portion Shemini (Leviticus 9-11) and begins the portion Tazria (Leviticus 12-13). ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Shemini (Eighth)**<-

...for these are in the neck. "I called him, but he gave me no answer" <note>Song of Songs 5:6</note>. For behold, I dwell among other nations and they do not hear the voice, but only the nickname <note>the external manifestation</note>, as it is written: *“Has a people ever heard the voice of God...”* <note>Deuteronomy 4:33</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: **"Upon my bed at night"** <note>Song of Songs 3:1</note>, the Assembly of Israel <term>Knesset Yisrael: the mystical personification of the Jewish people and the Shekhinah</term> said: "Upon my bed I complain before Him, that He should unite with me in my Sanctuary and I shall bless Him with perfect joy." For so we have learned: the union of the King <note>The Holy One, Blessed be He</note> occurs only when many righteous ones and the two holy Jerusalems below are found in the world. Rabbi Abba was traveling to the village of Kanos (others say Parakpos) toward the cave of Lod, and Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hiyya were with him. Rabbi Yose said: It is written, **"A woman of valor is the crown of her husband"** <note>Proverbs 12:4</note>. "A woman of valor"—this refers to the Assembly of Israel. And in the firmament, there is a cloud from the side of evil. These are Amon and Moab, whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, cannot tolerate in the world, as it is said, and we see in the end that these are thorns and thistles that press Him outward, and He cannot endure them.

Rabbi Abba said: "A woman of valor"—this is the Assembly of Israel, for she is guarded by many types of weapons and many watches that are found in the world. **"The crown of her husband"**—as it is said, *“A crown of glory,”* and it is all one. "A woman of valor"—for behold, in the union with the King, she grasps many hosts, many watches, and many righteous ones in the world, and they all call out to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and to her, as it is written: *“On the day of his wedding”* <note>Song of Songs 3:11</note>, **my friends**. While they were walking, Rabbi Abba saw each one say a word regarding this. Rabbi Abba opened and said: **"A woman of valor, who can find?"** <note>Proverbs 31:10</note>. It is not a matter of difficulty; "A woman of valor" is as we have said. "Who can find"—as it is said, *“That which shall befall you in the end of days”* <note>Genesis 49:1</note>. "Who can find"—to wage war through her. "Who can find"—who shall merit to be with her in exile and to be found with her constantly?

**"Her value is far beyond pearls."** Her value <note>original: *mekherah*, which can also mean 'her sale'</note>. From her place, she shines for him. But for all those who are not found with her in exile and are not complete in their order, she "sells" them and delivers them into the hand of other nations. As it is said: *“And the children of Israel sold [themselves] to the Lord”* and *“He sold them into the hand of Sisera”* <note>Judges 4:2</note>. And then they are all far from those supernal holy pearls <note>the divine emanations</note> that do not give them sustenance, because she is "valor," and "her value is far beyond pearls." Rabbi Hiyya opened the following verse and said: **"The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he shall lack no spoil."** "The heart of her husband trusts in her"—this is the Holy One, Blessed be He, for because of her, when He lowers her into the world to be found upon it, He entrusts all His merits into her hand, and all of them are near to her, and because of this, "he shall lack no spoil." Rabbi Yose opened the following verse: **"She does him good and not evil all the days of her life."** "She does him good"—she prepares good for the world and merits good for the palace of the King and the children of the palace. "And not evil"—unlike that which is written: *“And the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil.”* "Good" is her portion at the time when those "days of heaven" shine upon her and unite with her as is fitting; these are "the days of her life," because the Tree of Life prepares her existence and provides for her, and at that time "she does him good and not evil." Rabbi Abba said: This is beautiful, and all the verses are explained well.

->**A Woman**<- <note>Portion of Tazria</note>

**A woman** when she conceives <note>Leviticus 12:2</note>. We have learned: *“This is the law of the burnt offering...”* <note>Leviticus 6:2</note> and so on. Rabbi Abba said: Heaven forbid! We have learned that the Holy One, Blessed be He, decrees over that opening of the drop whether it will be male or female. And "This is the law of the one who rises" <note>a play on the word *Olah*, burnt offering/rising</note>—the law of the one who rises refers to one who gives birth to a male. Rabbi Yose said: Certainly, the Holy One, Blessed be He, distinguishes between the drop of the male and the drop of the female. And because His wisdom knows it, He decrees upon those drops whether it be male or female. This is difficult: "gives birth to a male"—for since she conceives, she gives birth, as it is written: *“and gives birth to a male.”* The verse should have said: "A woman when she is pregnant and gives birth to a male." Why does it say "when she conceives <note>literally: 'seeds'</note> and gives birth"? Rabbi Yose said: It is found that from the day she conceives until the day she gives birth, she has no thought but for her birth, whether it will be a male or... <unclear>evil/female</unclear>! This is "A woman when she conceives and gives birth to a male."

**A woman** when she conceives. Rabbi Hezekiah opened: *“How manifold are Your works, O Lord!”* <note>Psalms 104:24</note>. How many are the works of the Holy King in the world...

# Tazria

## Main Text (The Zohar)

They are bound together and sown as one, and later each one emerges individually. When the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note>, performs His works, He does so with Wisdom, and with Wisdom He takes them all as one and sows them; afterwards, each one emerges in its proper time. This is the meaning of: **"In wisdom You have made them all"** (Psalms 104:24). Rabbi Elazar said: "How great is Your goodness, which You have hidden away for those who fear You" (Psalms 31:20). How concealed are the works of the Holy King! They are all hidden within Wisdom, for **"In wisdom You have made them all."** They are all included in Wisdom and do not emerge outward except through known paths toward <term>Understanding (Binah)</term> <note>The third Sefirah, representing the "womb" where the seeds of Wisdom are developed</note>, and from there everything is made and all is established—"and by understanding it is established" (Proverbs 24:3). Therefore, **"In wisdom You have made them all,"** for Understanding fills the earth. Your "possession" <note>referring to the end of Psalms 104:24, "the earth is full of Your possessions"</note> refers to the <term>Assembly of Israel (Knesset Yisrael)</term> <note>The Sefirah of Malchut, the spiritual archetype of the community of Israel</note>, which is filled by everything, as we have said:
> "All the rivers flow into the sea..." (Ecclesiastes 1:7)

"The earth is full of Your possessions," for she brings them forth afterward.
> "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created" (Genesis 2:4)

"When they were created" <note>original: *be-hibare’am*</note>—He created them with the letter *He* <note>A classic midrashic play on words: *be-hibare’am* can be read as *be-He bera’am*, "with the letter He He created them," referring to the feminine aspect of the Divine</note>. For this reason, "the earth is full of Your possessions."

Come and see: At the moment a person comes to sanctify himself to unite with his female, if his intention and holy will are focused, a different holy <term>Spirit (Ruach)</term> is awakened over him, comprised of male and female. The Holy One, Blessed be He, signals to a certain appointee <note>an angel</note> named *Lamed-Segol* who is in charge of the embryos of human beings, and that Spirit reaches his hand. He informs the angel which place to assign to it, and it follows the male's assistance. Another is included with that appointee—the male assistance of <term>Sovereignty (Malchut)</term>—and he receives it to assign that Spirit to all that was deposited. This has already been established. Then the Spirit descends and a deep "form" <note>original: *golema*, a physical mass or vessel</note> is present, which stands in the supernal image. Within that form, the Spirit is included. That form goes and stands in the world, all as one, becoming entwined within it. While this form is deeply entwined, the person stands as his own "golem" <note>unformed physical mass</note>, and the world stands as they are joined together.

King Solomon warned human beings and said:
> "Until the day breathes and the shadows flee" (Song of Songs 2:17)

These are two. And in the Book of Sorceries of Ashmodai <note>A legendary source of forbidden or esoteric knowledge mentioned in the Zohar</note>, we find that those who sow with a different [intent] draw from the side of the Spleen <note>associated in medieval medicine and Kabbalah with melancholy and the "Other Side"</note>. They cling to... <unclear>and a cup for the stranger with a tooth</unclear>... or after those forms of his descend. At times these are words, and at times they are his forms which are tied. At the time he prepares his will for them, for their assignment, what happens? When he deviates and leaves the domain of his Master, he gives his "deposit" <note>the seed/soul</note> to the Side of Impurity <note>original: *Sitra Achra*</note>. Through these etchings of his, at various times, two spirits [descend] to those fallen forms and are prepared in those forms of his, resembling human beings. They inform him of matters of wisdom and matters of goodness at known times. These are two spirits that were not included in the general rule of the body; they intended to be included, but they remain forms. They are prepared and they inform the person of things. This is what happens when one leaves the domain of his Master and gives his deposit to the Side of Impurity.

Come and see: a person must watch himself to be purified... and not to entrust it to the "Other Side," for he does not need another thing like it... for how many blessings and invitations are there for that matter to receive it! From that time on, blessings do not surround him, for he is from the "Other Side." When they see that they are fit for that goodness, it ascends to the field and to the Other Side... and when he precedes and invites a person, that form ascends for him and joins him... that Spirit that was clinging to him at all times is taken and prepared in him, and it joins him and never returns to him as a human being. Then he knows that he has been distanced from everything.

Come and see: at the time the soul descends to the world, it wanders through the worlds together with the female of the lower Eden. From below, the glory of the spirits of the <term>Righteous (Tzaddikaya)</term> stand in rows upon rows. Afterward, it goes to be nursed and descends to the firmaments... and all of them are kindnesses... and that holy form stands over him until he emerges into the world.

<summary>This page discusses the mystical process of conception, explaining how divine Wisdom and Understanding (Chochmah and Binah) govern the formation of the soul. It warns that improper intent during union can divert the soul-deposit to the "Other Side," resulting in spiritual impurity rather than a holy form.</summary>

<meta>This page begins the commentary on the Torah portion "Tazria" (She Conceives), continuing the mystical exploration of human birth and spiritual formation. It transitions from the general secrets of creation to the specific laws of childbirth and circumcision.</meta>

-> **Tazria** <-

## Main Text (Zohar)

When that flowing river <note>A reference to the divine emanation of Yesod, the source of life</note> emerges into the world, it flows and joins directly, and deep things increase with it, as has been stated; so too is the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note>. And all these things are found within a person and depend upon him. This is what is written: <note>original: "Hada hu de-ketiv"</note> *For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow.* <note>Job 8:9</note> "For all our days" refers to all of us. From the day a person is conceived below until the day of birth, human beings do not know the works of the Holy One, blessed be He, how great they are and how exalted they are. This is what is written: *How manifold are Your works, O Lord!* <note>Psalms 104:24</note>

Come and see: all those in the world are male and female. And when they emerge, they emerge as male and female together, and afterwards they separate according to their way. If a person is worthy, they later join together as one. This is his "soulmate," and they unite in a single union, both in spirit and in body. As it is written: *Let the earth bring forth the living soul after its kind...* <note>Genesis 1:24</note> and we have established this. "Let the earth bring forth"—everything emerges from her, the "living soul," as we have established: this is the spirit of the First Man <note>Adam HaRishon</note>. This is what is written: *Of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden.* <note>Genesis 3:3</note> "The fruit of the tree" refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, "in the midst of the garden" refers to the Shekhinah.

Behold, it is written: *If a woman conceives and bears a male child* <note>Leviticus 12:2</note>. It does not say "male and female" together, as is the way of the world that causes it. Rabbi Eleazar said: It is not so, for behold, all are included as male and female together and are separated afterwards. "And bears a male"—they are included together from the side of the Right <note>The attribute of Mercy/Chesed</note>. "But if she bears a female"—they are included together, female and male, from the side of the Left <note>The attribute of Judgment/Gevurah</note>, which dominates the male. The Right is more powerful, and the male is subdued in those days when it does not dominate; then that male who emerges from the female side is weak in all his ways like a female and is not called "male." But any male who emerges from the Right is dominant, and the female who emerges from him is subdued. For the weak side does not dominate, and regarding this, it is written: *and bears a male.*

And how many spirits and chariots emerge at one time into the world! From the day they emerge, they do not investigate their own souls until they are settled in the body. And how long does this take? Three days. This is what is written: *And the third day...* <note>referencing the time needed for the spirit to settle</note>. *And she shall be unclean seven days; as in the days of her impurity.* All seven days, the higher lights do not come to her to be found within her. All the time of the seven days, the spirit wanders in the body to find its place. Then it is written: *It shall be seven days under its mother* <note>Leviticus 22:27</note>, a complete intention to settle the spirit and body, to appear before the Matron <note>The Shekhinah</note> and to be bound there as spirit and body. *And thirty days and three days she shall continue in the blood of her purifying* <note>Leviticus 12:4</note>—to settle the spirit in the body. And these three days, what is their function? During these three days, the child's blood is like white [milk], not resting from its agitation, like the three days of the Right, and regarding this: *and thirty [and three].*

<column-break/>

[Right Column]
**And on the day**
...day, and thirty-three days she shall continue in the blood of her purifying. "In the blood of her purifying"—firstly, and afterwards "days of purifying." And regarding "the blood of her purifying," this refers to the blood of circumcision, the blood of the crown <note>the corona of the covenant</note> that comes from the child... all these days... "she shall continue in the blood of her purifying." "Purifying" <note>original: "tohorah"</note> is stated generally, and the final letter *He* is not mentioned <note>referring to a grammatical/mystical nuance in the Hebrew spelling</note>, so that you do not say "Purification" specifically for the Matron, but "purifying" in general. "The blood of purifying" refers to these pure bloods. *She shall touch no hallowed thing, nor come into the sanctuary...* Come and see: every single day when the [divine] rule... the altar... to distance... and she was worthy for us.

## Commentary (The Faithful Shepherd)

[Left Column]
**The Faithful Shepherd**
<note>original: "Ra'aya Meheimna"</note>
*And on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.* <note>Leviticus 12:3</note> This commandment is to circumcise on the eighth day, the sign of the Holy Covenant <note>original: "Kayyama Kadisha"</note>. This is an exalted matter, as it is written: *The secret of the Lord is with them that fear Him; and He will show them His covenant.* <note>Psalms 25:14</note> To whom? To those who are of the high degree of holiness, to maintain the Holy Covenant, not below to be revealed to [unworthy] men. And the secret of this Holy Covenant—they have established it and tied it to the desire of the righteous. And this secret of eight days is for... over the world for all the holy people, as it is written: *And on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.* And also "the eighth" refers to the Holy Covenant and is a sign of support for all levels. And they clarified to disqualify the [unholy] covenant by removing the foreskin <note>original: "orlah"</note>...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of Parashat Tazria, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of circumcision (Brit Milah) and the laws of ritual purity following childbirth. It maintains the mystical tone of the Zohar, interpreting physical acts as reflections of celestial processes.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

---

**[Right Column]**

Those who fulfill the **Covenant** <note>original: *Brit*</note>. For behold, in the exile, the serpent and those gathered with him seek to prevent the holy nation from removing that **foreskin** <note>original: *Orlah*; the mystical "husk" or *kelipah* that conceals holiness</note> from before the Holy Covenant. This is because all their service and preparation is surely to establish the foreskin above, in front of the Holy Covenant of Existence. For all the actions that Israel performs below awaken actions above. And because of this, at the time when that foreskin is seen by all the holy nation above, the foreskin is "visited" <note>judged or dealt with</note>. From here we learn that the foreskin must be placed in the **dust** <note>original: *afra*</note> for the "Other Side," because it is written: *And the serpent’s food shall be dust* <note>Isaiah 65:25</note> and *Dust you shall eat all the days of your life* <note>Genesis 3:14</note>. From here we see it is not proper for it to be found before that place <note>the site of the Covenant</note>, for they stir it up from before this Covenant. And they merit, when it is removed from this Covenant, that the dust is for them. Trust follows that serpent below; before the loins, he makes his dwelling in the dust, as it is written: *For dust you are, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life.* And since he is holy, when one removes it [the foreskin] from before him, he hates his dwelling in the dust and seeks to rectify it. Thus, regarding the serpent, at the time when you are required to remove the foreskin, you must prepare dust for him to establish his dwelling within it. Every person who needs to bring that first son before the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: *Kadosh Baruch Hu* (abbr. *KB"H*)</note>, so that he shall not die, must pass the edge of the knife and appear before the Holy One, Blessed be He. It is a pressing sacrifice to rectify his son. And this sacrifice is like the sacrifice of an animal; this one is for a time and that one is for a time, as it is written: *And from the eighth day and further it shall be accepted* <note>Leviticus 22:27</note>. It shall be accepted as if one performed a portion of it; once one portion has passed over him, then he is accepted as a sacrifice. And one does not approach from these buildings to be purified surely except through that portion of the spirit of the Holy Covenant, and until all is in the spirit of the world, etc.

**[Left Column]**

To them in holiness, when corresponding to that which they were established in the "breath" <note>the soul-breath</note>, they are spirits. For **thirty-three days** <note>The period of purity for a mother after bearing a male child</note> she is spared over them every day, and these spirits are bound in the breath of the Crown <note>Keter</note> of the world. Just as He does not dwell upon the Crown of [so-and-so], so all His works are in this breath upon which they were established. *She shall touch no holy thing* <note>Leviticus 12:4</note> so as not to appear upon them. And if she bears a **female** <note>original: *Nekevah*</note>, as we have established, the **Left Side** <note>original: *Sitra Schmala*; the side of judgment and rigor</note> rises higher and is built from it. And because of this, all is doubled <note>the 66 days of purity for a girl vs 33 for a boy</note>, the distance of the female from the **male** <note>original: *Dechura*</note> to bind the spirit in the breath. For the Left was not taken in this way in its day, and it is found with greater strength.

---

->**If a woman conceives and bears a male child, etc.**<-
<note>Leviticus 12:2</note>

Rabbi Yehuda opened: ***There is none holy as the Lord; for there is none beside Thee; neither is there any rock like our God*** <note>1 Samuel 2:2</note>. This verse is difficult. *There is none holy as...* implies that there is another "holy one," because it uses the comparative "as." *And there is no rock like our God* implies there is another "rock." But surely, *There is none holy as...* refers to the many holy ones who are from Him, the holy ones above, as it is written: *The matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones* <note>Daniel 4:14</note>. Israel is called holy, as it is written: *You shall be holy* <note>Leviticus 19:2</note>. And all of them are holy, but they are not holy *as* the Lord. And this is because it is written: ***For there is none beside Thee.*** What does "none beside Thee" mean? Rather, the holiness of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is "beside" <note>or "without"</note> that which is called theirs. For He does not need them to sanctify Him, but they are holy through Him. This is "For there is none beside Thee"—their holiness is not without Thee. *And there is no rock like our God*—as we have established, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is like a **Craftsman** <note>A play on the word *Tzur* (Rock) and *Tzayar* (Artist/Form-giver)</note> who designs and rectifies the form and breathes into it the breath of life and brings it out into the air of the world. This is *And there is no rock like our God*—there is no Form-giver <note>original: *Tzayar*</note> who is called a "Rock" <note>original: *Tzur*</note> like the Lord. As in: *The Rock in whom they took refuge* <note>Deuteronomy 32:37</note>. And it is written: *Upon the rock* <note>Exodus 17:6</note>, *Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb.* And all of these are called "Rock." But *there is no rock like our God*, for His is the dominion and the kingship over all.
Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Hezekiah were sitting one night before Rabbi Isaac. They rose at **midnight** <note>original: *Palgot Leila*; a significant time for mystical study</note> to labor in the Torah. When they went outside, they saw a star running three times toward another star, and its light was hidden. Meanwhile, they heard two voices from two sides. One voice to the North side for service, and a voice...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Tazria**<-
<note>Tazria: The name of the Torah portion, meaning "She conceives."</note>

What is below, and that voice that travels and is gathered into your place, the hidden part of the secrets of the Female that is open—receive upon yourselves the Lamp of below, which is the **Righteous One** <note>original: "Tzadik," referring to the sefirah of Yesod, the generative foundation</note> who begets daughters. That voice passed through and entangled Rabbi Isaac and Rabbi Hiyya. They said: "This is surely the delight of the awakening of Eden, to be joined with the Holy King." Rabbi Isaac said: "He is to be joined with Him, with the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu"</note>, but from within his surroundings, from his cause toward Him, until they are found, and the King extends to her the **thread of loving-kindness** <note>original: "chut shel chesed"</note>." And the secret of the matter is as we have said: *“And the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand, etc.”* <note>Esther 5:2</note>. Do not say that he extends the thread of loving-kindness only to her, but rather the King of Life extends it to her and to all those who are joined with her. "Come, let us join as one," they sat.

Rabbi Isaac opened and said: *“And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone, etc.”* <note>Genesis 2:18</note>. Why does the verse open this way? He said to him: "It has been stated that concerning this it is written 'for it is good' regarding the male, because man was destined to be separated. And it is written, 'It is not good for man to be alone,' yet at that time it was also written, *'Male and female He created them'* <note>Genesis 5:2</note>." We have learned that <term>Adam was created with two faces</term> <note>original: "Du-Partzufin." A mystical concept that the first human was a single being with both male and female fronts/faces joined back-to-back</note>. If so, why do you say "It is not good for man to be alone"? It is because he did not labor with his female, and he had no support facing him, because she was at his sides and they were as one from the back. In that state, "man was alone." *“I will make him a helper against him”*—what is "against him"? It means facing him, face to face, to cleave to one another, face to face. What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do? He <term>sawed</term> <note>original: "Nesirah." The mystical process of separating the joined male and female aspects so they can face each other as independent beings</note> him and took his female from him. This is what is written: *“And He took one of his ribs”* <note>Genesis 2:21</note>. What is "one"? This is his female. And He designated loving-kindness for her, to prepare her like a bride, and brought her to be placed before him face to face. While she was still attached to his side, man was "alone." Afterward, two ascended and three stood as one.

Come and see: at the time when she was gathered to the man, the Holy One, Blessed be He, blessed them. This is what is written: *“And God blessed them”* <note>Genesis 1:28</note>, just as one blesses a bride with **seven blessings** <note>The Sheva Brachot recited at a Jewish wedding</note>. From here we learn that a groom and bride, once they are blessed with the seven blessings, are established as one in the likeness of the Supernal [Divine] realm. Therefore, a groom who comes to be joined with his wife—this secret is "Face to Face"—and his union, as it were, creates two desires above. The Holy One, Blessed be He, dwells in that union with joy when they are in a state of mercy. But when they are in a state of anger, come and see: one who joins with the wife of another, he lies against everything, for he lies against the Holy One, Blessed be He. Therefore, the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not grant him [easy] repentance; his repentance is suspended until he departs from the world. This is what is written: *“Surely this iniquity shall not be forgiven you until you die”* <note>Isaiah 22:14</note>. When? At the time he enters into repentance in that [other] world and sees his deeds before him.

Rabbi Eleazar said: "One who lies in this matter—will his repentance be accepted until he is judged in the furnace of Gehenna? How much more so for one who lies against the Holy One, Blessed be He! And how much more so if he forces the Holy One, Blessed be He, to create a <term>form</term> <note>original: "Diyukna," a divine image or spiritual blueprint</note> of a bastard through another man's wife, thereby binding the supports of the King."

Rabbi Hiyya opened: "And his palate shall not drop... etc." This refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He. "Robbing the poor in your houses"—who is the poor one? It is the one who desires another below, for she is his soulmate. We have learned there: "All the priests of the world..." the whole blessing flows to the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written, "His palate drops..." This refers to the one who cleaves to his wife to look upon her, a union that is clear. Therefore, he receives the whole blessing as it flows from the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the **Assembly of Israel** <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael," the mystical personification of the Jewish people and the sefirah of Malchut</note>. Heaven forbid that their union should be anything but through the seven blessings. But what of an unmarried woman? So too, one who cleaves to the wife of his companion, who is holy in the likeness of the Supernal realm through the union of the seven blessings—the Holy One, Blessed be He, will break him. As they have established: "Stolen waters are sweet," but for this, "his palate drops" [in judgment]. Furthermore, one who calls a commandment-based union "sinful"—who will have pity on him? He mars the form and the Supernal arrangement. For one who lusts after the wife of his companion to cleave to her...

## Tazria

...more of the inner faces, and for this reason, he turned away and not forever. There is a side of the face above and a face below, and wings for the inner parts; the Almighty hides, and it is written: "the lintel and the opening," etc. Rabbi Elazar opened his discourse and said:
> **"And he said, 'Let me go, for the dawn has broken'"** (Genesis 32:27)

And so on. "And he said to me," etc. He was bound in the hands of Jacob. However, happy are the righteous, for the Holy One, blessed be He, is called theirs, and He never leaves them forever. This is what is written: "He will never let the righteous be moved." And what is written? "And he touched the socket of Jacob’s thigh." Rather, he struggled for his generations. And what was said? It is written: "And he lodged there that night in the camp," and it is written: "And he rose up and passed over the ford." What was the reason that Jacob was destined to cross them at the stream in the night? Rather, he saw an **Accuser** <note>original: *mekatreg*; the spiritual adversary or prosecuting angel</note> walking among his camps. Jacob said: "I will cross to the other side so that no confusion shall be found behind me." What did he see? He saw the "god" of the nations <note>the guardian angel of Esau/Edom</note> walking in a flame and ruling among their camps. Jacob said: "It is better that I leave from here, for the river separates the structures and no confusion will be found." Immediately, "He rose up and passed over the ford... and Jacob was left alone." This is his portion and his teaching: one who is found alone in a house at night, or like those in a house together—how much more so at night! What is the danger? The damaging spirits and the various classes of "portions" that go alone at night and are able to cause harm. Come and see: "And Jacob was left alone," and then "a man wrestled with him," etc. We have learned that the **Accuser** of Judgment <note>original: *mekatreg d'dina*; the force of strict justice</note> comes, and his hatred is from that side. What is his side? Above, it is the exile. As soon as the **light** <note>original: *nehora*; the morning light representing Mercy</note> arose, Jacob’s strength prevailed over him. For the Accuser comes from the night, and his power is the night; he could not prevail over him. And as the light arose, Jacob’s strength was strengthened and he seized him and prevailed over him. When the angel saw that the light was rising, he said to him: "Let me go, for I cannot prevail against you." He could not prevail because the light was rising and his strength was broken, as it is written: "In a cool wind..." and "like the young of the cattle." And all the "sons of God" knew—what did they know? That all those who come from the **Side of Judgment** <note>original: *sitra d'dina*</note> are called. Then Jacob strengthened himself and spoke to him. The angel said to him: "Let me go, for the dawn has broken." What is this time? It is the time of praise, when the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He, is found. And he said: "I will not let you go unless you have blessed me." It should have said "unless you bless me" <note>future tense</note>; why "unless you have blessed me" <note>past tense</note>? Rather, Jacob said to him: "Surely my father blessed me with those **blessings** <note>original: *birchan*</note> that he intended to give to Esau, and I am afraid of you because of those blessings that I seized. If you do not agree with me, the Accuser will prosecute me with legal claims." Immediately, he said to him: "What is your name?" and he said, "Jacob." And he said further: "Your name shall no longer be..." What did he say to him? Rather, he said this: "It was not through wisdom or through **deceit** <note>original: *okva*; a play on the name Yaakov/Jacob, meaning 'heel' or 'supplanter'</note> that you gained those blessings. Your name shall no longer be called Jacob—for it was not by the 'heel'—but rather Israel." And from then on, he certainly admitted it to you, and from him the blessings went forth, because he saw the gravity in it. And for this reason, he admitted it, and all the hosts of his camps admitted them. "For you have striven with God <note>original: *Elohim*</note> and with men and have prevailed." With *Elohim* <note>The text notes the correction to the Divine Name</note>—these are all those who come from the side of the "harsh spirit." And "with men"—this refers to Esau and his camps. "And you have prevailed"—you had power over them and they could not overcome you. And Jacob did not leave him until he admitted to him those blessings, and "he blessed him there." And come and see: at the hour when the light rises, all those masters of judgments are subdued and are not found, and everyone speaks of the Holy One, blessed be He. And that hour is a **Time of Will** <note>original: *idan d'reuta*; a moment of divine favor</note>; it is the time of the Bride, and the King extends to her and to all those found with her from the spirit of the Thread of Kindness <note>Chesed</note>, to be found within the colors of the Holy King, as has been said. And come and see: at the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, is found in every vision, and those who are found with Him, the Living Beast awakens the initial Will to the Prophet, and finds him in the longing of the Bride. Then he is appointed from the side of the Spirit, and many hosts are found on the side of the Spirit, all the worlds. And when he stands to awaken wisdom and the initial Will...

...for glory and for the crown. And it is not at the time when the spirit is awakened; for then everything is found in secret and becomes filled. We have learned that the lower world is formed in the likeness of the upper world, so that the one is found to be the counterpart of the other. A person must ensure that their will is directed above toward the Holy One, Blessed be He, so that divine favors are found in the world. All these are the portions of the righteous, who know how to attach their will to the Holy King. Of them it is written: *But you who held fast to the Lord your God are all alive today.* <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>

**"When a man** shall have in the skin of his flesh a rising, a scab, or a bright spot..." <note>Leviticus 13:2</note>. At the end, she says, "Do not gaze upon me"—not that seeing is forbidden to us, but she asks that we do not look at her with contempt because she appears darkened to Israel. One should not look at her as one looks at something common or profane. "Do not gaze upon me"—truly do not look at me [in this state]. Why is she dark? Because of the sins of old, she was struck with blackness. 

There are two types of darkness mentioned here: One is *“because the sun has tanned me,”* meaning the Sun <note>The masculine divine light, Tiferet</note> has departed from me and no longer shines upon me, leaving me darkened. The second is *“my mother’s sons were angry with me.”* The phrase *“tanned me”* <note>original: shezafatni</note> implies that when the sun shines, the colors are bright, but when it departs, all those bright colors depart. "They were angry with me"—these are the forces that come from the side of "Harsh Judgment" <term>Din: the attribute of severity</term>. They were all angry with me and placed burdens upon my head. When Israel entered into exile, they were like those who are burdened and placed under a yoke, unable to open their mouths. *“They made me keeper of the vineyards”*—to dwell in exile and to guard the nations in their dwellings, while *“my own vineyard I have not kept,”* for I was unable to guard them as before. Now I must labor in the vineyards of others because I did not labor in my own.

Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose were walking on the road. When they reached a certain field, they stood by a certain fence. Rabbi Yose said: "The covering of the clouds is present; we have no permission to look upon joy from the day the Holy Temple was destroyed." He then spoke of the earth and the salt... <note>The text here becomes a complex linguistic play on the words for "Earth" (Eretz) and "World" (Tevel)</note>. Is "Tevel" not the earth? Rather, the "Earth" refers to the Holy Land, while "Tevel" refers to the rest of the lands of the world. As we have said: *“And He shall judge the world (Tevel) in righteousness,”* for Tevel depends on righteousness, and it is all one matter.

Rabbi Hiyya said: The "Earth" is for the righteous, but "Tevel" and its inhabitants are for those who are like the "primordial serpent." Rabbi Yose said: How do we establish the verse *“For He has founded it upon the seas and established it upon the floods”*? <note>Psalms 24:2</note> This refers to the "Earth" being founded upon the "Waters," for all things emerge from the Upper River that flows out of Eden to provide sustenance for the lower worlds and to awaken the Holy King. And because of this, *“The river of God is full of water...”* <note>Psalms 65:10</note> providing for every living thing...

## Main Text (Zohar)

His face is red like strong blows. Rabbi <term>Pinhas</term> <note>A prominent sage in the Zohar's circle</note> said: One who has a corner in his house and does not give a person time <note>i.e., is stingy or inhospitable</note>, for this pushes him away; thus it is hinted that his hands will be afflicted with evil diseases, and these we do not call **sufferings of love**.

Rabbi Pinhas said: These push and push away, for sufferings of love strengthen the life of a person, as it is said: Come and see, it is written:

The letters *He*, *Aleph*, *Nun* shine here, and all of them are called a **plague of leprosy**.
The end of the verse says: *and it shall become a plague of leprosy on the skin of his body*. What is this? A plague of leprosy is like a bean-size, like its vow, as a general rule. And it is written:
> He shall be brought to Aaron the priest, etc. <note>Leviticus 13:2</note>

For all those that appear on the outside, it is written: *And the priest shall see him and pronounce him unclean*, for certainly those that appear on the outside of human beings come from the **side of impurity** <note>original: "Sitra Achra"</note>, and these are not called sufferings of love.

Rabbi Yose said: Our Rabbis taught <note>original: "Tanu Rabbanan"</note> that it is written:
> Better is open rebuke than hidden love <note>Proverbs 27:5</note>

If this rebuke stands from kindness, it is hidden from people; in this manner, one who rebukes his friend out of love needs to seal his words from other people so that he does not shame his friend. Then his friend rejoices in him, and they are in love. His words are life to him, provided he is not shamed before other people. So too, the **Holy One, Blessed Be He** <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu"</note>, when He rebukes a person, He rebukes everyone in love. At first, He strikes him in his inner bones. If he repents, it is well; if not, He strikes him beneath his garments. And these are called **sufferings of love**. If he repents, it is well; if not, He strikes him openly on his face before everyone, so that they may look at him and know that he is a sinner. And these are the mercies of the One who strikes here. That man said... <unclear>textual corruption</unclear> ...for the Torah is thus, as it is written:
> At the head of the noisy streets she calls out; at the entrance of the gates in the city she utters her sayings <note>Proverbs 1:21</note>

And what life is there in me for the Torah to you? For it is seen before you that when it is written in submission before the **Holy One, Blessed Be He**, and not only that, but the Torah requires humility. That man opened and said:
> Who is a God like You, pardoning iniquity, etc. <note>Micah 7:18</note>

He casts his hands... <unclear>textual corruption</unclear> ...arousing Heavenly assistance here. He opened and saw everything that he had seen in the days of his vanity:

This verse we learned in the house of Rabbi Dostai, which he would say in the name of Rabbi Yochanan ben HaChait. *I have seen everything in my days of vanity.* Now, since King Solomon was wiser than everyone, how could he say this—that he saw everything during the time he walked in the darkness of the world? For anyone who strives in the darkness of the world sees nothing and knows nothing. Rather, it was said: In the days of King Solomon, the **Moon** <note>original: "Sihera," symbolizing the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> stood in its fullness, and peace was spread over all the inhabitants of the world. This is the "Breath" <note>Hevel</note> found in everything, from water, fire, and air, like the breath that comes out of the mouth, including everything. And he saw everything through that breath of his which he grasped.

*There is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness.* Come and see: at the time when the children of Israel are in the world... all this departs from the **Moon** forever, and it takes all the sin... to be filled with light and mercy... in order to mate with the **Moon**. But when the building is destroyed and the wicked increase in the world, and the light below is diminished, it is written then: *A righteous man perishes in his righteousness.* It does not say "the" righteous, but "a" righteous man perishes, for he is not seen in the **Moon**, and he does not take sustenance and joy to give life to her and mate with her. And regarding this, *a righteous man perishes in his righteousness*—this is the **Moon** which is not found to be mated with. A voice is heard that does not see the command as it used to be, and then the entire Left Side is awakened, and the wicked scorch the world like a flame.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on Parashat Tazria, focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the soul and the severe metaphysical consequences of speech. It connects the creation of man in Genesis to the laws of spiritual impurity (Tsara’at).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Tazria (She Conceives)** <-

In this world, **there is a wicked man who prolongs his life in his wickedness** <note>Ecclesiastes 7:15</note>. What is "his wickedness"? It refers to that specific "crown" <note>a lower spiritual level or shell</note> to which he clings.
Furthermore, **there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness** <note>Ecclesiastes 7:15</note>. For when the children of men in the world are meritorious and attain merit through their good deeds, the "Righteous One" <note>referring to the divine attribute of Yesod</note> perishes in his righteousness to give to those below through their merits. This is like one who extends himself through their merits so that through his death all faces are made radiant; and Goodness is not withheld from them, nor are they darkened forever. And what is in his hands? That he does not lead them according to his own will. Regarding this, it says to David: "Do not fret because of evildoers, nor be envious of those who work unrighteousness." He said: Surely the Holy One, blessed be He, will act for me according to the law, for there was a secret here to erase them by their own hands, yet I did not do so, nor did I subjugate them either in secret or in the open.

Furthermore, his son opened the discourse and said: **"And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground..."** <note>Genesis 2:7</note>. "And He formed" <note>original: *Vayitzer*</note> is written with two letters *Yod*, representing the two inclinations: the <term>Good Inclination</term> <note>original: *Yetzer Tov*</note> and the <term>Evil Inclination</term> <note>original: *Yetzer Ra*</note>. One corresponds to death and one corresponds to life. "The Lord God" is a full Name. "The Man" includes both male and female. "Dust of the ground"—this is the dust of the Holy Land from which he was created, and this is the site of the Holy Temple. **"And breathed into his nostrils the breath of life"** <note>Genesis 2:7</note>—this is the <term>Holy Soul</term> <note>original: *Neshama Kadisha*</note> which is found from the "Life of the Above." **"And man became a living soul"** <note>Genesis 2:7</note>—man was included in the holy soul from the side of the Above which embraces the earth, as it is written: "Let the earth bring forth a living soul"—the living soul of the Above.

Come and see: as long as this <term>Holy Soul</term> clings to a person, he is beloved by his Master. Many guardians protect him from all sides; he is marked for good above and below, and the <term>Holy Presence</term> <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note> dwells upon him. But when he sins, he distances the Presence; she departs from him, and the Holy Soul no longer clings to him. Then, from the side of the <term>Evil Serpent</term> <note>original: *Dachvya Bisha*</note>, a certain spirit is awakened that wanders through the world, which only dwells in a place where the supernal holiness has departed. Then the person becomes defiled and is blemished in his flesh, as they have all said.

And come and see: this "living soul," which is supernal and holy, the entire Holy Land is found for her sake and is included in her; then we call her *Neshama* (Soul). It is she who ascends above and speaks before the Holy King; she enters all gates and none may stay her hand. Because of this, she is called the <term>Speaking Spirit</term> <note>original: *Ruach Memalela*</note>, for all other things have no permission to speak before the King except for this one.

And for this reason, the Torah warns and says: **"Keep your tongue from evil..."** <note>Psalms 34:14</note> and it is written: **"He who guards his mouth and his tongue [guards his soul from troubles]"** <note>Proverbs 21:23</note>. Because if his mouth and his tongue speak evil words, those words ascend on high, and at the moment they ascend, all [the heavenly hosts] proclaim: "Depart from the King's sanctuary!" For so-and-so has opened a place for that powerful Serpent. Then the Holy Soul is removed from him and departs; she can no longer speak as she did in former times of goodness. And this Soul ascends in shame before the whole world, and they do not give her a place as they did before. Regarding this it is written: **"He who guards his mouth and his tongue guards his soul from trouble"** <note>Proverbs 21:23</note>. "His soul" <note>original: *Nafsho*</note> literally—that which used to speak is now made mute because of the evil speech.

Then the spirit, which is the portion of all, returns to its place. And when that "Evil King" <note>the destructive force</note> ascends in his portion, they know that they have sinned before the powerful Serpent. Many spirits are awakened in the world, and a lower spirit from their side finds that this man has awakened it with an evil word. Since the Holy Speaking Spirit has been removed from him, that [evil spirit] then dwells upon him and drags him down, and then he is <term>Shut Up</term> <note>original: *Sagir* - the technical term for a leper's quarantine</note>. Just as a person's dwelling is affected because of an evil word, so is his punishment for a good word that came to his hand—which he was able to speak but did not. For he blemished that Speaking Spirit, which was prepared to speak above and to speak below, all in holiness. How much more so if he sees people on a crooked path and he is able to speak to them but remains silent and does not speak. This is like the darkness of which it is written: **"I was dumb with silence, I held my peace even from good; and my sorrow was stirred"** <note>Psalms 39:3</note>. "Stirred" refers to the afflictions of poverty, and regarding them is the voice of King David...

<summary>This passage explains that the human soul is a "speaking spirit" derived from divine holiness. When a person uses speech for evil (Lashon Hara) or remains silent when they should speak words of correction, the Holy Soul departs, allowing an impure spirit to dwell on them, resulting in the physical and spiritual affliction of leprosy (Tsara'at).</summary>

# Tazria

The King is my portion and my inheritance, as it is written <note>Psalm 25:16</note> **"Turn to me and be gracious to me."** What is the meaning of "Turn to me"? It is like the other verse where it is written, "And he turned." Rabbi Hiyya, Rabbi Yose, and Rabbi Hezekiah were walking on the road. Rabbi Hezekiah said that Rabbi Hiyya applied this verse to them: <note>Proverbs 4:18</note> **"But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, which shines brighter and brighter until the full day."**

**"When a person has a mark of leprosy on their body, they shall be brought to the priest..."** <note>Leviticus 13:9</note>. Rabbi Yose said: The colleagues have awakened many interpretations regarding this "mark" (<term>Nega</term>: a plague or stroke). The Priest knew how to distinguish between the pure and the impure. He knew which afflictions were "suffering of love" <note>Chastisements brought by God to purify a person out of love</note> and which were meant to distance the master from his Creator. It is written <note>Ecclesiastes 5:5</note> **"Do not let your mouth bring your flesh into sin,"** so that you do not cause a "mark" to appear in the world. Do not let your mouth speak evil <note>Lashon Hara: derogatory speech</note> and stir up wicked deeds. From here we learn that a person's silence is necessary when they wish to avoid the consequences of what they speak.

Rabbi Isaac said: This verse is difficult. Does the Holy One, blessed be He, wish to strike a person or create bad occurrences? If so, there would be no justice in this world or the world to come, and the ruins would never be repaired! As it is written <note>Psalm 81:14</note> **"My people would not listen to my voice."** Rather, this is certainly for him and his children, to remind him of his life when things are cut off, and you shall "apply your heart." What is "apply"? It means from the power of holiness, to turn toward kindness, to remember him and show him grace. And so David said: "Do not let your mouth speak evil," meaning do not let a person's mouth cause a "mark" in the world, for a harsh judgment is triggered in the world, which is the mark of leprosy.

Regarding the "mark of leprosy" (<term>Nega Tzara'at</term>), the colleagues awakened the idea that "Tzara'at" is as the Targum <note>The Aramaic translation of the Bible</note> renders it: *Segiru* <note>meaning "shutting up" or "confinement"</note>. And Rabbi Judah asked: Why does the Targum say *Segiru*? And why does the verse open with "it is a mark" rather than "it is a plague"? Rabbi Yose said: This is a doubt for the priest, and even more so for the children. And this is what is written: "When a mark of leprosy is in a man," it is actual kindness <note>meaning the affliction is a hidden kindness to spark repentance</note>, and from here it descends to strike the mark so it is found in each one like an arrow.

Rabbi Isaac said: This is the secret of the matter, as it is written that the river of His sanctuary turned aside because the people of the world caused it. This is the meaning of "He has defiled the sanctuary of the Lord." Truly defiled! Rabbi Eleazar said: Why "defiled"? Because the Divine Presence (<term>Shekhinah</term>) departed from it, and a harsh, empty, and lacking power was seen. Come and see: all the powerful waters that seek to enter are removed, and the structures are passed over, and a harsh and hollow serpent descends. Then the sanctuary is found to be struck, as it is said: "I will put a mark of leprosy in a house in the land of your possession." And it is written: "And he shall break down the house." This is linked to the "beast of the field which the Lord God had made," who said to the woman, "Even though God said..." This caused the sanctuary below to be like the sanctuary above <note>in terms of being affected by sin</note>. This is "defiling the sanctuary of the Lord" because of the flight of the soul, as the powerful serpent rises. See that the righteous find a cup of purity, but the foolish and evil have their portion above and below. As it is written: "And the Lord sent fiery serpents (<term>Seraphim</term>) among the people." It does not say "the leapers" but "the burners" <note>Seraphim can mean both angels and burning serpents</note>. It is written: "Seraphim stood above Him"—"above Him" certainly. Then the "harp" is in all of them, and there is no opening. And about this it is written: "Such is the way of an adulterous woman; she eats and wipes her mouth..." What is "adulterous"? Literally adulterous. "She eats and wipes her mouth and says, 'I have done no wrong.'" Rabbi Isaac said: The deficiency of the Bride <note>the Shekhinah</note> is found below because she was defiled above; and she is only found above when she is found below through the sins of the people, for the Bride is dependent on this and that.

**"And if a man's hair falls out from his head..."** <note>Leviticus 13:40</note>. Rabbi Hiyya opened with the verse <note>Ecclesiastes 2:13</note> **"Then I saw that wisdom has an advantage over folly..."** just as light has an advantage over darkness. What is the "advantage of wisdom over folly"?
