<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on Parashat Tazria. It focuses on the necessity of opposites—specifically how wisdom is only truly recognized through the lens of folly, and light through darkness.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Tazria**<-
<note>Leviticus 12:1–15:33; the title means "She conceives"</note>

In the gathering of Jonah and Matos, they entered into the Holy Palace. Rabbi Yose read, and this one read it and wrote it by the hand of the King, and said: **"Then I saw that wisdom has an advantage over folly, as light has an advantage over darkness"** <note>Ecclesiastes 2:13</note>. Now, is this verse not known? Has it not been said? Who does not know that wisdom has an advantage over folly? Even one who has never known wisdom in his days and has never tasted of it knows that wisdom has an advantage over folly as light has over darkness. Why then did he need to say of himself, "Then I saw"?

Rather, thus we have learned: what is "wisdom" and what is "folly" in this verse? It comes to show that they are called after the pattern of the Supernal <note>Upper/Divine</note> realms. There is a Right and there is a Left in the Upper World, and there is a Right and there is a Left in the Lower World. There are levels upon levels in holiness, and there is that which is over them, as it is written: **"For one higher than the high watches, and there are yet higher ones over them"** <note>Ecclesiastes 5:7</note>. There are seven crowns of the Right above, and correspondingly there are seven pillars below to strengthen the Holy Wisdom. Because of this, they are called the "Seven Mothers." The beloved world <note>the world of emanation</note> is taken by the Mother <note>Binah/Understanding</note> for the Brain, for the Beginning, the First. And the matter of its nature is everything.

And as much as Wisdom ascends through the degrees of Wisdom to be called "First," all of them were said to correspond to the Crowns above, and everything here was made from it. The beginning of this side corresponds to that side in the spirit and the brain within it, and there is nothing that does not have its opposite in everything. In the beginning, the lower worlds were established through judgments.

Rabbi Yitzchak taught: Come and see, all these worlds that she <note>the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> has, and all that is contained beneath her, would not be established except when they are resting as one. In this manner, Solomon, the King of the world, said they are established through one another. For everything is sustained by it, and He is in everything that is sustained by Him; without Him, the worlds would be consumed above and below. This is what is written: **"Do I not fill heaven and earth? says the Lord"** <note>Jeremiah 23:24</note>.

And initially, regarding the language, it is written: **"Let every soul [praise the Lord]"** etc. "The advantage of wisdom over folly"—the explanation of this is all in the language. It comes to say: **"Then I saw that wisdom has an advantage over folly,"** meaning specifically *from* the folly itself there is an advantage to wisdom. For when there is no goodness in the world, wisdom and its words are not recognized. We have learned: it is an obligation for a person to labor in wisdom to learn from its goodness and its measure, so that wisdom may be known through it. Because of this it is written: **"To behold the beauty of the Lord and to inquire in His temple"** <note>Psalms 27:4</note>. For if there were no darkness, light would not be recognized, and the benefit of the world would not be seen from it.

We have learned: "That wisdom has an advantage"—to the actual Wise One. For Rabbi Shimon said: One is not called "Wise" and the spirit does not shine wisdom to the world, and it is not given, except by means of the folly that is done below. Why was there light? Because of the darkness. If there were no darkness, the benefit of wisdom would not be seen. Because of the folly that is done, the light shines even more. This is "the advantage of wisdom over folly"—wisdom in general from folly in general. And so it is below: if this folly did not dwell in the world, wisdom would not dwell in the world.

This is what Rav Hamnuna Sava <note>The Elder</note> did: when he would teach the students the matters of wisdom, he would first present before them chapters of foolish words <note>humorous or mundane introductory remarks</note>, because there is a benefit to wisdom because of it. This is what is written: **"A little folly is more precious than wisdom and honor"** <note>Ecclesiastes 10:1</note>, because it provides a preparation for wisdom and honor for wisdom. And regarding this it is written: "And you shall add wisdom and seal it with folly."

Rabbi Yose said: "More precious than wisdom and honor"—meaning the preciousness of wisdom and its beauty, and the honor of the Glory of all that is above. What is it? "A little folly." For the more that folly is seen and revealed, the more the preciousness of wisdom and honor is revealed above, more than anything that resembles it. "As the advantage of light from darkness"—the benefit of light is only known from the darkness. And forever, what is the preparation of light? It is wisdom. If not for wisdom, the Torah would not be known, and because of wisdom, the light ascends and is honored.

Rabbi Yitzchak said: One who eats sweet things does not know the taste of sweetness until he tastes bitterness. Who can tell what is sweet? Only one who has tasted this bitterness. And this is what is written: **"God has made the one corresponding to the other"** <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14</note>, and it is written: **"Good..."**

It cites the practice of Rav Hamnuna Sava, who used "foolish words" to prepare his students for deep wisdom.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

What is the secret of the three within it? From this, do not let go. These three are the levels of names by which a human being is called:
**Adam** · **Gever** · **Enosh** · **Ish** <note>These are four Hebrew synonyms for "man" or "person." The Zohar ranks them by spiritual significance.</note>.
The greatest of them all is **Adam**, because it is written: > And God created **Adam** in His own image <note>Genesis 1:27</note>, and it is written: > For in the image of God He made **Adam** <note>Genesis 9:6</note>. It does not say *Gever*, *Enosh*, or *Ish*. 

Rabbi Yehuda said: If that is so, look at what is written: > When any **Adam** <note>original: "Adam ki yakriv"</note> among you brings an offering to the Lord <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. It does not say *Gever*, *Enosh*, or *Ish*. Whoever desires to bring an offering must be of the highest quality. 

Rabbi Yitzhak said: Come and see, the sustenance of the world—both the upper and lower realms—is the offering brought through the unification of the Holy One, Blessed be He. And what is it that may draw near before Him in this unification? It is called **Adam**, for he is the most precious of them all. 

He replied: If so, what of this which is written: > When an **Adam** shall have in the skin of his flesh... <note>Leviticus 13:2</note> and so on, and it becomes > a plague of leprosy in the skin of his flesh? 

He said to him: For this one, the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to purify him more than all others, because he stands at the highest level of them all and should not remain in such a state <note>i.e., in a state of impurity or "leprosy," which the Zohar views as a spiritual blemish on the divine image</note>. Therefore, it is written regarding the *Adam*: > **he shall be brought** to the priest. It does not say "he shall come," but "he shall be brought," for whoever sees him is obligated to bring him before the priest, so that the Holy Holy Image <note>term: Diyukna - the mystical form or "blueprint" of man that mirrors the divine</note> should not remain in that condition. 

Yet it is written: > When any **Ish Ish** <note>man, man</note> has a discharge <note>Leviticus 15:2</note>, and regarding a man who sins it says > when an **Ish** has in the skin of his flesh... the priest... <note>referencing various purity laws</note>, but it does not say "he shall be brought" regarding them. 

He said to him: But look, it is written "And it shall be," yet the word **Adam** is missing. If the word **Adam** is missing, why is he not called **Adam**? He replied: An **Adam** who is called a "servant to the King," as it is written: > Not so with My servant Moses <note>Numbers 12:7</note>. Moses, My servant, is here called **Ish** <note>referring to "The Man of God"</note>, and because of this, he is elevated. 

He said to him: If so, look at what is written: > The Lord is a **Man** <note>original: "Ish"</note> of war <note>Exodus 15:3</note>, and it does not say **Adam**. He replied: > The secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him <note>Psalms 25:14</note>. He said: If so, I have seen the difference between them all, and after this, I have not yet merited the full understanding. He said to him: Go to Rabbi Abba, for I have learned from him on the condition that it not be revealed.

He went to Rabbi Abba and found him expounding, saying: When is the "Completeness of the Name" <note>term: Selimuta - perfection or wholeness</note> established? When the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits upon His Throne. Until He sits upon His Throne, completeness is not found, as it is written: > and upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of an **Adam** upon it from above <note>Ezekiel 1:26</note>. This implies that the name **Adam** is the sum and the completeness of everything. 

Rabbi Yehuda said: Blessed be the Merciful One that I have found you in this! He said to him: If so, it is written "The Lord is a Man (*Ish*) of war" and not *Adam*? He replied: That would be a degradation <note>to use the term of "completeness" in a context of war/division</note>. Come and see: completeness of all is found, and for this reason, He is called *Ish*. But here, the completeness of all and the inclusion of all is why He is called **Adam**. He recited over him: > The law of Your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver pieces <note>Psalms 119:72</note>.

He said to him further: It is written, > Lord, You preserve **Adam** and beast <note>Psalms 36:7</note>, and it does not say *Ish* and beast. He replied: Is it not so? It is written > from **Adam** unto beast <note>Exodus 11:7</note>. He said to him: That which is written "Adam and beast" is like that which is written: > from the cedar that is in Lebanon even unto the hyssop that springs out of the wall <note>1 Kings 5:13</note>. This is the "fullness of the verse," which takes the highest of them all and the lowest of them all. So too here: the highest of all and the lowest of all.

He said to him: But it is written: > and there was no **Adam** to till the ground <note>Genesis 2:5</note>. Come and see that everything in the world exists only as the "Building of Adam," and they all exist and are found in the world because of him. They were all delayed until he who is called **Adam** arrived. This is what is written: [And every plant] of the field before it was in the earth... "Before" <note>original: "Terem"</note> means "not yet" in the translation, because the Upper Image <note>Diyukna</note> had not yet been established. This is why it says "and there was no Adam"—meaning all things were held back for the sake of this Image until it appeared. Because of this, they did not appear except in the Image that was fitting for it. This is what is written: > And the Lord God formed the **Adam** <note>Genesis 2:7</note>, because, as we have established, he is the completeness of all and the inclusion of all.

It was taught: At the hour when Adam was created, he stood upon a hundred pillars and was crowned, as it is written: > The throne had six steps <note>1 Kings 10:19</note>. Therefore, this one was created in the side of life, fitting to sit upon the Throne. And come and see: once Adam was created, everything was established—all that is above and below—and everything was included within Adam. 

It was taught: Rabbi Yose said, it is written: > As for the likeness of their faces, they had the face of an **Adam** <note>Ezekiel 1:10</note>. This is the "all of the all," and everything is upon them according to this Image. Rabbi Yehuda said: But it is written, "and the face of a lion on the right side for the four of them"—was it not decreed from the beginning?

# Tazria

Observe the ways that were spoken of, all of them (34b) in three colors, and in the formation that is not engraved with all colors and all forms, as we have learned: his face and the covering of the throne—not the end of the throne, but below, in the actual likeness of Adam <note>The "Likeness of Adam" refers to the Primordial Man (Adam Kadmon), the spiritual blueprint of the universe</note> who includes all colors and all forms. Rabbi Isaac opened: Everyone who is seen under the dominion of Adam is called so because those below are in the likeness of Adam. For there is another "man" who is at the end; at first, he came with a supernal spirit like a book of merit. When Adam was created, he was in this supernal holy likeness, and two spirits came with him from two sides, from the right and from the left, both belonging to Adam. The spirit of the right is called the **Holy Soul** <note>original: "Nishmata Kadisha"</note>, as it is written:
> And He breathed into his nostrils the **breath of life** <note>Genesis 2:7</note>
And the spirit of the left is called the **Living Soul** <note>original: "Nefesh Chayah"</note>. It is life, and it descends from above to below, and it does not settle with the other. When the "Koph" <note>The letter Koph often symbolizes the "ape of God" or the external forces (Sitra Achra) that mimic the holy</note> entered the Sabbath, and it is the nest of man, they were made from the side of the spirit; they spread out into the world but their bodies were not completed, and they were not created like this body as male and female, and they were born into the world—and these are the "plagues of the children of men" <note>A reference to demons or spirits that lack physical bodies</note>. <term>Come and see</term> <note>Aramaic: "Ta Chazi" - a standard Zoharic opening for a new insight</note>: the higher ones among them do not attach below; they hang in the air and overhear what they hear from above, and from them, those below gain knowledge. <term>Come and see</term>: from the assembly of holiness, three brains and crowns emerge. The brains of the assembly are engraved and hidden together on the side of **Strength** <note>original: "Gevurah" - the attribute of Judgment</note>, which are called "Gevurot" (Strengths/Judgments). They join together and become one body. And when these enter as a body, they search for "man and not man," as we have learned... everything is a living soul that comforts, for it is written that all is judgment and all is one.

Rabbi Judah said: We have learned this. It was not in the hands of Rabbi Isaac to bring this sweetness before Rabbi Shimon. He said to them: Come and see the section we have learned, where it is written:
> This one shall be called Woman, for from Man was this one taken <note>Genesis 2:23</note>
And the proof of these is "this" (Zot) is lacking, and here is freedom, which is the male. Rather, thus is the proof: she is all in one scale, ascending and reaching the lower judgment. They are hidden and joined in the **hair** <note>original: "Se'arin"</note> of this one, to be called a "cut male." And when the **storm** <note>term: "Se'arah" - a play on the word for hair (Se'ar), implying a storm of judgment</note> of the spirit is removed from him, he is subdued, and the lower judgments are not present. Because of this, he is called **pure** <note>original: "Tahor"</note>. For one is not called pure except from the side that weakens [the impurity]. When one emerges from the impure, he is called pure, as it is written:
> Who can produce a pure thing from an impure one? <note>Job 14:4</note>
Certainly from the impure. And here it is written:
> And if a man’s hair falls out from his head, he is bald; he is **pure** <note>Leviticus 13:40</note>
And come, the spirit of this living soul is the assembly of holiness. Because of this, the skull of the spirit of this one is entirely red like a rose, and the hairs are red within red. From it, lower crowns branch out below that awaken judgments in the world. When the **storm/hair** is removed from him and the supernal **Kindness** <note>original: "Chesed"</note> is revealed, everything is subdued and he is called "supported." Rabbi Judah said: If he is called "supported," he should be called **holy** <note>original: "Kadosh"</note> and not "pure." He replied: If he were "holy," he would only be called so when the hair is hanging. For holiness depends on the hair, as it is written:
> He shall be **holy**, he shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow long <note>Numbers 6:5, regarding the Nazirite</note>
But this one is called "pure" from the side of those hanging below him. In this manner, the hair is removed from him and he is purified. Every vision seen from the side of the spirit and the judgments hidden in it is not purified until the hair is removed from it. Once the hair is removed, it is purified. And if you say "Man" is not so, for he is the perfection of all and Mercy is found in him—therefore it is not so for him, for all are holy and sanctified in him. But the "living soul" is judgment, and judgments are hidden in it; it is not subdued until the hair is removed. <term>Come and see</term>: the **Levites**, who come from this side of Judgment, are not purified until their hair is removed. As it is written:
> Thus shall you do to them to cleanse them: sprinkle the water of purification upon them, and let them pass a razor over all their flesh... <note>Numbers 8:7</note>
And because they should be further wise, they need the Priest <note>The Kohen, who represents Chesed/Kindness</note> who comes from the side of supernal Kindness to elevate them, as it is written:
> And Aaron shall offer the Levites as a wave offering before the Lord <note>Numbers 8:11</note>
Just as is fitting for this living soul to be sent, so that when it desires to be further sweetened—

## Main Text (Zohar)

...more so to reveal within it the **Supreme Mercy** <note>Hebrew: *Chesed Elyon*</note>, and it is covered and concealed below, and there was joy as the crown of Adam. And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to illuminate the hair in this vision, it is not in vain that the hair is darkened, as it is written: *and the appearance was like a lamp* <note>original: *melyukas* - likely a Greek-derived term for a lamp or light</note> in this very vision. And it is not in vain that the hair is darkened until the hair is removed by the spirit, so that the teachers may look upon them and break all those crowns that are joined in the hair. Returning to it, it is written: *And it was...* <note>Reference to Genesis 1:3 "And there was light" or the continuation of the discussed verse</note> at the time when the King's son comes to arrange the head and the hair of the head, and with it, the end of the appearance. Three things, and *you shall do for them for purification*. What is *and you shall do for them*? In the likeness of that which is Above. The end of the hidden things is the water of purification, the remnants of the dew of the male principle, for he who finds the water of purification, they are the remnants of the dew. In the time to come, it is written:
> *I will sprinkle clean water upon you* <note>Ezekiel 36:25</note>

And they shall enter in purity in the likeness of that which is Above, for the rectifications of this vision below are like the **Supreme Mercy**, and it is purified from everything. And we have learned: it is written to strike with a razor and not with scissors. Rather, it is because the hair must be removed at its root, and the lower judgments <note>Hebrew: *Dinim*</note> shall be removed from their cycles. And at the time when deeds are mended below, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to remove this hair and to prune it so that it shall not be found and shall be healed, as it is written: > *If his head be made bald* <note>Leviticus 13:40</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: The greatest of all these visions of hair is that which the Holy One, Blessed be He, made below in the likeness of that which is Above, and called it "Baldness" <note>Hebrew: *Kereach*</note>. When? At the time when the moment is in the hand of this vision of the opening of the "Baldness of the Voice." And when the baldness covers his head, it is all hair, and they strike to purify from the strength of the ornaments of kings; it was decreed in his eyes and he opened to purify. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to say: Why did I make you in the likeness of that which is Above? It is not the time for ascending in the worlds, death is below, and it is among the lower ones, as it is written: > *And they went down alive into the pit* <note>Numbers 16:33</note>. What is *and it was the pit*? It is **Gehinnom** <note>Purgatory/Hell</note>, for there the living creatures rest, and there is no one to have mercy on them, and they are ready to be quickened and raised up when the Holy One, Blessed be He, awakens to act and to quicken them, as it is written: > *The Lord kills and brings to life; He brings down to the grave and raises up* <note>1 Samuel 2:6</note>.

**And if** his head be made bald from the corners of his face. There are three faces and the life of the faces. And who are the faces? These rise up, those who search the faces of wrath. And all the types that hang from those faces are strong, all of them are strong, those who do not have mercy. And when the hair is removed from the side of those faces, they are all removed and gathered. For it was taught: all those that hang from the hair of the head are higher than the others and are not as strong as them; but all those that hang from the side of the hair of those faces are all strong and mighty. And because of this, his face glows like the void <note>Note: likely should read "like the space" or "like the furnace"</note> because of the intent of what is written regarding the **Spark of Hardness** <note>Hebrew: *Botzina de-Kardinuta* - a Kabbalistic term for the primordial spark of restricted light/judgment</note>, and regarding this it is written: *His face is their portion.* > *The face of the Lord is against those who do evil* <note>Psalms 34:17</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: What is "like a plague" <note>Hebrew: *Nega*</note> that is silent? It is a literal plague. And the life returns below, and the "cup" <note>spiritual vessel</note> is not removed, as it is written "to the white" to be silent. Rabbi Yose said: He who brings down, does not bring down below but into the "cup," in the manner of the bull and the cup. Rabbi Isaac said: Even though he brings down below, the life of the redness does not go like a plague, as it is written: > *Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow* <note>Isaiah 1:18</note>. And when they all return, mercies are found and the weapons [of judgment] are not found <margin>(Variant: are uprooted)</margin>. The teaching says: it is written "it is a plague" and it is written "it is a plague"—one male and one female. Rather, when the female is found because of the sins of those below, it is written "it is a plague." And when the male is not to be purified because of the sins of those below, it is written "it is a plague." And these matters are known <margin>(Variant: judgments)</margin>, those that come from this side and the merits that come from that side. And the sacrifices that are needed to be brought are known, as it is written: > *a male without blemish* <note>Leviticus 1:3</note> and it is written > *he shall bring a female without blemish* <note>Leviticus 4:32</note>, for behold, it is known from which matters the judgments come and from whom the merits come, which are guarded like this or like that. And regarding this it is written: > *The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit* <note>Psalms 51:19</note> to bring out the morning sacrifice, for it is not written "a broken spirit" regarding those, but for the worlds and the saturation of those who go and hang. *And if the priest shall see...* Rabbi Yose taught, etc.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on Parashat Tazria, specifically addressing the spiritual roots of physical skin afflictions and the sanctity of human union. It connects the role of the Priest (Kohen) to the divine attribute of Mercy (Chesed).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Tazria** <note>Leviticus 12:1 - "When a woman conceives"</note><-

> "O Hearer of prayer, unto You all flesh shall come" (Psalms 65:3)

"Hearer of prayer" refers to **the Holy One, blessed be He**. **Rabbi Hezekiah** said: It should have said "Hearer of prayers" <note>plural</note>. Why does it say "prayer" <note>singular</note>? Rather, this "prayer" refers to the Throne of Prayer <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note>... and regarding this, it is "Hearer of prayer," which is the Prayer of the Hand <note>The Tefillin worn on the arm, representing the feminine aspect/Malchut</note>... "Unto You all flesh shall come" with the claims of the weary body... and afterwards "when there shall be a mark of leprosy in the skin of the flesh." <note>Leviticus 13:2</note> Therefore it is not written "all spirits shall come," but "all flesh shall come." What is "unto You"? It is as it was said: "And he shall be brought to the Priest" <note>Leviticus 13:2</note>—this is **the Holy One, blessed be He**, who is **Chesed** <term>Chesed: The divine attribute of Loving-kindness and Mercy</term> and the Priest. Come and see, first it says "Aaron the Priest" and later it says "the Priest" without qualification; this is **the Holy One, blessed be He**, who is Mercy...

> "When a person has on the skin of his body..." (Leviticus 13:2)

"And he shall be" <note>Hebrew: *Ve-hayah*</note> refers to **the Holy One, blessed be He**. Come and see, because upon Him depend all judgments and all holiness. Come and see, it should have said "to strike and to rebuke and to bring up." Rather, all is a rebuke... to cause him to turn back <note>in repentance</note> so that the matter may ascend before Him. **Rabbi Isaac said**: Thus we have learned, the "plague of leprosy" <note>Hebrew: *Nega Tzara'at*</note> is a powerful force that spreads in the world. *Tzara'at* implies "closure" <note>Hebrew: *Segiru*</note>, as it was said: a closure of the male aspect arose, a closure of the female aspect arose, so that [blessing] does not descend to the world. "When it shall be in a man"—in a man generally. "And he shall be brought to the Priest"—this is the lower Priest <note>the human Kohen</note> who is prepared to open that closure and to raise the prayers that are found through his hands, as blessings above and below, so that the "closure" is removed and the guards of mercy are awakened over all. Therefore, "he shall be brought to the Priest."

**Rabbi Abba said**: Woe to the children of the world who are not found [worthy] and do not know the glory of the **Matron** <term>Matronita: The Shekhinah/Divine Presence as a Queen</term>. It is written of them: "And I have set you apart from the peoples, that you should be Mine" (Leviticus 20:26). And it is written: "Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be holy; for I am holy" (Leviticus 11:44). If they distance themselves, where is their holiness? Their will should not be to distance themselves from Him... In what way are human beings found flawed and separated from the holiness of their bodies, so as not to be found perfect and exalted above all? For this reason, the union of human beings should be at [proper] times, and they should know how to direct their will to cleave to **the Holy One, blessed be He**. At what time? At midnight, when **the Holy One, blessed be He**, enters the Garden of Eden to delight with the righteous, for then is the **Time of Favor** <term>Sha'ata de-Re'uta: A cosmic window of divine openness</term> to cleave to them.

And the companions who labor in the Torah join with Her <note>the Shekhinah</note> then to find the Holy King, and they occupy themselves with the Torah in the assembly; then there is a will to be sanctified with the holiness of **the Holy One, blessed be He**, and to direct the will to cleave to Him. And those companions who labor in the Torah, their union is at the time when the other [divine] union is found... to direct the will to cleave to **the Holy One, blessed be He** and the Assembly <note>the Shekhinah</note>, for that is the Time of Favor when all above and below are blessed. See the people who distance themselves from Him and act like animals. Where is their holiness to be found holy? Where are those holy souls that descend from above? And King Solomon cried out and said:

> "Also, that the soul be without knowledge is not good" (Proverbs 19:2)

"Knowledge" <note>Hebrew: *Da'at*</note>—this is **the Holy One, blessed be He**. "Is not good"—this refers to those who are sold to their [evil] deeds. "Not good" means that from the "Other Side" <note>the Sitra Achra/forces of evil</note> there is drawn upon them a soul that is not good, because they do not direct their intention to **the Holy One, blessed be He**. One who is drawn after the **Evil Inclination**, his whole will and intention is not toward **the Holy One, blessed be He**, and from the side of the **Evil Inclination** there is drawn upon them a soul that is not good... and he certainly sins in everything. Therefore, evil afflictions rest upon them... to show that **the Holy One, blessed be He**, watches them... until they are found worthy and crowned.

<summary>This passage explains that the Priest (Kohen) acts as a channel for Divine Mercy (Chesed) to heal the "closure" caused by leprosy. It emphasizes that human intimacy must be sanctified and timed to coincide with the Divine union at midnight to draw down holy souls rather than impure ones.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of spiritual purity and impurity, specifically focusing on the laws of the "leprous house" (Tzara'at HaBayit) from the Torah portion Tazria. It connects the physical act of building a home with the spiritual intention of the builder.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And their works are prepared as before and are blessed. Because of this, those who come from the **Side of Impurity** <note>Aramaic: *Sitra de-Masaba*, the realm of unholiness</note> and those who come from the **Side of Purity** <note>Aramaic: *Sitra de-Dachya*</note> are recognized by their strength before the Priest. In this manner it is written:
> <note>Leviticus 14:34</note> When you come into the land of Canaan... and I put the plague of leprosy in a house of the land of your possession.

Is this a "good tidings" <note>The Zohar asks why the Torah uses the language of a gift ("and I shall give/put") for a plague</note> that was found by those who merited to enter the Land? Indeed, the masters have established that they found hidden treasures that [the Canaanites] had hidden in their houses, and [the plague] was a means to bring them out for Israel. But come and see: those of Israel who cleave to **the Holy One, Blessed be He**, the Holy One, Blessed be He loves them, as it is written:
> <note>Malachi 1:2</note> I have loved you, says the Lord.

And because of His love for them, He brought them to the **Holy Land** to settle His **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note> among them and to dwell with them, so that Israel would be found holy above all the people of the world. Come and see, it is written:
> <note>Leviticus 14:46</note> And he who comes into the house... shall be unclean.

And so, at that time [when the Canaanites lived there], when they performed their labors, they would say: "This is for the temple [of idols]," "This is for the shrine," "This is for the ritual." And so, at all those times, because holiness rests upon their hands, that work is sanctified <note>referring to the Israelites</note>. And when it ascends, it ascends to the place of holiness. In this same manner, one who performs a labor for **Idolatry** <note>Hebrew: *Avodah Zarah*</note> or for the "Other Side" which is not holy—once he mentions it during that labor, an **impure spirit** <note>Aramaic: *Ruach Masaba*</note> rests upon it. And when his work ascends, it ascends in that thought. In the manner that so-and-so slaughtered for an idol, they cleave to it just as the impure spirit desires. And they would cry out for their defects <margin>Variant: for their trust</margin> and their filth to the Side of Impurity above. And when they began to build, they would speak a word, and once it was mentioned by their mouths, the impure spirit would descend upon it. When the work was finished, the impure spirit remained.

When Israel entered the Land, **the Holy One, Blessed be He** desired to purify them and bring them close to His gate, and to clear <margin>Variant: and to build</margin> a place for the **Shekhinah**, so that the Shekhinah would not dwell amidst impurity. And because of this, through that plague of leprosy, they would tear down the buildings that [the Canaanites] had labored over and established. Come and see: if this act were not for the finding of treasures, the buildings would remain as a testimony for later generations, as they were behind them. And regarding the dust of that place, it is written:
> <note>Leviticus 14:45</note> And he shall break down the house.

And it is written:
> <note>Leviticus 14:42</note> And he shall take other mortar <note>literally: "other dust"</note>.

This is so that the impure spirit will be removed, and the house will be cleared and sanctified as before, and be established; and Israel will be in holiness as a holy dwelling, for the Shekhinah to be guarded among them. And regarding this we have learned: when people begin to build, they must mention that it is for the service of **the Holy One, Blessed be He**, etc. Because it is written:
> <note>Jeremiah 22:13</note> Woe to him who builds his house without righteousness...

And then the assistance of Heaven rests upon him, and the Holy One, Blessed be He invites holiness upon him and proclaims "Peace" over him:
> <note>Job 5:24</note> And you shall know that your tent is in peace...

What is the meaning of "And you shall visit your habitation and shall not sin"? Rather, "you shall visit" means to declare the matter with his mouth when they are building, and "you shall not sin" is written so that he may live. But if one invites the "Other Side" into his house—such as one who builds with a different intention—from the day it is established, the impure spirit dwells in it and does not depart. That man does not leave the world until he is found in that house <note>suffering for it</note>, and whoever dwells in it can be harmed, for that dwelling has an impure spirit resting in it which harms whoever is found there. And it is a wonder how well-known it is that one is harmed in such a house. One who builds his house like this, it is like a blemish on his body, a blemish from his fortune, and it leads to destruction afterward. Truly, a man should flee to the mountains and not dwell in it; he should dwell in a cave of dust and not dwell in it. And because of this, the Holy One, Blessed be He had pity on Israel, who knew nothing of this matter when they [inherited] those houses. He spoke below to show them, to let them know and let them taste it through the plague. If another strong plague dwells in the house, it will take him out and remove him from the world. And then: "He shall break down the house, its stones and its timber," because it is despised. "And he shall break down the house"—not everything, but so that the building shall [eventually] be established.

## Tazria

There is no service of the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note>, like this: only when this spirit of impurity <note>original: *ruach mesava*</note> is removed can a person truly be purified. We see that those who are bound by the "husks" <note>the *kelipot*, or shells of evil</note> of their companions and desire to remain there—even when they see the afflictions that strike them—do not remove themselves from that house. One calls to his friend and says, "Let us gather in a house that is not pure," and certainly there is a blemish in that house at all times. Rabbi Yose was once in a house and saw a shadow on the wall <note>or "filth in a bowl" depending on the variant reading</note>; he heard a voice saying, "Gather and enter into our dispute." He was shaken before he could even pray. They said to him, "Let us eat." He replied, "A great master is here." Rabbi Yose hurried and was afraid. He saw that it was a type of damaging spirit that passes over the words of its companions to remain in the corners.

Rabbi Hiyya said to him: Come and see, these spirits surround people like the inhabitants of a nest. They come from their own side to anyone who fears sin and seeks to be purified, and even they cannot hinder their dwelling as long as they do not act according to their kind. See, it is written regarding the death of a man: "from fear." He said to him: Because he sinned, he is delayed from the light. But the verse is written: "Peace from fear in your tents" and "The rod of God is not upon them" <note>Job 21:9</note>.

**"And he who owns the house shall come and tell [the priest]..."** <note>Leviticus 14:35</note>. "And he shall tell"—it should have said "and he shall see," or "and he shall bring and tell." He said: In every place, this is a matter of wisdom, and they have already established it.

> "Something like a plague has appeared to me in the house" (Leviticus 14:35)

It should have said "A plague has appeared to me." Why "Something like a plague"? Because it is written:

> "I will put a plague of leprosy in a house of the land of your possession" (Leviticus 14:34)

If it is visible to everyone, why say "Something like a plague"? Rather, at the moment this spirit enters a companion, they are revealed, and they accuse one another. Therefore, "it appeared to me" implies that which was hidden is now revealed, and that which was revealed is now hidden. Afterward, they will see it exactly as it was—a plague in his house that was hidden from his companion. This "telling the priest" is a matter of wisdom. Then the priest comes and clears the house, and they provide him with wisdom and he sees. Once there is wisdom and everything is gathered, then it is written that you shall find good things. These are called "good," for the previous ones were not good, nor were they within the category of holiness and purity.

Rabbi Yehuda asked: How do we establish the verse that says, "houses full of all good things which you did not fill" <note>Deuteronomy 6:11</note>? If the spirit of impurity dwells within them, how can they be "full of all good"? He said to him: "Full of all good" refers to wealth—to silver, gold, and everything else. But "all good" also refers to the removal of the "Other Side." One wicked person <note>referring to the previous Canaanite inhabitants</note> and his call, yet all the houses of Egypt were full of sorceries and errors. However, for the sake of the wealth that was passed on, here too it is for the sake of wealth and property. Israel received two types of wealth: one when they left the exile of Egypt, and one when they came to this land. All of this was certainly to sanctify the land and to remove the spirit of impurity from the land and from the midst of Israel. When a house was demolished, wisdom was found in it, and wealth was found to build his house, so that he would not grieve over his house and would maintain it as a dwelling of holiness.

**And a man** who has a bright spot <note>original: *baheret*</note> in him, etc. Rabbi Yose said: We have seen that the afflictions that surround a person are like a bird's nest. Rabbi Isaac said: There are twenty reasons why one causes a bright spot to appear, and we derive them all from here. When one sees a blemish, he calls one or two witnesses to testify. From here on, the curse is added like two and two, and it does not change, as it is written:

> "A single witness shall not rise up" (Deuteronomy 19:15)

Rabbi Hezekiah was sitting before Rabbi Hama. It is written: "a plague that is white-reddish." This is a plague because it has returned to its color. Rabbi Hama opened and said: It is written that the sins shall be like scarlet, etc. All of these are the sufferings of a penalty in order to purify them, so that they do not remain stained. We have learned that the priests do not rule over them, for they are all liable—red to red and white to white. Through ten categories, this is proven to be pure, and through this, merit and life dwell within him.

<summary>This page discusses the spiritual nature of house leprosy, explaining that the physical affliction was a means to reveal hidden impurity and eventually replace it with "holy wealth" and divine wisdom. It also touches upon the role of the priest and the necessity of removing the "spirit of impurity" from the Land of Israel.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of Parashat Tazria (Leviticus 12-13), specifically focusing on the spiritual and physical diagnosis of leprosy (tzara'at) and the mystical significance of colors.</meta>

## Tazria

And if you should say, it is written of Esau that he was "ruddy" <note>Genesis 25:25</note> and it is written of David <note>1 Samuel 16:12</note> "And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy," <note>original: *admoni*</note> [what is the difference?] Rather, this [David] is the appearance of gold that is worked, but the other [Esau] is not the brightness of gold that is attached. It is written of him [Esau], "ruddy, all over like a hairy garment," in the filth of that serpent. But it is written of David, "with beautiful eyes, and goodly to look to."

Come and see: Redness at first, where whiteness is not seen in it—this is like the strike of a worm. When it comes to be purified, whiteness appears first, and then redness is seen in it; this is the purity for inspection. And it is written <note>Leviticus 13:3</note> "and the priest shall pronounce him unclean," for there was born in him a redness for inspection. And the priest was an expert in all those colors. Sometimes a color of purity would appear to him, and he would wait to see if another color was born in him, or if he should purify him. And this is what is written: "and the priest shall pronounce him unclean," etc.

Rabbi Isaac and Rabbi Judah were walking on the road. Rabbi Judah said: It is written <note>2 Kings 5:27</note> "The leprosy therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee, and unto thy seed for ever." If he [Gehazi] sinned, why should his children suffer? He said to him: He spoke more than the secret of his prophecy; he sinned in that which was not written from his body, but from his excellence, and for this he cursed them all. Furthermore, he said to him: "You laughed at the pepper in the sesame; you went up to the aloe and laughed at two portions, for he divided it for him in a cutting." <note>This passage uses highly cryptic Aramaic metaphors for Gehazi's greed and betrayal of Elisha's spiritual authority.</note> And the laughter of the wicked is a wall to me for searching; and your desire has crossed over all other things. And whoever passes over this is dead to the World to Come. For all the children who serve me, your sesame shall not be for rest; you shall be dead in this world and in the World to Come. And because of this, "the leprosy of Naaman shall cleave unto thee and unto thy seed"—the color of the baldness to be known, and the color of the redness to be known.

Rabbi Yose said: <note>Habakkuk 1:8</note> "as a leopard" <note>original: *namer*</note>. The leopard has spots. Rabbi Isaac said: In the general rule of the prey, they all rule, and there is nothing like this color, as it is written: "a leopard and spots." And because of this, the dominion of that serpent—which is written as the "upper life"—does not rule at all over the crowns of colors like the leopard and its spots. And because of this: "This is the law of the plague of leprosy," like the spots of the leopard.

Rabbi Isaac was going to Cappadocia. On the way, he saw a man who was burdened with a bundle on his shoulders. He said to him: "The mountain of the chest is like your shoulder; do you not have bread?" He said to him: "I am grateful." He went on his way and saw him enter a certain cave. He went on his way and saw a knot of smoke rising from under the earth, and that man entered into a certain redness and was hidden from him. Rabbi Isaac was afraid and bent down at the mouth of the cave until he was sitting there. 

Rabbi Judah and Rabbi Hezekiah passed by; he saw them and approached them and told them the event. Rabbi Judah said: Blessed is the Merciful One who saved you! For this is the cave of the "Closed Sorcery," and all kinds of that baldness are sorceries. They are prepared to mention to the living the wisdom of your life; the children of the "Other Side" <note>The realm of evil/impurity</note> are many, or more, to perform sorceries, and they do not guard themselves from them, and they become "closed" [lepers]. And all kinds of sorceries are like the serpents of the cave.

While they were walking, they encountered a man who was coming, and his belly was swollen, and he was tied upon a donkey. They said to him: "What are you?" He said to him: "A servant, and this is because I am tied upon the donkey." He said to him: "See, he was tied." He said to them: "He was in a village of the children of Rome, and you read in it a white 'Hallel' <note>Song of Praise</note> every day, and he would return to his house and labor in those words," etc. Many things happened; finally, he dwelt in that house and we saw nothing. One day, my son entered the house to review the words; a "blue spirit" <note>A harmful spirit or demon</note> passed by and struck him. His mouth, his eyes, and his hands were twisted, and he could not speak. And I have come to the cave of the "Closed Sorcery" to see if they will tell me a word that will help me. Rabbi Judah said to him: "And likewise my house..."

<meta>This page continues the discussion from the Zohar on Parashat Tazria, focusing on the spiritual laws of habitation and the metaphysical consequences of building a home without holy intent.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Tazria**<-
<note>Leviticus 12:1–15:33</note>

A house—you have known from before this time that another person <note>referring to a spiritual entity or a previous inhabitant</note> was within it below. He said to him: I know that a wise man is destined to be below in it, and one man and his household will be masters of the sickness <note>original: *marei de-mar'a*, likely referring to the plague of leprosy in houses</note>, and their possessions are the "donkeys of the spirit" of the house. And afterward, several people were in it and they did not establish themselves. They said: This is what the colleagues have said, "Woe to their lives who transgress their words." Rabbi Judah opened and said: *Woe to him who builds his house without righteousness and his upper rooms without justice* <note>Jeremiah 22:13</note>. For wherever **Righteousness** <note>original: *Tzedek*, referring to the Divine Presence or the Sefirah of Malkhut</note> is found, all spirits and all damaging demons flee from it and are not found before it. And despite all this, if one precedes and takes a place for another evil one, who surrounds him with many stones, the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, looks upon it. He said to him: This is so, for even the **Holy Name** does not dwell in an impure place. And because of this, freedom is observed in a void place; the Holy Name does not dwell in it, for it belongs to both of them. And if the Holy Name was in a void place from before, all the spirits and all the damaging demons of the world are not able to harm it, Heaven forbid, as long as the holiness is near it. And when he strikes and touches the nest <note>metaphor for the source of impurity</note>, he heals the place and expels the **impure spirit** from its place. And afterward, they build the house with stones and wood, and all of them are meritorious for it, as they were previously in the **Side of Holiness** through **Righteousness**, which goes toward the Holy Name, and Holiness guards over it. And despite all this, there is another atonement: he should distance the house from its place, from the original foundation, by two handbreadths. Now, if it is not seen and our words do not strike the one who prosecutes with that impure spirit to remove him from his place, what is his remedy? If he can leave, he should vacate the house well. And if not, he should strike it as before with other scrapings and plaster, and all of it shall go out and he shall spit upon it from the first place, and rebuild it upon the **Holy Name**. And despite all this, that spirit is not subdued from the first place, for a building of holiness does not dwell upon an impure place. To center and pierce—why does he need to trouble himself so much? At this time it is written: *That which is crooked cannot be made straight* <note>Ecclesiastes 1:15</note>. From the day the Holy Temple was destroyed, protection <note>original: *chasuta*</note> is not found in the world; because of this, a man must be careful so that he may be in the gate. They said: This man built in this way and before him. Rabbi Isaac said: It is forbidden for us to embrace him and toward the Great Creator who voices... <unclear>illegible</unclear> ...at the void of his place. Now that the Sages have pitied the distant ones of the world, the distant ones of freedom, they have hidden from all; it is forbidden for us to appear before them. Blessed be the Merciful One who saved us from their burning, and for this man it is forbidden. Rabbi Judah said: But have we not learned, "One may heal oneself with anything except **idolatry**," etc.? <note>Talmud Pesachim 25a</note> He said to him: This is regarding if they were, and not only that, but it is written: *You shall show them no mercy* <note>Deuteronomy 7:2</note>, and *one who passes his son or daughter through the fire* <note>Deuteronomy 18:10</note>. They went on their way. That man went to look at a cave, and a serpent was dwelling for him in the cave; when he went out, the serpent came to bind him from behind, blew a smoke of fire, struck him on the head, and killed him. While they were waiting, the serpent went up and found him dead; he took him... <unclear>illegible</unclear> ...and they did not find them. After one day, at the time when Rabbi Judah and Rabbi Hezekiah were walking, he cried before them and told them the event. Rabbi Isaac said: Have we not seen many merits for you, that it is forbidden to look? We have learned: Blessed be the Merciful One, for all His works are truth and His ways are justice. And all of them are in His examinations to walk in the path of truth in this world and in the world to come, and concerning them it is written: *But the path of the righteous is as the light of dawn* <note>Proverbs 4:18</note>. Rabbi Eleazar said: In all the works of a man, he must dedicate them to the **Holy Name**. What does "to the Holy Name" mean? To mention with his mouth the Holy Name over everything that he does, for everything is for His service, so that the **Other Side** <note>original: *Sitra Achra*</note> shall not dwell upon it, because it is always ready near human beings and can take dominion over that work. And because of this, if we have set a bowl, it was found and guarded over it.

<summary>This passage discusses the spiritual dangers of building a home without holy intention, warning that impure spirits (Sitra Achra) can inhabit physical structures. It emphasizes the necessity of dedicating all actions and buildings to the Holy Name to ensure divine protection.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Tazria**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, meaning "She conceives."</note>

...upon a soiled spirit. And as for one who washes thus, he who is appointed over him from the <term>Other Side</term> <note>Aramaic: Sitra Achra; the realm of spiritual evil or impurity</note> has no need of him. And then it is written: <note>Deuteronomy 23:10</note> *“And you shall keep yourself from every evil thing.”*

Rabbi Eleazar was traveling to see his father <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> and Rabbi Isaac was with him. Rabbi Isaac said: "Let us speak words of Torah as we walk." Rabbi Eleazar opened and said: <note>Genesis 12:13</note> *“Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister.”*

This verse is difficult. Would Abraham, who was God-fearing and the beloved of the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, say such a thing about his wife just so they would turn away from him? Rather, although Abraham was God-fearing, he did not rely on his own merit; instead, the Holy One, Blessed be He, put the merit of his wife before his own merit. For it is known that because of the woman who goes with him, wealth comes to a man, and all is for her sake. He returned to his thought as they were descending to Egypt: what a wise wife! Whoever merits a wise wife merits everything. And it is written: <note>Proverbs 31:11</note> *“The heart of her husband safely trusts in her...”*

And Abraham was traveling with the miracle of an angel who went with him, and he relied on her merit so that they would not be able to harm him, and the proof is thus. For this reason, he did not give any cause for severity <note>judgment</note> to his wife herself. Furthermore, an angel was walking before the woman and said to Abraham: "Do not fear for her; I have come before to arrange to bring out wealth from the other nations and to guard her from everything." And then Abraham did not fear for his wife, but only for himself, because the angel was not with him, but only with her. He said: "Behold, she is protected, but I might be killed." And because of this, he said: *“Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister... that it may be well with me for thy sake.”*

"That it may be well with me"—it should have said "for her," as it is written: <note>Genesis 12:12</note> *“And it shall come to pass, when the Egyptians shall see thee, that they shall say, This is his wife...”* and because of this, "they will kill me" is what should follow. Rather, "that it may be well with me" refers to the life of the woman. "That it may be well with me" in this world first, regarding wealth. "And my soul shall live because of thee"—in the Upper World. For if you do not stray from the path of truth, I shall merit wealth in this world because of you; but if you stray from the path, that path is death. But "my soul shall live because of thee" in this world because of you. And because that angel was before her to guard her, what is written? <note>Genesis 12:17</note> *“And the Lord plagued Pharaoh... because of Sarai.”*

Certainly, she would say to the angel, "Strike!" and he would strike. And because of this, Abraham did not fear anything at all, for she was protected. And as for what they said—that he feared for himself—it was because he did not see the same protection with himself. Come and see: at times Sarah commanded the angel to strike Pharaoh, and he brought plagues. Sarah established a sign for the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>Knesset Yisrael; the spiritual personification of the Jewish people</note> in Egypt. Rabbi Isaac opened: <note>Micah 7:15</note> *“According to the days of thy coming out of the land of Egypt will I show unto him marvelous things.”*

The Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to bring <term>Redemption</term> to His children, just as in the time of the days when the Holy One, Blessed be He, rose up to guard them and to show those plagues, as you have said, and He established them for the sake of Israel. Come and see the difference between this redemption and the redemption from Egypt: The redemption from Egypt was against one king and one kingdom; here, it will involve all the kings of the world. And then the Holy One, Blessed be He, will be honored throughout the whole world, and they shall all know the dominion of the Holy One, Blessed be He. And they shall all be struck with upper plagues, twofold, because they all oppressed Israel.

And then the dominion of the Holy One, Blessed be He, shall be revealed, as it is written: <note>Zechariah 14:9</note> *“And the Lord shall be king over all the earth.”* And then they shall all bring Israel as an offering to the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: <note>Isaiah 66:20</note> *“And they shall bring all your brethren...”* Then the Patriarchs shall stand in joy to see the redemption of their children as in the beginning, as it is written: *“According to the days of thy coming out of the land of Egypt will I show unto him marvelous things.”*

->Rabbi Isaac said, and all of them:<-
<margin>And remember</margin>

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Zohar's commentary on the Torah portion of Metzora (Leviticus 14). It establishes a thematic link between physical leprosy and the spiritual neglect of Torah study, emphasizing the protective presence of the Shekhinah (the Divine Presence).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Portion of the Law of the Leper**<-

**And the Lord spoke** to Moses, saying: This shall be the law of the leper in the day of his cleansing, etc. <note>Leviticus 14:1-2</note> Rabbi Abba opened the discussion with the verse: **"Be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment."** <note>Job 19:29</note> The word for "judgment" (*shaddun*) is written in a way that suggests "demons" (*shedin*). How much must human beings guard their paths and look toward the Holy One, blessed be He, so they do not stray from the proper path, nor transgress the words of the Torah, nor forget them! For anyone who does not labor in the Torah and does not exert effort in it, it is as if—if it were possible to say such a thing—he "cuts the saplings" <note>A classic Kabbalistic metaphor for causing a rift in the Divine unity</note> and causes a blemish. He drives away the freshness of the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence</note> from him. And those guardian angels who walk with him depart from him. Not only that, but they proclaim before him and say: "Depart from the vicinity of so-and-so, who has no concern for the honor of his Master!" Woe to him, for the Shekhinah has departed from him and he is given a portion in the evil path. But when a person exerts effort in the service of his Master and labors in the Torah, many guardians are ready to protect him, the Shekhinah dwells upon him, and they all proclaim before him: "Give honor to the image of the King!" <note>The human soul as a reflection of the Divine</note> Thus, the honor of the King is recognized in this world and in the world to come; happy is his portion. Come and see: when a person neglects the Torah after having labored in it, a decree of death is issued against him and against all the people of the world. Regarding the wicked, it is written that a sharp sword is drawn. Because of this, "Be afraid of the sword," meaning the "bandits" <note>spiritual forces of destruction</note> etc. "For wrath brings the punishment of the sword"—what is this "wrath of the sword"? We have learned that the Holy One, blessed be He, has a sword with which He judges the guilty, as it is written: **"The sword of the Lord is filled with blood."** <note>Isaiah 34:6</note> This alludes to the beginning of the Crown <note>Keter, the highest Sefirah/Divine attribute</note>. Therefore, "Be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment," so that you may know there is one who holds the sword against lawlessness and malice, a sword that consumes everything. This is what is written: **"This shall be the law of the leper."** <note>The word for leper, 'Metzora', is traditionally interpreted as 'Motzi Ra'—one who brings forth evil speech.</note>

---

**This** shall be the law of the leper. Rabbi Elazar opened with a discourse on the pleasant praises of how human beings are sustained. This verse has been explained, but come and see: people do not exert effort to listen or look toward the will of their Master, and every day [warnings] skip before them, yet no one pays attention. At the hour when night falls and the gates are opened, the Female of the Great Abyss <note>A reference to the source of the 'Other Side' or demonic realms</note> awakens, and many damaging spirits are found in the world. Then a deep sleep falls upon all the people of the world, and even upon all those who possess a living awakening, and visions rule the world, informing people of things—some of which are false and some of which are true—and because of this, they are bound in sleep. When the North Wind awakens and the night is divided <note>Midnight</note>, then the [harsh forces] cease, and the Holy One, blessed be He, enters the Garden of Eden to delight with the righteous. At that time, all the [birds] beat their wings beneath the wings of the rooster and call out, and all the people of the world awaken in their beds, but there is no one to awaken his spirit toward the Holy One, blessed be He. When the light comes, it calls out, and all the hosts and ministers above gather to face the glory of the morning, etc. Then many gates are opened in all directions, and the Gate of Kindness (*Chesed*) is opened, through which the Assembly of Israel <note>Knesset Yisrael, another name for the Shekhinah</note> gains merit for all the people of the world. This is the meaning of: **"And he planted a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba"** <note>Genesis 21:33</note>. But there is no one who awakens his spirit to join with his Master...

<summary>This page introduces the spiritual causes of leprosy, linking it to the abandonment of Torah study and the subsequent loss of Divine protection. It also describes the cosmic shifts that occur at midnight when the Holy One enters the Garden of Eden to delight with the souls of the righteous.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the spiritual consequences of slander (Lashon Hara) and the process of the soul's purification after death, transitioning into the ritual laws for the leper (Metzora) from Leviticus 14.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **The Leper** <-

They bend and stand before the King when they are awakened against him, and they seize him like a prisoner. No merit is found for him to be acquitted. Then it is written <note>Leviticus 13:46</note> "And he shall be covered... the priest shall pronounce him unclean and shut him up." For before a person departs from this world, he undergoes many judgments while the soul is still with the body, before they are separated from one another. And there is no one who notices, even at that time when the hour arrives for the soul to separate from the body, until the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note> is revealed. Then the soul rejoices in the love of the Shekhinah and goes out toward her. If the person is righteous, the soul binds to her and cleaves to her; but if not, the Shekhinah departs and the soul remains, wandering and mourning over the ruin of the body. 

This is like a donkey-driver whose donkey does not separate from him but goes around following him. Afterward, the soul cleaves to many judgments until it is surrounded by them at the hands of <term>Dumah</term> <note>The angel in charge of the souls of the deceased</note>, and the body is judged in the grave until it returns to the dust. The soul departs this world through judgments, and through the strength of the acceptance of its suffering, it is released from the place where the righteous dwell. After it has received its punishment and the time for its purification arrives, it is then raised up from there and wrapped in garments, like a person wrapped in a cloak. They ascend with the soul until it reaches the lower <term>Garden of Eden</term>, where it bathes in the river of fire and is perfumed with the scents there, all of which are like incense of myrrh and frankincense. Then they ascend with it until it is brought as an offering upon the altar. This is what is written <note>Leviticus 14:2</note> **"This shall be the law of the leper in the day of his cleansing: He shall be brought unto the priest,"** referring to the High Priest above <note>The archangel Michael or a celestial spiritual force</note>. For a soul that is not found worthy in this world has no remedy in this manner, and if it is "crooked, it cannot be made straight."

**"This shall be the law of the leper."** Rabbi Isaac opened the discussion: <note>Ecclesiastes 1:5</note> **"The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down..."** This verse has been explained regarding the wisdom of a person while he exists in this world. Then "the sun ariseth and the sun goeth down" at the time a person departs from this world; if he is found in <term>repentance</term>, then "to his place he pants, where he arose"—he shines there. And if he is righteous, he is entirely pure, and he may eat of the holy things. 

Come and see: The Holy One, Blessed be He, prevails over the laws of the world. It is written that because of <term>evil speech</term> <note>Lashon Hara; gossip or slander</note>, a person is stricken with leprosy. We have established that the verse **"This shall be the law of the leper"** <note>Hebrew: *Metzora*</note> means "This is the law of the one who brings out an evil name" <note>Hebrew: *Motzi Shem Ra*, a wordplay on *Metzora*</note>. Rabbi Hiyya said: Anyone who utters evil speech, all his limbs become defiled and he is fit to be shut away, because that evil word ascends and awakens an <term>impure spirit</term> over him. It is found that as he acts below, so is the matter awakened above. 

He opened and said: <note>Isaiah 1:21</note> **"How is the faithful city become a harlot!"** Whoever deviates from the faith of her husband turns into a harlot. "It was full of judgment"—the Holy One, Blessed be He, pushes her away. Because she turned her word to another, the spirit of holiness departed from her, and "now murderers" dwell there. If this happened to Jerusalem, the holy city, how much more so for other people. This is what is written: "The law of the leper." Rabbi Judah said: "This shall be"—certainly this stands against him to exact punishment, as the end of the verse proves. **"In the day of his cleansing, he shall be brought to the priest."** What does this teach us? It teaches that for one who possesses an evil tongue, his prayer does not enter before the Holy One, Blessed be He, for an impure spirit has been awakened against him. But once he returns in repentance and accepts his penance, what is written? "In the day of his cleansing, he shall be brought to the priest."

---

**"And the priest shall command** to take for him that is to be cleansed two living birds..." Rabbi Isaac and Rabbi Yose were walking before Rabbi Shimon one day toward Ein Dor. He knew everything from the breath of their hearts, saying: "Regarding these matters, we do not speak as mere travelers, but from your hearts." And it was said. They were brothers to him. He opened and said: <note>Leviticus 14:4</note> **"Then shall the priest command to take for him that is to be cleansed two birds alive and clean, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop."**
