<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the purification of the leper (Metzora) and the spiritual mechanics of the Tabernacle service. It follows the previous section's focus on the "side of impurity" and the necessity of ritual cleansing to restore the Divine Presence.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**The Leper (Metzora)**<-

Come and see, **come and see**: when a person exerts themselves in the service of their Master and engages with the Torah, <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kadosh Barukh Hu"</note> rests upon them and the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note> is found before them. However, as soon as a person turns toward sin, the Shekhinah departs from them. <term>The Holy One, Blessed be He</term> distances Himself from them, and all the sides of their Master’s holiness distance themselves. Then, a spirit of impurity rests upon them, and all the sides of impurity come to be found there, assisting the person in their decline. After they exert themselves and return in repentance, <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> causes Kindness <note>The Sefirah of Chesed</note> to descend upon them.

Come and see, it is written: *“Then the priest shall command to take for him that is to be cleansed two live clean birds...”* (Leviticus 14:4). Since it says "two birds," would I not know they are "live"? Rather, this refers to the service of Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>, for all life—actual life—comes from there. The lower Wisdom stands facing the upper Wisdom <term>from the hidden faithful treasures</term>. *“And cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop.”* The "scarlet" <note>literally "worm of crimson"</note> comes from the side of the red, from the lower <term>Strength</term> <note>Gevurah</note> as before. And the "hyssop" is a small image <note>representing humility</note>; therefore, the cedar wood and the hyssop are joined as one, and upon this the letter *Vav* is found as one. They are found as one husk and one kernel, and they are called "small" and "lower," and all of them return the person to their Creator. For they are purified through these lower elements—the cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet—which are found on this side but depend on higher matters.

**Rabbi Yehuda** and **Rabbi Isaac** were walking on the road and they sat in a certain field and ate. After they finished their prayers, they stood up and went on. **Rabbi Yehuda** opened with words of Torah and said:
> *“She is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her, and happy is everyone who holds her fast.”* (Proverbs 3:18)

The "Tree of Life" is the Torah, which is a high, great, and mighty tree. It is called the "Torah of Truth" because through it, things that were hidden and unknown are revealed. The life of all higher life is contained within it, and from it, life goes out to those who "lay hold of her." For those who hold onto the Torah hold onto everything, above and below. *“And happy is everyone who holds her fast.”* These "supporters" are those who support the students of the house of study <note>the patrons of scholars</note>. Come and see, as they have established: "and her supporters etc." <term>for the faithful ones</term> who go out from her are "happy." These are the supporters who do not falter but rather support the Torah from afar to the ends. "From afar" refers to the Head of all, which is searched out, as it is written:
> *“From afar the Lord appeared to me.”* (Jeremiah 31:2)

"From afar" refers to <term>Wisdom</term> <note>Chokhmah</note>, which is the head of the whole body, and the body spreads out through it until it reaches the foundation that assists the sides. All its supporters establish the pillars of the foundation, who are those who support the words <term>of the hidden ones</term> below. These are the supporters of the Torah from afar until the foundation of the body, and all assistance depends on it. Thus one is strengthened and merits the lights that nourish <term>the faithful treasures</term>.

**Rabbi Isaac** opened:
> *“And the Lord called to Moses, and spoke to him out of the tabernacle of the congregation, saying...”* (Leviticus 1:1)

In the word *Vayikra* ("And He called"), there is a small letter *Aleph*. Why? Because the letters of the word were standing before the Master in the Sanctuary, and then He invited him as one invites a guest. The letter *He* here is a small *He*, while elsewhere it is a large *He*. *“If any man of <margin>you</margin> bring an offering...”* This is for the strength of the *He*. Come and see: impurity comes from their side <term>from the service of the hidden</term>, but from the higher side, from the side of the King’s poverty <note>referring to the Shekhinah's lack when separated from the King</note>, there is much lacking. When the <term>Matronita</term> <note>The Queen/Shekhinah</note> comes below to the King, the upper <term>Matronita</term> acts and gives her goodness to strengthen her, so she may be found in a state of purity. Therefore, when this goodness enters the King, it only enters with the Matronita, returning power to her. The impurity of the offering is for the King, and therefore the offerings are like a gift. Afterward, "and the Lord spoke"—there is no lack in His goodness to the Matronita, and all His vessels were meant to appease the King. When merit comes, the King is appeased by this. Because of this, the offerings are for her, to remove the dwelling of the "other side" from her, to prepare the Sanctuary, and to enter always into the words of purity. For this, the higher arrangement was prepared, and he is called the <term>High Priest</term>, as it is written:
> *“You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.”* (Psalms 110:4)

And because of this, everything that is needed from the King’s house is nullified <note>meaning, provided without limit</note>, and there are no words to describe it, praising everything for those who enter the house of the Matronita, because for her...

<summary>This page explores the spiritual restoration of the leper through symbolic elements like cedar and hyssop, while also interpreting the "Small Aleph" in Leviticus as a sign of the Shekhinah's humble state and her relationship with the Divine King.</summary>
<keywords>Metzora, Shekhinah, Tree of Life, Wisdom, Small Aleph, Vayikra, Matronita, High Priest, Purity, Impurity</keywords>

--- Page 111 ---
<meta>This page continues the discourse on the purification of the leper (Metzora) and the laws of the bodily flux (Zav/Zavah), transitioning into a mystical interpretation of divine judgment and the "cup of consolation."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And now, the serpent <note>original: "chivyan" - referring to the forces of impurity or the primordial serpent</note> scratches because of the Temple, and as it is written: *And he shall take for him who is to be cleansed two birds...* <note>Leviticus 14:4</note>. **Rabbi Yehuda** opened and said: *Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord...* <note>Isaiah 38:2</note>. Hezekiah turned because he saw from the side of the crown of **Splendor** <note><term>Hod</term>: the eighth Sephirah or divine attribute, often associated with the legs and the endurance of prophecy</note> at first a form, but afterward it was angry and fallen. This is what is written: *He turned his face to the wall*, and it is not simply written "he turned his face." He turned his face to the wall and it [the vision] fell, and because of this he turned his face and smiled at their haste. And afterward, what is written of him? *And he spoke, his name was his lie, and in his wrath and in his dream.* And so the Holy One, blessed be He, bans the guilty in this manner in this world; He shines His face upon them like a master who shines at first, but afterward becomes angry and kills. And the Holy One, blessed be He, mixes for the guilty a living [cup] and sets it before them so they shall descend; and life is not changed for them from the assembly of the **World to Come** <note>The spiritual realm of reward after death or in the Messianic era</note>, for they have no portion in it and shall be destroyed from all. Those who come to be purified, they are assisted, and the Holy One, blessed be He, purifies them and brings them close to Him, and proclaims over them: *Peace, peace, to him that is far off, and to him that is near* <note>cf. Isaiah 57:19</note>.

**And if a woman** *has a discharge of her blood many days out of the time of her impurity...* <note>Leviticus 15:25</note>. **Rabbi Chiya** opened and said: *Behold, you are fair, my love; behold, you are fair; your eyes are as doves* <note>Song of Songs 1:15</note>. This verse is difficult; why must it say "Behold, you are fair" once, and then "Behold, you are fair" again? Rather, the Bride is beautiful until she says to the friends of the world—and that is the day on which she made a place to eat—and that is the day on which the Holy One, blessed be He, will take vengeance on the "serpents" <note>the oppressive nations</note> who distressed Israel. For on that day, there is praise before the Holy One, blessed be He, and she [the Assembly of Israel] claims from Him to perform judgment and to gaze upon them, and for the inheritance, He has authority over all: *And I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle* <note>Zechariah 14:2</note>. **Rabbi Isaac** said: There are two times for the Holy One, blessed be He; one when He rejoices with her, and one when she comes before Him, and in all of them the Holy One, blessed be He, wages wars in everything. And when that day comes to wage war, they rejoice and long for the other day; and He takes up armor upon armor and wages war against all the beloved and lowly "serpents." This is what is written: *For the day of the Lord of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and lofty, and upon every one that is lifted up; and he shall be brought low* <note>Isaiah 2:12</note>. **Rabbi Shimon** said: *And if a woman has a discharge of her blood...* This is what is written: *The war of the Lord draws near, blood from the sickness.* Sickness is certainly blood, as it is written: *If she has a discharge of her blood many days out of the time of her impurity.* This is what is written: *And the appointments of the Lord are upon the evil, and His merit is upon you.* For we have learned: When the Holy One, blessed be He, brings retribution to the world, the guilty hasten the retribution through their sins to come into the world. "Or if it flow beyond the time of her impurity," this is what is written: *And I will further [v'yasafti] chastise you* <note>Leviticus 26:18</note>. What is "And I will further chastise"? I will add judgment upon judgment and strengthen blood upon blood, more than what exists when the war of the Lord's blood approaches. It is written: *I will not again [lo osif] curse the ground any more for man's sake* <note>Genesis 8:21</note>. What is "I will not again"? Rather, I will not give any more "addition" to that war, except in a manner that the world can endure. And yet it is written *v'yasafti* [I will add/further]. Rather, it is written "to chastise" [yisra] and not "to overpower." This is what is written: *Or if it flow beyond her impurity, all the days of the flux of her uncleanness.* What is "all the days of the flux of her uncleanness"? Rather, the serpents scratch at their own bones through their sins, and afterward they scratch at others, for *you have defiled the sanctuary of the Lord*, and a spirit of impurity is awakened upon them. He who comes to be purified is certainly assisted. **Rabbi Hezekiah** said: I was sitting before Rabbi Eleazar one night; they rose at midnight to labor in the **Torah** <note>original: "Oraita"</note>. **Rabbi Eleazar** opened and said: *The cup of consolation was in goodness...* The cup of consolation was in goodness because at the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, smiles with Kindness [Chesed] in the world, when a man walks in the marketplaces and is seen before all—for all the merchants of goodness belong to the Holy One, blessed be He, in the world—and He performs goodness and kindness for him in the world. And because of this, a man should show himself openly in the marketplace and perform goodness, so that another goodness may be guarded for him. This is what is written: *The cup of consolation was in goodness.* The end of the verse says "and pushed." And "the cup of wrath" is not written as "pushed," nor is it written that "the cup of wrath" finally "bowed," but rather "the cup of wrath pushed"—for at the hour when anger hangs over the world, it is not for the pious man to show himself in the marketplace, and tomorrow...

It contrasts the "cup of consolation" given during times of divine favor with the "cup of wrath" during times of judgment.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic commentary on the spiritual roots of affliction and the mystical union between the Divine and the Community of Israel. It transitions from the laws of the "Metzora" (leper/afflicted one) to a profound discourse on the Song of Songs.</meta>

# Metzora
<note>The title refers to the Torah portion dealing with skin afflictions, interpreted here as spiritual imbalances.</note>

## Main Text (Zohar)

To approach and fly through the world, for when the spirit dwells in the world over all those who worship, and whoever encounters it and is weakened before it, he is judged with this judgment. And then it is written: *and he shall be attached* <note>original: "נספח" (nispach). Cf. Isaiah 14:1 or Leviticus 13:2. In this context, it refers to the scab or attachment of the affliction to the skin.</note>. All judgment emerges from a significant soul and does not dwell thus upon the world; therefore, healing is distant, and it shall be according to the hand of his sin, an observation for every side. And be aware that all these are corruptions of the spirit; let it not go outside and let it not be seen in the marketplace, so that it does not dwell upon you.

Come and see: because "God has made one opposite the other" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14; a core Kabbalistic principle that for every holy force, there is a corresponding "other side" or shadow.</note>. Just as when goodness dwells in the world, it dwells over everything, so too when judgment is corrupted in the world, it dwells over everything, and whoever encounters it is caught. Come and see: when the heart is corrupted in the world, many branches hang, emerging from that supernal sword. A head emerges, and whoever sees that sword—it is a supernal red Elohim <note>The name Elohim represents the attribute of Justice/Judgment</note>, blood on all sides. Then they decree laws, and many swords are awakened. (At that time, boundaries are cut and many laws are enacted below). All of them are *holders of the sword upon their thigh* <note>Song of Songs 3:8</note>, and it is written: *and his sword was drawn in his hand* <note>Joshua 5:13</note>. All of them are found ready to execute judgment, and whoever encounters them is seized. It is written here: *Behold now, your servant has found favor in your eyes, and you have magnified your mercy...* <note>Genesis 19:19</note>. This is because in every place where judgment dwells, all is corrupted, whether in the city or in the desert, and in the surroundings of the city.

Furthermore, he opened and said: *Set me as a seal upon your heart...* <note>Song of Songs 8:6</note>. "Set me as a seal"—the Community of Israel <note>The Shekhinah, the feminine aspect of the Divine</note> said this to the Holy One, Blessed be He: "Set me as a seal." What is this seal? It is the seal of the signet ring <term>Gushpanka: a Persian-derived term for a royal signet ring or official seal</term> of Truth. *As a seal upon your heart*—this is the seal of the **Tefillin** <note>Phylacteries</note> of the heart <note>The hand-tefillin, placed on the bicep opposite the heart</note> when it rests upon the heart. *As a seal upon your arm*—this is the "weak hand" <note>The left arm, where tefillin are bound</note> upon which that arm rests, providing strength and power. And when she says "Set me as a seal," what does she require? What is "as a seal"? Like those **Tefillin** of the head which bring goodness to the whole body, etc. This is the **Tefillin** of the arm upon the heart; through this, a man is found to be an image of the Supernal pattern.

*For love is as strong as death*—What is "as strong as death"? It means that no hardness is found in the world like the separation of the soul from the body; so too they desire never to be separated. And regarding this is the love of the Community of Israel for the Holy One, Blessed be He—that they shall never be separated. For this reason, the Prayer of the Hand <note>The hand-tefillin</note> is tied to the arm to fulfill that which is written: *His left hand is under my head...* <note>Song of Songs 2:6</note>. *Jealousy is as harsh as the Grave* <note>original: "Sheol"</note>—like all the levels of Gehenna <note>Purgatory/Hell</note>, the worship of the "Other Side" is not sustained. As it is written below, Gehenna is prepared when it is ready to judge. And they are not subdued as one, nor do they incline to be humbled by all. When "jealousy is as harsh as the Grave," it is because there is no jealousy except that which comes from love. From within love comes jealousy, and whoever is jealous for the one he loves, it is harder for him than that level of the Grave <note>Sheol</note>, which is the harshest of all levels of Gehenna. *Its flashes are flashes of fire, a flame of God* <note>Song of Songs 8:6</note>. And what is this "flame of God"? This is the fire that emerges from within the Shofar <note>The ram's horn, symbolizing the breath of life and divine emanation</note>, comprised of spirit and water. And from within that Shofar, everything is ignited because of the engraving of the world. In this manner, in jealousy for the Holy One, Blessed be He, and in the time that she is jealous for Him, woe to the one who encounters this, for he will be burned. It is further written: *For in the hand of the Lord there is a cup, and the wine is red; it is full of mixture...* <note>Psalms 75:9</note>. They will not be able to weep, etc. *Many waters*—this is the right arm, which must be tied to the prayer on the left arm to fulfill: *and his right hand embraces me.* "Many waters"—this is the Supernal River from which branches emerge to every side, and all of them flow and are drawn from it; all the sources of "many waters," the worship of the "voices of many waters" that emerge and are drawn from it. And all the rivers... Heaven forbid... since the love with which a man loves the Holy One, Blessed be He, he shall intend for Him.

That was removed from the world. And that spirit, a powerful wind, did not depart from blowing until the lower beings—the drops, the bones, and all of them—attained merit. ## Main Text (Zohar)

**"And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him"** <note>Genesis 32:2</note>
"And Jacob went on his way"—this means he was going toward his father. Come and see: all the time that Jacob was settled with Laban, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> did not join with him and was not found with him. And if you say, "But it is written: 'And the Lord said to Jacob, Return to the land of your fathers and to your birthplace, and I will be with you'?" Go and see: he desired to separate from Laban, and when he separated from him, the Divine Radiance and His Kingdom came toward him and surrounded him as is the way. Come and see: it is written "and they met him" <note>original: "vayifge'u vo"</note>; it should have said "they met before him." Rather, they came to be included within him and to surround him as is the way. What does "to be included within him" mean? Come and see: first, "the camp of God"—this is one. Afterward, "and he called the name of that place Mahanaim [Two Camps]"—this is two. One from the side of Judgment and one from the side of Mercy. And there were angels from this side and thirty from that side, and regarding this it is written "and they met him," and everything is precise. And Jacob said, "When I saw"—this refers to them being prepared for him. What is "mercy"? It is that which descends to them.

## Commentary (Tosefta)

**Addition**
<term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> and Rabbi Yose, his father-in-law, were walking on the road to Lod. Rabbi Yose said to Rabbi Eleazar: "Perhaps I have erred in my path; what is the meaning of 'And Jacob went on his way' etc.?" He said to him: "I did not know until they were walking and reached the cave of Lod." They heard a voice saying: "Two worlds are walking upon them; the first is the desire of the mind, and these were the holy hosts that passed before Jacob." Rabbi Eleazar went ahead and saw a branch in a shroud and said: "Blessed be the Lord of the world, such a teaching is better for us than anything else." They heard—though I do not know how to explain it for how long—the voice saying: "On the contrary, Isaac was doubled over his father, and the verse is precise." He said to him: "Father, I saw his weakness." And he replied that on the contrary, Isaac was the one who passed by Jacob when he was assisted by the King. He said to him: "My son, go and throw into the sea." Your grandmother... <unclear>textual corruption</unclear> ...and this did not happen in a vacuum; it happens to all the righteous at the hour when the righteous encounter the holy ones of His radiance and see the supreme holy merit. And come and see: Isaac stood at the end of his breath. But at the holy hour when the structure is on the Throne of Glory, which accompanies everything, it is uprooted upon the Kingdom, and the righteous are supported. Their thickness before them is as it is written: "And the Fear of Isaac was with me" <note>Genesis 31:42</note>. Thus far.

And at that hour, Isaac was established at the end.

<meta>This page marks the transition from the end of the Torah portion Metzora (The Leper) to the beginning of Acharei Mot (After the Death). It continues the Zoharic discourse on the spiritual origins of Esau and Jacob, moving into the mystical requirements for serving God with both fear and joy.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

They are destined to be like the darkness of night that goes out in a procession <note>original: "matroni," likely referring to a royal entourage or the feminine aspect of the Divine</note> in bright colors, in patterns and gardens. Thus Esau was made, and an old age that shall waste away from sorrow. Regarding this, we have learned that a person must focus their intention at that hour <note>referring to the time of marital union</note> on the will of their Master, so that holy children may emerge into the world. And if you say Isaac did not focus his intention—it is not so; rather, he focused in holiness, but his intention was directed toward the "end of that place" <note>a mystical reference to the lower spiritual realms or the "end" of the holy side</note>, and it was agreed upon when that first drop emerged in that very place. Therefore it is written, "he was entirely like a hairy mantle" <note>Genesis 25:25</note>. Come and see: David emerged in a state of "ruddy" beauty and appeared holy to his Master, and regarding this it is written:
> **And he was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a good appearance** (1 Samuel 16:12)
But Jacob, in his remembrance, leaves to Esau those drops <note>of the lower realm</note>, but his intention of will was for the higher portion of blessing and strength. They ascended in that place which is the "end of all," and because of this it is written:
> **Behold, I have made you small among the nations; you are greatly despised** (Obadiah 1:2) <note>referring to the eventual downfall of the spiritual root of Esau/Edom</note>.
Rabbi Judah used to teach this: Esau is called "First," as it is written:
> **And the first came out ruddy, all over like a hairy garment** (Genesis 25:25)
And the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "First," as it is written:
> **I am the first and I am the last** (Isaiah 44:6)
"And with the last, I am He." And the First <note>God</note> is destined to take vengeance upon the first <note>Esau/Edom</note> and to build the First <note>the Temple</note>, as it is written:
> **A throne of glory, exalted from the first** (Jeremiah 17:12)
And regarding the building of the future, it is written:
> **The first to Zion, behold, behold them; and I will give to Jerusalem a messenger of good news** (Isaiah 41:27)
Come and see: Jerusalem is destined to be a wall above and to approach even the Throne of Glory of the King. This is what is written:
> **At that time they shall call Jerusalem the Throne of the Lord** (Jeremiah 3:17)
Then it is written:
> **And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold** (Isaiah 30:26)
Then:
> **On that day the Lord shall be one and His name one** (Zechariah 14:9)
He alone shall reign, the Lord alone. <note>He shall reign in His oneness, the Lord alone</note>

---

->**Portion of Acharei Mot (After the Death)**<-

---

**And the Lord spoke** to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, etc. "And the Lord spoke to Moses"—
Rabbi Judah said: Since it is written "And the Lord spoke to Moses," why is there another time and another mention of "And the Lord said to Moses: Speak to your brother Aaron"? The first speaking should have been enough. However, thus we have learned: it is written, "And He called to Moses and the Lord spoke to him," and it is written, "And he went up to the Lord," etc. They have already established that the matter here refers to one level, and afterward another level. So too here: "And the Lord spoke to Moses" is one level, and afterward "And the Lord said to Moses: Speak to Aaron your brother" <note>regarding the entry</note> inside, within the Veil. And everything rises in one balance, and from one line it was done. "After the death of the two sons of Aaron"—
Rabbi Isaac opened:
> **Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice with trembling** (Psalms 2:11)
And it is written:
> **The Lord your God you shall fear, and Him you shall serve** (Deuteronomy 6:13)
Because of this, the verses stand together. Rather, thus it is taught: "Serve the Lord with fear"—for every service that a person performs, they must first learn to be mindful and to dread in fear of their Master. Because of the fear of their Master, it will be found that they perform the commandments <term>mitzvot: religious duties/commandments</term> of the Torah. And regarding this it is written:
> **The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord** (Psalms 111:10)
And therefore, anyone who does not find fear in the world has no reward at all for adding more in this world, except because he entered and consumed the words of the Torah and the commandments of the Torah. For afterward, a person will be found performing the commandments of the Torah with joy, as it is written:
> **Serve the Lord with gladness** (Psalms 100:2)
Rabbi Abba said: "Serve the Lord with fear" is a secret of the matter <note>a mystical mystery</note>.

<summary>This page concludes the discussion on the spiritual lineage of Esau and Jacob, contrasting their "firstness" with God's eternal "firstness," and begins the portion of Acharei Mot by exploring the mystical necessity of serving God through both fear and joy.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**After the Death**<-

This is what the Holy King <note>original: "Malka Kadisha"</note> performed below by the hand of the faithful one. Here, as we have established, it is written: *And you shall go down...* This refers to the descent of the letter *Yod* [י]. The Holy One, blessed be He—so did Rabbi Eleazar call Him—performed it by the hand of that pure one to perform the service of your Master. From another place, the meritorious ones [attain] a place, and because of the service, one who [serves] his Master is strengthened. He then said: "By the hand." The "hand" is the beginning of the lower realm [reaching] to the upper realm. Come and see: regarding the sons of Aaron, this we have established, and it has been said. Come and see what is written: *After the death...* and afterwards, *Speak to Aaron your brother* <note>Leviticus 16:2</note> **that he come not at all times into the holy place** etc., to atone for those who seek to be established.

For in every place where it mentions "the death of the two sons of Aaron," it is a hint to "After the death," as we have proven from here. Why does it say "the two sons of Aaron"? Is it not known that they were his sons? Rather, so we have learned: until this point they stood in their own authority and not in the authority of their father. And because of this, **when they drew near before the Lord and died**, for they pressed the hour <note>i.e., they acted prematurely or forced a spiritual event</note> alongside their father and without permission, because he was proven to be His servant. As it is written: **when they offered strange fire**, for it is taught in one place it is written "when they offered strange fire" and in another it is written "when they drew near before the Lord" etc., and so it is.

And because of this, it is written here "the sons of Aaron" and it is written "in their drawing near." We learned that Rabbi Hiyya said: One day he was traveling on the road to stand before Rabbi Shimon to learn from him the portion of Passover. I happened upon a certain mountain, and before it were gathered bushes like a single fence, and two men were there. While walking, he heard the voice of those men saying: <note>Psalms 48:2</note> **A song-psalm for the sons of Korah, Great is the Lord and highly praised** etc. And he saw this "song-psalm." Thus we learned: Rabbi Shimon wondered at this mountain which is a "double song," which is surrounded by the side of the chains <note>mystical levels or "links"</note>. And because it is surrounded by the side of the chains, two [aspects] are said regarding the songs: **A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day** and similarly **The Song of Songs which is Solomon's**. This is a song above all songs. "A song-psalm" is a song corresponding to the psalms of the sons of Korah regarding those who sit at the gate of Gehenna <note>Purgatory</note>. And they see them; they show that those who sit at the gates of Gehenna etc. This song is like the day of which it was spoken. I drew near to them and saw them, their faces deep as one. They said: [We are] hewers of stone, and two days a week we are separated from the day, in a valley like a hole, because people do not go up to us every single day. I saw that all were portions.

Furthermore, they opened and said: Whenever the righteous depart from the world, judgment departs from the world, and the death of the righteous brings atonement. And so it is in this generation. And because of this, we read the portion of the sons of Aaron on the Day of Atonement <note>Yom Kippur</note> to be an atonement for the sins of Israel. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Occupy yourselves with the death of these righteous ones, and it will be accounted to you as if you were offering sacrifices to atone for yourselves. For we have learned: all the time that Israel is in exile and cannot offer sacrifices, [the mention of] their death [atones]. And those two goats <note>of the Yom Kippur service</note> that they would offer, He gave them as a blessing for the two sons of Aaron, and they shall be atoned for. For thus we have changed [the status], as it is written: **And these are the names of the sons of Aaron the priests** etc. And it is written here... and we have known Eleazar and Ithamar. And it was awakened and said... what of Eleazar and Ithamar? The voice was... and as it is written. And there is none who teaches it otherwise... for all of them and we have known all of them... below like the eyes of both Eleazar and Ithamar. For all... they were corresponding to the Sanhedrin <note>The High Court of 71 elders</note> who were hidden before Moses. And because of this, their death atones for Israel. And regarding this it is written: <note>Leviticus 10:6</note> **And let your brethren, the whole house of Israel, bewail the burning**. And Rabbi Shimon saw... as if to say the voice of all the beauty and its glory from heaven... and thus two were not found like them in Israel. *And the Lord spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron...*

<meta>This page concludes a discourse on the merit of Jacob protecting his ancestors and descendants, specifically linking Jacob's righteousness to the rescue of Abraham from the furnace and the later salvation of Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. # After the Death

He continued, opened his discourse, and said: *"Therefore, thus says the Lord to the house of Jacob, who redeemed Abraham..."* <note>Isaiah 29:22</note>. This verse is difficult. It should have said, "Thus says the Lord who redeemed Abraham." Why does it say, "to the house of Jacob, who redeemed Abraham"? Rather, here the sages established and it was said: Jacob redeemed Abraham. For at that moment when Abraham was cast into the furnace <note>Referring to the Midrashic tradition of Nimrod casting Abraham into a furnace for his monotheism</note>, the Accusers said: "Is it for the sake of Ishmael who will come from him that he should be saved?" The Holy One, blessed be He, replied: "There is Isaac, who will stretch out his neck upon the altar." They said: "But there is Esau who will come from him!" He replied: "There is Jacob, who will be a perfect throne, and all his children will be perfect before Him." They said: "If so, it is by his merit [Jacob's] that Abraham is saved." This is what is written: *"...who redeemed Abraham; Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face now wax pale. For when he sees his children, the work of My hands, in the midst of him, they shall sanctify My name"* <note>Isaiah 29:22-23</note>. Who are these "children, the work of My hands"? These are Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, who gave their very bodies to the flaming furnace to sanctify the Name. "Jacob shall not now be ashamed"—why is Jacob mentioned here? It is written that Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah were called "the children of Judah" <note>See Daniel 1:6</note>; therefore, it should have said, "Judah shall not now be ashamed." Why Jacob? Rather, so it was taught: At that moment when they were taken out to be cast into the furnace, each one stood and spoke before all those nations, kings, and rulers. Hananiah said: *"The Lord is for me, I will not fear; what can man do to me? The Lord is for me among my helpers... It is better to take refuge in the Lord..."* <note>Psalms 118:6-8</note>. Mishael opened and said: *"And you, fear not, O My servant Jacob, says the Lord... for I am with you, says the Lord, to save you..."* <note>Jeremiah 30:10-11</note>. At that moment when they all heard the name of Jacob, they wondered and laughed in mockery. Azariah opened and said: *"Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One"* <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note>. This is what is meant by: *"One shall say, 'I am the Lord's'"*—this is Hananiah; *"...and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob"*—this is Mishael; *"...and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord, and surname himself by the name of Israel"*—this is Azariah <note>Isaiah 44:5</note>. At that moment, the Holy One, blessed be He, struck His heavenly host <term>Pamalya: the celestial retinue of angels</term> and said to them: "With what significance do you weigh the words these three have spoken? I shall answer them." They opened and said: *"That they may know that You alone, whose name is the Lord, are the Most High over all the earth"* <note>Psalms 83:19</note>. At that moment, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to the Archangel <note>Likely referring to Gabriel, the angel of fire</note>: "My throne! How significant are the words these righteous ones have spoken before You!" He replied to Him with that matter in which all their lives depend: *"Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face now wax pale."* Just as Jacob stood to save Abraham in the furnace, he stands now to save these. This is what is written: *"Thus says the Lord to the house of Jacob, who redeemed Abraham..."*—it is weighed with the praise of their whiteness <note>Meaning their faces did not turn pale with fear or shame</note>. We have learned: All those who were liable for this matter were burned in that fire, and the spark of the flame killed them. By what merit did these [three] deserve to be saved? Because they were praising before the Holy One, blessed be He, and sanctifying the Holy Name, and the Holy Name descended and rested upon them, and they were saved from that burning fire.

The two sons of Aaron approached this altar but were not saved; the Holy Name did not descend, and they were burned in the fire. Rabbi Isaac said: It is written, *"After the death..."* and it is written, *"...and they died."* Since it says *"After the death of the two sons of Aaron,"* do I not already know that they died? Rather, we have learned: There were two deaths. One was "before the Lord," and one was because they had no children; for anyone who does not merit children is considered dead. Therefore, it says both *"After the death"* and *"and they died."* Rabbi Abba said: What is the meaning of that which is written: *"And Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord, when they offered strange fire before the Lord, in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children; and Eleazar and Ithamar ministered..."* <note>Numbers 3:4</note>. What does one have to do with the other—that they had no children and that Eleazar and Ithamar ministered? Rather, the secret of the matter is this: they died because they had no children, and this was certainly so. But this is for the inhabitants of the world to learn, that they did not bring [souls into the world]. For these did not die except the death of their bodies, but the death of their souls did not occur... <note>The text cuts off as it begins to discuss Ithamar</note>

<summary>This page explains how Jacob's merit saved Abraham from Nimrod's furnace and later saved Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. It then begins an analysis of the death of Nadab and Abihu, suggesting their lack of children was a spiritual form of death.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Torah portion Acharei Mot. It transitions from the laws of the High Priest's service to the esoteric significance of the death of Aaron’s sons and the zealotry of Phineas.</meta>

## After the Death

->**After the Death**<-

"He took for himself one of the daughters of Putiel... and Phineas was born to him" <note>Exodus 6:25</note>. Through the merit of the Levites and their families, Phineas merited his learning, as it is written concerning the mercy and merit of the Levites. Because of this, the death of the righteous <note>is mentioned here</note>. And you might say they died—the priests did not die, Heaven forbid! <note>The Zohar often suggests the righteous "live on" in a higher spiritual state</note>. The measure of the text certainly implies mercy, and for this reason it is written: **Phineas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest** <note>Numbers 25:11</note>. Now, Phineas the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest was a priest in those days. Regarding Phineas, it is written "the priest" in every place, yet regarding Eleazar it is not always written so, except in places like "before Eleazar the priest" or "and Eleazar the priest said." On this matter: your bodies died, but your souls did not die; they exist in the spirit. They appear as a pair, like a "son of a day." And the letter *Yod* was added <note>original: יוד (Yod)</note> and placed between the letters of the name Phineas <note>original: פינחס (Pinchas)</note>, for this *Yod* includes two as one, and this is the secret of the "fullness" that was spoken of.

Rabbi Eleazar asked his father <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note>, of blessed memory: "Take these two, for they were two who rejoiced." They were not found as two, but as two halves of a body, for they had not married; therefore they were included as one, as it is written: "and Phineas was born to him," through the merit of mercy. And the *Yod* of Phineas was not given to him to diminish him, but rather like the point of a piercing <note>original: נקב"ה (female/piercing)</note>, meaning to straighten the crookedness below. For the opening of this holy covenant entered and was cast into another domain. Just as the first was crooked below, like a stranger, so the first was crooked as it is written in Ecclesiastes: **"That which is crooked cannot be made straight"** <note>Ecclesiastes 1:15</note>. But through the "stranger" it was rectified, as it is written, **"and the master of the house is great."** Just as there it is grace and mercy, so here one sees grace and mercy. Through a blow they were rectified here; even the first who were far were brought near. For it is written "in their drawing near," and here he brought the distant one near, and the King was happy to be near the distant one.

Immediately, **"And Phineas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, and rose up from among the congregation"** <note>Numbers 25:7</note>. Thus he rectified the crookedness of the first. Then the *Yod* was given in his name to join them as one, and he was made fit through the killing <note>of the sinners</note> to repair the crown they had damaged at first. As it is written: **"Behold, I give unto him my covenant of peace"** <note>Numbers 25:12</note>. "My covenant" was lacking that crown because of the "smallness" <note>a mystical state of diminished light</note> at first. But now that it is rectified, it is written: "Behold, I give unto him my covenant of peace"—literally "My Covenant" shall be with him in perfection. For this reason, the *Yod* was given on the side, and through this, they are sustained and consumed in it, to find that what was crooked at first is now rectified, and perfection has come with him. Rabbi Eleazar kissed his hands and said: "Blessed is the Merciful One that we have merited this power and it was not hidden from us."

Rabbi Yose said: At this time of Yom Kippur, this portion is established for the atonement of Israel in exile. For the order of this day turns away wrath. And because the death of the sons of Aaron atones for Israel, from where do we learn this? From the fact that any end <note>death</note> involving the suffering of the righteous brings atonement for sins. Anyone who grieves over the suffering of the righteous, their sins are removed from the world. For this reason, we read the portion **"After the death of the two sons of Aaron"** <note>Leviticus 16:1</note> so that the people shall hear and grieve over the loss of the righteous, and their sins will be atoned for. Anyone who grieves over the loss of the righteous or sheds tears for them, the Holy One, Blessed be He, proclaims concerning him: **"Your iniquity is taken away, and your sin purged"** <note>Isaiah 6:7</note>. Not only that, but his children will not die in his lifetime, and of him it is written: **"He shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days"** <note>Isaiah 53:10</note>.

**And the Lord said** unto Moses: "Speak unto Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, that he take up the censers out of the burning..." <note>Numbers 17:2</note>. Rabbi Shimon opened and said: **"All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea is not full"** <note>Ecclesiastes 1:7</note>. Rabbi Shimon said: Woe to the children of the world, for they have no eyes to see and no heart to observe. They do not know and do not pay attention to look upon the will of their Master—how they exist—and they do not awaken from their slumber until that day comes when darkness and gloom cover them, and the Master demands the account.

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic exposition of the Torah portion Acharei Mot. ## Main Text (Zohar)

->After the Death<-

The Master of the deposit <note>referring to God as the guardian of souls</note> exacts our debt from them. Through the mystery of those who are cursed, all their days a curse is upon them, and their souls do not support them each and every day. The return of truth is a possession for all who sell it, and regarding wisdom, it is written: "How long, you simple ones, will you love simplicity?" <note>Proverbs 9:4-5</note> **"Whosoever is simple, let him turn in here; as for him that void of understanding, she says to him: Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled."** But there is no one who inclines his ear, and no one whose heart is awakened. Come and see: in the later generations that shall come, those who occupy themselves with the Torah and its hidden secrets shall be gathered to their place (<margin>another version: to speak holy words</margin>), and there will be no one found to close or to open. Woe to that generation! And from all of them, "it shall be forgiven" <note>Numbers 15:26</note> cannot be applied to a generation such as this, until the generation when the King Messiah comes. Then knowledge shall be awakened in the world, as it is written <note>Jeremiah 31:33</note> **"For they shall all know Me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them."**

Come and see, it is written <note>Genesis 2:10</note> **"And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became four heads,"** and it is written <note>Jeremiah 17:8</note> **"And spreadeth out its roots by the river."** In the Book of Adam the First, it is taught that from the power of the "Life of the Heavens," life goes out to the world. These are called <term>the Life of the King</term> <note>original: Chayei Malka</note>, and they exist to establish that great and mighty Tree <note>the Sefirotic Tree of Life</note> which provides food for all. We call these "Living Waters," for in them the creatures find their sustenance and exist beautifully. That river which goes out from the deep depths is gathered, descending as if in a flow, and they are for relief and assistance, as it is written: "The pillars of his sword shall sink to establish that which was troubled." These are the walls and garments, and they are not gathered except when the crowns stand as supports. These two are called <term>Jachin and Boaz</term> <note>the two pillars of Solomon's Temple, representing the Sefirot Netzach and Hod</note> and Sapphire. From there, all those streams go out and are channeled as one level called <term>Tzaddik</term> <note>The Righteous One; the Sefirah of Yesod</note>, as it is written <note>Proverbs 10:25</note> **"But the righteous is an everlasting foundation."**

All of them go and are gathered into that place called "Sea," which is the Sea of Wisdom. <note>Ecclesiastes 1:7</note> **"All the rivers run into the sea..."** And if you should say that they reach a place where they cease and do not return, it is written afterward: **"Unto the place whither the rivers go, thither they go again."** Because that river never ceases forever. "They go again"—to what place do they return? To those two supports, [the pillars]. To go through that *Tzaddik* to find blessings and joy. This is the "Spirit" we learned of for sustenance, and the river to go forth, etc. And regarding this <note>Psalms 104:27</note> **"These all wait upon Thee, that Thou mayest give them their food in its season."** What is "its season" <note>Hebrew: *Ito*</note>? This is the "season" of the *Tzaddik*. This is the <term>Matronita</term> <note>The Matron; the Sefirah of Malchut/Shekhinah</note> who is called "Season" <note>Hebrew: *Et*</note>. It belongs to the *Tzaddik*, and therefore they all wait for this "Season." All those below wait for this. And this Spirit is the vitality from the power of the Eye; "all wait upon Thee," as we have established.

Come and see: when the "Season" stands established and is joined with Him, all the worlds are in joy, all the worlds are in blessing. Then the ladder is found with its upper and lower parts. But when the sinners of the world cause blessings not to be found there, it is as if the Female—Heaven forbid—is on the "Other Side" <note>the realm of evil/impurity</note>. Then judgments are awakened in the world and the ladder is not found. When the people of the world want to be blessed, they cannot, except through what is written, so that the "Later One" may be awakened and the *Matronita* be blessed, and blessings be found in all worlds. At that hour, Moses asked before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: Kadosh Baruch Hu</note>, but He did not say a word to him. He wept for the world: "By whose hand shall they be blessed?" The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "Is it to Me you speak? Speak to your brother [Aaron] who holds the keys to the blessings above and below." **"And the Lord said unto Moses: Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place..."** <note>Leviticus 16:2</note> For there are times before the Holy One, Blessed be He, when Favor is found and blessings are found and prayer is not withheld. And there are times when Favor is not found, and blessings are not ready, and harsh judgments are awakened in the world, and times when judgment is suspended. Come and see: there are times when the hour of Favor is found, and times when the hour of Judgment is found, and times when the hour of Rebuke is found and they are suspended. There are times when a greater Favor is found...

It emphasizes that the High Priest Aaron's service is essential to timing these spiritual connections to ensure blessings rather than judgment reach the world.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Aharei Mot (Leviticus 16). ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**After the Death**<-

To open [the gates] for them, and they gaze upon Him, for judgments are found and hang over everything. Happy are those in this world who are found worthy, for there is nothing like the judgments found in the world. And happy are they when days of favor <note>Hebrew: *Ratzon*</note> are found in the world and the worlds are sweetened. And happy are they when days of judgment are hanging and present, even in the "Time" <note>Hebrew: *Et* (עת). In Kabbalah, "Time" often refers to a specific spiritual level or manifestation of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) that can manifest as either judgment or mercy.</note>. It is written:
> To everything there is a season <term>Et</term>, and a time for every purpose... <note>Ecclesiastes 3:1</note>
And it is written:
> But as for me, let my prayer be unto You, O Lord, in a time <term>Et</term> of favor... <note>Psalms 69:14</note>
And it is written:
> Seek the Lord while He may be found... <note>Isaiah 55:6</note>
And it is written:
> Why, O Lord, do You stand afar off? Why do You hide Yourself in times <term>Etot</term> of trouble? <note>Psalms 10:1</note>
And it is written:
> From afar the Lord appeared to me... <note>Jeremiah 31:2</note>
And there are times when He is near, as it is written:
> The Lord is near to all who call upon Him... <note>Psalms 145:18</note>
Because of this: **"That he come not at all times <term>Et</term> into the holy place..."** <note>Leviticus 16:2</note>. The Rabbi said: We have already established this matter in its time, and so it is seen. The Holy One, blessed be He, warned the lower ones to be careful so they would not err in that sin in which the sons of Aaron erred, for that "Time" is well-known; therefore, one must not err by forcing another "Time" before the King. And this "that he come not at all times into the holy place"—meaning, even though he sees a time that is given into his hand to sweeten the world, he should not turn to it to bring it near to the Sanctuary, for that sin and the intoxicating wine are one and the same. <margin>Another version: to bring it near to the Holy One, blessed be He, for that "Time" is known, therefore...</margin> **"That he come not at all times into the holy place."** And if he desires to know how he shall enter, the verse concludes: **"With this <term>Zot</term> shall Aaron come into the holy place."** For this is the "Time" that is grasped in the bond of love that burns, and he shall enter the Sanctuary, but "not at all times." Come and see, Rabbi Yosei said, it is written:
> He has made everything beautiful in its time <term>Et</term>... <note>Ecclesiastes 3:11</note>
We have established this matter regarding the time <margin>of the Heavens</margin> which is holy. And so we have learned: "He has made everything beautiful in its time"—this is the secret of the Creation, that the companions should not be mixed among them, specifically "in its time" and not in another. Because of this, the warning to Aaron: "That he come not at all times into the holy place," but rather how? He shall enter "With This" <term>Zot</term>, as we have established, for it is written:
> With this <term>Zot</term> shall Aaron come into the holy place. <note>Leviticus 16:3</note>
Rabbi Eleazar was sitting before his father. He said to him: It is written regarding the assembly of Korah, "Separate yourselves from among this congregation." What is "Separate yourselves"? It is like what is written, "And I will cut off <note>original: *ve-hikharti*</note> that soul from among its people." Heaven forbid that this was the case with the sons of Aaron, for it is not written of them that they were "cut off" as it was with the assembly of Korah, of whom it is written, "Separate yourselves from among the congregation." And it is written, "Behold, we perish, we are undone, we are all undone," for all of them were those who offered the incense <term>Ketoret</term>, and their matters were hidden and they died, for they were certainly consumed. But these [sons of Aaron] were not consumed, Heaven forbid. It is written, "That he come not at all times into the holy place," and it is written, "With this shall Aaron come into the holy place," because at the gate of "not at all times," it shows him how many times he may enter. Rabbi Eleazar said to him: This has been said, and it is one matter, and we knew of these. But regarding what the sons [of Aaron] sinned with "Time," to warn here, what is the seal? Heaven forbid, "that he come not"—so it is understood and the matter is settled in his eyes. Come and see: all the sacrifices and all the burnt offerings of this day are for the Holy One, blessed be He. But this was pleasing, like this incense. For the incense is the most excellent of all, and because of this, they would bring it into the innermost chamber with a burning flame. And what is the seal? Because of this, people are not made like other sacrifices and burnt offerings as they are with the incense, for all the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, here is to be bound <term>itkatar</term> and to be tied more than anything else. And for this reason, it is called *Ketoret* <note>The word *Ketoret* (incense) is linked to the Aramaic root *KTR*, meaning to bind or knot.</note>, and this is the time, and he bound it. He opened and expounded:
> Because of the savor of your good ointments... <note>Song of Songs 1:3</note>
Look at this verse, for so it is. "Because of the savor"—from the inheritance. The savor of the incense, which is subtle, excellent, and the most internal of all. And when that savor rises to be bound in that highest brain, everything is awakened, one with the other, and they are bound as one. And then the lamps are lit and return to the nostrils through the "savor of your good ointments." And then the oil is poured from level to level, those levels of the holy name. "Your name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the maidens <term>alamot</term> love you." What are "maidens"? As we have established, they are literally "worlds" <term>olamot</term>, from this world to the world to love You, all of them over the worlds, and all is one. And in the book of Rav Hamnuna the Elder it is written: What are the "maidens"? All of them:
> She gives food to her household, and a portion to her maidens. <note>Proverbs 31:15</note>

It distinguishes the death of Nadab and Abihu from the rebellion of Korah and emphasizes the incense (Ketoret) as the ultimate tool for binding the divine realms together.</summary>

## After the Death

->**After the Death**<-

...for its actions and its nakedness <note>referring to forbidden unions or spiritual flaws</note> were in the world of darkness. It was created as a support and for the constellation before it, and from there all the lower blessings are found, and the upper and lower beings are blessed through it forever. "To the world of darkness" is a good word for the lower world, for through this word, the hearts of the images are found. And because this incense <term>Ketoret: literally "binding" or "knotting"</term> is bound in the secret of the Supernal, it is used before the Holy One, Blessed be He, more than all other sacrifices and burnt offerings. Regarding this, it says: *Because of the fragrance of your goodly oils... draw me, we will run after you* <note>Song of Songs 1:3-4</note>. A herald calls out: *Therefore the maidens love you.* Wisdom and all the hosts <term>Ochlosin: celestial legions or multitudes</term> are all held within it, and until this is found, they are all hanging within it. Thus, *The King has brought me into his chambers*—this is the secret of the King entering his chambers with joy and gladness; so too the Bride and all the hosts. A rebuke to all the hosts: at the time when the Assembly of Israel <note>the Shekhinah</note> is forgiven and blessed, they all rejoice, and judgment does not rest then upon the world. And about this it is written: *Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad* <note>Psalms 96:11</note>.

*For I will appear in the cloud upon the Ark cover* <note>Leviticus 16:2</note>. The Rabbis taught the secret: Happy are the righteous in whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires their honor. A rebuke: A king of flesh and blood, a living man, rides upon his horse; so too the Holy One, Blessed be He, causes them to ride upon His, as it is written: *And Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven* <note>2 Kings 2:11</note>. Here, see what is written: *That he die not, for I will appear in the cloud upon the Ark cover.* This is difficult; they brought it down into a pocket <note>an idiomatic expression for a hidden or difficult concept</note>. For it says: *And Moses entered into the midst of the cloud*—into the actual midst of the cloud. *For I will appear in the cloud upon the Ark cover.* Furthermore: *And the Lord will create over every dwelling place of Mount Zion... a cloud and smoke by day* <note>Isaiah 4:5</note>. And it is written: *For the cloud of the Lord was upon the Tabernacle by day* <note>Exodus 40:38</note>. And we find it written: *And the Lord came down in a cloud* <note>Numbers 11:25</note>.

*I will appear in the cloud upon the Ark cover*: This is found in the place that is their root, which are the actual Cherubim <term>Keruvim: the winged figures atop the Ark</term>. We have established that the Cherubim sit below, and it is found that twice a day they say a throne-song with their wings. At the time when those below take upon themselves the holiness of the King, they spontaneously lift their wings and spread them, covering the Ark cover <term>Kaporet: the gold lid of the Ark of the Covenant</term>. Afterward, they fold their wings and hold them <margin>Version: and they hold their wings</margin> as it is said: *And the Cherubim shall spread out their wings on high, screening [sochechim]* <note>Exodus 25:20</note>. It says *sochechim* <note>active screening</note> and not *sechuchim* <note>passive state of being screened</note>, for they stood in "This" <margin>Another version: in This</margin> and were moved like the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term>.

The Rabbis taught: What is sought here by the phrase *For I will appear in the cloud upon the Ark cover*? And it is written: *With this [Be-Zot] shall Aaron come into the holy place* <note>Leviticus 16:3</note>. At that moment, he did not see the Shekhinah when he entered. Rather, the cloud would descend, and when it descended, it reached the lines of the Ark cover, and the wings of the Cherubim were stirred, and they covered them and sang a song. And what song did they sing? *For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised; He is to be feared above all gods* <note>Psalms 96:4</note>. This they sang when they lifted their wings. At the time they spread them, they said: *For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but the Lord made the heavens* <note>Psalms 96:5</note>. When they covered the Ark cover, they said: *Before the Lord, for He comes to judge the earth* <note>Psalms 96:13</note>. The world shook like a lightning bolt; *He will judge the peoples with uprightness.* And their voice was heard in the Holy Place, in the Sanctuary. Then the incense was in its joy, and they were prepared as they were prepared so that everything would be blessed. And the sound of the wings of the Cherubim rose and fell, and they sang the song and covered the Ark cover, and they lifted them—this is the meaning of *screening*. Specifically *screening*, because their voice was heard from within it. As it is said: *And he heard the voice...* <note>Numbers 7:89</note>.

Rabbi Yose said: *He will judge the peoples with uprightness*—established in "uprightness" <term>Mesharim</term> as it is said: *The upright love you* <note>Song of Songs 1:4</note>. This is to include the two Cherubim, male and female <term>Dechar ve-Nukba</term>, who are certainly "uprightness." And because of this, *He will judge the peoples with uprightness.* And it is written: *And he heard the voice speaking to him from between the two Cherubim... and He spoke to him.* Rabbi Yitzchak said: From here we learn that in any place where male and female are not found together, it is not fitting to see the face of the Shekhinah. Thus: *And He shall grant you peace [Shalom]* <note>The word Shalom implies wholeness/completion</note>. And we have learned it is written: *He is righteous and upright* <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>—male and female. So too here, the Cherubim are male and female, and regarding this it is written: *You have established uprightness* <note>Psalms 99:4</note>; *He shall judge the peoples with uprightness.* And because of this, *their faces shall look one to another*, as we have already established.

# After the Death (Acharei Mot)

**It was taught:** Rabbi Jose said, one time I was traveling on the road to reach a place to see—another explanation <note>original: "Davar Acher"</note>—Rabbi Yaisa and Rabbi Hezekiah and their companions. It happened that they were going to see Rabbi Phineas ben Jair. When they reached him, he opened [his discourse] and said:
> "A Song of Ascents: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity." <note>Psalm 133:1</note>

What is the meaning of "brothers to dwell together in unity"? It refers to the Bride <note>The Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> and Phineas, brothers—see the light <note>original: "Ayin Or"</note>—and they saw at that moment that they were as one, like swallows <note>or perhaps "eagles"</note> face to face. It is written, "how good and how pleasant." But when the Male <note>The Holy One, Blessed be He</note> turns his face away from the Female <note>The Shekhinah</note>, woe to the world! In such a state it is written, "And on the day of her longing, judgment is finished." "Judgment is finished" is certainly written. And it is written, "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne" <note>Psalm 89:15</note>, for one does not go without the other. And when Justice <note>Mishpat</note> distances itself from Righteousness <note>Tzedek</note>, woe to the world! Then it is written, "And on the day of her longing, judgment is finished." And now, beloved ones, you have come while the Male is not occupied with harshness. He said, "You have come to my portion; sit, for the day is becoming balanced so that the Bride may be crowned to be face to face. You have come for freedom; stay with me." They said to him, "We have come to the Bride, to the Master." One of them slipped behind to return to his companions, and thus it is written before the Master. While they were walking, he opened and said:
> "I am black but comely, O daughters of Jerusalem..." <note>Song of Songs 1:5</note>

The Assembly of Israel <note>Knesset Israel/Shekhinah</note> said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: "I am black" in exile, "but comely" through the commandments of the Torah. Even though Israel is in exile, they do not abandon them. "Like the tents of Kedar"—these are the sons of Keturah (another version <note>original: "Sifra Achra"</note> reads: "Kuria") whose faces are always darkened—and yet, "like the curtains of Solomon," like that pillar that supports the dwelling, as it is written, "Who stretches out the heavens like a curtain" <note>Psalm 104:2</note>. "Do not gaze upon me because I am swarthy"—he explains <note>original: "Mefaresh"</note> that "I am swarthy" because the sun has tanned me, for I did not look closely enough to be illuminated as is fitting. And what do Israel say? "My mother's sons were incensed against me." These are the meritorious "mother's sons," those great ministers appointed over the other nations. This is literally "my mother's sons," for "He cast down from heaven to earth..." <note>Lamentations 2:1</note>. And when "He cast down from heaven to earth," then "they made me keeper of the vineyards." Why? <note>original: "Mai Ta'ama"</note> Because "my own vineyard I have not kept." And we learned: "my mother's sons" certainly agreed against me; that is to say, when the Earth <note>Shekhinah</note> was removed from Heaven <note>The Holy One</note>, as we have established, for it is written:
> "And his sister stood from afar." <note>Exodus 2:4</note>

And here it is certainly removed. "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity." And we even established "together" <note>Hebrew: Yachad</note> as the Bride, and even "also together" <note>Hebrew: Gam Yachad</note>. "Brothers to dwell" in general. Since it is written "also" <note>Gam</note>, it includes all those above, for all dominion longs for the place where it is found. To Him, "Behold how good and how pleasant," etc. These are the companions who sit as one and are not separated from one another. At first, they appear as strangers to one another, in a war where they seek to kill each other [intellectually], but afterwards they are in brotherly love. What does the Holy One, Blessed be He, say? "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity." "Also" <note>Gam</note> comes to include the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> with them. Not only that, but the Holy One, Blessed be He, comes to listen, and it is pleasing to Him and He rejoices in them. This is what is written:
> "Then those who feared the Lord spoke to one another, and the Lord hearkened and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before Him..." <note>Malachi 3:16</note>

And we learned from the companions here: just as you were at first, from this time forward, do not separate from one another until the Holy One, Blessed be He, rejoices with you and calls "Peace" upon you, and your building is found to be peace in the world. This is what is written:
> "For the sake of my brothers and friends, I will now say: Peace be within you." <note>Psalm 122:8</note>

See! While they were walking, they reached the house of Rabbi Phineas ben Jair. Rabbi Phineas came out and kissed him <note>or "met him"</note>. He said, "I have merited to receive the Divine Presence! Blessed is my lot." He prepared for them couches with mattresses and fine coverings. He said to him, "Simeon, the Torah does not require this." He removed them and they sat. Rabbi Phineas said, "Before we eat, let us hear some words of Torah." For the Holy One, Blessed be He, has suspended all His matters upon them. They spared the man who does not fear the yoke and the stumbling block, let him speak to them. He does not fear the yoke, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, has agreed...

It emphasizes that when scholars study in harmony, the Divine Presence dwells among them, bringing peace to the world.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

In Him. He did not fear from below, just as one who does not fear the humble poor. Rabbi Eleazar’s son said to him: "Rabbi Eleazar, stand in your place and speak a new word before Rabbi Phinehas and the rest of the companions." Rabbi Eleazar stood, opened his discourse, and said:
> **"And the Lord spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron..."** <note>Leviticus 16:1</note>

This verse must be looked into, for its arrangement is established by this: for it is written in the [following] verse, **"And the Lord said to Moses: Speak to Aaron your brother"** <note>Leviticus 16:2</note>. What is the difference regarding the section of this verse above? Why is it written, **"And the Lord spoke to Moses after the death,"** which is what He said to him, and afterward, **"And the Lord said to Moses"**? Rather, the reason for the verse is that He gave the incense of spices to be offered at a time when death would not be removed by it, except by <term>another power</term> <note>original: "כט אחרא" - likely referring to the "Other Side" or a specific restrictive force</note>. Why? Because Aaron is the joy of the world in the world. But the Holy One, blessed be He, desires to look upon the world through you and the children of the world above; behold, the incense of spices is handed over to you from all others and beyond. And then death will not be removed by it except by <term>another power</term>. When [Nadab] and Abihu preceded [their time] during the life of their father to offer what they were not guarded for, this matter caused them to err in it. And three [times] the staff was raised—who caused them this error? He did it. What is written? **"And the Lord spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron,"** and what did He say to him? **"In their drawing near before the Lord, and they died."** It is not written "by their drawing near," but "in their drawing near." Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, did not cause it from below; they forced the hour during the life of their father and erred in that which is written:
> **"Which He had not commanded them"** <note>Leviticus 10:1</note>

"Them" He did not command, but Aaron He did command. And if the two sons of Aaron, because they forced the hour during the life of their father, caused themselves so much [harm], how much more so for me in the presence of my father and Rabbi Phinehas and the rest of the companions! His brother Rabbi Phinehas kissed him and blessed him. Rabbi Shimon opened and said:
> **"Taste and see that the Lord is good; happy is the man who takes refuge in Him."** <note>Psalms 34:9</note>

"Sixty warriors are around it..." <note>Song of Songs 3:7</note> These are the "Bed of Solomon." What is this "Bed"? This is the Throne of Glory of the King, of which it is written at that time that she has her husband. "Solomon" [Shlomo] is the King to whom peace [Shalom] belongs entirely. "Sixty warriors are around it" who take hold of the side of harsh Judgment—sixty lashes of fire <margin>Variant reading: sixty armed ones and types of knots</margin> for the Voice of the Master to be enwrapped in the sign of the appointed one, the support of the mighty Chariot. From it are cast sparks of mighty fire that are joined in the exits <margin>Variant reading: as the exits</margin> like seventy branches and strikes of the Throne that consumes. And these sixty armed ones and small weapons are from those mighty warriors of that Supernal Might [Gevurah] of the Holy One, blessed be He, appointed from the warriors of Israel. And three [times] regarding this bed, what is written of it?
> **"She rises while it is still night"** <note>Proverbs 31:15</note>

When she is nourished from the right side <margin>Variant reading: from the side of Judgment</margin> **"and gives prey to her household."** What is "prey"? Everything is prey and sustenance from it. With the Bride comes a sword to cut from below and provide sustenance in every place to perform Judgment, and they are called the "Masters of Wailing and Lamentation."
> **"Every man with his sword upon his thigh"** <note>Song of Songs 3:8</note>

Then the fire of fear is on the thigh of the warrior "because of fear in the nights." They have established this as the fear of Gehenna, etc. But "because of fear in the nights" means: from what place do they take fear? From that place called <term>Fear</term> <note>The Sefirah of Gevurah, associated with Isaac</note>. Thus:
> **"And the Fear of Isaac was with me"** <note>Genesis 31:42</note>
> **"And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac"** <note>Genesis 31:53</note>

"In the nights"—at times when they are appointed to perform Judgment... [The text continues with mystical associations of the Leviathan and the "Youth" (Metatron) who holds the keys to blessings].

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **After the Death** <-

And the spirit rests on four sides; this is a force for this side and that is a force for that side. And so all four colors <note>referring to the four Archangels or the four faces of the Chariot</note> subdue the boundaries in this manner. And when they are included as one, it is written: *(As for the likeness of their faces, they each had the face of a man)* <note>Ezekiel 1:10</note>. For all of them are thus illuminated, and their "nostrils" are included as one above; two rise and descend, and two drip with their purity. They pass through rising and entering mountains <insert>other versions: they are superior and rising</insert>. All of them are brains from the surrounding sides, and the brain for the Crown <term>Keter: the highest Sephirah</term> is uprooted from there and they rise to another day. There is no number to the living creatures <term>Hayyot: holy angels</term> that are hidden on this side.

Two, for example, suckle every day to investigate the hollows and the pastures, and this is the "spirit of the book" of concealment, as it is written: *And Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim two men to spy secretly, saying...* <note>Joshua 2:1</note>. And these suckle from beneath the surrounding side, two daughters like copper that barks <insert>other versions: and these suckle from the side that does not move its voice, two copper bells</insert>. And regarding this it is written: *And Jericho was shut up*—these are the "daughters of man" <note>referring to the walls or inhabitants</note>. And these are divided like the leaves <insert>other versions: drops</insert> of that bed. And this is what we learned as it is written: *Behold, wisdom is as sweet as water, harlots to the king.* And this is the "End" <term>the Shekhinah in her aspect of Judgment</term> and not from the beginning of time. And like the brain of the "Evil Inclination" below, and Aaron received from behind the Holy One, Blessed be He. What is written? *As for My people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them* <note>Isaiah 3:12</note>. And he pushes into it the *Chashmal* <note>a celestial glow or angelic rank</note>, seventy branches that hang here and there. And how they are all red like a rose! And from here a child, one branch that is more red, which rises and descends. And all are covered on this side. It is a sickness to eat with intent, like a living creature that is made to leap upon the mountains and skip over the fences until it flies like the leaf of a donkey <note>possibly a metaphor for a lowly or stubborn force</note> with its claws and can [eat].

Then he commands and returns to his time of goodness. Fortunate are Israel who prepare his "prey" <note>the sacrifices</note> to return him to his place <insert>other versions: to his river</insert>. He enters like the female of the Great Abyss when the masters of spears and swords rise, who are without number. Their price is the hidden upper ones of the supports of this bed. Thousands of thousands and tens of thousands stand on all sides of this bed, above it and below it. All are before him <insert>other versions: and from it downwards all worlds are before him</insert>. And they stand from beneath; all of them go out with much anger and chariots that are without number, and they come and rule in the world until the Shofar is blown and they are gathered. And so it is like the roar of claws that seize; this bed includes them. This bed, its feet seize the four sides of the world. All are supreme, like the Bride who is found above and found below, like the "waters from above" and "upon the earth beneath," and regarding this it is written: *The All.* What was it? Like a cloud that is ready for all above and below. And the foundations of this bed are a dwelling... she shall be called the Greatness of All, hinted at in this strength. Because of this, a person needs to direct his mind above to unify the Holy Name, the matter he seeks to unify.

And regarding this we learned it is written: *With **this** (Zot) shall Aaron come into the holy place* <note>Leviticus 16:3</note>. With "this" <term>Zot: a name for the Shekhinah</term> he seeks to bring holiness to its place. From "this" place he must call before the Holy One, Blessed be He. And regarding this it is written: *If they were wise, they would understand **this**, they would consider their latter end* <note>Deuteronomy 32:29</note>. That is to say: Behold, they should look at the throne, how to seize **This** (Zot) according to her strength, and how all those hosts stand before her and are seized in service to take vengeance from the guilty. *Immediately they would understand their latter end* and they would guard their deeds and not sin before the Holy King.

Furthermore, Rabbi Phineas said: Every man who is worthy of the Torah and guards it, this **This** (Zot) guards that man and decrees upon him a permanent existence, that [the Torah] shall not depart from him, from his children, or from his children's children forever. And so: *This is My covenant with them, etc.* <note>Isaiah 59:21</note>. They sat to learn until Rabbi Phineas said to the companions: "Let each and every one say a new word of Torah at the table before Rabbi Phineas."
