# After the Death (Acharei Mot)

Because they merited her, of whom it is said: *Wisdom is better than weapons of war* <note>Ecclesiastes 9:18</note>. For behold, at the end of the world, permission is not given to know all those righteous of truth—those who labor in the Torah day and night and crown themselves with the commandments of the Torah in this world to enter with them into the World to Come. *But the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard* <note>Ecclesiastes 9:16</note>. For people do not look at him, nor do they wish to join him or lend an ear to his words. We have learned: whoever goes to lend an ear to the words of Torah is blessed in this world. But for those who turn their backs on it—even if one calls to the Holy King and gives honor to the Torah, of him it is written: *This day you have become a people to the Lord your God* <note>Deuteronomy 27:9</note>.

Come and see: One day the companions were walking with Rabbi Shimon. Rabbi Shimon said: I see that all the nations go on, while Israel is lower than them all. What is the reason? Because the King has removed the <term>Matronit</term> <note>The Matronit is the Shekhinah, the feminine aspect of God, often depicted as a Queen or Mother in exile.</note> from His house and she goes outside without a gate. This is the meaning of: *For a slave-girl when she displaces her mistress, the earth trembles... for a servant when he reigns... and a churl when he is filled with food... and a handmaid when she inherits from her mistress* <note>Proverbs 30:21-23</note>. Who is the "slave-girl"? She is the "alien crown" <note>The Sitra Achra or "Other Side," the forces of impurity.</note> that took up zeal during the time Israel is in exile. As it is written: *Even to the firstborn of the slave-girl who is behind the millstones* <note>Exodus 11:5</note>. "Behind the millstones" used to be her place, but now the slave-girl inherits from the mistress.

Rabbi Shimon wept and said: A King without a Matronit is not called a King. A King who clings to a slave-girl—her heat is the Matronit's shame; it is his [the King's] honor that is diminished. The spirit of the word is destined to call out for the Matronit's atonement, and the spirit shall greatly redeem the Daughter of Zion and the shepherds of the Daughter of Jerusalem. Here the King will direct Himself to you, for He is "Righteous" and He plants. That is to say, the <term>Tzadik</term> <note>The Righteous One, referring to the Sefirah of Yesod, the foundation and procreative force of the divine realm.</note> is the planter. Because He rides upon the side behind Him—the alien crown—and nourishes it, about this it is written: *Humble and riding on a donkey* <note>Zechariah 9:9</note>. "Humble"—not as before. "Riding on a donkey"—as we have established. [The divine flow] is caught in the two lower nations because they received their alien zeal... and we have already established these words. As it were, *He is righteous and saved* <note>Zechariah 9:9</note>—certainly more than all of them. Because until now the Righteous One [Yesod] circulated without Justice [the Shekhinah], but now they shall be coupled as one; "He is righteous and saved" for He no longer dwells with the "other crown."

The dependence of the Righteous One is on Kindness and Grace... *The Lord is good to all* <note>Psalms 145:9</note>. This verse is difficult; it should say "The Righteous is good to all." What is this "Kindness" and "Grace"? It is actual Kindness. And what is this Kindness? Kindness for the Matronit, so she does not have to cling to the other crown called the "slave-girl."

Rabbi Yitzhak said to Rabbi Shimon: By the life of the power before my Master! We have learned that it is written: *And the Righteous is the foundation of the world* <note>Proverbs 10:25</note>. One says the world stands on seven [pillars], and another says the world stands on this one [the Tzadik]—how are these words reconciled? He said to him: They are all one matter. For there are seven [Sefirot], and among them is one pillar called "Righteous" (Tzadik), and they stand upon it, and the world is sustained by it. When the world is sustained by it, it is sustained by all seven. Therefore it is written, *The Righteous is the foundation of the world*, and we have established this in many places.

Come and see: This slave-girl is destined to rule over the holy vision below, just as the Matronit was above in the beginning, as it is written: *Righteousness lodged in her* <note>Isaiah 1:21</note>. But now, *a slave-girl when she inherits from her mistress*—all of them. And the Holy One, Blessed Be He, is destined to return the Matronit to her place as before. And then the joy will be seen. Shall I say the joy of the King or the joy of the Matronit? The joy of the King, because He returns to her and separates from the side of the serpent's blemish. And the joy of the Matronit, because she returns to be coupled with the King. This is what is written: *Rejoice greatly, O Daughter of Zion...* <note>Zechariah 9:9</note>.

Come and see, it is written: *And it shall be a statute forever unto you* <note>Leviticus 16:29</note>. It should have said "And it shall be for you." What is "a statute forever" (*Chukat Olam*)? In every place, "Statute of the World" refers to the decree of the King who enters all appointments after this and seals them, like one who seals with a holy engraving. "Statute of the World" in this...

# After the Death (Acharei Mot)

## Main Text (Zohar)

He marked and engraved all His hidden treasures and all His concealed things. At once, it speaks of **on the tenth of the month**. "On the tenth" specifically, as we have established regarding the verse: *you shall afflict your souls* <note>Leviticus 16:29</note>. Certainly, this is so, and it has been stated. When [the lights] are gathered, the matter certainly depends upon the Assembly of Israel <note>The *Knesset Yisrael*, a mystical personification of the community of Israel and the Divine Presence/Shekhinah</note>. Because of this, they all descend and return, trembling more than on any other day. Even though this matter there is because of the "wine" <note>A reference to the "wine of Torah" or the intoxicating nature of divine judgment/rigor</note>, all the commandments are the commandments of the Holy King, each one in its proper place, and so it is. Furthermore, see that on this day, all joy, all light, and all the generosity of all the worlds depend on that Supernal Day <note>The realm of Binah/Understanding, the source of the "Tenth Day"</note>, for all merits are stored and emerge from it. Then, all those stars and constellations shine with light and joy until they are all appeased. At that time, all those judgments are calmed by the light, and judgment is not executed; therefore, *you shall afflict your souls*. Rabbi Isaac said: The Master has established this from the body of the Mishnah. It was hidden in the storehouse until they denied the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: *Kadosh Barukh Hu*</note>, as it is written:
> What portion have we in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. <note>1 Kings 12:16</note>

And this has been stated. We find another verse where it is written: *far from the death of your house, David.* Heaven forbid it should be so! Rather, this "House of David" is called out as it is written:
> House of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the Lord. <note>Isaiah 2:5</note>

"House of Jacob" is like another interpretation: *the house of My glory I will glorify* <note>Isaiah 60:7</note>. "Come, let us walk in the light of the Lord" refers to the light of the Lord of which it is written:
> The Lord will command His lovingkindness in the daytime. <note>Psalms 42:9</note>

From Eden, it goes out to the Garden, and He planted this Garden to take delight in it with the righteous who dwell within it. Come and see, it is written:
> **But** on the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement... and you shall afflict your souls. <note>Leviticus 23:27</note>

And it is written:
> And it shall be a statute forever... in the seventh month. <note>Leviticus 16:29</note>

What does the word "But" <note>Hebrew: *Ach*</note> come to teach here? He said to him: It comes as a limitation. Since it says *you shall afflict your souls*, it is written *but for the month*. Later it says *but on the tenth*. "But" implies an exemption from the affliction, for the matter depends on the tenth. He said to him: Is it not written *on the first day you shall take*? <note>Referring to Sukkot</note>. We have learned that "But" divides. See, it is permitted to remove the waste from the leek <note>A legal comparison to Sabbath/Festival laws regarding sorting food</note>; so too here, "But on the tenth of the month" means it is permitted to do what is necessary for the soul. Regarding *you shall afflict your souls*, it is taught that this affliction is only found from midday onwards, and he is exempt [beforehand]; thus "But" divides the requirement of afflicting your souls. Rabbi Eleazar said, it is written:

-> **For** on this day He shall atone for you... <- <note>Leviticus 16:30</note>

It should have said "to atone for you." Rather, "He shall atone for you" <note>The Hebrew *Yekhaper Aleikhem* can be read as "He shall atone *over* you"</note> is to include the Power that is hidden in its source, to strengthen this day on every side, to provide space for the Bride and to strengthen her, and not just "upon you." That is to say: for your sake, because of the fear you have on this day, as it is written: *before the Lord you shall be clean*, so that judgment shall not rule over you. Rabbi Judah said: Happy are Israel, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires them and wants to purify them so that no sin shall be found among them, so that they may be members of the Palace and ready for the Palace. And a proof for the future is written:
> And I will sprinkle clean water upon you... <note>Ezekiel 36:25</note>

Rabbi Judah opened and said:
> Out of the depths I have called You, O Lord. <note>Psalms 130:1</note>

We have learned: At the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, He sought to create Man. He consulted the Torah. She said before Him: "You wish to create this man, but he is destined to sin before You. He is destined to provoke You. If You deal with him according to his deeds, the world will not be able to stand before You, nor will that man." He said to her: "Is it for nothing that I am called **God, Merciful and Gracious, Long-suffering**?" Even before the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, He created **Repentance** <note>Hebrew: *Teshuvah*</note>. He said to Repentance: "I seek to create Man in the world, on the condition that when they return to you from their sins, you shall be ready to forgive their sins and atone for them." At every single hour, Repentance is ready for human beings. And when people return from their sins, this Repentance returns toward the Holy One, Blessed be He, and He atones for everything. All judgments are suppressed and sweetened, and the person is purified of his sin. When is a person purified of his sin? At the time when he enters into this Repentance as is fitting. Rabbi Isaac said: He who returns before the Supreme King at the door...

## Main Text (The Zohar)

->**After the Death**<-

**Out of the depths.** *A song of ascents: Out of the depths I have called to You, O Lord* <note>Psalm 130:1</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: "Out of the depths I have called to You"—this refers to a hidden place above, the "depth of the well" from which springs flow to every side. This depth of depths is called **Repentance** <note>The Hebrew *Teshuva* (Repentance) here refers to the Sefirah of Binah, the Divine Mother and source of cosmic renewal</note>. Anyone who desires to return and be purified of their sins before the King must call upon the Holy One, blessed be He, from that very depth: "Out of the depths I have called to You." Come and see: when a person sins before their Master and brings an offering upon the altar, and the priest atones for them and prays on their behalf, Mercy is awakened and Judgments are sweetened. Then, Repentance pours out blessings into the flowing springs, and all the "lamps" <note>The Sefirot or divine lights</note> are blessed together, and the person is purified of their sins.

Come and see: The Holy One, blessed be He, brought forth ten holy crowns above. He is crowned with them and clothed in them; He is they and they are He, all as one, like a flame bound to a coal <note>original: *ke-chidu de-nachasha* - a metaphor for the unified link between God and His attributes</note>, where there is no separation. Corresponding to these, there are ten crowns below that are not holy. These are attached to the "fingernails" of a holy crown called **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note>. Because of this, they are called "wisdoms," and they numbered ten. These wisdoms descended to the world and were all found in Egypt, except for the quality of Kindness <note>Chesed</note> which did not spread through the world [in that dark form]. All those sorcerers and magicians possessed more knowledge of sorcery than all other people in the world.

When these sorcerers wished to gather for their works, they would go out into the fields to the mountains of darkness and the crevices between the rocks. They would perform their rites and encircle that place with water. Afterward, they would gather in those crevices with the water surrounding them and offer sacrifices to those "kinds" <note>demonic species</note>. These spirits would then draw near to them in those mountains. Through their errors, they would offer sacrifices and learn from them, and thus they went astray. This is what is written:
> *You shall not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you dwelt, and you shall not do as they do in the land of Canaan...* <note>Leviticus 18:3</note>
And it is written:
> *...nor shall you walk in their statutes.* <note>Leviticus 18:3</note>

Come and see: when they would offer sacrifices in the field and summon them, all the evil kinds would gather and appear to them in the form of **satyrs** <note>original: *se'irim* - goat-demons</note>, all covered in hair, and they would inform them of whatever they sought to know.

Come and see, Isaac—what is written of him? *And Jacob went near to Isaac his father, and he felt him, and said: "The voice is the voice of Jacob..."* <note>Genesis 27:22</note>. <note>The text here enters a complex discussion regarding the "voice" of Jacob versus the "hands" of Esau, contrasting the power of prayer with the power of the sword and sorcery</note>. 

Rabbi Hiyya said: Regarding those lower crowns that are not holy, they circle about and "fly to the place," and this is the crowning of the "Bride" <note>here referring to the "Other Side's" version of the feminine presence</note>. Rabbi Isaac said in the name of Rabbi Judah: The "opening" of the wicked leads to the "damagers" <note>mazikin - harmful spirits</note> of the world. Rabbi Yose asked: "If so, is it good for the wicked that they become damaging spirits in the world?" He replied: "It is a punishment without rest. Is there any pain like that which is prepared for them in that world?"

Rabbi Hiyya said: We have learned that the "expiration" of the wicked occurs when they depart from the world. Many "officers of justice" <note>angels of destruction</note> are ready to receive them and bring them into Gehenna. They are subjected to three judgments every day in **Gehenna**. Afterward, they are joined by mocking spirits who roam the world and mislead the wicked who were offered repentance but refused it. Then they are returned to Gehenna, and so it happens every day.

After they go about in that manner among humans, they return to their graves. The "worm of the body" <note>the decay of the physical form</note> meets them and consumes them. Those sorcerers would go to the graveyards and perform their magic, causing a "spirit of madness" to cling to a person, attaching a **phantom** <note>original: *nephicha* - a hollow or blown-up spirit</note> to them. Afterward, they would enter into that phantom.

## After Death

It flies off in that crown <note>original: "keter"</note> (that which is not intended) and they are scattered to the four sides and raised to the four corners of the grave. Then they strike their wings and gather together, those wings and those evil species, and they bring that soul and it enters the grave and speaks with them. Rabbi Isaac said: How fortunate are the righteous in this world and in the world to come, for they are all holy. Their body is holy. Their soul <term>Nefesh - the lowest level of the soul, associated with physical life and the body</term> is holy. Their spirit <term>Ruach - the middle level of the soul, associated with emotions and moral virtues</term> is holy. Their breath of life <term>Neshamah - the highest level of the soul, the divine spark of intellect and God-consciousness</term> is the Holy of Holies. These are three levels corresponding to the pattern above. As we have learned, Rabbi Judah said it is written:
> The sun rises, they gather together, and they crouch in their dens <note>Psalms 104:22</note>
This refers to the ascent of the Supernal First Man. Three levels are attached as one: **Nefesh**, **Ruach**, and **Neshamah**. And the highest ascent is the entry of the **Neshamah**. For Rabbi Jose said: All of them are as one for the **Nefesh**. And the accompaniment of the **Nefesh** ascends to be gathered. And when a person is occupied with this **Nefesh**, they pour upon him a single crown called **Ruach**. This is what is written:
> Until a spirit is poured upon us from on high <note>Isaiah 32:15</note>
Then he is strengthened when a person is awakened by another to gaze upon the Throne of the Holy King. And when a person merits that **Ruach**, they crown him with a high holy crown that includes everything, which is called **Neshamah**. It is called the "Breath of God" <note>original: "Nishmat Eloah"</note>. And it finds wisdom in the **Ruach** through the secret of the Garden, the breath of God the King. And this verse that is written:
> And I praised the dead who have already died <note>Ecclesiastes 4:2</note>
Since it is written "I praised the dead," why does it add "who have already died"? Rather, it means those who have already died in this world while in the service of their Master. And we have learned: the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> made three dwellings for the righteous. One is for those righteous who have not departed from this world; when the world needs mercy, they are alive and dwell like eagles, and they bring the **Neshamah** down upon themselves. They see and make the matter known to those who sleep in Hebron <note>A reference to the Patriarchs buried in the Cave of Machpelah</term>, and they awaken and ascend to the Lower Garden of Eden, where the spirits of the righteous are clothed in crowns of light and are hidden away. And the Holy One does their will and has pity on the world. And those **Nefesh** spirits of the righteous are found in this world to protect the living, as it says, "and the living shall lay it to his heart." And this [soul] does not depart from this world, in order to gaze and to know and to supervise the generation. And this is what the companions said: they are known as the "bridge of the world." But the punishment of the wicked is like a deaf person; regarding this it is written:
> That soul shall be cut off from its people <note>Genesis 17:14</note>
And the second dwelling is above, where the Holy One makes high and precious dwellings in the likeness of this world and in the likeness of the upper world—palaces, crowns, and colors that are beyond counting. Fragrances and scents ascend every day, and in this place the soul called **Ruach** of the righteous circles. The dwelling of that **Ruach** is where they circle, and every single **Ruach** is clothed in a precious garment in the likeness of this world and in the likeness of that upper world. The third dwelling is that high holy dwelling called the <term>Bundle of Life - the ultimate resting place of the highest souls</term>, for there that high holy level called **Neshamah** delights. This level is attached to enjoy the supernal delight, as it is written:
> Then you shall delight in the Lord, and I will cause you to ride [on the high places of the earth] <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>
And see, in the hour when the world needs mercy and those righteous ones merit it, that **Nefesh** which is found in the world protects the world. The **Nefesh** ascends and goes and strikes [the gates] in the world and informs the **Ruach**. And the **Ruach** ascends and is crowned and informs the **Neshamah**. And the **Neshamah** informs the Holy One, Blessed be He. Then the Holy One has pity on the world. Then they descend from above to below: the **Neshamah** informs the **Ruach**, and the **Ruach** informs the **Nefesh**. And as it is written regarding "praise" and "the scent of his fragrance," they all join and are crowned as one, until they see and are nourished to come before the Supernal King. And they return to their place in the Crown. This is what is written:
> And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, all flesh shall come [to worship before me] <note>Isaiah 66:23</note>
And in the hour when the world needs mercy, the living go and inform the **Nefesh** spirits of the righteous, and they weep upon their graves to inform them. Because they have permission to attach themselves to the Throne like a soul.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the relationship between the living and the dead, specifically how the souls of the righteous act as intermediaries during times of worldly distress.</meta>

## After Death (Acharei Mot)

Then the <term>souls</term> <note>Aramaic: *Nefesh*; the lower level of the soul most connected to the physical world</note> of the righteous are awakened and they gather and travel, wandering to the <term>Sleepers of Hebron</term> <note>The Patriarchs and Matriarchs buried in the Cave of Machpelah</note>. They inform them of the world’s suffering. Then they all enter the gateway of the Garden of Eden and inform the "Spirits" <note>Aramaic: *Ruchin*; the middle level of the soul</note>. Those spirits who are crowned in the Garden of Eden ascend to their stations and inform the "Higher Soul" <note>Aramaic: *Nishmata*; the highest, most divine level of the soul</note>. Finally, the Higher Soul informs the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, and they all seek <term>mercy</term> for the living, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, takes pity on the world for their sake. Regarding this, Solomon said <note>Ecclesiastes 4:2</note>: **"And I praised the dead who have already died..."**

Rabbi Hiyya said: This is well for those who are alive, but is there no one who knows how to inform the dead to come [to our aid]? Rabbi Isaac said: At the time when the world needs rain, the living appear to the Sleepers of Hebron. And what is written? <note>2 Samuel 23:20</note> **"And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada..."** <margin>Another version: to bind</margin> Then there is fear for all those who know that the world is in distress, yet they do not appear and do not know how to inform them, for they all cry out over the lack below, yet you do not ascend to that place. Alternatively, the soul of repentance—they all ascend and return before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>; they all gather and seek mercy and inform those Sleepers of Hebron. They enter and inform the Spirit in the Garden of Eden as we have said, and those spirits all return to weep and mourn over the world's suffering. Woe to them, for they all gather in vain!

Rabbi Yose said: The decree of the Torah is that the lower ones, through their actions, are all in darkness. And they are all beneath <insert>another version: below</insert> their sins; because of this, they shall not go there without darkness, and they all need repentance to seek a request before them. Rabbi Hezekiah said: For all of them, a fast is decreed. Rabbi Yose said: Even if only one person in that day and in the whole world returns in repentance like a young girl <note>meaning with great fervor or sincerity</note>, then they all join together to seek mercy for the world.

We have learned: Rabbi Judah said: One day Rabbi Hezekiah and Rabbi Yose were walking on the road. They happened upon the trunk of a tree and sat down. They sat near a graveyard, and Rabbi Yose had a staff in his hand which he struck against the ground. While they were sitting, a certain grave was agitated before them and cried out: "Woe, woe! For the world is in great distress! Pity the lack of everything below! Pity the serpent who prepares to find guilt against us and to strike us with shame; in their freedom, inform them!"

Rabbi Hezekiah and Rabbi Yose looked at him. Rabbi Hezekiah said: "Are you saying to him: 'Death, pity and spare'? You have prepared yourself for death! For once the world sat in distress, and the living came here to arrange for us with a Torah scroll, and they all forced themselves before us toward the Sleepers of Hebron. And when they joined as a congregation with the spirits of the righteous, it was found before them that this destruction was before us. That serpent was disqualified and looked with an evil eye at the King because of what was found. And a vision appeared further in the Holy Place; he read and added, hearing two portions, and they said they surrounded and looked with a staff at the King who sits with them, and they took me and forced me at that time from the Academy."

Until a certain elder at the end of their nicknames... <note>The text here becomes highly cryptic and fragmented, involving mystical shorthand</note> and the book lived... so much was purified here. And then Rabbi Eleazar son of Rabbi Shimon was awakened, who is buried with you, and he sought for them and the world was pitied. Then they surrounded us at that time. And what is it that they raised him... the sins of the grave? No. And it comes toward Wisdom. There is no one who awakens to stand before the Sleepers of Hebron, for I fear that money which they pushed away from me and forced me. And it is taught: they are sealed to the Higher Soul... for the world is found in distress. And until it is shaken to see, who will go first to inform those righteous of truth, the Sleepers of Hebron, that you have died... like that smoke of a Torah scroll?

Rabbi Hezekiah said: "Heaven forbid! The world is not in such distress, and therefore do not be so shaken." Rabbi Hezekiah and Rabbi Yose stood up and went to say to them: "In the hour that merits are found in the world, the world only exists because of the dead." Rabbi Yose said: "At the time when the world needs rain, one appears to them, to the dead, and behold it is written: 'And David...'"

## Main Text (Zohar)

And regarding the phrase "one who consults the dead" <note>Deuteronomy 18:11</note>, it is lacking. He said to him: Until now, we have not seen a death that causes fear for the soul above. "One who consults the dead"—this is precise. It refers to the wicked of the world, those nations who worship idols, who are always found to be "dead" <note>The Zohar often teaches that the wicked are considered dead even while alive</note>. But as for Israel, those who are righteous in truth, why would he call them "the dead"? For they have already died at another time and are not hidden; they have already died and are now open and alive. Furthermore, when the other nations go to their dead, they come with sorceries to stir up evil species upon them. But all of Israel, when they go to their dead, they go with great longing before the Holy One, blessed be He, with fasting before Him, and all because their souls are holy. They are like a mercy before the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Holy One, blessed be He, has pity on the world because of them. And concerning this we have learned: when a righteous man departs from this world, he is not removed or hidden from all the worlds, for he is found in all worlds even more than before. For in his lifetime he was found in this world alone, but afterward, he is found in three worlds and is available to them, as it is written: <note>Song of Songs 1:3</note> **The maidens love you**—do not read it as *alamot* (maidens), but as *olamot* (worlds). Blessed is their portion.

Come and see, it is written: <note>1 Samuel 25:29</note> **And the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life**. "And the soul of my lord shall be"—this refers to the soul <note>original: *nishmata*</note> of the righteous man which is prepared for him. Rather, as we have said, blessed is the portion of the righteous, for they are all tied one to another: the lower soul <note>term: *nefesh* - the vital/animal soul</note> to the spirit <note>term: *ruach* - the emotional/intellectual soul</note>, and the spirit to the higher soul <note>term: *neshamah* - the divine spark</note>, and the higher soul to the Holy One, blessed be He. Thus it is found that he goes out in the "bundle of life." Rabbi Eleazar said: That which we said regarding the exile of a Torah scroll—that even from one synagogue to another it is forbidden if they do not tremble—how much more so to a distant place. Why? Is it because it is distant? Rabbi Judah said: As we have said, because they are stirred up over it and will seek mercy for the world. Rabbi Aha said: When the Divine Presence <note>term: *Shekhinah* - the feminine indwelling presence of God</note> wanders like this, from here to there, until she says: <note>Jeremiah 9:1</note> **Oh, that I were in the wilderness, in a lodging place of wayfaring men** etc. So too here, from synagogue to synagogue, and afterward to a distant place, and afterward "in the wilderness, in a lodging place of wayfaring men." Rabbi Judah said: The people of Babylon are afraid and did not even move [the scroll] from synagogue to synagogue. He said: Rabbi Shimon said to the companions: In your days, the people of the world will not need to guard this. Rabbi Yose said: The righteous protect the world in their deaths even more than in their lives. For it is written: <note>2 Kings 19:34</note> **For I will defend this city to save it, for My own sake, and for My servant David's sake.** Yet in their lifetimes, this is not written. Rabbi Judah said: What merit is it that it is written "for My sake and for My servant David's sake," weighing one against the other? Rather, it is because David merited to be attached to the Holy Chariot <note>term: *retikha kadisha* - the divine structure of the Sefirot</note> to protect it, and because of this, all is one. Blessed be He forever and to all eternity.

->**After the doings** of the land of Egypt, wherein you dwelt, you shall not do<- <note>Leviticus 18:3</note>

And the joy with which the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices over it is open and revealed. Every verse of joy and every section of joy is open and revealed. For it was taught: Rabbi Judah said: The rest of righteousness is like a priest to the world. And who was Tamar? Rabbi Abba said: This section proves that joy is open and revealed, and behold, everything is found in joy. And it is not found afterward that it is called "the opening of the eyes" except without an opening, and the space is a space that is wide. And it was taught: What is this "opening of righteousness"? It is for the goodness of life. Come and see and know the comfort before the mercy of the Holy One, blessed be He, how He remembers this world with the children of men. And because He knows, the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills the statutes upon them. And the sickness—behold, just as the dream was, Bathsheba saw, and who are the blessings to stand to melt the king's enemy? So too here, the dream was Tamar, who waited from the day the world was created. And she sat in the "opening of the eyes." Who is the "opening of the eyes"? It is the whole, and the voice, and he sacrificed, the opening of the voice. And it is written: <note>Psalms 118:19</note> **Open to me the gates of righteousness** etc. "Eyes"—for all the eyes of the world are toward this...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the Book of Leviticus, specifically the portion of Acharei Mot. The text transitions into a deep allegorical reading of the story of Judah and Tamar from Genesis 38, viewing their union not as a human failing, but as a cosmic necessity for the establishment of the Davidic line and the unification of Divine attributes.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

To this entrance they bring: **"on the side of the altar"** <note>Leviticus 1:11; original: "al yerekh ha-mizbe'ach"</note>. What is the benefit? As we have established: **"and he beholds the likeness of the Lord"** <note>Numbers 12:8</note>. And so we have established that Tamar established the matter below, and blossoms blossomed, and she acted with the spirit of faith. Judah assisted, and the Name <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> was with the Holy Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine indwelling presence of God</term>. The letters Yod-Heh-Vav of Judah's name were combined for the union. Just as grace follows the path of sin, so "she covered her face," as we have established. Because she covered her face, all was Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: the second Sephirah, representing the flash of intuition</term>, and from below her mouth the world was kindled when they agreed. And she said, "I have done no iniquity." Why? Because she covered her face and there was no one who knew her secret to turn away from her.

**"And he turned aside to her by the way"** <note>Genesis 38:16</note>. Literally "to the way," to be joined in union at the beginning. **"And he said, 'Please, let me come in to you'"** etc. Behold, we have established that he turned everything to its proper place. "For he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law." "For she was his daughter-in-law" <note>Hebrew: "kallato"</note>—the Aramaic translation renders this as "the silence of the world." Why did he not know? Because the wings were covering her to receive the miracle and the earth to become wise and to establish the world. "For she was his daughter-in-law" <note>kallato</note>—this is the actual Bride <note>kallah</note>, as it is written: **"Come with me from Lebanon, my bride"** <note>Song of Songs 4:8</note>.

And she said, "What will you give me, that you may come in to me?" The Bride opened with a good name. And he said, "I will send a young goat from the flock." This is like a king who had a holy, wise daughter who walked in his palace. The king desired to be joined with the Matron <term>Matronita: the Divine Mother or Shekhinah</term> above her and to dwell with her. She said, "Who will give to me the King in his palace?" He said, "From everything I will forgive the bond, and I will come to her alone from my Name and my Throne." Thus: **"Come, let us be wise, I will send a young goat from the flock."** And we have established this regarding "Do not boil a kid in its mother's milk"—how many children come from this. And regarding this, it is not written "I will give," but "I will send"—to man, to your lion, to return him, but he shall be extended in the palace.

And she said, **"What pledge will you give me until you send it?"** These are the signs of the Matron who is joined to the King in union. **"And he said, 'What pledge shall I give you?' And she said, 'Your seal, and your cord, and your staff'"** <note>Genesis 38:18</note>. These are the bonds and the ornaments of the Bride to be joined; they are three, for everything is entwined in three, and the Bride is blessed as one—the secret of the male. Immediately, "he gave them to her and came in to her, and she conceived by him."

And it says, "about three months later." Why three months? After the months are revealed. And we have established that "about three months" refers to the three months of anger that awaken for the merits in the world through the children of men. And she goes out from the crown to meet him. Then "it was told to Judah, saying: 'Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the harlot.'" Behold, everything was agreed upon in one bond. What is written? **"Bring her out and let her be burned"** <note>Genesis 38:24</note>. Just as it is written: **"He has cast down from heaven to earth the beauty of Israel"** <note>Lamentations 2:1</note>. "And let her be burned"—like the burning of the Temple in exile. What is written? "She was being brought out"—to be drawn into exile. And she sent to her father-in-law, saying: **"By the man to whom these belong..."** It is not written "by the man from whom these are," but "by the man to whom these belong"—his signs are found. "Please identify them." And Judah identified them and said, "She is more righteous than I." "Righteous" <note>Tzedakah</note> certainly. He turned and said "from me" <note>mimeni</note>, as it is written: **"For the Lord is righteous, He loves righteous deeds; the upright shall behold His face"** <note>Psalms 11:7</note>. Righteousness <note>Tzedakah</note>. The righteousness of the Lord is "from me"—from this first foundation, "from him" the inheritance was found.

Rabbi Yose said: What is written after this? Judah was crowned with another crown. He said to him: The Bride was bound, this one in that one. Her father-in-law was hanging behind her. Rabbi Eleazar said: This portion contains supreme wisdom in many ways when one looks at the words. From it, secrets are hidden to pour out the Holy One, blessed be He, and His judgments in every place. And she knew and prepared herself to teach the world the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, because from her came forth ruling kings and humble ones to rule over the world, and our holy spirit acted. Rabbi Abba said: This portion is bound in the spirit of the wisdom of the Torah, and all is hidden and concealed. And the Torah in its entirety is agreed upon in our holiness. And you have no word in the Torah in which the supreme Holy Name does not stand, as it is written and revealed...

# After the Death (Acharei Mot)

Because of this, the secrets of the holy Torah are inherited by the celestial beings, yet they are revealed as a mystery to the inhabitants of the world. In this manner, it is written regarding the building of **the Lord** <note>original: "יי'" - the Tetragrammaton</note> and His establishment in Jerusalem. For just as the Sanctuary is meant to join the holy mind <note>the divine intellect or "Mocha"</note> as is fitting, so too is the Crown <note>Keter</note> kept in concealment; therefore, everything is hidden and stored away. Come and see: anyone who diminishes even a single letter from the Torah, his life and his days are diminished in his youth. He is like one who speaks falsely against the holy Name of the High King.

Rabbi Isaac said: The praise of Egypt is divided in the book, just as we have established that the deeds of Canaan were intended to lead the world astray into many deficient fields. Regarding this, it is written: *Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be to his brothers* <note>Genesis 9:25</note>. All of them are inscribed as doing holy things, yet they perform deeds in secret. Just as it is written: *According to the deeds of the land of Egypt, where you dwelt...* <note>Leviticus 18:3</note>.

Rabbi Yehuda saw that they performed evil deeds <note>original: "זנין בישין" - wicked types of actions</note> to seize the land, so as not to defile your ground. And it is written: *And the land was defiled.* *According to the deeds of the land of Egypt...* Rabbi Hiyya opened and said: *In the corners of the earth...* Come and see: The Holy One, blessed be He, said He would cleanse the land from all the filth of the nations that sought to pollute it. Like a person who turns over a garment and shakes the dirt from it. And all those who are buried in the Holy Land, He will cast them outside, to purify the Holy Land from the "Other Side" <note><term>Sitra Achra</term>: the realm of spiritual impurity or evil</note>. As it were, the land was forced to endure the great ones of the nations and receive their impurity; but He is destined to purify it and remove them.

Rabbi Shimon was walking among the mountains of Tiberias, and every place where he found a serpent or a wild beast, he would remove it and purify the land. Come and see, it is written: *And it was defiled* and *You shall not defile yourselves.* Rabbi Yehuda said: Happy is the portion of one who merits during his lifetime to make his dwelling in the Holy Land. For whoever merits this, merits to be drawn toward the dew of the heavens above that descends upon the land. And whoever merits to be buried during his lifetime <note>meaning, while still alive he chose the land as his home</note> within the Holy Land, merits to be buried later in the Supernal Holy Land.

But for one who does not merit this during his life, and they bring him to be buried there after death, concerning him it is written: *And you came and defiled My land* <note>Jeremiah 2:7</note>. For he descends and brings the authority of the "Other Side" with him, and his body comes under the authority of the Holy Land. As it were, he makes the holy profane and the profane holy. But whoever merits that his soul departs in the Holy Land, merits to be buried under the wings of the Divine Presence <note><term>Shekhinah</term>: the indwelling feminine aspect of God</note>, as it is written: *And He will atone for His land and His people* <note>Deuteronomy 32:43</note>. Not only that, but if he merits it in his life, a holy spirit is constantly drawn over him. But whoever dwells under a foreign authority, a foreign spirit is drawn over him.

Come and see: when Rav Hamnuna the Elder went up to prepare his place, the members of the Night Academy stood up. He said to them: "By your lives, I have the strength for the path so as not to stumble, but do not let the deposit be lost to the destroyer." Fortunate are all those who did not merit to see the bitter waters, but returned the deposit <note>the soul</note> of their Master to its place. Rabbi Isaac said: Therefore, anyone who performs evil worship defiles the land. The land departs, and woe to that man, for the Holy Land will not receive him afterward. Concerning him it is written: *Let sinners be consumed from the earth, and let the wicked be no more* <note>Psalm 104:35</note>. Then, *Bless the Lord, O my soul. Hallelujah.*

***

*My judgments you shall do, and My statutes you shall keep, to walk in them...* <note>Leviticus 18:4</note> Rabbi Abba said: Happy is the portion of Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, desired them more than all the idolatrous nations. Because of His love for them, He gave them laws of truth. He planted within them the Tree of Life and placed the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> among them. What is the reason? Because Israel is marked with the Holy Sign <note>the mark of circumcision</note> like crowns, and they are recognized as belonging to Him. Just as palaces and buildings are recognized by their signs, so too, all those who are not marked with the Holy Sign are like carcasses...

# After the Death (Acharei Mot)

They are recognized as coming from the side of impurity; therefore, do not join with them and do not become defiled among them through the words of the Holy One, Blessed be He. It is forbidden to make known to them a word of Torah, because the Torah is entirely the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and all the letters of the Torah are bound to the Holy Name. Anyone who does not strive and is not bound to the Holy Name <note>original: *Shema Kadisha*</note> (another version: in the holy fear) as is fitting, it is forbidden to make known to him a word of Torah or to allow him to labor in it.

The Rabbi opened his discourse: **"This is the statute of the Passover: no foreigner shall eat of it"** <note>Exodus 12:43</note>. And it is written, **"A sojourner and a hired servant shall not eat of it"** <note>Exodus 12:45</note>. Now, if regarding the Passover sacrifice, which is merely for eating <note>physical consumption</note>, the Torah says it is a holy matter and a connection for all, yet they are forbidden to eat of it or approach it until they are circumcised—how much more so for the Torah, which is the Holy of Holies of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and a Name supreme over all!

Rabbi Eleazar said: Fortunate is the portion of Israel, for they were privileged to learn Torah. The companions have already awakened <note>discussed</note> that in every matter concerning the nations, it says: **"He declares His words to Jacob, His statutes and His judgments to Israel"** <note>Psalms 147:19</note>.

Rabbi Eleazar continued: Come and see how fortunate are Israel, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, planted a holy, supernal teaching within them, as it is written: **"For I have given you a good doctrine"** <note>Proverbs 4:2</note>. "To you," and not to the other nations of the world. And because the Torah is a supernal, precious treasure, hidden from all, it is entirely "hidden and revealed" <note>original: *satim ve-galya* - referring to the literal and mystical layers of meaning</note> within the mystery of the Name.

Come and see: Israel exists in two levels, hidden and revealed. We have learned that there are three levels bound one to another: The Holy One, Blessed be He; the Torah; and Israel. Each of these levels consists of a "hidden" and a "revealed" aspect.
*   The Holy One, Blessed be He, is level upon level, hidden and revealed.
*   The Torah is likewise hidden and revealed.
*   Israel is likewise level upon level.

The witness for this is: **"He declares His words to Jacob, His statutes and His judgments to Israel."** These are two levels: Jacob and Israel—one revealed and one hidden. What does this mean? Anyone who is circumcised but has not yet ascended in the Holy Name <note>perhaps referring to spiritual maturity or the "revealed" stage of Jacob</note>, all the words that are revealed in the Torah are made known to him on the lower mystery, namely the weight of the commandments of the Torah and no more, until he rises to the other level. This is what is written: **"He declares His words to Jacob."** To Jacob, specifically. But **"His statutes and His judgments to Israel"** refers to one who is at a higher level. For it is written: **"Your name shall no longer be called Jacob [but Israel]"** <note>Genesis 35:10</note>. "His statutes and His judgments to Israel"—these are the mysteries of the Torah, the laws of the Torah, and the secrets of the Torah, which are not permitted to be revealed except to one who is at the higher level as is fitting.

And if this applies to Israel, how much more so for the idol-worshipping nations? Anyone who is not circumcised and is given even a small letter of the Torah, it is as if he destroys the world and speaks falsely against the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: **"If My covenant be not with day and night, I would not have appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth"** <note>Jeremiah 33:25; the "covenant" is traditionally interpreted as circumcision</note>.

Come and see, it is written: **"And this is the Torah which Moses set before the children of Israel"** <note>Deuteronomy 4:44</note>. Before the children of Israel, and not before other nations. The sages of the world, such as Hillel, were witnesses to this, for they told their students not to make known a word of Torah until they were circumcised.

And you, the holy word of the Torah is for the meritorious. These are the words of the Heavenly Court, matters that the people of the world cannot grasp with their intellect or elevate with their will. When they speak in their impurity, even the supernal angels cannot grasp it, because these matters are hidden within the Holy Name. Four hundred and five myriads of worlds all hang from the point of the one thousand and seventy-two holy Names engraved below, upon which the upper and lower beings depend. The four supports of the Throne of Glory hang from one side to the other, and from the expansion of the "Aleph" <note>the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often representing unity or the beginning of emanation</note> they all stand. They are supported by the mysteries of Wisdom <note>term: *Chokhmah* - the first flash of divine intellect</note>, hidden and concealed in the depths. All the surrounding sides emerge from that lower point beneath the Aleph. From here onwards, it depends on the separation of the Aleph, and there is no end to the calculation of the Wisdom revealed here.

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Acharei Mot. ## Main Text (Zohar)

->After the Death<-

Thus we have learned: the sustenance of all and the faith of all is to bind the bond of faith, joining one to the other until they are seen as one. And for one who strives to be bound in that bond of faith, and for one who does not strive and is not bound by it, it is written of him: *“No stranger shall eat of the holy thing”* and *“No uncircumcised person shall eat of it.”* <note>Leviticus 22:10, Exodus 12:43</note> For behold, the spirit of impurity from the "Other Side" <note>term: Sitra Achra; the realm of evil or impurity in Kabbalistic thought</note> is aroused to mingle with the Holy. Blessed be the Merciful One who separated Israel as marked children with the holy mark <note>note: referring to the sign of circumcision</note> from among the nations and their waters. Concerning them it is written:
> **“Yet I had planted you a noble vine, wholly a right seed.”** <note>Jeremiah 2:21</note>

And because of this, *“You will give truth to Jacob”* <note>Micah 7:20</note> and not to another. *“The law of truth was in his mouth.”* <note>Malachi 2:6</note> Rabbi Eleazar prostrated himself upon his hands. That pious one said: It is written,
> **“For the Lord will not cast off His people for His great name’s sake,”** etc. <note>Psalms 94:14</note>

*“For the Lord will not cast off His people.”* Why? Because all is to be bound together as one. And how much did Israel strive for the Holy One, Blessed be He? Through that holy mark that is sealed in their flesh. And because of this, *“the Lord will not cast off His people,”* which is to say, for the sake of His great Name that is sealed within them. Come and see: the Torah is called "Covenant." The Holy One, Blessed be He, is called "Covenant." And this holy mark <note>circumcision</note> is called "Covenant." And all is to be bound as one, and one shall not be separated from the other. Rabbi Yose said to him: "Torah" and "Israel" are well understood. But from where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is called "Covenant"? He replied: As it is written, *“And He remembered for them His covenant,”* etc. <note>Psalms 106:45</note>—this is for eternity, as has been stated. *“And these My statutes you shall keep.”* "My statutes" (*Chukotai*)—these are the hidden treasures of the King. "My ordinances" (*Mishpatai*)—these are the decrees of the Torah. Rabbi Judah said: All those gatherings from the place called "Righteousness" (*Tzedek*) are called "My statutes," and they are the King's decrees. And in every place called "Ordinance" (*Mishpat*), they are called the judgment of the King, for He is the Holy King. The Holy One, Blessed be He, is King of the whole world; all is His, for He is the Holy King in the place where two portions are grasped as one. And concerning this it is written:
> **“Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne.”** <note>Psalms 89:15</note>

And they are Judgment and Mercy, and because of this, "Statute and Ordinance." Furthermore, it is written, *“Statutes and ordinances for Israel.”* For Israel, and not for the other nations. What is written?
> **“He has not dealt so with any nation,”** etc. <note>Psalms 147:20</note>

And we have learned: even if a gentile strives but does not perform the commandments of the Torah, he is considered like nothing. And it is forbidden to reveal to him the secrets of the words of Torah. And concerning this we learned: "An altar of stones"—this is a literal altar of stones. And the sages stood, for the intention behind it stands, and the serpent shall not cease from him. Because of this, it did not succeed in his hand, for he is a gentile and it did not benefit him. And regarding this it is written: *“For if you lift up your sword <note>original: "martach" - likely a variant or typo for "charbach" (your sword)</note> upon it, you have profaned it.”* <note>Exodus 20:22</note> Because of this, *“He has not dealt so with any nation”* is written. *“And as for His ordinances, they have not known them”*—forever and for all eternity. Another thing: one does not give them the secrets of the Torah or the hidden things of the Torah. As it is written:
> **“For the Lord’s portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance.”** <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>

*“Happy is the people that is in such a case; happy is the people whose God is the Lord.”* <note>Psalms 144:15</note>

**"The nakedness of thy father, or the nakedness of thy mother, shalt thou not uncover"** <note>Leviticus 18:7</note>. Rabbi Hiyya opened his discourse: **"As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons,"** etc. <note>Song of Songs 2:3</note>. How precious is the love and the companionship of the Bride! How much does <term>Knesset Yisrael</term> <note>The Community of Israel, representing the Shekhinah or the Divine Feminine</note> praise the Holy One, Blessed be He, for she praises Him with this! Above all others, she is found to praise Him as an "apple" and not as anything else—whether in colors, in scent, or in taste. Everything was and went, and it is written "apple" because she praises Him in everything: in colors, in scent, and in taste. Just as the apple is a sight for all to see, so is the Holy One, Blessed be He, a sight for all. Just as the apple is found in colors <note>red, white, and green, representing the different divine attributes</note> as we have established, so is the Holy One, Blessed be He, found in supreme colors. Just as the apple has a scent finer than all other trees, so is it written of the Holy One, Blessed be He: **"And his scent like Lebanon"** <note>Hosea 14:7</note>. Just as the apple’s taste is sweet, so is it written of the Holy One, Blessed be He: **"His mouth is most sweet"** <note>Song of Songs 5:16</note>. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, praises the Community of Israel with this taste, and we have established what is fitting for this, as it is said.

Rabbi Yehuda said: At the time when there are righteous people in the world, the Community of Israel emits good fragrances and is blessed by the Holy King, and her face is radiant. But at the time when there are guilty people in the world, as it were, she does not emit good fragrances, and she tastes from the <term>Sitra Achra</term> <note>The "Other Side," the realm of spiritual impurity and evil</note> which is bitter. In that state, it is written: **"He has cast down from heaven to earth [the beauty of Israel]"** <note>Lamentations 2:1</note>, and her face is darkened.

Rabbi Yose said: At the time when there are righteous people in the world, it is written: **"His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me"** <note>Song of Songs 2:6</note>. But at the time when there are guilty people in the world, it is written: **"He has drawn back His right hand"** <note>Lamentations 2:3</note>.

Rabbi Hezekiah said: From the verse **"A whisperer separates a chief friend"** <note>Proverbs 16:28</note>, we learn that the King is separated from the <term>Matronita</term> <note>The Matron or Queen, another name for the Shekhinah</note>. This is what is meant by: "The nakedness of thy father, or the nakedness of thy mother, shalt thou not uncover" <note>Meaning: do not cause a separation between the Divine Father and Mother through sin</note>.

Rabbi Eleazar was sitting before his father [Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai]. He said to him: This conduct of the world is found to be like the Matronita. And if there is an accuser in the world, it is found that the Matronita is struck. He said to him: It is like a King who had a son from the Matronita. As long as that son does the will of the King, the King makes his dwelling with the Matronita. But as long as that son does not do the will of the King, the King separates his dwelling from the Matronita. So it is with the Holy One, Blessed be He: as long as Israel does the will of the Holy One, Blessed be He, He places His dwelling in the Community of Israel. But as long as Israel does not do the will of the Holy One, Blessed be He, He does not place His dwelling there. And come and see: because Israel is the firstborn son of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: **"Israel is My son, My firstborn"** <note>Exodus 4:22</note>, and this Mother is the Community of Israel, as it is written: **"Forsake not the teaching of thy mother"** <note>Proverbs 1:8</note>. And come and see: whenever Israel is distanced from the King’s palace, as it were, the Matronita is distanced with them. Why? Because the Matronita did not sanctify the standing of this son, to strike him and to draw him after her with discipline. For the King never strikes this son Himself; rather, He leaves everything in the hand of the Matronita to rebuke the son, to strike the son, and to lead him after her to stand before the King.

# After the Death (Acharei Mot)

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Because they do not return <note>in repentance</note>, the Name is then called *YHVH* <note>original: הוי'</note> when the King ascends higher and higher because of the sins of mankind, for they are not worthy of Him. In that hidden world, the *Yod* and *He* <note>the first two letters of the Divine Name</note> ascend to Him because merits have not been established. Then it is called *YHVH* because the *He* has ascended to Him along with the *Yod* <note>variant reading: the *Vav* and *Vav*</note>. At that time, Repentance <note>the Sefirah of Binah</note> is not found. Because of this, the lower *He* <note>the Shekhinah</note> has departed, for she is no longer joined with Repentance. When the heavens and Repentance were previously connected, they did not desire <note>to sin</note>, but then the *He* and *Yod* ascended to the *Vav* and *Yod* above, and it is called *YHVH*. When the Sanctuary was destroyed and Repentance departed, and the protections were removed from above them, they then sinned and said: "Woe to us, for the day has turned" <note>referring to the light of the Divine day fading</note>. This "day that has turned" is the Supernal Day called Repentance, which has departed and passed away because you were not worthy. That day, which is known for extending the "Right Hand" to receive sinners, has turned away from everything and is no longer found. Regarding this, they said:
> **"Woe to us! For the shadows of evening are stretched out."** <note>Jeremiah 6:4</note>

For the desire of the destructive forces that surround the nations has increased, allowing them to rule over <note>Israel</note>. The King, the letter *Yod*, ascended higher and higher; the Temple was burned, the people went into exile, and the Matron <note>the Shekhinah</note> was expelled. It is written that she was expelled, but later, when the *Yod* returned to its place, she was found weeping. The Matron was expelled and went away—who could support her? The Temple was burned, the people were exiled, and He saw their cities in ruins because <note>blessings</note> were withheld. Then it was written:
> **"And in that day did the Lord God of Hosts call to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to girding with sackcloth."** <note>Isaiah 22:12</note>

Then the heavens were clothed in darkness. Then the *Yod* and *Vav* <note>the male aspects of the Divine Name</note> moved away from one another, and the Supernal *He* <note>Binah</note> moved from its place to another side. Their habitations were not found, for the Male and Female <note>Tipheret and Malkhut</note> were not found together and did not dwell as one. Then He ascended and struck His dwelling; He wept on high. Rabbi Elazar said: "A powerful weeping is fixed in my heart on this side, and joy is in my heart on the other side; for I have heard words that I have never heard until now. Blessed is my lot!"

### The Nakedness of Your Brother’s Wife
"You shall not uncover..." What is the meaning of "your brother's wife"? Rabbi Shimon said: "We have learned that all matters of the Torah are both hidden and revealed. Just as the Holy Name is hidden and revealed, so too the Torah—which is the Holy Name—is hidden and revealed. Here, everything is revealed and known, yet also hidden as we have established." This verse is as follows: "Your brother's wife" refers to the time when the Matron is joined with the King, and He is called "your brother." Now that she is in exile with you and removed from the King, she is called "your brother's wife." We have learned that the Holy King did not dismiss her with a permanent divorce from His crown, as it is written:
> **"Thus says the Lord: Where is the bill of your mother’s divorcement, wherewith I have put her away?"** <note>Isaiah 50:1</note>

Heaven forbid! She is certainly the wife of the King, even though she is in exile. Therefore, He commanded concerning her twice. Once, when the Woman is with the King in a single union, she is called "your mother," as it is written: "The nakedness of your mother you shall not uncover." Do not act in a way that causes them to be distanced from one another, causing her to ascend above you, as it is written: **"and for your transgressions was your mother put away"** <note>Isaiah 50:1</note>. And once, when she is in exile with you and revealed outside the King's palace, she is called "your brother's wife." Even though she is distanced from Him, do not act in a way that removes her from your protection. Sometimes she suffers because of you, and you do not guard her in exile. Could you imagine <note>Heaven forbid that you should say</note> "the nakedness of your brother's wife you shall not uncover"? Why? Because "it is your brother's nakedness." Even though she is distanced from the King, the King's watchfulness is always upon her, and she requires extra guarding before Him; do not sin against her.

Rabbi Shimon opened:
> **"For the Lord your God walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you..."** <note>Deuteronomy 23:15</note>

"For the Lord your God"—this is the Shekhinah, who is found among Israel. All the time they are in exile, she watches over them constantly from all sides and from all the other nations, so that they do not destroy Israel. For we have learned: the Sefirot cannot...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->After the Death<-
<note>original: "Acharei Mot" - the title of the Torah portion in Leviticus 16:1–18:30</note>

The foolishness of Israel causes them to deny [the truth] until Israel exchanges the word of the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> for the sake of the appointed ministers of the other nations. Then the foolishness of Israel prevails over them, and [the nations] gain dominion over them and decree many evil decrees upon them. But when they return in repentance to the Holy One, Blessed be He, the strength and power of all those ministers of the nations are broken, and the strength and power of the foolishness of Israel is broken, and they are separated from it all. And regarding this it is written: **"And your camp shall be holy"** <note>Deuteronomy 23:15</note>, for a person must not be defiled by his blemishes, and he should dwell upon the words of the Torah. For if he does [sin], they remove him [from holiness], as it is said: **"And you shall be defiled by them"** <note>Leviticus 11:43</note>, written without the letter *Aleph* <note>The Zohar notes that without the Aleph, the word "and you shall be defiled" (ve-nitmetem) can be read as "and you shall be dulled/blocked" (ve-nitamtem) in the heart</note>. And the beginning of the matter is that there are two hundred and forty-eight limbs in the body, and all of them are found to be heated when they come to commit any sin. Therefore, it must be found that **"your camp shall be holy."** What is "your camp"? These are the limbs of the body. **"And He shall see no unseemly thing in you"** <note>Deuteronomy 23:15</note>—what is an "unseemly thing" <note>ervat davar</note>? This refers to forbidden sexual relations <note>arayot</note>. In another version <term>S"A</term> <note>Sefarim Acherim / Other Books</note> it is hinted at in what we have established: that if it is so, the "tail" destroys and burns. And regarding this:
> **The nakedness of your father’s wife you shall not uncover** <note>Leviticus 18:8</note>
For what reason <term>M"T</term> <note>Mai Ta'ama</note>? Because it is written, **"it is your father’s nakedness,"** as we have established.

Furthermore, for three things Israel is delayed in exile: because they treat the Divine Presence with contempt in exile; because they turn their faces away from the Divine Presence; and because they remove themselves from before the Divine Presence. All of these we have established in our Mishnah <note>referring to the hidden traditional teachings of the Zohar circle</note>.

Rabbi Abba was traveling to Cappadocia, and Rabbi Yose was with him. As they were walking, they saw a man coming toward them who had a mark on his shoulders. Rabbi Abba said: "Turn aside! What does this mark show? For the shoulders of this man testify against him that he has transgressed the forbidden sexual relations of the Torah; in such a manner was he trampled upon his shoulders." Rabbi Yose went and saw the mark; it was as if he had it since he was a youth. He asked: "What forbidden relation was found in him?" [Rabbi Abba] said to him: "I still see on his shoulders that they testify to a transgression of the Torah's laws on forbidden relations."

Rabbi Abba called to him and said: "Tell us, what is this mark on your shoulders? What is it?" He said to them: "I beg of you, do not delay this man any further, for his sins have risen up in his very bones." Rabbi Abba said: "What is it?" He replied: "One day I was traveling on the road and I stayed with a man at an inn and I stole from my master. And all that night I took hold of his wife. In the morning we rose and a powerful man stood over us. We looked that day, and they bound this [mark] upon me, from this side and from that side, and this mark entered into the brain, and it was found by a certain person to be like a brand."

[Rabbi Abba] said to him: "Rejoice, for he is a pious man." He asked: "Is he Rabbi Solomon?" He said to him: "What healing did he give you?" He replied: "A dream that went forth. And from that day I have returned in repentance <note>Teshuvah</note>. And every day my shoulders prove it, as a vision and a gathering before the Holy One, Blessed be He <term>K"BH</term>, for He is the Support of the worlds over that sin. And with the wiping of tears, I wipe my shoulders."

Rabbi Abba said: "By the Life [of the World]! Since your repentance has been heard, the mark shall be removed from your shoulder. May a light shine upon you, and your iniquity be passed away, and your sin be atoned." He said it to him twice, and he saw [the mark]. He said it a third time, and the mark was removed. Rabbi Abba said: "Certainly my portion has risen to remove this from you, for you were found to be a master of repentance." He said to him: "From now on, what should I do?" He replied: "Occupy yourself with the Torah day and night." He asked: "What is your name?" He said: "Eleazar." He said: "Certainly your name caused your portion in life, and it shall be as your witness." Rabbi Abba surrounded him and embraced him.

At another time, Rabbi Abba saw Rabbi Shimon <term>D"Sh</term> <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> in his dream, who was sitting and expounding: **"A brutish man knows not..."** and he completed the verse. And between this and that:
> **A brutish man knows not, neither does a fool understand this.** <note>Psalms 92:7</note>
And so on. How foolish are the people of the world who do not gaze, and do not know, and do not look to know the ways of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and upon what the world stands. What prevents them from knowing? Their own foolishness. Because they do not look into the Torah. If they would look into the Torah, they would know the ways of the Holy One, Blessed be He. "Neither does a fool understand this"—one who does not look and does not know his days.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**After the Death**<-

The mouths of the righteous who walk in the ways of the world are wise to purify that radiance which spreads over their hands; they are wise and understanding, yet [this radiance] does not spread over the wicked, the guilty ones who transgress the words of the Torah, as it is written:

<note>Psalms 92:8</note>
To leave them to be destroyed from that world <note>The World to Come</note> and to become dust beneath the feet of the righteous, as it is written:
> **"And you shall trample the wicked, for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet."**
<note>Malachi 3:21</note>
They taught regarding this and said: "He awakens like half-palms and acts like sand." Rather, fortunate is the portion of the man who strives in the Torah to know its paths and the paths of the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>Aramaic: Kudsha Brich Hu — the standard Rabbinic name for God</note>, for anyone who strives in the Torah out of awe is striving in His very Name. Just as the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, acts through His days, so too the Torah acts through its days. 

Come and see: one who transgresses the words of the Torah, the Torah ascends and descends and makes a mark upon him, like a cup of dregs marked upon his face, so that those above and those below shall look at him, and all the "Mercies" <note>Angelic forces of kindness</note> curse his appearance. And you shall see that all those "Eyes of the Lord" that see and rule in the world to know the debts of the children of men—they all lift their eyes and gaze at the face of that man and identify him, and they all open [their mouths] against him: "Woe! Woe to him in this world, and woe, woe to him in the World to Come!" Withdraw from the surroundings of so-and-so, for the holiness has departed and an <term>impure spirit</term> <note>Aramaic: Ruach Mesava — a spiritual defilement</note> rests upon him. And all those times below, he is marked in his face to return to life when the spirit from the side of impurity departs from him. 

And these are the guilty ones who are strong of face, whose appearance shows they are to be left out of the World to Come. And we have learned: that righteous, meritorious one who strives in the Torah and is beloved by the Holy One, Blessed be He—[God] draws over him a single <term>thread of lovingkindness</term> <note>Aramaic: Chuta de-Chesed — a spiritual aura of grace</note> and marks it upon his face, and that mark is seen by those above and below. Likewise, one who transgresses the words of the Torah, an impure spirit finds him and marks his face, and those above and below flee from him, and they all proclaim about him: "Withdraw from the surroundings of so-and-so, who has transgressed the words of the Torah and the commandments of his Master!" Woe to him, woe to his body! This chief impure spirit is found with him, and the Torah is not within him, and he is light <note>insignificant</note>, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, has no portion in him and leaves him to be lost from the World to Come.

A Rabbi said to him: "From where do you know this? You have spoken well." He replied: "Thus I have learned, and I have seen that this is the secret of the 'deficient ones'—all of them, such as those who will not return [to God], for no word stands before repentance. And thus I learned from a vision I saw once: there was a mark on a man's face, and one day we were walking on the road and met a certain righteous man, and through his hands that mark was removed from the other." He asked him: "What is your name?" He replied: "Eleazar." And I called him "Eleazar the Latter." He said to him: "Blessed is the Merciful One that I have seen you and merited to see you like this. May your portion be whole in this world and in the World to Come." He said to him: "Fortunate is the one I have encountered." He stayed before him and he brought him to his house; he prepared before him a platter <note>Translation note: "Kortisa" — a serving dish or table</note> of copper and the meat of a third-born calf. 

After they ate, that man said to him: "My Master, show me one thing regarding the matter of the <term>Red Heifer</term> <note>Aramaic: Turtah Sumka — the ritual cow used for purification in Numbers 19</note>. I have the warmth of the calf's meat that I have eaten. And one day, before it was conceived and born, I was wandering in the pasture in the desert. While I was leading it, a man passed before me. He said to me: 'What is the name of this heifer?' I saw its kind, but on the day it was born, I did not call it by its name. He said to me: 'Bathsheba' <note>Daughter of Seven</note>... it shall be called for atonement. And while I was returning the spirit to her, I saw him. And I rejoiced at that word."

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**After the Death**<-

Now that we have merited for the Torah to be stirred by this matter—and from the day that Rabbi Hamnuna the Elder passed away, there has not been a man who could illuminate the Torah for us like him—and here I am afraid to say a word of Torah that I have not learned <note>Rabbi Abba expresses humility, fearing to innovate without a direct tradition from his teacher</note>. Yet I have observed this matter, and it is a matter of Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: the second Sephirah, representing the flash of intuition and the "Father" principle</term>, though I do not know it [fully]. Heaven forbid! It is certainly a matter of Wisdom, and it is a sublime hint for the upper and lower worlds. But come and see: seven names are called from the side of the Spirit of Wisdom. As it were, it is written of her: "all seven." Seven cows, and torn ones, and changing ones, and gathered ones, and hidden ones, and pure ones, and painful ones—and the staff is missing from the count. For behold, it is written: *And the Lord spoke to Moses and to Aaron...* <note>Numbers 19:1</note>. And that man spoke well who said "Bathsheba" <note>literally "Daughter of Seven"</note>, for all is the Spirit of Wisdom. Heaven forbid! Blessed is the Merciful One who loaded you with this word. Blessed is He, for He preceded me and taught me at first to merit that which is written:
> "Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near, saith the Lord" (Isaiah 57:19)
Here, when I was far off, He preceded me and taught me so that I might become near. Rabbi Abba recited over him: "Peace be to thee, and peace be to thy house, and peace be unto all that thou hast."

**The nakedness** of your father’s sister you shall not uncover. Rabbi Isaac opened the discussion:
> "And if a man shall take his sister, his father's daughter, or his mother's daughter, and see her nakedness..." (Leviticus 20:17)
There we have learned: for one hundred and thirty years, Adam separated from his wife and did not beget children. From the time Cain killed Abel, Adam did not wish to couple with his wife. Rabbi Yose said: Because death was decreed upon him and upon the whole world, he said, "Why should I beget children for terror?" Immediately, he separated from his wife. Then two female spirits used to come and couple with him, and they gave birth. And those they bore were the damaging spirits <term>Mazikin: harmful supernatural entities</term> of the world, and they are called "the plagues of the sons of men." These rule over human beings at the entrances of their houses, and in the night, and in the bathrooms. But as soon as a man reaches the entrance of his house and the holy Name <note>Shaddai, often found on the Mezuzah</note> is placed upon the shoulders above, they all flee and distance themselves from him. This is what is written:
> "Neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling" (Psalms 91:10)
"Plague" refers to those "plagues of the sons of men." And come and see: at the time when Adam existed in the Supernal Image <note>the divine form of Adam Kadmon</note>, in the holy image, the upper and lower beings all feared him; they approached him and made him king over this world. After he sinned, he brought death upon himself and took all that filth. Later, Cain was born there. In his union, all the guilty generations of the world and the dwelling of demons <term>Shedim</term> and spirits were established and attached there. Because of this, all spirits and demons have a "half" within them—from here and below <note>the physical/impure side</note>, and a "half" from the Kingdom above <note>the spiritual/pure side</note>. And so, when they were born from that other side <margin>The Other Side (Sitra Achra): the realm of evil or impurity</margin> from the side of the sea, some were halves of spirits that emerged from the impurity as it is written. He begot from those spirits in houses of imagination, resembling the upper Sephirot and the lower Sephirot. And it is written:
> "The sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair..." (Genesis 6:2)
And they all went astray after them. And one male was found who came to the world from the heights of the side of Cain, and they called him Tubal-Cain. And one female emerged with him, and creatures go astray after her, and she is called Naamah. From her emerged other spirits and demons. They hang in the air and inform others who are found below. This Tubal-Cain brought weapons of slaughter into the world. And this Naamah excites human beings and attaches herself to this side. Even now she exists, and her dwelling is among the waves of the Great Sea. She goes out and mocks men, warming herself from them in dreams with that desire of male and female. From that desire, she conceives and brings other types [of spirits] into the world. And those children she bears from men appear to the "stars of the throne" <note>referring to certain celestial or demonic hierarchies</note>, and they conceive from them and give birth to spirits. And they all go to the first Lilith <note>the primary demonic female figure in Kabbalah</note>, and she raises them, and she goes out into the world and seeks children...
