# After the Death (Acharei Mot)

And at the hour when the wrathful heat <note>referring to the demonic feminine force</note> is kindled and she clings to him to kill them and to gaze upon the spirits of the wicked, she goes with that spirit. Then, three holy spirits are summoned and they fly before her and take that spirit from her, placing it before the Holy One, Blessed be He. There, they are exchanged before Him in such a manner; for them, there is a lack of holiness, but for the righteous, they are sanctified and become holy. If a holy man is found, he does not fear her. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, summons those holy angels we mentioned, and they take that wicked one <note>the demonic force</note> so she cannot gaze upon him. This is what is written:
> *Evil shall not dwell with You* (Psalms 5:5).

And from this: *No evil shall befall you, nor shall any plague come near your tent* (Psalms 91:10), because *He will give His angels charge over you* (Psalms 91:11). And it is written regarding rescue and escape: if a man is not found holy and draws upon himself a spirit from the side of impurity <term>Sitrah Achra: the "Other Side" or realm of evil</term>, then she rejoices and laughs with that wicked man. If she kills him, she ascends with that spirit and never departs from it. He lives under those "matrons" who kill them. 

When those three holy ones are summoned and take the spirit from her, it is not because they were found in the side of impurity to have the power to kill them, but because the man did not sanctify himself. He ate without intention to gaze [upon the divine] and was defiled. Because of this, she can rule over the body but not over the spirit. 

Sometimes it is found that she goes out from the people into the world to strike. If a man is found in the knot of strong desire <note>lustful thoughts</note>, awakening his dwelling to see with his "wisdom" <note>euphemism for reproductive focus</note>, and his will is in that desire which he has in his dream—then the child born from that side comes from wrath. For in her desire, she was present. When Lilith goes out and shows herself to him, and his mind is on her, he is tied to her. She raises him like those who serve the side of wrath. She is found with him many times and does not kill him. This is the man who, in every new moon, is diminished and nothing is ever born from him. For every new moon, when the world is renewed, Lilith goes out and wanders over all those she has raised and laughs with them. Then that man is diminished and weakened. 

Happy are the righteous who sanctify themselves with the holiness of the King! Concerning them it is written:
> *And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, all flesh shall come to worship before Me, says the Lord* (Isaiah 66:23).

King Solomon revealed these matters in the *Book of Desires of the King*. Found therein are one thousand four hundred and fifty types of impurity by which human beings are defiled. Solomon revealed this! Woe to the people whose hearts are stopped and closed; they do not know, they do not hear, and they do not observe how they stand in the world. Behold, the "mud" <note>materiality/sin</note> and the filth are before them, yet they do not look. For they cannot find understanding except through the "mud" of the Torah <note>original: "titu d'Oraita" - likely a play on words between 'clay/mud' and the 'depths' of study</note>, as it is written:
> *If there be among you any man, that is not clean by reason of a chance that happens by night...* (Deuteronomy 23:11).

"That is not clean"—specifically; "by reason of a chance that happens by night"—specifically. We have established these words in the "mud" of the Holy Torah, for so it is written in the Holy Torah:
> *Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be holy; for I am holy, the Lord your God* (Leviticus 11:44).

We learned: the Crown of Suffocation <note>a mystical term for a restrictive spiritual state</note>. Everything was arranged by Adam in his wisdom, but he was caught by another spirit and fathered this [impurity]. From here, the generations of the righteous are genealogically assigned in the world, as are the pious ones of the Holy One, Blessed be He. 

*Chesed* <term>Chesed: the Sephirah of Loving-kindness</term> is in the world. In every place, a deep root was born that returned the world to the likeness of Above. We have established this in the hidden parts of our Mishnah, as it is written:
> *And if a man shall take his sister, his father's daughter, or his mother's daughter... it is a wicked thing [Chesed hu]* (Leviticus 20:17).

<note>The Zohar notes that the word "Chesed" is used here paradoxically. While it usually means "kindness," in the context of incest, it refers to an unbounded, "unfiltered" overflow of energy that bypasses holy boundaries.</note>

It is "Chesed" certainly, for after this, the branches of kindness incline and go out from the death above and spread. That which was near becomes distant. Then the branch strengthens and labors to be joined as one in the Tree <term>The Sefirotic Tree of Life</term>, as it was at first in the beginning of the world. Because it is written:
> *I have said: The world shall be built in Loving-kindness [Chesed]* (Psalms 89:3).

But from here onwards, men who defile themselves in it are like those who close their eyes in a bubble. We have learned.

It contrasts this impurity with the holiness of the righteous and concludes with a mystical interpretation of "Chesed" (kindness) as the foundational but sometimes misused energy of creation.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**After the Death**<-

**We have learned:** "The nakedness of your father’s sister" <note>Leviticus 18:12</note> is as it is written:
> For the ways of the Lord are right, and the just shall walk in them... <note>Hosea 14:10</note>
Happy is the portion of the righteous who know the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, and see how much hidden wisdom exists in all His portions. Come and see: the seal of "Another Matter" <note>original: *Davar Acher*, a common euphemism for evil or idolatry</note> rose up through mercy and love that is never separated from its radiance, and the seal and the embrace and the radiance of the Crown <note>term: *Keter* - the highest of the ten Sephirot or divine emanations</note> stands before Him; He opens it and sees the mystery when it is opened. His mate opens with Him. Below is Kindness <note>term: *Chesed* - the Sephirah of expansive love</note>, and He spreads over them, and the established trunks emerge above, and the branches spread out and gather to become "this" below. And it enriches itself with wisdom high above until they couple as one, and they join with one another. The matter revealed to them is that it is Kindness; it is certainly He. For He joined them as one—the **Yod** with the **He** <note>note: the first two letters of the Tetragrammaton, representing the union of Wisdom and Understanding</note> rose up. This union of theirs depends on His kindness. In the "Constellation" <note>term: *Mazal* - here referring to the divine influence flowing from the beard of the Ancient of Days</note> that accompanies it, their union and their love are never separated. The **Yod** is tied to the **He**, and the **He** is tied to the **Vav**, and the **Vav** is tied to the [final] **He**, and the **He** is tied to everything, and all is one knot and one matter, never separating from one another.

As it were, we see that [sin] causes a separation, as if the world were destroyed, and it is called the "uncovering of the nakedness" of all. But in the time to come, the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to return the Divine Presence <note>term: *Shekhinah* - the feminine indwelling presence of God</note> to her place, and everything will be found in a single union. As it is written:
> On that day the Lord shall be one and His name one. <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>
And it is a wonder, for this is not Kindness. Those who gave life to the world caused it to be that "One" is not found, for the Matronita <note>term: *Matronita* - the Noble Lady or Queen, representing the Shekhinah</note> is distanced from the King, and she is not found in union for the supernal unity. She is distanced from the King and he does not open to her, because the King without the Matronita is not crowned with his crowns of joy as he was previously when he joined with the Matronita, who crowned him with many crowns and many lights, and placed holy crowns upon him. As it is written: "Comfort and mercy in death." When Solomon sinned and decreed to join with the Matronita, he then crowned Him for the supernal unity as is fitting. But when the King is not found with the Matronita, then the supernal Life-Force takes her crowns. And from then on, the shame of the walls is hidden and they are not found in one knot. As it were, "One" is not found.

But when the Matronita returns to the place of the Palace <note>term: *Heikhal*</note> and the King joins with her in one union, then everything will be joined as one without separation. And regarding this it is written: "On that day the Lord shall be one and His name one." "On that day"—at the time the Matronita returns to her Palace, then everything is found to be one without separation, and then:
> And saviors shall ascend Mount Zion to judge [the mount of Esau]... <note>Obadiah 1:21</note>
As we have learned, Rabbi Shimon said: This is the restoration of the Matronita in her garments to her Palace, until the kingdom of Esau is judged and takes the vengeance of the blow that caused all of this. Afterward, you shall see the King, and there will be great joy. This is what is written:
> And saviors shall ascend Mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau <note>ibid.</note>
first. And afterward: **and the kingdom shall be the Lord's**. See, this "kingdom" is the Matronita; this is what is written: "and the kingdom shall be the Lord's." And after they couple as one, what is written?
> And the Lord shall be King over all the earth; on that day the Lord shall be one and His name one. <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>

---

**The nakedness** of your father’s brother you shall not uncover—and you shall walk in Judah, which is Israel below. And your father-in-law’s sister, this is Jerusalem below. For your laws, they will protect Israel among the nations, and it will be destroyed... <note>The text here becomes highly elliptical and symbolic</note> and we strengthened the Levites... and all is in the drifting of this world, and He troubled them... as we established: "Your friend and your father’s friend do not forsake" <note>Proverbs 27:10</note>—this refers to the King. For Rabbi Shimon said, Rabbi Yehuda said: "My brother lives, my friend lives, my friend lives"—why such mercy? Even so, let that matter never be removed, and He is called the "Friend of All." "Your friend and your father’s friend do not forsake," for the brother and friend of the matter... so that their love shall never depart from here.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**After the Death**<-

Because of this, regarding those things that are hidden, come and see: they come with known engravings <note>original: *reshimin*, markings or impressions</note> and are sealed in mercy, except for the righteous of truth who are the pillars of the world. Rabbi Shimon said: Do not wonder that it is not only above; come and see that the twenty-two letters <note>The Hebrew alphabet</note> that are engraved in the whiteness <note>The white fire/parchment of the Torah</note> are all explained within these ten Names. Each and every Name takes hold of these twenty-two; Crown <term>Keter: the highest Sephirah</term> and Kingdom <term>Malchut: the lowest Sephirah</term> are all engraved and hang in a known way. Because of this, the holy support is gathered in these twenty-two, and all these Names are the strength to establish the world from those letters, so that one may be included in the other. And upon His Holy Name they engrave Him with other letters so they may be gathered into one another, until they are all bound as one.

And whoever desires to know the engravings of the Holy Names should know those letters that are hinted at in every Crown <note>Keter</note>; by this, he shall know and be established in all of them. This is their engraving in all those letters that are hinted at and known in every Crown that explains the world that is winked at <note>hinted at through subtle gestures</note>, and thus it ascends. Then the companions engrave them <insert>variant reading: and to gather them, they engrave them</insert>, and it is good, for every Crown strengthens its fellow letters, as we have established. Happy are those who labor only in the letters hinted at therein, for they are all known to the companions. Thus we have established: happy are the righteous in this world and the world to come, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, honors them and reveals to them the higher secrets <note>original: *razei ila'in*</note> of His Holy Name, which He does not reveal to the holy ones above <note>The angels</note>.

And how was Moses able to be crowned among the holy ones <note>the angels in the cloud</note> when they all could not approach him together, [he being] precious and like coals of silence? Such fear! Who was it that allowed Moses to stand among them? It was only the merit of the Torah that he held; for anyone who toils in it, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is with him to know His Holy Name <insert>variant reading: His Holy Names</insert>, both hidden and revealed in each one as is fitting. Then he cleaves and knows more than all the children of the world.

Come and see: when Moses ascended the precious cloud among the holy ones, a certain angel met him, as the companions established, and they were flaming and blowing sweetly. And so he sought to hide him in the hidden place, and the angel of fire <insert>variant reading: the threshing floor</insert> hid his blood. Then Moses remembered the Holy Name that was engraved in the desire of the letters, and he was shaken and trembled until Moses ascended among them. Thus, for each and every one, his portion is merited, and we have established these words.

Come and see: in the "Arrangements of the Matronita" <term>The Shekhinah or Divine Presence</term> we have established that these "nakednesses" <note>forbidden sexual relations</note> are those that shall not be revealed, and are coverings. There it is written: "A priest, the daughter of a priest," for the world is protected by them, and they are the foundation of the world, as we have established. And whoever reveals one "nakedness" from among them, woe to him, woe to his soul! For by this he reveals other nakednesses. The matter is concluded like the translation <note>The Aramaic Targum</note> of "passing over the leavened for the white": do not covet your neighbor's wife, because it is foul, and all of them. And one who unites with another below, as if in fear, and passes over the whiteness entirely.

The beast of the word <note>the "living creature" or *Chayah*</note> was carved for him, standing before the crushing. And when he sees the reception of deeds in the generation of the King. Rabbi Yose said: Prepare everyone who sins and is separated; however, the first strength is removed from him and he is greatly weakened. Woe to him, he does not ascend to repentance <note>Teshuvah</note> and it does not benefit him.

If so, how did David not separate from Bathsheba and the Crown? He said to him: Bathsheba was his, and it was known before the Holy One, Blessed be He, that Bathsheba was destined for David from the day the world was created. What then delayed him? That he killed her husband <note>Uriah</note> who saw his portion, and on that day he killed others. In mercy he searched, for it was not yet the time for the Crown. David came and killed his generation, and for David the hour was pressed before the Holy One, Blessed be He, to show him and to act thus. Afterward, it was counted as repentance for David. For the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to unite David to establish for him the supernal holy kingdom, and in this, He turned to David, He turned.

Come and see: Rabbi Yose said, what is meant by that which is written: "Wait for the Lord" <note>original: *Chaki Hashem*</note>? "For the Lord" <note>original: *L'chi Hashem*</note> is destined to give a good reward to the righteous in the time to come. So too, the Lord is destined to exact punishment from the wicked in the time to come, as it is written: "Thus are the transgressors," etc. It is written "Wait for the Lord" and it is written "Go, eat the bread of mercy" regarding the King.

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the mystical implications of human conduct, specifically focusing on the laws of purity and their cosmic resonance. It follows the previous discussions in Parashat Acharei Mot regarding the sanctuary and the priesthood.</meta>

# After the Death (Acharei Mot)

The beloved [Creator] acts with the Attribute of Mercy, like a general of the people who subdues the Attribute of Judgment. For we have learned: Samael <note>The name of the primary accusing angel/Satan</note> is full of the names "Lord God" <note>original: YHVH Elohim</note>. If they [humanity] merit, it is "Lord" [Mercy]; if they do not merit, it is "God" [Judgment]. Rabbi Shimon said: The wicked create a blemish above. What is this blemish? It is exactly as we have established and as has been stated. We learned that it is written: *And to a woman in her menstrual uncleanness you shall not approach to uncover her nakedness.* <note>Leviticus 18:19</note> Rabbi Yehuda taught: The way of the pious is that all their children are pious, for the silver crown <note>The Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> dwells among them. This is not the case in other generations. Because of this, these matters are explained but not spread abroad. In other generations it is not so, and at times the generations of the world are not [worthy], and then to reveal [these secrets] to those who know, they are afraid. When Rabbi Shimon would speak the secret of this verse, all his pores would flow with tears like springs, and all the words they spoke were filled with tears in their eyes. He revealed [the secrets] just as it is written: *Mouth to mouth I speak with him, clearly and not in riddles.* <note>Numbers 12:8</note>

For once Rabbi Isaac asked: He said, a quarrelsome egg <margin>(variant: for a quarrel)</margin> that comes out of the smoothness of the womb <margin>(variant: and it stinks)</margin> like a lyre, and it split into four sides. Two kings from the simple [level], one king and one firmament in the firmament <margin>(variant: like a humble appearance)</margin> for a long time. Rabbi Abba said: You have performed a holy service before the Holy Degree, and it is written: *Mouth to mouth I speak with him.* Heaven forbid that before the egg is split, you should be removed from the world. And so it was in the generation of Rabbi Shimon. We learned: In the days of Rabbi Hezekiah, he said: When [the secret] is gathered in, open your mouth and let your words shine. After Rabbi Shimon passed away, they used to say: *Do not let your mouth bring your flesh into sin.* <note>Ecclesiastes 5:5</note>

It is taught: Rabbi Shimon said: By the life of the world's pillars, I look out, as it is written: *All his generations shall not come to anger before their Master.* We learned: When harsh judgments are awakened below in the world, here it is written: *The secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him* <margin>(variant: and in the secret) (variant: and the fools of the generation)</margin>. "Holy" is said here, and it is necessary to reveal that it goes to this place to ascend. For we have learned: At the time when Judgment is strong above, it is awakened because of the sinners of the world. It [the Accuser] surrounds and joins with the Female <note>The Shekhinah</note>, and she is diminished. At that time, the Male <note>The Holy One, blessed be He</note> separates from her as if in fear and ascends, and she is called "unclean" <term>Mesaba (Unclean): A state of spiritual displacement where the Divine Presence cannot receive the flow of blessing</term>. And it is not for the Male to approach her, like this suffering woman. The Voice is removed, like a blind man who fears to look. Trembling and crowns and five types of uncleanness descend to the world, which are drawn from the Crown of Harsh Judgment. And seven great crowns from their side are divided like females and cling to them. Woe to the one who approaches this [impurity]! For whoever approaches this shows a blemish above. For through this sin, a strong jealousy is awakened above. They [the forces of impurity] are profaned and they enter a place where they should not be, to join with the Female. And when they approach, the Male leaves, and the Female ascends. The secret of the hair and the nail are hateful, and then judgments begin to be appeased in the world. And they will all be found [guilty], for *you have defiled the sanctuary of the Lord.* The sanctuary of the Lord is defiled by the sins of human beings.

We learned: What is written: *And a wall shall be between you and the trembling*? Four crowns of uncleanness are prepared against the Female when he joins with her in darkness. And four crowns and four types <margin>(variant: judgments)</margin> are awakened above, and four crowns below. The secret of the hair and the nails are hateful, and then judgments are awakened in all of them. And we learned: When the woman seeks to be purified, in the manner explained, the Voice from the cave of the Rabbi intends to strengthen the [removal of] uncleanness and to count the counting [of the seven clean days]. And all that filth <term>Zuhama (Filth): The spiritual residue of the "Other Side" or evil inclination</term> which is in this [state], in the vision of the Kingdom, the side of the nails will be awakened. And she raises her Master and her children. Therefore, they need a straight path and a time to pass them away entirely, so they do not awaken bitterness in the world. For we have learned: A person should not seek to take evil portions, for we have learned: Five and four hundred and five types of evil are drawn to that filth of the surroundings. It is taught: It is strong, and all of them are awakened in that filth of the nails. And they pass by and see that one must pass over them with the sharpness of a knife <note>A metaphor for the rigorous separation of purity from impurity</note>, so that they do not hang upon them and they can pass them away.

## After the Death

->After the Death<-

...as a vision of the time of Kindness <note>Hebrew: *Chesed*</note>, and the judgments are subdued and found there. And that [accuser] passes by, and he [the priest] strikes and subdues him. Thus said Rabbi Shimon: <term>The Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>The standard rabbinic title for God</note> said, **"Bring it to Me for atonement"** <note>A famous Talmudic phrase where God asks Israel to bring a sacrifice to atone, as it were, for His own act of diminishing the moon</note>. This is certainly so that the bitterness shall pass and be sweetened. Whoever seeks "upon Me" <note>Hebrew: *Alai*</note>, as it is written: "Seraphim stood above Him," and it is further written: "In the midst of the festivals, unto the Lord," for they bring him into the chamber. That which is below, belonging to the Matron <note>The *Matronita* or *Shekhinah*, the Divine Presence in its feminine aspect</note>, also here: "Bring it to Me for atonement"—literally "upon Me"—so that it may be sweetened and pass away, and the serpent shall not be found in the place of the surroundings. And why? Because of the teaching that pushes away and lifts up words that are not needed. And because of this, it is written: "And he shall not sin," so that the joy shall not be approached [by evil]. Blessed is the generation that has this son, and see how he surrounds him; blessed is his portion among the upper and lower beings. Concerning him it is written:
> Happy are you, O land, when your king is a free man (Ecclesiastes 10:17)

What is a "free man"? One who raises his head to the heights to explain words and does not fear, like one who is a free man and there is none to compel him. And he does not fear this "your king," who is the wicked one, the exchange of sickness, the exchange of wisdom. For when Rabbi Abba would announce, "Who is for you, Shimon?" they would run after him and say, "Blessed is the Lord!" Rabbi Shimon said: It is written, "The daily burnt offering of the Sabbath on its Sabbath," and "The daily burnt offering of the festival on its festival." Why all this? Rather, it is all one ascending level, the joy of the bride and the sweetness of one to the other. This is found when the <term>Ancient Holy One</term> <note>Aramaic: *Atika Kadisha*, referring to the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note> is revealed, and then there is the sweetness of all and the rectifications. It is written:
> A Psalm, a song for the Sabbath day (Psalms 92:1)

Literally "for the Sabbath day"—the Sabbath that <term>The Holy One, Blessed be He</term> finds; then joy is found and the gift is increased, for the Ancient One is revealed and the union is prepared. So too here, as one, the moon is established, for the sun is with her in the joy of the light of the Ancient One above. Because of this, this offering was above, so that everything would be sweetened and joy would be found in the world. And regarding "Bring it to Me for atonement," the word is precise. Three times it is written: "The burnt offering of the Sabbath on its Sabbath, besides the daily burnt offering," for one must intend to go higher and higher, more than on other days. And regarding **"besides the daily burnt offering,"** it is precise. We have learned: It is written of Hannah, "And she prayed *upon* the Lord"—the word "upon" <note>Hebrew: *Al*</note> is precise. For children depend upon the <term>Holy Constellation</term> <note>Aramaic: *Mazla Kadisha*, referring to the flow of divine influence from the highest source</note>, as we have established. And you have no word in the Torah, even the smallest, that does not hint at Higher Wisdom, and from it hang mounds upon mounds of secrets of Higher Wisdom. And this is the meaning of "his locks are wavy" <note>Song of Songs 5:11; the Hebrew word for wavy, *taltalim*, is read as "mounds" of laws</note>. Rabbi Yose said: I will prove this wisdom to you; go out, sit, and read this verse which is written:
> Cast your burden upon the Lord (Psalms 55:23)

The word **"upon"** is precise, for the appointments depend on the <term>Constellation</term> <note>The source of destiny/influence</note>. Rabbi Yehuda would read **"upon"** in the verse:
> For this let every godly man pray to You in a time of finding (Psalms 32:6)

**"For this"** <note>Hebrew: *Al Zot*</note> certainly refers to the "time of finding." We have established that "a time of finding" is as it is written:
> Seek the Lord while He may be found, call upon Him while He is near (Isaiah 55:6)

This is the "time of finding," at the hour when the lights shine and are found, and the kindnesses are sufficient and bless everything. "Only in the flood of great waters"—who is the "flood of great waters"? This is the Ancient One, the springs and the crowns from which they suckle, and from which one merits to draw near and ascend there. "To him they shall not reach"—for they do not merit it and are not able. Rabbi Yitzhak said: It is written, "My sister, my bride..." I seek a seal. Blessed are the righteous, for how many upper hidden treasures are hidden for them in this world! The Holy One, Blessed be He, delights in them in the worlds, as we have established. And it was said: Rabbi Hezekiah said, we find:
> No eye has seen a God besides You, who acts for those who wait for Him (Isaiah 64:3)

It should say **"He shall act"** <note>future tense</note>, but rather "He acts" <note>present/continuous</note> certainly; this is "He shall add fifteen years to your days." And this is "And she prayed *upon* the Lord"—it is all one. Blessed is the portion of the righteous in this world and in the world to come.

-> # Portion of "You Shall Be Holy" <-

**And the Lord spoke** to Moses, saying: Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy. <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> <note>The son of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, a primary figure in the Zohar</note> opened the discussion: "Do not be like a horse or a mule, without understanding..." <note>Psalm 32:9</note>. Yet they all remain asleep, wrapped in their own garments <insert>variant reading: in their booths</insert>. Woe to them, woe for their shame! For the Torah, as it honors itself, says: "Whoever is simple, let him turn in here; as for him who lacks heart, she says to him..." <note>Proverbs 9:4/16</note>. What does "lacks heart" mean? It refers to one who has no faith. For whoever does not labor in the Torah has no faith within him and is flawed in everything. "She says to him"—from here we learn the severity of the punishment for all his sins. What is the meaning of "and she says"? It is to include and strengthen the Supernal Torah, which calls him "lacking heart," flawed in faith. For so we have learned: anyone who does not labor in the Torah is lacking, and one should not draw near to him or even perform his burial. How much more so for one who delves deeply into the Torah yet lacks faith. And our Rabbis taught: we have learned that any man who walks on the way and does not have words of Torah with him forfeits his life. How much more so one who joins on the way with someone who does not respect the glory of his Master or his own glory, and does not care for his own shame. Rabbi Judah said: It is a grave matter for one who does not care for his shame—how can he twist the branch of the henna <note>meaning: how can he corrupt his own roots or essence?</note>. To Master Rabbi Eleazar, this was an addition to the generation, and below it is a word, etc. And regarding what is written, "Do not be like a horse or a mule, without understanding": Happy are the righteous who labor in the Torah and know the way, etc., for the sake of the name of the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu" — the standard Zoharic name for God</note>, and they sanctify themselves with the holiness of the King. They are praised as "holy ones," for it is said: "Sanctify yourselves and be holy" in everything. Because of this, they draw down the spirit of holiness from above. Their bodies are like a ledger of the world; they are all righteous of truth and are considered children of the King, like holy ones. Woe to those who are weighed in the balance and found wanting, the wicked who are all hypocrites and whose deeds are hypocritical. Because of this, they give their children a face of <term>Impurity</term> <note>original: "Mesavuta" — spiritual defilement</note>. "Do not be like a horse or a mule"—who do not recognize the times <insert>variant reading: who are silent</insert> regarding everything. So it is written here "without understanding," and it is written there: "The dogs are greedy, they never know satiety; and they are shepherds who cannot understand" <note>Isaiah 56:11</note>. # Holy Ones
"You shall be..." Rabbi Isaac opened with the verse:
> Ah, land of the buzzing of wings, etc. <note>Isaiah 18:1</note>

Is it because of the "land of the buzzing of wings" that a rebuke is found in it, as it is written, "Ah, land of the buzzing of wings"? Rather, Rabbi Isaac said: At the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world and desired to reveal the deep things out of the hidden, and light out of darkness, they were included one within the other. And because of this, light emerged from darkness, and from the hidden, the deep emerged and was revealed; one emerged from the other. From good, evil emerges, and from Mercy <term>Rachamim: the divine attribute of compassion</term> emerges Judgment <term>Din: the divine attribute of strict justice</term>, and they are all revealed one within the other. The Good Inclination and the Evil Inclination, the Right and the Left. Israel and the other nations, white and black <note>original: "chivvar ve-uchma," referring to the symbolic colors of mercy and judgment</note>, and everything is dependent one upon the other. It was taught: Rabbi Isaac said in the name of Rabbi Judah: The whole world was only brought into being through a single binding of smoke <margin>(It seems to me: of smoke)</margin> in a knot. And when the world is judged with Judgment, it is judged as it is included within Mercy. If it were not so, the world could not stand for even a single moment. And what have we established regarding these matters? As it is written:
> For when Your judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness <note>Isaiah 26:9</note>

And at those times when Judgment hangs over the world and Righteousness <term>Tzedek: often associated with the Shekhinah or the feminine divine presence</term> is crowned, many "masters of wings" <note>Angelic or spiritual forces</note> are awakened toward her. Masters of harsh judgment who rise in the world spread their wings from this side and from that side to spread <margin>(It seems to me: to block/close)</margin> over the world. Then the wings are awakened to spread over them and to gaze with a harsh spirit, and they circle the world to do harm. Then it is written: "Ah, land of the buzzing of wings." Rabbi Judah said: The world's inhabitants are caught in sin, except for those who are truly righteous. And because of this, as it were, it is found that if one comes to be purified, they assist him; if one comes to be defiled, they open the way for him, as we have established. Rabbi Yose was walking on the road and Rabbi Hiyya met him. He said to him: Surely the companions have established what is written regarding the house of Eli:
> The iniquity of Eli’s house shall never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering <note>1 Samuel 3:14</note>

By sacrifice and offering it is not atoned, but it is atoned by the words of Torah. Why? Because the words of Torah rise above all the sacrifices in the world, as we have established, for it is written:
> This is the law <term>Torah</term> of the burnt offering, of the grain offering, of the sin offering, of the guilt offering, of the ordination offering, and of the sacrifice of well-being <note>Leviticus 7:37</note>

The Torah corresponds to all the sacrifices in the world. He said to him: It is certainly so, for anyone who exerts himself in the Torah—even if a decree of punishment was issued against him from above—it is better for him than all sacrifices and burnt offerings, and that punishment is torn up. Because they know that the Master, the Holy One, blessed be He, is appeased by it. And come and see: a person is never truly purified except through the words of Torah. Therefore, the words of Torah do not receive impurity, because they stand to purify those who are impure. And piety is found in the Torah, as it is written:
> It will be a cure for your body and a tonic for your bones <note>Proverbs 3:8</note>

And it is written:
> The fear of the Lord prolongs life <note>Proverbs 10:27</note>

Similarly, it is found in the Torah, as it is written:
> The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever <note>Psalms 19:10</note>

What is "enduring forever"? That it stands constantly in its purity and is never removed from him. He said to him: "The fear of the Lord" is written, not "Torah." He replied: It is certainly so, for the Torah emerges from Strength <term>Gevurah: the attribute of power/judgment</term>. He said to him: And generally it emerges from here, as it is written:
> The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord <note>Psalms 111:10</note>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Whoever strives for the Torah here below is subsequently sanctified, as it is written: *You shall be holy* <note>Leviticus 19:2</note>. It does not say "You were holy," but *You shall be*—meaning you shall certainly become so. Happy are the people of Israel and their Sanctuary, as it is written:
> *And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation...* (Exodus 19:6).

There are three levels of holiness: the holiness of the Torah, which is a holiness that rises above all other sanctities; and the holiness of the Higher Wisdom <term>Hokhmah: the primordial flash of divine intuition</term>, which is hidden above all. He said to him: Is there Torah without Wisdom? Certainly, Wisdom without Torah and Torah without Wisdom are as one single degree; they are all one. However, the Torah is found within the Higher Wisdom; it stands within it and is planted all around it on every side. While they were walking, they encountered a man at a crossroads <margin>variant: at a collection of stalls</margin> riding on his horse, reaching out his hands to a branch of a tree. Rabbi Yose said: This is what is written, *Sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy* <note>Leviticus 11:44</note>. If a person sanctifies themselves from below, they are sanctified from Above. This is the meaning of: *You shall be holy, for I, the Lord, am holy.*

**Rabbi Habiba taught:** This entire Torah portion is the "Seal of Truth" of the Body <note>referring to the central importance of the laws in Leviticus 19 to the spiritual structure of the human form</note>. Within this portion, the highest mysteries of the Torah are arranged. Within the Ten Utterances <note>The Ten Commandments</note>, their decrees, branches, and higher commandments, every single word in this portion is suspended. Rabbi Abba said: Why are the portion regarding forbidden sexual relations <term>Arayot</term> and the portion of *You shall be holy* placed next to one another? It was taught thus: anyone who guards themselves from these forbidden relations is certainly made holy. Here, one is to be sanctified with the holiness of their Master. And the colleagues have already awakened this discussion: When is the proper time for a person to be sanctified? Come and see: one must sanctify themselves according to the will of their Master so that they are not led astray; this is from midnight onwards, or exactly at midnight. For at that hour, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, is found in the Garden of Eden and the Higher Holiness is awakened. That is the time to be sanctified. This applies to all Torah scholars who know the ways of the Torah; midnight is their time to rise and labor in the Torah, to bond with it so as to draw a holy soul from the Holy King. The inclusion of the soul through the desire of all is found in their union at that hour, to bring forth the will of acceptance, as it is written:
> *You are children to the Lord your God* (Deuteronomy 14:1).

And why are they called "holy"? Because it is written: *You shall be holy, for I, the Lord, am holy.* And it is written:
> *And he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in its season...* (Psalms 1:3).

**You shall be holy.** Rabbi Abba opened the discourse:
> *And who is like Your people Israel, one nation on the earth?* (2 Samuel 7:23).

Come and see: among all the nations of the world, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, desired none but Israel alone. He made them "one nation" and called them "one nation" after His own Name. He crowned them with many crowns through many commandments. Because of this, the *Tefillin* <note>phylacteries</note> of the head and the *Tefillin* of the arm are worn to crown a person in the likeness of the Supernal realm. Thus, a person is found to be complete in everything; at that moment, when a person is crowned by them and sanctified by them, they are made complete and called **One** <term>Echad</term>. For one is not called "One" unless they are complete. One who is flawed is not called "One." Therefore, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, is called "One" in the perfection of all—in the perfection of Wisdom and the perfection of the Community of Israel <term>Knesset Yisrael: the mystical personification of the people and the Shekhinah</term>. For this reason, Israel below are called "One." Furthermore, when a person wears *Tefillin* and wraps themselves in the garment of the commandment <note>the Tallit or prayer shawl</note>, they are then crowned with holy crowns in the likeness of the Supernal realm and are called "One." Because of this, let the "one" come and occupy themselves with the "One." The Holy One, who is One, occupies Himself with the one [Israel]. For a King only occupies Himself with that which is fitting for Him. Thus it is written:
> *But He is at one, and who can turn Him?* (Job 23:13).

The Holy One, Blessed Be He, is only found within "One." Afterwards, He returns to seek out the one who participates in the Higher Holiness to become one. Then He dwells within this person and not within another. And when is a person called "One"? At the time they are sanctified with the higher sanctities <margin>variant: crowns</margin>. And come and see: at the time a person is called "One," at the time they are sanctified...

# Holy Ones

## Main Text (Zohar)

When a person is found in a union of male and female and directs their intention toward holiness as is proper, then that person is considered "complete" and is called **One** <note>Hebrew: *Echad*. In Jewish mysticism, unity is a divine attribute; human union mirrors the unity of God</note> without reservation. For this reason, a man must gladden his wife at that hour, to prepare her with a single will alongside him. Both of them should intend as one toward that King <note>The Holy One, Blessed be He</note>. And when both are found as one, then everything is one in soul and in body. In soul, to cleave to one another in a single will; and in body, as we have learned: a man who is not both male and female <note>i.e., unmarried or not in union</note> is only "half a body" and is not called "one." 

But when male and female are found together, then they are made into one body. It follows that they are one soul and one body, and such a person is called **One**. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, dwells within that "one" and brings forth a spirit of holiness into that "one." And these are called the children of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it has been said. And because of this, the verse says: **"You shall be holy, for I, the Lord, am holy"** <note>Leviticus 19:2</note>. Happy are the people of Israel, for the Holy One did not establish this matter in any other place but in Himself, as it is written: "For I, the Lord, am holy," so that they may cleave to Him and not to another. Therefore: "You shall be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy."

## Commentary (Faithful Shepherd)

->**The Faithful Shepherd**<-
<note>The *Raya Mehemna* is a later layer of the Zohar, often attributed to the soul of Moses, focusing on the mystical reasons for the commandments.</note>

| [Column 2] | [Column 1] |
| :--- | :--- |
| **"A man, his mother and his father you shall revere..."** <note>Leviticus 19:3</note> and so on. "A man, his mother and his father you shall revere, and my Sabbaths you shall keep; I am the Lord." We have learned in this portion that all the commandments of the Torah regarding the obligation to father and mother are included here. Rabbi Yose also said: they are all one matter of obligation, for the verse equates the reverence for mother and father to the reverence for the Holy One, Blessed be He. Just as one is obligated to honor [God], so too [the parents]. And since a woman is not always in her own power <note>referring to a married woman's obligations to her husband</note>, the verse here mentions the mother before the father <note>In the Ten Commandments, the father is mentioned first; here, the mother is first to show equal status in reverence</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: What is written above? "You shall be holy." He said: all this is to sanctify oneself in union as one. From what source is there an extra reason for this holiness? From the honor due to them, as it says "his mother and his father you shall revere." Rabbi Yehuda said: the obligation of "his mother and his father you shall revere" is like that of the Sabbath. And the Rabbi began to explain the connection, for later it says "and my Sanctuary you shall revere." This is placed nearby to show that both are made as one. Here too, the mother is placed before the father, and elsewhere the father before the mother, to show that both are as one to cleave to Him. "And my Sabbaths you shall keep"—this commandment includes the laws of the Menstruant <note>Niddah</note> and all fears are established in one balance, as it is written: "And you shall keep the Sabbath for it is holy to you." And it is written: "Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it." Rather, one is for the "Father" and one is for the "Mother" <note>Referring to the mystical sefirot of Chokhmah and Binah</note>. It is written here: "A man, his mother and his father you shall revere and my Sabbaths you shall keep," and it is written there: "My Sabbaths you shall keep and my Sanctuary you shall revere." What is "my Sanctuary"? It is like the Temple. | "A man, his mother and his father you shall revere, and my Sabbaths you shall keep." This commandment is weighed equally, as it was said: the honor of father and mother is weighed against the honor of the Sabbath. This establishes the honor and shows the comparison, as the verse says (Proverbs 3:9): **"Honor the Lord with your wealth."** <note>The Hebrew word for "wealth" (Hon) is interpreted here through Gematria/numerology</note>. If you purify the soul, it rises to the count of ten, referring to all the matters of the Work of Creation. In every place, "the wise shall inherit honor," and the "wise" are those who possess the life of honor, which is nothing other than the Torah. Because you live by all the words of the Torah, that is its glory. And for these Sages of the Torah, who have acquired honor through wisdom—and not the fools of whom it is said "but fools carry away shame." For anyone who does not know the Torah is called a "fool," as it is written: **"A fool does not understand this,"** and "This" <note>Zot</note> is nothing other than the Torah, as it is written: **"And this is the Torah which Moses set."** The Faithful Shepherd said: Because I am weak, I have opened this portion with general principles of the commandments to provide a little help to strengthen you, the delicate Matron <note>The Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> of the Mishnah, to tend to your garden according to the commandment of this Crown <note>Keter</note>, which is the commandment to stand over you as a King above. Acquire honor for yourself, O King of the worlds, and see the Image <note>Diyukna</note>. For your Mishnah is entwined with praise, and the King acquires the camp of majesty in the worlds. Stand, Faithful Shepherd! He stood and raised his hands above and said: May it be Your will, Cause of Causes, You who are exalted above all heights until there is nothing above You, You are He! |

# Section: Kedoshim

## Main Text (The Zohar)

### Right Column
He opened his discourse and said: "Moreover, *My sanctuaries* <note>original: 'mikdashai'</note> refers to those who sanctify themselves at this time. This is in the same manner as the verse: *And from My sanctuary you shall begin* <note>Ezekiel 9:6</note>. Do not read it as 'from My sanctuary' but rather 'from My sanctified ones' <note>The Zohar often uses wordplay, changing vowels to alter the meaning from a physical building to holy people</note>. Just as there it refers to My sanctified ones, so too here it refers to My sanctified ones, who are 'fat and blood' <note>referring to the internal devotion of the person as a sacrifice</note>.

->**A man**<- *shall fear his mother and his father* <note>Leviticus 19:3</note>. Regarding this, it is written elsewhere: *But you who held fast* <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note> *to the Lord your God are all alive today.* These are the people of Israel who cleave to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the people are alive because they cleave to Him; they are bound together as one. Come and see: when a person sanctifies himself below, in the manner of the Fellowship <note>the circle of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> who sanctify themselves from Sabbath to Sabbath, it is a time when Divine Will is found and blessing is present. Then all are bound together as one, corresponding to the Sabbath, and the female of the dream <note>a mystical reference to the soul's state</note> is like the Sabbath.

And concerning this it is written: *A man shall fear his mother and his father*, for they are a single union like one body at the time they were commanded. *And My Sabbaths you shall keep*—these are prepared for the soul just like that body. Furthermore, *And My Sabbaths you shall keep* contains a secret: "My Sabbaths" is plural to indicate a union of two as one, to join together from Sabbath to Sabbath, as we have established.

As it is written: *To the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths* <note>Isaiah 56:4</note>. Who are these "eunuchs"? These are the companions of the Fellowship who restrain themselves <note>literally 'make themselves like eunuchs'</note> all other days of the week in order to labor in the Torah, and they wait from Sabbath to Sabbath. Here, *grace and they shall keep My Sabbaths*. Then, *and they choose that which I desire*. For this reason, *And My Sabbaths you shall keep* refers to the union of two, and not just the soul. *And My Sabbaths you shall keep* refers to the Assembly of Israel <note><term>Knesset Yisrael: the mystical personification of the Jewish people, often identified with the Shekhinah</term></note>, and everything is left bound one to the other. All of this is the portion of Israel.

<column-break/>

### Left Column
Rabbi Hiyya said: Always, from every ascent to this... <note>The text here becomes highly cryptic, dealing with the movement of the 'Will'</note> to step with desire, as it is written: *And he went for life.* And here, it is the language of the second unification to become one. It rises with strength to be inherited by this birth after it was covered in patience—one and not two, without end before you. And because of this, it was said then that these are the words to awaken in glory at first, and afterwards in glory as one. It comes to the children of Israel to stand over them, a well and for life, and living waters stepped around from this side to that side.

And in standing, they hand over these repetitions, but only after there is no more for this one in the "Desire of Israel." And the honor that gives him Wisdom <note><term>Chokhmah: the second Sefirah, representing intuitive flash or the 'seed' of thought</term></note> which includes the ten Sefirot <note><term>Sefirot: the ten divine attributes or emanations through which God interacts with the universe</term></note> from below to above, and they are seen in sanctifications. He pauses in faithfulness for honor, and in this they prepared to let the small be like the great, to succeed from every group. From them, Wisdom is a single bride, for all of them are on the right, and truly from below. And the Supernal Crown <note><term>Keter: the highest Sefirah, representing Divine Will</term></note> comes upon his head. There is nothing after your cloud, and no taste for the individual, but life above for the one, to sustain life in a prepared way, so that faithfulness may be within it.

And just as He is in all that is above this, and two, and life and life, so too life makes the world from it. Because he works in levels and colors without labor, without the burdens of the womb that are broken, all work of love is to be bound then and in everything. Then one says: *Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place* <note>Ezekiel 3:12</note>. He has a place in the manner of the evening, and twelve [is] the glory of honor for the wise of the Torah. One is obligated to treat it as a precious wine within, and Israel is to be sanctified in it in everything. So too the hidden daughter of greatness and the Kingdom <note><term>Malkhut: the final Sefirah, associated with the physical realm and the Shekhinah</term></note> to live in her. The daughter of honor is for the elder, and life is to perform the union. His sustenance is to the right, the commandments of counsel, and all to establish his words which are repeated by the hand of grace and counsel. Therefore, one says "Glory," and at the time of opening, "Glory" is for the wise and for the life within, for the honor of this world. And life he made immediately without any labor at all, and until he is over them all, to give life to his children, to strive in honor to repair the prayer <note>original: 'tzalota'</note>.

### Bottom Section
Of Wisdom and life for the lower honor, like atonements to arrange without then life; and life you shall hand over to me, over his words they cry out forever. And beneath, the rains go up and repeat to be acquired and arranged for the honor that goes, and for the honor of the one. And in this, let the joy of my feet step, and to make life in all His commandments, and to fill with strength in all the commandments that shall not be cut off, and in this—life.

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Kedoshim (Holiness), focusing on the spiritual consequences of neglecting the Torah and the distinction between serving God as a "son" versus a "servant." It maintains the mystical vocabulary of the Zohar, specifically regarding the emanations of the Divine.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Holiness<-

To Him, the King, he unifies Him and does not stray from faith. Regarding the verse we read, "neither rest nor change from the side of the commandments," one must act to turn aside the glory of the "hollow" <note>referring to the empty or demonic shells, the Kelipot</note> so that it does not belong to the "Other Side." For the Holy One, blessed be He, does not give His glory to another god. Those who despise and diminish the commandments are the wicked "people of the land" <note>term for those ignorant of Torah</note> who do not look upon the glory of the Torah. How can they say, "Hear our voice and have mercy on us," in all our prayers? The Voice of Life belongs to Him, and if one does not honor His glory by looking into the freedom found in my commandments and performing the service of the Master, how can he pray to Him? Except for one who hears from the Sages and acts, for it is a logical conclusion: he enters and hears. And despite all this, one who does not receive the Kingdom from His messengers, how shall he be detailed, and what is his counting?

It is written regarding freedom: "Moses received the Torah from Sinai and handed it down to Joshua." <note>A quote from Ethics of the Fathers 1:1</note> Here, the reception is quiet. And after the memory of all of them, so too one who receives the word of the commandment from the Scripture, it is supported and gathered. Through this reception, he is appointed. And one who receives can ascend and act with his eyes, as we established regarding the "Shema" and the "Reading" to ascend into the Torah of the Night. It is said that the Voice is like the voice of the Reading which releases the embrace, even though the commandment is gathered like a bond. We come from the side of the Reading, and it is released to ascend in its instruction. Thus, they are found gathered, unlike the people who have no transgression from the dwelling of the Torah. But the essence of the reading is the Voice, and it is written that there is no end to His power, and there is no King or Master over Him to bring out an answer in the instruction. He is the Cause of Causes, for where He is, there is no end to the gathering of the clarity of the Torah. May it be Your will that You do not move from the King and from my word, nor from my dwelling. And so, one who "kills himself" over the Torah <note>a metaphor for total devotion and self-sacrifice in study</note>, the Voice shall call to be sustained in him and not cease.

But one who does not labor in it to perform the service of the Sages, even if he performs the action, it is not the same. However, if he is faithful, he is obligated to let Him rule over all that is his. But one who does not labor in the Torah and does not listen to the Sages to hear from them the commandments to fulfill them—like a people who are supported but lack—he violates a <term>Prohibitive Commandment</term> <note>original: "Lo Ta'aseh" - one of the 365 "Thou shalt not" laws</note>. Such a person is considered like the nations of the world, acting like the people of <term>Samael</term> <note>The primary angelic figure of evil/prosecution in Jewish mysticism</note>. As it is said of them: "Fools carry away shame," for they do not wish to receive the Torah. Anyone who has no Torah in him has no glory, as it is said: **"The wise shall inherit glory"** <note>Proverbs 3:35</note>.

Despite all this, the masters of the Academy say that all "Glory" refers to the "Good" called thus, and in everything, he acts for the <term>Kingdom</term> <note>original: "Malchut" - the final Sephirah, representing Divine Sovereignty and the Shekhinah</note>. This is on the condition of not receiving a reward. But "Rest" is found in the Supernal Glory and Kindness. And if they wish to perform the service, it will be painful for him, except for Kindness, until he acts against his will. If he is willing and blessed, they do not coerce him. But if he does not wish to act, what is written of him? He is a rebel, and he does not "hear our voice," and they cause pain to the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often depicted as the feminine aspect of God</note>. But a servant who listens "on the condition of receiving a reward," if he does not perform the service of his Master's command, he is removed from the house.

One who was able to act for his son acts with Kindness. He said to him: "Holy Gathering, who is the one who studies but does not perform the service?" He is cursed. In the end, they mixed for him an evil mixture. This does not refer to Israel, who are called "Nadi" <note>noble/willing</note> of the trial that was abolished. This spirit is "and they mingled among the nations," and this caused the killing of Israel and the destruction of the Holy Temple. Because of this, we do not receive converts in the days of the Messiah, so they shall not have power.

Esau is already like a servant to Israel. You are the <term>Kingdom</term> to establish the "Good Servant" and the "Evil Servant" from the side of <term>Metatron</term> <note>The highest archangel, often called the "Prince of the Countenance"</note>. The Good Servant is the one who performs all that is to come. The Evil Servant is <term>Samael</term>. One whose portion is the Kingdom, he shall be a "Treasured Son." From the side of the "Son," he merits and inherits the Kingdom. And how does he inherit it? If he performs the service with Kindness and Heat <note>passion</note>, because the Kingdom is the "Left Hand of the King." Regarding this, it is said: "Why does your eye wink?" The portion of the servant is from the body, but the service to the King is the main business. Therefore, the "Gathering" <note>the community of Israel/Shekhinah</note> nurses from the Kindness. There is no separation there, for it is Truth. You shall inherit the Kindness of the Torah below, providing refreshment and rest, as our Rabbis taught: "Inheritance and Rest." The Torah is the Word, Wisdom is the Male, and Understanding is the Female. And so it is with all the commandments, for all who stand for the Torah shall have no lack.

## Main Text (Zohar)

...a closed and sealed garden. But a crown that is snatched away possesses no goodness. And so, whoever sees it and finds no goodness in it, finds neither reward nor death <note>Zohar III, 83a</note>. Because of this, his portion is not sweetened to grant life's reward in this world; yet in this portion, it is called the "portion of life" and is called "the World to Come." It is not called "reward" because life <note>original: כגוונא, "in the manner of"</note> consists of gifts. These are gifts given in joy to the receiver, not through distress, nor through speech, nor through action. It comes through a **holy union** <term>Zivug: a mystical coupling of divine energies</term> to cleave to Him. It is known that he is a "son of gifts" from the fullness of his river that never ceases—not preceding you so as to receive it through action, nor through speech, nor through deed. He spoke his Will from the beginning, and you and your hidden matters are the teachings of the Elders that never cease; all delights ascended one to another and they sported in grace, etc. Rabbi Shimon opened and said: Despite all this, a son is nourished by the Prophet; all life that draws near is pure, as it is written:
> **Honor your father and your mother** <note>Exodus 20:12</note>
This comes to include your elder brother. And even if all your sides are upon you, mixed in joy and peace, and there is no "monkey" <note>likely a reference to the "ape-like" quality of the physical body compared to the soul</note> to the First Man at all; surround and honor the Will in peace. This is the flow of the King's river; in every place there are blessings and supports for your life, of good and evil... for it is good, and the river of his seal is good. And we have learned: the King shall be established in his foundation to be a "son of the house" for prayer. These are from the side of the **Kingdom** <term>Malkhut: the feminine divine presence</term> of its creation. So too from the side of **Understanding** <term>Binah: the divine mother</term> of its creation. Now you are a "son of the house" from the side of the portion of Kingdom, to give birth to a "son of the house" from the side of the Son of God <note>original: Ben Yah</note>, the endurance of **Beauty** <term>Tiferet: the central divine male principle</term>. And all your words and the vision of the Prophet are for you because you have partnered in the world and in rest to bind the Holy One, and they agree with the King in his place above and over Israel below. And because of this, all the silver shall be judged... and they are called "His," for the priest and prophet dwell in their portion. Through this, the commandment of your life is fulfilled, a commandment for Israel in the future for the King, the Holy One, Blessed be He. You shall surely set a King over you, and it shall be fulfilled in them: "And he was King in Jeshurun" at the beginning. And all shall be led after you, like lamps that are all led in the movement of greatness to spread over all **Lovingkindness** <term>Hesed</term>, because after his ascent you shall be crowned with him. The time of prayer is a crown over all, hidden and concealed within. And it emerges and spreads over all the **Sefirot** <term>Divine emanations</term> and arranges them for His sake—this one great, this one small, and this one intermediate. He increases them for their companions and chooses them, binding them and uniting them. Thus, He desires Lovingkindness, aiming for Israel in every commandment of His, and each one returns as is fitting for him... and the intermediate is bent toward the garden. You shall bind them in one bond to their Life in the Heavens, to make them all one body in spirit, to bless the Holy One, Blessed be He, to sanctify Him and bless Him in his degree through thought. Go in joy to exist thus, and benefit from the support upon you... until here.

**A man** shall fear his mother and his father, etc. <note>Leviticus 19:3</note>. This commandment to honor father and mother requires a person to elevate, to benefit, and to honor them just as a person must honor the Holy One, Blessed be He. From the side of the spirit—the scent of beauty and delight—the body is refined. A person must honor his father and his mother from the side of his body and for the delight of these two. For here, they are partners with the Holy One, Blessed be He; they make for him the body and the skin, and they are partners in the formation of those drops in awe and honor. In this manner, **three partners** <note>The Talmudic concept that God, the father, and the mother all contribute to a child's formation</note> are found above in the spirit of Man. The First Man—the "alphabet" of his body was from dust, but not from the dust of this place. Rather, it was from the dust of the Sanctuary above. **Father and Mother** <term>Abba and Imma: the divine archetypes of Wisdom and Understanding</term> established him, and the Supreme King partnered with them and arranged in him the "Nostrils of Life," and he was created. In this manner, they are found above and below. Therefore, a person must fear the Holy One, Blessed be He, and fear his father and his mother. Just as the First Man had no one to protest against him... one checked and supported his liver, and a pure body was made... more than all those kings who ascended to the shadow. And when the holy body is created, the Supreme King arranges in that Righteous One all openings and partners with them and opens them above. For when they see him, help and delivery and piety are granted.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Kedoshim (Holy Ones)**<-

In this manner, the "Ape of Drinus" <note>A cryptic Zoharic reference to a lower, imitative spiritual force or a specific type of demon</note> is considered like their pot, full of flavor, because it emerged from the work of Samael <note>The primary figure of evil in Jewish mysticism</note> and his end. For he is the one who extended himself and diminished his own body, needing to commit adultery with the profane, like a mask or a book. As it is written: *And the Lord God made for Adam and for his wife garments of skin, and clothed them.* <note>Genesis 3:21</note> At that time, the Holy One, Blessed be He, made a <term>garment</term> <note>original: "nadik" - a rare term for a covering or mantle</note> like a cloak, not to be repaired from before or after. This was because of the shame and the time until Enoch came and abolished that sword, and Abel offered his sacrifice and incense from his silver. And so it is with all sins that are scrutinized from the beginning. Afterward, the Holy One, Blessed be He, prepares a place, and sides and vengeances are made at their end, and the body is prepared at the beginning. And because of the shame above and below, a person comes to the world and must fear the various "sides" and honor them as has been stated.

**Do** not turn to idols, and molten gods you shall not make for yourselves. <note>Leviticus 19:4</note> Rabbi Hiyya opened: "Do not turn to the harshness of this day," etc. "Do not turn"—and who is the day belonging to the King that we should not turn to? For it is written: *For His eyes are upon the ways of man.* <note>Job 34:21</note> And it is written: *Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? saith the Lord.* <note>Jeremiah 23:24</note> The conclusion of everything is that the Holy One, Blessed be He, observes all deeds and enters into judgment over all of them, whether good or bad; *God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.* <note>Ecclesiastes 12:14</note> And from this, He said, "Do not turn." Rather, so we have learned: every person must guard himself from his sins so that he does not sin before the Holy King. Come and see: everyone who commits a sin, 그 sin ascends and stands before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and says, "I am from the deed that so-and-so performed." And the Holy One, Blessed be He, keeps it before Him to gaze upon it every day, to remember him because of it. If he transgresses the words of the Torah, that transgression ascends before Him and says, "I am from the deeds he did," and the Holy One, Blessed be He, counts it, and it stands there to look at him and rebuke him. And this is certainly the Lord and the power over all of them... what is that which stands before Him? Come and see what is written: *Remove the transgression from your sight so you do not die,* to pass that sin from before Him so He does not look at it to rebuke him. And regarding this: "Do not turn to the harshness of this day," and to his mercy, and to his sin. Rabbi Yose said: and so from here it is implied, as it is written: *Your iniquity is marked before Me.* <note>Jeremiah 2:22</note>

Rabbi Yose the Younger came before Rabbi Shimon one day and found him sitting and expounding on what is written:
> And the man said: The woman whom You gave **with** me, she gave me of the tree, and I ate. <note>Genesis 3:12</note>
This implies that Adam and Eve were created as one and in one body. For it is written *whom You gave **with** me* and it is not written *whom You gave **to** me*. He said to him: If so, is it not written *I will make for you a helper as a counterpart*? <note>Genesis 2:18</note> And it is not written *before you*. He said to him: If it were written "before you," I would have said so, as it is written *whom You gave with me*. But "counterpart" is what is written. He said to him: But is it not written:
> And the Lord God said: It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a helper as his counterpart. <note>Genesis 2:18</note>
"I will make him" *now*? <note>Implying a new creation rather than a separation</note> He said to him: It is certainly so, that Adam was "alone" because he had no support from his female side, because she was in his sides <note>back-to-back</note> as we have established. And as for what is said, "I will make him a helper"—it is because it does not say "I will *create* for him a helper," since it is written *male and female He created them* <note>Genesis 1:27</note>, but "I will *make*" is written. And what does "I will make" mean? It implies to *prepare* or *fix*. For He cut her from his sides and prepared her with her adornments and brought her before him. And then Adam was found to be "by himself" <note>separated</note> and he had a support. 

And we have learned: the radiance of the First Man <note>Adam Ha-Kadmon</note> was from a supernal crown, a light that they lost. A radiance such that no creatures were able to look at it. And even Adam did not look at it until the time they ate and sinned, and their radiance [was diminished]. Then they looked at the "other side" <note>the realm of evil</note> and it was known to them to look there. And behold: *And Adam knew Eve his wife.* <note>Genesis 4:1</note> He "knew" in all ways; he knew in perfection; he knew to be acquainted with her and to look at her. And we have learned: tell a person there is no division in the "sawing" <note>the mystical separation of the male and female aspects</note> of wisdom, so that he does not come to evil thoughts and be uprooted from the matter.

## Main Text (Zohar)

...to another. And when Rabbi Shimon <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the central figure of the Zohar</note> would perform all these visions in the city, the people would follow after him and see the beautiful grace flowing from his eyes. He would say to his companions: "See that you do not turn away." For anyone who gazes into the Book of Wisdom at the time it is revealed will see a priestly thought <note>A holy, meditative spark</note> rising upon them. *Turn away my eyes from beholding vanity...* <note>Psalm 119:37</note> **and do not make for yourselves molten gods** <note>Leviticus 19:4</note>. This is literally according to his wisdom, at the time that evil thought rises. Those who are "secular" and "hollow" are called "molten" <note>A play on the Hebrew word *masekhah* (molten/mask), implying a lack of spiritual substance</note>.

**Do not turn to idols, and do not make for yourselves molten gods** <note>Leviticus 19:4</note>. Rabbi Zakkai said: It is forbidden for a person to gaze upon the "hollows" of the idolatrous nations, nor to focus one's intentions on them, nor to delight in them; one must not look at them at all, for it is forbidden for a person to look at that which causes one to go astray.

Rabbi Abba opened his discourse: **Turn to me and be gracious to me; give Your strength to Your servant** <note>Psalm 86:16</note>. "Turn to me and be gracious to me," etc. Did the Holy One, Blessed be He, not have any other beloved in the world besides David, that he should say "Turn to me and be gracious to me"? Rather, so we have learned: The Holy One, Blessed be He, has another "David" <note>A celestial archetype or the Sefirah of Malkhut/Kingship</note> who is appointed over many supernal hosts and guardians. And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to have mercy on the world, He gazes upon this one, and his face shines, and he illuminates the worlds and gives life to the worlds.

The beauty of this David shines to all the worlds, from the head and the skull that runs through the embroidery <note>A mystical description of the divine physiognomy</note> like the seven boundaries and the species found here. This is for the sake of establishing the great love to receive it. From his peacefulness and his love, he looks toward the Holy One, of whom it is said that His eyes are toward him to gaze upon him. Because his grace is beautiful in everything, as it says, *Your eyes are like the pools...* etc.

**Turn your eyes away from me** <note>Song of Songs 6:5</note>. For at the time those eyes gaze upon the Holy One, then the sparks of every side are awakened in His heart like a love for him. And in the peacefulness of that love, he says: "Turn your eyes away from me," for your eyes turn to the "Other Side" <note>The Sitra Achra, or realm of impurity</note> when they burn for Me with the heat of love. And regarding this, it is written of David: **He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and goodly to look upon** <note>1 Samuel 16:12</note>. And because David's gaze was beautiful and beloved by the Holy One, he sought to cleave to Him. David said, "Turn to me and be gracious to me," for he is like the "Righteousness" <note>Tzedek/Malkhut</note> that lacks its own blessing.

It is implied that he entered with Jacob into the Garden of Eden, which is the secret of the Holy Apple Orchard <note>A Zoharic term for the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note>. And how can the Garden of Eden enter into that? How great is the Garden of Eden in its capacity! How many holy radiances dwell upon it! Rather, the Holy One has another supernal, holy Garden, and in that Garden is His love, and He cleaves to it; it is guarded only for the Holy One alone to enter. And this is the "Holy Kindness" that is always present with the righteous. This was found in Jacob, to enter with him... he who laughs and lives and nursed from the Kindnesses.

And we have learned: This teaches that the Land of Israel was folded up beneath him <note>A famous Midrashic concept where the physical land shrinks to accommodate the righteous</note>. But how could the Land of Israel, which is four hundred parasangs by four hundred parasangs, be uprooted from its place to sit beneath him? Rather, the Holy One has another supernal, holy Land, and it is called the "Land of Israel." It is beneath the level of Jacob, who is holy upon it. And the Holy One grants kindness to Israel because of His love for them, to dwell with them, to remember them, and to protect them from everything—the portion of the "Land of the Living."

Come and see: It is forbidden for a person to gaze at the place where the Holy One dwells... and just as the Holy One desires the pious man to gaze upon Him, so he is distant from Him. And come and see: It is forbidden for a person to gaze at the rainbow, because it is the vision of the divine union <note>The rainbow represents the Sefirah of Yesod/Covenant</note>. It is forbidden for a person to gaze at the "Sign of the Covenant" <note>Circumcision</note> because it alludes to the "Righteous One of the World." It is forbidden for a person to gaze at the fingers of the Priests at the time they spread their hands <note>During the Priestly Blessing</note>, because the Glory of the King <note>The Shekhinah</note> rests upon them. To gaze upon that which is forbidden is a distance that should not be crossed. You shall not make for yourself a carved image.< It says, *I am the Lord your God,* in correspondence to >I am the Lord your God.< There is a hint here that you shall inherit merit in correspondence to >Honor your father and your mother.< And it says >You shall keep My Sabbaths< in correspondence to >Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy.< *You shall not swear by My name falsely* corresponds to >You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain.< *You shall not steal* corresponds to >You shall not steal.< *You shall not deal falsely nor lie to one another* corresponds to >You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.< *The adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death* corresponds to >You shall not commit adultery.< *You shall not stand idly by the blood of your neighbor* corresponds to >You shall not murder.< Thus they have established that the entire Torah is included in this portion. **Rabbi Hiyya** said: At first, it said "the Lord your God," "Remember the Sabbath," "You shall not murder," "You shall not commit adultery," "You shall not steal"—all in the singular tongue. But here it says "the Lord your God" [in the plural], "You shall keep My Sabbaths," "Do not turn to idols"—all in the plural tongue. However, we have learned that at the time Israel was found in the world [at Sinai], they were found before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "קב"ה" - the standard Hebrew/Aramaic reference to God</note> as all one, with one will <note>original: "רעותא" - mystical will or desire</note>, just as it was on the day they stood at Mount Sinai. Therefore, everything was said to them in the singular. Later, it is said in the plural because they were no longer found in that same unified will. **Rabbi Eleazar** was traveling to see **Rabbi Yose son of Lakonia**, his father-in-law, and **Rabbi Hiyya** and **Rabbi Yose** were with him. When they reached a certain field, they sat beneath a tree. **Rabbi Eleazar** said: Let each person say a word of Torah. **Rabbi Eleazar** opened and said: >You shall not go about as a talebearer among your people< and besides this, you shall not know. Even though they did not know the glory <note>original: "יקרא"</note> of the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> so well, they followed the calculations of their wisdom. Later, they saw many miracles and many acts of power, and the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> took them for His service.
