## Main Text (Zohar)

When a person's days arrive to depart from the world, the Holy One, blessed be He, divides his soul and gives him life and <term>Torah</term> <note>The Aramaic "Tor" here likely refers to the "order" or "boundary" of life</note>. **"The wages of a hired worker shall not remain with you all night."** <note>Leviticus 19:13</note> Come and see: it is written that a man who is impoverished is as if his soul and the souls of his household were taken from him. He is a staff <note>A support or branch</note> in its literal sense; the Holy One, blessed be He, [counts] his days and returns his deposit from that world. For all those <term>images</term> <note>Aramaic: *Babu'im* - spiritual reflections or shadows of a person's deeds</note> that emerge from him all that day, they all ascend before the Holy One and stand before Him. Afterward, his soul and the souls of the wise of his house ascend and stand within those images of his mouth. And then, even if he separates himself from the commandment for several days and several years, they are all uprooted from him and depart from him.

And come and see further: his soul does not ascend above. This is what Rabbi Abba said regarding those who cause distress to [workers] and wrong them. It was established: could this apply even if the worker is wealthy? The verse says, **"and to it he sets his soul,"** <note>Deuteronomy 24:15</note> which precisely includes every person, not just the poor. And this is what Rav Hamnuna the Elder used to do: when a worker finished his labor, he would give him his wages and say to him: "Take your reward that you deposited in my hand, take your deposit." Even with an animal or a donkey, he would say, "I do not wish to withhold the reward." He would say, "The animal is a deposit in your body, do not let it be deposited in my hand. How much more so the deposit of the soul." For the deposit of the soul should not be entrusted to anyone but the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written: **"Into Your hand I commit my spirit."** <note>Psalm 31:6</note> Rabbi Abba said: Blessed is the portion of the masters [of Torah]. He said to him: Even regarding the body it is written, **"The wages of a hired worker shall not remain with you all night,"** and it is written, **"the sun shall not go down upon it."** <note>Deuteronomy 24:15</note>

But come and see: day by day, if the day does not rule over it, the day ascends as a staff and lives for him, and He gives him his soul as one who completes that day. And because of this, **"on his day you shall give his reward, and the sun shall not go down upon it."** And that which is said, "shall not remain all night," is because his soul does not ascend, and that soul ascends and is reconciled with the Master of the House. As Rabbi Hiyya saw, he opened and said:
-> The verse of his crown <-

**"You shall not curse the deaf, nor put a stumbling block before the blind..."** <note>Leviticus 19:14</note> This verse is according to its literal meaning. But this entire section, we have learned from it many other hidden matters, and they all hang one upon the other. Come and see: one who curses his fellow, [the curse] ascends before Him and provokes him as if he shed his blood, as they have established. And this verse, that one should not be angry with him and curse him—that word ascends. There is no word that comes out of a person's mouth that does not have a voice, and every voice ascends above, and many "accusers" <note>Spiritual prosecutors</note> join with that voice until it ascends and awakens a place of great depth, as they have established. And many are awakened against that man because of the evil word that came out of his mouth.

And **"before the blind you shall not put a stumbling block"** is according to its literal meaning, and they established it as one who causes another to sin. And so too, one who strikes his adult son. **"Before the blind you shall not put..."** is like one who does not see the way and another speaks [misleadingly] to him. As we have learned, for it is written that the King of the World is hidden, and He says all these things, and this person transgresses. **"Before the blind you shall not put a stumbling block"** because it is written regarding his fellow in the World to Come. For we have learned: one who walks in the path of Torah in this world, and one who looks into the Torah as is proper, has a good portion forever in the World to Come. For that word of Torah that comes out of his mouth is a labor and a healing in the world, and it ascends above. And many holy angels join with that word, and it ascends as a crown and is crowned with a holy crown, and is washed in the river of the World to Come which flows and emerges from Eden. And then a supreme light is drawn and emerges, and that man is crowned with it every day, as we have said. But one who toils in the Torah and does not know how to labor in it in the path of truth and the path...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Holy Ones**<-

And all things ascend from the side of that word <note>The "word" refers to the speech or intent of a person</note>, and then the paths are clear and there is no one to be broken by them. Everything is similar to it, except for one who is rebuked and squeezed in the world and finds no place. Who is it that rebukes him? It is the one who turns him away from the straight path before Him.
> **"And you shall not put a stumbling block before the blind"** (Leviticus 19:14)
And because of this, it is written:
> **"But you shall fear your God; I am the Lord"** (ibid.)
One who walks in uprightness will not stray into other paths, and no one who rebukes him will be established against him. He is under the authority of his Master above, and he clings to Him like a tail <note>original: "k'gnubta" - an idiom for following closely or being attached</note>, and he knows every single word that ascends. The Holy One, Blessed Be He, rejoices in that word and receives it, planting it around that stream. These words then become active, traveling and encircling in sweetness, just as it was said, "it shall be constant." King David said:
> **"Teach me, O Lord, Your way; I will walk in Your truth"** (Psalms 86:11)
And it is written: "Lead me in a straight path because of those who lie in wait for me." Fortunate are those who know the paths of the Torah and exert themselves in it in an upright way. For those who wander, the paths of life are narrow above, for they have corrupted their ways. Because of this, it is written:
> **"The law of truth was in his mouth"** (Malachi 2:6)
Is there then a Torah that is not truth? Heaven forbid! Rather, it refers to those who say to another—one who does not know and is not truthful—a word that is the opposite, a word that is not truth. Because of this, it is written "the law of truth was in his mouth." Despite all this, one should humble himself <note>original: "makni leh" - to lower oneself</note> like a vessel to learn the words of Torah from every person, even from one who does not know as much, because through this he will be awakened in freedom and will come to learn from others who do know. Eventually, the Torah will be found in freedom through the path of truth. Come and see: a person should look at the Torah and the commandments in this world; even if he does not perform them for their own sake <note>term: "Lishmah" - performing a commandment purely for the love of God</note>, through doing them not for their own sake, he will eventually come to do them for their own sake. Rabbi Yose opened the verse following it:

<margin>31</margin> > **"You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment..."** (Leviticus 19:15)
"You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment" is understood according to its literal meaning. However, it has been said that this portion contains high and precious matters regarding the commandments of the Torah. This verse is understood from its conclusion, as it is written: **"In righteousness shall you judge your neighbor."** Come and see, there are levels here: "Justice" <note>Mishpat</note> and "Righteousness" <note>Tzedek</note>. What is the difference between this one and that one? Rabbi Rahumai said: This one is at ease and this one is sweetened by it. Any awakening of judgment that is not "Justice" <note>Mishpat</note> as one, has no mercy in it and no leniency. But the awakening of "Justice" <note>Mishpat</note> has mercy in it, and it can endure everything. As the verse says: "In righteousness shall you judge your neighbor." Why? Because "Righteousness" <note>Tzedek</note> alone is judgment, and it is not sufficient unless they are both as one in a single commandment. In this manner: "You shall not respect the person of the poor, nor honor the person of the mighty." Both come in a single commandment. With "Righteousness," could it be that everything is strictly according to its purity? The verse comes and says "you shall judge," for one must clarify them together, and one should not be found without the other. In this perfection of purity, why is all this? Because the Holy One, Blessed Be He, is present there. Therefore, one must strive to act below according to the pattern above; one acts exactly according to His pattern above. Come and see: The Holy One, Blessed Be He, sets up the Throne of Judgment at the hour when the judges sit. He prepares to establish the Throne of the Holy One, Blessed Be He. And what is the Throne? They are "Righteousness" and "Justice." This is the secret of:
> **"Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne"** (Psalms 89:15)
And one who judges a case must imagine himself sitting <note>gloss: meaning "to sit"</note> on the Throne of the King. If one of their faces is marred, the King's Throne is flawed. Then the Holy One, Blessed Be He, departs from the Throne of Judgment and does not stand by their judgment. Then the "old wine" <note>an idiom for harsh, stored-up judgment</note> is stirred up to rise, and the Lord says... and the Holy Spirit says: **"Be exalted, O God, above the heavens"** (Psalms 57:6).

## The Faithful Shepherd (Ra'aya Meheimna)

**"You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment... but in righteousness shall you judge your neighbor."** This commandment is to rebuke one's fellow, coming to strike him <note>metaphorically, with words of correction</note> with the presence of mercy toward him. So that anger is not stirred up within him, it is written: "For as the Lord does, so He rebukes." For the Holy One, Blessed Be He, acts and rebukes the one who comes to Him. A person should learn the delights of the Torah; the Holy One, Blessed Be He, when He comes to rebuke a man, He rebukes him with love, in secret, face to face. He heals him, turns to him, and does not rebuke him publicly to shame him.

## Main Text (Zohar)

Where does he return and listen to his will? First, he informs him in secret in order to reprove him and to awaken him so that the man does not sin against him, and he does not sin between them. Afterward, if he accepts, he lives in secret and brings him close, and this informs him because they stand together. At the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, decrees for him at the hour when there are illnesses in the world, they stand opposite and inform him that there is no guilt in him that he should return from, and they seek for him—if he accepts properly, it is well; and if not, he is informed that he is burdened with his load in the garments of all, to be strong over him and given to the prophet. If he accepts, it is well; and if not, the words are hidden to do his will and he shall never prevail. In this same manner, a person must reprove his fellow: first in secret, then between friends <note>literally: "between love"</note>, and afterward publicly. From all these, they will restore him and he will do his will. And regarding this it is written: **You shall surely reprove** <note>Leviticus 19:17; the Hebrew repeats the verb "reprove" twice: *Hocheach Tochiach*</note>. "Reprove" (*Hocheach*) in secret so that no man knows of it; "you shall reprove" (*Tochiach*) between closeness and love. **Your neighbor** (*Et Amitecha*)—this refers to doing so publicly. And for this reason, "you shall reprove" is not written first without "reprove." If you reprove him, let it be in a way that he is not shamed; do not say it to him or rebuke him even in secret in a way that says, "See how you have erred in your ways to be purified." And with these words, he should mention the things he did before him, that he is such and such. Because out of pity he knows his deficiency and will be removed from receiving the rebuke. And regarding this: "Reprove," and if not, "you shall reprove," and afterward "your neighbor" publicly. From all this: **And do not bear a sin because of him**, for if a person reproves his fellow and is peaceful in reproving him publicly, he shall not bring before the Holy One a rebuke to make him forbidden... and the Holy One, Blessed be He, will not be angry with him, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, cares for the honor of everyone, even the lowly.

All of Israel are these witnesses... **"And My servant whom I have chosen"**—this is Jacob, as it is written: **"And He said to me, 'You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified'"** <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>. And it is written: **"And you, do not fear, My servant Jacob."** And there are those who say this is David; and David is called "servant," as it is written: "For My sake and for the sake of David My servant." "Whom I have chosen"—this is David, for the sake of **"so that you may know and believe Me and understand that I am He."** What is "I am He"? That I have desired the house of David, and like Jacob, he is truly one. **"Before Me no God was formed"**—for we have learned that the Holy One, Blessed be He, called Jacob "God" (*El*), as it is written: **"And He called him 'El,' the God of Israel"** <note>Genesis 33:20</note>. The Holy One, Blessed be He, called Jacob "El," for "before Me no God was formed and after Me there shall be none," and because of this "I am He," all as it has been said. And he is called "no," for the voice of David was... and there is no other after him. Come and see: when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world to establish every single thing, each one was on its side, and He appointed over them celestial powers. You do not have even a small herb or a mountain on earth that does not have a celestial influence <term>Mazal: literally a constellation or destiny-shaping star</term> over it above. And everything they do in each one, etc., what each one does is by the strength of that celestial influence above that is appointed over it. And all of them are hidden decrees, engraved upon the heart... there is no power to depart from...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Holy Ones**<-

These stand outside. And all of them are appointed from the day the world was created, assigned as rulers over every single thing. And they all move according to the word of those above, each one taking their portion, as it is written: *She rises while it is yet night, and provides food for her household and a portion for her maidens* <note>Proverbs 31:15</note>. Since they receive that "portion" <note>Hebrew: *Chok*</note>, they are all called "Statutes" <note>Hebrew: *Chukot*</note>. And that portion belongs to her surroundings. They come from the heavens, and they are all called the "Statutes of Heaven." And from here we learn that they come from the heavens, as it is written: *For it is a statute for Israel...* <note>Psalms 81:5</note>. It is written: *You shall keep My statutes* <note>Leviticus 19:19</note> because every single one is appointed over a specific matter in the world through that statute. For this reason, it is forbidden to exchange species or to mix one species with another, because this uproots each power from its level and denies the Celestial Retinue <note>The assembly of angels and spiritual forces</note> and the King’s public sages.

What is the meaning of *Kilayim* <note>Forbidden mixtures</note>? It is like one who goes and places another in the house of the Matron <note>The *Shekhinah*, the Divine Feminine presence</note>, a "bride" <note>A wordplay on *Kallah* (bride) and *Kilayim*</note> from a foolish house, so that she cannot do anything. *Kilayim* implies a prevention of all those powers and matters from their proper service. *Kilayim* is a confusion; it creates a confusion in the power above and the King’s public sages, as we have said. And because of this, regarding all forbidden mixtures, the reason is: *it shall not come upon you* <note>Leviticus 19:19</note>.

Come and see: *But of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, you shall not eat of it, for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die* <note>Genesis 2:17</note>. This was the sin that corrupted the King’s commands; he exchanged the Tree of Life—in which life, peace, and the end of faith are suspended—and attached himself to "The Other Side" <note>The realm of evil or impurity</note>. And we have learned this: a person must always show an action below that mirrors the pattern above, performing the work as it is required. And if, Heaven forbid, he does something else to complete a different matter that is not required, then come and see: just as a person who brings down a stalk below, the Holy Spirit above exerts itself and decrees and brings forth and labors over it. But when He sees an action below in a crooked way, He does not wish to exert Himself; then it withers, and another spirit that is not required—which reaches him from the outside, from the Evil Side—comes forth and labors over it. Whoever has that impure spirit laboring over him shows a defect in the action below on the Other Side.

It is written in the exposition regarding the "completion and opening" <note>A technical weaving term</note> of the side of one who presses wool and linen together—whoever joins them as one. Their "living beings" <note>Spiritual essences</note> are according to the pattern of their living beings; He gave them all their statutes there, to be bent into their proper forms when the work is done as it should be. Furthermore, the exposition on "completion and opening" teaches that to perform impurity is like joining them as one. Regarding all their faith, when they are not according to their likenesses, as it is written: *She works willingly with her hands* <note>Proverbs 31:13</note>. And the cutting of these statutes is found there in that general rule of their likenesses; nothing is done for any man who is not found according to their likeness. One who comes to join them as one brings upon himself a spirit that is not required. This matter applies to one who goes and buys or receives wisdoms that do not come from the [holy] side, but rather from the Other Side; therefore, one should not desire to join them together.

The offering of Cain was distanced from the offering of Abel. And regarding the garment of forbidden mixtures, the reason is *it shall not come upon you*—it shall not come upon you, simply stated. Another spirit shall not come upon you to defile you. Thus, a man must show an action on the [holy] side, such as in his clothing and his quiet covering, so that the Holy Spirit, the Supernal Spirit, may hover over him to sanctify him. And come [and see]: those who seek to be sanctified are sanctified from above, as it is written: *Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be holy; for I am the Lord your God* <note>Leviticus 20:7</note>. And regarding the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil—if that caused the arrival of death in the world, how much more so for one who performs an action on the side that is not required?

"Ox and Donkey"—these are wisdoms; from this side it is called "Ox" and from that side it is called "Donkey." And regarding this it is written: *You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together* <note>Deuteronomy 22:10</note>. Do not create a confusion together, because it causes the Other Side to join together to destroy the world. But one who separates them increases [blessing] in the world. Spare everyone who separates them in that manner, just as the donkey is not found... <note>The text trails off into the next page</note>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Blessed are those who dwell as one. If a man hates peace, he brings hatred upon himself and upon the whole world. What is the nature of Cain’s sacrifice? He opened <note>The Zohar often uses "opened" to mean "began a mystical discourse."</note> with forces of harshness, and it is known that these open with impoverished words and levels: <term>Qof, Resh, Beit, Shin, S"M</term> <note>original: "קוף ריש בית סין ס"מ". Regarding the sacrifice of Abel, they were joined one with the other, and the spirit of all was in him. Cain, however, was a mixture of confusion that was not purified. The <term>Other Side</term> <note>Sitra Achra: The realm of evil or impurity in Kabbalah.</note> was not subdued, for debt, destruction, and waste come from that side. In all sustenance, from that which is not pure, death and the stain of sin are attached. These two paths joined, and because they joined as one, no benefit came to the world. They have remained joined even unto this day.

Their side remains standing. And what is it that brings his bone <note>or "essence"</note> like the deed of a sale? It did not awaken above. Those sides joined together and were able to strengthen themselves. Witnessing this is the "bitter saliva" that was not removed. The sides sought to awaken over them. The <term>Holy Spirit</term> <note>Ruach HaKodesh</note> exists so that people may be holy, to be found in the world—both in this world and in the World to Come. Therefore, what is the Priest? When he puts on his breeches, they must be upon his flesh, and when he girds himself, he must bind his precious garments in unity. For they do not wish to sell these openings to the visionaries. It is not written "from his opening," but rather "the Holy One and the Priest." To sustain the bosom, they must appear in this way. Rather, these camps, when they seek to sanctify, are like a mind that is fined when it turns to the side <margin>(Note: The branch-cutter)</margin> of the enemy's will. For injustice comes from this side, and evil coldness comes from it.

Because of this, they must appear in their holiness and not in confusion, as we have said, so that a man may be atoned for all those sins that come from that side. When he enters the Sanctuary, a place of wholeness and peace, and all those services of perfection—even though they are joined, we have no concern, as we said regarding the "sparkling of the strings," for there all the supernal radiances are found and joined. And all those others <margin>(Another version: words)</margin> of the Sanctuary are found. How many types of poverty are kept away from us by this? All of them are included there in the supernal colors. Blessed are Israel, for the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> gave them the <term>Torah of Truth</term> <note>Oraita de-Kashut</note>, the Torah of Faith, and He desired them above all other nations. Rabbi Hiyya opened following him and said: *“When you come into the land and plant all manner of trees for food, then you shall count their fruit as forbidden [uncircumcised]... and all its fruit shall be holy, for giving praise to the Lord.”* <note>Leviticus 19:23-24. Come and see: a tree does not produce fruit except through the earth, and the earth brings them forth. This is a commandment for the world. For until three years, the earth is not prepared by it and is not found <margin>(Another version: slumbering)</margin> with it. After it is completed and they are prepared as one, then there is perfection. This is the mystery of the Female: until three times for conception, there is that which does not reach completion. After three periods, the Female is prepared with that power to be endangered <note>or "to dwell"</note> as one. Then that power is the perfection of all and the atonement of all. After it goes out, until three times, it has no power above. For then it is elevated by its constellation to one place, favored by all. The third is for the vision that is prepared in it and found <margin>(Another version: slumbering)</margin>. Thus it is written: after three years, the supernal power is appointed over it, and it is written: *“In the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, for giving praise.”* What is "Holy for giving praise"? It is like a calculation to praise the Holy One, Blessed Be He. Up to here, from here on is the mystery of the matter. And it is written:

->**Kedoshim (Holy Ones)**<-

The Assembly of Israel <note>The *Shekhinah* or Divine Presence</note> presents herself to the Holy One, blessed be He, and goes forth to be found. It is written: **“It shall be holy, a praise-offering to the Lord”** <note>Leviticus 19:24</note>. (Page 80, Side A) What is the praise of these presentations? It is "Holy." And we have learned: the praise of these presentations is the Assembly of Israel, for she stands as the adornment of the Throne, and then she is "Holy," and a holy praise is found. The Holy One, blessed be He, joins with her, and then sustenance is provided to the world, to every single portion as is fitting for it. From this point onward, all are blessed and begin to eat in the perfection of all things, in the likeness of the Above and the Below. But until all is perfected from Below and Above, it is forbidden to eat from it. And all is the authority of the Below, for no (Page 80, Side B) portion of the Land is found within it. And the commandment is that one who eats from it sees himself as having no portion Above or Below. And if he recites a blessing over it, it is a vain blessing, for the Holy One, blessed be He, does not yet rest upon it and has no portion in it. May the Merciful One save us from those who do not look to the honor of their Master! Fortunate are the righteous in this world and the World to Come; of them it is written: **“But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn.”**

Rabbi Yose opened the scriptural discussion and said:

**“You shall not eat anything with the blood.”** <note>Leviticus 19:26</note> Behold, Wisdom is a place that compels uprightness, and all these verses are written each as is fitting. Rather, the verse comes to awaken all of them, as it is written: **“You shall rise up before the white-haired”** etc. <note>Leviticus 19:32</note>. "Before the white-haired" refers to the hidden Ancient of Days <note>The highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note>. "You shall rise" means that one must stand in His presence. From here we learn that a person must stand before a Torah Scroll. And so said Rabbi Hamnuna the Elder (on page 19): when he would see a Torah Scroll, he would stand before it and say, "You shall rise up before the white-haired." When he saw a wise man of white hair, he would stand before him (Page 80, Side B) and fulfill: **“And you shall honor the face of the old man.”** In this manner, a person must stand in his presence before a <term>Talmid Chacham</term> <note>A disciple of the wise; a Torah scholar</note>, because he stands in the Supernal Holy standing and reaches toward the Supernal Holy Crown (Page 80, Side B: reaches toward the *Atik* / Ancient One). **“And you shall honor”**—Rabbi Shimon said: from here is a hint to the Written Torah and a hint to the Oral Torah. And we have learned: this verse comes for an interpretive purpose, **“You shall rise up before the white-haired,”** as the companions have awakened the meaning: "You shall rise up before the white-haired." It says to a person: before the "booth" <note>the physical body</note> departs, he should stand in the standing of the All in the world, for this is what shines for him at the end of his days. For a person cannot find [this light] when he sees old age and cannot look upon it, unless his whole life was in strength and his life was good. And King Solomon cried out and said: **“Even a child is known by his doings”** etc. <note>Proverbs 20:11</note>. In this manner it is written: **“Remember your Creator in the days of your youth”** <note>Ecclesiastes 12:1</note>. Rabbi Eleazar said: Certainly this is the way that is not accepted before us, and it cleanses the way of the Holy One, blessed be He. He opened and said: **“For the Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish”** <note>Psalms 1:6</note>. What is "For the Lord knows"? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, knows and watches over the way of the righteous to do them good and to lead them, and He goes before them to guard them. And because of this, from the time one goes out on the way, he must conduct this portion of the Holy One, blessed be He, and He will partner with them. And because of this it is written: "For the Lord knows the way of the righteous." "But the way of the wicked shall perish"—it perishes on its own, because the Holy One, blessed be He, does not partner with it.

## Main Text (Zohar)

One recognizes the voice of his way and does not walk in [evil] paths. It is written "Way" <note>Hebrew: *Derekh*</note> and it is written "Path" <note>Hebrew: *Orach*</note>; what is the difference between this and that? Rather, a "Way" is that which many people have trodden and walked upon. A "Path" is that which is opened for a brief moment, not a trodden road at all, as in "a path to join with workers of iniquity." <note>original: *ve-orach le-chavrah im poalei aven*</note> And it is written: "But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, that shines ever brighter until the full day." <note>Proverbs 4:18</note> He said: "shines and shines." <note>referring to the doubling of the word 'light' in the Hebrew verse</note>

-> # Portion of Emor: To the Priests <-

**And the Lord said** unto Moses: Speak unto the priests the sons of Aaron, and say unto them: There shall none defile himself for the dead among his people. <note>Leviticus 21:1</note> Rabbi Yose opened [his discourse]: This corresponds to that, as it is written above, "and life is with him, kindness, for the Lord sought good," etc., and "the sparks of death shall die," and adjacent to this is "Speak unto the priests." This implies that since He warned Israel to be holy in general, He warned the priests to be holy [specifically], and likewise the Levites. For the priests, from where do we know this? As it is written: "Speak unto the priests." For the Levites, from where? As it is written: "And unto the Levites you shall speak and say unto them." <note>Numbers 18:26</note> This is so that they may all be found meritorious, holy, and pure.

"Speak unto the priests, the sons of Aaron." The sons of Aaron? Do we not know that they are the sons of Aaron? Rather, "the sons of Aaron" and not the sons of Levi; for Aaron is the beginning of all the priests in the world, in whom the Holy One, blessed be He, delighted above all others in order to bring peace to the world. Because Aaron's likeness <note>original: *admu* - his form or resemblance</note> caused light to ascend. For all the days of Aaron, he strove to increase peace in the world. And because his likeness was such, the Holy One, blessed be He, brought peace to this world through him, corresponding to the Mouth Above. And because of this: "Speak unto the priests, the sons of Aaron."

"Speak unto the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say unto them." Rabbi Yitzhak opened:
> "How great is Your goodness, which You have hidden for those who fear You," etc. <note>Psalms 31:20</note>
How great is Your goodness—how exalted and precious is that Good which is called "the Good of the Lord." "How great is Your goodness"—he returned to our preparation <note>or "foundation"</note> through which the Holy One, blessed be He, performs good in the world and does not withhold it at any time, for by it the world is sustained. And it continues: "which You have hidden for those who fear You." For we have learned: the Holy One, blessed be He, created that world when He created the [initial] world, and He hid it for the righteous for the time to come. This is what is written: "which You have hidden for those who fear You; You have wrought for those who trust in You." "You have wrought"—at the time the world was created, that light was clear and bright from one end of the world to the other. When the Holy One, blessed be He, looked upon the wicked who were destined to exist in the world, He hid that light. This is what is written:
> "And from the wicked their light is withheld." <note>Job 38:15</note>
And He is destined to shine it for the righteous in the world to come. This is what is written:
> "But unto you that fear My name shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings." <note>Malachi 3:20</note>
Come and see: at the hour when a person is about to depart from this world and is a sick man, three messengers come over him, and he sees there what a person cannot see while he is on the side of [this] world. And that day is a day of supreme judgment, for the King seeks His deposit <note>term: *Pikdona* — the soul, which is viewed as a divine spark entrusted to the body</note>. Happy is that man whose deposit is returned to the King just as it was given to him. If that deposit is found like the filth of the body, what shall he say to the Master of the deposit? He lifts his eyes and sees the Angel of Death standing before him, his sword drawn in his hand, like a flame bound with knots <note>or "bands"</note> in the stature of that man, and the soul has no escape at all. All judgment is separated from the body. And the man sees nothing else but the Divine Presence <note>term: *Shekhintah* — the indwelling feminine aspect of God</note>, and out of the love for the Divine Presence, the soul breaks forth to receive [it]...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the sanctity of the priesthood and the spiritual laws of purity. It follows the previous discussions on the holiness of the Tabernacle and the specific requirements for those who serve within it.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Emor<-

To receive the Divine Presence <note>Hebrew: *Shekhinah*; the feminine aspect of God that dwells among humanity</note>. After life departs, the strength of His hands remains to cling to her and be received as a body; this is the secret that the sages established. After the spirit departs from the body and the body remains without a soul, it is forbidden to embrace the body without burial, as it is written:
> His body shall not remain overnight upon the tree, but you shall surely bury him on that day <note>Deuteronomy 21:23</note>
Because of the death that comes upon all those who remain a day and a night without burial, it gives the "husks" <note>Hebrew: *Kelipot*; the shells of impurity or evil forces</note> a place to ride upon the body and delays the holy work. It is possible that he received a crown upon him to bring him like a hidden treasure; therefore, on that very day he should depart for his own good. As long as the body is not buried, the soul does not enter before the Holy One, blessed be He, and it cannot inhabit another body like a second treasure, for they do not give the soul another body until the first is buried. This is a hint to a person: when one dies below, they are not seen to be given another below until the first is buried. Because of this, another matter: his body shall not remain on the tree. Another explanation: when the soul separates from the body and seeks to go to that world, it cannot enter that world until they give it another body from the Throne, and afterward it can enter. From this you may know that a person has two bodies: one in which he is seen below by human beings, and one in which he is seen above among the holy high angels. As long as the body is not buried, it causes distress to the soul, and a spirit of impurity <note>Hebrew: *Ruach Mesava*</note> is prepared to rest upon it and to weaken that body. Because that spirit of impurity is present, one should not want to leave that body alone, for the spirit of impurity is found in its company, and it becomes defiled like all the earth where a body without a soul is found, which defiles it and makes it more impure. Regarding this, one must search and see not to become defiled or impure, because you are holy and the spirit of impurity shall not rest upon you, and you shall not be defiled. **"Speak to the priests," Rabbi Isaac said.** "Speak **to the priests**" specifically, just as all the works of the priests are unique, so is this stringency unique. It is mentioned once and then a second time to warn them about their holiness so they do not become defiled. For one who serves with the holy crown <note>Hebrew: *Keter Kedusha*</note> must be found holy in everything. "He shall not defile himself for any dead person among his people"—this refers to a soul without a spirit of impurity, yet the spirit of impurity hovers over them. For the descent of the spirit of impurity upon the bodies of Israel is because the holy spirit was engraved within them, and just as holiness seeks to be joined. And the priests, who are holy with holiness upon holiness, must not be defiled at all, because it is written:
> For the crown of the anointing oil of his God is upon him <note>Leviticus 21:12</note>
And it is written, "For the anointing oil of his God is upon him," for the Lord, and he is like the pattern above, a praise below.

## Commentary

| The Faithful Shepherd | The Commandment |
| :--- | :--- |
| This is to dwell as a covering every day, weeping in the Holy Temple; this is to establish the secret of the destination. And life is a secret in this manner, because it is written that the World to Come increased with weeping upon the head of the covering at first, and later at the time when it licks and covers all the weeping, as it is written: **"Like the good oil upon the head"** etc. And it is written: **"For the crown of the anointing oil of his God is upon him"** etc. And regarding this, it is hinted that he wrote his words to trample the weeping and to gather them every day, two and outgoing, corresponding to the bonds of Judah, two and invited and all the rods. And the hands of the covering were revealed, they broke the weeping in everything... | It is written: **"Like the good oil upon the head, running down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron, running down over the collar of his robes"** <note>Psalm 133:2</note>. This verse, the sages established it all regarding the "good oil upon the head." And that oil descends... |

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of Parashat Emor, specifically the laws of priestly purity. ## Main Text (Zohar)

...a child according to his measures, for from there her children are measured. And he is seen in full and gazed upon in full on all sides, as it is written: "And he went out and moved toward the lower realms." In this same manner are the children of the luminaries <note>original: *botzinin*, referring to the sparks of divine light</note>. And the horse ascended to its heights... and he rested and delighted in that lower realm like soft silk below...

He called to them, their secret is the end and the beginning, and to them the end is the beginning. It is written: **"Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: None shall defile himself for the dead among his people"** (Leviticus 21:1). "None shall defile himself"—what does this mean? Rather, it refers to that **High Priest** <note>The celestial archetype of the priest, often associated with the Sephirah of Chesed (Kindness)</note>. Rabbi Judah said: It is written, "And the priest who is greater than his brothers." Indeed, it is as has been stated. And Rabbi Isaac returned to the subject: The priest who stands below, in the likeness of the one above, must be found in greater holiness than all others, as has been stated.

**"And for his sister** a virgin, who is near to him..." (Leviticus 21:3). What is written above? "Except for his kin who is near to him..." Rabbi Isaac opened his discourse:
> **"Who is this that comes from Edom, with crimsoned garments from Bozrah..."** (Isaiah 63:1)

"Who is this that comes from Edom"—from the far end, going clothed in garments of vengeance <note>original: *bukma*</note> against Edom, who destroyed His house, burned His palace, and exiled the **Assembly of Israel** <note>original: *Knesset Yisrael*, the mystical personification of the Jewish people and the Shekhinah</note> among the nations. He comes to execute eternal vengeance upon them until all the mountains are found to be mountains of blood from the slaughter of the nations. He shall call to every bird of the sky to feast upon them, and all the beasts of the field; they shall feed upon them for twelve months, and the birds of the sky for seven years, until the earth cannot bear their likeness. This is what is written:
> **"For the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Edom"** (Isaiah 34:6)

Until those garments are reddened, as it is written: "And I have stained all my raiment." The vision of Obadiah regarding Bozrah was because from that power came the garments of the world to prevail over Israel, and they began to burn the Palace. And when Edom destroyed the mountains and cast down the foundations, this is what is written:
> **"Remember, O Lord, against the children of Edom the day of Jerusalem, who said: 'Raze it, raze it, even to its foundation!'"** (Psalm 137:7)

This is the generation for His garment—those garments of vengeance that He is destined to wear. The color is pressed <note>dyed deep</note>, as it is written in Amos: "I will press you down..." (Amos 2:13). To strengthen Israel, Isaiah saw that vision of judgment that He would perform. He opened and said:
> **"I who speak in righteousness, mighty to save"** (Isaiah 63:1)

He who is "mighty to save" is the one of whom it is written, "I speak in righteousness and justice," and He is literally Righteousness <note>Tzedakah</note>, and He is mighty to save. And why all this? Because they caused the Assembly of Israel to **lie in the dust** <note>original: *shkhivat le-afra*, a state of spiritual and physical degradation</note> in exile, and to be counted as shards, as it is written:
> **"She has fallen, she shall rise no more, the virgin of Israel"** (Amos 5:2)

But in the end, He will do all this and don garments of vengeance against them to raise her up. Indeed, His garment—as it is written: "And I have stained all my raiment." And why all this? Because it is written: "And for his sister a virgin, who is near to him, who has had no husband." God is the portion of Esau <note>Edom</note>, but his work was not hers, as it is written:
> **"For the Lord knows the way of the righteous"** (Psalm 1:6)

He shall not be defiled by those garments of vengeance, for He is destined to hide within them the white garments <note>symbolizing mercy</note>, as it is written: "For she has..." because she lies in the dust and He desires to raise her up. This is what is written:
> **"Arise, shine, for your light has come"** (Isaiah 60:1)

**"They** shall not make baldness upon their head" (Leviticus 21:5). Rabbi Yosei said: "They shall not make baldness" is written with a missing letter *He*. Rather, it refers to that Higher Opening, which is the **Oil of Greatness** <note>original: *meshach rabuta*, the anointing oil of holiness</note> that flows to all seven days, as it has been stated:
> **"For seven days he shall consecrate you"** (Leviticus 8:33)

That which is shown from it is called the "Head." Because the head of the High Priest reflects the Supernal Head, therefore the priest must not show any bone or defect in it at all. And regarding this, it is written of the priest. He opened and said:
> **"When the Lord restored the captivity of Zion, we were like dreamers"** (Psalm 126:1)

It is written: "And this is the return..." regarding the poverty of the exile. For they were found in exile for only seventy years, as it is written:
> **"For after seventy years are completed for Babylon, I will visit you"** (Jeremiah 29:10)

And it is written: "We were like dreamers." What does "like dreamers" mean? Rabbi said: Those who woke from the herald's call after seventy years.

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Emor (Speak)** <-

...aside. And come and see, it is written: *For seven days he shall consecrate you* <note>original: "ki shivat yamim yemalle et yedchem"</note>. These **seven days** refer to that Supernal Place <note>The sefira of Binah, or Understanding</note> which includes all other signs, and it is called **Seven** and it is called **Return** <note>original: "Teshuvah," usually translated as Repentance, but here meaning the return of the soul to its source</note>. These matters are established as it is written regarding one's fast: if one repents, they tear up his sentence even if it were for seventy years. Those seventy years correspond to the "Seven Faces of the King" <note>The seven lower sefirot or divine attributes</note> which cover your sins; the entire decree is torn. Why? Because the inner life is comprised of seven days, all of which are included in the "Seven" called "Return." Because of this, everything returns in repentance and his decree is torn through all of them, and certainly, for seventy years there is no battle. In this same manner, the Priest is crowned with the Seven, which is called "seven days," and the "Living Face" within him is that Seven which sustains everything, for all holiness that rests upon him is called from it. Therefore, they must be careful not to approach [the service] with a creeping thought <note>distracting or impure intentions</note> lest the inner aspects become defiled instead of purified. Thus, the Priest must be found in greater perfection than anyone else, for he represents the Supernal Vitality of all. There is a Priest in the lower congregation and a Priest in the Supernal congregation. Just as the Supernal Vitality is above all, so is the Supernal Priest, as it is written: *upon whose head the anointing oil was poured, and that is consecrated to put on the garments...* <note>Leviticus 21:10</note> and *consecrated* <note>literally "filled his hand"</note> as it is written: *seven days he shall consecrate you* <note>Leviticus 8:33</note>. The other priest is the lower priest. And because of this, it is written: *And the priest that is highest among his brothers, upon whose head the anointing oil was poured... to put on the garments,* as we have said. And because he is holy in the likeness of the Above, it is written: *Neither shall he go out of the sanctuary.* Rabbi Aha opened and said:
> *Righteousness belongs to You, O Lord, but to us confusion of face, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem...* <note>Daniel 9:7</note>
And to all Israel, those near and those far. Because of His love for them, He gave them the Torah of Truth to know the way of the Holy King. And anyone who strives in the Torah, it is as if he strives in the Holy One, Blessed be He, for the entire Torah is the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Therefore, one who occupies himself with the Torah occupies himself with His Name, and one who distances himself from the Torah is distant from the Holy One, Blessed be He. Come and see: **Righteousness belongs to You, O Lord** <note>original: "Lecha Hashem ha-Tzedakah"</note>, just as it says *Yours, O Lord, is the greatness and the power.* What is "Righteousness"? It is the place where all "faces" and longings are attached, and a single line holds them all and they are found in it. "But to us confusion of face" is the place where all faces and longings are distanced from it. Righteousness is the coming of truth and the longing of the bride, and the longing of the faces is the joy of the bride. <insert>But in the end, truth is distanced from whoever is shamed.</insert> Because there is no joy, Righteousness is distanced from him, and the radiance of the faces is removed. Come and see: the Supernal Priest must appear with beauty of face, with light of face, and with joy more than anyone else. He must not appear in sadness or anger, but everything must be in the likeness of the Above. Happy is his portion, for of him it is written: *I am your portion and your inheritance* <note>Numbers 18:20</note> and it is written *The Lord is his inheritance.* Therefore, his face must appear entirely in radiance and in his garments, so that he does not blemish himself at all, as we have said.

To repair the house of the Holy King, and he testifies and calls thus to the King, and they give to him all those repairs of his house, as the verse says: **And she gives prey to her household and a portion to her maidens.** <note>Proverbs 31:15</note> Who are they? Come and see, the Holy One, Blessed be He, looked and sealed...

# Emor

And the eyes are closed <note>original: "סתמת עי'"</note> because all is a holy invitation when it comes to opening. And because the Holy One, blessed be He, is found by means of the Holy Writing, the eyes are closed by the purity of that which is sanctified as is fitting. And what is it? It is "and man became a [speaking] priest" <note>A mystical play on Genesis 2:7, "a living soul," here linked to the priest's service</note> to the Other. And the eyes are closed to the holy Other so that all may be strengthened in holiness to open and receive. Blessed are Israel in this world and in the world to come, for of them it is written:
> **"And I have separated you from the peoples, that you should be Mine"** (Leviticus 20:26)
Just as Israel is separated from all, they are found in holiness to open and receive. Furthermore: "And you shall sanctify yourselves, and you shall be holy; for I am the Lord your God." Again, he opened and said:
> **"Salvation belongs to the Lord; Your blessing be upon Your people. Selah"** (Psalms 3:9)
"Salvation belongs to the Lord"—so we have learned: Blessed are Israel, for in every place they go, the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note> is revealed with them. When Israel goes out from <term>Exile</term> <note>Galuta</note>, the redemption is not for Israel alone, but for the Holy One, blessed be He. Rather, they have established this through many verses, and here "Salvation belongs to the Lord" is certainly so, and "Your blessing be upon Your people, Selah." Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, is found upon Israel to take them out of Exile and to do good for them, "Salvation belongs to the Lord" is certain. And regarding this we have learned that the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells with Israel in Exile; He returns and gazes and sends away your pain and has mercy on you.

**"Any man of your offspring throughout their generations who has a blemish"** <note>Leviticus 21:17</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: Because he is <term>blemished</term> <note>Pagum</note>, and whoever is gathered [to his people] lacking to the serpent <margin>Another version: to the Oikumene (the inhabited world)</margin> for a man who is found blemished has no <term>faith</term> <note>Meheimanuta; in the Zohar, this refers to the mystical alignment with the Divine realms</note> in him. And what is this blemish? It is a lack upon him; he is not like a priest who must be found complete in the spirit of faith more than all others, as they have established. Rabbi Eleazar was sitting before his father-in-law, and he said: It is a lowly thing that before a pious man the Shekhinah is present here, for a man made a blemish and made one for his father-in-law in general; to this one he said "his face is like a reed" and yet he is faithful. He said: A priest like this, they have come to profane him; he has a heel of profanity, a mere power. He said: In the future he will be completed in the Sanctuary, here and all of them. <margin>Another version: In the future for all who are worthy; woe for this, the letter Aleph goes out from all</margin>. Rabbi Eleazar said: A priest who is found not to have faith within him is not a "son of faith." Come and see: The Holy One, blessed be He, said, "Any man who has a blemish shall not approach," for behold, holiness above does not dwell in a blemished place. He opened and said:
> **"To the Torah and to the Testimony! If they do not speak according to this word"** (Isaiah 8:20)
"To the Torah and to the Testimony"—who is "Torah" and who is "Testimony"? Rather, "Torah" is the **Written Torah**, and "Testimony" is the **Oral Torah**. It does not dwell in a blemished place, for behold, it is hidden within the Written Torah. It is written: **"Bind up the testimony, seal the Torah among my disciples"** (Isaiah 8:16). "Bind up the testimony"—this is the Oral Torah, because there the Nazirite of the Covenant is set apart, and in the Testimony the bond of the upper existence is tied to show that all is one. And from there downwards, the paths and trails of the Holy One are separated, and from there it divides and becomes four heads, and from there the paths spread out into all the worlds. "Seal the Torah"—this is the seal of the paths, which is the Written Torah. See that it comes "among my disciples"—these are the holy prophets. "And he set up the right pillar and called its name **Jachin**, and he set up the left pillar and called its name **Boaz**" <note>The two pillars of Solomon's Temple, representing stability and strength</note>. And from there the paths separate for all; they are faithful and stand in existence forever, to be the strength of the **pillars of marble** <note>original: "amudei shesh," also hinting at the number six</note>. And all has no existence except through Faith, for this is the holiness of all of them in His world; when these join as one, all is complete, all is one. No place is blemished, and regarding this we have searched, for all is complete, and "Melchizedek, King of Salem [Wholeness]" and "In Salem also is His tabernacle." And because of this, the "All" does not dwell except in a complete place. And therefore, "anyone who has a blemish shall not approach," just as a sacrifice that has a blemish shall not be brought near, as it is written: "it shall not be accepted for you." And see this matter: The Holy One, blessed be He, only dwells in a broken place, as we have learned, for it is written:
> **"With him who is of a contrite and humble spirit"** (Isaiah 57:15)
Does a blemished place stand more than all? For it is written, "with him who is of a contrite and humble spirit," because he humbles himself to hand himself over to the Exile; the Exile of all is upon him, and this one is "complete." And see, all is written "And with..."

## Main Text (Zohar)

Furthermore, regarding the "crushed," the "maimed," and the "extended" <note>original: "bishur u-marus u-sarua" - types of physical defects mentioned in Leviticus 21</note>, it is certainly true that the Holy One, blessed be He, uplifts those who are of a low and humble spirit. It is written thus because the praise below must be like the pattern above; it must be more complete than any man. For this reason, it says to all of them, as it is written: "Throughout their generations" <note>Leviticus 21:17</note>, the word is written deficiently <note>missing a letter 'vav' in the Hebrew spelling</note> to show that a **blemish** <note>original: "mum"</note> is a deficiency.

Come and open [the discussion] and say: If you say there is no harm in merit, or if you say our portion is cut off and there is no harm, or if the Holy One, blessed be He, says there is no harm—He is surely good. However, the end of the verse proves it, for Israel was confused. There were those appointed as priests who were destined to offer upon the altar, yet they defiled the Sanctuary. They said to the Master of the Universe, "What does it matter to the Holy One, blessed be He?" and they were the ones saying "there is no evil." The Holy One, blessed be He, answered them by returning the very word they spoke.

He said: "Israel, you say that anyone who approaches the altar for service—what does it matter to the Holy One, blessed be He? Look at the end of the verse, what is written? 'Offer it now to your governor; will he be pleased with you or accept your person?'" <note>Malachi 1:8</note>. If a human being among you were to bring a gift to a human king, and we have learned that they arrange it for him, if it were flawed, would he be pleased with you? Would he accept your person for such a gift? If a human being brings a gift before a human king to find favor, he must be whole. This is a matter of faith. Therefore, anyone who is deficient, who has a **blemish**, shall not approach.

Rabbi Yose said: In the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will make Israel complete, and they will be found perfect in everything. There will be no mark of blemishes among them at all, so that they alone will be the restoration of the world. The garment of a man, which is the restoration of the body, shall be returned and given like a cloak. When they awaken from the dust, they shall rise exactly as they were [when they passed]—the blind, the mute, and the lame—so that people will not say it is someone else who has awakened. Afterward, the Holy One, blessed be He, will heal them, and they will be found complete before Him. Then the world will be complete in everything, and on that day "the Lord shall be one and His name one" <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>.

---

**"When a bull** or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall remain seven days under its mother..." <note>Leviticus 22:27</note>. Rabbi Yose opened:
> "Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains; Your judgments are a great deep; O Lord, You preserve man and beast." <note>Psalm 36:7</note>
This verse must be examined. But come and see: <term>Righteousness</term> <note>Tzedek</note> is the <term>Holy Crown</term> <note>Keter Kadisha - the highest emanation</note> above. "Like the mighty mountains" refers to the high, holy mountains called the "Mountains of Pure Balsam." Because she <note>the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> ascends to be bound with them above, all judgment is unified as one, for in that judgment there is no mercy.

"Your judgments are a great deep"—Judgment <note>Mishpat</note> is <term>Mercy</term> <note>Rachamim</note> which descends below <margin>Another version: to that place</margin> to repair the worlds. He has pity on everything and performs judgment with mercy to sustain the world. Because it is mercy, "O Lord, You preserve man and beast" together as one. "Man and beast"—the scholars established that even a man who makes himself [humble] like a beast, for man and beast, the law of kindness and the law of the beast are one.

Just as a male child is circumcised after eight days, so too "it shall remain seven days under its mother, and from the eighth day onward it shall be accepted as an offering made by fire to the Lord." This is so that a Sabbath may pass over them <note>The animal must experience one Sabbath, representing divine completion, before it is fit for sacrifice</note>, as the scholars have established.

Rabbi Hiyya opened: "O Lord, when You went out from Seir, when You marched from the field of Edom, the earth trembled and the heavens poured..." <note>Judges 5:4</note>. Come and see: Happy are Israel in this world and the world to come, for the Holy One, blessed be He, desires them and they cling to Him, and they are called a holy people with the Lord. He raises them to the highest level called <term>Holiness</term> <note>Kodesh</note>, as it is written: "Israel is holiness to the Lord, the firstfruits of His harvest" <note>Jeremiah 2:3</note>. As we have established, Israel is counted many times as clinging to Him in the heavens, and they are hinted at like the spices below. All of them are like "Your people Israel, one nation on earth." The other nations do not cling to Him and have no portion in the Holy Unity.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Emor**<-
<note>Emor: "Speak," the name of the Torah portion beginning at Leviticus 21:1</note>

...clinging to the side of the master who is not holy. And come and see: at the time when the **Holy One, blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> desired to give the Torah to Israel, He invited the congregation of God <note>the spiritual assembly of Israel</note> to it. Afterward, they sought to receive the Torah when the time of holy knowledge arrived, a supernal time [reaching] to the hollow of the Great Abyss. Wine was before the Master of the World, a table of joy <insert>some versions: of the appointed time</insert> for two thousand years before the world was created. The **Holy One, blessed be He** [saw] many uncircumcised ones who were not marked in the Covenant. The **Holy One, blessed be He** said to him: "The Throne, the Throne of the Male <note>referring to the Sephirah of Yesod/Foundation</note>, even their times and the standing of the Torah shall not be prepared before you." This is what is written: *He measures against you* <note>original: "metapeach kenegdecha"</note>, for there are two wickednesses; the Torah was not given except because it is a holy standing, and only to one who possesses the holy standing <note>the mark of circumcision</note>. And one who [studies] Torah but is not circumcised on the side of the two covenants <note>Milah and Priah</note> lies against the standing of the Torah, lies against the standing of the Righteous One <note>the Sephirah of Yesod</note>, and against the Assembly of Israel <note>the Shekhinah</note>. For the Torah was given according to the place [prepared for it] and not to another. Rabbi Abba said: He lies in three supernal places—he lies against the Torah, he lies against the Prophets, and he lies against the Writings. He lies against the Torah, as it is written:
> **This is the Torah** <note>Numbers 19:14</note>
He lies against the Prophets, as it is written:
> **And all your children shall be taught of the Lord** <note>Isaiah 54:13</note>
Instruction is for those "taught of the Lord" and not for another. And it is written:
> **Seal the Torah among my disciples** <note>Isaiah 8:16</note>
Instruction is for them and not for another. He lies against the Writings, as it is written:
> **He established a testimony in Jacob and set a Torah in Israel** <note>Psalms 78:5</note>
And it is written:
> **Surely the righteous shall give thanks to Your name** <note>Psalms 140:14</note>
Who are the "righteous"? This refers to the Righteous One <note>Yesod</note> and the Assembly of Israel <note>Shekhinah</note>. Those who are not circumcised and have not entered their covenant shall not be judged worthy to be given the holiness that is the Torah. **Rabbi Hiyya** said: When the **Holy One, blessed be He** exerted Himself on Mount Sinai to give the Torah to Israel, the earth shook and trembled. This is what is written:
> **The earth feared and was still** <note>Psalms 76:9</note>
Come and see: when [man] rests in his place, it is not said of him that the supernal spirit [rests on him] until he is circumcised. Once he is circumcised, the spirit of supernal awakening is stirred upon him, etc. and he increases in the depth of the Torah to stir upon himself a greater awakening, etc. and he performs the commandments of the Torah to stir upon himself a greater awakening. And if he is covered <note>uncircumcised</note>, etc. and he begets [children] in profanity, they have no portion in the Holy King. But this one [the circumcised] is then a man who rules, complete in everything. Woe to one whose circumcision is a source of shame at the time he is born, for it is a matter that has shame at the time of birth and is found upon him. And because of this it is written:
> **When a bull or a sheep or a goat is born** <note>Leviticus 22:27</note>
It does not say "calf," nor "lamb," nor "kid," nor "young goat," but rather "bull," "sheep," or "goat," for these possess their [full] form at the moment they are born.
> **It shall be seven days under its mother** <note>Leviticus 22:27</note>
Because that matter <note>the mundane state</note> is found in it, and it must be prepared. And how is it established? When one Sabbath passes over it; otherwise, it is not established. Furthermore, it is found in the form of the profane, and after that matter is established in it, it is written:
> **And from the eighth day and henceforth it shall be accepted as an offering made by fire to the Lord** <note>Leviticus 22:27</note>
By the standing of one Sabbath that passed over it. And a man, by the standing of one Sabbath, is established in the awakening of this world and its mundane nature. After a man is circumcised, the supernal spirit is stirred upon him, and the Assembly of Israel passes over him, and the Holy Throne rests upon him, and a supernal soul is stirred upon him—the spirit of that holy world—as it says:
> **And I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood, and I said to you: In your blood, live** <note>Ezekiel 16:6</note>
"In your blood" <note>plural in Hebrew: *bedamayikh*</note> refers to two. There, when Israel left Egypt, they merited through the blood of the Passover and the blood of circumcision; then it was written "In your blood, live." Here, what is "In your blood"? Rather, it refers to two: one of the circumcision <note>Milah</note> and one of the uncovering <note>Priah</note>. One is the decree for the Assembly of Israel and one is the uncovering for the <term>Righteous One, Foundation of the World</term> <note>Tzaddik Yesod Olam: the phallic Sephirah that channels divine flow</note>. And these two bloods make a man holy through them in the standing of the World to Come; "In your blood, live." **Rabbi Shimon** said:
> **The secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him, and His covenant to make them know** <note>Psalms 25:14</note>
"The secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him"—this is the Assembly of Israel. "And His covenant to make them know"—this is the Righteous One, Foundation of the World, in a [mystical] knot.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Emor<-

In the beginning, the word *Yud* <note>The first letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing the point of creation</note> is three prayers for all, the wall of all, the highest of all. And this is what crowns the perfection of all sides, beyond all spirits; upon it, faith depends. There is no descent in the spirit that stands in this letter, the perfection and height of all; this letter is the hiddenness of all sides. When it goes forth, it goes forth as a King with his legions. And it returns afterward, and without being seen, the King is hidden within it; through it, he goes out, closes, and opens. Behold, the perfection of all above and below. And it has been said: *He* <note>The second letter, representing the Divine Mother/Understanding</note> is known, *He* is the one, and all the perfection of the three colors in connection is written in *Yud-He-Vav* <note>The first three letters of the Holy Name</note> to establish it. And all is one matter; it is the perfection of the Holy Name, the perfection of above and below. For this reason, they prepare it like the form of a *He* at the time it stands crowned with its crowns.

Come and see: every single letter of the Holy Name is established with the perfection of all. The name *Yud*—it has been said—is the perfection of all. *He* is the perfection of all of them, and their embrace is within it alone. It has been said regarding the image of the *He*: it is the perfection of all of them, whether on this side or on the other side, it is the perfection of all. And within it is an extra perfection to crown them all; this is the "All" that stands, and the companions have awakened this.

Come [and see]: **"And it shall be seven days..."** <note>Leviticus 22:27</note> *Yud-He-Vav* and the "All" are engraved as we have learned. *Vav* and *He* are the seven days included as one. *Vav* is the secret of the seven days; *Vav* is one, including all of them. There are three *He*s and two sons, and all are one. Two are included within it: the secret of the Daughter and the Firstborn as one. "Seven" implies that the Upper *He* is the entirety of the lower [realm]. This is what is written: **"Seven days and seven days, fourteen days"** <note>Kings I 8:65</note>. **"It shall be seven days under its mother"** <note>Leviticus 22:27</note>. Under their mother, the seven days are crowned, as it is written: **"Yours, O Lord, is the greatness and the power..."** <note>Chronicles I 29:11; these represent the seven lower emanations</note>. And because of this, the seven days below are for the glory of the lower [realm] which is "under its mother," as it is written: **"Until the barren woman has borne seven, and she who has many children languishes"** <note>Samuel I 2:5</note>. The "barren woman" of the house has borne seven—these are the seven days of the Festival of Sukkot. "She who has many children languishes"—these are the sacrifices of the Festival which decrease in number every day. And come [and see], these ascend higher and higher, and they descend lower and lower. The Holy One, Blessed Be He, has compassion on all... <note>The text here contains cryptic abbreviations and shorthand common in manuscript transcriptions</note> they ascend from below to above, as it is written: **"And your seed shall be as the dust of the earth"** <note>Genesis 28:14</note> and it is written: **"And you shall spread abroad to the west and to the east,"** like the stars of heaven. And afterward, they ascend above all and are established like a High Crown (*Keter*) over all. This is what is written: **"But you who held fast to the Lord your God [are all alive today]"** <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>.

---

**"And whether it be a cow** or a sheep, **you shall not kill it and its offspring in one day"** <note>Leviticus 22:28</note>. Rabbi Yose said: according to the translation <note>The Aramaic Targum</note>, "it and its son." This refers to the "Barren Woman" of the lower realm, to know it and follow after it, and not to [harm] the Crown of Wisdom... the matter is known: **"You shall not slaughter in one day."** Rabbi Yehuda said: What is the reason? Is it because of the animal's pain if they are in one house together, or if one is slaughtered now and the other later? He said to him: There are those who explain it that way, but it is not so; rather, it is literally "in one day."

Come and see: we have learned that a fast is good for a dream <note>A common Talmudic and Kabbalistic concept that fasting can avert a bad omen from a dream</note>... and the essence of the fast must be on that very day, not on another day. What is the reason? Because there is no day below that does not ascend to another day above. And when they seek mercy through fasting for a dream, the exchange of that day is not removed until that "lot" is canceled. It is similar to the "other day" we learned about... in this manner, you have no day that does not have an upper day taken over it. Therefore, one must be careful not to pass the inner essence on that day, so it is not blemished before the other days. And we have learned: as the action is below, so the action is awakened above. A person should perform the action below properly.

## Main Text (Zohar)

And it was so, in order to awaken the <term>Source of Influence (Mazal)</term> as is fitting above. When a person performs an act of kindness in the world, they awaken Kindness <note>the sefirah of Chesed</note> above. And when the Moon <note>the Shekhinah</note> comes and is crowned by the Congregation of Israel, that person is remembered for mercy below. This awakens mercy for that time, crowning the Congregation with mercy, for it is a difficult day for them—a day of accusation and prosecution because of the darkness that has come upon it. Just as it is here, so it is there. Therefore, for every living thing, a person must perform an act of "Remembering" <note>Zakhor</note> so as to awaken [mercy] on that day and turn its face [toward the light]. We have learned: the nullification of cruelty is to refrain from harshness and from all other [idolatrous] nations, so that worldly actions are not seen in him, for the "Masters of the Eyes" <note>Divine observers/angels</note> stand over a person during that action. Everything that is fit to be seen—the action of the "Kashra" <note>binding/connection</note> below—depends on the word being awakened for the Master.

**Rabbi Shimon** opened and said: "And Isaac smelled the scent of his garments... like the scent of a field which the Lord has blessed" <note>Genesis 27:27</note>. This scent was the spirit of wisdom within him, and it allowed us to look into the end and the beginning, and he saw the secrets of the end according to the knowledge of the Holy One, in order to sustain the world through it. Through this matter, the hand of the Herald <note>the celestial announcer of decrees</note> acts, for all other judgments of the world are proclaimed by the Herald before they are established in the world. But at this time, the Herald was not called; rather, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, was over him and called out: "A voice! The voice of the Lord is for the hungry." From that moment, other appointees were put in charge of the world, those in charge of the gates. Woe to the person who has nothing with which to return himself in <term>Repentance (Teshuvah)</term> and to bring himself down into the awakening of this inner light above. For it is written, "The King of Kings," and as it were, all the appointees of the King are broken by His will.

And regarding this, Jacob said to his sons, "Why do you show yourselves?" <note>Genesis 42:1</note>. Why do you create an inner appearance above and below, making the King's matter visible while all the appointees are making their proclamations? For I have heard "that there is grain <note>Shever - also meaning 'breaking'</note> in Egypt; go down there" and let your bodies be seen as satisfied, so that you do not deny the service above. Come and see how much strength Jacob had; he did not want to "Remember" <note>bring attention to his state</note>, but rather it is written "he denied," so that no flaw would be found in his actions.

**Furthermore**, he opened and said: "And this is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the children of Israel before his death..." <note>Deuteronomy 33:1</note>. It is written "and his hand was established," for one must raise the right over the left to show the unification of the action below, so that the action above is awakened. It is written:

> "And on the tenth day of the month, a Shofar blast... in the seventh month..." <note>Leviticus 25:9</note>

What is the "Shofar blast" <note>Teruah</note>? It is the Shofar that breaks the dominions, that breaks the rule of all [foreign] servants. We need to show the Shofar in a straight appearance, not bent, to show the closeness of all, for this day shines and everyone must show the action. Therefore, it is a Shofar and not a horn <note>Keren</note>, to show a "cut" like this: Kindness <note>Chesed</note> toward those who have sinned in this world and the world to come, so that the meritorious among you know how to cleave to the Holy King and awaken the power above, to pour out holiness that transforms them. Because of this, it is written:

> "Happy are you, O Israel; who is like you..." <note>Deuteronomy 33:29</note>
> "But you who cleave to the Lord your God are all alive today." <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>

## Commentary (Ra'aya Meheimna)

**The Faithful Shepherd**

**"And you shall keep** My commandments and do them..." <note>Leviticus 22:31</note>. We have learned regarding the commandments of the King of the world, as it is written: "And you shall keep My commandments and do them." If we seek an exemption, why the transgression? Furthermore, all the commandments for the inheritance are established in two ways: for Remembrance <note>Zakhor</note> and for Keeping <note>Shamor</note>. "Remember" refers to the <term>Masculine (Dekhura)</term> and "Keep" refers to the <term>Feminine (Nukba)</term>. Why is it written "And you shall keep all My commandments"? Rather, they are all in the Throne. "And you shall keep" refers to *Shamor*. "And you shall do them" refers to *Zakhor*, for all is one secret. "Remember" is the branch of this, to remember the matter below for rectification and to receive that spirit from above. The commandments of the Torah are for this purpose—the house of the word and the "shells" <note>Klipot/outer layers</note> of the commandments for remembrance—all of them for the Male and Female, and all is the Holy Spirit.
