## Main Text (Zohar)

"And you shall not profane My holy name, but I will be sanctified among the children of Israel..." <note>Leviticus 22:32</note>. This is a commandment to sanctify Him every day, to cause His holiness to ascend from below to above, just as the supernal beings sanctify Him, until His holiness rises to its proper place. And the secret of this is: "And I will be sanctified among the children of Israel." In the lower world, there are three levels below. You have established this holiness: just as there is holiness above all, so there is holiness in the middle and holiness below, and all are within the secret of the lower realm. Holiness at the very highest is in the secret of the Fullness. Holiness in the middle and below are three levels that are one. **Holy** (<term>Kodesh: the essence of holiness</term>) refers to the **Supernal Crown** (<term>Keter Elyon: the highest of the ten Sefirot or Divine emanations</term>) which is below <note>original: "de-letata," referring to its manifestation reaching down</note> and now for all levels, and they make it a "Crown of Standing" <note>referring to the Kedushah prayer recited while standing</note> and it is called "Holy." From there, a masculine expansion spreads out, the path of the hidden sustenance. As for the middle level, once it expands within to be made, then the "engraved mark" <note>original: "kartis," a seal or mark</note> of the letters *Qof-Vav-Dalet* <note>the root of Kadosh</note> is the masculine within the holiness. From this expansion, a further expansion spreads below in time to all levels. Once it is hidden in its descent, then the "engraved mark" of the Prophets <note>referring to the source of the Kedushah in Isaiah</note> is *Chet-Gimel-Pe-Vav*.

And it is called "Holy" <note>Kadosh</note>. And this is what we have established: why is it called "Holy, Holy, Holy" <note>Kadosh, Kadosh, Kadosh</note> when it should be called "Holy" <note>Kodesh</note>? This is the secret of all secrets. At the time when it is found below, it is called "Holy" <note>Kadosh</note> above. For there, the spirit is to be contemplated within this, and so too the Voice certainly. And Israel sanctifies below in the same manner as the supernal angels above, as it is written of them: "And one called to another and said: Holy..." <note>Isaiah 6:3</note>. And once Israel sanctifies, they raise that holiness to the highest height until the "Vav-Spirit" is prepared, which is the highest of the high. Once they are hidden to ascend above by means of that "Holy" etc., then it is called "Holy" above. It is found that this is in the voice of the world's secrets upon the wings that are the supports. And they are hidden, standing for their song, and they are settled in it by the voice of the radiance, and then it is called "Holy." Afterward, the radiance of the "Holy" descends until it nullifies all into one, which is precise regarding the precious secret to sanctify everything below. Once it nullifies everything, then it is called "Holy." And the spirit is sealed for all of them.

And for those whose will is in the three levels we mentioned, in all of them there is a newness that gives them the holiness of the One. Can one not pour out more will? By guarding the voice, it is done, and all is with strength from within the supernal holiness. Below, to sanctify one's own body and soul as "holy," and above, to look to spread the curtain of holiness until it descends, and this spirit is "And I will be sanctified among the children of Israel" through the word *V'nikdashti* ("And I will be sanctified"). And the secret of this, "For I am the Lord who sanctifies you," is to be found in the secret of the atonement of their holiness, and therefore we do not do this except after the "Ten" <note>a Minyan/quorum</note> in the Diaspora alone. And afterward, when every word is finished, "The whole earth is full of His glory," he should include himself in the wrap of holiness to be sanctified below within the voice of the whole, and the secret of this is "And I will be sanctified in My glory."

And afterward, he shall perform the specific generation to be entirely sanctified as we said, "Facing them" <note>referring to the angels</note> who act toward their Master: "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place." This is the supernal guarding. And afterward: "The Lord shall reign forever..." This is the inclusion below. And in every generation and day, the Sabbath is "Holy, Holy, Holy..." This is for the days of the Holy One to sanctify the Torah of the Sabbath, which is the new totality. And afterward, "Facing them: Blessed be the glory of the Lord"—where is His glory? And afterward, "The Lord shall reign forever." The secret of this is that one must find all of this holiness as one: "Holy" as we said; "Blessing" in "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place"; and "Kingship" in "The Lord shall reign forever." And above all, therefore, every man must prepare and direct his will every day. Until...

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on Leviticus 23 (Parashat Emor), focusing on the metaphysical unity of the Divine and the significance of the Jewish festivals. It maintains the thematic continuity of the Zohar’s exploration of how earthly actions mirror heavenly realities.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The order of counting them is "evening and morning," for the night has no completion without the day, and the day is not complete without the night; they are not called "one" except when intended as a single unit. From here we learn that **the Holy One, blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> and the **Community of Israel** <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael," a mystical term for the Shekhinah or the collective soul of Israel</note> are called "One." Without this union, they are not called "One." <note>Discussion of the unity of the Divine and the Community of Israel</note> Come and see: when the **Community of Israel**—the **Divine Presence** <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note>—is in exile, as it were, He is not called "One." And when will He be called "One"? At the time when Israel emerges from exile and the Community of Israel returns to her place to be united with the Holy One, blessed be He. This is what is written: 
> "On that day the Lord shall be one and His name one." <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>

For this reason, "it was evening and it was morning, one day"—without this union, it is not called "one." Come and see: the "Appointed Times of the Lord" <note>The Festivals</note> exist to unite everything and to crown everything as one in perfection, so that Israel below shall be like the pattern above, one corresponding to one. It is understood how the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel are called "One," but how are Israel below, who are invited to be in the likeness of the pattern above, called "One"? Rather, in the manner of the lower world, Israel is called "One," as it is written:
> "One nation on the earth." <note>2 Samuel 7:23</note>

All of them together are called "one nation" with Her <note>the Shekhinah</note>, and not by themselves alone. For while it says "Who is like Your people Israel, a nation," that would be enough; but they are only called "One" when they are "on the earth," in the likeness of that Earth <note>the mystical Land/Shekhinah</note> which is in the likeness of the world above. Because of this, everything is bound together in one intention. Fortunate is the portion of Israel.

And it is well to add in line 17 after the word "Holy"... and these are his words: <note>The text here provides a cross-reference to a previously printed section of the Zohar to avoid repetition, noting a specific textual emendation regarding Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai.</note><-

# **These**
are the appointed times of the Lord, sacred convocations, which you shall proclaim in their appointed season. Rabbi Isaac opened with the verse:
> "To You, my heart has said: 'Seek my face'; Your face, O Lord, do I seek." <note>Psalms 27:8</note>

The companions have established the meaning of this verse in several places, but this verse is stated thus: "To You, my heart has said"—King David said this on behalf of the Community of Israel toward the Holy King. And what did he see? "To You, my heart has said"—because of You, my heart spoke to the inhabitants of the world, returning them to You so they might take hold of You. For because of the Supreme King, he said "Seek my face"—these are the **Crowns of the King** <note>original: "Atrei Malka," referring to the Sefirot or divine attributes</note> which He holds and which hold Him; they are His Name and He is His Name, a single essence. Therefore David said, "Your face, O Lord, do I seek"—every level, strength, and seeking His face always.

Come and see: King David took it upon himself to sing songs on behalf of the Community of Israel more than any other person in the world, and to speak the words of the Community of Israel to the King. This is "To You, my heart has said: Seek my face"—because of You, my heart said to the people of the world: "Seek my face." These are the "Appointed Times" and "Festivals," for all of them are invited to that place called "Holy" <note>original: "Kodesh"</note> in order to crown each one on its day and each one in its time. And all of Israel, from that "Deep of Deeps" <note>a reference to the hidden divine source</note> where the streams and springs emerge, are called "Sacred Convocations" <note>literally "Invitations of Holiness"</note>. They are invited to that place called "Holy" to be crowned there and to be found there, so that they may all be sanctified as one and joy may be found among them.

Rabbi Abba said: "Sacred Convocations" are those invited by the "Holy," and when the times and seasons are called by the Priest <note>representing the attribute of Mercy</note> and his sons, it is like a King who invites his household to a feast, to set before them all kinds of delicacies of the world, and he opens for them a jar of wine that is good in scent and good for drinking. So too is the preparation of the food that they are invited to eat and drink. Thus, "Sacred Convocations"—since they are invited to the King's feast, they are invited to the good and fine wine that is preserved, for "Your love is better than wine." And regarding the "Sacred Convocations," it is written "which you shall proclaim in their appointed season." So we have established that they shall be "Sacred Convocations" for Israel below, to be called "Holy Invitations." Since they are invited from the "Holy" above, you are "Holy Invitations" below. Prepare for them, then, the feast and the joy, for this is shown to you so that you may be called "Holy Invitations" and all shall be invited.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the mystical significance of the Jewish calendar. It focuses on the distinction between the Sabbath and the three pilgrimage festivals (Passover, Shavuot, and Sukkot), explaining why the festivals are called "Holy Convocations" while the Sabbath holds a unique, inherent status of holiness.</meta>

# Emor

All of them are invited before the realms above and below. As it is written: -> *These are the appointed festivals of the Lord* (Leviticus 23:4) <-
What is the meaning of "festivals of the Lord"? <term>Rabbi Shimon</term> <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note> said: They are called this because they are designated by the measure of the realms above, and from above to below. All of them are sanctified and crowned (**another version:** and delighted) on that day, all of them to be bound in a single bond within the King’s knot. Why is this? Just as the King inherits from the Father and Mother <note>The divine attributes of Wisdom (Chokhmah) and Understanding (Binah)</note> and desires that Holiness and is crowned by them, so too all those who are unique to the King must be invited to that supreme place called "Holiness," so that they may all be united in the King’s attribute. Therefore, they are called "festivals of the Lord," and subsequently "holy convocations," for in them He is crowned as King. *Which you shall proclaim in their appointed season.*

Israel has two portions from the King’s crown. Israel has a supreme portion in Him, as it is written: -> *But you who held fast to the Lord your God...* (Deuteronomy 4:4) <- and *For the Lord’s portion is His people.* And from the supreme side of Holiness, Israel has a high portion. Therefore, it is fitting to invite them and to prepare joy and a feast before them, and to rejoice with them. One who invites another must show him joy and provide many delicacies to honor that guest.

Consider a King who invites a precious guest. He says to the members of his palace: "On all other days, each of you was in his own house, one doing his work and another going about his business. But on this day of mine, when everyone delights (**another version:** is crowned) in my joy, I have now invited a supreme and precious guest. I do not want you to be occupied with work or business, but rather to be like those who offer blessings. Let everyone be prepared in the manner of this day of mine, and prepare yourselves to receive that guest with shining faces, with joy, and with benefit. Prepare a precious feast for him, so that my glory may be seen in you from all sides."

So said the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> to Israel: "My children, all other days you are occupied with your work and business. On this day of mine, I have now invited a supreme and precious guest before you. Receive him with shining faces! Invite him and prepare a supreme feast for him, tables set in the manner of this day of mine. Therefore: *you shall proclaim them in their appointed season.*"

Come and see: at the time when Israel below rejoices and prepares a feast for the Holy One, Blessed Be He, setting their tables and preparing themselves in supreme garments of honor, the angels above say: "What is this goodness of Israel?" The Holy One, Blessed Be He, says: "They have a supreme guest today." They say: "Surely he is Yours, from that place called Holiness!" He says to them: "Is not Holiness within them? They are called 'Holy' to Him. It is fitting for them to invite a guest who comes from My side, for they cling to Me and are one with the side of Holiness, as it is written: -> *Israel is holy to the Lord* (Jeremiah 2:3) <- Since Israel is called 'Holy,' the guest is surely theirs. Because they invite the guest from Holiness, it is written: *Holy Convocations* <note>Literally 'Callings of Holiness'</note>." They all opened their mouths and said: *Happy is the people for whom this is so.*

There are three such invitations from the side of Holiness and no more: The Festival of Matzot (Passover), the Festival of Weeks (Shavuot), and the Festival of Booths (Sukkot). <term>Rabbi Abba</term> said to him: "Is the Sabbath not an invited guest from Holiness?" He replied: "It is not so, for two reasons. One: the Sabbath is certainly called 'Holiness' itself, as it is written: -> *And you shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you* (Exodus 31:14) <- And second: the Sabbath is not an 'invited guest,' for it is Mine, the inheritance of the Brother <note>Referring to the inherent connection between the Sabbath and the Divine</note>. It is certainly Holiness itself and not a guest. All the festivals are invited into Holiness and crowned by the Sabbath, and they delight in it like a day of feasting and pleasure; therefore, the Sabbath is not called a 'season' or 'appointed time' <note>The word 'Moed' implies a meeting or invitation, whereas the Sabbath is a permanent dwelling</note>."

It is like a son who enters the house of his father and mother; he eats and drinks whenever he desires. Consider a King who had an only son, beloved to him, whom he gave food to sustain him and clothes to cover him. The King said: "It is time to invite those who support my son, to show my honor and my love for them." He invited them for this purpose. But the son himself—he does not need an invitation to the 'appointed time' to eat and drink in his father's house; he is there whenever he wishes. This is what is written: -> *Who is like You among the mighty, O Lord? Who is like You, majestic in holiness?* (Exodus 15:11) <-

<summary>This page explains the mystical nature of the Jewish festivals as "guests" from the divine realm of Holiness, which Israel is tasked with hosting. It distinguishes the festivals from the Sabbath, which is viewed as an inherent, permanent state of holiness rather than a temporary invitation.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Emor**<-
<note>Emor: "Speak," the name of the Torah portion in Leviticus 21:1–24:23.</note>

To sanctify and to become as one, so that they are joined together <insert>page 92 for the Mishnah</insert> in joy as one in holiness; and the invitation from the holiness of the Sabbath is not like any other.
> **Six days shall work be done** (Leviticus 23:3)
Regarding the Sabbath day, who performs the "work" <term>Melakhah: creative labor forbidden on Sabbath</term>? Rabbi Yose said: It is written,
> **For in six days the Lord made the heavens and the earth** (Exodus 20:11)
And it does not say "in" <note>original: בששת (Be-sheshet)</note> the six days <note>The Zohar notes the missing preposition to imply the days themselves were the instruments of creation</note>. And the companions have already established this: every single day performs its own work, and the portions of the times of labor are divided. Rabbi Yitzhak said: If so, why are they called the "six days of the profane" <term>Chol: ordinary or non-sacred time</term>? To show the profane. Rabbi Yose said: That place is distanced <unclear>from the eye</unclear> because of them; for this reason, they are called profane days. Rabbi Chiya said: Because work must be done during them, and because they are not called "holy." And whatever is not called holy is called profane. And until the companions established them in their order between the holy and the profane, what is the "separation" <term>Havdalah: the ceremony marking the end of Sabbath</term> here? Rather, holiness is a thing unto itself, and others come from it. And these are for work, and those are for guarding; and guarding is found in them at all times from the Holy One. Rabbi Yehuda said: The joy and the longing for the fragrance of the Sabbath is included in everything, because this day is crowned with beauty and is seen, and holiness is added upon its holiness, which is not found so in other days. For it is holy, and it is crowned with holiness to add holiness upon its holiness. For this reason, the profane and the day of joy of the upper and lower worlds all rejoice as one. And all the worlds are blessed; they are all established on this day. The fragrance of the upper and lower worlds is on this day, on the day that stands between them. It is like a king who made a wedding feast <term>Hillula: a celebratory feast, often mystical</term> for his son, and he uniquely crowns him with a crown. The world prepares for him; he says to him: "The bride is on this day, joy for all." One side below, regarding the fragrance of the assembly, there were strangers in his hand who required killing, strangers who required dividing. Because of the glory of this day of the King’s joy, He leaves aside His judgments and keeps to the joy of the King. So is that day of the King’s wedding feast with the Matronita <term>Matronita: The Shekhinah or Divine Presence in her feminine aspect</term>; it is the joy of all, and the joy of the upper and lower worlds is seen upon it. In the joy of the King, all those who are "not" <note>referring to forces of the "Other Side"</note> shall not be aroused on it, until it is written:
> **And you shall call the Sabbath a delight** (Isaiah 58:13)
What is "delight" <term>Oneg: spiritual pleasure</term>? Because it is not found except Above, after the Supernal Holiness rests upon it.
> **Then you shall delight in the Lord** (Isaiah 58:14)
For this delight is "upon the Lord," and it is the end of the day of the wedding feast, for the King is crowned with that crown of delight. He returned and "called the Sabbath a delight," which is not found so on other days. On this day, the children of the King are required to invite and arrange three meals <note>The Shalosh Seudot: the three mandatory Sabbath meals</note> for the glory of the King, just as we have established. When they dream, when there is destruction for him—and here, a man should not arrange two tables at every meal, one for the Sabbath and one for the guest <term>Ushpiza: a spiritual or physical guest</term>, because it is written:
> **He always ate at the King’s table** (2 Samuel 9:13)
The sufficiency is at the King’s table for that guest who comes to him. And therefore, a man must arrange the table to say to the King, and He gives from it to the guest. Rabbi Elazar said: The third meal of the Sabbath, when the delight is awakened—does the guest suffice for him or not? If he does not suffice for him, the guest is found eating from the King’s table. If he does suffice for him, he is found to be internal to the King’s meal. Rabbi [Abba] said: This is like a king who invited a guest to him, and he removed the food from before himself and offered it to the guest; it turns out the King did not eat with him from the King’s food. The King stood and gave him to eat, and all this because he is the King’s guest. And so Rav Hamnuna the Elder did not establish [separate tables] for guests at this meal. And afterwards they arrange the table for the guest on this day. From where do we know? For the order appears again: "your handful," and remember the matter, and "you shall give your handful" <note>referring to the showbread or sacrificial portions</note>. Because on this day, all faith is bound within it. Rabbi Shimon said: It is a deed not to <note>variant: to clean</note> the King’s meal for the guest, for the table is like the Sabbath. The King’s meal rises to the level of Passover, even though it is not the guest's portion. I have seen it thus: he is a guest all that day, and everything is to elevate him, and alone he does not ascend, just as it should not be.

## Main Text (Zohar)

To cause the **Community of Israel** <note>The mystical personification of the Jewish people, often identified with the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> to be sanctified in the meal of the King, and they established the Shabbat meal during the Passover festivals. For the Shabbat meal is sanctified in several ways: first, for the sake of rest and <unclear>bitterness</unclear> <note>likely a scribal error for "delight"</note>, as a person must be found in joy; and second, for the sake of the Bride <note>The Shabbat is personified as a Bride</note>. And all the bread was not found from the "tastings" and above the arrangement, as it is written: "the Bride." In this, it is not a call to arrangement; this is "come," as the witnesses said. Because it is written: *Who is this that comes from Edom?* <note>Isaiah 63:1</note>. Therefore, everything is invited to be revealed, unlike the practice of the Shabbat meal, through which they are nourished. And what is found in it in its holiness, they receive from the **Holy Apples** <note>A mystical name for the Garden of Eden or the Shekhinah</note> which are blessed, and those above and below are blessed by them. And what is the "incense"? It is the Torah. Every palate <note>or "wise one"</note> would do thus. **Rabbi Shimon** <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, at the time he departed from the Shabbat meal, would crown his table and gaze into the **Work of the Chariot** <note>Ma'aseh Merkabah: the deepest mysteries of the Divine realm</note>. He would say: "This is the meal of the King, whose splendor and food are radiant." Because of this, Shabbat is found to be generally superior to all times and festivals, and it is called "Holy," and not just a "Proclamation of Holiness" <note>Shabbat is intrinsically holy, whereas festivals are "proclaimed" holy by the court</note>. **Rabbi Yehuda** said: All the festivals are called "Proclamations of Holiness" because we are provided for by this [the Divine], except for the Day of Atonement <note>Yom Kippur</note> where joy is not found, for they are of the "Male" side <note>Judgment/Severity</note>. But those three times [the Pilgrimage Festivals] are sanctified for the joy of the Bride, to be provided for by the **Holy One, Blessed be He**. He returns and descends to the nicknames <note>metaphorical descriptions</note>, and it is written:
> And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God <note>Deuteronomy 16:11</note>
On this day of Shabbat, no "maiden" <note>external spirit</note>, nor any anger, nor any distress from the whole world shall touch [you], because it is a day of the King's wedding celebration, where souls are added in the likeness of the World to Come. **Rabbi Yehuda** was attached [to this]: It is written, *Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy* <note>Exodus 20:8</note>, and we have learned: "Remember it over wine." Why over wine? He said to him: Because wine is the joy of the Torah, and the rest of the Torah is the holiness of the Bride. And what wine gladdens the King? That wine crowns the King with his crowns. He returns to wait and broaden like the Kinneret <note>Sea of Galilee</note>, like King Solomon with the crown with which his mother crowned him. And we have learned: Regarding the Bride, we need to show a person's action, that holiness is not found without wine for the Bride. *For your love is better than wine*—from the wine of the world. *We will mention your love more than wine*—this refers to the sanctification of Shabbat over wine. And what is established? This is for Tamar.

->**And in the Month**<-

**And in the month**, the dominion is like the fourteenth day of the month, etc. **Rabbi Hiyya** opened:
> His palate is sweetness, and he is altogether [desirable] <note>Song of Songs 5:16</note>
"And he is altogether..." until "The voice of my beloved knocks..." The **Community of Israel** <note>Knesset Yisrael</note> is angry toward the Moon <note>the Shekhinah</note> in the Edomite exile, for the children of Babylon did not <unclear>diminish</unclear>. "The voice of my beloved knocks"—this is the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, who says, "And I will remember My covenant." "And my heart is awake"—for He guarded them so they would not perish in exile. "Open for me"—open like the holiness below. And the rest of wisdom is the page of the upper gates. "Open for me, my sister"—for the opening is above for me as is fitting, so that the prophets shall not enter. For how good is wisdom; it opened above for me. Thus, if the palate did not open your opening, the voice of the palate [is heard] so that they do not bend to me. Likewise: "Open for me, my darling," etc. And regarding "To David," he asked everything above from the King:
> Open for me the gates of righteousness <note>Psalms 118:19</note>
The palate in this meal, this is the opening of the heights above to the King:
> This is the gate to the Lord <note>Psalms 118:20</note>
To be found by Him and to cleave to Him. And regarding "Open for me, my dove, my perfect one," my bread, etc., because He is with you and to be with you like a horse of the worlds in the crown of the **Holy One, Blessed be He**. He was killing from his lamps all those he killed in his exile, and he took levels from above to below upon them. And because of this, in the standing of the holy [place], they were separated and joined like the Community of Israel to be desired by Him. Then, why did they show it to him at the opening? There were two [types of] blood: one of the Passover and one of Circumcision, to dwell there. And it was sprinkled on the opening as a sign of faith—one for the palate and one for the whole. And the [space] between them revealed the matter. And it is written: *Upon the two doorposts and upon the lintel*, in order to show faith. ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Emor**<-
<note>The name of the Torah portion: "Speak"</note>

The holy bond, after they were awakened <note>referring to the spiritual forces</note> they acted etc. until they were separated and their Chariot <term>Rechika: the divine vehicle or structure of spiritual forces</term> was revealed. And then He gave them a bond in a single supernal point, in the bond of Faith <term>Mehemanuta: a Zoharic term for the realm of Divinity/Sefirot</term> as one, as it is written:
> The King has brought me into his chambers (Song of Songs 1:4)
which is precisely not from the Altar <note>original: Mizbe'ach</note> and we have discussed our statutes. Come and see: at the hour of the **union of the Altar**, peace is found with the Altar, and the lower crowns <note>impure or external spiritual forces</note> are not found so much in the world. For at first, from the side of the evil species, they are entangled and awakened in the world; but at the hour of the **union of the Altar**, their side is covered and hidden. After this, they awaken before the King, and then it is written:
> And I have oxen and donkeys (Genesis 32:6)
<note>In Kabbalah, the "ox" and "donkey" often represent the forces of the "Other Side" being tamed or separated.</note>
For the holy union is found, and it is a "vigil" for all. Rabbi Isaac said: Therefore, the restoration of everything is on this day, and in the night is found a "day for the House of the Lord" <note>original: YHVH</note> for those who belong to them, the masters of the house, the goodness of all that we have learned to nourish the Torah (which is the image) as one; and the Lord is for those who are recognized by them. Because of this, the holy people of Israel prepare the "house" for them all that day, and through their hands, those who enter may enter, and they are the portions and they complete their joys. Happy are the people of Israel in this world and in the world to come.

Rabbi Isaac said: This day is for total purity, as in this verse "it is a voice," for on this night the holy supernal union is awakened and everything is found to be:
> It is a night of vigil <note>original: Leil Shimurim</note> unto the Lord (Exodus 12:42)
What is the meaning of "vigil" <note>Shimurim is plural in Hebrew</note>? It refers to two times from the side of reality—for all the children of Israel throughout their generations. For from here onwards they were divided and bound in the bond of the holy circle, and they went out from the "other will" <note>the influence of foreign gods/powers</note>. Because of this, they prepared themselves with much "dust" <note>humility or physical preparation</note> and the crowns see their purity and the change of the holy blessings. And then the **Groom and Bride** <term>Chatan ve-Kallah: the Sefirot of Tiferet and Malkhut</term> are crowned with the crowns of supernal desire, and a man awakens his mother-in-law <note>interpretive: likely referring to the Binah/Understanding</term> as a case for the free man. One day of... <unclear>four palms</unclear> of that species of...

Rabbi Hiyya said: The companions have already established this as corresponding to the **Four Exiles**. But it is well explained according to the way of Joseph the Elder, who said: Since the holy union is found on this night, and the union is in four bonds which are four levels, and they do not separate one from another when the union is found. And so they are mixed as one because... with the words of the Holy One without... in her. And because of this, this night is changed from all other nights, like the change of the "mixed dipping" <note>referring to the Seder rituals</note> in all of them, to rejoice on this night because it is holiness forever and ever.

And another said regarding the four exiles: they are wrapped... for such is the level called, and they do not search for the fledgling but for another supernal level that stands over it and binds it, and this does not bring out a witness even in these two levels. (Regarding those levels) above, it is found that these four are the four exiles. Rabbi Judah asked Rabbi Abba: What is the meaning of that which is written, "not a day like a house-covering," and it is a joy for all seven days? They said: The Hallel <note>psalms of praise</note> is not completed all seven days <note>of Passover</note> as it is on Sukkot, where it is found for nine days, rising in the concealment of holiness every single day. He said to him: You have spoken well. But it is known that here <note>on Passover</note> Israel was not yet bound as much to the Bride as they were bound later <note>at Sinai or Sukkot</note>. Therefore, on this night the union is found, and they were bound in that joy, making a completion for all those upper levels... but until now Israel was not bound in that... they were separated and their Chariot was revealed and then they received freedom, but they did not enter as they entered later. Because of this, on Sukkot the completion of everything is found, and the joy of everything, more than all. Until now they had not merited and completion was not found in it... and Israel had not yet bound themselves to the line of righteousness of life. And regarding the joy of all and the completion of all, because it is the portion in which they are bound. For since on Sukkot the night and the union are found, the entire bond of everything is found in the knot of the union, and not like the side of Israel, for when the union is found in her, those two are found...

Afterward, she enters the inner chamber from the words of the "Maidens" <note>original: *almatta*, referring to the angelic attendants</note> who prepare the crown, the kingdom, and her ornaments to ready her for their Master. All these preparations are made because she is the likeness of the desired vision. All spirits and longings surround her, ready to bring the Bride; and the Bride, the Matron <note>original: *Matronita*, the Divine Presence/Shekhinah</note>, comes alone with her maidens, and they are joined in that place which was prepared in that likeness of the desired vision. They have prepared for her to enter His kingdom, to cover her, to crown her with her crowns. Tomorrow, when the Son comes to be united with the Matron, He will prepare the palace, the garments, and the ornaments, as it is said: So the Holy King and the Matron and her companions are like a flame and heat upon her, for everything is prepared so that the King is upon her, and the Matron and her companions dwell together and are never separated. This is what is written:

> Lord, who shall dwell in Your tent? <note>Psalms 15:1</note>

And so on: "He who walks uprightly and works righteousness." Who is he? These are the ones who prepare the Matron with her ornaments, her coverings, and her crowns, and each one "works righteousness." Rabbi Hezekiah saw and said: If we had only merited to come into the world to hear these words, it would be enough! And this is the portion of those who labor in the Torah <note>original: *Oraita*</note> and know the ways of the Holy King, for their dwelling is like a white light upon them. Of them it is written:

> Because he has set his love upon Me, therefore I will deliver him <note>Psalms 91:14</note>

And it is written: **I will set him on high**, because he has known My name.

### [Right Column - Main Zohar Text]

In the seventh month, on the first day of the month.
Rabbi Isaac opened the discourse:
> Blow the Shofar in the new moon, at the hidden time for our feast day. <note>Psalms 81:4</note>

Happy are the people of Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, brought them close to Himself from among all the idol-worshipping nations. He desired them and brought them close from a distant place. As it says: "And Joshua said to all the people, Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the river in old times" <note>Joshua 24:2</note>. This is to show that from a distant place He desired them and brought them close to Him, as it is written:
> And I took your father Abraham from the other side of the river... <note>Joshua 24:3</note>
Thus the verses are to be looked into: Did not all Israel know this? Had they not heard it? Rather, the Torah is entirely sweet and revealed, just as the holy heavens are both hidden and revealed. For the entire Torah is the Holy Name, and therefore it is sweet and revealed for the life of Israel...

### [Left Column - Raya Mehemna]

In the seventh month, on the first day of the month. This is the commandment <note>term: *pekuda* - a divine precept</note> to blow the Shofar on Rosh Hashanah. Why? Because it is the day of judgment for the world, as we have established. For it is written: "Blow the Shofar in the new moon, at the hidden time for our feast day" <note>Psalms 81:4</note>. For this is the time to hand over the account to the Wise One. And the Holy One, blessed be He, because of that opening, allows the Accuser <note>original: *mekatreg*, the prosecuting angel/Satan</note> to speak and demand judgment against the guilty on that day. For the Holy One, blessed be He, appointed this Accuser to bring judgment upon the whole world, and set for him a known day to demand before Him all the judgments of the world. For the Holy One, blessed be He, made him to be near Him to instill fear before the King, and his authority is over all. This is the secret of: "And God has made it so that men should fear before Him" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:14</note>. That is, they should do justice before the Accuser, and He prepared him before the Holy One, blessed be He, so that he would receive power over the whole world. And all this is because...

## Main Text (Zohar)

**[Right Column]**

And Jacob awakens Mercy for Abraham, and the Assembly of Israel <note>Knesset Yisrael, the spiritual community of Israel</note> is established. Then, both of them find delight in Jacob—this one from this side and that one from that side—and the harsh forces cannot prevail and are cast outside. Thus, there are three orders <note>sets of Shofar blasts</note>, all in one arrangement. Another arrangement: a bent sound <note>the Tekia</note> that rises and takes Abraham from his place and draws him down to the place where the strengths of Isaac dwell, and they establish Abraham within them.

**The second order:** a bent, broken sound <note>the Shevarim</note>, not as strong as the first. Not that the sound of the blast itself is weak, but that sound does not possess the same power and strength as the first, for there the strength was powerfully prepared. Rather, regarding those below who dwell in Judgment, the strengths are more relaxed, and all of them show compassion to Abraham through them and are subdued before him.

**The third order:** a straight sound <note>the Teruah/Tekia</note> that rises and is crowned with the image of Jacob. It draws him down to that place where the power of Might <note>Gevurah</note> dwells, and he stands facing them. Abraham is on this side and Jacob is on that side, and they <note>the Judgments</note> are in the middle. Then they are all subdued and become silent <note>variant reading: and are found</note> to both of them. Thus, all the orders are seen by the Master.

**The final order:** which seeks to gather both of them and to pour <note>variant reading: and to look</note> between them to Isaac as at first, so that he may be inherited in his place and not go out with his strengths to the outside. Then all the Judgments are subdued and Mercy is awakened. For this reason, one must direct his heart and will toward these sounds and return in repentance before their Master. Then, when Israel prepares and arranges the sounds properly, this Shofar and Israel—with the will for the Kindness <note>Chesed</note> of the Shofar's sound—ascends. And when it returns, it crowns Jacob and participates in everything. Another throne is set down, and then joy is found in all, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, has mercy on the world. All the accusers of Israel are removed from Him, and all are found in their dwellings.

From below, he clothes himself in exiles and prayers. Once they merited to be included in Jacob, all those weapons and strengths and angers that were ready to break were no longer found there, and Israel emerges from Judgment with a portion and with blessings.

### Lower Section
A word in the holy light above. Rabbi Elazar said: It is written, **at the full moon [covered] on our feast day** <note>Psalm 81:4; the Hebrew word *Bakeseh* implies both the full moon and something hidden</note>, for the moon is covered and judgment is covered. And regarding this, the day of covering is not hidden when the moon is covered and does not shine, and regarding this: **at the full moon [covered] on our feast day**—through this which is covered from the moon. And how much does the whole merit and all the beauty shine, as it is written: "After the cloud, more blowing," then "Lord, in the light of Your countenance they shall walk." We have learned: the day the moon is covered and does not shine lasts until the tenth of the month, when all of Israel sits in complete repentance <note>original: "teyuvta"</note> and the supernal seal is written. And the covering for that day is like the goodness of warmth, to extinguish all [judgments]. And regarding this it is written, **it is the Day of Atonements** <note>Leviticus 23:27</note>. It should have said "Day of Atonement" [singular]; why "Atonements" [plural]? It is because two lights shine as one: the <term>Upper Lamp and Lower Lamp</term> <note>referring to the Sefirot of Binah and Malkhut</note>. And every day it illuminates the world, it shines and its secret is not hidden, and because of this it is written "at the covering on our feast day."

Woe! to the world when he departs from it, and Woe! to the generation that will be in the world when you are taken from them and they remain orphans without you. Rabbi Hiyya said to Rabbi Abba: This which he said to the Holy One, blessed be He, what does it mean? And when it is covered from Him, we call it "Holy" from the Father <note>Chokhmah</note>, reaching Wisdom like waves that unite. Then "she is my sister, the daughter of my father but not the daughter of my mother," for she reaches the Wisdom of the Father... and on this day of Yom Kippur, there is joy... because the union is not found where the Father reaches... the generation surrounds the children and all of them rejoice who stand before Him all day. He said to him: He is wise in the secret of the male medicine, a dream and its voice is pure before his Master, and he returned in repentance.

# Main Text (Zohar)

Through repentance and the sanctifications of the Holy One, blessed be He, He said to [the people]: "A year of rest shall be a complete one for your children throughout the generations." Those who stand at this time in merit, life is granted to them all to receive them. He <note>The Divine Presence/The Holy One</note> rises from the Throne of Judgment and establishes Himself upon the Throne of Mercy to have compassion upon them. And David said: "I have sinned, for I know the Lord will hear my voice when I supplicate." Regarding this it is written:
> For with You is forgiveness, that You may be feared. (Psalms 130:4)

And it is written:
> For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light do we see light. (Psalms 36:10)

---

->**But**<-

On the tenth day of this seventh month, it is the Day of Atonement <term>Yom Kippur: The Day of Atonement, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar</term>; it shall be a holy convocation for you. Rabbi Hiyya opened the discourse:
> A Maskil of David: Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered. (Psalms 32:1)

"A Maskil of David"—we have learned that the Book of Psalms is called by ten types of song:

## The Faithful Shepherd (Raya Mehemna)

**The Commandment** to fast on the Day of Atonement: This is so that the Accuser <note>The Satan/prosecuting angel</note> shall not approach the merits [of Israel]. As we have established, all those who return in complete repentance stand before all merits, as has been explained in several places. End of section.

## Main Text Continued

Such as: *Niggun* (Melody), *Maskil* (Instructional Song), *Michtam*, *Mizmor* (Psalm), *Shir* (Song), *Ashrei* (Happy), *Tefillah* (Prayer), *Halleluyah*. And regarding these, he said *Maskil*, which refers to joy. And all those songs are known; what is the meaning of *Maskil*? It is from the Lord, to grant wisdom for life to those who seek it. This path <note>original: "חתרא" - likely referring to a crown or a specific path of wisdom</note> is one where they contemplate that place called *Maskil*, as in "He who is wise (*maskil*) in a matter shall find good." And because it is called thus, forgiveness and the freedom of all freedoms <note>The Jubilee/Binah level of consciousness</note> depend upon it. Behold: "Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered." What is "covered of sin"? It has been established that this "covering of sin" comes from the covering of the miracle, which is Kindness (*Chesed*), to receive every forgiven sin. 

Come and see: when a person sits in repentance and returns to [God], and does not revert to his old ways, [his sins] are forgotten. But if not, they are publicized above and publicized below. Heralds go before him and proclaim: "So-and-so, son of so-and-so, is bent over by his companion, bent over above, bent over below! Woe to him, for he has damaged the image of his Master! Woe to him, for he does not care for the honor of his Master!" A voice reveals his shame above, as it says, "The heavens shall reveal his iniquity, and the earth shall rise up against him." But when he says "I have sinned," the King covers his transgressions. Sometimes a single sin is covered, and sometimes it is not called "covered of sin."

Rabbi Abba said to him: "Until now I have not reached the root of this matter, though you have spoken well." He then brought a teaching from the *Baraita* regarding freedom. Alas! Is a sin covered in such a way? What is "covered of sin"? Rather, there are two matters of wisdom in this, and both are as follows: One, as we have learned, is that the meritorious deeds a person performs in this world create for him a garment of glory to be clothed in for the World to Come. But if a person prepares good deeds and also performs evil deeds, the Holy One, blessed be He, [examines] them. If the evil and the sin outweigh the good deeds he did previously—Heaven forbid—he is destroyed from the world and from the world that is to come. What does the Holy One, blessed be He, do? In His grace, He looks at the sin first. If the eye of mercy is upon him, those good deeds are preserved and not lost. They are stored in the treasuries of the Supreme King, and a garment is prepared from his deeds. The Holy One, blessed be He, covers him with the grace of his deeds <note>original: "הדא הוא דכתיב" - This is that which is written</note> "forgiving transgression" and using kindness to cover and repair them in that world... and the sin is covered so that he may be repaired and examined... for "covered of sin" means the sin is covered below. It does not say "he who covers" but "covered." And secondly, when that sin is hidden from before [the Prosecutor] and cast into the depths of the sea, for that which is in the depths of the sea is never found again, because the waters cover them...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Emor<-

"Virgins, there are all their sins." <note>original: *betulot yesh kol chatatam* - a mystical wordplay on Song of Songs 6:8</note> What is the meaning of "constellations <note>original: *mazalot*</note> of *Yesh*"? Rather, it is a precious secret, and thus **Rabbi Shimon** established it:
All those who come from the "Strong Side" <note>the side of judgment or severity</note> and are attached to evil species, like the lower crowns—such as Azazel <note>the scapegoat sent to the wilderness</note> on the Day of Atonement <note>Yom Kippur</note>—he is called the "Constellations of *Yesh*." It is written that all the children [of Israel] are atoned for through him, like a crown that slays the garment of silver. This we have seen: he is the "Constellations of *Yesh*," and their constellations are called "Constellations" from that holy *Yesh* <note>the divine source of "Being"</note>. Truly, the constellations are of silver, and because of this, all the sins of Israel ascend to him (other books: *to Him*) and he receives them, and his children are purified. For he is the sin of the spleen. What is the spleen? It is the "uncovering of the eye," and because of this, he uncovers the eye of all and takes the soul of the body. And on this day, how does it stand? The "Constellations of *Yesh*" and the reading of the binding take the smallest part of the body. What is it? The "reading of the body" is the Evil Inclination <note>original: *Yetzer HaRa*</note>, which is struck and made filthy.

**Rabbi Yose** said: We have learned that it is written, "And Aaron shall cast lots upon the two goats" [Leviticus 16:8]. This is the honor of Azazel; they perform a death-rite for the destroyer of the world's ruins. For the Devourer <note>the Accuser/Satan</note> takes nothing except what is given to him from the living. But because the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices on this day, He guards it; and so that [the Accuser] does not take a portion on this day, He allots it to him. As **Rabbi Yehuda** said: A bribe is given to him so he does not find a pretext, like a lot that is cast, for he sets his eye upon the lot. "By the lot"—and it is well, for he says, "This is the portion of Judah, this is for me," and so on. And here, as soon as the lots ascend into the hand of the Priest, they sparkle from his hands and revolve like crowns. This is what is written: >And the goat upon which the lot fell< [Leviticus 16:9]—"upon him" specifically. And not only this, but in every place where there is a slanderer <note>original: *dilaitor*</note> and his terror, he requires permission to take his end. As long as he is occupied [with his portion], he leaves Israel alone on this day, and does not go to confuse the world. This is what is written: >And the Lord said to the Satan, "From where do you come?" etc.< [Job 1:7]. We have learned: Simply, what is this "crown"? It is the one for Azazel, the accuser of Israel.

And here the companions have awakened to the truth: at that hour when Israel was prepared to cross the sea and be avenged of the Egyptians, that [Accuser] said: "They are crossing into the Holy Land, and it is revealed that these are not fit to enter it. If Your judgment is true, let them be judged here like the Egyptians. Why are these different from those? Let them all die as one, or let them all return to Egypt!" And was it not a true claim? For they [the Egyptians] worked them and afflicted them for four hundred years, yet they [the Israelites] did not complete the count, but only **210** <note>The numerical value of the Hebrew word *Redu* (descend), signifying the actual years spent in Egyptian bondage</note> and no more. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "I will provide a distraction." He wanted to bring [the Accuser] near to Him so that he would be occupied and leave His children alone. Immediately, He said to the Satan: >Have you considered my servant Job, for there is none like him on earth?< [Job 1:8]. Immediately, He gave him a burden of words. >Then the Satan answered the Lord and said, "Does Job fear God for nothing?"< [Job 1:9].

A shepherd who needs to pass his flock across a river is met by a wolf who comes to accuse/attack them. What does the wise shepherd do? He says, "What shall I do? If I open the gate to cross, the wolf will attack me." He looks around and sees a strong, powerful he-goat. He says, "I will set this one against him." While the wolf is occupied with the goat, the shepherd crosses the entire flock, and they are saved from him. So too, the Holy One, blessed be He, (other books: *a great and strong he-goat*) placed a "sin" <note>Job</note> before him, so that while he is looking at it, His children pass by and no accuser is found against them. Immediately: >And the Lord said to the Satan, "Have you considered..."< [Job 1:8], until the Holy One, blessed be He, paired them together, as it is written: >Behold, all that he has is in your hand< [Job 1:12]. While he was looking at [Job], he left Israel alone, and no accuser was found against them. So too here, on this day, this "goat" is provided for him, so that he is occupied with his own kind and with that which he strives for, and he leaves Israel alone. They told a parable: It is like a king who gives a small gift to a commoner, and the officer of the king drags him before the king. It is a small matter for the king, but sometimes that king does justice for his sake. **Rabbi Isaac**...

## Main Text (Zohar)

And come and see, said Rabbi Isaac: Before a king, there is one who circles from behind <note>referring to the Accuser/Satan</note> and later speaks to him and presents to him all those errors that were committed and all those evils. But when the King sits and forgives and pardons them, the world is found in joy. So too here, the Holy One, Blessed be He, stands to guard Israel constantly. Before the King, Israel gives this gift <note>the scapegoat</note>, and it is as if this gift opens a door for all the evils and all the errors and all the sins that Israel committed. And he <note>the Accuser</note> comes and praises Israel and becomes a defender <term>Sanegor (advocate)</term> for them. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, turns all the anger away from His people, for it is written: *For you shall heap coals of fire upon his head.* <note>Proverbs 25:22</note>

Rabbi Yose said: Woe to the people of the earth who err in the error of this accusing goat <note>the scapegoat</note>, for it is intended to occupy the prosecutor who is appointed over them, so that because of it, he comes to find merit for Israel. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, turns all those sins back upon the head of their enemy <note>the Accuser</note>, for it is written: *He remembers their falsehood and sets it before His eyes.* Rabbi Judah returned and asked: How did the wise of the world know about this goat? It does not leave Israel for even one day in the world. Come and see: All that day, he <note>the Accuser</note> gazes at that goat, and because of this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, atones for Israel and purifies them from all sins, and no accuser <term>Kategor (prosecutor)</term> is found before Him. Afterward, he comes and praises Israel, and then everything is forgiven. And the Lord says to the Satan: "Let the sin be beneath you, according to the deeds of Israel." Thus the accuser is made into a defender and goes his way.

Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, says to the two sides of the Throne <note>the attributes of Mercy and Judgment</note> appointed before the Judge: "Behold, he stands over My children constantly." It is found that this one goat is found at the opening of all their sins and all their errors. And all that they sinned and trespassed before Him—all of them agree that the sins should return to rest upon his own people <note>the forces of evil</note>. Rabbi Abba said: All the sins and offenses cling to him, as it is written: *And You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea* <note>Micah 7:19</note>, and they all return upon the heads of the holy people's enemies. And by the power of the goat, they carry *all their iniquities unto a land cut off.* <note>Leviticus 16:22</note>

On this day, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is crowned with the crown of supernal crowns, and He is holy among the upper and lower beings. He atones for himself <note>the Priest</note>, for his household, for the priests, for the Sanctuary, and for all of Israel. At the moment he enters to atone, he directs his mind to the head of Faith and rejoices in the "inn" <note>a metaphor for the Divine Presence/Shekhinah</note>, as it is written: *And he shall finish atoning... upon the Mercy Seat and before the Mercy Seat.* And how does he do this? Like one who hides a bundle (<margin>Another version: like a drop</margin>) to subdue [the judgment], and he rejoices like a circle, like drops to subdue the side of the knot (<margin>Another version: the connection</margin>). Then he intends and arranges and humbles himself, counting: "One; one and one; one and two; one and three..." <note>The High Priest's traditional counting while sprinkling the blood</note>. For the "One" is the foundation of all, the "One" of all is Kindness <term>Chesed</term> to receive it; "One and one" is for the Crown <term>Keter</term>. Afterward, "One and one" refers to Grace and Kindness for those two which are like a vision and never separate. The Crown reaches the "One" which is the wall of all, strengthening the end. And he humbles his voice and says: "One and three, one and four, one and five, one and six, one and seven," in order to find and build this "One," which is the Supernal Mother <term>Binah</term> in known levels, down to the Lower Mother <term>Shekhinah</term>. Thus the priests are found deepening their intentions for the Assembly of Israel. Until this time, two priests shine as one: one for the Upper Day and one for the Lower Day, and regarding this it is written "Day of Atonements" <note>Yom HaKippurim is plural in Hebrew</note> as has been said.

Rabbi Isaac returned: A single knot <note>a rope</note> was tied to the leg of the High Priest when he entered; if he were to die there, they would pull him out. And how did they know [his status] with such caution? At that moment, his color would change, and it would be known that the Priest was still inside (<margin>Another version: in the Sanctuary</margin>) alive. And when he emerged in peace, it would be known because his color turned to white; then there was joy among the upper and lower beings. If not, all were found in sorrow, and they knew that their prayers were not accepted. Rabbi Judah said: When he entered and closed his eyes, he did not see what was not permitted. He would hear the sound of the wings of the Cherubim singing and praising; then the Priest knew that all was in joy and he would emerge in peace. Furthermore, through his prayer, he knew that the words were emerging in joy and were accepted and blessed as they should be...

For then the Matronit is distanced from the King, and the vision of her is withdrawn, and freedom never goes forth from her. Happy are Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, allots them freedom so they may be found in purity. And they all stand before Him because it is written:

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the portion of Emor, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the Sukkot festival and the Clouds of Glory. It follows the previous discussion regarding the wilderness wanderings and the merits of the leaders of Israel.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

From the spices <note>referring to the incense components</note> comes a vision that cannot be fully grasped. The **Clouds of Glory** existed in the merit of **Aaron**, as it is written: *“For eye to eye they shall see You, O Lord”* and it is written <note>Leviticus 16:13</note> *“and the cloud of the incense shall cover.”* Just as there <note>in the Holy of Holies</note> there are seven, so too here there are like seven; for regarding the incense, seven clouds are bound together as one. Furthermore, Aaron is the head of all seven clouds, and he is bound to the "House of Hebron" <note>a mystical reference to the sefira of Chesed/Mercy, associated with the Patriarchs</note>. 

Regarding the merit of **Miriam**: she is the breath and the movement within this **Well** <note>the miraculous Well of Miriam that followed Israel</note> as it is called. And in the Book of Aggadah <note>homiletic traditions</note> it says regarding the verse <note>Exodus 2:4</note> *“And his sister stood from afar to know...”*—this refers to the **Well of Living Waters**, and it is all one unified bond. When Miriam died, the Well departed, as it is written <note>Numbers 20:2</note> *“And there was no water for the congregation.”* At that moment, the "Mistress of the Well" sought to depart, she who was constantly present with Israel. When she saw the six clouds that were bound above her, she became bound within them. 

When Aaron died, those clouds departed, and the specific cloud associated with him departed with them. **Moses** then came to arrange them for Israel, as it says <note>Psalms 68:19</note> *“You ascended on high, you took captives, you received gifts among men.”* *“You received gifts”*—this refers to those gifts that were there previously: the Well and the Clouds. This Well is the **Well of Isaac** <note>Gevurah/Judgment</note> and these Clouds are the **Clouds of Aaron** <note>Chesed/Mercy</note>. 

Rabbi Isaac asked: Why did Aaron merit this? Because he is bound to the clouds and he offers the incense all day long, bringing satisfaction to all as one, and they are all blessed through his hands. 

Come and see: The Holy One, blessed be He, made a crown bound with them—seven Clouds of Glory—and bound them to the **Assembly of Israel** <note>the Shekhinah</note>. For a cloud that is not bound below is not like the others, and all seven were with Israel in the wilderness. Why? Because they are all from the **Side of Faith**. And regarding this, it is written <note>Leviticus 23:42</note> *“In Sukkot [booths] shall you dwell for seven days.”* What does this imply? Because it is written <note>Song of Songs 2:3</note> *“In his shadow I delighted to sit, and his fruit was sweet.”* A person must show themselves as sitting beneath the <term>Shadow of Faith</term> <note>Aramaic: Tzila de-Meheimanuta; the spiritual protection of the Shekhinah found within the Sukkah</note>. 

Come and see: those elders who were contemporary to Aaron used to sit in the Shadow of Faith beneath those clouds. Once Aaron died, one cloud departed—which is the "Right Hand" of all—and when that one departed, all the others departed with it, and they all appeared diminished. Come and see what is written <note>Numbers 20:29</note>: *“And all the congregation saw [Vayiru] that Aaron had perished.”* Do not read it as *“they saw”* [Vayiru] but as *“they feared”* [Vayiyrau]. Immediately <note>Numbers 21:1</note>: *“And the Canaanite, the king of Arad... heard... and he fought against Israel... for Israel came by the way of the Atharim.”* He heard that those clouds had departed and the "Guide of the City" <note>Aaron</note> had died, for all those clouds were bound to him. 

Rabbi Isaac said: *“The Canaanite, the king of Arad, who dwelt in the South”*—if you say these are the destroyers that Joshua encountered, it says *“Amalek dwells in the land of the South.”* This is because he broke their defenses, for regarding Amalek it was said that they were there first. 

Rabbi Abba said: *“And the Canaanite heard”*—what does this imply here, now that the clouds had departed? It is like that which is written <note>Genesis 9:25</note>: *“And he said: Cursed be Canaan, a servant of servants shall he be to his brothers.”* Here we learn: whoever removes themselves from the **Shadow of Faith** is called to be a servant to the servants of servants. This is the meaning of *“and he fought against Israel and took some of them captive”*—he took servants from Israel for himself. 

Therefore it is written: *“All the native-born in Israel shall dwell in Sukkot.”* Anyone who is from the holy root and stock of Israel shall dwell in Sukkot beneath the **Shadow of Faith**. But one who is not from the holy stock and root of Israel does not dwell in them and removes himself from beneath the Shadow of Faith. 

It is written <note>Hosea 12:8</note>: *“Canaan, in his hand are the balances of deceit.”* This refers to **Eliezer**, the servant of Abraham. And come and see: it is written *“Cursed be Canaan,”* yet because this Canaan <note>Eliezer</note> merited to serve Abraham, and since he served Abraham he sat beneath the **Shadow of Faith**, he merited to leave that curse with which he was cursed. Furthermore, it is written of him *“Blessed,”* as it says <note>Genesis 24:31</note>: *“And he said: Come, you who are blessed of the Lord.”* 

What does this teach? That anyone who sits beneath the **Shadow of Faith** inherits freedom for himself and his children, and is blessed with a supernal blessing. But anyone who removes himself from the Shadow of Faith inherits exile for himself and his children, as it is written: *“And he fought against Israel and took some of them captive.”*

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the holiday of Sukkot from the "Ra'aya Mehemna" (The Faithful Shepherd) section of the Zohar. It focuses on the spiritual identity of the Sukkah as the "Shadow of Faith" and the invitation of the divine guests (Ushpizin).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar - The Faithful Shepherd)

->**Emor**<-
<note>The name of the Torah portion: "Speak"</note>
->**The Faithful Shepherd**<-
<note>A specific layer of the Zohar where the soul of Moses, the "Faithful Shepherd," reveals secrets to the rabbis.</note>

**Regarding Sukkot**, our Rabbis taught: The Loving-kindness <note>Hebrew: *Chesed*</note> of Abraham is bound within the Sukkah, as it is written <note>Isaiah 4:5</note> *the cloud of the Lord was over them by day.* And it is written that the cloud stood below to spread out. This day, one sees the clouds of Loving-kindness, as it is written <note>Psalms 90:17</note> *And let the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us.* One cloud was like dew with them... and these are the six <note>Refers to the six directions or the six emotional Sefirot</note>, and the cloud that was missing is as it is written, *and the pillar of fire by night.* This provided light for Israel from the darkness, and those six were guided by it.

Our Rabbis taught: This is to show that Israel dwells within the Mystery of Faith. It is shown that Israel dwells in the Mystery of Faith without any fear at all, for the Accuser <note>The Satan/prosecuting angel</note> is separated from them. All those who press into the Mystery of Faith dwell in the Sukkah, as we have established, for it is written <note>Leviticus 23:42</note> *All who are native-born in Israel shall dwell in booths.* Whoever is of the Mystery of Faith and of the holy seed of Israel shall merit to dwell in the Sukkah. This is explained in many places. After this comes the commandment to bring an offering every day. This offering is the portion of all the brothers <note>The other nations/spiritual forces</note>, because they all take hold of the Tree <note>The Tree of Life/Sefirotic system</note> below. Regarding the "lot," they all receive blessings so that they do not cause harm; they are all blessed through the joy of Israel. Thus, a portion of blessings goes to all the other nations who take hold and are divided through Israel. All these offerings are taken from the pure to be established for the other nations who are far off. The Holy One, Blessed be He, keeps His children close so they may be protected... and the blessings of the Lord are for those who are pleasant... and all the supernal accusers are removed from the beloved of Israel. All those below... the offering is for them so that it all rises and approaches the Holy One, Blessed be He. The Sukkah is spread over everyone to protect them... so that the generations of His children shall be established in Sukkot and receive His closeness... so that there is no nation like Israel whose portion and service is for the Holy One, Blessed be He. Thus the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is exalted above and below as is fitting. And all the supernal hosts open and say: "Who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth." Until here.

**Rabbi Eleazar** opened with the verse <note>Jeremiah 2:2</note> *Thus says the Lord: I remember for you the kindness of your youth, etc.* This verse was said concerning the Assembly of Israel <note>The *Shekhinah*</note> as she went through the desert with Israel. *I remember for you the kindness*—this refers to the Cloud of Aaron which traveled with them to renew the lights that were found upon you and shone upon you. *The love of your bridal days*—for they were included in you <margin>Some versions read: and all of them were included in you</margin> and they crowned you and prepared you like a bride who puts on her jewelry. And why all this? Because of *your following Me in the wilderness, in a land not sown.* Come and hear: when they dwelt in the wilderness, in this <term>Shadow of Faith</term> <note>Aramaic: *Tzilla de-Mehemanuta*; the mystical definition of the Sukkah as a protective spiritual shade</note>, the Divine Presence <note>The *Shekhinah*</note> spread her wings over them from above, and Aaron was blessed and sealed in his dwelling with his generation.

Rabbi Isaac said: Abraham and the five righteous ones and King David made their dwellings with him, as it testifies <note>Leviticus 23:42</note> *In booths you shall dwell seven days.* It is written "seven days" and not "for seven days." This is like the verse <note>Exodus 20:11</note> *For in six days the Lord made the heavens, etc.* <note>Meaning the days themselves are the building blocks of creation</note>. A person should rejoice each and every day in his portion with these guests who dwell with him.

And Rabbi Abba said: It is written *In booths you shall dwell seven days* and later *they shall dwell in booths.* First "you shall dwell" <note>singular/command</note> and then "they shall dwell" <note>plural/descriptive</note>. Rather, the first refers to the Guests and the second to the people of the world. The first is for the Guests, like that of Rav Hamnuna the Elder; when he would enter the Sukkah, he would stand with joy at the entrance of the Sukkah from within and say: "Let us invite the Guests!" He would spread a holy table, stand on his feet and bless, saying: <term>In booths you shall dwell</term>. "Sit, <term>Holy Guests</term> <note>The *Ushpizin*: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, Joseph, and David</note>, sit! Sit, Guests of Faith, sit!" <margin>Another version: to live</margin> He would rejoice and say... the portion of the Assembly of Israel is the portion of Israel, as it is written <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note> *For the Lord's portion is His people, etc.* And he would sit a second time for the people of the world who see...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the festival of Sukkot from the previous folio, specifically focusing on the mystical guests (Ushpizin) and the ethical requirements of hospitality and charity during the festival. It transitions into the 'Ra’aya Meheimna' (The Faithful Shepherd) section regarding the commandment of the Four Species.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

One who sees his portion within the holy nation excels in all matters of faith by receiving the <term>Ushpizin</term> <note>The seven mystical "guests" or founding fathers who visit the Sukkah: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, Joseph, and David</note> to rejoice in this world and in the world to come. A person must bring joy to the poor, for the portion of those guests invited belongs to the poor. One who sits in the shadow of faith and invites these supernal guests—the guests of faith—but does not give them their portion <note>i.e., fails to feed the poor</note>, all of them stand over him and say:
> **"Do not eat the bread of a stingy man..."** <note>Proverbs 23:6; original: "Al tilcham et lechem ra ayin"</note>

It turns out that the table he prepared is his own, and not the Holy One's, blessed be He. Concerning him, it is written:
> **"I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festival offerings..."** <note>Malachi 2:3; original: "Vezareti feresh al pneichem... feresh chageichem"</note>

Woe to that person at the time when those guests of faith rise from his table! Rabbi Abba said: All the days of Abraham, he would stand at the crossroads to invite guests and prepare a table for them. Now that [the poor] invite him, and all the righteous ones, and King David, and they are not given their portion, it is the most difficult thing of all, and it is called:
> **"Move away from the tents of these wicked men..."** <note>Numbers 16:26; original: "Suru na me'al ohalei ha'anashim ha-resha'im ha-eleh"</note>

And they all ascend and say: <term>Isaac</term> says:
> **"...but the belly of the wicked shall feel want."** <note>Proverbs 13:25; original: "U-beten resha'im techsar"</note>

<term>Jacob</term> says:
> **"The morsel you have eaten, you shall vomit up..."** <note>Proverbs 23:8; original: "Pitecha achalta teki'enah"</note>

And all the other righteous ones say:
> **"For all tables are full of vomit and filth, so that no place is clean."** <note>Isaiah 28:8; original: "Ki kol shulchanot mal'u ki tzo'ah bli makom"</note>

<term>King David</term> spoke of the laws of oppression... <note>The text here contains difficult Aramaic shorthand regarding David's role as the representative of the poor</note> because David was the "shield" for the poor, and he was made a guest, but [the host] did not want him, did not invite him, and did not give him his portion. Since King David is the "Crown" and the "Right Hand" that sustains the world, the person who deprives him is more condemned than anyone. Rabbi Eleazar said: A person is not exempted from acts of loving-kindness except by what he is able to do, as it is written: "according to the gift of his hand." One should not feel coerced, but should first satisfy himself and then give what remains to the poor; yet the spirit of all the guests remains with him. When the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices with him, He calls out a blessing upon him:
> **"Then you shall delight in the Lord..."** <note>Isaiah 58:14; original: "Az ttit'anag al Hashem"</note>

And Isaac calls out over him:
> **"No weapon formed against you shall prosper..."** <note>Isaiah 54:17; original: "Kol kli yotzer alayich lo yitzlach"</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: King David says this because all the weapons of the King and the King's battles are entrusted to David's hand. Therefore, whoever rejoices with his portion... Jacob says to him: "Then your light shall break forth like the morning..." and the other righteous ones say: "And the Lord shall guide you continually and satisfy your soul..." King David says: "No weapon formed against you shall prosper," for he is appointed over all types of weapons. When a person merits all these merits, the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come is written of them:
> **"Your people shall all be righteous..."** <note>Isaiah 60:21; original: "Ve-amech kulam tzaddikim"</note>

### The Faithful Shepherd (Ra'aya Meheimna)

-> **"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day..."** <- <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>

This **commandment** is to take the <term>Lulav</term> <note>The palm branch used on Sukkot</note> as is proper during these days... this is the secret of what we established: "And you shall take" refers to a redemption, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, took Israel at this time of judgment. So too, they should seek the Holy One, blessed be He, as their portion. The first [species] is the Lulav, which is prepared to take on the secret of the "Image of Man" (<term>Tzelem Adam</term>) and so it is below.

...The Holy One, blessed be He, called him "Image," as it is written: "And God created man in His own image." Furthermore, he is called by the name "Elohim" (God/Judge) at the time he brings truth and merit into the world... as it is written:

---

"Man in His image." And we have well established that it is written: **"Let us make man in our image, after our likeness"**—this was said at the time of the [divine] union. And such is the intention of both: "Image" (<term>Tzelem</term>) and "Likeness" (<term>Demut</term>) are one, emerging from the Male and Female. "And God created man in His image"—we find that at the time of the union, the King is present.

## Main Text (Zohar)

I have observed below that the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note>, arranged a single **image** <note>original: *dyoqna*, a divine prototype or form</note> like the countenance of a human being, which is the powerful conclusion of all things. It stands upon its base and its tail, and its completion strengthens the mystery of praise. To see it is to behold a human being in his movement, a totality that concludes like the human countenance. In smallness, the human is entirely joined, and until he stands (or if he does not yet stand), that entire arrangement is destroyed in its movement and is found there—that human was not created. And "their slain shall be remembered for generations," all those who do not return to Him until they are bowed forever. When the Priest bows, all are increased in that which is not visible to you, as a gathering, and you shall walk in life. And their surroundings merit and will be diligent at the time when the spirits go out from their chambers, each and every spirit to be prepared before the Holy King in his glorious preparation, like the countenance that stands in this world. And from that image, a glorious preparation emerges, this spark, and the fullness of the spirit's prayer and its precedence in this world at the time when the union is found. There is nothing in the world that is not found, all of them according to their kinds. For all of Holy Israel, who are the life of the Holy Bride and the Holy Chamber, they are found according to their kinds. But regarding all those who are struck and invited from the side of **impurity** <note>original: *mesabuta*</note>, they are found according to their kinds. Therefore, a person should not mix with what is not his own, such as the practices of idolaters, because there is the life of holiness and the life of impurity.

Come and see the difference between Israel and the nations who worship idols, etc., until the parable of the King who invited guests:
