## Main Text (Zohar Continued)

**"On the eighth day, it shall be a restricted assembly (Atzeret) for you"** <note>Leviticus 23:36</note>. For this day belongs to the King alone; its holiness is specifically for Israel. This is like a King who invited **guests** <note>original: *ushpizin*</note>. All the members of his palace attended to them. Afterward, the King said: "Until now, you and I have attended to all the guests, and you offered sacrifices for the other nations every day. From here on, you and I shall be as one, for a single day." For all the hidden things are contained in **"it shall be a restricted assembly (Atzeret) for you."** "For you"—to bring your sacrifice for yourselves. To all the guests of faith, the King is found constantly, and in the uniqueness of the King's joy, they are all gathered with Him and are present. Therefore, it is written "Atzeret," which the Targum translates as "a gathering" <note>original: *knishu*</note>. And this day is Jacob, the movement of joy, and all those guests dwell with him. Regarding this, it is written: "Happy are you, O Israel, who is like you?" and it is written: "And He said to me, 'You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified.'"

**"And they shall take to you pure olive oil"** <note>Leviticus 24:2</note>. It is written, "for the light," etc. Rabbi Eleazar said: They have already established this. See how the Holy One, Blessed be He, joined this portion to the portion of the Festivals. Rather, all of them are in their appointed times, to kindle the greatness of the Master upon it. And it has been said: through the hands of Israel, the upper and lower worlds are blessed, and to kindle the **lamps** <note>original: *butzinin*</note>, as they established: "Oil and incense rejoice the heart"—the joy of the worlds.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the sanctity of the Sabbath, focusing on the spiritual mechanics of speech and the cosmic joy that descends from the highest realms. It follows the previous discussions on the sacrificial service and the festivals in the Book of Leviticus (Emor).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

of the upper and lower worlds. Rabbi Abba opened his discourse with the verse: <note>Psalm 32:11</note> **"Be glad in the Lord and rejoice, O righteous."** "Be glad in the Lord," as it is written elsewhere: <note>Psalm 100:2</note> **"Serve the Lord with gladness,"** and we have established that the Holy One, blessed be He, desires for a person to gladden Him and to be found joyful before Him. A person should be in a state of joy with Him, because that joy belongs to the Holy One, blessed be He, of whom it is written: "And she was hidden," <note>original: *ve-nistarah*; likely a reference to the hidden nature of the Divine Presence or the 'Inner Room' of the heart</note> and my intention is focused on Him, on the Holy One, blessed be He, the King of all. "Be glad in the Lord" refers to the time when judgments are subdued and Mercy is awakened. When Mercy is awakened, then it is written, "and rejoice, O righteous," for the <term>Tzadik</term> <note>The masculine aspect of the Divine, often associated with the sefirah of Yesod</note> and <term>Tzedek</term> <note>The feminine aspect, the Shekhinah or Malchut</note> are blessed as one. The "desire of the righteous" is fulfilled as it has been said, for these are blessed for all eternity and they provide sustenance to all the worlds. "And shout for joy, all you upright in heart"—these are the children of Faith <note>original: *meheimanuta*</note> who are sanctified through them.

Come and see: it is said that one should not perform any mundane labor, for even the breath of words that one brings forth to create a sound—may his spirit be exhaled <note>a harsh idiomatic expression of warning</note> [if he speaks mundane things]. For here, laughter and frivolous talk are the portion of the "Other Side." But tranquility and the "incense of weeping" <note>referring to the bittersweet nature of deep prayer</note> are joined as one, because it is written: <note>Proverbs 27:9</note> **"Oil and incense gladden the heart."** Through this deed [of sacred speech and joy], Divinity is found above, and joy is found above, and all is bound together as one in a proper vision. Through the action below, the action Above is awakened. Rabbi Yehuda said: It is proven that the awakening below proves the awakening Above. Just as the Priest below awakens [the light] through the service below, so too is the action Above awakened.

Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Isaac were walking on the road. Rabbi Yose said to Rabbi Isaac: It is written: <note>Isaiah 58:13</note> **"And you shall call the Sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord honorable... and you shall honor it, not doing your own ways, nor finding your own pleasure, nor speaking a word."** What does "speaking a word" mean? What is the great flaw [in speaking] on the Sabbath? He replied to him: It is certainly the Divine Will that you should know that there is not a single word that comes out of a person's mouth that does not have a "voice," which ascends on high and awakens another matter. And what is that matter? It is that which is called "profane" <note>original: *chol*; mundane or non-sacred</note> from the six weekdays. Any awakening of the profane on the Holy Day is a flaw; it pushes away and acquires [negativity]. The Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah</note> asks: "Who is this who wishes to separate our Union? Who is it that brings the profane here?" The **Ancient Holy One** <note>original: *Atika Kadisha*; the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note> does not manifest and does not dwell upon the profane. For this reason, a "mediator" <note>referring to thought or business negotiation</note> is permitted—why? Because thought does not perform an actual deed, and no "voice" is made from it to ascend. But after a word leaves the mouth, that word becomes a voice that pierces the air and the firmaments, ascending on high to awaken another matter. Regarding this, it is written: "from finding your own pleasure [or speaking your own words]." But one who brings forth a holy word from his mouth—a word of Torah—it becomes a voice that ascends on high, and the holy ones of the King are awakened by it and are crowned upon the head. Then, joy is found above and below.

He said to him: It is so. Come and hear a matter: anyone who shows [mundane] pleasure on the Sabbath, does he commit a flaw against the Sabbath? Heaven forbid! If you say he does not commit a flaw, yet he ceases from the service of Faith and its delight—for this reason, the joy of the Sabbath would be withheld from him, God forbid. I have heard this matter: that no one in the world is more scrutinized from Above than those [who neglect Sabbath joy], because this day is a joy above and below. It is the joy of all joys, the joy in which all Faith is found. On this day, even the wicked in **Gehenna** <note>The purgatorial realm of the afterlife</note> have rest. Thus, if a person has no joy and no rest [on the Sabbath], he is excluded from all the worlds, upper and lower. They all cry out against him: "Woe to the one who brings the profane into the soul!" At the moment when the **Ancient Holy One** is revealed on this day, and is found in His crown, the exile [of the soul] ascends and stands before Him. Then all decrees of judgment are torn asunder so as not to be awakened against him. It was explicitly agreed by the "Six of the King" <note>The six lower sefirot/eminations</note> that on the day of the Bride [Sabbath], everything is torn, because from the **Ancient of Ancients** all freedom and all strength are sent forth, and it is found to be sent by way of the "Right Hand" <note>The attribute of Mercy/Chesed</note>. Regarding this, we have learned: "They tear for him a decree of seventy years." Who are these "seventy years"? These are the seven [emanations] of His wisdom upon him, all those seventy crowns of the King in which He is revealed. All are torn because the **Ancient Holy One** grants rest to the person. And so the words...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the sanctity of the Sabbath and the proper conduct regarding dreams and fasting, transitioning into a discussion on the concealment of divine secrets. It corresponds to Zohar III, 105a-105b.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Emor (Speak)**<-

These are the ones who are awakened by their dreams on the Sabbath. It is like a king who made a wedding feast <term>hillula</term> <note>A celebratory wedding feast, often used in the Zohar to describe mystical unions</note> for his son and decreed provisions for all the days of the feast. All the world rejoiced, but one man was grieving, holding a club. The king came to the celebration and saw all the people rejoicing as was fitting, and so on. His eyes fell upon that man holding the club, looking sorrowful. He said, "Why is it that all the people of the world rejoice at the wedding of my son, yet this one holds a club?" Immediately he commanded, and they went out and removed him from his presence <note>variant reading: from his bond</note>. So it is with those who are bitter with fasting on the Sabbath; all the world rejoices, but they are sorrowful and are marked with the club. At the time when the <term>Holy Ancient One</term> <note>Atika Kadisha: The highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note> is revealed on this day and is found to be joyful, a man holding a club is worthy of being shamed. All those heavenly supports that remember [the soul] will not be repaid by the one who rejoices in it on another day. There is a secret in this, that he is called "one who entices the day," as it is written: **A Sabbath to the Lord** <note>Exodus 20:10</note>, a day in which no mundane thing is found. And those who surround themselves with fasting, which is a slight to that day—that day does not ascend until it calls out judgment upon them. Woe to them who satisfy a grudge on the Sabbath day. For this reason, [joy must be] on that very day and not on another day, for there is no secret of one day that applies to another day. Whatever a day has prepared for its own time, it performs; what is not prepared for its time, it does not perform. Therefore, a man should not seek to displace [the joy] from this day to another day. And because of this, "Remember the day on its day," and we have learned: do not remember it for another day. And come and see: for those who are awakened by dreams so that mercy may be stirred for them, it is a beauty for that man that they did not awaken him and did not inform him in a dream, for they are called "protected," as it is written: **Evil shall not dwell with You** <note>Psalms 5:5</note>. And it is written: **He shall not be visited by evil** <note>Proverbs 19:23</note>—he shall not be visited by evil because he is protected from evil. Rabbi Yosei said: It is written, "From your money you shall turn." Since it is written "From your money you shall turn," who mentions "remembering"? Rather, until the matter is decreed properly and spoken, it is certainly so; the clarity of the matter implies that it is written "remembering." Fortunate are Israel in this world and in the world to come, for of them it is written: **And He shall say to you, My people...** <note>The Hebrew text here appears to be a fragmented or corrupted citation of a verse regarding God's protection of His people</note>.

### Vayetze (And he went out)
When Israel came to... and he was an Egyptian man, etc. <note>Refers to the story of the son of the Egyptian man in Leviticus 24</note>. Rabbi Yehuda sighed and said: He went out from the general community of Israel; he went out from the totality of all; he went out from the totality of <term>Faith</term> <note>Meheimanuta: The mystical structure of the Divine realms</note>. They struck him in the camp... and for all of them, every vision that comes from the filth of the seed is ultimately revealed before him. Every vision is a prophet to him, and the filth of the pot is a cup that has nothing in it and has no portion in the totality of Israel.
The master opened and said: **It is the glory of God to conceal a matter, but the glory of kings is to search out a matter** <note>Proverbs 25:2</note>. "It is the glory of God to conceal a matter," for a man has no permission to reveal hidden things that were not handed over to be revealed—matters that the <term>Ancient of Days</term> <note>Atik Yomin: The aspect of the Divine that transcends time</note> has covered, as it is said: **To eat to fullness and for a stately covering** <note>Isaiah 23:18</note>. "To eat to fullness" refers to a place where there is permission and no more; "and for a stately covering" <note>original: "l'michseh atik"</note>—certainly a "stately covering." Another explanation: "To eat to fullness" refers to those words of those who know the paths and ways to walk in the covenant of Faith properly; and because of the generation of Rabbi Shimon, they surround themselves with [wisdom]. "And for a stately covering" refers to other generations that were like a tongue that does not merit to eat and be satisfied and to have matters revealed within them, but rather for a "stately covering," as you say: **Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin** <note>Ecclesiastes 5:5</note>. In the days of Rabbi Shimon, when he would say to the companions, "Open your mouth and let your words shine," the crown that surrounded them would say, "Do not let your mouth," etc. In his days, it was "to eat to fullness," the crown that surrounds; but "for a stately covering" refers to the companions who stammer and do not stand firmly in the words. Another explanation: "To eat to fullness" refers to those matters that are revealed, and "for a stately covering" refers to those matters that are hidden.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Torah portion Emor, specifically focusing on the laws of the blasphemer (Leviticus 24). It explores the mystical distinction between cursing "gods" (lower powers or idols) and the specific prohibition against pronouncing or cursing the Tetragrammaton (the Holy Name). The dialogue involves the central circle of the Zohar, including Rabbi Abba, Rabbi Yehuda, and Rabbi Yose.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Emor**<-

Come and see: it is found that a person should not enter into the "Side of Evil" <note>The *Sitra Achra*, or the demonic realm</note>, for anyone who comes to be defiled by it—holiness does not dwell within him. For whenever a person is defiled, he is immediately hidden away and comes to pass through another gate; he comes to transgress against the **faith** <term>Meimanuta: the mystical system of true belief and the structure of the Divine Sefirot</term> of the **Holy Name**, and eventually comes to worship other idols. Concerning this, it is written:
> *“There shall be no strange god among you; nor shall you worship any foreign god.”* (Psalms 81:10)

And there is no worse "faith" for a person than this. Regarding this, it says:
**“Any man who curses his God”** <note>Leviticus 24:15</note>—referring to the idols, for he curses that evil faith that he labored over at times, and therefore they do not know if his heart is true to them. Regarding this, it says **“he shall bear his sin,”** but regarding the one who blasphemes the **Name of the Lord (YHWH)**, it says **“he shall surely be put to death.”** Rabbi Yehuda said: If so, let it just write "he shall bear his sin." Why does it say "he shall bear his sin"? It should have said "the sin of his fellow." Rather, it is as we established: "his god" is stated generally and not specified <note>referring to lower powers or false deities</note>. Rabbi Hiyya said: **“When he curses his God”** is general and not specified, and he shall certainly **“bear his sin.”** But whenever it concerns the **Name of the Lord**, **“he shall surely be put to death,”** for here hangs the **faith** of all, and one has no permission to cast a burden upon it at all.

Rabbi Yose said: Certainly this **faith** is the faith of the **upper and lower worlds**, and upon this all the worlds stand. In one bond and awakening hang thousands upon thousands and myriads upon myriads of worlds of longing. Regarding this we learned: these are tied to those, and those to these, in many thousands of myriads of worlds <note>Alternative version: worlds</note> hanging in every single place. They rise and are established in the **faith**, and that which the upper and lower beings cannot grasp is hidden and concealed within them. Upon them hang **this world and the world to come**, and they support one another. Regarding this it is written:
> *“I said, I will guard my ways, that I sin not with my tongue.”* (Psalms 39:2)

And it is written:
> *“Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin.”* (Ecclesiastes 5:5)

Rabbi Hezekiah opened his discourse:
> *“No hand shall touch it, but he shall surely be stoned or shot through; whether it be beast or man, it shall not live.”* (Exodus 19:13)

How can this be compared? If regarding Mount Sinai, which is a mountain like all other mountains of the world, because the glory of the **Holy King** appeared upon it, it is written: **“No hand shall touch it, but he shall surely be stoned or shot through,”** then how much more so for one who approaches the King Himself? If regarding Mount Sinai, where a person could have reached out his hand, it was forbidden out of honor as we said—and it is written **“No hand shall touch it”** generally, even in a way of honor—then for one who puts his hand into the "holiness of the holiness" <note>the inner sanctum or the Divine Name</note> before the King, how much more so!

Rabbi Yose opened and said:
> *“Draw not nigh hither; put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.”* (Exodus 3:5)

And if for Moses—who from the day he appeared knew the **Supreme Holy One** and never departed from his house—it was written of him **“Draw not nigh hither,”** the Holy One said to him: "Moses, you have not yet merited to gaze upon the Glory that is above you." If it was so for Moses, who was so close to the "holiness of holiness," then for one who approaches the "holiness of holiness" before the King, how much more so!

Rabbi Abba said: **“Any man who curses his God shall bear his sin.”** Come and see: when Israel was in Egypt, they knew the powers of the stars of the world that are appointed over the other nations, and each one had his own fear <note>object of worship</note> from among them. Once they were bound in the bond of **faith** and the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, brought them close to His service, they left their previous fears and drew near to the **Supreme Holy Faith**. Because of this it is written:
> *“For they are life...”* (Proverbs 4:22)

**“When he curses his God”**—these refer to the worship of the stars. Since they are still appointed by the King to remember the world, one who curses and shames them **“shall bear his sin,”** certainly, for they exist by His permission and they lead the people of the world. But **“he who blasphemes the Name of the Lord shall surely be put to death.”** Is his sin like the others? No, rather **“he shall surely be put to death”**—he shall be put to death in **this world** and put to death in the **world to come**. For those others, **“he shall bear his sin,”** because he shames the works of the King's hands, the servants of fear who were appointed; but while it is forbidden to shame them, he is not liable for death because of them.

Rabbi Abba was walking on the way, and with him were Rabbi Eleazar, Rabbi Hiyya, Rabbi Yose, and Rabbi Yehuda. They reached a certain turn in the road... <note>The text breaks off into a narrative about their journey</note>

It uses the examples of Mount Sinai and Moses at the Burning Bush to illustrate the extreme sanctity required when approaching the Divine.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Emor (Leviticus 21-24). The previous section likely discussed the unity of the Divine and the hidden mysteries of creation. Here, the Zohar addresses the inherent goodness in all created things and the symbolic identity of the Shekhinah (the Divine Presence) as the Rose of Sharon.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Emor<-

The knot of the bond where all are unified and not found <note>referring to the hidden unity of the Sefirot</note>. Rabbi Shimon said to him: "The sun of the world is lacking for you!" <note>A metaphor for a lack of enlightenment or clarity</note>. They stood and arranged the wisdom, for whoever finds the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note>, merits works of truth. He opened his discourse and said:
> "And God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good." <note>Genesis 1:31</note>
According to the law of the supernal fortress, it is found that "God saw everything that He had made"—even snakes, scorpions, mosquitoes, and snails, and those things that appear to be destroyers of the world; regarding all of them it is written, "behold, it was very good." They all support the world and sustain the world, though human beings do not know it. 

While they were walking, they saw a snake crawling before them. Rabbi Elazar said: "Let us see its craftiness, for a miracle will happen." That snake ran before them and encountered a viper; they fought one another on the road, one against the other, and both died. When they reached them, they saw both lying on the road. Rabbi Shimon said: "Blessed is the Merciful One who showed us a miracle, for anyone who looks upon this snake—whose existence is not for his own sake—and looks with an evil eye, he will not be helped. No man should say of it..." He cited the verse:
> "Show them no mercy." <note>Deuteronomy 7:2; a play on words regarding the snake's danger</note>
> "No evil shall befall you, nor shall any plague come near your tent." <note>Psalms 91:10</note>
The Holy One, Blessed be He, does everything for His mission, and we must not treat with contempt anything that He has fashioned and made. Regarding this it is written:
> "The Lord is good to all, and His mercies are over all His works." <note>Psalms 145:9</note>
And it is written:
> "All Your works shall praise You, O Lord." <note>Psalms 145:10</note>

Rabbi Shimon opened:
> "I am the rose of Sharon, the lily of the valleys." <note>Song of Songs 2:1</note>
How beloved is the Congregation of Israel <note>original: *Knesset Yisrael*, the Shekhinah</note> before the Holy One, Blessed be He! He praises her and she praises Him. How many praises are prepared to adorn the King constantly! And all the portion of Israel is held within the delight of the holy portion, as it is written:
> "For the Lord’s portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance." <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>
"I am the rose of Sharon"—this is the Congregation of Israel in the beauty of her fairness in the garden below. "Of Sharon"—for she sings <note>a wordplay on *shir*, song</note> and praises the Supernal King. This is the Congregation of Israel. And why "the rose of Sharon"? Because she desires to be watered from the deep river <note>original: *nachla amika*, referring to the Sefirah of Binah</note>, the source of the rivers, as it is written: "The Sharon shall be like a wilderness." "The lily of the valleys"—which stands in the depth of all. "The lily of the valleys"—how its colors change in the depths, as it is written:
> "Out of the depths I have called to You, O Lord." <note>Psalms 130:1</note>
From the Congregation of Israel, that place where the deep rivers flow and never cease. "The lily of the valleys"—the lily of that place which is called "deep" because it is hidden from all sides. 

Come and see: at first it is greenish, green like the assembly of green leaves; afterwards it becomes a red lily with shades of red and white. A lily like the body of the leaves; a lily that is found changing and transforming from color to color. The first lily is from the assembly that desires to be joined with the King. The assembly, after it has cleaved to the King with the kisses of the palate, is called a "lily," as it is written:
> "His lips are lilies." <note>Song of Songs 5:13</note>
"The lily of the valleys"—for she is found and finds color, sometimes for good and sometimes for evil, sometimes for Judgment <note>Din</note> and sometimes for Mercy <note>Rachamim</note>.
> "And the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes..." <note>Genesis 3:6</note>
This is because human beings do not know and do not look or observe. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, He established it so that they might cleave to Him, so that He might be found as One and everything as one, and all should be a singular cleaving that never changes or turns, within that bond of faith <note>original: *kitora de-meimanuta*</note> where all is tied together as one. And the Tree of Life was in the midst of the garden. 

But after they sinned, they strayed from the path of faith and left the unique and supernal source of all sources. They descended to cleave to a place that changes and transforms from color to color, from good to evil and from evil to good. They descended from above to below, and they fell into the lower colors which are varied. They left the One above who is singular and never changes. Thus, man's heart turned toward that appointed power <note>the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil</note> which is sometimes for good, sometimes for evil, sometimes for Mercy, and sometimes for Judgment.

Like that...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Emor**<-

Through that matter <note>the Tree of Knowledge</note> to which they cleaved, it came to be that "they sought out many schemes" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:29</note> and clung to them. This was the cause of life turning away and clinging to death. What is it that is written: **And the tree of life in the midst of the garden** <note>Genesis 2:9</note>? This is the tree called "Life," for whoever takes hold of it never tastes the taste of death. But he <note>Adam</note> clung to that other side, which is both life and death, as it is written of it: **Her feet go down to death...** <note>Proverbs 5:5</note>. And it is written: **And I find more bitter than death the woman** <note>Ecclesiastes 7:26</note>. Because he clung to the place of death, he abandoned the place of life. Therefore, death was decreed upon him and upon the whole world. Had he taken hold of the Tree of Life, all the worlds would have existed in life <note>original: *be-chayyei*</note>. If all the judgments had come and gone, and he had consumed this and benefited from all, it would not have been so. Rather, it is like the way Adam stood on his feet; all the judgments stood before him and feared him, and they were like servants following after their King. He saw them, and all of them were submerged, bowing and kneeling before him, and they all followed him. Once he saw that Adam was drawn to that place <note>the Tree of Knowledge</note> and clung to it, they were all found behind him, and he brought death upon himself and the entire world. Then Adam was found in many states: sometimes for good and sometimes for evil, sometimes at rest and sometimes in pain, sometimes shining and sometimes darkened, sometimes in mercy and sometimes in death. He did not remain in one constant state because that place caused it for him. For this reason, it is called "the flaming sword which turns every way" <note>Genesis 3:24</note>; it turns to everything and is called "Good and Evil." It turns from mercy to judgment, from peace to war. It is written: **But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it** <note>Genesis 2:17</note>. The Supreme King, out of mercy for the work of His hands, had pity on him and said to him: "But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it." In the end, he did not listen to Him, but was drawn after his wife and was driven out forever, for the woman reaches to this place and no further, and the woman caused death for all. Come and see: regarding the world to come, it is written: **For as the days of a tree shall be the days of my people** <note>Isaiah 65:22</note>. "As the days of a tree"—that specific Tree which is known <note>the Tree of Life</note>. And it is written: **He will swallow up death for ever; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces** <note>Isaiah 25:8</note>.

->**Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen. May the Lord reign forever, Amen and Amen.**<-

# ## Portion of Behar Sinai

**And the Lord spoke** unto Moses in Mount Sinai, saying. He mentioned the Assembly of Israel and said to them: "When ye come into the land..." <note>Leviticus 25:2</note>. Rabbi Elazar opened: "And the law of the world..." <note>referring to the cosmic order</note>. This verse we have established in several ways, as it rises and joins with the Holy King in a perfect union. The field remained on its hearth before Him all the night. Come and see: when it is night and the lower gates are still closed, the lower powers awaken in the world and go about and rule—the masters of lamentation and the "dogs" and "donkeys" <note>metaphors for destructive spiritual forces</note>. The wise and the providers do not rule and do not go about, except for those holy servants who gather together, such as Balaam and the sorcerers <note>referring to those who use the night for unholy power</note>. Then all the children of the world sleep, and death comes to lead them to the fire. At midnight, the <term>North Wind</term> <note>original: *Ruach Tzafon*; in the Zohar, this represents the awakening of the attribute of Gevurah/Judgment which, at midnight, sweetens into the joy of Torah study</note> awakens, and from that time, the palace is divided for this purpose, and the gates are opened. The lower spirits gather into their holes, and the soul ascends. The gates of the Garden <note>Eden</note> are opened until that palace reaches out to several sides of the world, and upon it is the hope...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the laws of the Torah, specifically focusing on the transition from the sacrificial service to the laws of the Sabbatical year and the Hebrew servant. It maintains the Sefirotic associations between the letters of the Divine Name and the cycles of time.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The wings of the rooster are opened and it calls out; then the Holy One, blessed be He, is found among the righteous, etc., praising the Holy One, blessed be He, until the morning comes. Once the morning comes, they find themselves sustained by that awe <note>original: *de-chila*</note> and it has an existence in the world. This is what is written: *on its firewood on the altar all night* <note>Leviticus 6:2</note>, for the wings of judgments and flames are stilled. Then Kindness <note>The Sefirah of *Chesed*</note> is awakened in the world, and it is like the day of all. Come and see: when Israel entered the Land, open judgments were not found in it, etc., for it rested upon the wings of the Cherubim, as it has been said, for it is written:
> *Righteousness lodged in her* <note>Isaiah 1:21</note>
Then she had existence from all, for Israel does not stand until they offer the afternoon sacrifice <note>original: *korbana de-bein ha-arbayim*</note> and the judgments are rectified. And the burnt offering would burn upon the altar, and then she had existence from all, and [judgment] was not found even below in the world. This is what is written: *when you rest... and the land shall rest* like the day and the awe.
**And the land shall rest** a Sabbath to the Lord <note>Leviticus 25:2</note>—literally a Sabbath to the Lord. An addition: Rabbi Eleazar [said]: *If you buy a Hebrew servant, six years he shall work, etc.* <note>Exodus 21:2</note>. Because every son of Israel who possesses a holy soul has his existence in that side which belongs to him; that Sabbatical year <note>term: *Shemita* - the seventh year of rest for the land</note> is for him to be gathered into it. And this is called the "Sabbath of the Land," and the awe of freedom <note>term: *Cherut* - associated with the higher world/Jubilee</note> is in it, in this manner. Just as you are like the day that acquires all, here is the Sabbatical release of all, in the manner of the spirit and the body. Come and see: it is like the day that the upper and lower [worlds] entered. Because of this, the upper *He* (ה) and the lower *He* (ה) <note>The two letters *He* in the Tetragrammaton (Y-H-V-H)</note> are in the manner of the ascent of the lower ones. The upper *He* is seven years times seven <note>The 49 years leading to the Jubilee</note>; the lower *He* is seven years alone—this is the Sabbatical year and this is the Jubilee. And when one looks into it, all is one. "And the land shall rest" in that manner of the earth; servants are guarded like the day. And in the seventh, *he shall go out to freedom for nothing* <note>original: *chinnam*</note>. What is "for nothing"? That he does not give his master anything. This too is a secret here; their exchange is written:
> *We remember the fish which we ate in Egypt for nothing* <note>Numbers 11:5</note>
Without a blessing, for the Yoke from Above was not upon us in Egypt. Come and see: servants are exempt from the Yoke of the Kingdom Above, and they are exempt from the commandments. Who [takes on] the Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven? Only through that Torah which they place upon him as a Yoke at first, in order to bring him out from the hiddenness Above. And if he did not receive that Yoke upon himself, he has done nothing. So too, a man must receive upon himself the Yoke at first, and afterwards he shall labor in it with all that is required. And if he did not receive this at first, he cannot labor. This is what is written:
> *Serve the Lord with fear* <note>Psalms 2:11</note>
What is "with fear"? With this [level] which is Wisdom and the Fear of the Lord, and this is the Kingdom of Heaven <note>The Sefirah of *Malchut*</note>. And because of this, it is the Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, and this is the Yoke at the beginning of all. Whoever merits prayer first by hand, because through it they enter afterwards into holiness. And if this is not found with him, holiness from Above does not rest upon him. Because of this:
> *With this shall Aaron come into the Holy Place, etc.* <note>Leviticus 16:3</note>
It is written: and this Yoke does not rest upon one who is bound to another. For servants are exempt from the Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, and if they are exempt from the Yoke, they are exempt from all else. For the [exemption] does not rest upon a man until he is found a prophet in this Yoke. And because of this, the sages of Israel were like those in Egypt—free. Even here, *he shall go out to freedom for nothing*. He was a servant, and all that he did was "for nothing," without the Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven. And even though his works were "for nothing," it is pleasant to release him after he was pressured in his life. And to be found in the manner [of holiness], they place upon him another Yoke so that he may go out to freedom. And if a man refuses to go out to freedom, it says:
> *And if the servant shall plainly say: I love my master, etc.* <note>Exodus 21:5</note>
This certainly causes a defect in him, for he has rejected the Yoke of the Kingdom Above and taken the yoke of another. And what is written?
> *Then his master shall bring him to the judges* <note>Exodus 21:6; original: *Elohim* - God/Judges</note>
*And he shall bring him to the door, etc.* "His master shall bring him to the *Elohim*"—to *Elohim* generally, regarding that which he defected, for He is called *Elohim*. And to another master he shall be brought, to the door or to the doorpost.

Because it stands there, it is from above, and the time that is called has already been stated. ## The Faithful Shepherd (Ra'aya Meheimna)

**Six** years you shall sow your field, etc. And in the seventh year <note>Leviticus 25:3-4</note> it is written: *The seventh shall be a Sabbath of solemn rest.* This is a commandment to merit this seventh year, which gives to the land a Sabbath unto the Lord. And behold, they established its place as the "Daughter of the Seventh." And its purpose is to release <note>note: "Shmita" literally means release or letting drop</note>, as it is written: *But the seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow,* etc. Money is released in the seventh. And to sound the alarm for the commandment of the seven Sabbaticals, to strike the flavor and the bonds for the poor of your people. Because the days of the seven Sabbaths of years, forty-nine years, are dependent upon this place. And for this reason, the Sabbaticals and the Sabbath of the Jubilee are a release of spirit for all. He leaves them to eat. And regarding this, whoever loves the seventh year from the side of the Shekhinah <note>the Divine Presence</note>, which is sanctified as seven, gives forgiveness to the poor, like the Assembly of Israel from the side of the Righteous One <note>term: Tzadik - referring to the Sefirah of Yesod</note>, the seventh for the Assembly. And he adds blessing to the world, and there is joy and strength from the side of the Higher Lord, of whom it is said "seven," to the place called Charity <note>term: Tzedakah</note>, to pour out blessing on the day of your rest. Seven cries to the right... and then for the Assembly of Israel, as we have established. For this reason, to rectify the general rule... forty-nine... for the Higher Mother, the Sabbath of Sabbaths, the Sabbath within which *you shall proclaim liberty* <note>Leviticus 25:10</note>.

# At Mount Sinai

And the wise should strive to arrange the Torah so that the Holy Temples may be sustained. Rabbi Shimon said: Behold, we have found from all that was said that the service of the King’s House <note>The Temple</note> in its innermost parts is like the King’s House in every place—like the King Himself, who is the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>. And he established for them a pillar, which is the pillar of all that belongs to Him. Just as in the King’s House and the Holy Temple, all of Israel need His company for their hearts, to learn from Him and to rectify themselves in the Holy Temple. Here, who is lacking in the interior? For those who are called the "Two Houses of the Lord." He said to him: Holy merit! There are two houses that are dedications for the heart, and they are two merits, and two inner houses—the two chambers of the heart. <note>The Zohar often parallels the physical architecture of the Temple with the spiritual anatomy of the human soul and heart.</note> And there are two sights in the various colors, and houses of flight... there shall be a redemption and a rest for the heart, to dwell in the heart for the protection of the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> and for those far away who are brought near. As it is written: "Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near," and we have established that "far" refers to one far from transgression, and "near" refers to one near to a commandment. At that time.

**The Commandment** <note>original: "Pekuda"</note> to sound the Shofar blast during the Jubilee year and on the New Year. Inside, they are renewed, those who are shaded face to face, mouth to mouth, such as the connection of the letters <note>referring to the mystical bonding of Divine names</note> face to face and eye to eye, and in the secret of the "whip that strikes the child." And everything was not "One" because the Holy One Blessed Be He was not with the Shekhinah. And the priesthood is further removed from the Shekhinah, distanced from her husband below. ## Main Text (Zohar)

...they are bound to dwell within his soul, and a defect that cannot be repaired with wealth, nor will they be diminished at all in the **World to Come**. Take from them a logical inference <term>Kal Va-Chomer (a formal rabbinic logical argument from minor to major)</term> regarding washings; for even though the ox is strong, its wings awaken the spirit of the Lord within it.

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **At Mount Sinai** <-

"The Lord’s portion is His people" <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>. And because of this, He gave them the Torah which is hidden. This is "My Name forever, and this is My memorial unto all generations" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>. And so they established it: the letters **Y-H** <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton</note> with "My Name" <note>Hebrew: *Shemi*</note> equals 365 <note>The number of negative commandments</note>. And the letters **V-H** <note>The last two letters</note> with "My memorial" <note>Hebrew: *Zichri*</note> equals 248 <note>The number of positive commandments</note>, making the full count <note>613</note>. From the end, He calls to Israel as a likeness of one who eats everything. And a friend and benefactor of yours takes a portion of his grapes and his metal. And because of this, "he shall divide with God," and so on. Israel must be enlightened in their conduct and their paths. The verse says: "When you walk, it shall lead you; when you sleep, it shall keep you; and when you awake, it shall talk with you" <note>Proverbs 6:22</note>. There are 365 students and a wise man... and all of them are portions... this one nourishes and remembers to speak these words, all of them are the 365 of the Lord on every side, and nothing goes outside of Him on any of His sides.

**And if** you shall say: "What shall we eat?" and so on <note>Leviticus 25:20</note>. Rabbi Yehuda opened with the verse: **"Trust in the Lord, and do good; dwell in the land, and cherish faithfulness"** <note>Psalms 37:3</note>. A person should always be mindful of his Master, and his heart should be righteous with supernal faith <term>Mehemanuta: the Aramaic term for mystical faith/trust</term>, so that he may be whole with his Master. For when he is whole with Him, all the people of the world cannot harm him. <term>Come and see</term> <note>Aramaic: *Ta Chazi*, a standard Zoharic invitation to deeper insight</note>: **"Trust in the Lord, and do good."** Here we have learned: through the action below, the action Above is awakened. This is what they established regarding the verse "And you shall do them" <note>Leviticus 26:3</note>—as if to say, you "made" them. For your awakening to perform repairs below awakens the Above. And the secret of **"and do good"** is as it is written, "and the strength of the good..." referring to the Righteous One <note>The Sefirah of Yesod</note>, as it is written: **"Say of the righteous, that it shall be well [good] with him"** <note>Isaiah 3:10</note>. Since those below perform these actions, certainly this "Good" is awakened. Then, **"dwell in the land, and cherish faithfulness"**—and it is all one. "Dwell in the land and cherish faithfulness," for you have no one who can guard her <note>The Shekhinah/Divine Presence, symbolized by the Land</note> until this "Good" is awakened toward her. Once it is awakened for her, as it were, He "makes" it, and then "dwell in the land" certainly—in tranquility he shall eat and delight with her, and "cherish faithfulness." This is the Land, and it is all one, and "faithfulness" is as we said. "And cherish faithfulness" means he provides for all her desires. But if this "Good" is not awakened toward her, she distances herself from him, and he cannot draw near to her... for he is like one who flees from death. For then a fire flees and burns the world for all its sins. But when this "Good" is awakened toward her, then the grace of the wine... <unclear>textual corruption</unclear>. Come and see: those of faith mention this desire every day. Who are the "children of faith"? Those who loosen their purse strings for her and do not pity their own wealth, knowing that <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> will give him more. <term>As you would say</term>: "There is one who scatters, yet increases more" <note>Proverbs 11:24</note>. And all this is because this awakens blessings toward him. He should not wait and say, "If I give this now, what will I have for tomorrow?" Rather, <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> gives him blessings without end, as they have established. And in this manner: **"And if you shall say: What shall we eat in the seventh year?"** and so on. What is written? **"Then I will command My blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years"** <note>Leviticus 25:21</note>. "And it shall bring forth"—it is mixed, and faith benefits him so that he does not worry about his Sabbatical year and the like, and does not perform work. It is written: "And I will command for you on the sixth day bread for two days," and so on. In this same way: "I will command My blessing upon you in the sixth year," and so on. Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose were walking on the way and reached a certain mountain. They found two men walking. Meanwhile, they saw a man coming toward them. He said to them, as if mocking, "Stand up for him!" <note>referring to a mezuzah or a holy object</note>. He opened and said: "It is written, these two eyes that were darkened..." <note>The story transitions into an anecdotal account of a traveler and a poor man</note>. One of you was blinded... two men, and he took out his food into his lap and came to the path and gave it to him, and he ate and gave him drink. His companion said to him: "What will you do for your own food, for we have nothing to eat?" He said to him: "What is it to you? I will go and sit with this poor man." He went until he had eaten everything he had... and he gave much to the traveler and went on his way. Rabbi Hiyya said: "This is what <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> desires, that it be done through us." Rabbi Yose said: "Perhaps... for that man, and for the sake of <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> to prepare before him this, in order to sacrifice to Him." While they were walking with that man on the way, his companion said to him: "Did I not say..."

## Main Text (Zohar)

Sometimes it is said: "You shall surely give" <note>original: *natan titten*</note> to the one who lacks. Rabbi Hiyya said: Every day, we would prepare a basket of food for ourselves. One day, they sought to find merit for a certain man, for his children were like those who are impoverished, lacking the radiance of life below, and now he was being praised by the Eye <note>referring to Divine Providence</note> and it was written of him as a male figure. Meanwhile, that man was sitting and resting under a tree, and he moved from there to sit in another path. Rabbi Yose said: God established a path for him, and saw that his poverty was meant to hint at a need for money. They stood and went, and meanwhile, they saw a palm-breadth of gold shining near him. Rabbi Hiyya said: Woe to that man if he should open his hand and die <note>meaning, if he takes it selfishly or without merit</note>. Rabbi Yose said: Blessed is that man whom the Holy One, blessed be He, loves so much. Meanwhile, a serpent descended from a hole and sought to kill him. That "palm-breadth" <note>referring to the gold or a protective spirit</note> stood over him and killed the serpent, striking its head while he watched. Rabbi Yose said: Did I not tell you that the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on him and his merit will not depart from him? Meanwhile, that man woke up, stood, and saw it. Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose took hold of him and gave him food to eat. After he ate, they showed him the miracle that the Holy One, blessed be He, had performed for him out of love. Rabbi Yose opened his discourse and said:
> Trust in the Lord and do good; dwell in the land and nourish yourself with faithfulness. (Psalms 37:3)

And all of this is the portion of a man who makes his dwelling place such that "Good" is awakened, and how much more so through Charity <term>Tzedakah: the act of righteous giving which balances the divine attributes</term>. For when Charity is awakened, "Good" is then awakened toward him, written with the letter *Yod*. As it is written:
> And charity delivers from death. (Proverbs 10:2)

This is because Charity is the Tree of Life. It was awakened against that serpent to strike it and kill those who take hold of it, and it improved them from the state of death. Who caused that serpent to be stayed and this "Life of Lives" to be awakened? It was that Charity which he performed; it is as if he "made" it above, as it is written: "Doing charity at all times." And so, he arose and was awakened.

## The Faithful Shepherd (Raya Mehemna)

**And you shall leave them as an inheritance** to your children after you... forever you shall work with them. This is the commandment to work with a Canaanite servant <term>Eved Kena'ani: a non-Jewish servant who has a specific legal and mystical status in Torah law</term>. As it is written:
> You shall work with them forever. (Leviticus 25:46)

And these are from the side of Metatron <note>the supreme angel and heavenly scribe</note>, servants upon whom the profanation of "Canaan, a servant of servants shall he be to his brothers" descends. Not just a servant of servants, but a servant to that "Eternal Servant" <note>Metatron</note> who is the tail of the tree. And if you say that he is a "thigh of fire" and a "small servant," it is not so in their essence. <margin>The burden of the servant is marked</margin> For he was tested and pierced, perhaps in his blessing when He blessed Abraham. Rather, certainly here lies the secret of Reincarnation <term>Gilgula: the cycling of souls</term>; the wheel turns and returns to the place of the "dark servant." This is the secret of the mixture of drops in a place that is not his own. See that he requires his own "garment" like a soul. The daughter of Ishmael entered, or the daughter of El, to all those who are mixed with evil. But his "drop" is the Good Light, as in "And God saw the light that it was good." He mixed good with evil, a servant on a high level... and from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil you shall not eat. The Holy One, blessed be He, is within you, for He mixed it and clothed him in the reincarnation of the Holy One, blessed be He—an action that is lacking the power to be recognized in the firstborn, to separate good from evil, which are the "donkey" and the "priest," impurity and purity, fit and unfit. Without the separation of evil from good, one cannot be awakened in it, and the good will have more power and it will become a "House of Beauty." The Holy One, blessed be He, separated them... to put a "taste" on both of them, after they stand for the World to Come. For he is the side of this world, as it is written of Joseph: "he was a youth with the sons of Bilhah," sustaining and nourishing, just as one establishes "you shall surely leave it with him." On the right, sustenance and nourishment are divided, and the vision is below, and the spirit is with your place and it shall be given to you... until it reaches the Kingdom <term>Malchut: the final Divine emanation associated with the physical world</term> and finds it. A complete righteous man is all-encompassing, with nourishment below; a complete wicked man has his vision above and his nourishment below. And besides this, there is the enmity between two levels... as revealed in the secret of the inns...

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Behar, focusing on the mystical status of the soul during sleep and the dual identity of the People of Israel as both "servants" and "children" of the Divine. ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**At Mount Sinai**<-

Because they know that the holy days and all [spiritual states] are hinted at from Above. When human beings sleep and are slumbering in sleep, [the soul] does not remain holy within them, as it is written: *And the eyes of the wicked shall fail* <note>Job 11:20</note>. Because of this, it is prepared for a person until they sleep; they know and establish it because [the Sitra Achra/Other Side] is not found to rule over him. A **new soul** <note>Aramaic: *nishmata chadata*; the Zohar teaches that the soul is renewed each night during sleep</note> is joined to him, in which there is rest for the Holy One, blessed be He. For he has established a desire-filled order through his mouth, and more worlds... and all his preparations are the rectification of the Throne below. It stands more firmly and is gathered into the **Foundation** <note>The sefirah of Yesod</note>, and he subdues it for the Holy One, blessed be He. And Sinai is in prayer... and by the word of the whole world... in the secret and the power of the Torah to establish oneself for existence... and not only that, but merit dwells in the place of the assembly... and for all the masters of the guard... the Garden of Eden... the light is whitened in many forms...

And because of this, he bent the offering in the eye, and man was hidden... for everyone who is accustomed... to make him righteous... righteous is his law and righteous are his intestines... and to be rectified through him with the merit of laughter <note>A reference to Isaac, whose name *Yitzchak* means "he will laugh"</note>... and he dwelt in it like the living... the dross was finished from him, and he bent the dross outward... Afterward came Jacob, and he joined with them and became a **servant** to the Holy Prophet <note>referring to Jacob's service to Laban</note>: *I will serve you seven years for Rachel* <note>Genesis 29:18</note>... to bring forth two drops of seed... and not the uncovering of nakedness... and he brought them out from Laban... and in the end there is no end... and the merit of the law in Isaac, and the merit of the intestines in Jacob... and because of this, a good servant causes... and an evil servant likewise... they made for the body... pleasures... from their love... in the numerical value <note>Gematria</note>... and from the other side the people...

---

**For** *the children of Israel are servants to Me* <note>Leviticus 25:55</note>. This is a commandment to leave off all types of labor in the Sanctuary and outside the Sanctuary. In the Sanctuary, in all those services called "Work" <note>Aramaic: *Avodah*; also means worship</note>; and in **Exile** <note>Galuta</note>, to look after the commandments of their Master, included in the laws of service like a servant who looks after his master for everything he needs. Because Israel are called "servants," as it is written: *For the children of Israel are servants to Me, they are My servants.* What is the reason they are servants? Because it is written: *whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt.* Regarding another servant it is written... from the burden of the Egyptians, to serve Him like a servant who works for his master who redeemed him from death and redeemed him from all the evils of the world.

They are called "Israel" by the Holy One, blessed be He; they are called **"Servant,"** as it is written: *You are My servant, Israel* <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>; and they are called **"Children,"** as it is written: *You are children to the Lord your God* <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note>.

When a person knows the Holy One, blessed be He, in a **general way**, then he is called a "servant" who performs the commandment of his master, but has no permission to search through his hidden treasures or the vessels of his house.

When a person knows Him in a **particular way**, then he is called a "beloved son," like a son who searches through the hidden treasures and the vessels of his father's house. And one is only called a "son" when he merits [closeness to] the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said: *Israel is My son, My firstborn* <note>Exodus 4:22</note>. And all this removes him from the category of a [mere] servant, to act for his Master in all services that will bring honor to his Master.

And so it is necessary for every man to be toward his Master as a **son**, to search into His hidden treasures and to know the **secrets** <note>Razin</note> of His house; and to be toward his Master as a **servant**, because these two levels are from Above, and a person needs to be crowned with them. They are the spirit of piety and holy **faith** <note>Mehaimanuta</note>. One is the spirit of a servant, and one is the spirit of a son. And what is called a servant? All of these. Just as we established: "For the children of Israel [are servants]," and all of them are one spirit of faith. A person must be crowned with these levels to be included in the secret of faith. A servant to perform all types of worship in exile... a high spirit that never rests... and this is what he said regarding other services... he rectifies and serves. And because of this, he is called "this," because that servant who serves is called "this," and everyone who needs to be crowned with this spirit...

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Zohar on Sinai** <-

This is to merit being a servant, to perform the service that is incumbent upon him, and to be crowned so as to reach this degree. <note>The "Servant" level represents disciplined, awe-based service.</note> Anyone who is blessed in all types of service before the world and its existence is called "blessed." Regarding this, happy is the portion of the one who merits this and stands before Him to know the One who sustains his heart with reward; his words are for the good of all prophecy, and this is the word that rules over all. One who exerts himself in the Torah to know the Holy One, Blessed be He, in general, should not perform his work as a mere laborer; rather, when he looks to know Him in a specific degree, he is then called a "Son." <note>The "Son" level represents service based on love, intimacy, and understanding of the Divine mysteries.</note> In the explanation of the voice of the yoke, like a scale, a person must include both of them: to be both a Servant and a Son, and to be crowned by the Holy One, Blessed be He. One whose service is of a lower nature must still establish within it the aspect of the Servant and the Sustainer, to be included in these higher degrees above. This is also a great holiness: for a servant to perform the service of the strength of the worlds, to cleave his will to the spirit of Wisdom, and to cleave to his Master in higher matters as is fitting. A Son cleaves constantly to his Father without any separation at all, and no one can protest his actions. A Servant performs the service of his Master and prepares the rectifications of the world. One who possesses both in a single inclusion attains Kindness <term>Chesed: the sefirah of expansive love</term>; this is the secret of all Faith in one inclusion without any separation at all, connecting everything as one. This is the "Man of the Holy One, Blessed be He," of whom it is written: *In all My house, he is faithful* <note>Numbers 12:7, referring to Moses</note>. He guards all the worlds, and in all types and standings they are remembered; from them emerges the King of all that is hidden, who holds them in His hand. And they all took pity and shone like this world, and they all took pity in the World to Come. This is the commandment and the thought, and for the resolution of man and the daughter of all worlds, they all cry out. It is necessary for all possessions and guards to be joyful before Him. He called to the Sustainer—those are the ones who are alone—and he called to the Master of Foundations to be for the Individual, to be before Him in Unity, and for Unity to be practiced by the Unique One. The secret of these two degrees is supported as one by the verse that is written: *And He said to me, "You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified"* <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>. "And He said to me, You are My servant"—this refers to the Servant. "Israel"—this refers to the Male <note>The "Son" or the higher masculine aspect of the soul</note>. They are all one, and then it is written: "in whom I will be glorified." Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen.

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the spiritual mechanics of holiness versus impurity, specifically focusing on the actions of Balak and Balaam as archetypes of sorcery. It corresponds to Zohar, Volume 3, Folio 110b.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**At Mount Sinai**<-

Corresponding to this, he made them through action. Come and see: there was <term>divination</term> <note>original: *kesem*</note>, and he was a great sage in his actions and in his whisperings—referring to Balaam. And such is the portion of every person who desires anything in this world through the service of the Holy One, blessed be He: he must awaken it through an action. For through an action below, an awakening is caused high above. And this action must be done in holiness, as the companions have established, and in a permitted manner.

For there is no matter or word of the mouth that does not depend upon an action to awaken it above. And just as we must awaken supernal holiness through both action and word, so too those species that come from the **side of impurity** <note>original: *sitra de-masabuta*</note> require their side to be awakened through action and the word of the mouth.

And as for Balaam, he was a greater sage than all the sorcerers of the world. He was a supernal sage within the "husk" <note>the *kelipah*, or the shell of impurity that conceals holiness</note>, as has been established. **Divination** <note>original: *kesem*</note> and **enchantment** <note>original: *nachash*</note> are two distinct levels. Divination depends upon a physical action. Enchantment does not depend upon action, but rather upon gazing and the word of the mouth. Then, a spirit of impurity is awakened upon them, which shows them things as they are, and he performs what he performs.

But Israel is holy; they are a force that is entirely holy. All their actions are intended to awaken the **Holy Spirit** <note>original: *rucha de-kudsha*</note> upon them, until "a spirit from on high is poured out upon us." And concerning this, it is written:
> For there is no enchantment in Jacob, and no divination in Israel. <note>Numbers 23:23</note>

For they are grasped within the side of supernal holiness; their actions come through holiness, and holiness is awakened upon them, and they are clothed within it.

Come and see: Balak was the greatest of all sages in divination, and Balaam son of Beor knew the exact hour. When Balak desired to join with him, what is written? "And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went with the instruments of divination in their hand." And Balaam’s work was as one with them. In the word of his mouth, he was greater than all the sorcerers of the world, and through the gazing of that "enchantment," he knew how to aim for the precise moment.

Therefore, Balak sought to combine the two matters: divination and enchantment. He intended to cast them against the Holy One, blessed be He, and His assembly. But before Him stood the "children of action" <note>the Israelites performing the Tabernacle service</note>, in whom all evil sides were prepared to be nullified. The sorcerers of the world could not draw near to them, for they all fled from before them. What were these actions? The appointed coverings, the holy exchanges, the conclusions of the Sanctuary, and the incense of spices that nullifies all wrath and anger above and below. They would sacrifice and draw near every day at the two altars to perform the service, the timing, the Showbread, the washing of the Basin, and many purifications for the action of the word of the mouth... and the two Tablets... to atone for the people and to dwell among them every day.

Once that wicked man [Balaam] perceived this, he said: "For there is no enchantment in Jacob, and no divination in Israel." For the Lord is his portion, his people, and "the shout of a King is among them." And "O My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab counseled" <note>Micah 6:5</note>. He remembers that and sets it aside—how Balak and Balaam joined to do them evil, but they could not... from the heavens the spheres told of the blow...

However, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: "In the places of My dwelling, be mindful at all times that you are grasped in Me." Then that wicked man, with his crafts and divinations, could not do you evil. But once you let go of your hands to sin against Me and committed harlotry at Shittim, what is written? "And the people began [to commit harlotry]..." <note>Numbers 25:1</note>. Then their protection was removed... and all this was "that you may know the righteous acts of the Lord" <note>Micah 6:5</note>. All those perfections that I performed for you were so that you would have the strength to be grasped in Him, so that no word in the world could harm you, and the wrath of above and below and evil species could not draw near to you...

Come and see: regarding the assembly of the "profane" <note>the mundane or impure forces</note> that strikes during the day or two, all their seals are upon the night. Many sages toil on the side of the profane... but the great seal over all is from the side of Holiness. And that wicked man was rebuked... a supernal blow from all... and he fell before his throne in the night... they worshipped with all his assembly... and there was no joining with him to let him know...

## Bechukotai

This is "And God was" <note>original: *vayehi Elohim*</note>, prepared for the peaceful ones, that which you merited with Him, and it shall be complete. <term>Your wise men</term> <note>referring to the magicians of Egypt or advisors of kings</note> are all in this manner; in every place they call upon Him with grace and mercy, and in the end, you merited His completion more than they established. And all these sorcerers and wise men were in your time, as it is written: "And the King [Pharaoh] gathered your wise men" <note>referring to Pharaoh's magicians in Exodus</note>, and "perfectly through the window." It is written here "through the window" and it is written there: "Through the window she looked forth and peered, the mother of Sisera" <note>Judges 5:28</note>. Therefore, they have already established it regarding Balaam; and concerning all of them it is written: "And God came to Balaam," "And God was with Balaam," and "And God came to Laban." Your wise men in the end reached the level of a prophet, and they are with him because they have no prepared place of their own. And if you say, "But it is written 'magicians' <note>Hebrew: *chartumim*</note>," rather, this matter is shared with emptiness, and they are a command like the magicians of the reading; and in this general rule, we see that the magicians are lacking. <margin>From here</margin> they were of this general rule, and because of this they were called so. And that wicked one [Balaam] would speak through his stylus <note>a play on *cheret*, the root of *chartumim*</note>, and they called him a prophet for the sake of the correction. Because of this it is written, "And God came to Pharaoh," and his sides were with you, speaking with a tongue, and seven windows. That wicked one used himself, for it is not written except "And God came." And if you say that he was found in prophecy as a prophet—rather, it was through many observations. In Ecclesiastes, there was a time he looked at the stars, the hour stood still, and "he did not go as at other times to seek omens." "And Balaam saw that it was good in the eyes of the Lord to bless Israel" <note>Numbers 24:1</note>. From the folly of the day, he looked at the stars and the hour, and it was not found in other living invitations, for great wrath was not found in the world then; he knew "that it was good in the eyes of the Lord to bless Israel." At that time, he attached himself [to the vision] apart from all the anger in the world and did not look at them. Come and see: at that hour when mercy is found, then he is sent to a place, and in the end, that wicked one knew the place to strike on the side of strength and wisdom. At that time, it was not found; what is written?
> "How shall I curse whom God has not cursed? And how shall I denounce whom the Lord has not denounced?" <note>Numbers 23:8</note>
And as my people, "remember now what Balak king of Moab counseled..." <note>Micah 6:5</note> and what Balaam son of Beor answered him. Because of this, all of Israel and all the collections of their Master, He prepared them so.

---

**If** you walk in My statutes <note>Leviticus 26:3</note>. Come and see how many times the decrees of life for freedom depend on that place; all this and three engraved engravings were found as a statute <note>Hebrew: *Chukkah*</note>, for they are not called so [otherwise], and decrees for freedom are viewed thus. "And keep My commandments": My judgments <note>Hebrew: *Mishpatai*</note>, this is the strength of another place, the male world engraved the world and the seal is in it. They are joined one to another, which are the lower ones, and all the commands of freedom, and all the decrees of freedom, and all the sanctities of freedom are in these matters. Because of this Torah, as it is written, "And take the Oral Torah," and regarding this, "If in My statutes" refers to all those decrees, laws, punishments, and commandments of the Torah in their grace in that place called "Statute" <note>*Chukkah*</note>. "And keep My commandments" refers to that place called "Torah," as it is written, "Every judgment is for the God of Jacob." This is tied to that, and not [only] to that; and all of this and that is the totality of the Holy Name. And for one who performs the words of the Torah, all of them are the "face" of the Holy Name, because Statute and Judgment are the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore, "If you walk in My statutes" refers to the <term>Oral Torah</term> <note>The traditional explanations and laws passed down verbally</note>, and "keep My commandments" refers to the <term>Written Torah</term> <note>The Five Books of Moses</note>, and this is the end of the totality of the Holy Name. "And you shall do them" <note>Leviticus 26:3</note>. What is "and you shall do them"? To the one who performs the commandments of the Torah and walks in their statutes, it is as if—if it were possible to say—he "made" Him above. This is the Holy One, blessed be He; approach His altar and they established it, etc., "and you shall do them." "And you shall do them" certainly refers to the flow and the awakening upon them to join one with another, so that the Holy Name is found as is fitting; "and you shall do them." In this manner, Rabbi <unclear>...</unclear> said: "And David made a name" <note>2 Samuel 8:13</note>. Did David actually "make" the Name? Rather, because he walked in the paths of the Torah and performed the commandments of freedom and increased his kingdom as is fitting, it is as if he "made" the Name above. There was no other king in the world who merited this.

<summary>This page discusses the nature of Balaam's prophecy as being external and dependent on specific astrological timing, contrasting it with the internal holiness of Israel. It then transitions into the mystical significance of the Torah's statutes and judgments, explaining that performing the commandments "perfects" or "makes" the Divine Name on high.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Bechukotai, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of charity and the unification of the Divine Name.</meta>

->Bechukotai<-

Even in this generation, how much service is performed at night, praising the Holy One, blessed be He, until the Holy Name rises like a throne <note>original: "k'khursaya"</note> according to the prayer that rises before Him in his days. It is as if he actually makes the Name itself. This is what is written: *“And the son of the Israelite woman blasphemed <insert>pronounced</insert> the Name and cursed”* (Lev. 24:11). And the pleasantness of David said, and regarding this it is written: *“And you shall do <note>or 'make'</note> them”* (Lev. 26:3). And if you say that those who are refined enough to do them and to establish the Holy Name as is fitting, all those blessings above are found through them and through their proper rectifications.

**And I will give** your rains in their season, etc. All these phrases of "And I will give" and "And I will place" are words that depend on them <note>the people's actions</note>; they are the rectification of your work, which is the Holy Name, as it is written:
> *And they shall keep the way of the Lord to do righteousness <term>Tzedakah: charity or justice</term> and justice* (Genesis 18:19).

Now, since it is written "And they shall keep the way of the Lord," why does it add "to do righteousness and justice"? Rather, whoever occupies himself with the path of the Torah, it is as if he is busy with righteousness and justice, and he "makes" righteousness and justice—which is the Holy One, blessed be He. Silver is hers and wine <note>original: "chamra"</note>—woe to the children of men who do not know and do not look upon the glory of their Master! Who makes the Holy Name every day? I would say: he who gives charity to the poor. Come and see, the establishment is thus: for the poor man desires it by right <note>din</note>, and all their food is by right. It is the place where Justice <note>Tzedek</note> is engraved, as it is said:
> *A prayer of the afflicted when he is faint* (Psalms 102:1).

This prayer is the "Prayer of the Hand" <note>the Tefillin of the hand, representing the Shekhinah</note> as we have established. And whoever gives charity to the poor man, he makes the Holy Name above. Charity <note>Tzedakah</note> assists properly because this charity is the Tree of Life, and Charity gives to Justice <note>Tzedek</note>, and when he gives to Justice, then this is joined with that, and the Holy Name is found to be complete. Whoever does this causes an awakening below, and certainly it is as if he makes the Holy Name. That is to say, just as he acts below, so he awakens it above. And regarding this it is written:
> *Happy are those who keep justice, who do righteousness at all times* (Psalms 106:3).

"Who do righteousness"—this is the Holy One, blessed be He; it is as if he "makes" Him. Come and find this through the wine: who is it for both of them? Because the poor man has no life of his own at all, except for what they give him; and the Moon has no light of its own, except for what the Sun gives it. Come and see: a poor man is considered as if dead. Why? Because that place <note>his spiritual root</note> causes it for him, for he is found in the place of death, and therefore he is called dead. He who brings life upon him by giving him charity, the Tree of Life dwells upon him, as it is said:
> *And righteousness <insert>charity</insert> delivers from death* (Proverbs 10:2).

And just as a man acts below, so it is actually done above. Blessed is the portion of one who merits to make the Holy Name above! Therefore, charity rises above all, and so the word "charity" is for its own sake, for it awakens Charity toward Justice and joins them as one, to make everything the Holy Name as is fitting. For this is below, and no name is found like "Charity," as it is written: *“In righteousness <note>Tzedakah</note> you shall be established,”* and this is said of the Assembly of Israel. And because of this: *“And you shall do <note>make</note> them,”* etc.

**And I will give** peace in the land, and you shall lie down and none shall make you afraid, etc. Rabbi Yose opened:
> *Rejoice in the Lord, O you righteous...* (Psalms 33:1).

"Rejoice in the Lord, O you righteous"—I am wondering about this verse as it was established: that a man needs to make the Good Inclination rejoice over the Evil Inclination. And it is good for everyone at the time when evening falls and a man lies on his bed, many "guards of the laws" <note>spiritual prosecutors</note> are awakened in the world and go wandering about. And that is the time to sing before the Holy One, blessed be He, and to fear, so that his soul is not found among them. For they are ready to gather and surround a man so that he does not let a word of folly <note>original: "tipu"</note> escape his mouth, so that he does not awaken them toward him and they are not found with him. This is what is written:
> *Commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.* (Psalms 4:5).

So that no word should leave his mouth. Come and see: at the time when Israel is found worthy before the Holy One, blessed be He, what is written? *“And I will give peace in the land”*—both above and below. The Holy One, blessed be He, joins with the Assembly of Israel then, and *“you shall lie down and none shall make you afraid.”* Why? *“And I will rid evil beasts out of the land.”*
