# Main Text (Zohar)

It shall not be lacking, so that it shall be among you. And come and see: the "side of death" <note>referring to the forces of impurity or the Angel of Death</note> and all his company are merely husks. At the time when the Holy One takes this side away, it is said: "and a sword shall not pass through your land." Rabbi Abba said: We have established that this means even a "sword of peace," such as the army of Pharaoh Necho <note>referring to a friendly army passing through to fight someone else</note>. "And a sword shall not pass"—neither the "side of death" nor its company. I will cause the evil force to cease so it does not pass through the land; even a mere passing shall not happen to you. Even the sword of other nations, and even an armed man, shall not pass through you. 

And regarding King Josiah, the sages established that he was seized because of the sins of Israel, as it is written: *The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the Lord, was taken in their pits* <note>Lamentations 4:20</note>. Here one must look closely: for we have learned that if the head of the people is good, all the people are set right through him. If the head of the people is not strong, all the people are seized for their sins. But here, the head of the generation was good and his deeds were proper, yet he was seized for the sins of Israel. For they did not believe in the Lord and did not listen to him, for Israel thought they were all as righteous as he was. In the end, Jeremiah said to him: "They do not stand with you," and because of that, he was seized for their sins. And as long as he is king over Israel, the light shines and seeks to ascend.

---

**"And I will set my Tabernacle among you..."** <note>Leviticus 26:11</note> "And I will set my Tabernacle"—this is the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>the Divine Presence, personified as feminine</note> who is called my "Pledge" <note>original: *Mashkona*</note>, for she is taken as a pledge for the sins of Israel. "And I will set my Tabernacle"—a pledge indeed! Like a person who has a beloved friend and wants to go and dwell with him. The friend says, "How do I know you will dwell with me?" for he is ashamed <note>or feels unworthy</note>, as it is written: *and I will accompany him.* The friend says, "Here is a pledge for you, so that I shall never be separated from you." 

So the Holy One, Blessed Be He, desired to dwell among Israel. What did He do? He took His most precious "object" <note>the Shekhinah</note> and brought her down to Israel. He said to them: "Take this, my pledge, to be with you, so that I will never be separated from you." For even though the Holy One, Blessed Be He, may be distant from us, He left His pledge in our hands, and we hold onto that precious object of His body. When we see His pledge, we know He will come to dwell with us. Thus: "And I will set my Tabernacle among you"—I will give a pledge into your hands so that I may dwell with you. And even though Israel is in Exile <note>original: *Galuta*</note>, the pledge of the Holy One is with them, and they never leave it. 

"And my soul shall not loathe you." Like a person who loves his friend and wants to dwell with him; what does he do? He takes his bed <note>original: *Arsa*</note> and brings it to his friend's house. He says, "Behold, my bed is in your house so that I will not distance my bed from yours." So the Holy One said: "And I will set my Tabernacle among you, and my soul shall not loathe you"—behold, my bed is among you. Since my bed is with you, you will know that I am not separated from you, and because of this, "my soul shall not loathe you."

For the Lord goes about as one who walks within your camp to save you and to deliver your enemies before you; therefore shall your camp be holy. 

Rabbi Isaac and Rabbi Judah were walking one night in a village near the Sea of Tiberias. They rose at midnight. Rabbi Isaac said to Rabbi Judah: Let us engage in the Torah, for this crown <note>the Torah</note> does not wish to be separated from the "Bundle of Life."

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar, specifically transitioning from the themes of leadership and the Tabernacle to the relationship between the Divine and Israel during times of exile. It draws heavily on the imagery of the Song of Songs.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Chukat** <-
<note>original: "Chukat" - The title of the Torah portion, though the text here bridges several sections.</note>

In their districts he shall be praised. What is written? *And he would return to the camp, but his servant Joshua the son of Nun, a young man, did not depart from the tent.* <note>Exodus 33:11</note> Why Joshua? Because he is like the **moon** <note>original: "ke-sihara"</note> in relation to the **sun** <note>original: "shimsha" - referring to Moses</note>. He is below, and he guards the **Matronita** <note>The Queen/Divine Presence</note>, and because of this, *he did not depart from the tent.* He did not receive permission to pass the burden to those below. So it is with the Matronita; she is in his hands, for they [the leaders] rule over her, and the Matronita shall be with them so they are not separated from her. It is unthinkable for her to be separated from the midst of Israel, never to return to them; rather, the Matronita remains with them, and because of her, He [the King] does not abandon them. In every place where Israel sinned against the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, His Matronita did not leave them, and He did not take her away from their midst. Even in every place where Israel was exiled, the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence</note> went with them. Regarding this it is written:
> *I will place My sanctuary in your midst, and My soul shall not abhor you.* <note>Leviticus 26:11</note>

Rabbi Isaac opened his discourse and said:
> *My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag; behold, he stands behind our wall...* <note>Song of Songs 2:9</note>

Worthy are the people of Israel, who merited that the Matronita was not taken from them by the Supernal King. For even though they are in **exile** <note>original: "galuta"</note>, the Holy One, Blessed be He, comes on every New Moon, Sabbath, and Festival to look upon them and to take delight in that Matronita of His who is with them, for she is His longing. This is like a King whose Matronita fled from his palace. What did she do? She took her son, the King’s longing and his beloved. Because the King’s mind is constantly upon her, it is found in her hand. Just as the King’s desire rises for the Matronita and for her son, he climbs through chambers, corners, houses, and **levels** <note>original: "dargin"</note>; he climbs to look and to peer through the cracks of the walls upon them. Once he sees them from the chambers, from the holes and the crevices of the wall, he then departs. So it is with Israel: because they are the King’s delight, that Matronita did not leave them. And because the King’s mind is constantly upon them, He is with them. Just as the desire of the Holy King rises for the Matronita and for Israel, He climbs through chambers and visits the hills—many levels—and climbs like a gazelle to look and peer through the crevices of the wall at them. Once He sees them from the chambers, this is what is written: *My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag... behold, he stands behind our wall.* It is written "wall" and it is written "levels." *He peers through the windows*—looking at the congregation with the eyes of the windows; *He peeks through the lattices* to look and observe Israel. Because of this, one must rejoice on that day when they see and know that He lives, and Israel rejoices in this day with You, O Lord, in revelation and joy.

---

**And if** you shall despise My statutes: <note>Leviticus 26:15</note> Rabbi Yose opened:
> *My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; neither be weary of His correction.* <note>Proverbs 3:11</note>

How beloved are Israel before the Holy One, Blessed be He, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to rebuke them and lead them in the straight path. As it is written, He is like a father to his son, whose very existence depends on him; he must lead him with the **rod** <note>original: "sarvita"</note> of **correction** <note>original: "tochachata"</note> so that he does not stray to the right or the left. This is what is written:
> *For whom the Lord loves He corrects; even as a father the son in whom he delights.* <note>Proverbs 3:12</note>

But for one whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not love, He suppresses His rebuke and removes the rod from him. It is written: *I will remove from you...* The Lord desires those who return to Him. His greatness and His rod are always there to lead them. Therefore, if He removes the rod and removes the correction, it is because He does not desire him, for his portion is far from His soul. He strikes you only to draw you near. Because of this: *My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; neither be weary of His correction.* He strikes, but do not be weary; you shall be mended by it. Do not be like one who flees from the healers. Come and hear: when Justice is awakened in judgment, many sides of purity are awakened on the right and the left. Many rods go out from there: rods of **Kindness** <note>original: "Chesed"</note>, rods of coals, and rods of rebuke. All of them go out and are awakened in the world to receive the voice of their supplications. And for those who are destroyed, the worthy ones receive Kindness...

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the portion of Bechukotai, specifically interpreting the "sevenfold" punishments mentioned in Leviticus 26. It transitions from a mystical description of the "Great Deep" to a poignant parable about the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) accompanying Israel into exile.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

In the hollow of the great deep <note>original: *be-nuqba di-tehoma rabba*</note>, droplets are planted, and a licking fire joins with them. Coals emerge, ascending and descending, and they are found standing opposite the children of men. This is what is written: "And I will scatter..." <note>referring to the scattering of Israel</note>. And it is said to them: "Return to the bottom to rejoice there," for at the time of their rebuke upon rebuke, He did not continue to receive praise for the sake of their praise. What does "did not continue" mean? He did not give a rebuke that would cause the judgment to rejoice in its own kind in the world, but rather a measured rebuke that the world is able to endure. And regarding this, it says: "And I will add <insert>to give</insert> rebuke," and it is a rebuke of life, in order to discipline the bottom: **sevenfold for your sins** <note>Leviticus 26:18</note>. If the world were to receive the full force of the Prophet's "jar" <note>a metaphor for intense prophecy or judgment</note>, the world could not endure it for even a single moment. This is what is written:
> If You, O Lord, should keep account of iniquities, O Lord, who could stand? <note>Psalms 130:3</note>
And yet you say, "sevenfold for your sins"? Rather, what is this "seven"? It is seven corresponding to them. And what is it? It shall not reach the "Seven of Investigations" <note>higher spiritual levels of judgment</note>; rather, from among the seven, the seven shall reach from below. And regarding this: "sevenfold for your sins." There are the "Seven of Investigations" and there is the "Daughter of Seven" <note>original: *Bat Sheva*, referring to the Sefirah of Malchut</note>. What is the difference between this and that? Rather, "Seven" is entirely for performing judgment and executing laws to take vengeance from them without the "Daughter of Seven." But the "Daughter of Seven" is to be joined as one, to illuminate and to rescue the Kingdom <note>original: *Malchuta*</note>, to make the Kingdom known in joy and in everything. "Daughter of Seven" is written; therefore, the Book of the City chose "seven times a day," which is choosing the seven as one, for they were nourished together, and it is all one matter. Rabbi Isaac said:

-> **And I will discipline** <-

**And I will discipline** you, even I, sevenfold for your sins <note>Leviticus 26:24</note>. "And I will discipline you" by the hand of other appointees, as we have established. "Even I, seven"—wait for the bottom to be opposite you; this "seven" is to be awakened upon you. This is the supreme love of the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note>. It is like a king who had an only son who sinned before the king. One day, he offended the king. The king said: "All these days I have beaten you and you did not accept it. From now on, what shall I do to you? If I drive you away from my gates and send you out of the kingdom, perhaps the bears of the field or the wolves of the field or bandits will overtake you and remove you from the world. What shall I do? Rather, I and you shall leave the world together." So too, "Even I"—I and you shall leave the land. "Even I" am with you; I and you in exile <note>original: *galuta*</note>, and we shall go out as one. And the King says: "What shall I do for you? Behold, I have beaten you and you did not smell the fragrance of purification. Behold, I come upon you with shield-breakers and masters of lamentation to groan for you, and you shall not be reached. If I send you out of the land, there is fear upon you from many bears and many wolves who will rise against you and remove you from the world. Rather, what shall I do for you? I and you shall leave the land and be in exile." This is what is written: "And I will discipline you" in exile, and you will say you are saved—"Even I" am with you, "sevenfold for your sins." This is what is written: "The blow was cast." The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "You have made yourselves such that we cannot dwell in the world as one. Behold, the Matron <note>original: *Matronita*, the Shekhinah</note> goes out from the Palace with you. Behold, everything is destroyed. My Palace is destroyed, for it is not fitting for a King to have a Palace except when he enters with the Matron. And the joy of the King is not found except at the hour when he enters the Palace to the Matron and is found as one with her in the Palace. Now that they are found together at the bottom, the Palace is entirely desolate. But what shall I do? Even I am with you." And because you have strived to be covered in exile, the Holy One, blessed be He, is found with you and does not ascend to rest. This is the wisdom of what is written: "And the Lord your God will return" <note>Deuteronomy 30:3</note>. And all shall go out, and in perfection, the Holy One, blessed be He, shall return with you, as has been stated. Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose were walking on the way and happened upon a certain cave in a jar-like hollow. Rabbi Hiyya said to Rabbi Yose: "That which is written:
> These are the words of the covenant... besides the covenant which He made with them in Horeb <note>Deuteronomy 28:69</note>
Rabbi Hiyya said: "But we have established these: those that were carved <note>on the tablets</note> and those from the mouth of Moses himself, as has been stated. And all these and those are the 'words of the covenant' that are below."

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Bechukotai, specifically focusing on the endurance of the Covenant during the exile. It transitions from the relationship between the Sabbath and the Covenant to the mystical bond between parents and children.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Bechukotai**<-
<note>Original: "Bechukotai" (In My Statutes). Though the header says "Chukat," the content clearly addresses the end of Leviticus.</note>

Seven times it emerges, and they were the count of the words of the **Covenant**. They depend on "Good" and "Very Good." The "Good" below is filled by the "Good" from the male principle, and the lower part of the male is **Righteousness** <note>The Sefirah of Malkhut</note>, which burns and ignites the Covenant. These words are the words of the Covenant, bound together as one. For this reason, "Remember" and "Observe" <note>The two versions of the Sabbath commandment</note> are tied together as one: "Remember" by day and "Observe" by night. Come and see, the Covenant is as one, and therefore the Covenant is certainly the essence of all things. In every place, the Covenant is in this place. Rabbi Hiyya said: It is certainly so, and therefore the Sabbath—which is "Remember" and "Observe"—is called "Covenant," as it is written:
> And the children of Israel shall observe the Sabbath, to make the Sabbath throughout their generations as an **eternal covenant**. (Exodus 31:16)

And it is all one matter, and this place is called "Covenant" in every place. Come and see, it is written "Peace"; the Priest is the **Foundation** <note>The Sefirah of Yesod</note>, which is the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He—the peace of the home, the peace of the world. "And I will multiply you"—even these seven tribes. This is **Righteousness**, this is certainly the Covenant. And because the words of the Covenant are beautiful, it says: **"And yet for all that"** <note>Leviticus 26:44</note>, when they are in the land of their enemies, and so on. "And yet for all that"—the word "And-yet" (*Ve-Af*) is as it is said, "Also (*Af*) my wisdom stood by me." "Also" (*Gam*) comes to include the one called "This" (*Zot*), who never leaves them. "When they are in the land of their enemies"—when they are all as one. "I will not reject them, nor will I abhor them," because there is not found in them the breaking of My covenant with them. He does not abandon them; "My Covenant" is the **Assembly of Israel** <note>The Sefirah of Malkhut</note>. Therefore, it says "to break My covenant with them." Rabbi Hiyya said: Here I heard a new matter that Rabbi Eleazar said: "I will not reject them, nor will I abhor them to destroy them" <note>Hebrew: *Lekhalotam*</note>—I have not rejected them and I have not killed them. "To destroy them" implies—Heaven forbid—that if one washes in a river, he is careful to receive it, and he enters as if entering before Him. Here, "I will not reject them nor abhor them" in any case, because the closeness of His soul is within them. He gathers them like a beloved. 

"To destroy them" (*Lekhalotam*)—it is written defectively, without the letter *Vav* <note>Leviticus 26:44. Without the Vav, the word can be read as *Le-Kallatam*, "For their Bride"</note>. Because of her, "I will not reject them nor abhor them," because she is the beloved of His soul. His love goes out even when she dwells below in the filth of the Throne. He never enters there without her. Since she washed there, she is like the eyes in the scent of the merchant, where all the good fragrances of the world are found. So too here: "And yet for all that, when they are together in the land of their enemies"—which is the marketplace of the Throne—"I will not reject them nor abhor them." And I see "for their Bride" (*Lekhalotam*), for the love of the one who is the beloved of His soul, who flies and wanders there, and she is to Him like all the good scents of the world, because of that Bride who is within them. And if she were not found there... Rabbi Yose opened and said:
> A son honors his father, and a servant his master. (Malachi 1:6)

A son honors his father... <unclear>textual corruption</unclear>... and they established it regarding food and drink and everything during his lifetime. But after he dies, is he exempt from him? No, for even though he has died, he is upheld in his honor even more. For it is written, "Honor your father." If a son goes on a crooked path, he certainly brings shame to his father. But when a son goes on a straight and proper path and mends his deeds, he certainly honors his father. He honors him in this world among people, and he honors him in that world before the Holy One, Blessed be He. And He has mercy upon him and settles him upon a throne of glory. Certainly, "a son honors his father," such as Rabbi Eleazar, who honored his father in this world and in that world. He opened and said: <unclear>textual corruption</unclear> thirty-nine crowns of worlds in this world and in that world, more than in his lifetime. Blessed are the righteous who merit holy children, upon whom the holy touch rests, who are called:
> All who see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed whom the Lord has blessed. (Isaiah 61:9)

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Zohar's commentary on the Book of Numbers (Bamidbar). It establishes the cosmological framework for the census of the Israelites, linking the physical world to the divine structure.</meta>

# ## And He Spoke

---

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **And He Spoke** <-

**“And the Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Meeting...”** <note>Numbers 1:1</note> Rabbi Isaac opened his discourse: “And Shaddai <note>The Almighty</note> cut off the kindness...” <note>original: "ויכרת שדי את החסד"</note> and so forth.
Come and see: At the hour when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, He made it in the image of the realms above and below. Everything was integrated, and His light shone from one end of the world to the other. All things were refined by it, and this Wisdom <note>term: Chokhmah (Divine Wisdom)</note> trembled, for one must gaze into it as in the verse, “And Shaddai cut off the kindness,” because of the name Shaddai.
Since it says "cut off," what does this mean? It refers to the levels that include male and female as one—one for the male and one for the female. Because of this, they were certainly "two faces" <note>term: Du-Partzuphin (the concept that the first human was created with two faces, male and female, joined together)</note>. The end of the verse proves this, as it is written: **“Male and female He created them.”** <note>Genesis 1:27</note> He included them from all sides. Even though the female is desired from her side, they were both from two sides so they would be complete in everything. He gazed with Wisdom above and below. But once man sinned, the "faces" were diminished, and Wisdom departed from him; he could no longer perceive anything except matters of the body.
Later, he fathered children from above and below, but they were not established—neither this one nor that one—until a son appeared from the lineage of Seth <note>original: "שת"</note>. This world is called "Sheth" <note>Foundation</note>, and they established it. Yet the lower world was not perfected <note>term: Istalus (Completion/Perfection)</note> and was not complete, nor was its existence found, until Abraham arrived. The world was not perfected until Abraham was found in the world, and he was born into the "Right Side" <note>term: Yemina (The Right Side, representing the attribute of Chesed/Loving-kindness)</note>, to take hold of the right hand of those who had fallen. Then Isaac came and took hold of the "Left Hand" <note>term: Shmala (The Left Side, representing Gevurah/Strength)</note> to establish it further. Once Jacob arrived, the world was established and did not falter.
Despite all this, the completion was not reached—meaning the full payment—until the twelve tribes and seventy souls went down [to Egypt]. Then the world was completed and reached its perfection when Israel received the Torah at Mount Sinai and the Tabernacle was set up. At that time, the worlds were established, and a sweet fragrance rose above and below. Once they walked in their ways and the Tabernacle was prepared in holiness, it was time to muster their hosts.

---

<summary>This page explains that the world was created as a reflection of divine symmetry (male and female) but lost its spiritual clarity after the first sin. It traces the restoration of cosmic balance through the Patriarchs and the Twelve Tribes, culminating in the Revelation at Sinai and the census of Israel.</summary>
<keywords>Bamidbar, Zohar, Creation, Male and Female, Two Faces, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Twelve Tribes, Mount Sinai, Tabernacle, Completion</keywords>

--- Page 238 ---
<meta>This page marks the beginning of the portion "Bamidbar" (In the Wilderness). It establishes a thematic link between the divine presence in the Tabernacle and the study of the Torah, focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the census and the necessity of blessings to ward off the "Other Side."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**In the Wilderness**<-

**The Hosts of the Torah:** How many are the hosts of the Torah, and how many are the hosts of the Tabernacle! Come and see: whoever seeks to settle in his place cannot truly settle until he mentions it with his mouth and prepares himself for it. So too here, the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: *Kadosh Baruch Hu*</note>, desired to count the hosts of the Torah and the hosts of the Tabernacle. They were all as one, inseparable from one another, mirroring the pattern above; for the heavenly hosts and the Tabernacles are inseparable and move as one. Because of this, their matters enter into the "account" <note>the census or mystical calculation</note> to be known through them, except for those others who have no account. And because of this, it is written:

> And the Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 1:1)

If it was in the Tent of Meeting, why mention the wilderness of Sinai? Rather, one refers to the Torah and one refers to the Tabernacle, this one as that one. Through this, one knows that because of the Assembly of Israel <note>the mystical personification of the Jewish people, often associated with the Shekhinah</note>, all is one and called a single precious glory. The letter *Vav* <note>representing the masculine divine force</note> hints at the congregation, like the sun and the moon, where the sun shines upon the moon, for then all worlds are found in peace. At another time, He proclaims to make it known that all commandments and labors are bound together under this authority. Rabbi Isaac opened his discourse:

> The Lord has been mindful of us; He will bless—He will bless the house of Israel... (Psalms 115:12)

"The Lord has been mindful of us; He will bless"—these are the "remembered" hosts who entered into the account, for He remembers them and the Holy One, blessed be He, blesses them and adds to them at all times. Come and see: one who states the sum of his companions, his children, or his wealth, must bless them and offer a blessing over them from that point forward, as it is written:

> The Lord your God has multiplied you, and behold, you are this day as the stars of heaven for multitude (Deuteronomy 1:10)

And what is written afterward?

> May the Lord God of your fathers make you a thousand times so many more as you are, and bless you, as He has promised you! (Deuteronomy 1:11)

These are two blessings: one is "The Lord God of your fathers..." and that is one. Afterward, "and bless you as He has promised you," to offer them blessing upon blessing. But if he counts the sum of his companions and does not offer a blessing over them, it is as said previously from Above <note>it draws negative spiritual attention</note>. If he adds a blessing, he is blessed from Above, and his own blessing must be performed in this manner—without an "evil eye" <note>jealousy or malice</note>. In all things, the Holy One, blessed be He, desires the love of the heart. If the Holy One, blessed be He, requires one who blesses his friend to do so with such a well-meaning eye and heart, how much more so for one who blesses the Holy One, blessed be He! He must have a good eye, a good heart, and love in his heart, for here His belovedness is "with all your heart." Come and see: the sages established that a blessing from Above does not rest upon a thing that has been counted. How then could the hosts be counted? Rather, a <term>ransom</term> <note>original: *kofer*; a symbolic payment or atonement</note> was taken from them. This has been established: they were not found <note>counted</note> until all that ransom was gathered and went up into the account. First, they would bless Israel, then they would count the ransom, and afterward they would return and bless Israel again, so that Israel was found to be blessed at the beginning and at the end, and thus no plague befell them. Why does a plague arise during a census? Because blessing does not rest upon a numbered thing; once the blessing departs, the <term>Other Side</term> <note>original: *Sitra Achra*; the realm of spiritual impurity or evil</note> rests upon it and can cause damage, because the protection of the ransom and redemption was not found to rise above the counting. "He will bless the house of Israel"—these are the women, who do not enter the census. "He will bless the house of Aaron"—for they bless the people with a good eye, a good heart, and love of the heart. "The house of Aaron" likewise refers to them being blessed by their own blessings. "He will bless those who fear the Lord"—these are the hosts of the Levites, and all are blessed because they fear the Holy One, blessed be He. "The small with the great"—even though these enter into the census. Come and see: when a census is conducted among Israel, they are blessed through this counting, for this counting is intended for blessing and for the completion of the perfection of the worlds. In the place where blessings go forth, they are counted, as it is written "in the Tent of Meeting"—the end <note>goal</note> of the union of the world's blessing, from which the radiance goes out to the world. Therefore it is called "Meeting" <note>Hebrew: *Moed*, also meaning "appointed time" or "assembly"</note>, for the radiance of the union of all goes out from it, and all is one matter. And it is written: "For there the Lord commanded the blessing..."

<summary>This page introduces the mystical significance of the census in the Book of Numbers, explaining that counting requires a "ransom" and double blessings to prevent the "Other Side" from bringing a plague. It emphasizes that the Tabernacle and the Torah are spiritually unified and that all divine service must be performed with a "good eye" and a loving heart.</summary>

<keywords>Bamidbar, Census, Tabernacle, Torah, Blessing, Evil Eye, Sitra Achra, Ransom, Tent of Meeting, House of Aaron</keywords>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

"There the blessing..." <note>original: "את הברכה וגו'"</note> Rabbi Yehuda opened his discourse: "Blessed are Israel before the Holy One, blessed be He. From what place are they blessed?" <note>See Psalms 133:3</note>
He said to him: "Is it because you are of this world, the world of building, that you do not gaze upon such glory of the Supreme King? Come and see:
At the time when Israel are found worthy before the Holy One, blessed be He, and the worlds were found deep and aligned as one,
like a Supreme Holy Tree in which the nourishment of all exists, it is blessed from the place where all blessings are gathered. And in it,
they are gathered and found upon the Mountain of Zion. From there they are blessed and found in abundance, from the place where all those
blessings emerge and do not delay in their coming forth. This is what is written: *May the Lord bless you from Zion* <note>Psalms 134:3</note>. And it is written: *Like the dew of Hermon that descends upon the mountains of Zion, for there the Lord commanded the blessing, life forevermore* <note>Psalms 133:3</note>. And this is the hidden treasure
of the world, as it is written: *Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God has shined forth* <note>Psalms 50:2</note>. 'Shined forth' means he illuminated everything; 'He shined forth from Mount Paran,'
and this is the light of all the worlds. And when this place is entirely in a state of belovedness, all is in a state of love,
all is in a state of peace. Then there is peace for all—peace above and below. This is what is written: 'Like a portion sent in your favor.'"

->**Every man**<- by his own standard, with the ensigns of their fathers' house, shall the children of Israel pitch... <note>Numbers 2:2</note> Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse:
*Rejoice with Jerusalem, and be glad with her, all you who love her...* <note>Isaiah 66:10</note> How beloved is the Torah before
the Holy One, blessed be He! For in every place where the words of Torah are heard, the Holy One, blessed be He, and all His hosts all listen
to his words, and the Holy One, blessed be He, comes to dwell with him. This is what is written: *In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you* <note>Exodus 20:21</note>. And not only
that, but the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note> is before him, as they have established. Come and see: the commandments of the Torah are supreme above. When a
man comes and performs a single commandment, that commandment stands before the Holy One, blessed be He, and is crowned before Him, saying: 'So-and-so
performed me.' And because of that person, he is awakened above. Just as he awakened it below,
so it is awakened above, and he makes peace above and below, as you say: *Or let him take hold of My strength, that he may make peace with Me; and he shall make peace with Me* <note>Isaiah 27:5</note>. 'He shall make peace with Me' above; 'Peace he shall make with Me' below. Worthy
is the portion of that man who performs the commandments of the Torah. 'Rejoice with Jerusalem'—because joy
is not found except at the time when Israel dwells in the <term>Holy Land</term> <note>Eretz Yisrael</note>, for there [the Divine] is joined below like a shoe <note>A metaphor for the physical world being the 'footstool' or 'shoe' for the Divine Presence</note>,
and then there is the joy of all, joy above and below. At the time when Israel is not found
in the Holy Land, it is forbidden for a man to rejoice or to show joy, as it is written: *Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad in her...*—'in her' specifically. Rabbi Abba saw a certain man who was rejoicing in a courthouse
in Babylon; he struck him and said: 'Rejoice with Jerusalem' is what is written! Rabbi Abba said: At the time when Jerusalem is in joy,
a man should rejoice. Rabbi Eleazar followed his own reasoning, for he said: 'Rejoice with Jerusalem' is the same as what is written: *Serve the
Lord with gladness* <note>Psalms 100:2</note>. It is written in one place: *Serve the Lord with gladness*, and it is written in another place: *Serve the Lord
with fear, and rejoice with trembling* <note>Psalms 2:11</note>. What is the difference between this and that? Rather, all is according to the state of Israel in the Holy Land.
When Israel is in the Holy Land, [they serve with joy]. Do they not serve the Lord with fear? No, but that [fear] is for the time
when they are in <term>Exile</term> <note>Galut</note> among the nations. Rabbi Yehuda said: But is it not written: *For you shall go out with joy*? <note>Isaiah 55:12</note> And this is because
it says 'you shall go out,' meaning from the Exile, and it is called 'joy.' But certainly, it is so: that all the time they are in Exile
and the Shekhinah is in the dust, it is not called 'joy' until the Holy One, blessed be He, comes to build her and raises her from the dust, saying: *Shake yourself from the dust... arise, sit down, O Jerusalem* <note>Isaiah 52:2</note>, and they shall be joined as one and He will raise her from the dust. Then joy shall be called 'the joy
of the Bride,' and then 'you shall go out with joy' certainly. Then many hosts will go out to meet the <term>Matronita</term> <note>The Divine Matron/Queen</note> for the joy
of the King, all without haste; *the mountains and the hills shall break forth into singing...* and it is written: *For the Lord will go before you, and the God of Israel will be your rear guard...* <note>Isaiah 52:12</note>

<summary>This page explores the mystical source of blessing in Zion and the requirement for joy to be tethered to the state of Jerusalem and the Divine Presence. It emphasizes that true spiritual joy is only complete when the Shekhinah is raised from the dust of exile.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->In the Wilderness of Sinai<-

**"Every man by his own standard, with the ensigns"** <note>Numbers 2:2</note> • These are the four camps of the Assembly of Israel <note>The spiritual collective of the Jewish people, often associated with the Divine Presence</note> which are the twelve tribes, twelve boundaries surrounding it on all sides, exactly according to the pattern Above. • It is written: <note>Psalms 122:4</note> **"Whither the tribes of Yah go up, as a testimony unto Israel..."** • The tribes of Yah, etc. • The "tribes of Yah" refer to these twelve tribes, the twelve boundaries below. They are called "tribes of Yah" without further specification because they are a certain testimony for Israel; and because of this, the spread <note>original: *prosa*</note> of the Tabernacle is within each and every one. • It is a certain cord, for the holy supernal power stands to strengthen its boundaries. • And it has been established as it is written: <note>Ezekiel 1:10</note> **"As for the likeness of their faces, they had the face of a man; and they four had the face of a lion on the right side..."** The form of Man includes them all. • And these were at the four sides of the world, spreading out in their forms, and all of them are included in the "Man." • Michael is on the right, Gabriel is on the left, Uriel is in front of them, and Raphael is behind them. • The Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note> is above them. • Two are from here and two are from there, and She is in the middle. • In this same pattern it is on the earth below: two from here and two from there, and She is between them. • Because they are all two standards <note>groups of banners</note>, what is written? <note>Numbers 2:17</note> **"Then the tent of meeting shall set forward, with the camp of the Levites..."** • And afterwards those other two. There are four camps for the four sides of the world, and they are found to be twelve; so too below, according to the pattern Above. • "And in the first place shall set forward the standard of the camp of Judah," toward the front and the east, corresponding to Michael. • And the camp of Reuben corresponds to the camp of Uriel. • This one is to the South, and that one is to the East. Regarding the Altar, this is what is written: <term>H.D. - Hadah hu dikhtiv</term> "South-East." And the camp of Dan is to the North. • The camp of Ephraim is to the West. • The camp of Dan corresponds to the camp of Gabriel; the camp of Ephraim to the West corresponds to the camp of Raphael. • Regarding the Altar, this is what is written: "North-West." • Everything corresponds one to the other until everything ascends and is unified in the Holy Name, which is the conclusion of all, the Supernal All, Holy of Holies. • For everything is included in Him. • And the East is the bearer of all, for it is the strength and power that goes out to the South, and the South goes out and hangs upon the conclusion of the East. • For the South emerges from its place and enters the conclusion of the East and strengthens it. • And from its sides are South and North, and that which is between them. • East, South, and North are repeated in it. • The letter **Vav** <note>The third letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing the "Male" aspect or Tiferet</note> is in the middle, and this is the "Male Son," as it were, who is between North and South. • And we have learned: one who places his bed between North and South will have male children, for the "Male Son" is between North and South. The world's directions are North and South, and so the Male is between them in this spirit. The final **He** <note>The last letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing Malchut/Shekhinah</note> is the West, and until the South alone, like the East which is the conclusion of perfection <note>original: *temimuta*</note> and is repeated in it. • And we have learned: from the side of the Father <note>Chokhmah</note> alone is repeated Supernal Kindness (*Chesed*). • From the side of the Mother <note>Binah</note> is repeated Might (*Gevurah*), in this manner corresponding one to the other. • And the judgment of mercy has been stated further on: "South-East," for the South's strength is like the East, which is the conclusion of perfection. And the strength of perfection only dwells in the "North-East" conclusion, because the South nullifies its strength in the East to join with the North, and the North to be included in the South, for the Left must be included in the Right. • "North-West," for the West, which is the final **He**, takes from the North, and from the North it goes to the West. • "West-South" goes to be joined with the South, just as the South hangs upon the East; and its strength goes to the conclusion of the West, going to be joined with the South. This is what is written: <note>Song of Songs 2:6</note> **"And his right hand doth embrace me."** "His right hand" is the South, as it were; it takes two sides from North and South. This is what is written: **"His left hand is under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me."** "His left hand" is the North and "his right hand" is the South. • And this spirit is the exchange of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and it was situated between North and South to measure and show it thus certainly. • And they still have possessions, as you say, to take their gifts between North and South, and thus Wisdom divided for those who would merit them, because the "embrace" is intended toward perfect Supernal Faith, as the conclusion of all toward the Holy One, Blessed be He, who is between North and South, and toward the Assembly of Israel to be bound between North and South, and they established it for the sake of males and in general...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the spiritual mechanics of the world, specifically focusing on how human actions below trigger responses in the divine realms above. It transitions into a discussion on the nature of sleep as a "Tree of Death" and the entrustment of the soul to God each night.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Through their deeds, an action is formed in the likeness of that which is above; and just as they act below, so it is awakened above <note>A central Zoharic principle: "As below, so above." Human behavior acts as a catalyst for divine emanation.</note> and established. Listen, see, and observe that which is hidden, and how he laughed and said: "Fortunate is my portion in this world and in the world to come." He opened his discourse and said:
> **"Who is the man who desires life, who loves days..."** <note>Psalm 34:13</note>
• The Lord, return and save, for since he has all the power to gaze into the light from above, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gazes upon him, both from his heights and from his depths • All shall speak of the Lord's inheritance, and "His glory shall shine upon you" <note>Isaiah 60:2</note>. And the Lord is the strength of our lives • Since the Holy One, Blessed be He, takes hold of him, he already has the power not to be enticed in that world by all the messengers of judgment • Here, in this manner, since he was born of his father, so he flourishes in this world and in the other world, and concerning you it is written:
> **"Let your father and your mother be glad, and let her who bore you rejoice."** <note>Proverbs 23:25</note>
• Since it is written "Let your father and your mother be glad," what is the meaning of "and let her who bore you rejoice," which comes to you personally? • Rather, "your father" refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He • and "your mother" refers to the Assembly of Israel <note>The Sefirah of Malchut, the feminine divine presence</note> • "and let her who bore you rejoice" refers to your mother below <note>The biological mother</note> • Rabbi Shimon would grant them his own joy, but the verse is found in the teachings where it is written: **"The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice"**—this is the Holy One, Blessed be He—**"and he who begets a wise son shall have joy in him"**—this is your father below • Another interpretation: **"The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice"**—this is your father below • **"and he who begets a wise son shall have joy in him"** • It is written with an additional letter *Vav* <note>original: "וְיוֹלֵד" (and he who begets) vs "יּוֹלֵד" (he who begets)</note> to signify the Holy One, Blessed be He, who is above • It is written:
> **"Into Your hand I commit my spirit; You have redeemed me, O Lord, God of truth."** <note>Psalm 31:6</note>
• Rabbi Eleazar said: This verse must be looked into. Have you ever seen one who deposits something into the hand of a King? • But surely, fortunate is the person who walks in the ways of the Holy King and does not sin before Him • Come and see: when night enters, the **Tree of Death** <note>Aramaic: *Ilana de-Muta*; refers to the state of the world at night when judgment prevails and the soul departs the body</note> rules the world, and the **Tree of Life** <note>Aramaic: *Ilana de-Chayye*</note> withdraws higher and higher. And because the Tree of Death rules the world alone, all the inhabitants of the world taste the actual taste of death <note>The Talmud states that sleep is 1/60th of death</note> because that Tree causes it. A person must precede this by entrusting the deposit of his soul into [God's] hand, like a person who gives a deposit to another; even if he is more indebted to him than the value of that deposit, it is not right to seize it, and the deposit is handed over to him. And if he is close to Him, certainly he is of the holy seed and does not hide his faith • So it is with this Tree: people come forward and give it the deposit of their souls, and all the souls of the world are taken, and they all taste the taste of death because this is the Tree of Death. And because they are all like a soul-deposit, even though they are all indebted to Him, since they were all handed over to Him as a deposit, He returns all the deposits to their masters • Come and see: this Tree of Death is worthy of being trusted by a person, even as the awakening of the Tree of Life is stirred in the world. And when is that Tree of Life stirred? At the time when the North Wind <note>The midnight hour, which in Zoharic tradition awakens the study of Torah</note> blows. And then, as it is stirred in the world, all the inhabitants of the world live and turn back, and this Tree of Death returns all the deposits that were entrusted to it, and they see actual life because that Tree of Life moves toward them • And its seal is here: the assemblies are joined, and those who awaken in the night while the Tree of Death still rules • even though this Tree of Death acts in reality, for it is written:
> **"From afar He does good, from the foolish one who seeks God."** <note>Interpretive variant of Psalms</note>
And let there be no opening of the mouth for a person to say, "I have been rescued and escaped in the night to labor in the Torah" • Rabbi Yehuda said: This nullification is certain, and so it is • But let us come to this very presence • He said to him: Certainly, what you have said is beautiful • He opened and said:
> **"How precious are Your friends to me, O God! How vast is the sum of them!"** <note>Psalm 139:17</note>
• Come and see: just as there is above, so there is below. There is a Right and there is a Left, and masters and nations • Israel is to the Right in the holiness of the Holy King • The idolatrous nations are to the Left, on the side of the **impure spirit** <note>Aramaic: *Sitra de-Ruach Mesava*; the "Other Side" or forces of evil</note>, and all of them are below all the levels, hanging, and all the levels are grasped one within the other.

## Main Text (Zohar)

...until they hang from the spirit and the coverings of scent <note>original: "rucha ve-khannuvania de-reicha"</note> like the shadow of a cup in colors, and all of it is a lower life-force. Because the cup is pressed, and because of this the nations of the world are found in a state of ruin; thus they are remembered.

Balaam looked at the two lower levels, and he saw into the lower void of the life-force, and he could not mention anything except through the spirit. For this reason he said: *How shall I curse whom God has not cursed?* <note>Numbers 23:8</note> because that supernal spirit was not found in judgment in those days. And even though we have established that this "God" <note>original: "El"</note> refers to the Holy Kingdom <term>Malchut: the final emanation of the Divine, often associated with the feminine aspect</term>, the <term>Nukva</term> <note>The female aspect of the Divine</note> of all, which stands for the goodness and kindness of this world. And for this reason it is called "God" <note>El</note> even though He is "angry every day" when judgment is found within it. 

And come and see: these names of God, we have established that through them the world is sustained, and the life-force of the Master of the Universe stands. "God" <note>El</note> stands to be paired with Him, and for this reason He is called "God Almighty" <note>El Shaddai</note>. And regarding this: *How shall I curse whom God has not cursed?* For in the lower <term>Nukva</term> the spirit is thus awakened below. 

Rabbi Eleazar wept, opened his discourse and said: *Her voice shall go like a serpent...* <note>Jeremiah 46:22</note>. He opened with the holiness of Israel in exile. The life-force surely goes like a serpent when its head is bent to the dust and its tail is raised; then the wicked one rules and strikes all those found before him. It is a dark window for the time when it ascends above and rules, striking the head that is bent below. And despite all this, the "window" leads the tail and strikes according to its travels. Even though the life-force is bent to the dust, it leads its travels. Because of this, he opened with the fear of the nations who take hold of the tail; they ascend above, rule, and strike, while the head is bent to the dust, as it is said: *She has fallen, she shall no more rise...* <note>Amos 5:2</note>. And despite all this, that spirit leads the tail and binds it, as it is said: *They made me keeper of the vineyards...* These are the nations of the world who are meritorious below. 

And it is written: *His hands... my right hand...* He said: "If I had gained nothing else in the world but this journey, it would be enough for me, for now I know how the nations and their dominion are remembered." 

Happy is the portion of Israel, of whom it is written: *For the Lord has chosen Jacob for Himself...* <note>Psalm 135:4</note>. Rabbi Eleazar said to him: "What is the meaning of 'for His treasure' <note>Segulah</note>?" He replied: "There are three colors <note>or levels</note> that are called 'treasure' <note>Segulah</note> both above and below in this <term>Nukva</term>: Priests, Levites, and Israelites. And all are one. These are the treasure of the Holy One, Blessed be He, above, and His treasure below. And this is what is written: *And you shall be a treasure to Me from among all the peoples.*" <note>Exodus 19:5</note>

->**And it shall set forth**<-

**And the Tent of Meeting shall set forth**, etc., the camp of the Levites. <note>Numbers 2:17</note> Afterward, what is written? *The standard of the camp of Ephraim according to their hosts.* <note>Numbers 2:18</note> And what is this? It is the Shekhinah <term>The Divine Presence</term> which dwells in the West. And we have established what is written: *And he blessed them on that day, saying: "By you shall Israel bless, saying..." and he placed Ephraim [before Manasseh].* <note>Genesis 48:20</note> Thus shall Israel bless—meaning Israel the Patriarch <note>Jacob</note>. What does this come to teach us? It does not say "Israel shall be blessed by you," but rather *Israel shall bless*—meaning the Holy Israel <note>the community/divine level</note> shall not bless the world except through you <note>Ephraim</note>, because you are in the West. 

And it is written: *I am God Almighty, be fruitful and multiply.* <note>Genesis 35:11</note> We learn that the Shekhinah stood with him, and then he said: *Thus shall Israel bless*, meaning through you the world shall be blessed. And come and see, it is written: *Now the eyes of Israel were dim with age...* <note>Genesis 48:10</note> but it is written *he guided his hands wittingly* <note>original: "shikel et yadav"</note>. What does "wittingly" mean? He sat upright and the Shekhinah bound him toward Ephraim, and the "head" of the Shekhinah came upon his head. Then he said: *By you shall Israel bless.* And the dwelling of the life-force is in the West. 

Certainly, the Shekhinah is in the West. And we have established this so that it may be between the North and the South, to be joined with the <term>Body</term> <note>The central sefirah, Tiferet</note> and to be in a single union. The North receives her under the head, and the South embraces her, as it is written: *His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.* <note>Song of Songs 2:6</note> And then we established that surely "Solomon's bed" is between North and South to be joined to the Body, and then all is one, so that the world may be blessed. We have learned: "Anyone who says 'A Psalm of David' <note>Psalm 145/Ashrei</note> three times every day <unclear>is assured a place in the world to come</unclear>..."

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the arrangement of the Sefirot (divine emanations) and the camps of Israel. It focuses on how the physical layout of the tribes in the wilderness mirrors the spiritual architecture of the universe, specifically regarding the "Yoke of the Kingdom" and the union of divine attributes.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And he opened [the discourse] and we established that because the **union** <note>original: *zivuga*; the mystical coupling of divine attributes</note> is not found between the North and the South except when the assembly takes upon itself the **Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven** <note>original: *ol malkhuta shamayim*</note> with awe. He arranges [the praises] surrounding Him like the mighty living creatures of the Holy One, blessed be He: "A Praise of David" and all the "Hallelujahs," which are the dwelling of the ten praises corresponding to the ten holy crowns <note>The ten Sefirot</note> of the Holy Name. And because of this, there are ten "Hallelujahs" following the conclusion of the ten praises, which are: "Praise God in His sanctuary..." etc., "Praise Him..." etc. <note>Psalm 150</note>. These are the ten "Hallelujahs," and all five [books of Psalms] begin their praise with "Hallelujah" and end with "Hallelujah." Afterward, they ascend to arrange the praise of the Whole, more than what was in it before. And when she <note>The Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> receives upon herself the <term>Yoke of the Holy Kingdom</term> <note>The acceptance of Divine sovereignty</note>, they return to her with Kindness <note>Chesed</note> as a sign for all to be sanctified by it.

Afterward, in the exile of the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence in the world</note>, where **Strength** <note>Gevurah/Judgment</note> is suspended and the crushed ones surround her, she is found in every wind (Page 19a) that is balanced between North and South to be joined in this union as a proper gathering. And these are the ones who arrange her every day in this manner... Therefore, this "Banner of the camp of Ephraim shall be on the West," and they are between North and South. South is from one side, as it is written: <quote>"The banner of the camp of Reuben shall be on the South side"</quote> <note>Numbers 2:10</note>. North is Dan from the other side, as it is written: <quote>"The banner of the camp of Dan shall be on the North side"</quote> <note>Numbers 2:25</note>. Ephraim is found between this one and that one; the West, which is Ephraim, is between North and South, just like the pattern above...

Thus he arranged them from the side of the "wings" bound in the spirit, whose prayer is to unify the **Unification** <note>Yichud</note> with the addition of the Higher Binding. They received upon themselves the **Yoke of the Holy Kingdom** every day as before. And in this way, you shall ascend in the holy binding to the South and to circle the sides of the world until they are bound in one knot...

There Rabbi Elazar asked his father [Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai], he said to him: "Is the assistance of the union of the Unification taught?" He said to him: "Rabbi Elazar, we have established words for every single side, and they are gathered here." And the whole matter is a sign of the "Binding of Righteousness." And so it is, like the circuit of the Altar <note>referring to the ritual sprinkling of blood on the corners of the altar in the Temple</note> which yields for him: to the Southeast corner, the Northeast, the Northwest, and the Southwest.

He said to him: "But one cannot do this until a person first takes upon himself the **Yoke of the Holy Kingdom** and places this yoke upon himself—yet you say that he should come to the South first?" He said to him: "Everything is as I have shown you, for here it is for the [first] corner initially, and you know that this is the **Yoke of the Holy Kingdom**. Afterward [he moves] to the South, for there is the path of the Unification to be paired with the East, which is **Higher Wisdom** <note>Chochmah Ila'ah</note>, for everything comes from the side of the 'Eater' <note>a mystical reference to the source of divine sustenance</note>. And because of this, from South to East, for the strength of the South is in the East, to be bound as one...

And what was said of the North—that it is the Higher Hiddenness, and from its side the North bends, and Judgments are awakened from its side, even though it is the Mercy of the Unification that we establish. And when she bends the North, she emerges in it, for it is included and tied to the South. Afterward, the Northwest—for from the side of the 'Eater' it bends thus, and from the side below the 'Daughter' emerges. And because of this, the Northwest is the first corner of the circuit, tied simply to its wing. Afterward, he intends to bind her to the South, for there is the connection of all, and the 'Body' is found in it. And the Southwest corner is found three times: once for a person to receive it initially, and afterward twice to bind it with the two 'Arms' to be joined as a 'Body' and to become all one. And this is the arrangement of the Unification... to strengthen it so that the 'Other Side' <note>Sitra Achra/Evil</note> shall not be found there, so that he is not punished. And he who performs the Unification...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the mystical significance of the wilderness (Bamidbar) and the spiritual preparations required for prayer and the unification of the Divine Name.</meta>

# In the Wilderness of Sinai

## Main Text (Zohar)

This unification <note>original: *Yihuda*</note> is as it should be, as we have said. Blessed is his portion in this world and in the world to come! For such a person knows how to arrange the complete support and the honor of his Master. Not only that, but the Holy One, Blessed be He, glories in him; as it is written <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>: *And He said to me, "You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified."*

The Rabbi opened his discourse <note>Psalm 25:1</note>: *A Psalm of David. To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul. O my God, in You I trust...* What did David see that led him to arrange this support in such a way? For do not all the pious ones of the "House of the Doe" <note>A poetic reference to the Assembly of Israel or the Shekhinah</note> ascend, and what is lacking that is not found within it? This cycle is shown to provide atonement.

But come and see: the Supernal Spirit is hidden among its companions. At the time it moves, it moves and ascends the Lower Tree <note>The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, or the lower spiritual realms</note> that hangs from it. It opens, spreads its branches, and covers everything. A "peg" is heard, and all the inhabitants of the world taste the taste of death. A person then collapses and gives over the deposit of his soul <note>original: *pikdona*</note>, which remains abandoned in the Divine hand as a deposit. Because He took them as a deposit, the deposit returns to its Master when the morning comes.

When the morning <note>original: *tzafra*</note> comes and his deposit returns to him, he must bless the Holy One, Blessed be He, who is the Supernal Faithfulness. Afterward, he rises, goes, and prays in the synagogue, crowned with frontlets <note>original: *totafot*, referring to the Tefillin</note>. He covers himself with the garment of merit <note>The Tallit or prayer shawl</note> and purifies himself like the sacrifices of old. Afterward, he binds upon himself the Yoke of the Kingdom <note>The acceptance of God's sovereignty</note> according to the arrangement of the righteous ones of David, which are the orders of the Yoke of the Kingdom. This arrangement of supports is where that Yoke rests.

Afterward comes the order of prayer to receive them as one. Come and see that although prayer depends on prayer, and the speech of the mouth is central, everything depends first on the root of the action, then on the spiritual level, and then on the word of the mouth. What is the "action"? It is that action which a person performs first in the likeness of prayer. A person cannot truly pray until he prepares the action in holiness <note>original: *benazir*</note> in the likeness of prayer.

First, the action: when a person rises, he must first purify himself. Afterward, he shall take upon himself the Yoke by spreading over his head the covering of life. Then he shall tie the knot of unification <note>original: *ktura d'yihuda*</note>, which are the Tefillin. What are the Tefillin? The prayer-box of the head and of the hand. These are to be established as a single bond, like a surrounding circle. Concerning this, it is written: *Engraved with the Names, surrounding beneath His feet...* And it is written <note>Song of Songs 8:6</note>: *Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm.*

We have established that this is the primary action: when a person goes to the synagogue, he purifies himself first like the sacrifices, as the word of the mouth dictates. Afterward, he takes upon himself this Yoke of the Kingdom by spreading over his head the covering of rest, like the Tabernacle <note>Sukkah</note> of King David, mirroring the action of spreading it over his head.

Then follows the Tefillin of the hand, which corresponds to the prayer said while sitting, and then the Tefillin of the head, which corresponds to the prayer said while standing. This action mirrors the speech; indeed, when the action and the speech are linked as one, they are complete. If the action is missing from the speech, it finds no place to rest and is not considered a "whole." It is as if the person is flawed above and below. Furthermore, we must demonstrate the certain action and then fulfill the speech upon it—this is the perfect prayer.

Woe to the person who turns his prayer away from the service of his Master! Concerning him, it is written <note>Isaiah 1:12</note>: *When you come to appear before Me...* and <note>Isaiah 1:15</note>: *Even though you make many prayers, I will not listen,* for the matter depends on both action and speech.

Come and see: when a person performs prayer truly through action and speech, and ties the knot of unification, observe how the upper and lower worlds are blessed through him. Then, after he finishes his prayer, a person should show himself as if he has departed from the world. For he has separated from the Tree of Life <note>original: *ilna d'chaye*</note> and pressed his feet toward that Tree of Death <note>original: *ilna d'mota*</note>, which returns his deposit to him. As it says, *And he gathered his feet into the bed* <note>Genesis 49:33</note>, for he has seen his end. He reveals the secret that one must be covered by that Tree of Death, folding its branches and its scent toward him, just as the Lord inclined His face at first...

<summary>This passage explains the mystical requirements for morning prayer, emphasizing that spiritual "unification" requires a physical action (wearing Tallit and Tefillin) to precede the spoken words. It describes the soul as a deposit given to God during sleep and returned in the morning, necessitating a specific sequence of purification and devotion.</summary>

<meta>This page marks the transition from the conclusion of the Torah portion Bemidbar (In the Wilderness) to the beginning of Naso (Take a Census). The text focuses on the spiritual mechanics of prayer, the danger of insincere devotion, and the mystical movements of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) during the exile and the night hours.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **In the Wilderness of Sinai** <-

And I have entrusted to you the deposit of the incense <note>original: "qetoreta" - referring to the mystical power of the incense offering to halt death and connect worlds</note>, and the unification <note>original: "yihuda" - the meditative act of declaring God's oneness</note>, and the proper performance of the service and the accompaniment as is fitting. And I rejoiced over this letter *He* <note>The letter H (ה) often represents the Shekhinah or the feminine aspect of the Divine</note> when it emerged to assist you and for life. And let him see that when he prepares himself like those who are exempt from the world, who emerge and are handed over to this place of death—because of this, there is no weakness in him, and there is none like him, light and swift, and there is no end to death. And in the end, he receives the arm of the King <note>The Holy Kingdom, the mystery of the Supernal</note> for the life of sins that are not atoned for until he departs from the world. Everything is spared and the iniquity is atoned for everyone until their completion. And through them, he gives himself over to life and to death, and is handed over like a hammer to this place for them as a deposit, like a crown. And it is not pleasing to depart from the world and be pushed away. 

And this restoration <note>original: "tiqquna"</note> requires the intention of the heart <note>original: "kawwanata de-libba"</note>, and then the Holy One, Blessed be He, has mercy upon him and atones for his sin. Fortunate is the person who knows how to appease his Master with desire and with the intention of the heart. Woe to him who comes to appease his Master with a distant heart and without desire, as it is written: *“But they flattered Him with their mouths, and lied to Him with their tongues; for their heart was not firm with Him”* <note>Psalm 78:36-37</note>. Behold, I say to you, O Lord, my soul has sinned, and all his words are with a distant heart; this causes him to be removed from the world before his days have arrived. In the time to come, there will be no one to awaken in the world to execute judgment. And because of this, a person must cleave his soul and his desire to his Master, and he should not come to the Prophet with a desire like a bear, for it is written: *“As water reflects the face to the face, so the heart of man reflects the man”* <note>Proverbs 27:19</note>. One who draws near will not be established before His eyes; strike it and establish it, except for the hour when he prepares himself for this. And from the pressure of the Holy One, Blessed be He, a voice goes out and says: "He shall not be established before My eyes." And they come and seek to burn him, to find himself not established for her like a darkness, until he prepares the heart and the vitality of the holy brain, and does not unify Him as is fitting. 

Fortunate is the portion of the righteous in this world and in the world to come; concerning them it is written: *“You are all beautiful, my love...”* and *“They loved my glory...”* etc. And it is written: *“Surely the righteous shall give thanks to Your name...”* <note>Psalm 140:13</note>. Rabbi Eleazar opened and said: "His hands are gold," if they were not prepared for the world except to hear these words of the Lord. Rabbi Judah said: Fortunate is our portion and fortunate is the portion of Israel, for they cleave to the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: *“But you who held fast to the Lord...”* <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note> and *“Your people are all righteous...”* <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>—all of them are meritorious.

-> # Portion of Naso (Take a Census) <-

**And the Lord spoke** to Moses, saying: "Take a census..." <note>Numbers 4:21-22</note> as it has been said, etc. Rabbi Isaac opened: *“Happy is the man to whom the Lord counts no iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no deceit”* <note>Psalm 32:2</note>. This verse—its beginning is not like its end, and its end is not like its beginning to look into it, and this has been established. Come and see: at the time of the exile of the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note>, judgment dwells in the world. Isaac instituted the Afternoon Prayer <note>original: "Mincha"</note>, and Supernal Might <note>original: "Gevurah" - the divine attribute of judgment and restraint</note> rules in the world until he comes and enters into rest in order to receive the Levite. And from the time that the exiles of the Shekhinah surround, a net is spread out to receive, and Lilith <note>A demonic figure representing the "Other Side" or forces of impurity</note> is awakened after all those guardians of the outer gates are awakened; they all awaken in the world and spread out. And all the inhabitants of the world taste the taste of death. And this is said: at exactly midnight, the net awakens as before, and the Holy Rose <note>A metaphor for the Shekhinah</note> ascends with fragrances, and her mouth praises and exalts with a voice. And then she ascends and tosses her head upward like a net, and departs.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on Parashat Naso, specifically focusing on the soul's nightly ascent and the spiritual mechanics of the Levites' service. ## Main Text (Zohar)

And the "dizziness" <note>referring to the chaotic forces of the "Other Side"</note> receives the soul. Then a herald calls out in the world: "Behold, it is time to awaken to follow the King!" And then you shall be found, and the sweetness of all is discovered. Fortunate is the portion of one who awakens for the Union <note>the mystical joining of the divine attributes</note> and abandons the "Other Side." When he comes out and the time awakens, he seeks Him; then the radiance of all is found as one. **Come and see:** at the hour when human beings sleep and taste the taste of death, the soul ascends above. It stands in the place where it stands and is examined for the deeds it performed all day. These are written upon the "opening of the mouth," because that word which a person brings forth from his mouth ascends and pierces the firmaments. It stands in its place until the night enters and the soul ascends and shows that word, presenting it before the King. This is what is written:
> Keep the doors of your mouth (<note>Micah 7:5</note>)

And then that word is judged, as is the sin that the person committed. Because of this, he is disturbed and given "shakings" <note>restless sleep or bad dreams</note>. When does this change? When the prayer arrives with its hidden sign.

## The Faithful Shepherd (Ra'aya Meheimna)

"From thirty years old and upward even until fifty years old, everyone who enters to perform the service of the ministry, and the service of the burden in the Tabernacle of the Congregation." This **commandment** is for the Levites to be singers in the Sanctuary. Even though we have established this above, here we must learn these matters, for through them they receive the sacrifice. They are from the side of the Left, which are the **Severities** <term>Gevurot: the divine attribute of judgment and strength</term>, and they must be gathered. The spirit of the matter is that the "Lord's kindness rests," but not the ordinary kindness in that secret. Michael is like a common priest compared to the **Long Face** <term>Arich Anpin: the "Long Suffering" or "Macroprosopus," representing the highest level of Divine Will/Mercy</term>, the Holy King. Despite the dominion of the Levites, the King has appointed them, and the commoner's cry is heard regarding the miracles. Through your command, the Lord's kindness rests, and the power of the song redeems the people. The harp is seized, the ox is seen in its glory, and the "sons of the ox" <note>referring to the power of the Left side</note> are subdued. The severity of his thigh is bound to turn and gather into the kindness of the wine of Torah, to occupy oneself above with the sacrifice before the King in kindness. And whoever does not have the secret of occupying himself with the Torah should stand before the Master in the night of Leah <note>a specific kabbalistic time for midnight prayer</note> to be hidden. At times, this saves one from several **Husks** <term>Kelipot: shells of evil or impurity that conceal divine light</term>, and from buffetings, vengeances, and all kinds of evil. Elijah is the guardian to teach by the hand of the voice... the King will bring him out to Understanding <note>Binah</note>, as the Masters of the Mishnah established. The praise comes from the foundation of the "Vav" of Elijah to fly... to receive the ascent... the glory of the heights stirs, and the mouth shall say:
> For a hand is upon the throne of God; the Lord will have war with Amalek (<note>Exodus 17:16</note>)

...Sound the **Shofar** <term>Shofar: a ram's horn used for ritual purposes</term> at the moon's concealment for the day of our feast. What is the Shofar? It is the "Vav" <note>the letter representing the central column/connection</note>, the voice that ascends from the throat... two sounds for the male... the voice of Elijah like the hint to bring forth the voice. Remember the wrapping of God against Amalek... the commandments are the crown of the Shofars. The Torah is its Voice, Understanding <note>Binah</note> is its Speech. Thus, the thought of the male ascends before the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <term>HaKadosh Baruch Hu: the standard Hebrew reference to God</term> more than all sacrifices and burnt offerings, as it says: "This is the Torah for the burnt offering, for the meal offering, etc."

## Commentary/Additional Section

...The kindnesses of the Lord... **Come and see:** it is written, "And he remembered the Kenite." This refers to the atonement of Cain... the father-in-law of Moses. And from all the Kenites, the children of Jethro... it says, "Strong is your dwelling place, and you put your nest (Ken) in a rock." Why is he called a "Kenite"? **Come and see:** it is written "the Kenite, and the Kenizzite," and it is said that he made a "nest" (Ken) in the desert like a bird, because he dwelt in freedom. He separated from the people who were in destruction and cleaved to the Holy One, Blessed be He. Thus, they merited the freedom to cling to His liberty. For when a man walks in His ways...

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the spiritual consequences of human actions, specifically focusing on the concept of "blemish" (defect) caused by sin and the restorative power of Repentance. It transitions from general principles to the specific mystical commentary known as the "Faithful Shepherd."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

In the portions of the Torah, a person draws upon themselves a supernal **Holy Spirit** <note>original: *Ruacha Kadisha*</note>, as it is written: *Until the spirit be poured upon us from on high* <note>Isaiah 32:15</note>. But when a person deviates from the right paths, they draw upon themselves "another spirit" from the **Other Side** <note>original: *Sitra Achra*, the side of evil/impurity</note>. That is an impure spirit that defiles. This side of impurity is awakened from the aspect of the **Female of the Great Abyss**, where the dwellings of evil spirits reside—those who harm human beings. They are called the "female of the world," for they were found and increased from the side of the first **Cain**. At first, he was like them, and he worshipped that "rain" <note>likely a reference to demonic influence</note> and drew a spirit upon himself from that place.

And those who investigate the measures <note>esoteric calculations or sorcery</note> that followed Cain were found in him. The Holy One, blessed be He, shows mercy to everyone who is found in Him and performs the commandments of the Torah; it is as if—if one could say such a thing—he sustains the worlds, the world above and the world below, and all wisdom and protection are healed. But whoever transgresses the commandments of the Torah, it is as if he creates a **blemish** <note>original: *pegim*, a spiritual defect or notch</note> above, a blemish below, a blemish to himself, and a blemish to all worlds. For those who separate from the "Right Hand" and sin (others say: deviate), their path is like a scale that is plastered over... <note>The text here uses cryptic abbreviations and linguistic play regarding the nature of sin and kindness</note>.

Come and see: when a person is "cut off," it is certainly because that person transgressed a single commandment of the Torah, bringing death upon himself and causing a blemish to the whole world—above and below. That debt remains hanging until the Holy One, blessed be He, establishes the world as it was at the beginning, and that blemish is removed from the world. This is what is written: *He will swallow up death forever; and the Lord God will wipe away tears from off all faces...* <note>Isaiah 25:8</note>. And because of this, it is written: *When they commit any of the sins of man* <note>Numbers 5:6</note>. "The Man" <note>Adam</note> refers to the **First Man** <note>Adam HaRishon</note> who sinned. *To commit a trespass against the Lord*: whoever removes his Master and turns away from the Way, he causes a blemish. Therefore, for every debt and sin that the world commits, and from their blemish, many merits are removed because of them, besides all that they cause above and below.
