## Naso

See, there are many times of crowning. At one time, thirteen measures of the <term>Ancient of Ancients</term> <note>Atika De-Atikin; the most hidden, primordial level of the Divine</note>, the most hidden of all, are found within this "arm" <note>an extension of Divine influence</note> here. At a second time, nine measures of mercy are seen, all of which are pure and shining from the Ancient One, the hidden of all. All of these are included when the Priest spreads his hands to bless the people. It is found that all worlds are blessed through this, for these measures are seen from the Ancient One, the most hidden of all. And all this occurs when the hidden measures come forth:
> **May the Lord bless you and protect you** <note>Numbers 6:24</note>

These three verses <note>the three lines of the Priestly Blessing</note> are a sign of twelve letters <note>referring to the mystical divisions of the Name</note> corresponding to them, and they are all intended for this purpose. All their entrances and paths are sweetened as one. The letters written in these three verses correspond to the three measures of mercy that include everything. For this reason it is written: **Say to them** <note>Numbers 6:23</note>. "Say" <note>Amor</note> as we have established: "Say" because one must meditate on all these hidden levels, all these degrees. "Say" refers to the hidden words above. "Say" is the "nose" <note>the breath/spirit</note> of the forty-eight companions, for they all speak of one <term>Chesed</term> <note>Loving-kindness</note>, as everything depends on Loving-kindness. All are blessed by this blessing in these three verses, as we have said, so that the upper and lower worlds may be included in this blessing.

Come and see, Rabbi Yose said: One time I sat before Rabbi Eleazar, the son of Shimon. I asked him: "Rabbi, what did David see when he said:
> **Of loving-kindness and justice I will sing; to You, O Lord** <note>Psalms 101:1</note>

and
> **Man and beast You save, O Lord** <note>Psalms 36:7</note>?"

He said to me: "The prayer of the Bride <note>the Shekhinah/Congregation of Israel</note> is directed toward this... Loving-kindness for her... and 'beast' <note>referring to the lower levels of existence</note>." I said: "Rabbi, I am seeking the secret of the matter." He said to me: "Everything has been stated. Come and see, Israel is called 'Loving-kindness' <note>Chesed</note> in the manner of the world above, and they are also called 'beast,' as it is written:
> **And you, My sheep, the sheep of My pasture, are men** <note>Ezekiel 34:31</note>

'The sheep of My pasture' refers to the 'beast' aspect. 'Loving-kindness' below is indeed Loving-kindness. And Israel encompasses both Loving-kindness and 'beast,' and for this reason: **Man and beast You save, O Lord.** Furthermore, the secret of the matter is that Loving-kindness is in the manner of the world above, and 'beast' is their lower aspect, and all are blessed through the Holy <term>Da'at</term> <note>Knowledge/Connection</note>. Loving-kindness is above and 'beast' is below. And because of this, all of them are within Israel: Loving-kindness, man, and beast—'You save, O Lord.'

And come and see: a blessing below is not found until it is awakened above. And from the awakening above, it is also found below. Everything depends on this, for good or otherwise, as it is written:
> **I will respond to the heavens, and they shall respond to the earth** <note>Hosea 2:23</note>

Rabbi Yehuda said: For this reason it is written **Say to them**, as a kindness to bless the upper and lower worlds together. **May the Lord bless you** refers to the upper world, as it is written "Thus shall you bless," and it says "to the children of Israel, say to them," as a kindness to bless them all as one. **And protect you** refers to the world below. **May the Lord make His face shine** refers to the upper world, **and be gracious to you** refers to the world below. **May the Lord lift up His face** refers to the upper world, **and grant you peace** refers to the world below.

Rabbi Abba said: They are all blessed as one. For this reason, the engraved letters of the Holy Name are included, and it is written that twenty-two letters are blessed through this. And this is mercy upon mercy, where no judgment <note>Din</note> is found. Is it not written: **May the Lord lift up His face to you**? Rabbi Abba said: Loving-kindness passes through so that no judgment shall be found at all.

Come and see, Rabbi Yose said: At the moment the Priest spreads his hands, the people should have the heart to be blessed by him, because the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>Divine Presence</note> rests upon his hands. Let it not be said that they do not see what is before them, for it is written:
> **For no man shall see Me and live** <note>Exodus 33:20</note>

They do not see with their physical eyes, but they see with their hearts. Rather, because the Holy Name is hinted at in the fingers of his hands, a person must be in awe. And for this reason, they are not permitted to look at the hands of the Priests, so that the people's attention does not depart from the Shekhinah. Come and see: at the moment the Priest spreads his hands, the upper and lower worlds are blessed. The people must stand in awe and truth, and know that at that hour, "Will" <note>Ratzon/Divine Favor</note> is awakened in all worlds, and there is no judgment in any of them. It is the hour when the Ancient of Ancients reveals His face, and peace is found in everything. Rabbi Shimon said: These three verses...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Priestly Blessing (Numbers 6:24-26), focusing on the spiritual disposition of the Priest and the cosmic battle between the "Good Eye" and the "Evil Eye."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The markings of the Name <note>original: "Yod Yod Yod," representing the Tetragrammaton</note> in the verse *May the Lord bless you* are all intended to manifest perfect faith and to draw blessings from the **Ancient Holy One** <note>The highest, most hidden level of the Divine, Keter</note>. To illuminate the Name, the **Small Face** <note>The manifest aspects of God, Zeir Anpin</note> is blessed by the Ancient One of All. For this reason, it says *May the Lord bless you* above, and *and keep you* here below, and so it is for all the verses. Furthermore, when one stands before the Priest, one should not look at him while he is chanting the three verses, so that the movement of the Priests as they spread their hands does not cause a distraction. One should say: "The King is righteous... the King is eternal," etc., to see that this is a time for mercy to be awakened in all worlds, and whoever needs his exile to be overturned in his youth, let it be turned to merit and mercy.

**And they shall put** My Name. What is the meaning of *and they shall put My Name*? It means that all the "limbs" of the Divine Name should be arranged, as it is written: *And they shall appoint them, every one to his service and to his burden* <note>Numbers 4:19</note>. They are to be established through their blessings in the two arms, right and left, so that the left is included within the right. They are to be established in their blessings like the blessings of the two worlds, for there are upper blessings and lower blessings. And they are obligated in this, as it is written: *And I will bless them*. We see regarding those Priests that it is written: *And I will bless those who bless you* <note>Genesis 12:3</note>, and it is written: *And I will bless those who bless you*. They bless the people, and the Holy One, Blessed Be He, blesses them. Therefore, it is written *and they shall put*, and it is not written "they shall say" or "they shall remember." Come and see: any Priest who is not loved by the people should not spread his hands to bless. There was an incident with a certain Priest who stood and spread his hands, and before he finished, he became a heap of bones. Why? Because he did not bless with love; he held a grudge and yet spread his hands and blessed, and he was not rectified that day. Come and see: any Priest who does not love the people, the people do not show him mercy, and he should not spread his hands to bless the people, as it is written: <term>He who has a good eye shall be blessed</term> <note>Proverbs 22:9; "Good eye" refers to a generous and loving spirit</note>. Do not read it as "shall be blessed" but rather "shall bless." Come and see: if Isaac the son of Isaac <unclear>textual variant</unclear>, what is written regarding that wicked Balaam? At the time he was told to bless Israel, he looked upon them with an evil eye so that his blessing would not be fulfilled. He hung his words upon that evil eye, as it is written: *The speech of Balaam the son of Beor*, meaning the son of Beor from that place <note>original: "Pethor"</note> who was more [expert in the evil eye] than all the people of the world. *And the speech of the man whose eye is opened* <note>Numbers 24:3</note>, for he opened the evil eye so that they would not be blessed and the blessing would not be sustained. Rabbi Judah said: This is so, and it is not right to find a defect (why should a defect be found?). For the eye is meant for blessing, as it is written: *Open Your eyes*—Your eyes are meant for blessing. And regarding the blessing, the way of the Resting Place is thus: the verse says, *And open Your eyes upon us*. But regarding that wicked one, it is written *whose eye is closed* <note>or "set," implying a fixed, malicious gaze</note> so that they would not be blessed through him. And Rabbi Isaac said: Similarly, a Priest who blesses with a "good eye," his blessing is fulfilled. But one who does not bless with a good eye, it is written: <term>Do not eat the bread of one who has an evil eye</term> <note>Proverbs 23:6</note>, *and do not desire his delicacies*—meaning, do not seek a blessing from him at all. Rabbi Yose said: It is written, *But the Lord your God would not listen to Balaam...* <note>Deuteronomy 23:6</note>. It says *to Balaam*; it implies that even Balak did all those things. Why *to Balaam*? Because he closed his eyes so they would not be blessed and hovered over them. Come and see, said Rabbi Yose: The Holy One, Blessed Be He, said to the wicked Balaam: "You close your eye so they won't be blessed? I will open My eyes!" And all the words you say, I will turn them into a blessing. This is what is written: <term>And the Lord your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because He loved you...</term> <note>Deuteronomy 23:6</note>. And it is written: *He who has a good eye shall be blessed, for he gives of his bread to the poor*. And "his bread" is as we have established, as it is written: *The bread of his God, of the most holy...* <note>Leviticus 21:22</note>. This implies that the most holy is the "bread of his God" which he eats, and similarly *for he gives of his bread to the poor*. Come and see how beloved Israel is before the Holy One, Blessed Be He, for the Upper Beings are not blessed except through the blessings of Israel. For we have learned: Rabbi Judah said in the name of Rabbi Hiyya, who said in the name of Rabbi Yose: At the time the Holy One, Blessed Be He, sends [blessings] to the worlds, they go to the upper ones until they reach Israel... *The Holy One is in your midst, and I will not come into the city* <note>Hosea 11:9</note>. This means: as long as the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence</note> is here in exile with us, the Upper One is not comforted, and all the rectifications are not fully established, as it were, for the Supernal King.

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic discourse on the spiritual significance of the Tabernacle's completion. It transitions from a discussion on Abraham's faith to the unique mystical status of Moses as the "husband" of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The holy candle proclaims: Rabbi Abba was walking on the road. Rabbi Isaac, the son of Rav Hiyya, met him and stood before him. He saw the Divine Presence <note>Hebrew: Shekhinah; the feminine aspect of God</note> and those who were before it, etc. The Divine Presence desires to be seen and to converse in the splendor and glory of the Holy One, to know the Lord. And it is written: <note>Isaiah 2:3</note> *And many nations shall go and say, "Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord..." for out of Zion shall go forth the law.* And behold, I seek to whom I should give and from whom I should learn those excellent words that we taste every day from the holy cycle.

What is the meaning of that which is written: <note>Genesis 15:6</note> *And he believed in the Lord, and He counted it to him for righteousness*? This refers to the "Kindness unto Abraham" <note>Micah 7:20; original: "Chesed l'Avraham"</note>. This implies that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave "righteousness" <note>Tzedakah</note> to Abraham and not as a seal to his blessing. "Kindness unto Abraham"—so we have established it, but was it not so? Behold, it is not written "and He counted it <insert>sin</insert> to him," but rather it was to him as kindness for Abraham and kindness for the Holy One, blessed be He. For we have learned: It is written, "And His appearance was changed." The Holy One, blessed be He, rested from the kindness in Your right hand. To this, that sharpness <note>intellectual acuity</note> is to know My name.

Come and see, for I am standing here. Abraham's strength brings forth kindness; "Kindness unto Abraham" brings forth a pious one <note>Chassid</note>. And to strengthen his fullness in another way: *So shall your seed be* <note>Genesis 15:5</note>. This was in the manner of the holy "wrapping" <note>a mystical state of Divine concealment/revelation</note> to know His name. And the Crown <note>Keter</note> of Judgments shall be awakened from Him, and you shall see that *So shall your seed be* is literal. At that moment, it was enough for Abraham to gaze and to know His name and to cleave to Him, because he was given the news. And because Judgments <note>Dinim</note> are awakened from Him, Abraham relied on that "Last One" <note>the final Sefirah, Malchut</note>, for even though Judgment is in it, all of it is Mercy <note>Rachamim</note>. He completed his faith in that "Last One" through Righteousness and Mercy.

Rabbi Isaac said: "So" <note>Hebrew: Koh</note> is the "Last One," the wrapping, and it is called Justice <note>Tzedek</note>, and Judgments are awakened from it. And Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>, even though Judgments are awakened from it—what do we learn? It is Justice. It supports Righteousness <note>Tzedakah</note> so that Judgments are not awakened from it, because it is Mercy. Furthermore, there is one secret regarding Kindness: What is written? <note>Genesis 24:1</note> *And the Lord blessed Abraham in all things* <note>Hebrew: Ba-Kol</note>. "All" is love, and all is mercy. And it is written: <note>Numbers 6:23</note> *Thus <term>Koh: a name for the Shekhinah</term> you shall bless the children of Israel.* And Israel is blessed, pushing it upward, because when Israel is blessed below, the blessing is blessed in all of them. And to know that "Blessed" comes: *Blessed be the Lord out of Zion...* <note>Psalms 135:21</note> *Blessed be the Lord out of Zion, who dwells in Jerusalem.*

---

**And it came to pass** on the day that Moses had finished <note>Numbers 7:1; the Hebrew word for "finished," *Kallot*, is spelled like *Kallah*, meaning "Bride"</note> etc. We have learned: Rabbi Yose said, on the day the Bride entered the wedding canopy. How did we establish "the day of the Bride of Moses"? Rather, it teaches that through the hand of Moses, she entered. Rabbi Judah said: But until now, had he not made a place for her? For it is written: <note>Exodus 40:35</note> *And Moses was not able to enter into the tent of meeting...*

Rabbi Isaac said: See, there is no "before" or "after" in the Torah <note>a principle that the Torah is not strictly chronological</note>. *On the day of the Bride of Moses*—the Bride of Moses certainly! For we have learned: Rabbi Eleazar said, what is the meaning of that which is written: <note>Psalms 68:19</note> *You have ascended on high, you have led captivity captive...*? Rather, at the hour the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: <note>Exodus 3:5</note> *Put off your shoes from off your feet*, the mountain trembled. Michael saw before the Holy One, blessed be He, and sought a claim regarding his loins <note>i.e., Moses's separation from his wife</note>. For is it not written: <note>Genesis 1:27</note> *Male and female He created them and He blessed them*? And no blessing is found except in one who is male and female together, yet You say to him to separate from his wife?

The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: Moses, spread out and ride! Now, here, I desire that you dwell with My Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note>, and for your sake, the Divine Presence shall descend to dwell with the people. Here, regarding this, they taught you: *You led captivity captive.* And what is "captivity"? My Divine Presence, which was taken with you. *You received gifts among men*—it is not written "among men" <note>plural</note> but *in Adam* <note>singular</note>, who is Above. And similarly, you say: it was found at the hour they established the mountain as the "Bride of Moses." Literally the Bride of Moses!

And Joshua, whom we see—it is written: <note>Joshua 5:15</note> *Put off your shoe* <note>singular</note>. Do not separate except at known times, for the Divine Presence was not wedded to him to such an extent, nor was it found in him, as it is written: <note>Joshua 5:14</note> *And Joshua fell on his face to the earth.* But here, it is the "Bride of Moses." And regarding "gifts," it is written as one gift. And the Bride is the portion of Moses, who was wise and sought her visitation above all other people in the world. *And the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand."* What is the meaning of "And it came to pass" <note>Vayehi</note>? Rabbi Isaac said: These are the Supernal Days, being prepared to be arranged.

# Portion of Beha'alotcha

**And the Lord spoke** to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and say to him, "When you raise the lamps," etc. **Rabbi Yitzchak** opened his discourse:
> And he is like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber; he rejoices like a strong man to run a race. <note>Psalms 19:6</note>
Fortunate is the portion of Israel, for **the Holy One, Blessed Be He** desired them and gave them the Torah of Truth, the portion of life, in which anyone who takes hold of it takes hold of the life of lives—the life of this world and the life of the World to Come. For anyone who exerts himself in the Torah takes hold of the body of life <note>original: "gufa de-chayin"</note>, and anyone who leaves the matters of Torah and separates from the Torah, it is as if he separates from life, because she is life and every word is life, as it is written:
> For they are life to those who find them... <note>Proverbs 4:22</note>
And it is written:
> It shall be health to your navel... <note>Proverbs 3:8</note>
Come and see: the portion of life takes hold from above to below, and it is the Name that possesses everything. On His mountain, He dwells and is exalted, and He spreads through the body of the Tree <note>the Tree of Life/Sefirotic system</note> as one. Two sides take hold of it: one to the North and one to the South, one on the Right and one on the Left. These are the supernal plantings, as has been said from the secret of the body of the Tree; the right arm is strengthened, and by that Ancient One <note>term: *Atika*, the highest crown of divinity</note> in whom they are strengthened, they are strengthened together and included as one. And the secret of *like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber*: who is the "bridegroom"? This is the Living One <note>Chayah</note> of the crown with which his mother crowned him on his wedding day. And the light of the chamber: this is the Living One of fire, for all the Priests are the daughters of the fellowship, the possession of Heaven, to whom is given the palace of all, which is called "the gift of Heaven." And then he goes out truly like a bridegroom, when he goes out to rejoice with his bride in the love of the soul, and he spreads his arms and receives her. In what manner? *And he is like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber.* The Name spreads toward the West <note>the Shekhinah</note>; as soon as the West approaches, the North side is awakened toward her first, and approaches the West and joins her with an embrace, as it is said:
> His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me. <note>Song of Songs 2:6</note>
Then he *rejoices like a strong man to run a race* to illuminate the Moon <note>term: *Sihra*, the feminine Presence</note> and to establish her. Come and see: *When you raise the lamps*—these are the lights <note>term: *butzinin*, divine illuminations</note> that are all lit as one from the Sun <note>the masculine principle, Tiferet</note>. **Rabbi Abba** opened and said:
> Shout for joy to the Lord, all the earth; break forth into joyous song and sing praises. <note>Psalms 98:4</note>
This verse was established by all the people of the world, and they are Israel, to whom **the Holy One, Blessed Be He** gave the holy Torah and taught...

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **When You Raise [the Lamps]** <-
<note>original: "Beha’alotcha" – the title of the Torah portion in Numbers 8</note>

And He taught them His ways to cleave unto Him and to keep the commandments of the Torah, so they might merit the World to Come <note>Exodus and the giving of the Torah</note>. He brought them near at the hour when Israel went out from Egypt, for then He removed them from "other authority" <note>the realm of spiritual impurity or foreign gods</note> and raised them up to be united with His Name. At that time, the Children of Israel were called **free men** <note>Hebrew: Bnei Chorin</note> from everything, for they no longer sat under other authority. He raised them to take hold of His Name, which rises above all and rules over the upper and lower worlds. Out of His love for them, He called them "Israel, My firstborn son," in the likeness of the Supernal Holiness. Until He slew every firstborn above and below, He protected them, and the upper and lower beings knew He was bringing them out. And it was for the Lord; at the time of the visitation, it was not your god, nor did he hiss <note>a reference to the serpent or demonic forces</note>; even the strong and the demons knew to submit and to know all, and the pious were hidden—they were not under the authority of another "upper one," but in His hand.

Come and see: on that night when the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to slay all those firstborn, as it has been said, at the hour when evening fell, the ministering angels came to sing a song of praise. He said to them: "Now is not the time, for another song is being sung by My children." At the hour when the night was divided, the North Wind awoke and sang; then He performed wonders, and Israel performed a song with a loud voice (page 13) and Israel sang and said "Hallelujah" with a loud voice. At that time, He made them **free men** from all, and they rejoiced in Him. Thus they were all protected, coming to the holiness of Israel.

They were circumcised by that blood <note>the blood of circumcision</note> and by the blood of the Passover lamb; they marked their houses with three marks: on the lintel and on the two doorposts. Why? They established this because it was a holy mark. When the Destroyer went out and saw that blood marked upon that entrance, he stood over Israel, as it is written: *And the Lord will pass over the door...* <note>Exodus 12:23</note>. Here one must look: did the Holy One, Blessed be He, come and slay? It says "He will not allow the Destroyer to come in." Rather, it is as it is written: *And the Lord smote every firstborn* <note>Exodus 12:29</note>—He and His House of Judgment <note>the Divine Court</note>.

From here we see that in everything, an action must be shown below so that it may be found above. Just as it is upon the Altar, so that the Destroyer is not found taking hold of the work, and just as one needs to be pure for the sake of the mystery. So it is on the **Day of Remembrance** <note>Rosh Hashanah</note>; when the "Evil Accuser" stands against Israel, we need words and weeping, and we need to show the mystery through the soul, as they established. And it is said: like a **Shofar**, to show a Shofar and to awaken the "Other Shofar" <note>the Sefirah of Binah, the source of Jubilee and freedom</note>. We produce through that sound both mercy and judgment as one, as is fitting. Just as the Supernal Shofar produces a sound that contains everything as one, so too we awaken mercy through our voices to weaken the Accuser so he has no dominion on this day. Thus mercies are awakened, and all the supernal intentions are directed from this side and that, and then "in the light of the King's face there is life."

Come and see: at the time the Priest prepares to light the lamps below, and he brings the **Incense** of spices at that hour, then the supernal intentions are bound together, and everything is tied as one. Joy and gladness are found in all worlds. As it is said: *Oil and incense rejoice the heart*, and *When you raise the lamps...* <note>Numbers 8:2</note>.

**Rabbi** Eleazar, Rabbi Yose, and Rabbi Isaac were walking on the road and reached those mountains. As they were walking, Rabbi Eleazar raised his eyes and saw those mountain peaks. They were arranged and smoke rose from them. He said to his companions: "Let us go, for the King's word does not fail; since we three are here, judgment shall not be found." He said to them: "How beloved are the words of Torah, for in every single word there are **high secrets**. The entire Torah is called 'Superior,' and it is interpreted through the thirteen rules of the Torah. 'Anything that was included in a general statement and then singled out... was not singled out to teach only about itself, but to teach about the whole general statement.'" <note>The 13th rule of Rabbi Ishmael</note>. And this is the mystery of the freedom of the All...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**When You Raise the Lamps**<-

Within the general **Whiteness** <note>original: *Chivra*; representing the attribute of Mercy</note> that emerges from it, a single **story** <note>original: *Sipur*; also punning on *Sapphire*, the radiance of the Sefirot</note> comes out into the world. It is not seen merely for its **surroundings** <note>the literal narrative</note> to show itself; certainly, it does not come to teach about itself alone, but to teach about the whole. And come and see: because that **story** by itself was not the main point, it emerged from the general body of the **Torah** <note>original: *Oraita*</note> not to show itself alone, but to show the **surroundings** of the entire Torah. It emerged because it is written:
> **And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.** <note>Genesis 8:4</note>
Certainly **this verse** emerges from the general body of the **Torah**. It looks like a worldly story—what does it matter to us if it rested here or if it rested in that place, in this or that territory? Rather, it comes to teach about the whole. Happy are the people of Israel to whom the supernal **Torah** and the **Torah** of truth was given. And one who perceives only the surroundings of the **Torah**—viewing it as that story alone—may his spirit deflate! For if that were so, it would not be the supernal **Torah** and the **Torah** of truth. But certainly, it is the holy supernal **Torah**, and **it is the Torah** of truth. Come and see: a king of flesh and blood—if it were not for his honor, he would not speak of common things, much less write them down. And if the words are as you think <note>i.e., only literal</note>, did the Supernal King, the Holy One, blessed be He, have no holy words to write and make into a **Torah**? Instead, He collected all these common matters, such as the words of Esau, the words of Laban, the words of Jacob, the words of Dathan, the words of Balaam, the words of Balak, the words of Zimri, and the like—all the stories that are written—and made the **Torah** from them? If so, why is it called:
> **The Torah of truth. The Torah of the Lord is perfect. The testimony of the Lord is sure. The precepts of the Lord are right. The commandment of the Lord is pure. The fear of the Lord is clean.** <note>Psalm 19</note>
And it is written:
> **And the writing was the writing of God.** <note>Exodus 32:16</note>
Observe these words of the **Torah**. Rather, it is certainly the **Torah of the Lord** and is called a **perfect Torah**. Every single word comes to show supernal matters. That word or that story does not come to show itself alone, but to show that general principle, as we have established. Come and see: **"And the ark rested..."** This verse refers to a time of danger <margin>pages 120, 150, 151 etc. for Tamar</margin> when anger hangs over the world and judgments dwell, and the Holy One, blessed be He, sits upon His Throne of Judgment to judge the world. On that Throne, just as it is hidden below, how many hidden records are within it, like the king's records? All are sapphires <note>original: *Sapirin*</note> that are opened there to be revealed, and because of this, no word is forgotten by the King. And see, the Throne is not established and does not rest except in the seventh month <note>Tishrei</note>, which is the day of anger, the day when all the inhabitants of the world are remembered; they all pass before that Throne. And regarding **"And the ark rested in the seventh month"**: in the seventh month, which is the judgment of the world. Upon **"the mountains of Ararat"**: these are the supports of the Throne, the masters of anger, the masters of wailing and howling, and they are all sharpened <margin>page 130, those who divide and gaze</margin> on that day before the Holy One, blessed be He. And how many "shield-bearers" <note>mighty angels/intercessors</note> are awakened in joy, and they all stand beneath that Throne for the judgment of the world. And Israel sends up prayer on that day, and they ask and supplicate before Him and blow the Shofar, and the Holy One, blessed be He, rises over them and transforms judgment into mercy. Then all those above and below open their mouths and say:
> **Happy is the people that knows the joyful sound (Teruah).** <note>Psalm 89:16</note>
And for this reason, we require on that day that the one who blows the Shofar must know the root of the matter and intend his heart toward the *Teruah* <note>the broken blast</note> and perform the act with wisdom. Regarding this it is written, **"Happy is the people that knows the Teruah,"** and it is not written "that hears the Teruah," as has been said. Furthermore, on that day when evening fell, they went up to a certain place and found a cave hidden above. Rabbi Eleazar said: Let one enter the cave. He looked and found it was more prepared than expected. He entered, for the day was pure, and he saw another cave with an opening like an eye in it. He heard a voice saying:
> **When you raise the lamps, toward the face of the Menorah shall the seven lamps give light.** <note>Numbers 8:2</note>
Here the Assembly of Israel <note>the Sefirah of Malkhut</note> takes up the story, and so said the Rabbi—

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**151**<-
->**Beha'alotcha**<-

He ascends and descends below to all those who are low, to receive from them. And from them come anger, wrath, heat, and strength. All of these would not draw near until Jacob descended and shielded the anger and heat, breaking the "wheels of the day" <note>A reference to the harsh solar/judgmental forces</note>. He stretched out his hand over the covenant and struck the holy living creature, the bird, etc. He struck with a holy spirit, a powerful bird, to consume the anger. And he stretched out his hand toward the sea and "split the waters" <note>Exodus 14:21</note>. He divided the sea from the waters of anger, and the waters were divided toward the side of Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: the second Sephirah, representing the flash of intuition</term> and toward the side of Jacob. Thus, "the waters were split" to this side and to that side, and because of this, they all joined together to be bound as is fitting.

**Here** <note>original: "כאן" (Kan)</note> at the end of this, the verse "And he stretched out the staff" is written, every single letter in a square box with this language:
These are joined together to be bound on the side of Jacob, and all those who are low are judged from his side. Wondrous is this work in its strength, like the Holy Name, in the manner of a covering to make known the freedom of the connection <term>Kitora: a mystical knot or bond</term>. One faithful connection to become a complete Chariot <term>Merkavah: the divine assembly or vehicle of God's presence</term>. And in the manner of a covering, they are all made. And the companions <note>The circle of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> know how to shield together as one, to strengthen the deeds as is fitting. And this secret is the connection of the covering, turning mercy into judgment and judgment into mercy, to assist Kindness <term>Chesed</term>, to be for life, for good, or for evil. Blessed are the righteous who know the secrets of the Torah and know how to shield with the covering of the Holy King. Blessed are they in this world and in the world to come.

**And here** <note>original: "וכאן" (Ve-kan)</note> I found some of the names of the angels from these three verses in a square, every name consisting of three letters in one box: forward, backward, and forward. "And from your right let there be light," but I did not print them before "Let there be the glory of our holiness."

**Behold** <note>original: "הא" (Ha)</note>, the covering is like the King's works in connections that are tied one to another. And when they are joined together, no one can stand before them. There are seven connections tied within them: three for the covering and four to bring the distant near and to build one connection. And these are the ones that are all dust, their visions joined one to another, and we see them as one connection with three *Yods* <note>The Hebrew letter Yod, often representing a point of divine energy</note>. The third is the perfection of all faith. The desire of the two pillars of the body stands upon them. The fifth is the oath, the crown of the covering, the power of life and the deep word of all, hidden from all in mercy. The seventh is like the first, as it was said, the crown of the wine, because the living creature finds rest for all. And because the living creature finds rest for all, they searched thus: it stands as the source of all branches that divide from its side. Seven levels go from one level to another <note>Perhaps should read: "that which is here"</note> to make known that it is one Chariot in all those things that are divided within it. And so from level to level, all are found behind that level which is appointed over them, and this is the establishment of the matter. 

And come and see: these levels are found in all faith below, and these are the seven clouds that sheltered Israel. Because of this, when the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> travels behind them, they all travel; all the levels are prepared within them, and then she is crowned as is fitting. Come and see that Aaron inherited the sea like the Sea of Kinneret. Why does Judah have a portion in it? Is not Judah like the whole kingdom? Rabbi Elazar said: This portion contains the work of the Menorah and the strength and all that is here. But since it is written, they brought the offering of the altar near above and every rectification below, the verse comes and repeats the work of the Menorah, which is a rectification above by the hand of Aaron. For the Menorah, with all its directions and designs, is entirely by the hand of Aaron the Priest. And come and see: the altar has twelve openings found in it, and this establishes the twelve boundaries, the four banners, etc., and all are twelve. And everything is in the likeness of that which is above. The Menorah is to the south...

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Beha'alotcha. The previous section likely discussed the initial instructions for the Menorah, and here the text transitions into the spiritual significance of the Incense (Ketoret) and the purification of the Levites.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Beha'alotcha (When You Ascend)**<-

To be appointed at the time when they are worthy to be kindled by the hand of the Priest <note>the Kohen</note>, and a proclamation goes forth regarding the sustenance of the world, and it was not made etc. to establish through action that which is proclaimed. It mentions the service and proclaims: "Stand as one for the joy of all!" and a voice to establish it, as it is written: **"Ointment and incense rejoice the heart"** <note>Proverbs 27:9</note>. And we see that there were two altars: one was the innermost of all, standing for joy, and one for offering sacrifices, which appears subordinate to the first. And he who sees and observes and knows the secret of the matter—the fats and the waste—knows that for this reason, the incense was only offered at the time when the oil was present. As found in the book of King Solomon, incense was for joy and to kindle the dwelling place. What is the reason? Because the scent is found from that which is outside, but the joy and the bond of everything is that innermost point where everything stands. And when this is awakened, all Judgment <note>Din</note> is removed and cannot execute judgment. For this reason, the incense stands to nullify death <note>original: "motna" - plague/death</note>. Therefore, incense is a "binding" <note>term: kitiro - a knot or bond</note> of everything, and it is offered in that innermost place. Happy are Israel in this world and the world to come; of them it is written: *And He said to me, "You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified."* <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

**108** **"Take the Levites..."** <note>Numbers 8:6</note> It has been established that they must be purified (*other books: blessed*) and prepared, and all of them must be bound together like the strength of the left arm and the side of Judgment <note>Din</note>. And anyone who comes from the side of the spirit must shave the hair, because judgment is changed in the world. Therefore, below it is done in this manner so that hair is not seen outside, and through this, the moisture and the shame of the hair are sustained. We have established and stated that then all those who come from the side of Judgment are blessed. Regarding the Levites it is written: **"And thus shall you do to them to cleanse them... and let them pass a razor [over all their flesh]..."** <note>Numbers 8:7</note>. The place of the Levites does not ascend to both sides except through the Priest, because the Right <note>Mercy</note> always leads the Left <note>Judgment</note>. On the day the Levites ascend to their place, two portions are spread out to receive them. When it reaches this "Cow" which is called the Red Heifer <note>Parah Adumah</note>, the Priest—every word and every preparation—depends on him. Because all the strength of the body stands in the right arm, and therefore the Priest is the right arm; all these stand in him to strengthen everything and to sustain the world. And therefore, it is not found in the Levites except in the body and the left, and the body is the root of all.

**Zot** **"This is that which belongs to the Levites..."** <note>Numbers 8:24</note> Come and see: five plus twenty-five years <note>referring to the age of service</note>, he ascends to his place to be crowned. When he reaches this level of fifty years, he removes the forces from the strength of the flame within him. Once he has struck and reached perfection, he faces that place to be bound within it. Furthermore, he is not bound with it quite so much so that he is not flawed, but rather to be strengthened. For every spirit is strong and stands not in weakness. He must not flaw that place where he is bound; the pressure of the spirit is strong and not weak. Therefore, one should not show weakness at all in any side. Happy is the man who observes his ways and knows wisdom, and does not fail or change, as it is written: **"For the ways of the Lord are right..."** <note>Hosea 14:10</note>.

**Vayedaber** **"And the Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai..."** <note>Numbers 9:1</note> Come and see: for what reason does it stop here and speak? It is because of the support of the Sukkot <note>Tabernacles</note>, for Israel thought they were finished with the wilderness. Once they had performed the service and rested as in the wilderness, they thought no more was needed. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, came and warned them about it, so they would not think the voice had passed... <note>The text here becomes a bit compressed regarding the transition to the Passover sacrifice in the wilderness</note>.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Torah's hidden nature, specifically focusing on the famous "Garments of the Torah" passage from the Zohar, Parashat Behaalotcha 152a. It follows the previous discussion on the lighting of the Menorah and the elevation of the soul.</meta>

## Behaalotcha

Thus, when the eye is focused <note>literally: "squinting" or "turning aside" to focus</note> to bind itself within the various levels, this light is made for them according to the manner he commanded them. From this point forward, in that place where all the commandments of the Torah were established—and regarding many places, what is meant by "many places"? It is like the Attribute of Mercy. Rather, it is a sublime mystery: there was an Elder and there was a Holy One. What is the difference between this one and that one? One is a measure and the other is a measure. This "Elder" is from the side of the Throne to the left, and thus it is at the time when all the commandments of the Torah were given through it.

**Rabbi Shimon** said: Woe to the person who says that the Torah comes merely to show stories and mundane matters! For if that were so, even in this present time we could create a "Torah" out of mundane matters, and with even greater praise than all of them. If it were only to show the things of the world, even the secular rulers of the world possess among them more sublime matters. If so, let us follow them and make a Torah out of them! 

Rather, all the words of the Torah are sublime matters and a most high mystery. The upper world and the lower world were established in a single balance. Israel is below and the supernal angels are above. Regarding the supernal angels, it is written: *He makes His angels spirits* <note>Psalm 104:4</note>. And when they descend below, they must clothe themselves in the garments of this world. For if they did not clothe themselves in a garment after the fashion of this world, they would not be able to exist in this world, and the world could not endure them. 

And if it is so for the angels, how much more so for the Torah—which created them and created all the worlds, and they all exist for its sake! Once it descended to this world, if it had not clothed itself in these garments of this world, the world would not have been able to endure it. Therefore, the story of the Torah is the garment of the Torah. He who thinks that this garment is the Torah itself and nothing else—may his spirit deflate, and may he have no portion in the World to Come! For this reason, David said:

> Open my eyes, that I may behold wonders out of Your Torah.
<note>Psalm 119:18</note>

Meaning: that which is *underneath* the garment of the Torah. 

Come and see: there is a garment visible to everyone. When fools see a person in a beautiful garment, they do not look further than that garment. But the essence of the garment is the body, and the importance of the body is the soul. In this same way, the Torah has a body—and these are the "Bodies of the Torah" <term>Gufei Torah: the essential laws and commandments</term>. This body is clothed in garments, which are the stories of this world. The fools of the world look only at that garment, which is the story of the Torah, and they know nothing more; they do not look at what is beneath that garment. Those who know more do not look at the garment, but at the body that is beneath that garment. But the wise—the servants of the Supreme King, those who stood at Mount Sinai—look only at the Soul, which is the root of everything, the real Torah itself. And in the time to come, they are destined to look at the "Soul of the Soul" <term>Nishmata d'Nishmata: the innermost essence or the Divine light within the Torah</term>. 

Come and see: Above there is also a garment, a body, a soul, and a soul of the soul. These matters are as follows: the "garment" is the mystery of the outer form; the "body" is the assembly of the soul, which is the "Beauty of Israel" <term>Tiferet Israel: the central Sefirah representing the Written Torah</term>. Regarding this, it is written: *He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life* <note>Genesis 2:7</note>—this refers to the "Beauty of Israel," which is the Torah itself. And the "Soul of the Soul" is the "Holy Ancient One" <term>Atika Kadisha: the highest manifestation of Divinity, Keter</term>. Everything is bound together, one within the other. 

Woe to those wicked ones who say the Torah is nothing but a mere story, and they look at this garment and no further! Happy are the righteous who look at the Torah as is proper. Just as wine cannot sit except within a jar, so the Torah cannot sit except within this garment. Therefore, one must look only at what is beneath the garment. All these words and all these stories are but garments.

---

**And the children of Israel shall keep** the Passover in its appointed season. See, it says "And they shall make" <note>Numbers 9:2; the Hebrew 'Veya'asu' can mean 'keep' or 'make'</note>. Rabbi Yose said: It has been taught that anyone who observes the Sabbath below as is proper, it is as if he "made" it above. For because of his actions, that matter is affected—as it were <term>Kivyakhol: a term used to avoid anthropomorphizing God</term>—as if he himself made it. And this has already been explained.

---

<summary>This page contains the Zohar's famous defense of the Torah's mystical depth, arguing that the literal stories are merely "garments" for a deeper body (laws) and soul (divine mysteries). It warns against literalism and explains that the Torah's structure mirrors the human hierarchy of garment, body, and soul.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar - Ra'aya Meheimna)

### [Right Column]

**"Any man** who shall be unclean..." etc. 
The phrase "Any man" <note>Hebrew: *Ish Ish*</note> is repeated twice <note>Numbers 9:10</note>. See, see: "man" refers to a man who is established before Him, as we translate it, but who has caused a blemish in himself. Another interpretation: a human being upon whom the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> rests, but—Heaven forbid—because he constricted himself and opened a pit for himself, another [spirit] entered him—Heaven forbid—and he opened a breach to become—Heaven forbid—a pit for himself, so that the supernal holiness would not rest upon him.

**"Or** on a distant journey." This should not be treated lightly, as if it refers only to transgressing commandments like a commoner or like those who are not kings. Rather, "on a distant journey" is as mentioned: if a person does not purify himself, they distance him from Above. Once they distance him from Above, he is considered as being on a "distant journey." From that power of the seed of Israel, they see him as being on a "distant journey" from the power that was meant to bring you close, when the Holy One, blessed be He, descended to you as the knots were tied. Rabbi Isaac said: But is it not written, "unclean by reason of a corpse or on a distant journey"? These are two separate things below.
From what is written, see that Rabbi Yose returned here before they could show it to him. A Priest <note>Kohen</note> after they showed it to him. And from what they showed him, his voice was pleasant. See, the supernal holiness shall not rest upon him, and they shall not perform the Passover sacrifice at the time that Israel performs it. And if you say: Behold, in the second month he performs it, but he has not yet rectified himself? Heaven forbid! Once he purifies and rectifies himself, behold, the second month is for performing the Passover, for as much as a person purifies himself, they purify him from Above. And if you say that he sees a higher level in the second month, it is not so; for the holy desire is to perform the Passover in its proper time, when they were elevated to go out and descended as one... first building the structure. Regarding the Foundation <note>Yesod</note>, do not say that the Supernal One can examine the world alone; He cannot rectify everything unless the Kingdom <note>Malkhut</note> of purity was there to have mercy... therefore they surrounded him with words... Rabbi [Simeon] said.

For once the Assembly of Israel <note>Knesset Yisrael</note> is adorned with the crown of the Priest, she will not be adorned... thirty times from the time... the people of Israel sit with their crowns... and all the hosts are in joy. And... as the voice fades... and the crown from the source of water, and the source is purified through it... <meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Beha’alotcha. It features a section from the 'Raya Mehemna' (The Faithful Shepherd), a layer of the Zohar where Moses (the Shepherd) reveals secrets to the later generations. The text transitions from discussing the spiritual refinement of Israel to a homily on the construction of the Tabernacle.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Beha’alotcha**<-
<note>Numbers 8:1, "When you step up to set the lamps"</note>

The "Mixed Multitude" <note>original: *Erev Rav*; the non-Israelites who left Egypt with the Jews</note> will remain with their faction until the end of time, when they shall be "purified, made white, and refined" <note>Daniel 12:10</note>. And the King <note>God</note> will remove the impurity from you, and the holy thousands of my people shall be healed. And all will be refined like silver is refined and tested. The Mixed Multitude will be humbled before you, and those who merit life will shine "like the brightness of the firmament" <note>Daniel 12:3</note>. These are the ones who gaze upon this brightness, which is called **The Book of Splendor** <note>original: *Sefer ha-Zohar*</note>, for the sake of life. It is like the Garden of Manna where the elders and the wise gather. Those who merit it are the family of priests who shall endure. All the songs and praises of your journeys would not exist if not for this book. Everything is revealed and made clear. The Mixed Multitude has no portion here. In the future, when the time comes for the light to rise and be called forth, the holiness will not be approached by those who are unworthy. My people shall dwell in peace, and the holiness shall not be profaned by the missions of the wicked. For the Righteous One <note>the Sefirah of *Yesod*</note> is written as the inclusion of all; he performs the service of the King. Thus, all the judges of the people who delve into the depths shall endure. You shall be refined from all your heart’s impurities through <term>Wisdom</term> <note>Chokhmah</note> and <term>Kindness</term> <note>Chesed</note> on the right side of your understanding. As David said: "Your right hand does valiantly," "The right hand of the Lord is exalted," "The right hand of the Lord does valiantly" <note>Psalm 118:15-16</note>. These three are found and called as one. You shall take up the voice and the vision because of the three hidden levels: <term>Crown</term> <note>Keter</note>, <term>Beauty</term> <note>Tiferet</note>, and <term>Foundation</term> <note>Yesod</note>. They are not found on the right or the left, but because everything is included in them to be offered up in the three hidden grades. A voice called out to you: "Behold, my servant shall prosper, he shall be exalted and lifted up, and shall be very high" <note>Isaiah 52:13</note>. You shall be completed through the two Messiahs. David spoke of the three "right hands" regarding the Messiah son of David—"The right hand of the Lord" mentioned three times—corresponding to the three "left hands" which are the Messiah son of Ephraim. He carries the voice of the left, which is <term>Strength</term> <note>Gevurah</note>, so as not to die from the cave of the left. Your voice shall be hidden within it. And because the voice is below, it is carried to <term>Understanding</term> <note>Binah</note>, for in it you have placed the wisdom of the heart. Look at the suffering of the Messiah son of Ephraim in your exile, in your captivity, in your very body. It is good for all kinds of judgment so that he does not die. Seek mercy for him! It is said of him: "For he lives" through the influence of <term>Understanding</term>. Therefore, he shall not die from the side of <term>Strength</term>, for life flows from <term>Understanding</term> to pass over him the knot of purity. He is bound to the killing of the Tefillin <note>phylacteries</note>. He shall increase the foundation and tell of the deeds of the twelve. He is carried to the voice of <term>Foundation</term> <note>Yesod</note>, and they are joined by <term>Wisdom</term> <note>Chokhmah</note> and <term>Understanding</term> <note>Binah</note>, right and left. In your three "rights" and three "lefts," the Central Column is written, which includes the three: <term>Crown</term>, Prophet, and Levi. So shall he be established. The letter *Vav* shall be joined to the *He* on that day. Right and left shall be joined with mercy and supplications, with many appeasements for her <note>the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note>. In that day, the voice shall rise to "raise up the falling tabernacle of David" <note>Amos 9:11</note>. Because of this, it is said that through his coming and through supplications, the **Faithful Shepherd** <note>original: *Raya Mehemna*; Moses</note> arose. It is written of him and blessed is he. The mouth of the King spoke: "Because you have opened the paths of the right and the left." They said to the Faithful Shepherd: "You have known all this, and through your hand it shall be revealed to all, in your humility." As it is said of you: "And the man Moses was very humble, more than all men" <note>Numbers 12:3</note>. You have merited to strengthen the goodness for your children. Acquire for us and for the holy assembly the ability to be in your shadow and your strength in these two worlds.

---

**And on the day** that the tabernacle was reared up <note>Numbers 9:15</note>. Rabbi Hiyya opened his discourse:
> "He has dispersed, he has given to the poor; his righteousness endures forever; his horn shall be exalted with honor." <note>Psalm 112:9</note>

"He has dispersed, he has given to the poor"—how well-explained this is. "There is one who disperses, and yet increases more" <note>Proverbs 11:24</note>. Anyone in the world who disperses and gives to the poor, life flies toward him and he increases in everything. He increases in the hour and increases in years. The verse should have said: "There is one who disperses and life is added to him." Why does it say "increases more"? It means that life from Above is added to him. Rabbi Yehuda said in the name of Rabbi Hiyya: The verse comes to teach that anyone who gives to the poor awakens the Path of Life to add to everything. He removes death. Then life and joy are found Above. But when a person does not give, and does not act in the hour of need, the Path of Life is hidden from him and the Path of Death is prepared for him. Therefore, "his righteousness endures forever."

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Beha'alotcha** <-

These are the appointed overseers for the four sides <note>the cardinal directions</note> who are beyond numbering. The third head <note>division</note> for the final time consists of fifty-seven thousand and four hundred, in the same manner as it is written. And how is this calculated? Just as the mountain surrounds the elders before them, so it is from behind them. Since this first [standard] was within it, and "the Tabernacle was taken down," all of them moved to their resting places and the traveling ranks returned to their places, all from their respective sides. Then, as it is written: *“When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved beside them; and when the living creatures rose from the earth, the wheels rose”* <note>Ezekiel 1:21</note>.

The second standard is the **East**, the sustenance of the Crown of the Living Creature <note>the *Chayyah* or angelic being</note> that belongs to the secret of the two overseers with it: **Samkiel** and **Muriel**. This living creature is the **Eagle**; it ascends and all the camps that flee before it rise on every side. Each one stands in the strength that supports the spirit of the spirit; their mouths bring forth [speech], and that spirit reaches this Crown, ascending to close and cover the body. All of them are your supports, and for this reason, "it shall spread its wings toward the South" in the same manner, as a likeness, like the Crown of the Upright. And this Crown covers and conceals the books, and all the camps that flee are fanned away and cease.

One from the side <margin>another version: the West</margin> before it ascends from below to above; many "birds" descend and enter, fluttering and ceasing, going and pressing. When the threads of the fleeing ones are cut, the dwelling returns like a vessel for all three hundred and fifty kinds. Even the camps that flee in two branches and their strength are as one. A voice is raised, and all the others ascend and descend, fluttering from their sides from several levels. There are three "heads" <note>leaders/divisions</note> that are as one, like the sides that are joined; all of them are as one in their numbering, and their numbering is swift. The first head is forty-six thousand and five hundred. The second head is fifty-nine thousand and three hundred. The third head is forty-five thousand and six hundred and fifty.

Two sides are like the faces of the two **Cherubim** that I saw before all the sides; every two are from a herald. All their hosts and all the guards, the small with the great, are all gathered together. Their appearance is like the plaster of all the firmaments; they are all like dew or like sand in the rains before Him. If a mistake is found in one of them, the one who is struck from one side to the other spreads a voice so that all those voices will not be known. Then all those guards are gathered at the time when another calls out; the voice breaks and does not spread. All those sides of this Crown are all gathered to be moistened in their travels. Corresponding to these are the *“two silver trumpets”* <note>Numbers 10:2</note>; in this manner, everything below [reflects what is above].

<term>Come and see</term> <note>Aramaic: Ta Chazei; a standard Zoharic opening for a new insight</note>: when these are traveling, what is written? *“When the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them”* <note>Ezekiel 1:19</note>, for they are gathered into their prophecies; in the likeness of the spirit, look at them all in this way.

The third standard is the mountain of the **North**. Two overseers are with it: **Kafniel** and **Hezkiel**. This mountain is from the **Left Side** <note>the side of Judgment/Gevurah</note>. Its horns ascend between its two eyes; they rage in their looking. Its eyes flame like a spark of burning fire; it gores and tramples with its feet. This **Ox** <note>the face of the Ox in the Chariot</note> spares all who move. From the hole of the **Great Abyss** <note>Tehom Rabbah</note> emerge many damaging bands <margin>another version: oppressive ones</margin>. All of them are victorious and pressing, standing in the wrath of all the strengths that hang before it, for all the strengths of the world all ascend and are written in the book.

At the hour when this terror flows before it, when the host pushes toward that male Crown and draws it like a measure, small and thin as one... <note>The text here becomes highly cryptic, referring to colors and lights</note>. And perhaps from the side of the South a river goes out that settles their weariness; the world could not endure the darkness below. There, darkness is not darkened; light, like many weavers, goes and presses like the darkness. And that one burns from this side; the fire of **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note> is darkened. And if you say there is no white mercy, there is mercy for Wisdom, red mercy, for there are two colors. Do not say it is otherwise, for so it is. And it acts higher and higher; thus it is gazed upon, and from there the hosts are moved. Beneath it, the white is established, just as the white mercy was gazed upon, and Wisdom sinned <note>or "inclined"</note> upon the white mercy, the crowns of the mouth to gaze upon the **Torah**. Come, there is one mercy that lives, and it is divided into four: three white...

## Main Text (Zohar)

Those [levels] divide into four directions, one and merit. And when this divides into four, three heads are found <note>original: *ishtakchu*; variant: *itachadu* - "united"</note> on these sides. Sometimes their radiance is a single head, a hidden thing that is not heard. From this, a second head is joined and one passes, and from this passing, a third head [emerges]. Three and life-forces pass, and four pass when those other levels are separated on their sides and have no goodness. All of them are levels upon levels, like many officers of the law who are below, fawning like dogs and biting like donkeys. Woe to one who is found among them and in their judgment on the "Evil Side." For without will, Raphael spreads out on the side of protection. On the side of **Man**, the supernal image is included upon him below. This <note>variant: *me'od* - "very"</note> voice in the horns of the mountain, all who provoke [the Heavens] above, [He casts] them to the Great Abyss. And He binds them so that the world does not burn in this fire. The voice that fills the thin [silence] is cast out, for one who merits <note>variant: *saka* - "looks/gazes"</note> the word as is proper, the word of recognition is not known at all. On this side, one is cast out from the path of the cleft; one who ascends is blocked and enters to be remembered in this place. Because of this: *And you shall sound a broken blast (Teruah)* on the South side. The purpose here is to burn, and not the voice that shows the *Teruah* to subdue the North wind, and because of the North side's place. Come and see: two trumpets, as they are from two sides, which are said to be from the East and from the South. These are the "Right Hand" to break the judgments and to subdue them. And regarding those [made] of silver and of gold: *And on the day of your gladness, and in your appointed seasons, etc., and you shall blow with the trumpets.* It is written both above and below. And these are Israel, whose voice is like harps, and they shall have a supernal portion over all other nations. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, returns to them with an addition of life, as it is said: *And He said to me, "You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified"* <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>.

---

**And it came to pass** when the Ark set forward, that Moses said, etc. <note>Numbers 10:35</note>. Rabbi Elazar said: Here one must look at the two [Nuns] of that lamp to burn. These are in two places here. Come and say: a "bent Nun" (נ) is known as the Female, and a "straight Nun" (ן) is as Male and Female, and we have established this in these two. *And it came to pass when the Ark set forward*—this shows that it returns later in the fledgling of the thirty-two. Come and see: *When the Ark set forward, Moses said, etc.* This is the time because it [the Shekhinah] is in exile. And we have established what is written:
> She is fallen, she shall no more rise, the virgin of Israel <note>Amos 5:2</note>
Rather, what is written forever?
> And the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord went before them a three days' journey, to seek out a resting place for them <note>Numbers 10:33</note>
Since this Ark was traveling, it is written "Supernal," and the Shekhinah sat upon the Ark. Come and see the love of the Holy One, Blessed be He, for Israel! For even though they are ground down from the side of Holiness, they did not want to find them [lacking], and at all times He turns His face toward them so they do not stand as a void world. See how the spirit blows like dew before them for three days. This *Nun* (נ) was spread out from here, and it is written "deep." And when Israel stood, He would turn His face and be hidden from the spirit, like this serpent of the season; when it travels, it turns its face to a bent place. And regarding *When the Ark set forward*, it was directed toward a place of strength for Israel, and its shoulders were opposite the spirit. And while the staff was striking, he said: *Rise up, O Lord!* Do not turn away from us to return to [Your place]. Therefore, it was directed and turned back toward them, in this manner, like one who turns his face to one who is beloved. And when the Ark would rest, then the *Nun* would turn its face from the side and return toward the spirit, and everything was restored. Rabbi Shimon said: Elazar, my firstborn, it is so. But here, its face did not turn away from Israel, for it is thus required to transform from the aspect of the "Other Side" above <note>variant: "to above"</note>. For the *Nun* is from the furnace, and this is in the gold-engraving of the word regarding the Ark. Rather, certainly He did not turn His face from them. And what did He do? At the time the Ark traveled, Moses said: *Rise up, O Lord!* Then the Ark and the Shekhinah stood on the other side, with faces toward Israel and toward the Ark. And because of this, it was then included within the Ark.

## Main Text (Zohar)

The Holy One, Blessed be He, <note>original: קד"ה/קב"ה</note> bestows wealth because they merited the World to Come, and it returns to him as **capital**. This capital is the fulfillment; it is the place where the soul is revealed. Likewise, the wise must strive to testify to this capital and receive it after departing from this world, because this capital is the portion of that world which does not exist in this world—except for that Palace from which it emerges. Man eats from its "fruits" <note>the secondary benefits or interest</note> if he merits it in this world, while the **capital** remains for him in that world to be consumed in the eternal life above. But one who considers only himself and follows his own desires, neglecting his soul and himself—his portion is disqualified; it returns and is not prepared to meet him in awe or to receive him above. Then, the "slain" <note>destructive spiritual forces</note> who consumed it shall not rule over him, and from the merit of that wealth and awe, the lack shall be consumed...

Likewise, a person must merit that which the Holy One, Blessed be He, grants him for that world; he eats from it in this world, and it returns to that **capital** in the World to Come to be clarified in the Light of Life. Rabbi Yose said: It is certainly written, "He who spares his money leaves it to others at every moment," etc. And why is this? Because of what the people of the world do, for they go and produce excess to be eaten by others besides themselves. Rabbi Abba said: This exchange and the spirit of the world come from that which is a destruction before Him...

Come and see: the beginning of "And he..." <note>referring to a scriptural verse</note> rises in a way that is not desired in shame. That voice was the voice of charity. And according to the claim that the Holy One, Blessed be He, established it to be so from your side and from the Heavens... now that reproach is found within him. For because of him, this suffering was found. Since it was said: "Because you have shamed her to follow him," and kindness and goodness are proper... <margin>from the mountain of Aram</margin> <margin>and holy</margin> <note>marginal notes likely referring to the source of the soul or the location of the revelation</note> ...the level of the Levite... like the sea... they shall consume and tear like the wilderness... and the Assembly of Israel <note>original: כנסת ישראל</note>. And Moses' vision was to descend; the Holy One, Blessed be He, loved him more than all the prophets of the world without any intermediary at all, as it is written: **"Mouth to mouth I will speak with him,"** and we have established this in several places.

->**"And Moses cried out to the Lord..."** <note>Numbers 12:13</note> They have established this: it is the secret of the thin voice of eleven letters, and Moses did not wish to lengthen his prayer further, because for his own sake <note>or for his own kin</note> he did not wish to trouble the King.<-

->**Behaalotecha**<-
<note>original: "When you step up" — the name of the Torah portion in Numbers 8:1–12:16</note>

To be found more [present], the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not seek His own glory, but rather the glory of Moses. In every place, the Holy One, Blessed be He, seeks the glory of the righteous more than His own. And in the time to come, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to claim the grievance of Israel from the idol-worshipping nations and to establish them in the joy of Zion, as it is written: *And they shall come and sing in the height of Zion...* <note>Jeremiah 31:11</note>. **And the Lord spoke** to Moses, saying: "Send for yourself men, that they may scout the land of Canaan..."
Rabbi Chinana opened [the discourse]: *Have you commanded the morning since your days; and caused the dayspring to know its place?* <note>Job 38:12</note>. It is written here "to strengthen from the morrow," why? "Send," said Rabbi Hiyya, at the hour when evening approaches and the sun is darkened, then Samael <note>The primary figure of evil or the "Accuser" in Kabbalah</note> rules and Judgments are found in the world and spread Above. Once the night enters, the gates of the lock open in the fifth spark, and many damaging camps [of spirits] wander in the world; he grinds them all in his struggles. They appear and stand in the drippings of the head, informing people of hidden matters—some false and some true. Sometimes their nicknames are found to be given permission to destroy, and all the people of the world sleep and taste the taste of death <note>The Talmud teaches that sleep is 1/60th of death</note>, as we have established. 

Come and see: when the North wind is aroused, then the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> is prepared, and they are found as one, a shield on the lower arm. The Holy One, Blessed be He, comes to delight with the righteous who are in the Garden of Eden. At that time, anyone who awakens to toil in the Torah <term>Torah: the Five Books of Moses and the broader body of Jewish law and mysticism</term> is joined with Her, because She and all Her "tongues" [languages/expressions] praise the Supreme King. All those found in the praise of the Torah are all inscribed in the Palace and engraved with truths, marked as weapons in [due] time.

We have established these two letters [Lamed and Kaf] to include twelve letters... here the division of midnight is revealed. <meta>This page continues the Zohar’s commentary on the Torah portion *Shelach Lecha* (Numbers 13-15), focusing on the mystical motivations behind Moses sending the spies and the spiritual nature of the Land of Israel.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Send for Yourself** <-

Because of that serpent which is prepared within, they shall stand as one when its time arrives. From this, every guardian of the orchard <note>original: *kofra*, referring to the protective shell or "husk" of the spiritual realm</note> acts according to the hour of gathering. When the labor pains arrived, wisdom and understanding were not found. If you wish to know of it: "Send for yourself" wise men for your own sake, in order to know. Come and see: If you say that Moses did not know the land and therefore entered it at that time—it is not so. Rather, he knew, but he desired to know more of it before he departed [from this world]. He ascended to those who "lick the dust" <note>a reference to the spiritual forces associated with the earth</note>, but since they did not answer the matter properly, he did not send another time until the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded him, as it is written: *Go up to this mountain of Abarim* and see the land, and it is written <note>Deuteronomy 34:1</note> *And the Lord showed him all the land.* And He did not show it to him alone, but rather all those who were destined to stand in every single generation; Moses saw them all. The companions have established this.

When Moses delayed in sending them, what did he say to them? <note>Numbers 13:20</note> *Is there a tree in it?* etc. What is the meaning of what he said? If you say he did not know, later he will say the matter. But here Moses said: "Heaven forbid, is there a tree in it?" If you knew that there was Life there <note>referring to the Tree of Life</note>, the external forces <note>original: *achitzan*, the "outside" shells of evil</note> would not go there. For Life was only found in the earthly Garden of Eden. He said: "Heaven forbid, is there a tree in it?"—meaning, is the [Tree of] Life there? If not, it is not here, and there is no purpose in entering. 

Rabbi Hiyya said: It is written, *As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him* <note>Proverbs 25:13</note>. My brother, come and see: who is this? This is the engraving <note>the mystical imprint of the soul</note>. And he looks through these windows to see if they bend toward another side and do not sin against the glory of their Master. If one exchanges one for another, he returns in sin... and the spirit of all is certainly gathered. Therefore, his judgment is hidden and his judgment is not publicized like the others, because from him, he does not seek sin and death, and it was not revealed. And it can be said it was not spoken of as revealed, and the Holy One, blessed be He, acted with honor for his honor. 

Rabbi Yose said: The gatherer of wood <note>referring to the man who gathered wood on the Sabbath in Numbers 15</note> was gathered and received punishment according to the hour, and his sin was not atoned for until Moses was established. As it is written, it was not known if it was atoned for his daughters to ascend and be sustained or not. Once the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke his name, it became known that his sin was atoned. 

Come and see: there are two windows, one above and one below. One is Life and one is Death. Whoever exchanges them causes death for himself in this world and has no portion in the world to come. And regarding this Solomon said, *He who guards the fig tree shall eat its fruit* etc. The Wrath and the Torah stand as one; the Torah is their root and house. And regarding the Ark, it is sold as all, and if in every place it is the *Ark of the Covenant*, the *Ark of the Testimony*. In every place, Aaron is the right arm, except for one instance where it is written *the sum of those who were numbered by Moses and Aaron* <note>Numbers 4:46</note>, which is a counting above. 

Moses knew that the Tree of Life was there, and because of this he wanted to know if it was settled in the land or not. Therefore <note>Numbers 13:20</note> *Be of good courage, and bring of the fruit of the land.* For the Tree of Life is desired by all, but they [the spies] brought only grapes, pomegranates, and figs, which hang and take hold in another palace <note>a lower spiritual realm</note>. Come and see:

-> **Send** <-

For yourself, wise men among your sons. Rabbi Yehuda opened: *As the cold of snow in the time of harvest...* This refers to the breath of the righteous and the good. *As the cold of snow*—this is for the body and the soul. *A faithful messenger*—these are the faithful messengers sent to Joshua. They brought joy and goodness, for the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the indwelling presence of God</term> returned to dwell among Israel and did not depart from them. But see what the first ones [the spies of Moses] caused: because they went after their own hearts, they caused thousands and tens of thousands to depart from Israel, and they caused the Divine Presence to ascend from the land and away from Israel. But those sent by Joshua brought joy and goodness. 

Rabbi Hezekiah said: *And he took...* Rabbi Yose said to Rabbi Hezekiah: Look at this, there is no life in your sons. He said to him: Indeed, see the verse, I have looked into it. Since Solomon said <note>Ecclesiastes 3:19</note> *For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them,* etc. Understand that all the words of King Solomon are all hidden levels of Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: the Sephirah of Wisdom</term>. If so, this verse has no portion [in the simple meaning], for it is an opening for those who are not children of faith <note>meaning the verse sounds skeptical or heretical if not understood mystically</note>.
