<meta>This page continues the narrative of the sages traveling on the road, a common setting in the Zohar for the revelation of hidden mysteries. It follows a discussion on faith and the divine nature of the human soul.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Faith is found within him. **Rabbi Elazar** said: It is so, and there is no need to search or look further. While they were walking, a man approached them. He asked them about the day before him and what would happen in the heat of the sun. They said to him, "Who are you?" He said to them, "I am an Arab <note>original: "Tay'ah," often used in the Zohar to represent a simple-looking traveler who reveals profound wisdom</note>, and I am a traveler and a guide." They said to him, "And your journey?" He said to them, "Until I come with you in words of the way, and there I find my path and my descent." **Rabbi Yose** took out a fruit from his provisions and gave it to him. He said, "I will walk with you in everything." He drank after he had eaten. They went up on the way and found a thin thread of a path, full of drops <note>perhaps referring to dew or small springs</note>, and they sat down. He said to them: The **Holy One, Blessed be He**, opens the way as they go, for here they are found on the paths by the hand of a son who goes to enter the house of study, and his building opens the paths. **Rabbi Hezekiah** said, "If it is by the hand of my son, it is good, but how do you know this? Rather, from the joy of another place one must look." That man said, "I will speak of the King, for sometimes in the redemption of the poor, a pearl is found." He said to him, "This verse that Solomon spoke, what of it?" He said to him, "How many of you are like those who plow after men who do not know?" They said to him, "Regarding what?" He said to them, "Regarding this, Solomon said this verse, and he did not say it from himself as if those words were worthy, but rather to repeat those words that the fools of the world say. And what do they say?"
> For the fate of the sons of men and the fate of the beast... <note>Ecclesiastes 3:19</note> 

The fools who do not know and do not look into Wisdom say that this world goes by chance <note>original: "mikreh," meaning happenstance or fate</note>, and they do not find upon them anything but the chance of man and the chance of the beast being one. And when Solomon looked at these fools who say this, he called them "beasts," for they make themselves like actual beasts by saying these words. And from here he called out above, and this is what is written:
> I said in my heart concerning the matter of the sons of men, that God might clear them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts. <note>Ecclesiastes 3:18</note> 

"I said in my heart"—and they were found in this, to look upon what? Upon "the matter of the sons of men," upon that word of foolishness that they said, "that God might clear them" <note>or "select them"</note> alone, and they would not be joined with other men. They say they have no faith, "and to see that they themselves are beasts." "And to see"—when they are people of faith—that those [fools] are beasts to themselves, and in their own minds they are like cattle, and not to be mixed with the treasures of faith according to this foolish view; and regarding this, "they are to themselves" and not to another. And what is their view?
> For the fate of the sons of men and the fate of the beast, one fate is to them all... <note>Ecclesiastes 3:19</note> 

May their spirits be exhaled! For they are cattle, they are fools, they are lacking in faith. Woe to them, woe to their souls! It would be better for them not to have come into the world. And what did Solomon write concerning this? He called out as a wise man and said:
> Who knows the spirit of the sons of men that goes upward, and the spirit of the beast that goes downward to the earth? <note>Ecclesiastes 3:21</note> 

"Who knows"—like those fools who do not know the glory of the Upper King and do not look at the path. The spirit of the sons of men "goes upward" to a precious upper place that the Holy One shows, to be seen by the Upper Light <note>original: "manhiro ala'ah"</note> from the glory of the Holy King, to be a "bond in the Bond of Life" <note>original: "tzrora d'chayye," a reference to the soul's eternal rest with God</note> and to be found before the Holy King in a perfect world; certainly, it "goes upward." But the spirit of the beast "goes downward to the earth," to that place which is for every [animalistic] man, as it is written:
> In the image of God He made man. <note>Genesis 9:6</note> 

And it is written:
> The soul of man is the lamp of the Lord. <note>Proverbs 20:27</note> 

How can those fools, who are not of the children of faith, say "they all have one spirit"? May their spirits be exhaled! Concerning them it is written:
> Let them be as chaff before the wind, and let the angel of the Lord chase them. <note>Psalms 35:5</note> 

These are found among them, for they are of the lower levels <note>original: "dargin tatta'in"</note> and they shall not be established for generations upon generations. Concerning them it is written:
> Let sinners be consumed from the earth, and let the wicked be no more. Bless the Lord, O my soul. Hallelujah! <note>Psalms 104:35</note> 

**Rabbi Hezekiah** and **Rabbi Yose** came and kissed his hands, saying, "All this was with you and we did not know!" And they all arose in the awakening of the way.

He clarifies that while the animal spirit descends, the human soul is a divine lamp that ascends to be bound in the eternal Bond of Life.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Zohar’s discourse on the spiritual consequences of faithlessness and the transformation of character through service to the Divine. It transitions from a homily on the "living dog and dead lion" to the specific narrative of the Spies (Meraglim) in the Book of Numbers.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

He was saying, etc. Regarding this alone, Solomon was [wise], and he chose it and called it "wrath." In this manner, he opened and said: "And turn away from evil in all that is in the lower side," for that side is evil and bitter. This "evil" refers to those who take their dwellings away from the Holy One, Blessed be He, and He gives them no portion in the World to Come. Thus it is written: *For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You* <note>Psalms 5:5</note>. Regarding this, Rabbi [Eleazar] said: "Evil" shall have no dwelling place above. For the scripture says of all [such people]: *The heart of the sons of men is full of evil* <note>Ecclesiastes 9:3</note>. Because of this, *madness is in their hearts while they live*; their error is fixed in their hearts, and they are lacking in faith <term>faith: *meheimanuta*, a central Zoharistic term for mystical trust and connection to the Divine</term>, and they have no portion in the Holy One, Blessed be He. And just as their lives are such, so is their faith in this world and not in the World to Come. This is what is written: *and after that they go to the dead* <note>Ecclesiastes 9:3</note>.

Come and see: The Holy One, Blessed be He, warned [Israel] and said: *Choose life, that you may live, you and your seed* <note>Deuteronomy 30:19</note>—in this world and in the World to Come. And the life of that world is [true life]. Those who stand lacking in faith, what do they say? *For to him who is joined to all the living there is hope* <note>Ecclesiastes 9:4</note>. Even though a man chooses [life] in this world, as he said, it is nothing, for this matter is in our hands: *For all the living there is security*—this is in their hands—*for a living dog is better than a dead lion* <note>Ecclesiastes 9:4</note>. How shall we have life in that world? And until this [is resolved], it is His will that they shall not dwell with the High King and shall have no portion in Him.

And even though all these verses are connected to the proclamation like other matters, Solomon’s proclamation came to scoff at those who stand lacking in faith, who have no portion in the Holy One, Blessed be He, in this world or the World to Come. He said to him: "The condition you wrote in that [document], go with it." He replied: "If I do this, the Torah will be doubled upon me, and furthermore, I will be liable for my soul." They said to him: "Why?" He told them: "Because the forgiveness is lacking, so arrange it for me in perfection." And King Solomon said the verse: *Stolen waters are sweet* <note>Proverbs 9:17</note>, as it is written "doubled." A pearl <note>original: *margla*, a metaphor for a precious teaching</note> opened upon this: "Behold, the children of faith are found, and those [without] faith are liable for their souls in this world and the World to Come."

As he was going, Rabbi Hezekiah and Rabbi Jose saw him. As they were walking, they encountered those people. "Our brother!" they said to Rabbi Hezekiah and Rabbi Jose. They asked: "What is the name of that man?" They said: "He is Rabbi Mani, and he is a colleague of the members of the fellowship." The colleagues arranged for him to know all the words from Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and from the masters of the fellowship. Rabbi Jose said: "Certainly, this is Rabbi Mani, who all his days did not want to show himself in what he knew." And regarding this, he said to us that a herald called out to him in the Torah, because the verse says: *Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him* <note>Proverbs 26:12</note>. Certainly, he is a faithful messenger, and blessed is the faithful messenger, and blessed is he who arranges matters in the hand of a faithful messenger.

Come and see: Eliezer, the servant of Abraham, was from the children of Canaan, as you say: *Canaan, in whose hand are the balances of deceit* <note>Hosea 12:8</note>. And of Canaan it is written: *Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be to his brothers* <note>Genesis 9:25</note>. But because he was a faithful messenger, what is written of him? *Come in, O blessed of the Lord* <note>Genesis 24:31</note>. Literally "Blessed of the Lord!" And for this reason, it is written thus in the Torah, because he left that curse and was blessed. Not only did he leave it, but he was blessed in the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and he was transformed below into an angel <note>original: *malakh*</note>, and this matter entered the mouth of the [sages].

# **Shelach Lecha**
(Send for yourself...)

**And Moses sent them, etc.** <note>Numbers 13:3</note>. They were all wise, they were all righteous, and they were the heads of Israel. But they took for themselves an evil counsel. Why did they take this counsel? Rather, they said: "If Israel enters the Land, we will be removed from being leaders, and other leaders will be appointed over us. For we were worthy in the wilderness to be leaders for all the tribes." And because they took an evil counsel for themselves, they died—they and all those who took counsel with them.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion "Shlach Lecha" (Numbers 13-15). It focuses on the spiritual dynamics of the spies' mission to Canaan, specifically contrasting the protection of Joshua and Caleb against the "evil counsel" of the other spies.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Shlach Lecha (Send for Yourself)**<-

**These** are the names of the men whom Moses sent, etc. <note>Numbers 13:16</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: What did Moses see that he did not send them on their way together? For it was revealed to him regarding Joshua <note>that he needed special protection</note>, while Caleb was in distress, saying, "What shall I do?" For Joshua went with the assistance of the prayer of Moses, who arranged for him a focused intention <note>Hebrew: *kavanah*</note> of speed, and joined a company over him in his exile because of Moses' concern. What did Caleb do? He turned away from their intention and went down to the graves of the Patriarchs <note>in Hebron</note> and offered his prayer there. Rabbi Judah said: He said to the Master of the World, "I am burdened with sins and heavy paths, and I hide upon the graves of the Patriarchs," for he was terrified of the giants, as it is written: *And there were Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the children of the Anak* <note>Numbers 13:22</note>. For anyone in such distress does not look at anything else. Thus Caleb, because he was ultimately in distress, looked at nothing else and went down to pray at the graves of the Patriarchs to be saved from the counsel of the others <note>the ten spies who brought a bad report</note>.

---

**And Moses** called Hoshea the son of Nun, Joshua. Rabbi Isaac said: Did he only call him by this name now? Is it not already written, *And Moses said to Joshua* <note>Exodus 17:9</note>, and *Joshua the son of Nun, a youth* <note>Exodus 33:11</note>, and *Joshua weakened* <note>Exodus 17:13</note>? Rather, Moses said to him: "May the Lord <note>the letters Yud-He</note> save you <note>Hebrew: *Yoshi'acha*</note> from their counsel." Rabbi Abba said: Since Moses sent him there, he needed to be complete. Just as we have explained regarding the "city" <note>Ar</note> which is the claim of the "watcher" <note>Ir</note> as we have established, and in that claim Moses bound him like this <note>original: *כהדא*</note>, so that Joshua would be found as before; the verse calls him this because of what was destined to be fulfilled. Moses said: "It is not certainly necessary to enter there except as we have seen and hoped to rectify."

---

**Whether** there is a tree in it or not, etc. <note>Numbers 13:20</note>. Rabbi Hiyya said: Did Moses not know that there were many fruit-bearing trees there? It was not about this or that, for he had praised the land to Israel many times, and he was satisfied with it. But the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him to look as before, for it is a land of olives, milk, and honey. Rabbi Yose said: We have been awakened by the herald, as it is written: *The tree was like a cedar* <note>referring to a spiritual Tree</note> to provide support. Rabbi Simeon said: This hints at wisdom regarding how they went at first, as it is written: *Is the Lord among us or not?* <note>Exodus 17:7</note>. He said there: "If He is below, it shall be for their success." He said to them: "If He who dwells in the land is like the land of the world, then 'is there a tree in it' and nothing more? But if He who dwells in the land is greater and more praised than any place in the world, you shall examine it; for from the Holy Ancient One <term>Atika Kadisha: the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</term> it flows, and the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> is drawn over it more than any place in the world." And thus you shall examine: *Is there a tree in it or not?* This is like the first question you asked to know this, as it is written: *Is the Lord among us?*—specifically "among us"—to see if He has a "Tree" <note>a reference to the Righteous One or the Tree of Life</note>. *And be of good courage and bring of the fruit of the land* to know its difference. *Now the time was the time of the first ripe grapes.* Why does it speak of "days" <note>Hebrew: *yamim*</note>? It should have said "the time of grapes." Rather, these "days" are those that are known; they were all joined at that time, and they merited the Tree that Adam reached in his mercy, as they say they were grapes. And regarding this, those "days" are known specifically as the *days of the first ripe grapes*.

---

**And they went up** into the South and he came unto Hebron <note>Numbers 13:22</note>. It should have said "And they came" <note>plural</note>. Rather, Rabbi Yose said: This refers to Caleb, who departed to the graves of the Patriarchs and was seen there. Caleb said: "Joshua has already been prepared with the assistance of prayer and can be saved from their intention; but as for me, what shall I do?" He took counsel to seek a request at the graves of the Patriarchs so that he might be saved from the secret of these profaners. Rabbi Isaac said: Behold, the end of the matter depends on all of them, for the change of the name <note>of Joshua</note> hangs over everything. And come and see: he was lacking until he was able to enter there, for it is written: *And there were Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai*, and the fear of them was visible, yet he was able to enter by the congregation.

It also provides a kabbalistic reading of Moses' question about the "tree" in the land, linking it to the Divine Presence and the Tree of Life.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the spies' journey to the Land of Israel, specifically focusing on their arrival at Hebron and the spiritual implications of their mission. # Shelach Lecha

In the cave, they saw the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> resting there, like one who enters to labor for the wise; for the time had come to enter their dwellings in the land. The Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu"</note>, beheld them, and there was no dispute until Hebron. We have learned in the house of study and we have taught: from whom did they emerge? Their will was struck by the "doubles" <note>likely referring to Machpelah, meaning "double"</note> that the Holy One, Blessed be He, cast into the earth, and they crawled from the power of the earth. From them emerged the strangers of the world, as it is written: **The secret of the wise** <note>original: "Sod ha-Nevonim"</note>. He returned from the world of the seekers of truth, where the foundations of the world are found. The seekers of truth—we have learned in the house of study and we have taught:

Rabbi Judah opened the discourse: **Thus saith God the Lord, He that created the heavens, and stretched them forth, etc.** <note>Isaiah 42:5</note>. How much must human beings look into the service of the Holy One, Blessed be He! How much must they look into the words of the Torah! For anyone who exerts themselves in the Torah, it is as if they offered all the sacrifices of the world before the Holy One, Blessed be He. Not only that, but the Holy One, Blessed be He, forgives all their sins and prepares many thrones for them in the World to Come <note>original: "Alma de-Atei"</note>. 

Rabbi Judah was walking on the road with Rabbi Isaac. He said: I wish to learn one thing. ## Main Text (Zohar)

**'And they went up into the South, and he came unto Hebron'** <note>Numbers 13:22</note>. They occupy themselves and issue decrees, these to the right and those to the left, which are the forms of **Freedom** <note>A mystical term for the Jubilee or the world of Binah/Understanding.</note>. And the "children of the giant" <note>Hebrew: *Yelidei Ha-Anak*</note> were born from the side of Severity <note>The sefirah of Gevurah</note>. 

**'And Hebron was built seven years'**—behold, these are the seventy branches of Freedom; it has seventy faces on every side. And this Hebron is "Freedom"; whoever exerts himself in it is called a "companion" <note>Hebrew: *Chaver*, a play on Hebron</note>. **'Before Zoan in Egypt'**—we have established that there is a "freedom" corresponding to "freedom" <note>A reference to the holy versus the unholy realms</note>. And this is the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. And this Hebron emerges from the Written Torah, as it is said: **'Say unto Wisdom: You are my sister'** <note>Proverbs 7:4</note>. # Section: Shelach Lecha

## Main Text (Zohar)

The evil tongue <note>original: "Lishna Bisha," referring to the sin of slander or Lashon Hara</note> has no end; it has troubled the world since the beginning. Words of an evil tongue are as harmful as a frightening spirit that wanders here and there. Rabbi Shimon said: Above all, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is zealous regarding the evil tongue, for it is written: **"Who have said: 'With our tongue will we prevail; our lips are our own: who is lord over us?'"** <note>Psalm 12:5</note>. Come and see how much that evil tongue accomplished: it caused a decree upon our ancestors that they should not enter the Land. Those who spoke died, and they caused weeping for generations to come, just as they established an evil tongue over everything. As it were, since they spoke against the Holy Land, it was as if they spoke against Him <note>God</note>. Because of this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, intended for all of Israel to be removed from the world, were it not for the prayer of Moses.

**"And they told him, and said..."** <note>Numbers 13:27</note>. Rabbi Hiyya said: Heaven forbid that they lied in their report! Rather, it is written "and they told him" and "they said"—each one divided the matter in his speech. "And they told" <note>Hebrew: *Vayagidu*</note> in every place implies a hint of wisdom, and so it was said here. "And they said" <note>Hebrew: *Vayomru*</note> is used generally to indicate the heart's intent. "And they said" is a command, as we have established in several places. "And they told" is the explanation of the matter in every place. This was to ensnare the heart of the people. In order to hide their intent regarding that Land—which you <note>Moses</note> praised every day—they spoke the truth at first, saying there is nothing like it: **"It surely flows with milk and honey"** <note>Numbers 13:27</note>. Rabbi Yitzhak said: One who wishes to tell a lie should first say a word of truth so that they will believe his lie later. Rabbi Hiyya said: Rather, they said, "You praised it every day and said there is nothing like it, that it flows with milk and honey, and it surpasses everything—but it is not so, for this fruit we brought is just one of the clusters they harvested." They meant to say: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, prepared this for Israel, but all your troubles and labors are only for a single cluster of grapes, and the Land requires more than double the effort." **"Howbeit the people that dwell in the land are fierce..."** <note>Numbers 13:28</note>. This was meant to say: "Behold, these men are warriors who sit outside to guard the paths, and here even the city dwellers are strong giants, and the cities are fortified, such that even if all the kings of the world gathered against them, they could not make a dent in them." Rabbi Yose said: Everything they said was with an evil tongue; they strayed from the truth, as it is written: **"Amalek dwells in the land of the South"** <note>Numbers 13:29</note>. They mentioned this specifically to weaken the heart, saying "the one who attacked us is there." Rabbi Abba said: Certainly they did not stray from what they saw, meaning: "That enemy whom you encountered before is ready and waiting here." And they are located in the South, which is the gateway to enter the Land. Immediately: **"And all the congregation lifted up their voice, and cried; and the people wept that night"** <note>Numbers 14:1</note>. That weeping became a weeping for generations, forever, because of that night. Rabbi Yose said: Woe to the shame of it all, to bring forth an evil report! It struck against everything—against the Land and against the Holy One, Blessed be He. Rabbi Yitzhak said: Against the Land is understood, but against the Holy One, Blessed be He—from where do we know this? He said: It is written, "Howbeit the people are fierce," implying they are stronger than the One above. And then "Amalek dwells in the land of the South"—this caused all that followed, as has been said, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to destroy them from the world, as it is written: **"Therefore He said that He would destroy them, had not Moses His chosen stood before Him in the breach..."** <note>Psalm 106:23</note>.

**"And now, I pray thee, let the power of the Lord be great"** <note>Numbers 14:17</note>. Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Yose said: Fortunate are Israel among the nations of the world, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired them, is called by their name, and is honored through them. The whole world was only created for the sake of Israel, that they might labor in the Torah <note>original: "Oraita"</note>, for the One is bound to the other. Israel below in this world are the foundation of the world and the foundation of all other nations when they do the will of their Master. Come and see: when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created man in the world, He prepared for him a supernal and precious soul, and gave him strength and power in the five-fold nature of the body and soul, which is the strength and brain for the whole body. From there the whole body is nourished, and all the limbs of the body are sustained from there. He took each one and strengthened it...

<meta>This page continues the esoteric commentary on the Torah portion Shelach Lecha. It focuses on the mystical anatomy of the Divine, specifically the "Upper Brain" (Mocha), and how the structure of the earthly Temple mirrors the celestial realms. It concludes with an interpretation of Moses' prayer for the Israelites after the report of the spies.</meta>

->**Shelach Lecha**<-

## Main Text (Zohar)

And it was strengthened through the upper world of life; its brain <note>Aramaic: *Mocha*, referring to the hidden wisdom or the highest level of divine consciousness</note> shines to the left and takes hold of it, but is not strengthened within it in this manner. This is the Holy Seal, and upon this seal, one body is formed. The extremities of the body <note>Aramaic: *Sifei de-Gufa*, the "ends" or limbs of the divine structure</note> were established like the outer pathways, and everything circles around the Thought <note>The divine plan or the Sephirah of Chokhmah</note>. Everything is a body, and all those extremities are sealed from the pure place which is the strength of all, and all things hang upon it. In that place, it is bound and unified with the Supernal Death <note>Likely a reference to the profound concealment or "nullification" in the source</note> that spreads above. So it was when the Holy One created the other world <note>The lower world or the physical realm</note>, a species established to lack all the species of the world. And it is clarified that all who are satisfied with life are lacking compared to Jerusalem. And in Jerusalem, every thought of every righteous person toils, yet it is lacking outside the House <note>The Temple</note>. And the "Son of the House" <note>The inner sanctum</note> is lacking compared to the Courtyards of Israel. These rows surround the Chamber of Hewn Stone <note>Lishkat HaGazit</note>, where the Great Sanhedrin sits. We have learned: there is no sitting in the Courtyard except for the kings of the House of David alone. And the Chamber of Hewn Stone is lacking compared to the House of the Hearth, and it [is lacking] compared to the Altar. The Altar is lacking compared to the Sanctuary <note>Heikhal</note>, and the Sanctuary compared to the Holy of Holies, where the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> dwells, along with the Ark-Cover <note>Kapporet</note> and the Cherubim. The mystery of it all is the purity of all the earth and the world. From here, all those inhabited places are nourished, which are the extremities of the body. All of this is nourished by the Brain of the Head. To show desire for this, He created the Holy of Holies, **"The place, O Lord, which You have made for Your dwelling"** <note>Exodus 15:17</note>. In this manner, it is higher and higher, carved in the mystery of the Supernal King with the precious, hidden Spirit. What is above corresponds to this, and the South lives towards the upper regions, life from life, and life from life. Come and see: just as the Male <note>The masculine aspect of the Divine</note> is lacking compared to many companions opposite him—seventy engraved knots from the side of the lights—and they surround those five that are within them. And they surround the four Chariots, and they surround that Holy City upon which the fourth rests. Come and see: there too are courtyards, and there is no sitting in the courtyard there except for their kings from the House of David alone. There they are settled and sit, and the Great Sanhedrin is found there in the Chamber of Hewn Stone. That Court is over them, serving one after another, and the place is prepared there for the High Holy Ones until it reaches the place where the Holy of Holies stands, in which everything is contained. There it is for every scent, and it is nourished from the Supernal Brain. To show desire for this, it is so. In this manner, it is higher and higher, carved in the mystery of the Supernal King until it is found that everything comes from the Supernal Brain, the most hidden of all. When they are all included, everything is bound one to another. Furthermore, when the Hidden Ancient One <note>Atika Kadisha/Atika Satima, the most primordial manifestation of God</note> is mentioned as Death, Brain, and Palate, to purify as the way of the "Anger of the Lord," He established it, and this is the "Power of the Lord." This is the word that comes from the Holy Ancient One, the most hidden of all hidden things: **"Let the power of my Lord be great"** <note>Numbers 14:17</note>. This means it shall be increased and magnified higher and higher, and shall be blessed and drawn downward, **"just as You have spoken,"** as they have established it: for Kindness <note>Chesed</note>, to distill from here all the generations that depend on the world and the world of worlds. "To say" <note>referring to the word *lemor* in the verse</note> means not in the context of distress; "to say" means in the context of relief and sweetness. **"The Lord is slow to anger, etc."** <note>Numbers 14:18</note>. And he established the words. Rabbi Isaac said: Truth is for the one who strikes... From here, Rabbi Hiyya said: They caused Him to depart from here, for when they mentioned themselves... [The text here becomes highly elliptical and fragmented]. And so he circled to call and to repair, for the staff could not say them... those who saw caused my garment... the companions were awakened. And it was said: The Holy One said, thus I have answered with arguments... and from you all the sweeping... in their place to call from him Kindness. And despite all this, I inclined to draw it from the book to enlarge the host and to bring back. This with that, which they were not able to reveal previously... they went out from the opening and sat at ease under the trees... since they are here and we have seen all this... for the World to Come. And they sat in the Sukkah... and they slept. Meanwhile, the appointee who was there...

<summary>This page explores the mystical correspondence between the architectural layers of the Temple (Courtyards, Altar, Holy of Holies) and the divine emanations of the "Supernal Brain." It concludes by interpreting Moses' intercession for Israel through the lens of drawing divine "Power" and "Kindness" from the most hidden source, the Ancient One.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And afterward, he said to them: "Arise and go out into the **Orchard of Wisdom** <note>Pardes: A term for the deepest, mystical level of Torah study</note>." When they went out, they saw these things and were shaken by them; afterward, they returned and investigated what was said in that verse:

**"In this wilderness they shall be consumed"** <note>Numbers 14:35</note>. This implies that in the "after" of the verse <note>the World to Come</note>, they are not consumed. And this assembly is for all the congregations; this is the assembly of the sons of the prophets. That **Appointed One** <note>Mamuna: A celestial official or angel</note> said to them: "Go out!" As they went out, he said to them directly: "Did you hear what was inside that level?" They said: "We heard a single voice saying: 'He who interrupts shall be interrupted; he who binds shall be bound; he who binds shall be blessed.'" He said to them: "Do you know what this is?" They said: "No." He said to them: "The Appointed One bathes in the river of the city, and like this **Youth** <note>Yenuka: Often a child prodigy or an angel in the form of a child</note> who gathers herbs from the field, your assembly was like him and his throne, and they arrived here. And who is this Youth? He who dug this cave; for once they entered inside the drop, they could not endure it and they died." And this Youth stands every day before **Benala** <note>A mystical name for a high angel or the Angel of the Covenant</note> with the reason that descends from the **Upper Academy**, and he says three things before him. Until then, Benala opened with the secret of hidden wisdom, belonging to all the masters of hidden secrets, which are: **"No eye has seen, O God, besides You"** <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>. This refers to the one who said: "He who interrupts shall be interrupted." He who interrupts the words of Torah for idle words, his life shall be interrupted from this world, and his judgment stands in that world. "He who binds shall be bound"—he who binds himself to the King will have a mark like a brand set upon him, and he shall be bound to the life of the worlds; and "he who binds shall be blessed." He who says "One" <note>referring to the declaration of God's unity in the Shema</note> shall be guarded to the utmost, for even if his baldness is tied <note>a difficult idiom for extreme vulnerability</note>, he will not be harmed by this at all. And whoever does this, his life shall be blessed. Furthermore, he said: "Two do not intend to be joined together, and they are three. And when they are three, they are one." These are not like those two silent ones of the Academy, for they are "The Lord, The Lord" <note>referring to the Divine Names in the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy</note>, long-suffering to be joined together, so that they may be the **Seal of the Signet of Truth**. And when they are joined as one, they are one, like the unity of the **Lord** <note>Adonai</note>. Furthermore, he said: "Two they are, and one is distinguished; every ruler over the world is drawn by the spirit, and it slaughters like the wrath of anger and is sealed." He said to them: "These are the two **Cherubim** about which it was written: **162** <note>The page number/reference</note>." And from the day that Joseph was hidden from his life for prophecy... <margin>Folio 44</margin> and one turned toward the assembly of the vision of Hallel, and **"He rode upon a cherub and flew; He soared on the wings of the wind"** <note>Psalm 18:11</note>. And he hid like the strike of anger upon the worlds; that one who rides upon it, for those who are from this place, his hidden things are wrapped in a voice. "Go out from here, and according to your strength, go out!" That Appointed One gave them a rose for each one, and they went out. When they went out, the mouth of the cave was closed and that river that was flowing from that tree was not seen before them at all, and they entered into another cave. They gazed upon that rose and entered there; they found that river at the mouth of the cave. He said to them: "Draw near and see the truth, friends, for it has not been lowered to be sold from the day it was hidden here, except according to those who entered and reached another Orchard, and that river was with them." When they reached those who were behind you, waiting to return, that river appeared in the **likeness of a man** in precious clothing, crowned like their own, and he sat with them as one. He said to those who dwell here: "Honor to the Master of this Academy who comes here, for from behind you they have come to the garden of the workers of the city here." One of them said: "Is there no property or place?" They said: "Yes." They provided two roses and smelled them; they said: "Dwell, Masters of the Academy, dwell and see the truth." They grasped gifts in this manner; they walked there through thirty laws that they did not know previously, and other secrets of the Torah. And they said regarding the Masters of Scripture, they found that they were saying: **"I said, 'You are godlike beings, and all of you are sons of the Most High'"** <note>Psalm 82:6</note>. "I said" refers to the reason of your initial state, answering to the hearing that "you are godlike beings," etc. But since you have drawn upon yourselves the **Evil Inclination** <note>Yetzer HaRa</note>, **"Indeed, like humans you shall die"** <note>Psalm 82:7</note>. Death was decreed upon Adam to make him fly away, so that that male child might appear, and like that wicked male who provokes and consumes his nickname...

<summary>This page describes a mystical journey through a cave into the "Orchard of Wisdom," where scholars encounter an angelic Appointed One and a miraculous Youth. It explores the spiritual consequences of interrupting Torah study and interprets the fall of man as the result of the Evil Inclination, contrasting human mortality with divine potential.</summary>

# Send For Yourself (Shelach Lecha)

-> **Shelach Lecha** <-

Rabbi Phineas said: Worthy is the portion of the righteous below! It is written: *And your faces, you shall turn* <note>original: "ופניכם אתם יפנו"</note>. He was mentioning the matters of this **Curtain** <term>Parsa: a mystical veil or barrier separating different levels of spiritual reality</term>. The **Evil Inclination** <term>Yetzer ha-Ra: the innate human drive toward self-interest or physical desire</term> is comprised of male and female; it lacks nothing. But the Evil Inclination is always inclined toward deficiency. It does not ascend into the Holy; they "bring up but do not bring down," yet in its removal, they "bring down and do not bring up." And because they call the Curtain "deficiencies," it does not prepare at all. He turned his face from passing the... <unclear>illegible</unclear>... for it is written *they shall turn* and it is not written *you shall turn*. And because of this, the Curtain and the hidden things were completed, for it is the will of the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "קודשא בריך הוא"</note> to sacrifice these curtains from the world above.

That Rabbi Hezekiah said: Truly worthy is our answer and our hope! For permission was given to speak to you, to know up to that place where the Curtain is spread. And how great is the portion of those who stand within a single dwelling! And there were the palaces of the Garden, and their canopies were covered with light on the side. They said these words. He said to them: These are the palaces of the Garden, and they see every day the brightness of the **Torah** <note>original: "אוריתא"</note> as is fitting. And they heard many new words in the Torah, but permission was not given to them to enter its gardens.

Rabbi Illai saw, and he saw peace in the place; they trembled and were amazed. They entered into the Garden, trembling and amazed; thus they all were buried, and immediately they come and are restored as bodies from the holy rivers. And they say to him: "When, when will he pass?" For every day the constellation of those who rest is consumed. At that time, the group that we established as before immediately stands as new bodies, shining like those holy bodies that stood on **Mount Sinai** <note>original: "טורא דסיני"</note>. In the likeness of the world below, they all stood on Mount Sinai as bodies without any filth at all. Once it grew dark for them, the Evil Inclination returned them to the bodies of the swords of the former bodies—alien bodies. This is what is meant by: *And the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb* <note>Exodus 33:6</note>. A voice called out: "Go and gather!" He stands upon his station, and every repair is arranged before him to rebuke. They all flew away and did not stand in their place to return by themselves.

The hopes of the nights of the Garden saw another opening. They entered there and saw a certain Palace... and they sat there. Two "Peaces" were there. They lifted their eyes and saw a single embroidered covering in all kinds of colors and triumphs of the world. And over it was spread a Curtain of hiddenness, a covering that the eyes are not able to look upon. And they were constantly looking and counting within that covering until the place where the Curtain is spread, for they saw nothing from there and beyond.

They bowed their heads and heard a single voice that was saying: "The firmament shall be gathered to him for the deficiencies upon it." The firmament strikes; it is the light of the first one that ascended above. The beloved of all is written concerning it. And they covered the firmament... as before they saw that he who gazes and sees, his eyes shall be dimmed. They saw that he who does not gaze, sees; and the strength of the eighteen was opened when he bows and strikes and is established. A bowed strength—he saw the evil could not prevail over it. They saw two **Cherubim** <note>original: "כרובין"</note> enter into his domain to be made. They saw that the spring was far from his desire. The approach of the firmament... to draw near and to be looked upon.

That voice ceased. They said to you: "Two worlds, there is no support within you." They said, "Yes." They brought out for you two roses; they smelled them. They said: "Wait until you hear two words of ancient mysteries from within the vision of the dwelling, and a herald shall always be within you." They said, "Yes."

Rabbi Shimon said: All these words and all that they saw, they wrote down. And when they reached here, it was written: "The desire of the ways..." and he did not go to... how were those two words? And he said to me: "My son, those two words—one rejoices the worlds and one destroys the worlds, according to the one below." Once they heard these two words, they said to them: "Worthy ones! Go out, go out! You have no further permission to hear." One of them brought out an apple and gave him the wine of his portion; it flashed within it and they went out. And of all they saw, they knew nothing. They went out from the presence... a man came to them and said: "Companions! Rabbi Illai, go to your path! Here is the mouth of the cave, and it is a radiance, and higher matters that you did not know shall be known to you." They went and sought...

<summary>This page describes a mystical journey into the Garden of Eden, where Rabbi Illai and others witness the transformation of souls into "Sinai-like" bodies and encounter the mysterious "Curtain" that veils divine secrets. The narrative emphasizes the danger of gazing at hidden things and the power of specific "ancient words" that can either build or destroy worlds.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Shelach Lecha 163<-

The Academy <note>Aramaic: *Metivta*; refers to the celestial school where souls study the hidden Torah</note> reveals these secrets and words to you. They went out, returned, and searched the cave, arranging these matters from all they had seen and passed through there. Meanwhile, Rabbi Chulafai arrived, shining like a new white fingernail <note>A image of purity and renewed light</note>. He said to them: "Surely permission has been granted to me to speak words to you." They joined together, searched the cave, and sat. They said: "Fortunate are those who see you, for your appearance is like the likeness of the Upper World. Open your eyes; have no fear and do not be dismayed, for the spirit of human beings and the strength of the Lord is upon all that you have seen on this mountain." Afterward, they replied: "If all the mountains are distant, my Academy is for this people in the wilderness." And they merited now what they did not merit in life.

And these heads of the Academy are all associated with the Covenant, Mercy, and the Tribes; their establishers gather toward the mountain of Aaron there, awakening toward him and forming his Academy. They are renewed there like the purity of the **holy dew** that descends upon his head, and the softness of the movement is seen upon him. With him are seen all the holy ones, the beloved of the Holy King, until they investigate here the Academy of Desires. They are hidden in the shadow of every subtle hidden Academy, wrapped like guardians of the Academy of the Priest and the Pious One <note>Aaron</note>.

The Academy of Moses—all of them stand outside and do not enter within, except for Aaron alone. At the time they read in the Book, there are no windows that can perceive Moses, for a source of covering is spread before him, surrounded by clouds of glory. Aaron stands within the Curtain <note>Aramaic: *Pargoda*; the celestial veil separating degrees of holiness</note> below Moses, and the Curtain divides and yet does not divide between them. All the heads of the Academies are outside the fabric of this Curtain. All around on the outside, clouds take hold. According to the holiness of the priesthood of the Torah below, so are those clouds arranged; they are absorbed in the fineness of the covering until the lowest level. That covering protects that source, a window of the path that shines more than all the lights of the world, which are those that Moses bowed before. His coverings are not seen at all, and there are no windows that see them except for that light which emerges from within that source.

After all those clouds, the staff <note>The Staff of Moses</note> is mentioned simply... it spreads to the greats of the Academy. How much is spread in all those windows of opening! When he reaches and places the image and the inkwell, he arranges them with many wonders, sources, and rivers that are required for every single word. All the drops and water of the spirit from below... so at these times, they all ascend constantly with the Academy of Life, and that day is called a Day of Celebration <note>Aramaic: *Hillula*</note>. All the merits are covered, and all the good days come before their Master, trembling and striving to know the Master of the Universe. Fortunate is this generation above all generations of the world! The Academy of Moses goes out and flies toward the Academy of the Firmament, and they appear and spread toward the Upper Academy. Concerning this, it is written:
> *My eyes are upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me; he who walks in the way of the perfect, he shall serve me.*
<note>Psalms 101:6</note>

Rabbi Chulafai opened his discourse and said:
> *You shall be wholehearted with the Lord your God.*
<note>Deuteronomy 18:13</note>

What is the difference between **Simple/Whole** (*Tam*) and **Perfect/Complete** (*Tamim*)? Regarding Abraham it is written:
> *Walk before Me and be perfect (Tamim).*
<note>Genesis 17:1</note>
But regarding Jacob, who was thirteen years older <note>referring to the age of circumcision</note>, it is written of him:
> *And Jacob was a simple (Tam) man.*
<note>Genesis 25:27</note>

See and investigate: he is called "Simple" (*Tam*) because no waste-matter <note>spiritual impurity or the foreskin</note> remained in him at all, for the **uncovering** <note><term>Periah: the second stage of circumcision where the membrane is pulled back to fully reveal the crown</term></note> was in him. Just as he was uncovered and the waste-matter was removed from before him—for the place that is attached to the waste-matter within the place of the uncovering is the "living tooth," the secret of the image of Samael <note>The figure of the Accuser/Satan</note> when he covers Lilith. And that mountain is called the "Simple Mountain," for the softness of the Throne... and the [Evil] Inclination was a simple mountain. Jacob feared it... and on this mountain, he performed the uncovering (*periah*) and removed the filth of the waste-matter like a dog. As we have learned in the Mishnah:
> *And God remembered Rachel.*
<note>Genesis 30:22</note>
It is written as a "visitation" and it is written as a "remembrance." Remembrance is placed in Jacob, who is the "Living Covenant," when Joseph was made. And when he took the mountain... so that Samael would not prevail. And likewise, Joseph is called the son of the mountain.

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Shlach Lacha (Numbers 13:1–15:41). The previous context likely dealt with the spiritual roots of the tribes or the spies; here, the text transitions into a mystical defense of Jacob’s character and the protective power of the blue thread (Techelet) in the ritual fringes (Tzitzit).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Shlach Lacha**<-
<note>Numbers 13:1, "Send for yourself"</note>

Jacob certainly took the birthright, and that [other portion] is the Mountain of Seir <note>The domain of Esau, representing the "Other Side" or impurity</note>. Come and see: Jacob is "simple" <term>Tam: simple, complete, or perfect</term> and a master of the house, while the inhabitant of that mountain [Esau] is a man of divisions. Come and see: just as there is a "Mountain of Assembly" on the side of the "uncircumcision" <note>The Orlah, representing spiritual blockage or evil</note>, when he enters and his days wither, troops emerge from him until he rests between the two companions who surround him—that one who goes to the pit, in houses of the world where humans do not dwell. And all of them emerge from this Mountain of Assembly. And this is in connection with the "evil donkey." Regarding all of them, it is said: *You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together* <note>Deuteronomy 22:10</note>, so that the seed of the supernal faith does not become intermingled. And so it is in the two academies.

But Jacob is "simple" <term>Tam</term>. Like the cloud of that "simple" one. And what is this *Tam* [תם]? It is the letters *Tav* [ת] and *Mem* [ם]. [It represents] the *Vav* [ו] and *Dalet* [ד] <note>The numerical and structural components of the divine name</note>, male and female. They were a totality of male and female as one; then he took all these letters for *Tam*. And he is "Truth" <term>Emet</term>. *You will give truth to Jacob* <note>Micah 7:20</note>, a totality of male and female as one, the peace of all, a connection that is never separated. And all the people go up to call them.

And his hidden levels are called—as it has been said—*Yesh* <term>Existence/Substance</term>, and this is *Tamim* <term>Whole/Perfect</term>. After the Wisdom <term>Chokhmah</term> departs and they enter within to be bound with the Right Hand above: *You shall be whole [Tamim] with the Lord your God* <note>Deuteronomy 18:13</note>. Certainly, just as He is whole, all is one. So too here, you shall be whole with Him—"with Him" certainly. Just as a person makes himself whole, he will take "Simple" [Tam] and "Existence" [Yesh] <note>Combining Tam and Yesh creates the word Tamim</note>.

Come and see as it has been stated: *Yesh* refers to all those holy levels of His that are called so and are never separated from Him. So too here, in this manner, it is to remove from you the "alien levels" and to be bound in the "Whole" [Tamim], to become like the holy levels, his spirit and the holy level [becoming one].

Come and hear: Corresponding to this is the spirit of Jacob. A person needs to be at all times "Simple-Existence" [Tam-Yesh] in this exact manner. Now, he explains that which was explained regarding the repairs of the Holy Moon <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note>: a sapphire stone seen in whiteness, and all colors are included in it and embroidered within it. And it is in that sapphire and whiteness that is truly hidden. And in that sea, within its many depths, a single power emerges and brings forth from it the color of *Techelet* <term>Sky-blue dye</term>. And this color is like a cloak [Tallit], and it is prepared for her to be strengthened in this color. It is not this color alone, for red and purple are within it. Rather, it is a wonder that is outside this acquired color.

In this manner, one would look at all of them in the embroidered sapphire, within and without, and they spread over it the inclusion of the blue [*Techelet*]. Just as there is a woman, there is this *Mezuzah* of *Yesh*, a totality of male and female. And there are those with an "Evil Eye" who look, and when they look, the color of blue is ready for their eyes, and their eyes cannot have power [over the person]. And these [fringes] are prepared for them in all properly embroidered colors, warming all sides forever.

In this manner, a man who wears the *Tzitzit* <term>Ritual Fringes</term> becomes "Whole" [Tamim] every day. "Simple" [Tam]—all his wings are properly prepared. "Sea" [Yam]—in that blue of the star of the depths of the levels of the sea, it strikes him until, when one looks at this man, he cannot look at him with an Evil Eye. And then he is truly *Whole with the Lord his God*. It is a new repair above and he is below. And after she [the Shekhinah] ascends among the upper levels, so too the man later ascends in his prayer into the upper levels. And this is what is meant by: *You shall be whole with the Lord your God*—"with Him" certainly.

Certainly, like a moment... it is repaired above and the man is repaired below. The companions [the circle of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai]—perhaps not those here—are prepared in this way to each be "Whole with the Lord." And regarding this: *In this wilderness they shall be consumed [Yitamu]* <note>Numbers 14:35; a play on the word Tamim/Whole</note>. And if you say it was said for [the generation of the desert], it is certainly so, for they were meant to each be "Whole with the Lord" in the Holy Orchard, the place where the Lord surrounds them, to be covered as one with Him. But now, each one is "consumed" [Tamim] in this wilderness, in a place far from there, so that the holy covering does not look upon them to be with the Lord as is proper. *And there they shall die*—as you have seen them do every day. And all your portion, holy companions who have merited all this, so too the two caves for your length... and you shall not find all this there in the academy of sinners. And give from afar, and this is what is written: *From the staff, turn away greatly from all...*

->**M A N K I N D**<-

->**Shlach Lecha**<-

They are all embroidered with colors that shine like flashing hues, flaming with all kinds of lights that flicker, ascending and descending here and there, glowing, subsiding, and shining. They strike one against the other, and their faces change toward those barriers; they do not shine on all sides. Above, there are those who circle and well up with "water within water" on all sides. These are doubled within those stones, and in their flaming, those "waters" do not know where they go. In the blinking of an eye, they all arise and purify themselves and are seen before the **Holy King** from the side of the South. Like a living skin, a voice is born from the "eye of the brain," and it pours out and provides water to the whole world. Whoever takes from them will be brought to the cities, and a great stranger shall enter them; he shall enter the cities like a day-old infant. Whoever comes from them will become wise and enlightened with wisdom. This "eye" emerges from within a single pearl, standing like a wall to the South. Those waters are swallowed within the field, and from there they go out to the place of the Sanctuary until they enter the Stream of Shittim <note>referring to the waters of purification or the location mentioned in Numbers 25:1</note> and wash away that impurity of the "brain of Shittim."

And these waters are like a skin because of those below. Males were invited there; he asked of the water, but they did not see by the stars in their waters to bow down before the Holy King. Furthermore, they shall be enlightened to know the hidden matters of the Supreme King within this Sanctuary. All thoughts shall be found there, except for the investigation of the precision of the Holy King. A single branch emerges within the center of that "eye." The **Head of the Academy** said: when one approaches that branch within the eye, the branch ascends higher and higher; the closer one gets, the more it ascends, circles, and moves away. For that branch is nothing but like a scent. That branch sustains the worlds; all the colors of the world are in its leaves. Its essence is not known, and they cannot know it. And the Great Master asked to reach that proof, but it was not proven; this is a support for them because of the multitude of his days. Whoever is worthy to know this shall know a single firmament that lives upon that branch, spread out above. That firmament was seen and succeeded by the **Head of the Academy**, and no more.

When a man looks at that firmament from a distance, it resembles blue <note>Techelet</note>; if he draws closer, it resembles red; closer still, it resembles green; closer still, it resembles a white for which there is no whiteness like it in the world. Look and see: it moves and is drawn like this branch, and that firmament makes a movement and is lengthened. Those who see it in the bridal chamber see more than the eyes can normally behold. <meta>This page continues the discussion of spiritual perfection and the covenant from the previous section of Parashat Shelach. It focuses on the mystical definition of being "whole" or "perfect" (Tamim) and transitions into apocalyptic visions regarding the end of days and the resurrection.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

One who guards the holy covenant <note>The sign of circumcision, representing sexual and moral purity</note> is called "perfect" (Tamim) throughout his generations, unlike those who corrupted their ways. Concerning this, it is written: **Noah walked with God** <note>Genesis 6:9</note>. Now, who is able to walk with Him? Rather, anyone who guards the holy covenant, the Divine Presence <note>term: Shekhinah; the feminine indwelling aspect of God</note> joins with him and travels with him. And because of this, it says: **You shall be perfect with the Lord your God** <note>Deuteronomy 18:13</note>. First "you shall be perfect," and afterwards "with the Lord your God." This is because once one guards this covenant, he ensures he will never be separated from Him. As it is written: **Walk before Me and be perfect** <note>Genesis 17:1</note>, a decree that stands forever. "Walk before Me"—from here we learn that a man should not follow behind a woman, but rather she should be before him <note>A traditional modesty law interpreted here mystically</note>, but here it refers to the Crown <note>The Sephirah of Keter</note>. It is written here "before" just as it is written "before Sodom," "from before," and "before you." "And I will send a King before you." Abraham, before he was circumcised, was "before" Him <note>in a state of incompleteness</note>. Therefore it is written: "Be perfect and walk before Me." Rather, "walk before Me" so that they shall not see the Wisdom until you are perfect. And so it is for everyone: once a person is perfect and guards the covenant, immediately he is "before Him" and he is crowned with the Crown. What is written? "For your 'afterward' is good." He was like a Nazirite <note>one consecrated/separated</note> and perfect. But the "uncovering" <note>term: Periah; the second stage of circumcision</note> had not yet been performed in him. And since the uncovering was not in him, what is written? "With God," and not "after God." He was not "before" Him because he was like a Nazirite. He was not "behind" because he had not undergone the uncovering. How then was he "with God"? He was close to Him but could not gaze upon Him. It is written: **And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of cloud and by night in a pillar of ash** <note>Exodus 13:21</note> etc. Once it mentions Israel, here the Holy One, Blessed be He, is like a guide. "For it is better for you to serve the Egyptians." As it were, His mind was changed. It is written: **And the angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud moved from before them** <note>Exodus 14:19</note>. They were all red <note>symbolizing judgment</note>, and regarding this, the Head of the Academy <note>term: Rav Metivta; a celestial teacher in the Zohar's visions</note> concludes that the Crown is everything.

The Head of the Academy said, as he prepared to fly <note>a mystical ascent</note>, that at the end, the "Knotted One" <note>a cryptic reference to a power or ruler</note> will spread the garment of the Kingdom and give it to the Medes. "And your life shall be divided" <note>a play on the word 'Perasin' from Daniel 5:28</note> was heard here. What does this mean? He said to him: It is thus. The Kingdom spreads its garment until it reaches the path. Afterwards, the King of Persia will rise and take many kingdoms, and he will rule over the Holy Land for twelve months. In the end, he will rise and kill many, and then he will fall, and **the holy ones of the Most High shall receive the kingdom** <note>Daniel 7:18</note>. Regarding the "division" (Perasin), the King of Persia is understood here. 

O, holy path! How much joy upon joy there is, like a gushing spring that pours out all kinds of powers. As it is written, the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the Assembly of Israel <note>term: Knesset Yisrael; the spiritual archetype of the Jewish people</note> all stand to level the leaves and the branches, and to gladden their hearts always. There is nothing like it for joy and strength forever. And how many are with Him! All of this is prepared for them in the ground of this Sanctuary; there are many services there. He said to him: By your life, Rabbi! By your life! Blessed is your portion, for all this is like a spring for the open mind. Sometimes they turn to anger because their eyes cannot look upward, for it [the light] goes from that ground of the Sanctuary. 

The Head of the Academy did not explain further, for it is hidden within the Jordan River. I will prove to you what is hidden in the cup of this matter, and you shall know what you shall know. This Jordan flows and extends at a certain time, and it is the Crown that emerges from Eden. Its power is not like this earth below, but rather it contracts. Once it reaches him, it contracts and then expands and enters the Jordan. Once it reaches the ground of the Sanctuary, it becomes entangled there for three days, neither expanding nor flowing elsewhere. 

The Academy told you that when that river returns, it does not turn around there. ## Main Text (Zohar)

And it is always from Wisdom <note>Hebrew: *Chokhmah*, the second of the ten Sefirot or divine emanations</note> that is made to surround the worlds according to their likeness, according to the likeness of that world. > The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life.
<note>Proverbs 11:30</note>

> And Sarai was barren; she had no child.
<note>Genesis 11:30</note>
From this statement, "And Sarai was barren," does a person not know she had no child? Why then does it say "she had no child"? Rather, the **Head of the Academy** said: She did not give birth to a physical child, but she gave birth to all her souls. When there is a clinging of repentance, those two righteous ones <note>Abraham and Sarah</note> give birth to many souls in their hidden treasury all the time they were on earth, just as the righteous do in the Garden of Eden. As it is written:
> And the souls that they had made in Haran.
<note>Genesis 12:5. The Zohar interprets "made" as spiritual procreation through teaching and holiness.</note>
How did they "make" them? Certainly, it was through this mystery.
That man said to him: If so, what is your name? At every New Moon, Sabbath, and festival, the males ascend to appear before the Holy King—the males and not the females, as it is said:
> All your males shall appear.
<note>Exodus 23:17</note>
And when they return, they bring back many new words <note>New insights into the Torah</note> and they repeat them before the **Head of the Academy**. These new words are repeated before the **Head of the Academy** regarding ancient mysteries. Then, "it is well with the righteous and ill with the wicked," for they all ascend in the "scale of power" before they come into the world. According to the tilt of the scale, so they have their portion in this world. The **Head of the Academy** lives and reveals tangibly what he hears above. He reveals a new word and no more. He brings in a light that does not ascend and strikes it; he prepares a "breath" <note>Aramaic: *Nofach*</note> where the light of the soul did not ascend, and he strikes it, and the light of the soul ascends. They desire one another to be illuminated, for there is no breath of the soul's radiance that does not shine until they strike it. Then the radiance of the soul shines and is desired like a breath, and breath is desired as the five breaths. Then its light ascends from within the soul, returning, exalting, and praising. From all his prayers and requests, he blesses his Master. Behold, then everything shines, for there is no breath that the soul cannot illuminate until they strike it. Then it shines and they desire one another. There is one who is not desired in the light, and the light does not ascend in him until they strike him. Then he shines. The "Other Side" <note>Aramaic: *Sitra Achra*, the realm of evil</note> seeks to do the same and strikes at the darkness, but whatever he strikes, "the lamp of the wicked shall be extinguished" by a sword and be scattered to all sides. He cannot illuminate at all. And then it is written: "For what kindness/goodness is after the King?" <note>Cf. Ecclesiastes 2:12</note>. He seeks to resemble Him but cannot. And regarding this: "The Lord tests the righteous, but the wicked and him that loves violence His soul hates" <note>Psalm 11:5</note>. He shines and strengthens in radiance; He tests all.
Then Rabbi Shimon bowed and struck the dust. He said: Word, word! I have pursued your crown from the time I existed, and now the matter is known to me. That breath H-L-Ch-R—how many new words come from the **Head of the Academy**! Happy is the life of one who humbles himself in this world; how much great laughter and elevation he has in that world! And thus the **Head of the Academy** opened: One whose "crowding" <note>suffering or humility</note> is small, his life is great; and one whose "crowding" is great, his life is small, as it is written: "And Korah lived..."

## Main Text (Zohar)

And so it is, when a person [raises] a voice, those [above] are awakened toward that voice. Solomon saw and feared to teach this hidden matter. Furthermore, King Solomon's wisdom did not know how to teach this. King Solomon saw it and knew it, but not in its entirety. Alas for what he did not know—what benefit is in that voice and how it dwells [within]. But the **Head of the Academy** <term>Rav Metivta: The celestial dean of the heavenly study hall</term> said this: King Solomon did not know this fine detail, for that voice is comprised of **spirit and soul** <note>original: *rucha ve-nafsha*</note> gathered from the bones, from the labor of the flesh, and from the foolishness of the body, and each one separates from the other. And when it reaches the end of the place where it dwells, it is found like death. All those sorcerers and diviners know words like their own whispers and they bow to the ground. They hear this voice where the spirit, soul, and the "vapor of the bones" <note>The residual life force remaining in the skeletal remains</note> join together, and they make known the teaching. And this is for them another [path].

Because of this, Solomon pursued the knowledge of what is made of that voice, but he did not know. And the whole portion is entirely truth: when a person awakens a voice, things join together and that voice is awakened, and it has no further permission—except like the likeness of the voice that the person awakened and no more. And if a person takes hold of his acquisition, it is like a testimony, but only for the blowing of the voice, because it cannot endure. What is the reason? Because when it first goes out, it wraps from one end of the world to the other end of the world, and it rests there; it cannot prolong the voice because it has no place to turn there as it did at first. Rabbi [Shimon] rejoiced and said: "If we only merited to hear this one word, it would be enough for me to be happy that we merited to hear words of truth regarding **that world** <note>The Afterlife/Heavenly Realm</note>." He said to him: "O holy pious one, if you knew the joy that was in that world before the Head of the Academy, you would strengthen your joy even more." He asked him: "What joy was there? Tell me all that you have."

The **Head of the Academy** opened with the verse: <note>Genesis 46:4</note>
> "And Joseph shall place his hand upon your eyes."

They said in wonder: regarding the eyes at the time of death, because the eyes contain the colors of **this world**. And the vision of this world, in everything that is closed off from it, takes hold of the **other world**. [When] the vision of this world is closed, one is strengthened by it and prepared by it. The vision of the eyes has no more vision in this world from that point onward. Solomon said this and brought down the initial restoration, and their soul is greater than the holy angels. He said to him: "Joseph shall place his hand" more than all the other sons. And if you wonder about the news and his eyes toward him, "And Joseph" refers to both, and "shall place his hand" because of his love for him. And because of this, we do not stand as a refuge like the power of this world, for this is a nullification for him. What is the meaning of closing the eyes of the living? It is so that your vision in this world is captured. Behold, here your vision is in its place, and from now on, another vision will be prepared for you at the end of the world. 

Rabbi Shimon said: "Take these for death; what benefit is there in these words for one who is dry and sick? Why is it necessary to open his eyes? Because the delight that is prepared for them is to be found in the vision of this world as it was at first." He said to him: "O holy pious one, certainly if all vision of this world is not closed from him and entirely destroyed from him, he cannot grasp the vision and the portion of **that world**." This world is the opposite of that world. Therefore, the support that was marked there responds thus: like a wall of a storm, this is the making of this world, for everything is made as it was at first, rising and nullifying it, making it like this world.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the nature of the soul's transition from the physical body to the spiritual "Celestial Garment" (Haluka de-Rabbanan). It connects the biblical figures of Esther, Mordechai, and Joshua the High Priest to the esoteric process of shedding "filthy garments" (the physical/sinful shell) to don garments of light.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Send For Yourself**<-
<note>original: "Shelach Lecha" — the title of the Torah portion in Numbers 13-15</note>

**He opened** by saying: First, all filth must pass away from him, and afterward he is made like this forgiveness <note>or "hollow space"</note>, and from here the body is made into a new creation. So it is here, said Rabbi Shimon: I certainly know that the Kingdom <note>the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> is there in a precious garment of the body, which is holy. And this is the sign: just as it is here, so it is there, surrounding and surrounding. When you see this surrounding the body, it is in the same manner that they stand in that world <note>the afterlife/spiritual realm</note>. He said to him: This matter was shown before the Head of the Academy <note>the celestial teacher</note>; two worlds were sweetened as one, which bore light upon laughter—a joy that has never been seen by the eye—and they brought this before the Head of the Academy. And he said: Behold, it was so in this world. From where do we know this? As it is written: *And it came to pass on the third day, that Esther clothed herself in royalty* <note>Esther 5:1</note>. She clothed herself in the very image of that world. "Royalty" <note>Malchut</note> here refers to the Holy Spirit, for it is written "Kingdom of Heaven." The spirit of impurity is the "other spirit" of this world, but Esther clothed herself in the Holy Spirit. And when she came before the King to plead, and he saw that garment of the divine image, his ears began to burn <note>with desire or awe</note>, and her soul nearly flew from her at his step. Mordechai was also thus, as it is written: *And Mordechai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel* <note>Esther 8:15</note>. "Royal apparel" certainly means the image of that world. And concerning this it is written: *For the fear of Mordechai fell upon them* <note>Esther 9:3</note>—the fear of Mordechai, and not the fear of Ahasuerus. Rabbi Shimon said: How many are these rectifications! Fortunate is the portion of the righteous, for they are certainly known in that world to be clothed in a garment of glory, a royal garment; and so it truly is. Come and see: regarding the Garden of Eden, it is written that the Holy Spirit hovers there, and the righteous are clothed in it just as they were in this world. And afterward, the Holy Spirit flies over the head of each and every one, and a crown is crowned upon them. And so it was for Mordechai, as it is written "in royal apparel"—the image of that world—and then "with a great crown of gold." This is the crown that circles the heads of the righteous in that world. When Israel received the Torah, they were in this state, until they sinned, as it is written of them: *And the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb* <note>Exodus 33:6</note>. They were stripped of that garment. And so it is written regarding Joshua the High Priest: *Take away the filthy garments from him*, and it is written: *And they clothed him with garments* <note>Zechariah 3:4</note>. These are the garments of that world, and from here we see they are holy. And from here we learn that as long as the body of this world remains in its grave, the soul is not clothed in the garment of that world; for it is written, *Take away the filthy garments from him* first, and afterward, *And they clothed him with garments, and the angel of the Lord stood by.* What is the meaning of "stood by"? This is the crown, which is called "the angel of the Lord," which stands over the heads of the righteous; this is the "standing." It stands over the head above, after they are clothed in this garment of glory. Two bodies cannot exist as one; as long as this [physical] one exists, the spirit cannot receive the other. When this one is removed, the other enters immediately. This one goes out and that one enters, just like the Good Inclination and the Evil Inclination. In this world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not desire that both should stand as one. He said to him: I am astonished at what is written: *And the Accuser <note>Satan</note> stood at his right hand to accuse him* <note>Zechariah 3:1</note>. Did the world act thus toward Joshua son of Jehozadak? O, Living Holy Beloved! How many hidden and sealed things are in these words! The companions who are buried <note>in study</note> know these things, but the rest of the world cannot know these secrets. When a person is in that world, what benefit does the Accuser have in accusing him? Is it not enough that he took his soul from him and killed him? He said to him: O, Holy Beloved, fortunate is your portion! Come and see: the Accuser's merit <note>or opportunity</note> was only to prevent that righteous man from being clothed in the garment of holy power. Once the Accuser sees that the prepared garment is pushed away and not considered for him, he accuses him. Why? Because once he is clothed in that precious garment—the garment of the Divine Image—the work of the Accuser is nullified and removed from the world, and this does not please the Accuser. Furthermore, as long as he is not clothed, the spirit of that body wanders in its image and the Accuser prosecutes it. But once he is clothed in this...
