## Main Text (Zohar)

By that merit, this precious [soul] causes the branch of weak fire and its body to be nullified, and it has no remembrance in the Holy Realm forever. And if you say that they visit the gravesites in spirit every night, it is not for the sake of the body, but like a naked brain <note>original: "mocha," referring to the essence or marrow</note> it wanders as long as the flesh remains in corruption, and the spirit watches over it, and in the pit it watches over the body. But now, as in the likeness of this living soul that is found, and is found with its ornaments, the bones are written in the spirit every night; the deposit of the spirit is not to bow down except over the flesh. If it is diminished or thin, come and see a hidden matter: just as the body of a human being is formed, so is the actual spirit of the Holy One, blessed be He—the soul from within the power of life.

Once the Holy Spirit gives the word, immediately its "chariots" <note>spiritual vehicles or structures</note> and their powers go to the bones and beautify them all from their connection, arranging them one upon the other. The "Other Side" <note>the realm of impurity or evil</note> gives the flesh and hides it, for the spirit comes to the flesh, but not from this side of its chariots. And so all those sinews and veins are found to be the blood for the side after these, and such are their powers—the blood and its strength. And these are the skin that is drawn over everything in their likeness. Afterward, the name and the vein connect as one and give feeling, water, whiteness, and dust to be placed upon these and to cover them all.

Afterward, each one takes the portion it gave, and the Holy Spirit and its chariots are nullified—the Holy Spirit remains and the soul ascends. The chariots of the Holy Spirit cause the bones to endure for them, and upon reaching the body, their bones [endure], and because of this it is written:
> **"And He shall invigorate your bones"** <note>Isaiah 58:11</note>
But regarding the flesh, it is not written so. As long as the flesh of the "Other Side" exists in its standing, it seeks to cause harm. When the flesh is subdued, it has no permission to gaze, for it has nothing to use, until it is written:
> **"And all his flesh is consumed from sight, and his bones that were not seen stick out"** <note>Job 33:21, with slight variation</note>
From before, it is seen that they erred in standing to cause harm, but they cannot, since "all his flesh is consumed and his bones that were not seen stick out." Do not appear to draw near to him, for his portion is like that; rather, each and every kingdom shall not seek them, nor shall it serve in their likeness. After the flesh is mourned/decayed, it will not seek judgment, nor will it go to cause harm, and it will not remind the person before the King of the Universe.

Rabbi Simeon said: Now I know these matters in their proper arrangement. And life and vitality were meant to be observed. Rabbi Simeon moved from his place and prepared himself: "He who seeks to know the matters of the end will surely be enlightened by these words." Come and see, I know that the house is covered <note>perhaps referring to hidden wisdom</note> so that you did not know all of them, but the companions know according to their light understanding. Rabbi [Simeon] said: Knowledge comes in six levels, and each one takes its portion of what was left. And all this precious matter—do not be astonished by it, for I know that you did not ask about your household, but about what is written:
> **"Behold, the Lord rides upon a swift cloud"** <note>Isaiah 19:1</note>
And what is a "swift cloud"? The investigators of knowledge [understand] from that bride and her spirit, and for her there stands power from their heat, in the likeness of the Supernal Knowledge. But the investigators of the "voice" <note>or "light"</note>—I know what your question is. He said: My workers, move yourselves and tie your knots, for the path is ready to be inherited, just as the end passes over the face of the breadth of the house.

In the hall of the mountain, toward the skin, there are **twelve gates** according to the dwellings of the Tribes of Israel. On one gate it is written **Reuben**, and on another gate it is written **Simeon**, and so all the Tribes of Israel are inscribed upon those gates as they ascend to appear before the Master of the Universe. Those who enter through the gate of Reuben are shown mercy, or they cover the spirit, and the gates are seen by them, and they do not escape outside. And so all of them—the gates will not receive anyone except one who is from that tribe which is stamped therein. And in that, they shall be engraved and recognized, each and every one. Three hundred and sixty-five columns for the crown from above are on every side; there are four sides. All those columns are called "Living Columns," because the light does not stand for them [unless] they are recognized.

->**Shelach Lecha**<-

Thus, there is one **Crown** <note>Keter: the highest emanation of the Divine</note>. And all of them, the windows, ascend and these descend. Those that ascend are like a specific pattern—what is this pattern? They triumph over the mountain of destruction. And is there an **Ancient** <note>Atik: referring to the highest, most hidden aspect of God</note> Mountain? Rather, it is a mountain that is above, where the sparks lick but cannot find it, because it is **Holy**.
What is the reason it is **Holy**? He is <term>Old</term> <note>Zaken: here implying the "Ancient of Days"</note> and is included and never weakened.

What is "pleasure" <note>original: "Ednah"</note>? The drawing down from Eden, the <term>Tree of Life</term> <note>Etz Chaim</note>. And because it is drawn upon her from the side of the Female, it is written "Ednah" with a *He* <note>the feminine suffix</note>, and therefore it is written "it was" <note>feminine form</note> and not "he was." "And my lord is old"—and even though he is old, is he not fit to father children? > And my lord is old <note>Genesis 18:12</note>
It is not so, but rather "advanced in days." In those supernal days that rejoice in peace like a guardian.

Above, in every single pillar, there are three boundaries where three colors strike: **red**, **green**, and **white**. Like every color, these are **angels** below, shining and gazing at the **green**, which is [the central line], and they are never covered, and there is no one who can stand over them.

When those types of nourishment and those precious stones go out behind the **wheels**, a voice is heard saying: "I have acted and painted, and Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains, O Lord." Around those pillars there are coverings, the work of a designer. They are like **red**, tied in a knot of holiness to every side, and it reaches to the "brain" of all, and it was...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Shelach Lecha**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion: "Send for yourself"</note>

The end of the path... and he robs that which has ascended from the worlds. Because they sought to judge his judgment below, the sin increased, which brought shame to the **Holy Throne** <note>original: "Karsaya Kadisha"</note> through its changes and thorns. He did not care to go to another to rectify his learning, and he filled his knowledge toward the Throne. It is a single suppression that does not spread or go outside; it takes within the Great Sea that comes and runs within it, a sickle in the moisture of the sea. This is symbolized by <note>Psalm 104:26</note> *There is the sea, great and wide... there is Leviathan, whom You formed to sport in it.* 

And like the protection of the basket above is the Living Creature <note>Chayah</note> of the two Cherubim, the work of the embroidery of the Holy King. The higher and lower beings cannot endure them. Beneath them, all of Israel is destined to stand, so that they do not go out from under their wings to the outside. Happy are all those who enter beneath their wings! Three thousand revolving wheels of <term>Metatron</term> <note>The supreme angel and "Prince of the Presence" in Jewish mysticism</note> who is chosen by <term>Kanfaniel</term> <note>An angelic name, likely meaning "Wing of God"</note> (<note>Another version: "Kavisokhas"</note>) as is fitting. 

The Head of the Academy—who can describe the power and glory of that honor? Who can speak your words, words that are renewed every day before the Head of the Academy? By the life of Rabbi Hiyya! From the power of the male spirits that ascend above, they are covered in this [manner], and from the power of the silver, they are all gathered into the Palace where it is written <term>this is the dragon's bread</term>. How many ancient words and deaths go out and ascend in them, and a secret is with them inside the <term>Palace of Sarah</term> <note>Heikhala d'Sarah - a heavenly abode for the souls of righteous women</note>. They rejoice in many new and ancient words, and deaths go out and a secret is with them, and they ascend into the <term>Palace of Jochebed</term> <note>Heikhala d'Yochebed - the mother of Moses</note>. So it is in all those Palaces. 

Now, Rabbi Hiyya, here is a secret for you: Come and see, support upon support, like a wind that goes out to gather the strangers and the hidden ones. All those who are "children of faith" ascend in judgment; they spread out as males and hidden ones and ascend. All those nursing infants are connected above within the Academy of the Firmament. They rejoice with great joy and ascend, and there is joy upon joy and gladness until the opening of their King and Creator. He says to them many new and ancient words, and they all inherit a joy like no other joy. Afterward, they enter through many curtains and many hidden palaces there, which shine with the "Anger of the Lord" <note>likely a mystical name for a specific light</note> within the Palace of Love. This is what is written in <note>Psalm 27:4</note> **"and to visit in His Palace."** Afterward, they fly and spark upward, and those fly downward and return to their places, dressing themselves as they were at first. Happy is your nation for all the good they await in that world!

<term>Rabbi Shimon</term> <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the central figure of the Zohar</note> said: "How sweet are the words I have heard! Happy is my lot that I have merited to hear all this!" All that day... thus they said to him: "Rabbi, three times we have permission to come to you, and after one day, your joy and love are drawn from your side." 

It is hidden and searched for beneath the place of the investigation of the mound of Hadnus until midnight. After midnight, the pillar of Isaac ascends and goes out and flies like this **Rooster** <note>original: "Tarnagola" - a symbol of the angel Gabriel or the awakening of the soul</note> that investigates the Man. The "Man" is a nickname for his Master over him. When this Holy Man strikes it, he opens voices, and all of them are according to your measure. At the hour when he calls, all the roosters of this world call out. A flame goes out from him and reaches them beneath their wings, and they call out to him. 

What does he call? In the first hour, he calls and says: <note>Psalm 29:4</note> **"The voice of the Lord is in power; the voice of the Lord is in majesty."** In the second hour, he calls and says: <note>Psalm 29:9</note> **"The voice of the Lord makes the hinds to calve,"** etc. In the third hour, he calls and says: "The voice of the Lord makes the nights to calve..." at the hour...

And this is the **celestial rooster** <note>A mystical being that awakens the world and the angels to praise God</note> that calls out and does not rest. Afterward, it calls as at the beginning and strikes, calling out all the deeds of the children of the world, because they are the <unclear>laborers</unclear> of the maidservant <note>original: "מחריה דאמתא"</note>. And the scribe stands in his <unclear>garments</unclear> and writes all the deeds of the children of the world every single day. And the crown <note>Keter</note> that calls all these calls, calls out everything that was written during the day.

And his feet are filled; we find that they are two levels: one that stands in the middle which is called "Great," and one that stands <unclear>at the edge</unclear> which is called "Small," which delay him, and he speaks, setting the world ablaze with his flames. And what do they do? As soon as the <unclear>atonement</unclear> rises and the flight of the basin emerges from the crown of the south, then they all join together and are made into two legs, two hooves like a calf, to fulfill that which is written: *And the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot* <note>Ezekiel 1:7</note>.

And you already know this spirit <unclear>is a branch of fire</unclear>. Within this <unclear>dwelling</unclear> there are three hundred and sixty-five palaces, corresponding to the number of days in the year, and at every single entrance it is written: *May there be peace within your walls and serenity within your palaces* <note>Psalms 122:7</note>. One does not know who strikes at the mouth of those who carry, but they are all warmed by the work of the basin—seven orders of **pearls** that are warmed, all of them in each and every one.

O holy pious one! How much does the Head of the Academy praise this palace! <unclear>It is for him</unclear> because of the four faces in the four sides of the world. The entire palace of the side of <unclear>bitterness</unclear>, its white stones are more numerous than all of them. <meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Shlach Lecha, focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the "Other Side" (Sitra Achra) and the testing of the soul. ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Send For Yourself (Shlach Lecha)**<-

In the contemplation of the vision, like a serpent, there is no measure to the works in the scroll within that are unknown in their timing. From it emerges a vein, and all that lives within it is like a cherub of brilliance; they emerge until the head of the firmament in many colors and coverings. From here, anger and violence pass through, and the needle and physical rings create a vision in this skin. The "Samekh" <note>The letter Samekh, often associated with the Primordial Serpent or Samael</note> further spreads its hands in bitterness and its vision, and afterwards "consumes his own flesh" <note>Ecclesiastes 4:5</note> by his own will. For he has no permission to rule over any other matter except for what is prepared for him through all the sins, transgressions, and toil [of man]. And afterwards, he has no permission except over his own; afterwards, there is dancing and joy in the fool without any knowledge at all, and he sees all the profit and vision afterward. And in secret, he has no permission—the bitterness from above and below—and all who sin in distress, their slaughterers consume them. They do not give strength through good deeds for them to emerge from his mouth, and they even fall from their crowns. Their voice is like the sound of grinding before the Holy King, for He is merciful and gracious. Woe to his own, the holy spirit; and over the holy soul, they are not able to rule at all. And over all, they shall be strengthened. And all that he sinned, that "Evil Destruction" <note>A name for a destructive demonic force</note> seeks to rule over the holy spirit, but afterwards he is unable, and he slips away and consumes his own crown. What profit does he have? And furthermore, the vision of their fall is entirely like a powerful nakedness, and there is no covering for the worlds, and they shall be revived.

Come and see, come and see for yourself, O King! Lest you say that he is holy to lick the dust like a serpent <note>original: "למלחך המוא כל קטיל כנו נטש"</note>. Rather, it is because he sees the will of his Master in this; he shows himself in his voice to do the will of the Holy One, Blessed Be He, like a hired harlot <note>This refers to the famous Zoharic parable where the King (God) hires a harlot (the Sitra Achra) to test the prince's (man's) loyalty</note>. She does not drip [honey] nor is she taken; she gazes and dances in joy before him. He is the living, holy, pious one, and he pushes her away. So it is with the sinner before the King, for it is the King's will [to test him]. All his intention in the lamentation of weeping is to dance and to be purified from being seduced. The Living God <note>El Chai</note> is thus for the low and the sinner... all because he is an "Old and Foolish King" <note>A traditional term for the Evil Inclination/Yetzer Hara</note> and he sins to rule over the spirit and all its offspring. Just as he is, so he is in the end—he rules over nothing but his own, his own flesh. And concerning this it is written: "And dust shall be the serpent’s food" <margin>Isaiah 65:25</margin>.

Come and see, and seek the Lord of the world. Waters rise from within the snow of the depths and seek to dig into the world. The vision of the wicked is greater than any sin in the world. And from the strength of their dwelling, they gather words from the sea of the open-eyed. And to the three, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, likened them: one is a covering of smoke from his pillar. And see, the world cannot stand even for a single moment. Those tears, when they double within the sea, a voice is heard between the sea and the Cave of Machpelah <note>The burial place of the Patriarchs in Hebron</note>. And the sound of their moaning is heard there. When they enter the sea, they awaken the first ones, and they stood and thought the Holy One, Blessed Be He, wished to overturn the world. A voice went out and said to them: "Do not fear, holy beloved ones! For your sake, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, remembers your children and He shall come to redeem them, though they are below."

He overturned his house; all of them ascend and are healed, the sicknesses in the scroll, and they are joined in the fire of the Holy Staff. Once they are seen below in this fire, the sicknesses are hidden and emerge behind you. And so all the sicknesses are hidden, and the sicknesses go out, all of them into the blue, to the vision of the capitals. Furthermore, they fly three times in the time of youth and go outside. And there stands a support like a sword below, calling out for an hour and a half. Afterwards, this is hidden; immediately there emerges from within the white of his covering the **Name of Twelve** [letters] below; it flies and hangs in the white for one hour and no more. Afterwards, this is hidden, and immediately fire emerges below, behind the **Name of Thirty** [letters] below. And they hang in the white for one hour, for him and his children. And immediately there emerges below a moisture for one [hour], the **Name of Twenty-Eight** [letters] below. They are all crowned with their crowns and stand for an hour and a half, for him and his children. And immediately there emerges, hanging in the white, the **Name of Crowns and Five** below in their fires, and they stood for an hour and three moments. There emerges below the **Name of Forty-Two** [letters] below. For the world it stands. How many pass below? All of them are not silenced.

# Parashat Shlach Lecha (Send For Yourself)

## Main Text (Zohar)

They transform for all the worlds, gathering outside, ascending and descending; none can endure them except for a great and pious man. This remains hidden after it stands for two hours, crowns, and two moments. At that hour, an engraving of a thick cloud and a voice emerges, standing and hanging in the air for an hour and a half. All these names do not emerge or appear except for once a day. For the <term>Living Creatures</term> <note>original: *Chayot* - the angelic beings described in Ezekiel's vision</note> pass through their house; you shall see them flying in the air and striking one against the other three times a day. When the poor of their house grind, these fly from here and go from there, and they all strike together. When you see there the <term>Head of the Academy</term> <note>original: *Rav Metivta* - the celestial dean of the heavenly study hall</note> surrounding, he reaches forward like a flash of fire; the house is below them, just as the dance of all the Living Creatures. From that place they emerge, and these are the **S** <note>The letter Samekh, often representing support or a specific mystical cycle</note>.

For every Sabbath Eve, when they sanctify the day and the surrounding area below to the lowest depths, and provide for the world, the holy thrones are prepared. Who has seen the holiness like the three hundred and ninety firmaments? How many appointees, how many rulers gather to their places! As soon as Israel below sanctifies the day, and the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> <note>The standard Rabbinic title for God</note> is awakened, then the <term>Tree of Life</term> <note>The central sefirah of Tiferet, the source of vitality</note> strikes its leaves. A spirit of serenity rests upon them, and those branches of the Tree sway, ascending scents to the <term>World to Come</term>. That Tree of Life awakens and brings forth souls, spreading them over the world.

And through all this, souls emerge and higher souls ascend; these awaken and those enter, these emerge and those enter, and the Tree of Life is in joy. And then all of Israel are crowned with the crowns of those holy souls, all of them in joy and gladness. Every Sabbath they have that joy, and it is like a day of delight for the righteous in the assembly, where they all ascend and delight in the <term>Supreme Delight</term> of the World to Come.

As soon as the Sabbath departs, all those souls fly off and ascend. Come and see: when the Sabbath enters, souls open to their Master over the holy people, and souls ascend on high. When the Sabbath departs, the souls ascend—those that surrounded Israel—and the souls descend, and the souls of the righteous merit this. Once all the souls that surrounded Israel ascend, they stand in their image before the Holy King. The Holy One, Blessed Be He, asks each and every one: "What new insight did you have in that world in joy?" And everyone who has a new insight of the Torah says it before Him. How much holiness does the Holy One, Blessed Be He, perform, as it were, for His service! And He says: "Hear the new insight of the Torah said by the soul of so-and-so!" <note>original: *Ploni* - a placeholder for a specific person's name</note> And they all establish that word in the two Academies—the one below and the Holy One, Blessed Be He, above seals that word.

Come and see: when a word of new insight in the Torah is created, and the soul that was renewed on the Sabbath occupies itself with those new words and they ascend on high, all the heavenly service-beings receive that word. Then the <term>Holy Living Creatures</term> <note>original: *Chayot ha-Kodesh*</note> beat their wings and clothe themselves in those wings. And when the Holy One, Blessed Be He, asks them and they do not know and are silent, then regarding the Holy Living Creatures, what is written? -> "When they stood, they let down their wings" <- <note>Ezekiel 1:24</note> just as it says, -> "For they stood, they did not [move]" <- <note>Ezekiel 1:25</note> and as it says, -> "And all the people stood" <- <note>Nehemiah 8:5</note>. And if you say "standing" implies silence, it is because when everything is at the ends, they move clearly to every side. The reed, the tongue, the hidden, the ceiled, the guarded. **S** Its standing is like their standing without movement. And regarding this, "standing" was explained by <term>Rav Hamnuna the Elder</term> <note>A prominent sage frequently cited in the Zohar for deep mystical secrets</note>.

He opened and said: -> "May He send your help from the Sanctuary..." <- <note>Psalms 20:3</note> "From the Sanctuary" refers to the holiness of His hands. **S** For He does everything according to the secret. All your desires, all that you find as another word. This is the basket of His hands in duality. Jacob and Isaac... this is the Grace After Meals with a summons. And if you do so, "May He grant you according to your heart and fulfill all your counsel," and in the merit of this Sanctuary, a great holiness. And through this word, they are crowned in the image in the Garden of Eden, from one booth to another booth. He opened and said: "Upon a high mountain..."

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the portion of Shelach Lecha. It focuses on the eschatological return of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) to Zion and the specific rewards prepared for those who remained faithful through the hardships of exile.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Shelach Lecha**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion: "Send for yourself" (Numbers 13:1)</note>

...from the Crown of Zion and so on, upon a despised and narrow mountain where a place is destined to be prepared. And behold, they have established that the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence, personified as feminine</note> shall return there and bring good tidings to the world, to all those living beings behind Zion. This is not a lowly thing below, for it is written: "All who see her shall say she reaches from the heavens." And to the sparks she shall go out and bring tidings, and it shall be like a flowing stream from behind Zion. A voice shall be heard in the world, and two kings shall be awakened in the world to wage war, and the Holy Name shall go out upon the world. What tidings shall she bring? She shall say: *Behold, the Lord God will come with might, and His arm shall rule for Him; behold, His reward is with Him, and His work before Him.* <note>Isaiah 40:10</note>

"Behold, His reward is with Him"—for the Holy One, Blessed be He, proclaims to all the **Heavenly Retinue** <note>The assembly of angels and celestial powers</note> and says to them: "Gather together and see! One who surrendered his soul for the **Sanctification of My Name** <note>Kiddush Hashem; martyrdom or extreme devotion</note>, what is his reward?" And they shall say: "Such and such." "One who suffered many insults and blasphemies every day for My sake, what is his reward?" They shall say: "Such and such." "One who diminished himself <note>through fasting or humility</note> every day for My sake, what is his reward?" And they shall say: "Such and such."

"Behold, His reward is with Him, and His work before Him." What is "His work" (*pe’ulato*)? It is as it is written: *Oh, how great is Your goodness, which You have laid up for those who fear You; which You have **worked** for those who trust in You...* <note>Psalms 31:20</note>. This is "My work" regarding the children of men. What is it? It is against the nations of the world who distressed their souls. What does it mean they "distressed their souls"? Can anyone rob or take from His hand what He desires to give? Rather, go and see the works of Mercy that the Holy One, Blessed be He, performs. Just as there was distress, so He gives healing. With the very "garment" <note>the physical body or circumstance</note> that was struck, He gives healing.

All the judgments and harsh decrees and the "house of prisoners" shall be turned to good. All the goodness that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to give to Israel in the time to come—the Holy One, Blessed be He, calls to the North and says to it: "Give up all the goodness and every good treasure to the assemblies who surrendered many purses <note>wealth</note> in this world for the Sanctification of My Name. Give the good treasures that belong to them." This is what is written: *I will say to the north, "Give them up!" and to the south, "Do not hold them back!"* <note>Isaiah 43:6</note>. All blessings come from the side of the South, and all the world's goodness issues from the South.

Behold, the Holy One, Blessed be He, shall awaken to remember her <note>Zion/the Shekhinah</note> and shall say: "The time has arrived to redeem My children and to give them a good reward for all they suffered in exile." And who remembers her? The "Firstborn" <note>Israel</note>, as it is written: *But Zion said, "The Lord has forsaken me, and my Lord has forgotten me."* <note>Isaiah 49:14</note>. It is like one who has something good in his eyes, and it seems as if it burns in his mind even more. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to her: "I know them all, and all that you have said." To the North He says: "Do not hold back!" Do not withhold their goodness; do not withhold their good reward. Just as they walked in their sorrows, so shall they walk in their canopies.

And this is the King who comes from the Crown, and from the strength of the dwelling of the *Shekhinah*. She shall ascend upon that high mountain and bring tidings to them. Immediately she shall go to Jerusalem and say to her: "Enter into them." She shall be established as at first. From there she shall not depart until the Holy One, Blessed be He, redeems the assembly. Then Zion shall be comforted as in the beginning, and they shall rejoice. *Cry out and shout, O inhabitant of Zion, for great is the Holy One of Israel in your midst!* <note>Isaiah 12:6</note>. What is "Great in your midst"? This is the Holy One, Blessed be He; see and behold, He has raised her from the dust of Zion, and says to her: *Shake yourself from the dust; arise, sit down, O Jerusalem!* <note>Isaiah 52:2</note>.

And when this happens, there is joy upon joy for the **Righteous** in the **Garden of Eden**. For this reason, merit comes to those souls who stand before the King regarding the "New Insights of the Torah" <note>Chiddushim; original mystical interpretations</note> of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and all His retinue. All those souls of the righteous who were in the Garden of Eden are all sustained by that word. We have heard this in the Holy Assembly...

## Main Text (Zohar)

A holiness that conceals honor upon honor and a crown upon a crown, crowning the **Wisdom** <note>Hebrew: Chokhmah; the second Sephirah or emanation of Divine intellect</note> of that person. ->**The Faithful Shepherd**<-
<note>The "Ra'aya Meheimna" is a distinct layer of the Zohar where the soul of Moses, the "Faithful Shepherd," teaches the mystical secrets of the commandments.</note>

**The first** of your dough you shall set aside as a gift, a cake (*Challah*)... <note>Numbers 15:20</note> This commandment is to separate the *Challah* offering for the Priest. *Challah* is found to be the numerical value of 43 <note>original: ע"ן - likely a scribal variant or shorthand for the calculation</note> and the holiness of **Understanding** <note>Hebrew: Binah</note> is one in a hundred, and there is an exemption of one in fifty for the Levite... the *Challah* is the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note>. In your houses, for these are their kings, there they wait. And in the *Challah* to spread there, the *Shekhinah* is there... it is written, "And Moses *besought* (Vayechal) the Lord" <note>Exodus 32:11; a wordplay on Challah</note>... to repair the 248 commandments... so that the completely wicked shall have merit to be vindicated... and all this is for my end. Thus far.

---

**And the Lord** spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them that they shall make for themselves fringes (*Tzitzit*) on the corners of their garments throughout their generations... <note>Numbers 15:37-38</note> Rabbi Hezekiah opened the discussion: "And he showed me Joshua the High Priest..." <note>Zechariah 3:1</note> How meritorious are Israel, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires their honor above all the inhabitants of the world, and gave them a holy portion, and gave them faithful vessels that remind them of the Torah in the path of truth.

Come and see: every time the Holy One, Blessed be He, sees Israel, they are all revealed before Him like high, holy levels, and the radiance of the King's holy honor rests upon them. No harm approaches them, just as one who is closer to the King than all others—his portion is greater than all the inhabitants of the world. Of him it is written: "Mouth to mouth I speak with him, in a vision and not in riddles..." <note>Numbers 15:8, referring to Moses</note>. All others saw the Word from a distance, as it is said: "From afar the Lord appeared to me." <note>Jeremiah 31:2</note>

Rabbi Hezekiah said: This is what I have learned. It is written: "And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi." <note>Exodus 2:1</note> The Holy One, Blessed be He, established this... "From the house of Levi"—this is the Holy One, Blessed be He, the place of **Higher Wisdom**, and that River <note>The flow of Divine emanation</note> joins as one so they are never separated. "From the house of Levi"—these are the chambers of the **Leviathan**, for this world is "this Leviathan which You formed to sport with." <note>Psalms 104:26</note> "And took a daughter of Levi"—this is the Holy One, Blessed be He, the place where the Moon's light is gathered.

"And the woman conceived and bore a son." <note>Exodus 2:2</note> ... I have learned this: before she is married she is called "the daughter of so-and-so," and after she is married she is called "the wife of so-and-so." "Daughter" and "Wife" are all one level of the Crown.

"And she hid him for three months." <note>Exodus 2:2-3</note> These are the three months where harsh judgment dwells in the world... What does this teach us? That before Moses came into the world, he was already watched from above, and the *Shekhinah* was joined with him from the day he was born. Rabbi Simeon said: The spirits of the righteous are present above before they come into the world.

"And when she could no longer hide him, she took for him..." <note>Exodus 2:3</note> What is "she took for him"? An ark of bulrushes, which she covered as a protection to be guarded from those "eyes" and "powers" that rule over the Great Sea, as it is written: "There is the sea, great and wide, where there are creeping things without number." <note>Psalms 104:25</note> And she covered it to be guarded from them with a covering of slime and pitch—two types, white and black—and she hid him below in a hidden place so he would not be recognized.

To be recognized by their forms, because he is destined to ascend to them. Fortunate is his portion to receive freedom and break the yoke of the broken. This comes from the side of the **Tree of Life**, which is holy, as it was said regarding the spirits "upon the mountains." Specifically "upon the mountains" and not upon the <unclear>Sinai</unclear>. It implies that those righteous ones, even before they descend into the world, are recognized above by all. And when the time comes for the souls of the righteous to descend below, they ascend as we have established. The explanation of the matter we have learned is that it implies fear, and if there is a soul... just as it has a body on the earth, it implies that in all sides, both above and below, it leads and pierces through; everything comes and is found, etc. They established the secret of what is written:

> Let the earth bring forth a living soul (Genesis 1:24)

Because of this, no one busied themselves with him except for the Holy One, Blessed be He, to bring him into the Inner Curtain <note>The *Pargod*, the celestial veil</note>. And because of this, the staff ascended with the supreme crown and with levels more precious than all the prophets of the world. Let us return to the vision behind the walls of the building: "And Joshua the High Priest was..." What did he see? That he was standing before the angel and clothed in filthy garments, until a herald went out and said: "Remove the filthy garments from him" <note>Zechariah 3:3-4</note>. That he is the Judge of his judgments, the one of whom it is written: "And do not fight before the angel, for it is an error." What...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Shelach Lecha<-

The wings <note>original: gadfin</note> are folded and raised as one, and the one of truth enters, though he is flawed toward the woman <note>referring to the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note>, to all the souls of Jacob. He descends to Gehenna. And King Solomon looked and saw the movement of the bosom like an elder of this world from below, to look at all times: "Let your garments be white" <note>Ecclesiastes 9:8</note>, at the beginning in the spirit to remember the matter of the fringes <note>Tzitzit</note> like an elder. And not for every person. For four kings go out from the whiteness for all of them. The ancient ones see, to look upon the Shekhinah at first; a quarter of the Priest hangs in the clouds to be included among them, thus there is no blue <note>Techelet</note>. The color of blue is for the joy of the Throne; they run like seven runners, bearing witness to the House of David and its restoration, and not his bosom below, and they do not stand in their places from that location. And regarding this: "And you shall see it and remember all the commandments of the Lord... and you shall not spy after [your hearts]" <note>Numbers 15:39</note>.

Like an opening of a gathering to establish all the many colors, to take all the blue of the pressure of the Throne that rises to the Crown <note>Keter</note> for a covering. It is written: "And they shall place upon the fringe of the corner a thread of blue" <note>Numbers 15:38</note>. It does not say "and they shall place upon the corner," but rather "upon the fringe," which does not rejoice except over the other threads. "And you shall see it and remember," and it is written "Remember the Sabbath day" <note>Exodus 20:8</note> to make the world for you. What is the reason for this? Rather, it is like a bride who fulfills a vow and explains all of it; and a father who loves his son wants to rebuke him, and finally says, "Be mindful of everything written for you." So too here: "And you shall see it and remember," for it is not a place where they strike with pains for words. In this manner, "And the voice of all that is written," keep it far and he shall live by it. Rather, when he lifts his eyes and sees the image of that which is written, he stands like a horse and reveals before the Lord, and they go out, and he knows the pressure of the eye for its life. That is to say, the bride sees the movement, for she sees and fears her King, to be responded to with favor and to have her prayer answered. One person studies it to be made a stone <note>perhaps referring to the punishment of stoning or spiritual hardening</note> because he sees with his eyes the stone of punishment. This commandment of the "wife of men" <note>a mystical reference to the soul or the Shekhinah</note> is to be found there. So too here: "And you shall see it and remember and do," and not just with the mouth, for the journey of the pure will cause you to remain meritorious for My service always. And then "you shall do," and "you shall not spy after your hearts and after your eyes," which are those other markings and labors. "You shall not spy etc." <note>Numbers 15:39</note>. And you shall not do evil, and because of this, this color of blue rises; blue is the likeness of the Throne of Glory. Just as the Throne of Glory causes a person to fear and to say, to be ashamed before Him, so too this blue causes a person to fear everything straight and to fear that everything lives to receive from this place, to cover in straightness. It is written: "From the wing of the earth we have heard songs, glory to the Righteous One; but I said, My secret is mine, my secret is mine, woe is me!" <note>Isaiah 24:16</note>. "From the wing of the earth"—this is the wing for the joy of the pressure of the wing of the earth. "We have heard songs"—these are the other threads that go out and hang from a high place in their bosoms, high paths that go out from the Supernal Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>. "Glory to the Righteous One"—this is the Righteous One <note>Tzadik/Yesod</note>, the Life of the Worlds, to prepare the threads, for their beauty comes from the cup, and every measure is included in two sides. And when we look at the humble one, "My secret is mine, my secret is mine"—this is the portion of the Supernal Spirit from which all places go out. And when one looks: the blue and the movement of the raised one to strike the place of fear, to fear the humble one. "My secret is mine," for how much he does not know how to rest, and upon what are they made to serve like these garments? For they call out without movement, they give testimony of the truth, and these are the garments that are entirely of the truth of their own bodies. And against the garments of their clothing without movement, it is called "against the garments." As it is written for the bread of the garments, for they are of the truth of the beginning of truth every day. Woe, woe to those who strip off, who rise in this Throne to consume the measures and their eyes. It is written: a memorial that calls to those against me, a stone like a tongue was filled regarding all their prayers. Woe to them, for they have no portion in the world to come! Meritorious are the righteous whose garments and perfections are known above, to do good for them in this world and in the world to come. **Tzade**. This commandment is the commandment of Tzitzit, which includes blue and white, representing judgment and mercy in everything, for the intention is not destroyed. Blue consumes "Remember," etc. And the pearl is white on the right, and blue on the left. The Middle Pillar <note>Tiferet</note> is more between the two of them, green. And in the three wisdoms from the words of the Mishnah, it is sealed; they call it seven markings of the secret between blue and white, and in every hope the movement is spread to call it a complete beauty.

**Rabbi Yehuda said:** How many are the ways that the Holy One, Blessed be He, acts to look upon the children of men! All of them are needed, and all stand before Him to receive <note>original: *lekabela*</note>. When a person walks, [the heavenly powers] stand before his feet to press upon them; they stand before him, proclaiming and saying: *He will guard the feet of His pious ones...* <note>1 Samuel 2:9</note>, *Guard your foot when you go...* <note>Ecclesiastes 4:17</note>, and *Level the path of your feet* <note>Proverbs 4:26</note>. He opens his eyes to look upon the world, and the "Masters of the Eyes" surround him. At times, the "Masters of the Wings" are ready to shield him from evil and harm. At times, the "Master of the World" surrounds him with the "Masters of Turning from Evil and Doing Good." Grace and windows and strength are written of, and *Satan stood at his right hand to accuse him* <note>Zechariah 3:1</note>. All of these stand over them as a liability above. A living person must look to the service of the Holy One, Blessed be He. All the "blind sides" <note>likely referring to spiritual forces of distraction or judgment</note> stand before him and wait to look upon him, waiting for the moment to seize him.

When a man wraps himself in many wraps <note>referring to the Tallit/prayer shawl</note> and places the Tefillin on his head, he fixes his eyes to lift his head and sees the holiness upon him. He is pious, and the straps rest upon his head, and the knots hang from this side and that side over his heart, so as not to look away from the glory of the King. He is pious; his hands are beloved below, tied like a knot of beauty. He raises his hands to look upon the glory of his Master. He wraps himself in the wrapping of the garment's fringes <note>Tzitzit</note>. Four "kings" go out before him; four witnesses of the King's truth hang from the four corners. And hanging from them are like grapes from a cluster. What is found for laughter? One, and many clouds hang from it, from this side and from that side. So too, this beauty is one, and many clouds of radiance and songs and circles hang from it.

There are seven runners <note>referring to the seven wrappings or threads</note>; they are the seven circles of the cluster that one must wrap himself in. Each and every one must look upon the thirteen <note>referring to the thirteen attributes of mercy or the thirteen windings of the fringes</note>, so that he may add to them, and by adding to them, he adds to the thirteen. And if he diminishes them, he diminishes from the cluster. It was a light wind for David the King, and he did not see it except to wrap himself in the merit of the crowns. What is the *Techelet* <note>the blue thread</note>? It is the *Tachlit* <note>the purpose/end</note> of everything certainly.

Rabbi Yehuda said: How great is the glory of the verses! Rabbi Yitzchak said: The seven wrappings are for the beauty of the signet ring, the ring of everything certainly. For life is wrapped sufficiently... on the hand that points. And there are three crowns... as they established it: a "help from the side." From here, it is the opening for all of them, and a single voice goes out. It is hinted at in the manner of the Hanukkah lamp; judgment goes out from one side... like the *Kinneret* <note>Sea of Galilee/Lyre</note>, and *Kinneret* is called after the left. Because of this, a lyre <note>Kinnor</note> was hanging above David's bed. For David is the beauty of David's lyre. They provide portions for the Holy King above. And thus the gardens enter until the firmament, and from the firmament until the Throne. And here it is written: *A portion of the King's food* <note>Daniel 1:5</note>. Why did he seal the drink of the King's portion? Because the King's portion and the wisdom and the engraving are crowned as one in the Kingdom. And it stands as a remembrance and an opening for all the surrounding crowns, as it is written: *Open for me the gates of righteousness* <note>Psalms 118:19</note>, and it is written: *This is the gate of the Lord* <note>Psalms 118:20</note>. It is written: *And you shall see it and remember all the commandments of the Lord* <note>Numbers 15:39</note>, to include in this all the surrounding crowns. And regarding these, the witnesses bear witness, and they do not stand in their likeness because of the beauty of the kingdoms... the supports of the portion... the Lulav and the Willow, etc. These are the supports of the Holy One, because they are whispered, as it is written: *To the Holy One of the Lord.*

Rabbi Yitzchak said: These are visions to look upon, how they hang from here and from there to the four sides of the world. From this side... and the spirit of the heart of life for everything, for all this world and for all that is upon it. And the heart rests upon it, and everything breathes in the heart that goes out from the wisdom above it. Rabbi Yitzchak said: The mountain that stands... is sealed with the engravings of the hair. Rabbi Yehuda said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, saw those who wish to draw the crown of His fear. Let that crown go to all of this, and the crown of the eyes that stand upon it. What are they? The eyes are all *the eyes of the Lord toward the righteous*. For everything... *that you do not go about after your own heart and your own eyes* <note>Numbers 15:39</note>. What is this like?

# Portion of "And Korah Took"

**And Korah took**, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi... <note>Numbers 16:1</note>. Rabbi Isaac opened: <term>"More to be desired are they than gold, even much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and the drippings of the honeycomb"</term> <note>Psalm 19:11</note>. How exalted are the words of the Torah! How precious they are, how beloved they are! They hang above, and they hang upon everything, because they are the <term>Holy Name</term> <note>original: "Shema Kadisha"</note>. Anyone who labors in the Torah labors in the Holy Name, and is saved from everything—saved in this world and in the world to come. Come and see: anyone who labors in the Torah takes hold of the Tree of Life, for since he takes hold of it, he takes hold of everything, as it is written: "She is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her" <note>Proverbs 3:18</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: Anyone who labors in the Torah, it gives him life from everything, life from death, as we have said; because freedom dwells upon him. Even among Israel, those who crown the Torah and are silent from all else are not found in exile. This is what is written: <term>"Engraved on the tablets"</term> <note>Exodus 32:16</note>—do not read it as "engraved" <note>Hebrew: Charut</note> but as <term>"Freedom"</term> <note>Hebrew: Cheirut</note>. This secret was established regarding the Torah. It is found that the power of the Right is entirely from the Right, as we have learned: and from God it is included in the Right. One who makes the Right into the Left, or the Left into the Right, brings guilt upon himself and quarrels with the Master of the World. Come and see: Aaron represents the <term>Right</term> <note>the attribute of Mercy/Chesed</note>. The Levites represent the <term>Left</term> <note>the attribute of Judgment/Gevurah</note>. Korah sought to exchange the Right for the Left because of what he did; and not only that, but an evil tongue <note>slander/gossip</note> was found in him, and he acted against everything. Rabbi Yehuda said: The Left is always included in the Right. Korah sought to change the arrangement of the upper and lower worlds, because he was included from above and below. <term>"And Korah took."</term> What did he take? He took an evil power for himself. Every child follows his Levite [ancestry] to be joined to the Lord, but he [Korah] moved away from Him. And not only that, but how much did he bring upon himself? Korah pursued his own Levite status to know wisdom, but in the end, he lost. Korah went into a dispute. What is a dispute? A <term>Division</term> <note>original: "Pelugta"</note>. A division of the upper and lower worlds. And anyone who seeks to change the arrangement of the world will be destroyed from all worlds. A dispute is a division of Peace, and whoever disputes Peace, disputes the Name of the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>...

## Main Text (Zohar)

...holy, because the holy heaven is called **Peace** <note>original: "Shalom"</note>. Come and see: the world only stands upon peace. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, it could not endure until He came and spread peace over it. Thus, the attribute of Peace was found to be the harmony of the upper and lower worlds, and then the world was established. Anyone who causes division against it perishes from the world. The Serpent divided against the attribute of Peace and slandered it. One who divides against peace takes another portion, as we have said—a portion of mundane matters <note>original: "millei de-chol," referring to non-sacred or "weekday" things</note>. One who receives the mundane does not merit the sacred, and to kindle mundane matters on the Sabbath is forbidden, for it divides against the peace of the world. Rabbi Yose said: It is written, **"Great peace have those who love Your Torah"** <note>Psalm 119:165</note>—Your Torah is peace. And it is written, **"And all her paths are peace"** <note>Proverbs 3:17</note>. Korah came to blemish the peace of the upper and lower worlds; therefore, he perished from the world below.

->**And they rose up** before Moses, etc. <note>Numbers 16:2</note><-
The companions have already explained this matter of Korah. Rabbi Shimon said: **"The called of the assembly"** <note>original: "Kru'ei Moed"</note>—the word "called" <note>Kru'ei</note> is written without the letter *Yod*, which suggests a connection to the five thousand. Thus it is: the kingdom of the earth is like the kingdom of the firmament. The secret of this is that all those supernal crowns of the **Holy Name** <note>original: "Shema Kadisha"</note> are attached to them. They are all invited to the place that sanctifies that "calling of holiness" <note>Mikra Kodesh</note>. I have seen that when a "Moed" <note>Appointed Time/Festival</note> is invited into the world, it is in the likeness of those supernal crowns invited from the Supernal Sanctuary. Here, it was prepared beforehand to crown them with supernal holiness. They knew the "Wisdom of Solomon" was prepared here, and it would be ready for all the portions. All these matters are ready to be crowned in this holiness at the times when the "Moed" dwells in the world, just as the changes stand above. From here we learn that their people are below, and therefore they are called **"the called of the assembly"** <note>Kru'ei Moed</note>, because they are below as a reflection of those above—**"men of renown"** <note>Numbers 16:2, literally "men of the Name"</note> indeed. They were not merely "wise in the Name," for there was no spirit within that day, as we have established. Therefore, they are called "men of the Name" specifically, for they praised themselves more than all others, and they attached themselves as is written.

---

->**In the morning** the Lord will show who are His <note>Numbers 16:5</note><-
Why "in the morning"? And why "holy" <note>Kadosh</note> and not "pure" <note>Tahor</note>? It is because they [the Levites] come from the side of "pure," but the Priest is called "holy." Moses said "morning" because that is when the crown of the Priest is awakened in the world. If you seek the Priesthood, here is the morning; perform the service of the morning, and then **"the Lord will show who are His and who is holy."** "Who are His"—this refers generally to Joseph. "And who is holy"—this is the Priest. Then "He will bring him near to Him." No one understands this matter: "morning" is established in **Kindness** <note>original: "Chesed," the right-hand emanation associated with the morning and the Priesthood</note>. This is the time. And it was taught: Aaron the Prophet <note>note: likely referring to his role as a spokesman/visionary</note> shall bring you near, just as the incense must be found and burned by his hand, so that everything is bound together. The one who finds this is the Priest. Because of this, "the man whom the Lord chooses shall be the holy one"—and not "the pure one." These are two levels: **Holy** and **Pure**. The Priest is Holy; the Levite is Pure. Therefore, "the Holy" is written.

---

->**And they fell** on their faces and said: O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh <note>Numbers 16:22</note><-
Come and see: they surrendered themselves to death. Why? Because it is written, **"And they fell on their faces and said: O God, the God of the spirits."** The word "spirit" <note>Ruach</note> is written deficiently. The Levite represents the fear of death, and in every place, the "falling of the face" <note>a specific prayer posture</note> is directed to that place. "Unto God"—He is the God [El] of pleasantness every day. **"God of the spirits"**—this is the place where the souls of the world reside, and all souls ascend there and descend again. Rabbi Yehuda opened: **"Hear my words, you wise men; and give ear to me, you who have knowledge"** <note>Job 34:10</note>. This was said regarding Korah. Come and see what is written: "When his friends heard, his anger burned because he did not have the strength for the deed," etc. For they were saying words that she [the Divine Presence] could not be praised by. Let the change be examined by whoever enters into wisdom...

## Main Text (Zohar)

Those wise ones who saw [the truth] would speak words of truth to everyone, to subdue [the heart] before Him, because they desire words of life. May a true life be upon them, and then one will accept the judgment upon himself and give thanks to the Holy King for it. What is written? **"While he is about to fill his belly, God will cast the fury of His wrath upon him..."** <note>original: "וחזיהו מכה את האויב בכרסיה"; the Zohar paraphrases Job 20:23</note> to return to the Crown <note>The sefirah of Keter</note> to receive, and he accepted the judgment upon himself, as it is written. Further, it is written: <term>Therefore, listen to me, you men of understanding: Far be it from God to do wickedness, and from the Almighty to do wrong</term> <note>Job 34:10</note>. "Therefore, listen to me"—they are destined in all things to find words [of truth]. "Far be it from God to do wickedness"—this refers to that which is written: He trembles and shakes every day. "And from the Almighty <note>original: Shaddai</note> to do wrong"—this [name] is placed close to receive this, and we have already established the meaning of the name <term>El Shaddai</term> <note>God Almighty; often interpreted in Jewish mysticism as "He who said 'Enough' (Dai) to the creation," setting boundaries</note>.

<term>For He repays a man according to his work</term> <note>Job 34:11</note>. Behold, when a man labors in this world and performs his work, yet sins before his Master, that deed hangs over him to find judgment for him. This is what is written: "For He repays a man according to his work"—that very deed repays him. And despite all this, if he sets his heart [to repent], because a person's children, his heart, and his will should be found before his Master, then <term>He would gather to Himself his spirit and his breath</term> <note>Job 34:14</note>. This is like the spirit of life, and it does not surround his soul outside to be found in engraved judgment.

Rabbi Yose said: We have learned that the spirit returns at hidden times to the Holy One, blessed be He. "For He repays a man according to his work"—to be found in his judgment. And there are meritorious deeds that a man performs in this world that elevate him to be found through his works when he departs from the world. What is written afterward? <term>Who gave Him charge over the earth? Or who laid on Him the whole world?</term> <note>Job 34:13</note>. "Who gave Him charge over the earth"—this refers to the brother who is close to him. "Or who laid on Him the whole world"—this refers to the members of his household. And then, for the sake of the world and its restoration, he rebukes [him]. What is written afterward? "If He should set His heart upon it." This man who is charged to build his house must direct his heart and his will toward that death <note>The Zohar here discusses the mystical intentions during the act of Levirate marriage or procreation to "restore" a departed soul</note>.

In all cases, when he sins with that woman for her beauty and her adornment, behold, it is not for the sake of the world's [restoration], for the will and the heart were not directed toward the deceased. Because of this, it is written that the importance depends on the heart; according to the will of the heart that was directed toward him, then "He would gather to Himself his spirit and his breath," and it reaches him and restores the world through him. What is written afterward? <term>All flesh would perish together, and man would return to dust</term> <note>Job 34:15</note>. "All flesh would perish together"—that body will rot in the dust, along with all that flesh and woman. "And man would return to dust"—this refers to the first one who was in the initial building, and he returns to the dust of the body's construction, just as it was at first. Therefore, the spirit and the soul are in the hands of the Holy One, blessed be He, and life is upon them, for He gathers all and they shall not be consumed from this world or the World to Come. Therefore, tremble and shake—
->Exaltation to all flesh!<-

**And Moses said** to Aaron: "Take the censer..." <note>Numbers 17:11</note>. Rabbi Hiyya opened [the discourse]: <term>The king’s wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise man will appease it</term> <note>Proverbs 16:14</note>. How much must people guard themselves from their sins and remember their deeds! For every single day, deeds are weighed and ascend, and they are observed above and written before Him. Therefore, a person must be careful, for how many times is the world judged? And then anger ascends before the Holy One, blessed be He, and judgment [is enacted] below. This is what is written: "The king’s wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise man will appease it." At the hour when the destroyers of judgment stand over the world and anger hangs ready to be found, then the righteous one whose heart is accepted before Him—then the anger is stilled.

It is like a king who was angry with his servants, for he sought to unleash his fury <note>original: "פנטזירא" (fantasia/officer/wrath)</note> upon them. A beloved friend of the king entered and stood before him, for he saw that the king was angry. That friend of the king was wise enough to be shaken with him, and the king rejoiced. Afterward, when the fury subsided, the king's hands were stayed from striking, and then that friend was a mediator for the servants and appeased [the king] for them. Thus: "and a wise man will appease it." So too here, when he saw that the anger was great... <margin>it is taught</margin>

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Korach, focusing on the mystical significance of the incense (Ketoret) and the specific duties of the family of Kohath (the Kohathites) in relation to the Tabernacle. ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Korach**<-

Come and see: *And Moses said to Aaron, "Take the censer..."* <note>Numbers 16:46</note>. This incense rises above all else; it is a whisper that reaches the Priest <note>The Kohen, representing the attribute of Mercy</note>, and it binds the "knot of faith" <note>original: "kitora de-meimanuta" — a mystical union of the divine realms</note>. This incense, as the sages have established, is the joy of both the upper and lower worlds. It is the binding of faith, the ascent of the divine will. For we have learned: *“Ointment and perfume [incense] rejoice the heart”* <note>Proverbs 27:9</note>. At that moment, the Holy One takes pity on His children; He cleanses and purifies that "Anger" <note>the divine attribute of Judgment</note>, and Mercy is awakened.

Rabbi Eleazar said: *“Do not cut off the tribe of the families of the Kohathites from among the Levites”* <note>Numbers 4:18</note>. This is because they are the body and the essential attachment of the Levites. *“But thus do unto them, that they may live, and not die”*—it is the duty of the Priest to prepare them, to bring them near to the Holy One, blessed be He. They shall enter into the domain of the Priest, for the Priest knows how to humble the power of the "Prophet" <note>here referring to a specific level of divine emanation</note> and no further. When they cover the holy vessels, it is done with great care and piety, so that they may draw near to see; for the King does not reveal His secret except to those who are broken and humble. Their words and their deeds are performed in mystery.

The Levites follow the path of the "Voice," while the Priests and the Kohathites represent the "Word" and the "Piety." They are entrusted with Judgment, for there are none like the Kohathites to sustain and publicize the matter. Every Priest is appointed with spirit and strength, and the Kohathites are the support of all things, rectifying the "Pressure" <note>the constriction of judgment</note> so that the "Right Hand" <note>Mercy</note> may draw near. For the Right Hand is destined to bring near all those who were cast away in the world from the "Left Side" <note>the side of Severity</note>. Just as with the incense, the pressure is transformed by a subtle, internal spirit. Come and see: when other powers surround to awaken an awakening [of judgment], and they are not found, then the internal purity awakens the Prophet and the Holy One, and judgments are silenced. At that moment, the "Darkness" departs.

Rabbi Eleazar said: *“This is the service of the sons of Kohath in the Tent of Meeting, about the most holy things”* <note>Numbers 4:4</note>. At the time when the sons of Kohath carry the Holy of Holies, the Priest comes and covers everything before they approach to carry it. They were never permitted to see what they were carrying; rather, everything was covered with a covering, as it is written: *“And when Aaron and his sons have made an end of covering the sanctuary... after that, the sons of Kohath shall come to bear it”* <note>Numbers 4:15</note>. The covering of the King's sanctuary is "Blue" <note>Tekhelet</note>, because this blue—as has been explained—is the "Crown" <note>Keter</note> that covers all. The sons of Kohath approach from within, but they only approach according to the vision of what goes out. *“And when Aaron and his sons have made an end of covering the sanctuary... they shall come to bear it,”* because the incense is an internal pressure, and everything the herald proclaims to the Priest must be handed over.

Regarding this: *“And Aaron took as Moses commanded, and ran into the midst of the congregation; and, behold, the plague was begun among the people: and he put on incense, and made an atonement for the people”* <note>Numbers 16:47-48</note>. This purity is internal, a spirit of strength. Then *“he made atonement for the people, and he stood between the dead and the living.”* This is the vision of Life that smiles at Death; then the "Relative" <note>the attribute of Mercy</note> is proven to be near, and the plague is stayed. This is the portion of the Priest, for he has power above and he has power below. His voice establishes peace in the upper and lower realms. Whenever peace is served, glory is found.

Rabbi Eleazar was standing before Rabbi Simeon, his father. He saw it written: *“And they shall pass through it, hard pressed and hungry; and it shall come to pass, that when they shall be hungry, they shall fret themselves, and curse their king and their God, and look upward. And they shall look unto the earth; and behold trouble and darkness, dimness of anguish; and they shall be driven to darkness”* <note>Isaiah 8:21-22</note>. See what is written! See this matter of day and night, where the measure of night is like the day. This is the spirit that has pity on sin. He said: this is because his portion is like one who pities, who does not toil except for this. And regarding your people, "Wine" came, "Toil" under the sun, as it says: *“In all your ways acknowledge Him, and He shall direct your paths.”* Come and see: all the appointments of the Name are full, all of them hidden within Wisdom. Many "Bald Spots" <note>a pun on the name Korach, which means bald</note> will be seen by the wicked, as it is written: *“In its midst is all kindness, the beginning of your hand to do; act according to your strength, for He is gracious in deed and sparing...”* See, the verse here contains all kindness, the beginning of your hand to work according to your strength—this is the order of Wisdom.

## Main Text (Zohar)

For the supreme wisdom is within him, more so than all the people of the world. He said this: anyone who rests the King upon his head is called a spirit of wisdom. **Come and see:** *Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your strength* <note>Ecclesiastes 9:10</note>. This means a person must include the Left <note>the attribute of Judgment/Gevurah</note> within the Right <note>the attribute of Mercy/Chesed</note>, and everything he does should be directed so that it all exists within the Right.

> *Whatever your hand finds* (Ecclesiastes 9:10)

This refers to the Left.

> *To do with your strength* (ibid.)

This refers to the Right, as it is said (Exodus 15:6):

> *Your right hand, O Lord, is glorious in power <note>original: "koach" - strength/power</note>.*

And since a person is careful that all his deeds are on the side of the Right, and he includes the Left within the Right, then the Holy One, Blessed be He, dwells within him in this world and brings him into the hidden treasury of the World to Come. Such a person will not die in the error that comes into this world; rather, he awakens mercy from the King and sits before Him, even if it were not otherwise fitting. Through wisdom and knowledge, a person leaves this world and escapes many houses of judgment. But if a person desires that the Holy King should atone for him in that world and give him a portion in the World to Come, he must strive in this world to include his deeds in the Right, and all his deeds should be for the sake of the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. For after he is gathered from this world, if he is found under harsh judgment in the law of Gehinnom <note>Purgatory/Hell</note>, there is no counsel, nor wisdom, nor any letters <note>of the Torah</note> to save him from judgment. **Come and see:** *For there is no action, nor accounting, nor knowledge, nor wisdom in Sheol* <note>the underworld</note>. In Gehinnom, there are chambers upon chambers. The lowest chamber is called Abaddon <note>Destruction</note>, and it has no support; those who did not walk in merit to be judged and then released go there. These are the assembly of rebels who descend to Sheol, and those who descend to Abaddon do not ascend ever again. 

One who possesses good deeds, or those who teach goodness—it has been established that every single night, before a person sleeps, he must make an accounting <note>term: Cheshbon - a spiritual audit</note> of the deeds he performed all that day, repent for them, and ask for mercy. Why at that specific hour? Because at that hour, the Tree of Death <note>the aspect of night/judgment</note> dwells in the world, and all people of the world taste the taste of death <note>sleep is considered 1/60th of death</note>. At that hour, one must make an accounting of his deeds and confess them, because he is tasting death. These people are called the "Masters of Accounting" <note>original: "Marey de-Chushbana"</note>. 

Likewise, one who strives with knowledge and wisdom to know his Master—when they pass him through to be found among those wicked ones who are driven into Gehinnom, because he walked and directed himself toward those higher levels, he will not stay there nor be looked upon among them. Regarding this, it is said: *there is no action, nor accounting, nor knowledge, nor wisdom in Sheol*—he will not look there, but only upward to the place of Wisdom, where lights and stars and many delights dwell, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, is there to take pleasure with the righteous in the Garden of Eden. Fortunate is the portion of the righteous in this world and the World to Come; of them it is written:

> *Surely the righteous shall give thanks to Your name; the upright shall dwell in Your presence.* (Psalms 140:14).

**And the Levite** *shall perform the service of the Tent of Meeting...* (Numbers 18:23). Rabbi Abba opened the discourse:

> *It is He who sits above the circle of the earth...* (Isaiah 40:22).

**Come and see:** When the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to create the world, it arose in His will before Him, and He created it through the Torah. Thus He looked into it and the world was established, as it was supported by its pillars. And it is written: *And I was beside Him as a nursling <note>original: "Amon"</note>.* It has been established: do not read it as *Amon* (nursling), but as *Uman* (architect/craftsman). When He came to create Man, and God said, *Let us make man...* (Genesis 1:26), it was to make known that He is called "Slow to Anger and Abounding in Mercy." At that hour when He desired to create Man, the radiance of his beautiful countenance spread from above to below, and all creatures and wise beings feared him. **Come and see:** The world was sustained but not fully built until the hour that Man emerged in his image, and everything was sanctified as the day <note>Sabbath</note> was sanctified. The Holy Throne of the King was established, and then the upper and lower worlds were completed, and joys were found in all worlds. At that hour when the day was about to be sanctified, spirits were emerging to be created with bodies, but the day was sanctified and they were not created <note>referring to the demons/spirits created at twilight on Friday</note>. Thus the world remained somewhat deficient in its work, and it was tied...

## The Faithful Shepherd (Ra’aya Mehemna)

**Every** firstborn of the womb of all flesh, etc. <note>Numbers 18:15</note> Come and see in the Book of Enoch: this **commandment** is to redeem the firstborn of a donkey, to redeem it for the World to Come. This is a holiness that is destined to encompass the world; it shall not be spread like a poor man. His prayer is destined to be honored before the worlds as in the beginning; he shall return to the days of old. It is written: **Lo, all these things doth God work, twice, yea thrice, with a man.** <note>Job 33:29</note> And Israel, because they have redemption, the whole Torah is a cup of salvation for them, for the end of the world. They were cast three times into exile, and in the final redemption, they shall be redeemed. They shall never again be arranged in exile. They wept and embraced him and said: "Faithful Shepherd! The Holy One, blessed be He, shall redeem you, and when Israel is redeemed through you, we shall be sanctified with them, and we shall live with you." This next **commandment** is to dwell upon the valuations <note>the laws of *Arachin*—vows of monetary value</note> of the "House of the Male" of Wisdom. The "House of the Male" is below, for good and evil, and one must receive the evil like the good. He gives her her valuation. But below, in the portion of life, it is said of her: "He shall sustain her," and "gold and glass cannot equal it." There is no valuation for her like this, to establish: **A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband** <note>Proverbs 12:4</note> and it is said of her: **A virtuous woman who can find? For her price is far above rubies.** <note>Proverbs 31:10</note> This is our *Shekhinah* <note>Divine Presence</note>, with whom Kindness (*Chesed*) goes; there is no valuation for her. And whoever approaches her, there is no valuation for her assembly. Just as they were for those who trampled her, all these have no valuation. Every single person blesses the redemption from whoever is able on this side. From the *Shekhinah*, no redemption is needed, for of the *Shekhinah* it is said: "To the Lord belongs your acquisition." My name and my cup... her redemption is established from the matters of her connection to Israel in the holiness of the *Tefillin*, the power of the Sabbath, the power of the Festivals, the power of the Covenant. She shares in several commandments whose redemption is like the *Shema* prayer, to labor for its own sake. These are the commandments that people enter into in order to receive a reward, and every commandment has a valuation in the world. But for the one who performs them for their own sake, there is no valuation or measure. The next **commandment** is to dwell in the Sanctuary... to the Priest of Kindness (*Chesed*)... every firstborn of the womb of all flesh which they bring to the Lord...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the commandments (Ra'aya Meheimna) found in the Zohar.
