# Korach

"The wicked prepares it, but the righteous shall wear it" <note>Job 27:17</note>. It is said regarding the wicked man: "Remember what the wicked one did." For everything that the Holy One, Blessed be He, takes away from the wicked, He gives to the righteous. For the Prophet said, "A voice of iron," <note>original: "קול ברזל"</note> which lacks the power to be told, "You are more cursed than all the cattle." And his portion is to be paid back outside of all the gardens. 

The Holy One, Blessed be He, looks upon the one who weeps, for his portion is where blessing reaches him. Our strength is to awaken in the heights, for the Master of the Universe is the one who subdues the side of judgment and awakens the Prophet with mercy, to subdue the anger of the "Other Side" <note>the realm of evil/impurity</note> and to burn it. Regarding the wicked, it is remembered: Who are the wicked? Those who cast an eye upon the gardens of the "Other Side" to take strength. But the man who is good subdues the animalistic nature to merit the Priest, to spread the light of kindness and to remove from himself the curse that is included in all the curses of the Torah. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings forth everything, and all blessings are in His mouth. Therefore, every person needs to set aside from his grain a portion for the Priest, which is the Great Offering, and a portion for the Levite, which is the Tithe. Through this, he is paid back with a portion from the King's table.

**The Commandment**
After this, to set aside the **Great Offering** <term>Terumah Gedolah: the first portion of the harvest given to the Priest</term>. The masters of the Mishnah established that from every "offering" <note>Terumah</note>, the Sages ordained that it must be separated from all roasted grains. Its secret meaning: Who is the one who wants to sustain the "Me" <note>Hebrew: 'Mi', referring to the higher hidden realm</note>? It is the secret of "He shall surely die." And this is the secret of the word "Me" <note>original: "מי"</note> in the verse "That they take for **Me** an offering" <note>Exodus 25:2</note>. "Take for Me" implies two times in a day, which is the secret of the Shema prayer. One must intend to crown the "Kingdom of Heaven" <note>the Shekhinah</note> forever and ever. And through the letters of the Name, the "Great Offering" is the Supernal Shekhinah, and it should be voiced in their throats. One must unify the Holy One, Blessed be He, through what is in their throats. The measure of their throats is full of the "Me" <note>original: "מלא מ"י"</note>. And also, "He and His Name are One." Furthermore, it is written: "You shall lift up an offering to the Lord" <note>Numbers 15:19</note>. "You shall lift up" <note>Hebrew: Tarimu</note> because the letters can be rearranged to spell "Exalt the [letter] Mem" <note>Tari-Mu</note>. These are the **Ten Sefirot** <term>the ten divine emanations</term> which are the ten forms of service. The Name "Yod-He" <note>YH</note> equals 15, and when you add the "Me" <note>Mem-Yod, which is 50</note>, it equals 100. This is what the Sages established: "And now, Israel, **what** <note>Hebrew: 'Mah', numerically 45</note> does the Lord your God ask of you?" Do not read it as "What" <note>Mah</note> but as "One Hundred" <note>Me'ah</note>, corresponding to the one hundred blessings a person is obligated to bless the Kingdom <note>the Shekhinah</note> every day. And this is why a person must taste [holiness] every day through the secret of "That they take for Me an offering." And how many offerings are there? There is the offering of the Torah, which is the "Holy Torah" that is unified with the Kingdom. And you shall take it for the Priest, for Moses stayed there forty days and forty nights, he did not eat bread and did not drink water. He became like the "Offering" to the Holy One, Blessed be He. And since the King did not eat, the servants did not eat, until after the service was completed with the laws for all the companions.

**The Commandment**
After this, to set aside the **Tithe of the Tithe** <term>Maaser Min HaMaaser: the portion the Levite gives to the Priest</term>. This is the Shekhinah from the side of the Levites. From the "Great Offering" of the Sages, which is from the side of the Priest, we come to the "Tithe of the Tithe" which belongs to the Shekhinah. The word "Tithe" <note>Maaser</note> contains the word "Ten" <note>Eser</note>, which refers to the ten letters of the crown. And why ten? To include the three crowns of the letter Yod (י י י) which equal 30, and the ten Sefirot which equal 10. All of this is the secret of the Mother <note>Binah/Understanding</note> and the addition of the letter He (ה), which completes the Tithe.

**The Commandment**
To set aside the **Tithe** from the side of the lower Tithe. "A Tithe from the Tithe" <note>Numbers 18:26</note>—what does this imply? From the lower side, all the crowns are one "Yod" (10). And the Shekhinah is the Tithe of the Sefirot, specifically the letter He (5). This is from the side of the prayer of the "Head Tefillin," which corresponds to the Kingdom, until the prayer of the "Hand Tefillin." The prayer of the afternoon <note>Mincha</note> is corrected above, and the Shekhinah ascends to the Prophet. This side is called the "Two Crowns," which are the two Yods (י י). "A shekel is twenty gerahs" <note>Exodus 30:13</note>—ten and ten. This is the "Holy Shekel," which is ten and ten. Furthermore, the two crowns of Yod and Yod come from the "Yovel" <note>Jubilee</note> and the "Yeter" <note>Remainder</note>. All together they are 30: ten above, ten below, and ten in the middle. These three crowns are Yod, Yod, Yod.

**The Commandment**
After this, to set aside the **Tithe for the Poor** <term>Maaser Ani: given in the 3rd and 6th years of the sabbatical cycle</term>. Our masters of the Mishnah established this in the Torah as twenty crowns. They are distributed as a crown for the Lord. The Tithe of the third year is 30, and the Tithe of the poor is 10. These are the "Great Portions" which are 40 crowns, totaling 100. And so they would perform 30 commandments, which are Yod, Yod, Yod. Sometimes it is paid in days, and sometimes in years, and sometimes in hours. Sometimes ten days are opened with a crown, and sometimes ten kings.
In the fifth...

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Korach** <-

...with their mouths and they are redeemed by it in the time of anger, "by the mouth of the Lord" <note>original: *al pi Hashem*</note>, and they direct their hearts "by the mouth of the Lord." They trembled to pass by the mouth of the Lord in secret. For when she <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> saw the four faces and the three pillars to the south, and thirty faces for every mouth until the end, they would encamp and they would journey. They guard the Shekhinah like a crown for those who guard the "knife" <note>likely a reference to ritual slaughter or circumcision</note> and have a "good eye" <note>a generous spirit</note>. Because of this, the Shekhinah does not move from Israel on every Sabbath, and they possess good eyes. And even on a weekday Sabbath <note>referring to the holiness found within the mundane</note>, she is protected and shaken, as in all the exile where she has an ascent and a revelation... to prepare her arrangement of the supernal colors which are the signs of Greatness, Strength, Beauty <note>The Sefirot: *Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet*</note>, and Foundation and Kingdom <note>*Yesod* and *Malchut*</note>. They spread their faces to receive the spreading of the children. And according to the secret of the merit that rests upon these serving souls, they wait and intend in every single commandment of the Torah for the "knives" <note>instruments of action</note>, the garments of the tongues, and the commandment is with them. And so they see the feast of their children... to receive the reward of the Holy One, blessed be He, in His blessing to clarify all hidden things. And for those who act and intend... to receive a reward in the life above them, like their eyes in their youth, and the damaging spirits and the kings of the enemy are separated from the children by their blessing. They opened above with comforts that were desired... and all of it is the ascent of the Faithful Shepherd <note>Moses</note>.

-> # Portion of "This is the Statute of the Torah" <-

**And the Lord spoke** to Moses and to Aaron, saying: This is the statute of the Torah which the Lord has commanded, saying, etc. <note>Numbers 19:1-2</note>. Rabbi Yose opened: "And this is the Torah which Moses set before the children of Israel" <note>Deuteronomy 4:44</note>. Come and see: the words of the Torah are holy, they are supernal, they are sweet, as it is written: "More to be desired are they than gold, even much fine gold; sweeter also than honey..." <note>Psalms 19:11</note>. Whoever exerts himself in the Torah, it is as if he stands every day on Mount Sinai and receives the Torah, for every single day that Voice does not cease, and it declares secrets from Sinai. It is written "The statute of the Torah" <note>original: *Chukat HaTorah*</note> and it is written "And this is the Torah" <note>original: *V'zot HaTorah*</note>. What is the difference between this one and that one? Rather, it is a supernal secret <note>original: *raza ila'ah*</note> according to his portion. "And this is the Torah" stands alone, and "The statute of the Torah" is all in one unity. Everything is within the Assembly of Israel <note>the *Knesset Yisrael*, a mystical name for the Shekhinah</note> when it is to be joined as one. Therefore, "And this is the Torah" is separate, and "Statute" <note>*Chukat*</note> is an addition to this secret; this is the harness of the whole which is one without separation. "Statute" implies the general and the particular in the measure of Male and Female <note>original: *dechar u-nukva*</note>. And because "And this is the Torah" is Male, and "This is the statute" is an addition, this is the "Statute of the Torah." This is the decree of the Torah. Come and see: "Statute" <note>*Chok*</note> is for the prophets, but "Statute-of" <note>*Chukat*</note> is the Matron <note>the Queen/Shekhinah</note> of harsh judgment that comes from the side of Mercy. Rabbi Yehuda said: But is it not written "The statutes of the Lord are true..." <note>Psalms 19:10</note>? ...Heaven forbid it should be so! This verse proves from its latter part that it is like the likeness of life and not death, and the elixir of life <note>original: *sama d'chayyi*</note> is mixed into it. He who merits it, lives and does not die, because the elixir of life is joined with the "Statute." ...Therefore, "And this is the Torah" is truly in one unity, in a perfect unity of Male and Female.

Rabbi Shimon, Rabbi Eleazar, and Rabbi Isaac were present at the house of Rabbi Phinehas ben Yair. Rabbi Phinehas said to Rabbi Shimon: In the hour that we eat from the pleasures of wisdom concerning you above, and the King is delighted by that which permission was not given to any other man in this portion, tell us a new word. He said to him: What is it? He replied: "This is the statute of the Torah." He said to him: It is light, yet I thought it was heavy...

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> Chukat <-
<note>Numbers 19:1; "This is the statute of the Torah"</note>

Rabbi Eleazar said: Blessed are you, Eleazar, stand firm in your standing, and see a single word in this section that proclaims itself, and others follow after you. <note>original: "קס"ר" - likely an abbreviation for Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai addressing his son</note> Eleazar, come and see: "This is the statute of the Torah" regarding the serpents and regarding the Torah to establish it. This verse must be looked into: they performed wisdom in the world and followed after it, and they nullified their lives. These are not merely worldly wisdoms, but rather within the judgment of the Torah, for through life they were nullified. And they saw that the nullification of a word of Torah brings the whole world near to ruin; rather, it was certainly within the judgment of the Torah. And through a high mystery this matter was done. Because the ancients were pious and righteous, this matter was not revealed among them. And from the time they laughed in the world, this matter was performed <margin>(what they passed through)</margin> in order to provide a place below, to become wise in matters of life through the Supernal Spirit, as they have established it. And it says: "Do not come near here; remove your shoes from your feet," etc. <note>Exodus 3:5; God speaking to Moses at the Burning Bush</note>. Why did the Master open with this? It was said that he was commanded regarding his wife, to separate from her and to bond with another lower level of Holy Light that came upon him. And that Master established him in a place of the secret, to pass him from this world and establish him in another world. And for all that death gives to a person in a good world, the nullification of his senses from his house is bad, like a vessel. For example, one who makes his feet before the split and suppresses them, and they ascend to another world, a place of another death, as it is written: "How beautiful are your steps in sandals, O daughter of a noble!" <note>Song of Songs 7:2</note>. This refers to the walking of the noble one; it is written that she was drawn, as it is written: "They are carried by me from the birth" <note>Isaiah 46:3</note>. And the spirit of the matter was laughed at among the companions. And this is so: when death takes them. But at the time they exist, they rise from thought, and it is given to a person in a place to be established; he performs an establishment in the fire above. The Master who goes in movement, and all is one place.

And come and see: a dead man who departs from the world without children is called a "daughter" in the script. He does not gather to his Master, and he returns to be separated in the world because he found no place, and no establishment preceded him to be repaired and to be prepared in another transition, as it is written: "And at the last, he will stand upon the dust" <note>Job 19:25; referring to the resurrection or the redeemer</note>, as they have established it. And if he was killed in a mystery, he does not wish to maintain his statute in this world; they seek to tie a Master to his feet, and that one below—they bind him and receive that Master to her to give him life. Because that Master, because of the death of the "thorn" <note>referring to the deceased brother</note>, is taken by the feet of the living to be established below, receiving that Master to her to begin again, for that dead man is between the "thorn" and the "place" in this deed. And this is as it is written regarding that Master who nullifies death from life. And the woman—this Master nullifies him from death, and requires the Master of that death, and he does not go with him to life. And the woman nullifies him to her to begin again, for "a woman is the crown of her husband" <note>Proverbs 12:4</note>; she takes him and receives him to her. And she must nullify that Master to the earth to begin again, for the building of the bodies of that dead man; and receive your teaching for them afterward, and he pours water upon it and receives him into another world. This soul of that Master pushes to the woman to begin again, so as not to be extinguished in this death in another dust, for this is "the secret of the silence." And he returns to the dust from which they were at first. When he moves to the dust, then the woman is opened and she prepares to perform a desire in the place and to establish him.

Come and see: to establish an establishment, he nullifies his Master and gives to the companions to establish upon him an establishment, for the "daughter of the noble" is a witness. "Now this was the custom in former times in Israel concerning redemption..." <note>Ruth 4:7; regarding the removal of the shoe to confirm a transaction or levirate duty</note>. This "Zot" (This) stands as the whole. To enter the striking when they were holy movements to establish every matter, from which there was an establishment. And then, "this was the testimony in Israel." And do not say that this was another wisdom, but rather a Supernal establishment, so that their deeds would be in the establishment of Above. Since for their wisdom they are liable in the world, like a man forced for the sake of another in the wings of a cup; and this is the Kingdom <term>Malchut: the final sphere of the Divine attributes, associated with the physical world and the feminine principle</term> for the repair and the spirit of the matter, and "silver shall not go up to the house" as it is written.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Chukat (Statute)**<-

**This** is the statute of the Torah. "This" refers to the seal <note>original: "chotama"</note> of the covenant that is never separated. When it is expressed, it is called "the Whole," and through its closeness, the male enters [the female]; the left side is feminine when they are joined. • The statute of the Torah • It should have said "from the Torah"; why "the statute of the Torah"? • Rather, "statute" and "joy" are one and the same. Everything is one, the letters Lamed and Kaf <note>forming the word "Lach" (to you) or "Kol" (all)</note> are joined in measure. This is shown to be called such, as it is said: "and you shall not rest with your neighbor." • The letter He <term>Sefirah Malchut/Binah - the feminine aspects of the Divine</term> is like wisdom, like a pregnancy. It deals with the sins of human beings, then from the brain comes the deviation and the killing, and I did not revive them. Over everything, it is called "except for them," for it is said of them that everything is in measure. They have no later [existence]... and the poor one is one of them, and in their joys are engravings... and everything is one word.

## Raya Mehemna (The Faithful Shepherd)

->**The Faithful Shepherd**<-

**Speak** to the children of Israel that they bring to you a heifer, a red heifer, whole, which has no blemish, etc. This heifer comes for merit, in order to bring merit to the Assembly <note>the assembly - representing the Sefirah of Malchut, the Divine Presence</note> which is near. • Male to male to make wise. The heifer of the grave from the impurity that is spoken of regarding the "shards of earthenware." • Danger hangs over it, and words were meant for the sick. The secret of the whole, and the elders of the secret of the exits: this heifer is Metatron <term>Metatron - the highest angel, often serving as a heavenly mediator</term> belonging to the side of Severity <term>Gevurah - the divine attribute of Judgment and Restraint</term>. It is a protective amulet against the gaze of the "Samael" <note>the Accuser/Satan</note>, appearing like a rose. As it is written: from the side of Lovingkindness <term>Chesed - the divine attribute of Mercy and Expansion</term> it rises to the foot for a blessing below... so too the engravings. Red signifies the decree of Judgment. • Whole: according to the beginning and the end, it is whole. • Which has no blemish • What does "whole" mean? As we say, the secret of the "Simple/Perfect" <note>Tam</note> from the side of labor, to be afflicted from the side of the letter Aleph... the secret of the "Simple" is a weak judgment. • A yoke: from the side of the Upper Shekhinah <note>Divine Presence</note>, for there are no voices there... the end of the whole is "whole," where the judgment of the Foundation <note>Yesod</note> rules. • And a yoke of battle is not there... from the side of the lower weak Severity, for she is "whole." • To that side, there is no Accuser, no Destroyer, and no Angel of Death, for that is the Upper Severity, which is a harsh judgment... from the side of the sacrifices. Until here <note>end of section</note>. • In a strong statute. • Which has no blemish in it:

> You are all beautiful, my love, and there is no blemish in you <note>Song of Songs 4:7</note>

• Upon which no yoke has come • "Yoke" is written as "Kallah" (Bride/Finished)... because it is the completion of darkness and conversation... "Upon which no yoke has come" is as it is written:

> A virgin of Israel, a virgin whom no man had known <note>Reference to Genesis 24:16</note>

## Main Text (Zohar) Continued

**And you shall give** it to Eleazar • The deputy priest... they established it. It reaches him and not Aaron. Why? Because Aaron is the "best man" of the Matronita <term>Matronita - the Divine Mother or Shekhinah</term>. Furthermore, Aaron does not come from the side of "Pure" but from the side of "Holy." Because this [the heifer] comes for purification, it was not given to him. Every matter that comes... was in seven washings. This is said because the "Good Knife" is called "Bathsheba" (Daughter of Seven), and all its works are in sevens. • Come and see: everything that is done... is in order to purify and not to sanctify. It is done for free; he does not slaughter and does not burn, so that Judgment does not conclude on its sides. Every Aaron is pressed into a degree... to be covered there and to look there. • This heifer, once it is made into ash, one must cast into it cedar wood, hyssop, and crimson wool. These have been explained. • Lovingkindness is "Pure" but not "Holy." • And it was "outside the camp" in a pure place, for it is only called so from the side of the "Impure Side" <note>the Sitra Achra or forces of evil</note> at first. The mystery of the whole is that which is written: "it is a water of sprinkling, it is a sin offering." Because all lower judgments and all those that come from the Impure Side, when the moon is opened... and from the side it is called and sits... a blow of the pulse is liable. Then they are all removed (aroused) and they depart and vanish from the world. Once they perform this act below, and all these judgments after the ash of the heifer, they cast upon it cedar wood...

<meta>This page continues the Zohar's mystical commentary on the Torah portion Chukat, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of purification and the flow of divine vitality. ## Main Text (Zohar)

...Cedar wood, etc. Then the power of the tongue is sanctified, and in every place where they [the forces of impurity] used to gather, they now fold their wings and flee because this word of theirs is hidden. In this manner, they do not gather at all and one is purified. And it is called **waters of purification** <note>Hebrew: *Mei Niddah*</note>, for these are waters that the whole world rises through, while the side of impurity <term>Sitra Achra; the "Other Side" or realm of evil</term> spreads through the world. Here, all types of impurity and all types of purity are included, and because of this, impurity and purity lead the world to freedom, as the companions have established. Cedar wood and hyssop—do this so that the companions shall not have cause to speak after you.

Rabbi Isaac opened his discourse and said:
> "He sends forth springs into the valleys..." <note>Psalms 104:10</note>

"...they flow between the mountains." All the "beasts of the field" <note>original: *chayto sadai*</note> drink from them. This verse was spoken by King David through the Holy Spirit, and one must look deeply into them. Come and see: the mystery of Higher Wisdom <term>Chokhmah; the second Sephirah and source of divine intuition</term>, though it is engraved and hidden on all sides, opens and draws from itself a single path. This word is guarded by two higher ones in the springs of the source of the "Flow of the Monkey" <note>original: *mazal kofa*; a cryptic Kabbalistic reference to a specific channel of divine influence</note> from which everything comes. From there, pure springs are drawn out and shine to every side. Just as that thin, unknown point drips and flows, that River flows and emerges, and from there springs and brooks are drawn out, filling the whole inhabited world with wisdom.

These are the high, holy rivers of the firmament that is within it, and they are all watered as one from that path of the high, holy word that emerges and flows to the Crown <term>Keter; the highest Sephirah</term>. And all the "beasts of the field" <note>original: *chayto shaddai*, though the text reads *sadai*</note> drink from them. This is what is written:
> "And from there it divided and became four heads." <note>Genesis 2:10</note>

So too, these hidden paths are the "beasts of the field" for all those sides and all those living creatures that desire the cover of the Almighty <note>original: *Shaddai*</note>. Do not read it as "field" <note>*sadai*</note> but as "Almighty" <note>*Shaddai*</note>, for He is the cessation and the spheres... <note>The text here uses dense wordplay between *Sadeh* (field) and *Shaddai* (Almighty) to explain how divine energy sustains even the lower realms</note>. These are the four "beasts of the Almighty," one for each side of the world, and they drink from those waters to receive each one. These are the spirits of those waters that go over them. And when they are watered from that Higher Source, all other things are watered, built, and established in their crowns. All of them return to known circles... "The birds of the sky dwell by them." These are the other higher levels... "The earth is satisfied from the fruit of Your works" <note>Psalms 104:13</note> below, and all the worlds are nurtured and blessed. This is the mystery of the blessing found in the depths of the River that is the source of all.

When the world returns to judgment, blessings are not found below in the world. Then the Sanctuary is destroyed, and many damaging spirits are found in the world, hovering in many places over human beings, and that spirit defiles them. Just as one who touches a corpse is defiled, so too does impurity rest upon anyone who approaches the "beasts":
> "You hide Your face, they are terrified..." <note>Psalms 104:29</note>

What does this verse speak of? It means: You hide Your face and they are terrified because they are not watered, and blessings are not found for the worlds. **"You take away their breath, they perish,"** and another spirit from the side of impurity is awakened, and a spirit of defilement rests upon people—upon those who have died. And for whoever takes hold of it, its radiance is struck down from the rest of humanity. This is why it is written: "...and they return to their dust." This is the "dust of the burnt sin-offering" <note>The Red Heifer</note> in order to be purified by it. This is the "Spirit of God" from the dust... to the Crown, returning to this dust to be purified by it. The spirit of defilement passes away, and another holy spirit is awakened in the world. This is what is written:
> "You send forth Your spirit, they are created... and You renew the face of the earth." <note>Psalms 104:30</note>

For purity exists below... and all the worlds are blessed. Happy is the portion of Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, gave them the counsel of the "remedy of all" so that they may merit the life of the World to Come and be found pure. Regarding the holiness of the World to Come, it is written of them:
> "I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean." <note>Ezekiel 36:25</note>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Chukat. It focuses on the symbolic deaths of the three siblings—Miriam, Aaron, and Moses—and how their departures represent the withdrawal of specific divine lights (the Well, the Cloud, and the Sun) from the world.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Chukat**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, meaning "Statute"</note>

**And they came**, the entire congregation, into the wilderness of Zin, etc. <note>Numbers 20:1</note> Rabbi Yehuda said: Come and see, the section of the Red Heifer <note>The *Parah Adumah* used for purification</note> is placed next to the death of Miriam. This has already been established, but because judgment was executed upon this heifer to purify, judgment was also executed upon this "virgin" <note>A mystical reference to the Shekhinah/Divine Presence associated with Miriam</note> and she departed from the world. Once Miriam departed, that Well <note>The miraculous "Well of Miriam" that followed the Israelites</note> which traveled with Israel in the wilderness also departed, and everything was removed as one. Rabbi Isaac said: It is written, *The daughter of Israel has fallen, she shall rise no more* <note>Amos 5:2; original: "Nafela lo tosif kum betulat Yisrael"</note>; this is a lamentation over the "Virgin of Israel." Is it only over her? No, but because everything is joined together in the likeness of the world below. Michael and Gabriel are as one, because she [the Shekhinah] draws near to the "Body" <note>The central Sefirah, Tiferet</note> so that it may be repaired through her. This is the "Spirit" of which it is written, *Your right hand and Your clouds.* The "Body" is that of which it is written, *I clothe the heavens with blackness* <note>Isaiah 50:3</note>, for the Sun was darkened because of her; in this same manner, *And Miriam died there,* etc. **And there was no** water for the congregation <note>Numbers 20:2</note>, for the "Judgment" <note>The source of the water/sustenance</note> had, as it were, departed from below. Afterward, the time arrived of which it is written, *And Aaron shall be gathered to his people,* and afterward the Sun of Moses was darkened, as it is written, *And die on the mountain... and be gathered to your people.* The voice of the "Right Arm" <note>Aaron, representing the attribute of Chesed/Kindness</note> was broken, and the "Body," which is the Sun <note>Moses, representing Tiferet/Beauty</note>, was darkened. And come and see: observe that there were none in the world like Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. And if you should say, "In the days of Solomon it was also thus," it was not so; for in the days of Solomon the Moon <note>The Shekhinah/Malkhut</note> was full and it was a time of building, but in the days of Moses the Moon was gathered in and peace was perfected. There were three siblings: Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. Thus, the staff of Aaron and Miriam goes to your children. Miriam is the Moon. Moses is the Sun. And Aaron is the Right Arm. Then the Left Arm returned. And some say it was Nachshon son of Amminadab as at first, when the Moon departed. With the death of Miriam, the Well departed; afterward, the Right Arm was removed (others say: below), which always draws near to the Moon as a statute, as a measure, and as a side. It is written, *And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took...* <note>Exodus 15:20</note> "The sister of Aaron" certainly, for he is the Arm that brings her near in joy and strength to the Body. Afterward, the Sun was gathered in and darkened, as we have established, for it is written, *And you also shall be gathered to your people.* And all of them—the departures of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam—were not [fully] found in the world [again]. In the days of Solomon, the Moon ruled in her perfection and was seen in the world. And Solomon was established in the Wisdom <note><term>Chokhmah</term>: The divine attribute of Wisdom</note> of her covering, and it shone in the world. Since the Moon below was like a merit, it provided nourishment and struck after a time until it became entangled in the "Western Horn" and no more, so that there should be no danger to the outsiders. Blessed is the portion of Moses, the Faithful Prophet <note><term>Naya Mehemna</term>: A traditional title for Moses</note>. It is written, *The sun rises and the sun sets...* <note>Ecclesiastes 1:5</note> We have established this verse. "The sun rises"—this refers to when Israel went out of Egypt, for the Sun shone and not the Moon. "And pants toward its place"—it is written "and the sun sets" as a reminder of the dawn of those who died in the wilderness; once the Sun went, it went to the place where it is gathered, "to its place," in order to give light to the Moon. "Pants and rises"—that is the name of Judgment that is gathered, and "rises" is certainly the name, for the Moon does not shine except from the light of the Sun. And this is the "Spirit" of which it is written, *It goes toward the south and turns toward the north* <note>Ecclesiastes 1:6</note>, for it does not cease to exist but remains to give light to the Moon. So it is with the Staff, and concerning this it is written, *What profit has a man in all his labor...* <note>Ecclesiastes 1:3</note> "What profit has a man in all his labor"—this refers to Joshua, who strove to give Israel the inheritance of the land, but did not merit to give the Moon its inheritance as was proper, for he lived for his people who were in Israel "under the Sun" of Moses. Come and see that shame and that reproach, because he served and did not follow after Him [God] directly, but rather "under the Sun," and he had no light of his own, but only the light that was reflected to him. If so, what benefit did he have, since he did not go here or there? And in every place where Solomon said "under the sun," he was speaking of his own level, which is "under the sun." And further proof: "under the sun" is his dwelling, and this is "under..."

<meta>This page continues the Zohar’s mystical commentary on the Book of Numbers, specifically the portion of Chukat. The discourse focuses on King Solomon’s words in Ecclesiastes (Kohelet), interpreting the physical world "under the sun" as a veil for the spiritual mechanics of the Sefirot (divine emanations).</meta>

# Chukat

## Main Text (Zohar)

"Under the sun"—and so it says regarding all his times—but this is certainly not the Spirit of the Master of All. And see, it is written:
> What profit has a man in all his labor which he labors **under the sun**? <note>Ecclesiastes 1:3</note>
Certainly. And see, regarding "under the sun," one might say this refers to "this side" <note>the material or lower realm</note>. And see, from one perspective, all his praise is for his labor under the sun for life, and this is the truth of the world. For what profit is there to a man in all his labor for the "First Kindness" <note>Chesed</note>, and likewise for all those second to it that stand like the Crown of the Letter *He*?
> It goes toward the south, and turns about unto the north... <note>Ecclesiastes 1:6</note>
As it is written: "From His right hand went a fiery law for them," and His right hand is the **South**. "Fiery law" is the **North**, and this is included in that: "the spirit whirls about continually." This verse is difficult: it should have said "the spirit whirls about and goes," so why does it say "the spirit goes"? Which spirit? This is the one "under the sun" which is called the <term>Holy Spirit</term> <note>Ruach ha-Kodesh</note>. What is this spirit that goes and circles to these two sides found in the Body? And regarding this, it is written "The Holy Spirit," through which the "Sun" is known generally, which is the portion of Israel. And see, the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence</note> is in twenty spirits. Who is the Shekhinah? These are the Sages who are the <term>Holy Chariot</term> <note>Merkavah; the spiritual structure that carries the Divine Presence</note>. They are three, and a generation, and four spirits found in them; they are the Inner Holy Chariot. And regarding this, it is written: "The wise man whispers"—the intention was the breath of his mouth, because all the appointments of the King are hidden in **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note>, and all are within the foundation of the Holy Palace. Human beings do not gaze upon them, and his appointments appear like words... how praiseworthy is it to reveal the King in His wisdom from the side of the assembly. Rather, certainly, every word of the King is hidden, hidden in Wisdom.

He opened and said:
> Wisdom is good with an inheritance, and a profit to those who see the sun. <note>Ecclesiastes 7:11</note>
Look, for we have learned a matter that seems without reason, and I do not know what it means. "Wisdom is good"—this is the Wisdom that exists "under the sun," prepared for the Throne. "Wisdom is good with an inheritance"—this is the side of the "Depths of Israel," who are all joined to it through their deeds. However, it is found to be "more a profit to those who see the sun"—to those who merit to be crowned by the Sun and to be bound to the Holy One, Blessed Be He. It is as precious as gold, and whoever takes hold of it lives in the life of this world and the life of the world to come. And this is what is written:
> And the profit of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to those who possess it. <note>Ecclesiastes 7:12</note>
What is "the profit of knowledge"? This is Life. And what is its "profit"? It is certainly Wisdom, for the Torah emerged from <term>Wisdom</term> <note>Chokhmah; the second Sefirah</note>. Furthermore, "Wisdom is good with an inheritance"—Wisdom is certainly with an inheritance, which is the <term>Tzadik</term> <note>The Righteous One; referring to the Sefirah of Yesod</note> of the world, who is the source of its praise. For these levels sit as one, and this is their <term>Sefirah</term> <note>Radiance/Emanation</note>. For all "profit to those who see the sun" refers to those who gaze upon it through the Sun, the strength of all, the praise of all. And this is the Knowledge <note>Da'at</note> of all, which is life, as it is established:
> Also, that the soul be without knowledge is not good. <note>Proverbs 19:2</note>
Who is this "soul"? This is the soul of King David, which is the Wisdom we mentioned. And because of this, "the profit of knowledge is wisdom," for from there the Tree is rooted and planted to all sides, and so to all those who take hold of it in this way. And regarding this, King Solomon was found only in this, his level, from which he knew everything. And he said further:
> I returned and saw under the sun... <note>Ecclesiastes 9:11</note>
And so with all of them. Fortunate are the righteous who toil in the Torah and know the ways of the Holy King and the supernal secrets hidden in the Torah, as it is written:
> For the ways of the Lord are right... <note>Hosea 14:10</note>

---

## Additional Text Section

**And he gathered:**
> That which is crooked cannot be made straight... <note>Ecclesiastes 1:15</note>
Rabbi Hiyya opened and wrote:
> Consider the work of God; for who can make straight what He has made crooked? <note>Ecclesiastes 7:13</note>
See, all the works of the Holy One, Blessed Be He, are justice and truth, and there is no one who can diminish them or strike His hand and say to Him, "What have You done?" For He does all according to His will. And praise be to the Creator.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Chukat. It focuses on the spiritual status of the righteous after death, specifically interpreting verses from Ecclesiastes (Kohelet) through the lens of the Zohar's cosmology. It connects the "dead" mentioned by Solomon to those who have achieved a higher spiritual state.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Chukat**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, meaning "Statute."</note>

"The dead," etc. King Solomon was wiser than the living, yet they are only called "dead" because they follow the path of truth in this world. As it is said: "As their names, so they are known." <note>A common Zoharic idiom suggesting that a person's essence is reflected in their title.</note> Indeed, the companions have established that a wicked person who does not walk in the path of truth is called "dead" even while alive, while the poor man is considered dead to the living. But certainly, all the words of King Solomon were spoken with Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: the second Sephirah, representing divine intuition</term>. It has been said: "Happy is he." Regarding "the dead"—if it were not written further, I would have said so; but since it is written, **"who have already died,"** <note>Ecclesiastes 4:2</note> another matter of Wisdom is found here. "Who have already died" implies they have departed from the world at another time and were prepared like the dust <insert>prepared for it and dwelling in the life of the world</insert>.

---

**[Two Parallel Text Blocks]**
<note>These columns contain fragmented mystical variations on the theme of judgment and the soul's refinement.</note>

| Left Column | Right Column |
| :--- | :--- |
| After they depart, from him dies and lives this fool | This is what is said: he dies and dies at the time he is prepared |
| The dead of the world are surrounded and he sits for judgment and strikes | In the place where they depart, and from them the dead arose and rejoiced at the end |
| It is said in that world, as it is written: "It shall not arise" | The end from the side of the world's sleepers, and he sits for judgment and strikes |
| Times (his lamp) when they received punishment and were struck | It is said in that world, behold it is written: "It shall not arise," etc. |
| And two certainly, and he rejoiced for him to be prepared as a righteous man | |

...more than the living who have not yet received their punishment. And regarding this, it is written: **"And I praised the dead who have already died."** Precisely so! These are the living, yet they are called "dead" for this reason: because they have tasted the taste of death. Even though they exist in this world, they are called "dead," and the righteous are called "dead" <note>This refers to the mystical idea that the righteous "die" to their physical desires while still alive.</note>. Furthermore, all their previous deeds stand for them <unclear>openly</unclear> and they are called "dead." "More than the living who are still alive" <note>Ecclesiastes 4:2</note>—for those have tasted the taste of death but have not received their punishment, nor do they know the life of that world.

Come and see: the righteous who merit to be bound in the **Bundle of Life** <term>Tzeror ha-Chayyim: the treasury of souls under the Divine Throne</term> merit to behold the supernal glory of the Holy King, as it is said: **"To behold the graciousness of the Lord and to visit His temple."** <note>Psalms 27:4</note> Their dwellings are higher and loftier than all the holy angels and all their levels. For that supernal place <insert>the Holy Mouth</insert> neither the higher nor lower beings merit to see, as it is written: **"No eye has seen a God besides You."** <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>

And those who do not merit as much in the vision they merit below, receive according to their portion. These do not merit to ascend to that place and see as the ones above see; these remain in their standing in the **Lower Eden** <term>Gan Eden ha-Tachton: the earthly or lower paradise</term> and no more. And if you ask: what is this Lower Eden? It is the Eden called **Lower Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah Tata’ah: associated with the Shekhinah or the feminine aspect of Divinity</term>. This stands over the Garden of the Throne. What is the difference between the Lower and Upper Eden? The difference is in the "vision from behind the veil." This Lower Eden is called the "Female Eden," while the **Upper Eden** is called the "Male Eden," concerning which it is written: "No eye has seen a God besides You."

This Lower Eden is called "a Garden for Eden" <note>original: "Gan le-Eden"</note>. See how they are found in the Lower Garden to be restored by this Eden that flows out every Sabbath and every New Moon, as it is written: **"And it shall be from month to month and from Sabbath to Sabbath."** <note>Isaiah 66:23</note> Regarding these, Solomon said: "More than the living who are still alive" <note>Ecclesiastes 4:2</note>, for these are of a higher degree than all of them. They are those who have "already died" and received punishment twice; they are called **"refined silver"** that has entered the furnace <term>Kura: a smelting pot used as a metaphor for spiritual purification</term> twice and emerged from it pure and clarified.

**"But better than both is he who has not yet been,"** <note>Ecclesiastes 4:3</note> for that spirit is holy above and was delayed far below, for he stands in his existence and does not have to receive punishment, nor does he have the debt of that supernal death.

<summary>This page explores the Zoharic interpretation of Ecclesiastes, distinguishing between the "dead" (the righteous who have purified their souls) and the "living" (the wicked or unrefined). It describes the hierarchy of the afterlife, specifically the distinction between the Male/Upper Eden and the Female/Lower Eden.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The upper half is exalted, and better than all is he who is neither separated nor revealed, and all his portions are in holiness. To merit this is to be a righteous, pious man <note>Aramaic: *chassida*</note> who guards the commandments of the Torah and fulfills them, laboring in the Torah day and night. He is not merely occupied with learning but is turned toward a higher level above all other human beings, and all desire (<note>Another version: are attached to</note>) the beauty of such a person. Come and see: at the hour when the Holy One, Blessed Be He, said to Moses, *“Aaron shall be gathered to his people”* <note>Numbers 20:24</note>, Moses was filled with a great trembling. He knew that his own "right arm" <note>A reference to Aaron representing the Sefirah of Chesed/Mercy</note> was being broken, and his whole body felt the distress. When the Holy One, Blessed Be He, said to Moses, *“Strip Aaron [of his garments]”* <note>Numbers 20:26</note>, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, brought down a balance of awe and trembling upon him. Yet he stripped Aaron... and Aaron the Pious was concerned for Eleazar his son, and through this, he merited to see the [spiritual] image of his son. Until that moment, his strength had not weakened, for the Clouds of Glory <note>The divine protection that surrounded Israel in the desert</note> departed and did not return except through the merit of Moses, and not through the merit of Eleazar.

**And Moses did** as the Lord commanded... <note>Numbers 20:27</note> showing this before the eyes of the entire congregation. This was so that they would know that Aaron, the holy one of the nation, was more beloved than all, and they should not say that he was disgraced by the hand of Moses. Moses comforted Aaron with words until they ascended the mountain, and all of Israel watched at the hour when Moses stripped the garments from Aaron and placed them upon Eleazar. Why Moses and not Aaron? Rather, Moses had clothed Aaron when he first ascended to the High Priesthood, placing them beneath the portion of the Robe. Now, Moses stripped from him what he had given him, and before him, he removed what he had bestowed. Both of them stripped Aaron of everything, and Moses removed the memory and hidden things before him. Before he was stripped, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, spread a garment of light to replace the portion Moses removed. For all the portions of the righteous are prepared by the Holy One, Blessed Be He. The Holy One, Blessed Be He, prepared a bed for Aaron and a lamp that burned as one, and from his own [light] he kindled that flame which burns every day and twice [daily]. Then the mouth of the cave was sealed, and they descended. Rabbi Judah said: The mouth of the cave remained open so that all Israel could see Aaron lying there, and by the merit of the cave, a light burned before him, and his bed was elevated and lowered, and a single cloud stood over him. Then Israel knew that Aaron had died, and they saw that the Clouds of Glory had departed. This is what is written: <term>And when all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead...</term> <note>Numbers 20:29</note> Come and see, the sages established that they wept for Aaron—the entire House of Israel, men, women, and children—for he was the beloved of them all. Rabbi Simeon said: These three holy, exalted siblings were not bound as one; one was set here, one there, and one in another place. Rather, they appeared together so that the clouds of Israel would be found [protecting them] when each one died, to shield them and to be endangered for them. Each one died as was fitting for them: Miriam in Kadesh, between the North and the South; Aaron on the "Right Side" <note>The side of Mercy</note>; and Moses as was fitting for him. That mountain [of Moses] was joined to the mountain of Aaron, and the burial place of Miriam was gathered to that mountain which is joined on two sides. For this reason, it is called <term>Mount Abarim</term> <note>Literally "Mountain of the Passages" or "Sides"</note> because the two sides of the mountain pass through and join this side and that side. All these are the portions of the righteous in this world and the world to come. It joins to the time to come as one, as we have said: in the Higher World to come, their merit stands in this world for the life of the generations. And in the hour when the mountain [the people] returns in repentance before the Holy One, Blessed Be He, and a decree is issued against them, then the Holy One, Blessed Be He, calls to the righteous who stand before Him to serve, and informs them; they nullify that decree, and the Holy One, Blessed Be He, has compassion upon Israel. Concerning these righteous ones, it is written: *“And the Lord shall guide you continually...”* <note>Isaiah 58:11</note>.

**And the people spoke** against God and against Moses... <note>Numbers 21:5</note> This section follows immediately after the matter of the Waters of Contention <note>Mei Merivah</note> involving Moses and Aaron. Rabbi Isaac opened [his discourse]: *“And it came to pass on the eighth day...”* <note>Leviticus 9:1</note>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Chukat, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of speech, the judgment of the fiery serpents, and the esoteric nature of the Well of Miriam. It maintains the Zoharic style of alternating between Hebrew scripture and Aramaic explanation.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Chukat [Statutes]** <-

And their King to the crown of the Kingdom <note>original: *Malchut*</note> etc. • A hidden birth in the Holy Spirit <note>original: *Ruach HaKodesh*</note> is desired, and for this reason it is written between the lines • And it was when the Philistines gathered to rectify the matter of the presence, and behold, it stands in the spirit as a whole, falling then, and their King to the hidden Kingdom • What is this Kingdom? If you say it is a Kingdom of glory and joy, it is not so, for it investigates the nights • In the hiddenness of the Kingdom that is clothed in the Supernal Holy Kingdom, and for this, the Holy Spirit is written • What is the reason it is written in this place? Because he guarded his mouth so as not to desecrate the edges of life, the hidden birth and its joy; for anyone who guards his mouth and his tongue etc. is clothed in the Holy Spirit • And anyone who desires to fill his mouth with it, and this is an evil word against Him • And he lives for them, for he loathes the knowledge of those who were burned by the serpent because of it, and behold its wisdom:

> **And the people spoke against God and against Moses** <note>Numbers 21:5</note>

• For they spoke an evil word, and its translation is: "and the people contended with Moses," saying "why have you brought us up?" They were all turning their faces toward destruction, to be burned like chaff, and the eye was there to observe them. And because of this, they all died, as it is written: <insert>And the Lord sent</insert> **the fiery serpents** • Why this language? They were serpents that came with fire in their mouths, biting and killing • What is "with fire"? It means the serpent's light is entirely consumed. Why did they sin? It was fire in their mouths, biting and scattering, a curse was in them and their innards were burned, and their deaths were full of weapons, departing to another place •

**And from there** to the Well; that is the Well etc. For here it says "to the Well" <note>original: *Be'erah* - with a feminine suffix</note> and later "Well" <note>original: *Be'er*</note> is not written. After the waters were gathered into the sea, it is written below, after the time of Isaac, who filled it with redness; "Well" is what is written. And this spirit is as it is written: "And the Levite, he shall perform the service" <note>original: *v'avad ha-Levi hu*</note> • Rabbi Chasda said: In every place it is "He" <note>original: *Hu* - masculine</note> but we read it as "She" <note>original: *Hi* - feminine</note>, for Male and Female are as one, and all of them are the Supernal "H" <note>The letter Heh, representing the feminine Shekhinah</note>, Female and Male together, for the "A" <note>The letter Aleph</note> is in perfection. Worthy are the Israelites who are below, for they have the strength to be in the likeness of the Supernal form of all. And because of this it is written: "He has made us, and not we ourselves" <note>Psalm 100:3</note>; it is written thus because it includes everything • Rabbi Shimon said: The spirit of the waters, this is the Holy Spirit that was written at first • Then the prophet came to the crown because of the water, to fill the bride. He calls out: "Take the spirit and sprinkle the water." He takes the spirit first and afterwards sprinkles the water. And as long as this spirit is not written, the waters do not flow. What does this teach us? That the Bride <note>The Shekhinah/Kingdom</note> needs to be awakened by a word at the beginning, and so too with a word below to rectify it, like the appearance of the deed • And here, as long as the spirit is not written, the waters do not flow, because that spirit is the Well; "It is the Well" <note>original: *Hi ha-Be'er*</note> we read • Why at first "to the Well" <note>*Be'erah*</note> and now "Well" <note>*Be'er*</note>? Rather, at first it was the Female in her measure, and now that it says "He," it is the inclusion of Male and Female investigated as one. And after the Male is repeated to the mouth, the word is Female, and so we read it for the Bride • Rabbi Chamya said: Why did the people stop? Because this Well did not depart from them • And if you say, how could they sin against it? Rather, it was like a mouth for the twelve tribes, and they were humbled and filled, and it went out to all sides • And then the Israelites, in the hour when they were lacking and needed water, stood over it and sang a song. And what did they say?

> **Spring up, O well; sing you unto it** <note>Numbers 21:17</note>

To bring forth water for the Bride, and to bring it forth from You. And so they said praise to this Well after the lack of the eunuch etc. • They spoke a word of truth, and so it is • Open the teaching: anyone who desires to awaken matters from Above, whether through action or through speech • If that praise or that word is not performed as is fitting, nothing is awakened • All the people of the world, they did not merit in that to awaken the word from Above • There are only a few who know how to awaken it. And the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>term: *Kudsha Brich Hu* - the standard Zoharic name for God</note>, is close to all, but if one does not know how to call to Him, He is not close, as it is written:

> **The Lord is near to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth** <note>Psalm 145:18</note>

• What is "all in truth"? Those who know the word of truth as is fitting, and so too the Bride • Here too, they spoke, and Israel spoke words of truth in order to awaken them •

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the Torah portion Chukat, focusing on the spiritual mechanics of prayer and the specific historical-mystical encounter between Moses and Og, the King of Bashan.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...to them in their hands, and to depart from Israel, and until they were banned, they did not awaken. And so it is even in the vision of the sorcerers' images, who look at various colors until they perform the acts of truth for their prophets, so that the words of truth do not awaken because they are found in these colors that they require; they are not made for their prophets. And even from the side of all lewdness, like other counts, the wisdom of the "Other Side" <note>The Sitra Achra, or the realm of spiritual impurity</note> does not look upon their prophets forever and they do not awaken toward them. Come and see, it is written:

> And they called upon the name of Baal etc. <note>1 Kings 18:26</note>

What is the reason? First, that they had no authority over that Baal at that hour, for the words were not proper in their eyes, and they thought that the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> was testing their kindness, and this is what covered the altars from you. Happy are the righteous who know how to call upon their Master properly. **Rabbi Shimon** said: Everything depends on the eye of the full light. Come and see: anyone who knows how to seek the deed properly and to arrange words properly, they certainly awaken toward him to find supernal matters for their prophets. And they give to all the world those who know how to arrange praise and arrange words. What is the "goodness" <term>Chatibu: a term for divine favor or beauty</term> of the righteous? It is that they know the root of the matter and the deed, and they know how to direct the heart and the will more than those others who do not know as much. However, those who do not know the root of the deed, all of this is merely an arrangement and no more; they do not merit the "goodness" of the crown on the shoulders of the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, who does not gather them in as a burden <note>The text suggests that mechanical prayer without intention is a burden to the Divine, whereas intentional prayer is an ornament</note>. But those who know and direct the heart and the will, they bring forth blessings from the place of Thought <note>The Sephirah of Chokhmah or Binah</note>, and they go out in all colors and paths in a good manner properly, until the upper and lower worlds are blessed. And from this supernal holiness, they are blessed by their hands. Happy is their portion, for the **Holy One, Blessed be He** is close to their prophets and is ready for them at the moment they call Him. He is ready for them at the hour of their vision in distress; He honors them in this world and in the world to come. This is what is written:

> Because he has set his love upon Me, therefore I will deliver him; I will set him on high, because he has known My name. <note>Psalm 91:14</note>

**And he said:** "Alas, my lord, lay not the sin upon us, wherein we have done foolishly," etc. **Rabbi Yehuda** opened:

> She is not afraid of the snow for her household; for all her household are clothed with scarlet. <note>Proverbs 31:21</note>

Come and see: the **Assembly of Israel** <term>Knesset Yisrael: the spiritual personification of the Jewish people, often identified with the Sephirah of Malkhut</term> is called from two sides: through Mercy <term>Rachamim</term> and through Judgment <term>Dina</term>. As it is written, when He desires, He is called with Mercy. Mercy is found in a place to be found in. When He desires to nourish with Judgment, a place is found to be found in and to watch over it. For so it is in every place; the word from above is not lacking until a place is found to watch over it. And concerning the Assembly of Israel, "she is not afraid of the snow for her household," why? Because "all her household are clothed with scarlet" <note>The Hebrew "Shanim" (scarlet) is interpreted here as "Shenayim" (two), referring to the two attributes of Mercy and Judgment</note>. He does not spare the secret... and so the **Holy One, Blessed be He** established it. It is written: "And he said: Alas, my lord, lay not the sin upon us." Others are complete in their purity in two kinds, this one and that one, until the head takes hold... What is the reason? Because they are the actual sign, until the head takes hold of your actual heat. See that he wants to explain that sign of that weight... This is Og, who was left like a shard, and the King of the House of God... and every furnace of a shard. What is written? "And all the giants of his house" etc. This is Og, who was crowned with his people. And the voice of that Holy One, since he saw Og that Israel was approaching him, he said: "Surely he is ready to approach," and he wanted to oppose him. Moses was afraid: how could he uproot the "seal" <term>Retima: a spiritual mark or seal of protection</term> that was cast like a shard? He said: "This is the right hand of my judgment," for the right hand requires purity. See, here is Eleazar... and it is not mine, and it appeared to the right hand... The **Holy One, Blessed be He** said: **"Fear him not"** <note>Numbers 21:34</note>. Do not fear that sign of his judgment, and even of the right hand do not fear. "For I have delivered him into your hand." Your power shall uproot him from the world, for his seal is flawed. And one who is flawed, you have the power to fix him by uprooting him from the world. By your power, he is pressed, and he shall be uprooted from the world by his words.

<meta>This page marks the conclusion of the Torah portion Chukat and the beginning of the portion Balak. It transitions from the military victories of Israel over the Amorites to the mystical and occult preparations of Balak, King of Moab.</meta>

# Balak

[The Amorite kings] were uprooted from the world, and their strong refuge was brought low. Their men were struck down, and now [the nations] feared for their very lives at the hand of Moses. Because of this, they all gathered together—Sihon and all his people and all that was his, as it is written:
> *And they struck him, and his sons, and all his people* (Numbers 21:35)
<note>The Hebrew text notes a variant reading: the written word lacks the letter 'Yod' (vav-tav-vav), but we read it as 'his sons' (vav-tav-yod-vav). The companions of the Zohar have established this tradition.</note>
Fortunate are Israel, for the Holy Assembly <note>The Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> comes for their sake. The Holy One, blessed be He, performed all these signs for them to remove the threat of death. The Holy One, blessed be He, did not break His covenant with the patriarchs, and now He connects Himself even with Israel, who are His children, for a blessing. As it is written: *“And your friend's son to scorch for the generation, an eternal covenant.”* <note>This appears to be a mystical interpretation of a proverb or local idiom regarding lineage and protection.</note> And it is written:
> *“As for Me, this is My covenant with them,” says the Lord: “My Spirit which is upon you... shall not depart from your mouth...”* (Isaiah 59:21)
-> **Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen.** <-

---

-> ### Portion of Vayera Balak <note>“And Balak Saw”</note> <-

**And Balak** the son of Zippor saw, etc. Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse: *And he saw.* What secret did he see? He saw a secret through the strength of wisdom <term>Chokhmah: The sefirah of Wisdom, often associated with deep insight or, in this context, occult knowledge</term>. And what did he see with his eyes? He saw through the strength of wisdom, as it is written: *“Your god abandoned your vineyard, the king of the Philistines through the window.”* <note>A reference to the mother of Sisera looking through the window in Judges 5:28, used here to explain mystical "vision."</note> What is meant by "through the window"? They all look through the window, like the mother of Sisera who peered and wailed. This "window" is surely the window of wisdom. For there are celestial windows for the stars, and there are windows of wisdom. There is one specific window where all wisdom dwells, and through it, one sees what is at the very root. Here too, *“And Balak saw”*—he saw through his own wisdom.

*The son of Zippor* <note>Zippor means "Bird" in Hebrew.</note>. As we have said, everything regarding the "son of the bird" is significant. For his secrets were conducted at times by using a metal bird <note>original: "k'tul tzippor"</note> engraved with herbs, fluttering in the air. He would perform certain deeds and whisper incantations to a snake, and that bird would come with a cloud in its mouth, fluttering before him. It would go to a certain sorcerer who offered incense before it, and it would show him many things. It would flutter its body, fly, and soar before his eyes to inform him of things.

Come and see: all of Balak's tools were centered on that bird. One day, he performed his rituals and took that bird, and it flew away but did not return. He was distressed in his soul until it finally came back. He saw a flame of fire flying after it, singeing its wings. Then he saw what he saw, and he became afraid and trembled. Why? Because he saw the bird standing there and he recognized the vision. All those who served that bird did not know its secrets as well as Balak did. All the wisdom that could be known through that bird, he knew.

When he would perform his divinations before it and offer incense, he would cover his head. He would whisper to it... <note>The text here describes a complex ritual involving seventy repetitions and the bird flying back and forth.</note> Then he became greatly afraid, as it is written: *“And Moab was sore afraid of the people, because they were many”* (Numbers 22:3). The word "Many" <note>Hebrew: Rav</note> refers to a great master of sorcery.

In earlier days, they would make this bird out of a mixture of gold and silver. The head was of gold, the mouth of silver, the wings of polished copper mixed with silver. The body was gold with silver spots, and the legs were gold. They would place weapons in its mouth, for the tongue of that bird was known [to be magical]. They would place that bird in a certain window, opening it toward the sun. At night, they would open it toward the moon. They would offer incense and perform deeds, bowing down before it...

<summary>This page concludes the narrative of Israel's victory over the Amorites and introduces the mystical background of Balak, King of Moab. It focuses on Balak's use of a magical mechanical bird (Tzippor) and occult "windows" of wisdom to perceive the threat posed by the Israelites.</summary>
<keywords>Balak, Zippor, Magic Bird, Occult Wisdom, Incense, Covenant, Moab, Sorcery</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion of Balak, specifically focusing on the spiritual conquest of the kings Sihon and Og as a precursor to the fear felt by Moab.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And this was divided seven times. From this point forward, that tongue <note>referring to the power of speech or a specific spiritual force</note> looks like the mouth of that serpent. Then, that tongue is like a serpent to look upon, and it speaks great things of its own accord, and it knows everything. Because this certainly went forth, *therefore it is said* <note>Numbers 21:27</note> and because of this, it speaks what another human being cannot know and cannot endure.

Rabbi Isaac said: It is found that there is darkness, and the darkness is a sea. We must observe why the faith of the Holy One, Blessed be He, consists of words of truth and faithfulness from Him. For once a word is spoken, everything is enacted and this goes forth to the outside. And there is much wisdom, and sometimes wisdom will depart from this vision according to its greatness; for in all worlds a word is a precious thing. So it is with the words of a man and the mixing of his thoughts according to the hour; so it is according to the hour of destruction, with rebuke and prayer, and with good deeds and many tears. They are the holy, supreme greatness over all worlds, a wealth of lights, and His holiness is gathered toward a man to perform the will of his Master. To sacrifice to another <note>referring to idolatry or the "Other Side"</note>, to strive and to awaken from here all those whose life was diminished by the wild beasts that devoured them. For example, in the world, there is a dwelling place where all life, great and small, are distant from one another. And a powerful wild ass <note>term: *Arad*, a type of wild desert creature often associated with demonic forces</note> is there. Og was among the wild asses of the desert, and his strength was mighty because he was a king here, such that all the kings of the world could not wage war because of the strength found here, and below he would strike and wage war with it. Sihon was the endurance and the breadth of the desert, and Moab relied upon him.

> *The border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites* <note>Numbers 21:13</note>

Come and hear: At the hour when Israel destroyed the land of Sihon, through the mystery that was performed in the Kingdom of Heaven, the ruling men over the other nations gathered and wondered how the kingdom of the Amorites was driven out. At that time, all those celestial powers <term>Shaltonin: angelic or demonic governors assigned to specific nations</term> who were appointed over the seven nations gathered and sought to restore the kingdom to its place. Once they saw the strength of Moses, they turned backward. *Therefore the rulers say, "Come to Heshbon"* <note>Numbers 21:27</note>. These are the celestial powers appointed over them to gather, and they said, "Come to Heshbon" <note>The Zohar plays on the word *Heshbon*, which means "calculation" or "account"</note>, calculating this judgment that drew near to him. *Let it be built and established* as it was at first, and let the kingdom return to its inhabitant. When they saw the might of Moses and the dominion of the Kingdom, they said:

> *For fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon* <note>Numbers 21:28</note>

Since it is written, "a flame from the city of Sihon," it implies that the city of Sihon was from Heshbon, as it is written:

> *For Heshbon was the city of Sihon, king of the Amorites* <note>Numbers 21:26</note>

The messenger of the King, whose name is *Kafak* <note>a cryptic angelic name</note>, said: "The time has arrived and is near." While they were saying, "Let the city of Sihon be built and established as yesterday," and they intended for Heshbon to be rebuilt for the dwelling of the Amorites, they then pleaded and said, "We cannot," because all their sorceries and all their wisdom failed against the strength of their Supreme Master. If we return to consider Heshbon being rebuilt, *behold, fire went out from Heshbon*. If we return to see the city of Sihon healed, *behold, a flame from the city of Sihon* certainly. Since that flame of fire is fixed there, no one can restore it to its former time, for from all sides we have no permission. From here on, see for yourself, Moab, that he who was a shield for you is broken. And because of this, once Moab saw that the strength of the tongue was broken, then:

> *And Moab was sore afraid of the people* <note>Numbers 22:3</note>

He was struck at once more than by death. *Because they were many*—for then he was great and numerous, as it is written:

> *Behold, I have made you small among the nations* <note>Obadiah 1:2</note>

And he was great in the land of Esau, as it is written of him, "and great." But because they saw and were shaken and trembled, as it is written:

> *All that Israel had done to the Amorites* <note>Numbers 22:2</note>

It should have said "what the people of Israel did." See, "all that" is included to encompass the Above and the Below. The yoke from Above, from their great celestial powers and ministers on high, and it covered their great powers and rulers below. And regarding "all that he did," it tells how great it is, following the great holy star of which it is written, "the stars of Israel." And the Living One, the Sustainer, the Holy One, Blessed be He, willed it so, and not from the "Other Side" <note>original: *Sitra Achra*, the realm of evil</note>. Once it went forth...

<summary>This page provides a mystical interpretation of Israel's victory over Sihon and Og, explaining that their defeat occurred first in the celestial realms among the "appointed powers" before manifesting on earth, which led to Moab's intense fear.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the spiritual trials of the soul, specifically focusing on the transition from the physical world to the Heavenly Academy. It draws heavily on the imagery of the High Priest Joshua from the Book of Zechariah as a model for the soul facing judgment.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Balak<-

That a shell <note>original: *kliffah*; refers to a spiritual husk or impurity that conceals holiness</note> emerges and does not pass; here it rests, the uncircumcision is found. Take to your heart the covenant of the Lord, etc. And upon it is the letter *Yod* from within, and to the Lord it shall be revealed afterward.

**And the Lord said** unto the Satan: "The Lord rebuke thee, O Satan," etc. <note>Zechariah 3:2</note> Rabbi Hiyya opened his discourse: "And he showed me Joshua the High Priest standing before the angel of the Lord," etc. <note>Zechariah 3:1</note> How much must a person <note>original: *bar nash*</note> guard himself in this world and mend his ways! For all the paths of a person are weighed and guarded; they stand open and demanding, seeking a pleasant scent. Judges stand to receive that which is hidden, and those who are pure of error and sight—whose sins are unknown—are supported so they shall not be looked upon. Look! For when a person spreads his hands before the world, how many times do accusers stand before him? And in the secret of what emerges—whether for good or for evil—it is according to what emerges from the mouth. Just as they are judged, so is a person judged in this world, both during his life and afterward. For all his words are in judgment. Yet the Holy One, Blessed be He, is always with mercy, and has mercy upon them all, for He does not desire judgment. Gather the deeds of the congregation, for thus said David: "If You, Lord, should mark iniquities, O Lord, who could stand?" <note>Psalms 130:3</note>. Here we must look: since it says "If You, Lord, should mark iniquities," Rabbi Hezekiah said: David mentioned two names of Mercy here. If iniquities or if kindnesses increase until they call out Above, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, sees that there was no mercy, and mercy did not gaze upon them—mercy and evil are like a fence to the closing of judgment, a level that follows him. And all deficiencies emerge from him; may He have pity on us and our words. "And if the Lord—who could stand?" Let us see who shall heal you then, for "your breach is great like the sea; who can heal you?" <note>Lamentations 2:13</note> until the Lord. And if these are hidden from you, who could stand? For all mercies are opened from Him. There, Joshua son of Jehozadak, a completely righteous man, entered into the innermost chambers to gaze upon the Heavenly Academy <note>original: *Metivta de-Raki'a*; the celestial study hall where souls and angels learn Torah</note>. A person is prophesied when the Academy is there to look into his judgment. And such is the way of the members of the Heavenly Academy: when they enter into judgment in the secret of the Priest, and mention all the children who are clothed in iniquity to return the hidden things. The court gathers and the spirit of a person is hidden as it enters, for two are sold because he entered before the pillar <note>original: *amuda*</note> that stands there to be gathered in the spirit of whiteness, as it is written regarding that pillar. And how many are those who ascend there! Because all those who labor in the Torah and sanctify themselves in it are immediately written for merit. The Academy is a shield in judgment; the members of the Academy are below and show it to him. And those two appointees emerge and examine him <margin>Correction: The Heavenly Academy</margin>. Immediately he approaches the inside of that pillar to be gathered there until the Academy forgives him. This is the meaning of "righteousness and life," for he is crowned with many crowns; all the members of the Academy crown him. But if it is another matter, and he belongs to that cup which they set outside, he is pushed inside the pillar until they bring him to the judgment of the appointee over time. And there are those whose wine ascends as a support, like the cups of the Academy. See who proves this: here is the portion of the merit from it; then they raise him there and merit that matter between the cup and the members of the Academy. And there are those whose wine they raise there for judgment, to clarify them and to make them merit. And another thing, etc. Behold, all who are meritorious, the person is released and departs from this world. And if he departs in such a manner, he is seen to be judged. And from all his companions, he said to him: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, has seen..." and thus I have heard, that certainly a herald proclaims: "A person [departs] from this world—Kindness!" Before he enters the Academy of the righteous, they raise him for judgment, and there he is judged in that Heavenly Academy. And there stands that appointee who punishes the "Side" <note>the *Sitra Achra* or the side of impurity</note> of them all. Whoever is acquitted from judgment, he lives. But for the one whom that appointee of punishment takes—he is nullified in his time, for they deliver him into his hands, and he is slung from there to below, "as a stone is slung out of a sling." <note>Allusion to 1 Samuel 25:29</note>
