<meta>This page continues the discourse on the spiritual forces of judgment and the character of Balak, transitioning into the famous narrative of the "Yanuqa" (The Child) of Kefar Sekhnin. This story is a cornerstone of Zoharic literature, emphasizing that spiritual wisdom can manifest in the young and that ritual precision (like washing hands) carries cosmic weight.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...a sling-stone <note>original: *kartifa* or *kustapira*</note>, as it is written: *“and the souls of your enemies, He shall sling them out as from the hollow of a sling”* <note>1 Samuel 25:29</note>.
And He plasters him into Gehenna <note>the place of spiritual purification/punishment</note> and he receives his punishment according to what was decreed. Come and see: *“And he showed me Joshua the High Priest standing before the angel of the Lord...”* <note>Zechariah 3:1</note>. The debate of that Heavenly Academy <note>original: *metivta*</note> regarding the reason he departed from this world: he entered before the angel of the Lord. This is that **Youth** <note>original: *Na'ar*, a title for the angel Metatron</note>, the Head of the Academy, who is Enoch; he decrees judgment upon all. And the Satan stands at his right hand to accuse them, so that they might descend to the depths. He stands constantly and says, "Give, give!" <note>demanding souls</note>; they stand ready for Gehenna. "To accuse him"—to mention his sins. Then it says: *“And the Lord said unto the Satan: The Lord rebuke thee, O Satan”* <note>Zechariah 3:2</note>. Why two rebukes? Rather, one is for Duma <note>the angel in charge of the souls of the dead</note> and one is for that one who doubles his efforts in Gehenna to stand constantly and weaken [the souls]. Come and see: the Supernal Satan is like a mountain, as they have established, who goes in the form of a mountain of fire. Evil spirits are prepared above because of them to strike them in a single moment; he snatches them in death and gives them to Duma to imprison them. And this is what is written: *“And Balak said unto the elders of Midian: Now shall this multitude lick up all that is round about us, as the ox licketh up...”* <note>Numbers 22:4</note>. A mountain that stands to swallow human beings. *“...the grass of the field”*—these are the living creatures of the field. That crack below makes it known. Rabbi Yose said: If so, it is written "all," for they do not watch him to know all the sorceries of that mountain, and a living man does not know and cannot perform his sorceries and divinations. Rabbi Yose said: Certainly it is so, he was proud and haughty. And the strength of that mountain is from when they dig to be painted with all life, and there are times when they call out, and all the times they call out the spirits of men. And those are evil days and days of strife...

---

**Rabbi** Isaac and Rabbi Judah were traveling on the road and reached a certain place called Kefar Sekhnin. They sought lodging in a house where there was a woman who had a son. Every day he would cry in his youth <note>or "at the break of day"</note>, and he would go up to the village school and return to his house. She saw those Sages and said to him [the child]: "Go down and draw near to these great men, and receive blessings from them." He drew near to them, but then did not draw near to arrange his speech. He said to her: "Mother, I do not want to draw near to them, for this day they did not recite the **Shema** <note>the central Jewish prayer: "Hear O Israel..."</note>. And thus have I been taught: anyone who does not recite the Shema in its proper time is under a cloud of rebuke all that day." They heard his voice, were shaken, and lowered their heads. They said: "Certainly it is so! This day we were occupied with the needs of a bride and groom who lacked what they needed; we were busy arranging their marriage and there was no one else to attend to them. So we busied ourselves with them and did not recite the Shema, for 'one who is occupied with a commandment is exempt from another commandment.'" They wondered at him: "How did you know?" He said to them: "By the scent of your garments I knew as you drew near to me." They were astonished, sat down, ate, and broke bread. Rabbi Judah’s hands were soiled, and he began the blessing before washing them. The child said to him: "If you are students of Rabbi Shimon [bar Yochai], you should have known that one must not bless with soiled hands. And one who blesses with filthy hands is liable for death!" That **Child** <note>original: *Yanuqa*</note> opened his discourse and said: *“When they go into the tabernacle of the congregation, they shall wash with water, that they die not”* <note>Exodus 30:20</note>. Therefore, if one who is not liable to appear before the King appears with filthy hands, he is liable for death. This is because the fingers of a human being dwell in the heights of the world. There is one finger that, when it is extended, is given over to the opening of the fear [of God]. It is written: *“And thou shalt make bars of shittim wood; five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the other side...”* <note>Exodus 26:26-27</note>. And it is written: *“And the middle bar in the midst of the boards shall reach from end to end”* <note>Exodus 26:28</note>. And if you say that the **Middle Bar** is something else, it is not so; it is within all of them, from the five. Not so, but that Middle Bar was within the five; there were two on this side and two on that side, and one stood alone—this was the **Middle Bar**, the Pillar of Jacob, the spirit that stands opposite...

<summary>The text discusses the spiritual mechanics of judgment and Gehenna before introducing the famous story of the Child of Kefar Sekhnin, who rebukes Sages for missing the Shema and for improper ritual washing.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the narrative of the "Yenuka" (the child prodigy) from the Zohar, Parashat Balak. The previous context involves the child astonishing visiting rabbis with his profound mystical insights into daily rituals.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Balak<-

Corresponding to this are the five fingers of every human being. In the hidden spirit, they are surrounded within, and upon them, everything else stands. These are the five runners <note>original: *rehitin*, referring to the channels of spiritual energy</note> called the five branches of the Tree of Life that flow through them. Through the Holy Spirit, he is awakened (**meaning** illuminated) in the folds of his fingers, and from there it is hidden. Regarding what you said, and regarding all the blessings that depend on those fingers: their explanation is that they extend over the hand. And by life! All of this is within them; there is no mention of His Name when blessing the Holy One, Blessed be He, except through them, for through them and all that comes from them, the Holy Name is blessed. And because of this, from the "Small Wisdom" <note>A reference to lower levels of mystical understanding</note> how is it that these things were not found? And they were not spread out to Rabbi Shimon’s companions. And he said: every gathering and every inclusion rises to the Side of Life, for the "Other Side" <note>The *Sitra Achra*, or the realm of impurity/evil</note> is filth and dirt, and the images of the "others" are a lie—emptiness—and they are unable to speak.

Rabbi Judah said: In the name of Enoch, how was it? The child <note>The *Yenuka*</note> remained silent for a moment, then stood before his father-in-law and kissed him. He saw him and said: "Show me your wisdom and teach me, and I will be your wise one and tell them." He saw him because he had acted righteously toward them. He saw him open [the discussion] properly, but it was not found to be as fitting as it should have been for his father-in-law. He turned back to them and saw him [the child] say: "You are mistaken regarding wisdom, and you have spared it from its proper place. Whenever the holy pious ones see the error of their crowns—by life! You are the high holy ones, how did you not find it? By life, you have erred in your crowns! Woe to the sight of your eyes, for you have opened your eyes but have not seen. Your heart (**meaning** my heart) is burdened with the First Crown to receive the yoke of the Torah. And since you did not merit that your heart should be burdened with your crowns, you did not see who is the wise one."

Rabbi Judah said to Rabbi Isaac: "It seems to us that this child is no ordinary human being." And that child was saying words of Torah and innovations of Torah, and they said: "Let us say Grace." He saw him and said: "You have certainly spoken well. Because the Holy Name is not blessed with this blessing except over a cup [of wine]." He opened and said:

> I will bless the Lord at all times, etc.
<note>Psalms 34:2</note>

And why did David begin by saying "I will bless the Lord"? Rather, David began because he required an "invitation" <note>*Hazmanah*—the formal preparation or summons to prayer</note> and said "I will bless" to show that wherever a person sits at a table, the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence</note> stands there, and the "Other Side" stands there as well. When a person invites another to bless, it is to subdue the Other Side, so that the Other Side is not included in the gathering. For if a person does not invite [others] to bless, the Other Side joins in and gathers to have a portion in that blessing. And by life! I wonder at the *Zohar* <note>The Radiance/Light</note> of the blessings, that they do not fear? Rather, it is from that portion which they bless that they [the holy sparks] are nourished.

And come and see that it is so: one blesses over that fruit and gives an invitation and blesses over it, and there is no portion for the Other Side. Before this, when that fruit was under the authority of the Other Side, they did not bless over it. And it is written:

> You shall not eat anything with the blood
<note>Leviticus 19:26</note>

But they bless over that fruit. And by life! The Other Side is blessed once it leaves its [the fruit's] authority; it is gathered in and they bless over it, and there is no [further] invitation for the blessing. And so it is with all the species of the world that they bless over; they are all an invitation to blessing, and there is no portion in them for the Other Side. And if you say: is it also thus for the Grace After Meals, that the Cup of Blessing was the invitation? Why is it so, and he blessed? He saw him and said: "Certainly! At first, when he was bread, he said the breaking of the bread was the invitation. But now for the Grace After Meals, we require a vessel for another invitation, for this cup belongs to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and not for physical nourishment." And in the manner that he performs the invitation, saying "Let us bless Him of whose food we have eaten," that was not the invitation [itself]; "Blessed be He of whose food we have eaten" is the blessing. So it is certainly, but he included another invitation. By their lives! The first invitation was the invitation for the Cup of Blessing, as it is taught. And regarding this cup, since he cast another invitation into it with the word of blessing toward the Upper World—from where all nourishment issues—it is also the Hidden Crown for the Hidden Upper World. And there is no invitation for it except through this level of the Cup of Blessing.

Rabbi Isaac said: "Fortunate is our portion that we are here."

***

## Main Text (Zohar)

In all the time of the world until now, I have not heard these words; certainly, I say that no man has engraved <note>or "comprehended"</note> them, etc.
He said to him: "Son, Angel of the Lord, His beloved, regarding that which you said:
> **"And you shall make the boards for the Tabernacle"** (Exodus 26:15)

From five for the boards of the rock of the Tabernacle, etc. And from this, in his spirit, to knowledge and what. He created them in a flash for the righteous, for all is known, those two. He said to him: "All this is what you said regarding the inner part of man, which I said, what is it to be struck? But a voice and a voice, and you did not find here to say." He opened and said:
> **"He has smeared their eyes from seeing"** (Isaiah 44:18) etc.

And does it say here the eyes of a man? Rather, by the permission of the King, as a body sees with its arm to bring forth Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: the sefirah of divine intuition</term> more than all the children of the world. Rather, the verse is certainly thus, as we have learned: "A man should not walk four cubits with an uncovered head." What is the reason? Because the Shekhinah <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence dwelling among humanity</term> rests upon his head. And anyone who covers his eyes and his garments on his head, they are like one who is offensive and stands over his head. And when his eyes are there, let him know that this light which is kindled upon his head needs to ascend, because the body of a man is like a wick <note>original: "karga," likely meaning a lamp-wick or vessel</note> and the light is kindled above. And King Solomon [spoke of] a window and wine and time at a distance, "let it not be lacking," for behold, the light that is on his head needs to ascend, and those are the good deeds. And regarding the one who covers his eyes on his head—not like another place. We have learned: the wise are pushed aside and the Shekhinah rests upon their heads. How did you not find this? It is written: "And the covering of their creation for the boards of the rock of the Tabernacle," and he said: "And from this in his spirit for the boards of the rock of the Tabernacle," which is like one and the second to one, the verses say. Third and fourth the verse does not say. For behold, the first and second do not stand on two sides, etc. He made and found from these two. We have learned: they and their ascent are as before. Rabbi Judah came and Rabbi Simeon said, and all is a portion. Blessed is the generation, for in your merit even the sparks of the house of the teacher <note>original: "zikukei d'bei rav," referring to the students or the brilliance of the academy</note> are passing engraved signs. Three times you said to them: "My masters, I beg of you, do not be silent about all this, for now is the hour." They said to her: "Blessed is our portion below, the ten of below are clearer than all other times, and this [year] 155 <note>original: "קנ"ה" (5155 / 1395 CE or a symbolic number)</note> is clear and our portion is renewed, flowing over all other times of the world." Rabbi Isaac said: "Father, they were not found by the 'Evil Eye' <term>Ayin Hara: the harmful power of a jealous glance</term> of a man." What is "into a multitude" <note>original: "v'yidgu," related to fish</note>? To increase upon the deed. They said: "Son, Angel of the Lord, there is no deed in man nor side of the Evil Eye that we have learned [that can affect you]. And it is difficult; let it cover you like its wings." Jacob said this verse through the Holy Spirit. If he said it through the Holy Spirit, it belongs to Wisdom. "The Angel"—he calls him an Angel, and he calls him the deputy of the gift of swords. Here he says "The Angel," but the teaching established it above in the place of reception, and it flies from within the Mirror <term>Aspaklaria: the divine lens or speculum of prophecy</term> of above, where all who are blessed are satisfied here. And if you say: "Behold, in several places she is called an Angel and does not come to sustain the worlds?" And once he rests in his place upon the two Cherubim, he leans upon the Lord. To ascend, when he appears to him as at first, he is called "Angel." To Jacob he did not appear thus, except in the image as it is written:

> **"Thus says the Lord: A voice is heard in Ramah..."** (Jeremiah 31:15)

"Rachel weeping for her children." And "Rachel came" is written with those levels of hers. She is certainly lacking her coming, and all these were prepared and appointed in her hand:
> **"For she is a shepherd"** (Genesis 29:9)

She leads them and is appointed over them. And as...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the nature of prophecy and the spiritual hierarchy of the Patriarchs versus Moses, transitioning into the laws and mystical intentions of the Blessing after Meals (Birkat HaMazon).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Balak**<-

On the way it is written: *And the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire* <note>Exodus 3:2, referring to Moses at the bush</note>. And if you say that the bush is superior to the blessing, for regarding the blessing it is not written "angel" but rather *And the Lord appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre* <note>Genesis 18:1, referring to Abraham</note>. There, in the blessing, it was below him <note>referring to a lower spiritual manifestation</note>, and this was with the name *Adonai* <note>original: "Aleph Dalet," the name associated with the Shekhinah or Divine Presence in the world</note> because at that time he had received the Covenant <note>Circumcision</note>. And that which was below until now was below him by [Divine] will. And what is the reason <note>Aramaic: *mai ta'ama*</note> he merited what is below? For then he was on the way of the "foot" <note>a lower level of spiritual travel</note> to connect and no more, and because their constellation <note>mazal</note> had [Divine] favor upon it.

But with Moses there was no separation, as it is written: *Moses, Moses* <note>Exodus 3:4</note>—there is no cantillation mark separating the names <note>original: *paska ta'ama*</note>, unlike what is written: *Abraham | Abraham* <note>Genesis 22:11</note>, where there is a separating mark. This is because [Abraham] was not yet complete—Heaven forbid—as he was previously. Its explanation: the vision between the "Abraham" of the surroundings and the "Abraham" of the beginning. But for Moses, it was a matter he could not look upon, as it is written: *And she saw him, that he was good* <note>Exodus 2:2</note>. And it is written: *And God saw that it was good* <note>Genesis 1:4</note>. Moses immediately connected to his own level. And because of this, "Moses, Moses" is said without a separating mark.

And to what shall we hint at the hidden treasures of Moses? As it is written: *The angel of the Lord*. Jacob called him "Angel" at the time he was departing from the world. Why? Because at that hour he was inheriting the "Daughter" <note>the Shekhinah</note>. Moses [did so] in his lifetime; Jacob after he departed from the world. Moses in the body; Jacob in the spirit and in the portion of Moses. **The angel who redeems me from all evil** <note>Genesis 48:16</note>—for he never drew near to the "Side of Evil," and evil could not rule over him. **May he bless the lads**—then Jacob was preparing his "House" <note>the Shekhinah</note> like a man who goes to his house and prepares it with its arrangements and adorns it with its ornaments. **May he bless the lads**—these are to be known, those who are appointed over the world, from whom blessings are found; they are the two Cherubim <note>original: *kruvin*</note>. **And let my name be called in them**—now he has prepared his house, and they ascend in his level because the secret of the "Body" <note>Tiferet</note> is mentioned in Jacob, to cleave to the place where the two holy "Arms" <note>Chesed and Gevurah</note> are mentioned. Afterward, **and these lads are blessed** then as is fitting: **And let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth**—to increase and shine within the waters, and they live as they are commanded from the depths to the dry land. Immediately these come—not so, but they emerge from the Great Sea to multiply and increase in the midst of the earth with protection. This is not the case for all the stars of the world.

What is written above? *And he blessed Joseph and said*—yet we do not find blessings here, for afterward he blessed him, as it is written: *Joseph is a fruitful bough*. Rather, since he blessed these "lads," Joseph was blessed, for they cannot be blessed except from within Joseph. And who are they who are protected by his sides and are not shown to be revealed? It is written: **And let my name be called in them**, and also my merit to cover over them; they are blessed from the hiddenness and are not designated for another. This is what is necessary to multiply the world.

They came and kissed him as before. They said: "In your canopies! See, you and your companion, for all that you have said until now is good and true." And the law is: *He who has a bountiful eye shall be blessed* <note>Proverbs 22:9</note>. What is the reason? Because it is written: "The eye of all." Who is sealed and prepared to provide food for them? Rabbi Yehuda came, the beloved son of the Holy One, blessed be He, and we have learned: **The host breaks the bread and the guest says the blessing.** One said: "There is no host here and no bridegroom." They ate, the verse was fulfilled, and we established it. For here is a "bountiful eye" <note>original: *tov ayin*</note> certainly, without your fear to rebuke until now.

He took the Cup of Blessing <note>original: *kos shel berachah*</note> and blessed, and his hands were moist and he was able to carry it. When he reached "For the land and for the food," he said: **I will lift up the cup of salvation, and call upon the name of the Lord** <note>Psalms 116:13</note>. He stood in his preparation with the "Chariot" on his right, and blessed them. At the end he said: "May it be the will for each one of you that life be found for him from the King in whom all life depends, and may the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: *Kudosha Brich Hu*</note>, be sweet to him." After he blessed, he closed his eyes for a moment, then opened them and said: "Friends, level for yourselves good paths, for all the worlds are His; follow Him and bless Him." They stayed in that house that night. They rose early...

It then transitions into a narrative where Rabbi Yehuda leads the Blessing after Meals, emphasizing the mystical intentions required when holding the Cup of Blessing.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the narrative of the companions traveling to meet the wondrous Child (the Yenuka). It follows the previous section where the companions were amazed by the child's wisdom and reported back to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

They hurried with joy. When they reached Rabbi Shimon, they recounted the event to him. Rabbi Shimon was astonished and said: "He is a son of a powerful mountain <note>original: "bar tverya takifa," likely referring to a person of great spiritual lineage or strength</note>, and he is a source of life for you and more so for me." He looked into the matter through the secret of Rav Hamnuna the Elder <note>A deceased master whose soul was said to be connected to the child</note> and recognized him. Rabbi Elazar said: "It is incumbent upon me to go and see that burning lamp <note>term: "butzina" (lamp/light) - a common Zoharic metaphor for a great soul or teacher</note>." Rabbi Shimon said: "This light is not meant to be extinguished in the house of this world, for a high matter resides within him. His life is extended so that the companions may merit from him." This spirit did not spread among the companions for one day while the companions sat and studied these priestly matters. Rabbi Elazar, Rabbi Abba, Rabbi Hiyya, Rabbi Yossi, and the rest of the companions were there. They said: "Behold, it is written:
> Do not distress Moab, and do not provoke them to war <note>Deuteronomy 2:9</note>

This was for the sake of Ruth and Naamah <note>Two righteous women of foreign origin: Ruth the Moabitess (ancestress of King David) and Naamah the Ammonitess (wife of Solomon)</note> who were destined to emerge from them for the redemption at the end of the generations. And just as Jethro and his descendants emerged from Midian, who were all righteous of truth, how much more so here. Furthermore, why were they permitted to strike Midian, as it says, 'The Holy One, blessed be He, took the vengeance of the children of Israel from the Midianites'? Even regarding Moab there are inner aspects to the matter, but the people of Midian were more prepared to be 'harvested' <note>spiritually separated or punished</note> than Moab." Rabbi Shimon said: "One who is destined to be gathered is not like one who has already been gathered. If so, the Elder and the Life-Force have already gathered them." He said to him: "Who gathered? Come and see, wait like a bird of prey <note>original: "takhche," a difficult term here used to describe waiting or watching</note>, wait constantly... just as a thief waits for his prey. Now, to gather, wait around it and no longer guard it. So too with Moab, who was destined for her prey, the Holy One, blessed be He, guarded them, as it is written: 'Do not distress Moab.' But Midian was taken and struck, and we gathered them, as it is written:
> Harass the Midianites <note>Numbers 25:17</note>

For from all of them, there was no longer a 'waiting' for them... I say her prey was the fruit of the sin of Peor <note>The idolatry of Baal-Peor</note>." He opened and said:

-> **And he said** <-
Moab to the elders of Midian, etc. Moab turned back because they waited, for Moab was destined to bring forth life from the depths. Rabbi Elazar desired to see Rabbi Yossi, the son of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakunya, his father-in-law. Rabbi Chasda, Rabbi Yossi, and Rabbi Hiyya were walking on that path and they encountered words of Torah all along the way. Rabbi Chasda said: "What is the meaning of that which is written:
> And he said, and they began... Do not distress Moab and do not provoke them to war, etc. <note>Deuteronomy 2:9</note>

And it is written:
> And when you come near opposite the children of Ammon, etc. <note>Deuteronomy 2:19</note>

He tests him with this matter. What is the difference between this one and that one? Rather, see that they were neighbors. And we have learned: whenever they approached the children of Moab, Israel appeared to them as if they were prepared for battle, yet they did not provoke them. But regarding the children of Ammon, Israel wrapped themselves in their cloaks and did not appear as if they were prepared for battle at all. And the verses prove this clearly. Rabbi Elazar said: "Certainly it is so, and we have learned that the generation was pushed aside like the dead, and the bitterness of Moab is as it is written:
> And she called his name Moab <note>Genesis 19:37 - 'Moab' can be read as 'From Father,' a name revealing the immodest origins of the nation</note>

Israel should not be brazen toward them... this brazenness and bitterness of Moab is found in this secret. To everyone, her love is visible, but her covering is distant. Israel covered their mercy toward them, wrapping themselves in cloaks like a Tallit <note>prayer shawl</note> so they would appear before them as truly thin/weak." And they established this. While they were walking, Rabbi Elazar saw a child, a child of about three parasangs <note>term: "parsa" - an ancient measure of distance, here perhaps referring to the child's age or the distance they traveled</note>, and they reached there. They approached that house, entered, and found that child sitting and arranging a table before him. As soon as he saw them, he approached them and said: "Holy beloved messengers, peace be upon you forever, you who are from above and the lower ones praise you. You who cover the stars... appearing on the dry land toward them." Rabbi Elazar was amazed and looked at his appearance, then returned to his previous state and wondered at him. Rabbi Elazar said: "I am ashamed before us... to bring out water and sand on the dry land... to perform a slaughter in the world." That child said in the spirit: "To your kingdoms, the support of Ammon and Moab is stirred within you. How did you look from your waters? If battle is not in your hands... you shall be without blood." He was astonished...

<meta>This page continues the narrative of the "Yanuqa" (The Child) from the previous section. Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Abba are traveling and encounter a young child who possesses supernatural wisdom. The discussion focuses on the mystical secrets of the table, the bread, and the symbolic relationship between wheat and sin.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Balak<-

Rabbi Elazar, Rabbi Abba, and Rabbi Phinehas were astonished. Rabbi Abba said, "Blessed is this path and blessed is our portion, for we have merited to see this." They prepared the table as before. That holy wise child said, "Seek the bread, for the delicacies of the King are within it. See and desire the living sacrifice; you shall seek the King in all His royal offerings."

Rabbi Elazar said, "Son of the Mind, holy wisdom! In all these merits, the sacrifice is found within them. We know how to place the sacrifice and the incense with will and with holy wisdom. But such wisdom as this I have never seen before; it nourishes the mighty ones of the world." That child spoke and said, "I have not seen it all, for it is written: *Let not him who girds on his armor boast like him who takes it off.* <note>original: "Al yithallel choger k'mifateach" - 1 Kings 20:11. A warning against overconfidence before a task is complete.</note>" They prepared the table with bread and everything that was needed.

Rabbi Elazar said, "How much joy is in my heart through the secret of new wisdom that will be renewed upon this table! Because of this, I see that the knowledge of the holy hidden treasures has windows within it." That child said, "Whoever desires bread over the cup of blessing may eat." Rabbi Elazar turned and brought the child close to him, saying, "Because you have humbled yourself, you shall be the first to offer the sacrifice. And the other joy of the sacrifice shall be the Crown of Wisdom <term>Keter Chokhmah: The highest emanations of the Divine</term>. For every opening, whoever desires fine flour, the King's offerings are in his hands."

Rabbi Elazar said, "It is fitting for you to show your kingship, your royal sacrifice." He opened and said: "*And it shall be, when you eat of the bread of the land, you shall set aside a gift for the Lord.* <note>Numbers 15:19</note> This verse was said regarding the 'Omer of the Wave Offering' <term>Tenufah: The waving of grain in the Temple</term>. What is the meaning of *Tenufah* (Wave Offering)? It is 'Life' (*Chai*), because the Priest brings life to it above, and they give an addition of life, and it adds life to us for the life of the Living One. Rather, certainly 'Life' is needed for the 'Snow' <note>A mystical reference to the white light of Mercy</note> and they established the gift (*Terumah*)."

"And the elders who expound say: 'Two speak,' and the elder is for every wave offering. What is it? A dream. Spirit for wisdom is here. Life, holy kindness, saturated with those who exalt it." They placed it before Rabbi Shemaya the Pious. He said, "Do you not know what the Wave Offering (*Tenufah*) is? What is the Staff? What is the Service? The Wave Offering of which we speak is actually *Tenu Peh* ('Give a Mouth' or 'Give Speech'). Its spirit is: *Give glory to the Lord your God.* <note>Jeremiah 13:16</note> For the 'Upper Mouth' is the Glory, which is certainly to be given to the Holy One, Blessed be He."

"And because of this, they returned to us to lift it upwards, to show that you do not give except that there should be a 'Mouth' (*Peh*). For there is no danger to the Supreme King except when Israel prepares it and gives it to the King—and this is the Wave Offering, lifting the desire and drawing the 'Arm' near to it. *And it shall be, when you eat of the bread of the land.* Why then is barley (*Se'orah*) given to them? Barley is offered because the 'First Storm' (*Se'orah*) departs with a cry forever. Barley is called *Se'orah* because its place is known as a 'Storm' (*Se'arah*)."

"**S** <note>The letter Samekh</note>—for it is in the middle, so that the 'Other Side' <term>Sitra Achra: The forces of impurity</term> has no portion there, for sin is there. But Wheat (*Chitah*) is the 'Severing' (*Karta*) that descends before him to tread, and it performs his will. And what is Wheat (*Chitah*)? It is the bride for all letters." Rabbi Elazar said, "It is 'Sin' (*Chet*) that we were meant to hear. Here we must say: 'Our bow is trodden.'" That child said, "Thus it rests before the lion's cub." Rabbi Elazar said, "Certainly we call it Wheat (*Chitah*). All nourishment is in its place, all of which have no 'Sin' (*Chet*) or 'Covering' (*Kes*), but here there is 'Sin' (*Chet*) and we call it Wheat (*Chitah*)."

The child said, "Is it not so? For 'Sin' (*Chet*) is troubled, and 'Covering' (*Kes*) is next to it. These coverings did not come from the side of holiness, for all is troubled. And if you say a sword does not go out, and you say to see it like a bow, these are given as a 'Severing' (*Karta*). Rather, it is to know the sin of Adam the First, of whom they said: 'It was Wheat.' You shall know all and this portion."

"**S** <note>The letter Samekh</note>—the side of Good is like a crown to every 'Other Side' and subdues it. They herald before him: 'Explain this matter and remove it far away.' Wheat (*Chitah*) is plain. It comes like a crown and they diminish Wheat from the covering. Isaiah came and explained it, as it is written: *And from beneath it, for it shall not draw near...* <note>Isaiah 54:14</note> in the holy place, in the middle, so that this sin which burns it shall be the sin. And the exchange between the letter *Tet* (ט) and *Tav* (ת) <note>The child is playing on the spelling of Wheat: Chet-Tet-Heh vs. Sin: Chet-Tet-Aleph</note> is the breaking of the 'Other Side' in the scattering of the word. You are the companions who did not place it before Rabbi Shemaya..."

<summary>The miraculous child (Yanuqa) explains the mystical secrets of the Wave Offering and the spiritual nature of Wheat, linking the Hebrew word for wheat (Chitah) to the concept of Sin (Chet) and the fall of Adam.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse in Parashat Balak, focusing on the distribution of spiritual sustenance and the hidden nature of the Holy Land. It follows a conversation between Rabbi Eleazar, his companions, and a mysterious figure named Isaac (often identified as a "donkey-driver" or hidden sage) who reveals deep secrets of the Torah.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Balak<-

I have heard from the masters of the donkey-drivers <note>original: "masila chamarin" - likely referring to traveling mystics who shared secrets on the road</note> that at the time when we are nourished, the Other Side <note>The Sitra Achra, the realm of spiritual impurity</note> has no portion. But is this not so? For everything that is consumed as **refuse** <note>Refuse/Excrement, common Zoharic term for the portion given to the Sitra Achra</note>—the Other Side has a portion in it. And what portion does it have? The sustenance that the wind drives away, as it is written: *The wicked are not so, but are like the chaff which the wind drives away.* <note>Psalms 1:4</note> And it is written: *For the wind passes over it, and it is gone...* <note>Psalms 103:16</note> This is because the Holy Spirit scatters it to all sides of the world so that it cannot be found in its place.

We have learned that the word "machi" <note>striking/threshing</note> refers to sustenance, and the straw and chaff go their way; therefore, they are exempt from tithing, for they have no portion in holiness. Grain is gathered into levels. And regarding the "hiku" <note>a type of vegetable or pulse</note> and the beet <note>silka</note> through which the first man (Adam) sinned, it goes with it, for everything is a herald of that sin. Rabbi Eleazar was astonished, and his companions wondered. Rabbi Eleazar said: "Certainly, it is so." Isaac said: "It is certainly so; it is a baldness <note>kerach</note> to the judge therein, for it is a burden for the Holy One to come into the world, and he prepares food for the beasts in general." And it is the spirit that goes in a distorted way, which we see every day, and there is no wisdom in them. And it is called "Bread of the Offering" <note>Lechem Terumah</note>, the food of that offering. And it is brought near as a whole, for it is written: *No stranger shall eat of the holy thing* <note>Leviticus 22:10</note> and all the holy things, etc. His bread is from the holy things, so that you shall not wonder: it is from the holy things, but not the "Holies" themselves, for "Holy" in its plain sense is not called "Offering" <note>Terumah</note>, as it says "Holy" from its scriptural context.

However, the Holy Land exists within the mystery of "Holy," and they interpreted "Land" not as being there like the eating of the Supernal realms, which exists as it is consumed and is never diminished, within the mystery of "in our midst" <note>bekirbeno</note> of this offering that is in the mountains, in the likeness of the spirit of Moses. Rabbi Abba said: "Certainly, the filter of the length is for your benefit." That Isaac said: "Certainly, I have been strengthened like a roof, and the water has been shaken for us." Rabbi Abba said: "The Holy Land has no authority for the 'Other' <note>the Sitra Achra</note>, and it does not go up there." Sustenance and straw were spoken of. That Isaac opened his discourse and said: *And God blessed the man in His image...* <note>Genesis 1:27-28</note> and it is written: *And God said to them, be fruitful and multiply.* <note>Genesis 1:28</note> And the "Living One" <note>Chai</note> for us below, who has pity on the living, did not create offspring for the world. Or, if the "Living One" had not labored with the impulse during the incident of the Golden Calf, they would not have produced offspring. Rather, certainly, if it were hidden because of the sin of offspring, and He made Man, it would certainly be that the decree would be decreed immediately to be done, as it is written: *Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.* <note>Genesis 1:28</note> And those offspring would all be like a gourd <note>kikayon</note>, everything would be completely closed. So too, the Holy Land, for no authority of the "Other" ascends there at all; it produced sustenance and straw that is not from the side of the "Other Stranger." That sustenance and straw are in the Other Side, which is not after holiness, like an ape behind a human being. Rabbi Eleazar and his companions came and kissed him. They said: "We have profited from the wine of this bald man <note>keracha</note> at this table." Rabbi Eleazar said: "Certainly it is so, for every kind of battle is in your hand, they are consumed by your hand." They came and kissed him as before.

He opened his discourse and said: *And three branches were on the vine...* <note>Reference to Genesis 40:10</note> etc. Up to here is the full sustenance, for they ate, and further on we see what was his, as it is written: *And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand.* <note>Genesis 40:11</note> And all the sustenance that was there was in the hands of Joseph, and it was clarified to him so that Joseph would hear and know. Behold, there are seven heavens, and they are seven palaces <note>Heichalot</note>, and there are those that are five. And all of them emerge from within the Supernal Ancient One <note>Atika Kadisha</note>. That wine which is drawn to him, and the "Heel" <note>Ekiev - referring to the lower end of the sefirotic chain</note> keeps distant and reaches it from the evening of that vine. Then the "Heel" draws that wine which is taken below to him, and he rejoices and bathes in that "him," as it is written: *And he brought him wine, and he drank.* <note>Genesis 27:25</note> Everything is bound together above and below. And until it is far and full and reaches it in the measure of the two "wavings" <note>tenufi</note>, and they gave it to him below and to him above, on two sides. Other than you, **Metatron** <term>Metatron: The supreme angel and heavenly scribe, often associated with the mediation between the divine and the mundane</term>, another "and he brought him wine," for the wise were added to by that wine. And the "Living One" for them, who saw water in it. He could not endure it, and he spoke clearly of Enoch and **Metatron** <term>Metatron: Here identified with the translated figure of Enoch</term>. And because of this, the taste was drawn to him, and it is wine seen from level to level, and all of them taste of it until Joseph the Righteous tastes it, which is the generation of all grace <note>chen</note>. Since it is good, *it flows smoothly for my beloved.* <note>Song of Songs 7:10</note>

The light of their shame shone forth and he appointed himself, and those of the lower prophets when they were tested <note>original: "נתיסון"</note> as sixty, such was their head. And the wine of which it is written "And the Lord said" is mine. Did you not know until He opened? Rather, to the lower realm the Holy One, Blessed be He, commanded not to use wisdom to settle the darkness, to return to the generation. He did not command this. And already, if you contend with Moab, the sixty will be consumed and destroyed. For from them emerges the vision that will give strength to Israel, and He will take vengeance with their vengeance. And this is for the stranger below, Ruth, from his darkness. And do not contend in any war; all this is to be abandoned below. This is for the wine, my Master. And if you say that Joseph and those elders who were for our instruction, their crowns were permitted—it is not so. Because all of them were from the scent of the staff, and what was forbidden to the staff is forbidden as well. This was his bread, and this was for killing. And that from all the strength in those who are seen for killing. And he wrote "leavened" as from all the sixty, everything for his witness, the destruction of the bride of the Lord. He hated all the earth to purify from them, from all those who did evil to Israel. The Holy One, Blessed be He, guards them and weeps, and takes from them sparks for all who are destined; from them comes good to the world.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Balak<-

Blessed is His anger, for it brought them forth until that good should emerge into the world, and afterward He takes vengeance and judgment from among them. Rabbi Eleazar <note>original: "Rabbi Elazar"</note> rejoiced and said: "It is certainly so, and this is the clarification of the King." That Child said: "From here onward, friends, prepare the chambers of the heart with judgment and the joy of battle." Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse and said:
> **Bless the Lord, you His angels, mighty in strength, etc.** <note>Psalms 103:20</note>

King David invited [the world] to bless the Holy One, blessed be He; he invited those who are His providers and His sustenance and the rest of the hosts and ranks to join with them in blessing the Holy One, blessed be He. This is what is written: **Bless the Lord, all His hosts... in all places of His dominion. Bless the Lord, O my soul.** <note>Psalms 103:21-22</note> The secret <note>original: "ס'" for "Sod"</note> of the Assembly is that every blessing is prepared for the King from on high to bless Him, as it is written: "Bless the Lord, you His angels, etc." And because of this, the strength of the King is awakened from on high. They were performing the "doing" <note>The aspect of action/Asiyah</note> until Israel came and stood at Mount Sinai and said, "We will do and we will hear" <note>Exodus 24:7</note>; they took that name from the ministering angels. Israel stands alone and the holy angels stand alone, in the order of the rungs and ladders of action. And regarding the "mighty in strength who do His word," first comes the doing and afterward "to hear." Fortunate are Israel who nullified [the separation of] "doing" from themselves and it was fulfilled through them. That Child said: "When we descend and rejoice. Do we find this [sanctity] alone without Israel and no other?" He said: "Fortunate is this finding and no other." That Child said: "From here, from the power of judgment, it does not begin. If she has those who move her as is fitting for one who wages war." The <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note> was found on high, and she was not given to the high angels alone; to Israel was given the portion of her life, the Sanctification <note>original: "Kedushah"</note>. The Sanctification was given to them alone, just as it was sold to Israel. The cord of holiness was not given to them alone; Israel would not rejoice if they did not sanctify the Sanctification even among these [angels] of Israel. And if you say it is written:
> **And one called to another and said...** <note>Isaiah 6:3</note>

When is this? At the time when Israel sanctifies below. And until Israel sanctifies below, they [the angels] cannot say the Sanctification, because the Sanctification rises through three worlds and not just two. And this is "And one called to another." "This to that" makes two. "And said" makes three. There are three worlds, and corresponding to them are three sanctifications. And because of this, you find that Israel raises the Sanctification from below. Rabbi Eleazar rejoiced and said: "It is so; these words we have established." And we have strengthened them, for these three sanctifications were given to Israel below from this verse:
> **Sanctify yourselves, and be holy, for I the Lord am holy.** <note>Leviticus 11:44</note>

"Sanctify yourselves" is one. "And be holy" is two. "For I the Lord am holy" is three. Here are three sanctifications. One hand worked so as not to depart from the heights until it rises afterward with strength; place it in your hand. From here on, you shall speak to the heights that you have placed in your hand. Again, after you have gazed, Rabbi Eleazar rejoiced in these words... Blessings from the goodness of all blessings go forth until they become a blessing in the "Segulah" <note>A special treasure or mystical property</note> from the goodness that is drawn down, and it is the resting of the waters in that blessing; immediately the waters turn into revealed colors of many kinds. And that goodness is visible; it is the drawing down of the vessel from within that "shining mirror" <note>original: "Aspaklaria de-Nahara," referring to prophetic or divine vision</note> that shines from below, from above to below. This is for the High King, for those who are the children of the heights, as it was said. "Bless the Lord," for those who dwell below merit it; afterward "Bless the Lord," because they are blessed to be found... to show His protection. And regarding this, David said... to seek Your face... And because of this, the beginning of the exile... "Bless the Lord," and to be found on our eyelashes... And since they merit this sign... to say "exile" and to find. And because of this, one must bless a person before he reveals his exile, and draw upon his eyelashes this sign... and he will sustain and bless the person first... for the high angels it is written "Bless the Lord," and for you the sign is an addition... That Child is certainly [wise], and he who wages your war, they are meritorious; you shall remember them and not forget them, for certainly the "Gevurah" <note>Strength/Severity</note> of a man who fights the war is in the heights.

## Main Text (Zohar)

...with desire and joy for them. What is the meaning of *Mighty in strength, who perform His word, to hearken to the voice of His word* <note>Psalm 103:20</note>? Rabbi Eleazar said: "You have already spoken." That child said: "I know that the word of your arm <note>referring to a previous mystical teaching or the merit of the sage</note> is sealed there, until it is not seen except to be struck by the Holy One, Blessed be He; the Crown <term>Keter: the highest of the ten Sephirot or divine emanations</term> is diminished. The Holy One, Blessed be He, splits it, and with this, we subdue this Crown and that Crown." Rabbi Eleazar rejoiced, and Rabbi Abba rejoiced. That child opened his discourse and said:

*I am black but comely, O daughters of Jerusalem... Look not upon me, because I am swarthy...* <note>Song of Songs 1:5-6</note>. These words have already been established <note>explained by the earlier sages</note>. But regarding this claim within the mystery of love: when the Face is toward the Beloved, who can stand before the intensity of that love? Because she cannot endure it, she diminishes herself to a very great smallness, until she is not seen at all except as the smallness of a single point. And what is she then? She is hidden from all her hosts and camps. And she says: *I am black*, for I have no light within me, appearing like a dark mountain. And this "blackness" is my heart, and I have no place to enter because of the boundaries of the gates; her coverings are darkened for her, for she has no garments. We have not merited, and Solomon <note>King Solomon, traditionally the author of Song of Songs</note>—this is like glass—says: *Look not upon me*, do not look at me at all, for I am like a tiny wisp of smoke. 

What do the "mighty men" do—those who are her strength? The Beloved above hears and knows that she is his beloved, in a love where her form and beauty are not visible at all. And then, from the voices and the ascents of those who are her mighty hosts, the Beloved comes forth from the palace. How many preparations! With how much longing and love and yearning he comes to her, to find her without any form or beauty at all. He draws near to her and cherishes her until she is crowned little by little from the hints and the longings and the joy of the Beloved who is with her, until she is restored and made according to her proper arrangement, her form, and her beauty as in the beginning. 

And this is the meaning of <term>Mighty in strength</term> <note>original: Gibborei Koach</note> regarding her form and beauty; for their power and might caused this. And concerning this it is written: *Mighty in strength, who perform His word*. They "perform" her, as it were, pushing and preparing and returning her to her original form. From this point onward, once she is prepared and made into her beautiful form as in the beginning, then they and all the other hosts stand *to hearken to what she says*, and she stands like a king amidst the army. And this is certainly "performing His word." 

In this same manner below: in a time when people are guilty, she <note>the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> is hidden and diminishes herself until she is not seen in any of her forms, like a woman [in distress]. The "mighty in strength" and the righteous of truth, as it were, "make" this word and restore her little by little to be made according to her form and beauty as in the beginning. 

The companions came and kissed him. Rabbi Eleazar said: "If not for Ezekiel the prophet, this wonder would not have been in the world... the priest is beautiful and established as in the beginning." That child said: "Heaven forbid!" They said to him: "Bless, and you shall be blessed, for it is a merit to bless." He said: "How holy you are! How many blessings are prepared for you, holy company, because you did not prevent me from blessing." 

He opened and said: *He who withholds corn, the people shall curse him; but blessing shall be upon the head of him who sells it* <note>Proverbs 11:26</note>. This verse, in its literal sense, refers to the community. But we have learned: every person should recite the Grace After Meals. And if one does not know how to give it <note>the blessing</note> to its Master, they do not bless him from Above, and the celestial fortune <note>Mazal</note> of that man who does not know how to bless is rebuked, until he learns how to give it to its Master and to the Name that they bless. And if he knows, he must be recognized and given the <term>Cup of Blessing</term> <note>original: Kasa de-Vircheta; the cup of wine over which the Grace is recited</note>. 

And one who prevents him from blessing, to receive it and not give it for sustenance—*the people shall curse him*. "They shall curse him" means they provoke him, or "the people" <note>Le'om</note> refers to the holy nation. They shall curse this man who prevented that person from blessing and receiving it. But for the unique son who provides for the "mother" <note>the Shekhinah</note>, give me the cup and I shall bless the Holy King who gave us bread to eat... for your vision is before them, strong words that merit them. And because of this, he prepared to bless. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, tied the verse to this restoration.

He shakes off all the sparks, a thousand words that prevent a person from being guarded. <term>YHVH</term> <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note> is the totality of all. And the blessing of the "bread of the wise" is for a person to be nourished, so that his son may be blessed to bless the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> and to unify Him through His commandments and the Torah. And the secret of the matter is written: -> What is His name and what is His son’s name, if you know? <note>Proverbs 30:4</note> <-
That name is known: **The Lord of Hosts** is His name. The name of His son is **Israel**, as it is written: -> Israel is My firstborn son. <note>Exodus 4:22</note> <- And even regarding Israel, all the keys of faith hang in his hands and are found within them. And it says: -> The Lord said to me, "You are My son." <- And so it is certainly, for the Father and Mother <note>The sefirot of Chokhmah and Binah</note> crowned him and blessed him with many blessings, and they commanded everyone: "Kiss etc." Kiss the hand of this son. He gave him authority over everything, that all should serve him.
He was crowned with the judgment of mercy. Whoever merits the male principle, merits the male; whoever merits mercy, merits mercy. All blessings from above and below ascend and are crowned in unity. And whoever withholds blessings from this son, his sins are spread before the Holy King. He is a literal robber. And the blessing of the "bread of the wise"—whoever blesses, and sometimes the "Cup of Blessing"—for the one who needs it, the <term>Other Side</term> <note>The realm of evil or impurity</note> is broken and subdued, and the side of holiness ascends. This is what is written: "And the blessing of the bread of the wise." Just as the serpent is removed before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, making the <term>Other Side</term> broken, so the Holy One draws blessings upon him from above, and that blessing which is sought rests upon his head. They gave him the cup and he blessed. And they proclaim concerning them: "A son in this constellation!" Even in the assembly of the hour, how much vitality and piety did this Bride have to subdue until that revolution? He raised the accentuation above with wisdom. "He went before them by day." Here is another matter of that house; the Holy One showed him a dream, and what is it? Wisdom. As it is written: -> By day the Lord commands His lovingkindness <note>Psalms 42:9</note> <-. And it is written: "Kindness is not cut off day and night." A day in which all days are included, a day that is prepared. The <term>Serpent</term> surrounds all days and pushes. And because of this, it is called "By Day." And for this reason, "He went before them by day." It was a light for them by day, and the Bride was held at night, as it is written: "And by night in a pillar of fire to give them light." This is the Bride, each one as is fitting for it. And we have learned: they proclaim day and night, let it be before you at every hour in silence, and bless Him as before. Rabbi Shimon was troubled and wept for this matter.
In wonder he said: "How much vitality is there, for all of it ascends like a thin piece of wood; when the fire ascends, it ascends for the moment and immediately is extinguished and departs. It is written "shall be blessed." Rabbi Abba said: "We have seen children who say sublime things, but they do not endure in the later days of the world." If a <term>Child</term> says one or two words for the moment alone, their end proves that they did not merit to learn Torah in Israel. But this one, whose light stands upon its foundation with perfect knowledge—it is not so. Furthermore, he has established his repentance on a path of shame before the Lord. And all...

He took a portion of divination and performed sorceries and prepared a plank. He would arrange a table and a cup for the investigations of his divination, as it has been said: for so the Other Side follows the Holy Crown like a monkey follows a human being. <meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the origins of the Torah, specifically interpreting Deuteronomy 33:2. It explains how the Holy One offered the Law to the guardian angels of the nations before giving it to Israel, thereby stripping those nations of their spiritual "husks" to purify the light for the Israelites.</meta>

## Balak

->Balak<-

**"From Seir unto them"** <note>Deuteronomy 33:2</note> means literally that the children of Seir <note>the descendants of Esau</note> said they did not want to receive it. From this, Israel gained merit, and a great, beloved light was revealed upon them. Likewise, **"He shined forth from Mount Paran,"** literally because the children of Paran <note>the descendants of Ishmael</note> said they did not want to receive it from Him. Thus, Israel gained merit and was illuminated with an even greater, fitting light.

And regarding what you asked—by whose hand was this revealed to them? Come and see: the world was covered, and it was revealed through your hand. The Torah <term>Torah: the divine Law and wisdom</term> emerged from the Holy Supernal Spirit of the Hidden King. When it reached the **Left Arm** <note>the attribute of Gevurah/Judgment</note>, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, saw that a spirit of evil was growing there. He said: "I must clarify and purify this Arm." He looked at it and struck that which produces evil, so that everything would be made right; for it was necessary to clear away every blemish from here.

What did He do? He called to **Samael** <note>the guardian angel of Esau/Rome, often associated with the accuser</note> and he came before Him. He said to him: "Do you want My Torah?" 
Samael asked: "What is written in it?" 
He said to him: **"Thou shalt not murder."** <note>Exodus 20:13</note> He skipped to the part that was necessary <note>to provoke a refusal</note>. 
Samael said: "This Torah is Yours, and let it remain Yours! I do not want a partnership in this Torah." He stood and argued before Him, saying: "Master of the Universe, if You give me this, all my dominion and laws will be undone, for my dominion is over killing, and without wars and my rule over the stars and constellations, Heaven forbid, everything would be abolished from the world!" 

<margin>The light emerged from Seir to Israel.</margin>

He said: "Master of the Universe, let the Torah be the portion of the children of Jacob, and let them take a share in it. Behold, there are eighteen thousand worlds before You; let them be Yours, and let the children of Jacob have their portion." And this is the meaning of **"And He rose up from Seir unto them"**—from Seir itself the light emerged for Israel. 

Samael said: "Certainly, if the children of Jacob receive this, they will be removed from the world <note>by its strictness</note> and will never rule." 
The Holy One replied to him: "I will give you a bribe, and you shall give them your blessing." 
Samael said: "Behold, my greatness and my strength are surrendered to Him." 
He showed him the light that was covered by the 'husk' of Samael, which was destined for Israel. This is what is written: **"And He rose up from Seir unto them"**—from Seir literally. For Samael is called "Seir" <note>meaning 'hairy' or 'goat-like'</note>, as it is written: <insert>Leviticus 16:22</insert> **"And the goat [Seir] shall bear upon him..."**—unto them, to Israel.

Once He had cleared this away and removed the evil residue from the **Left Arm**, He turned to the **Right Arm** <note>the attribute of Hesed/Mercy</note> and saw that it also needed to be cleaned of evil residue. He called to **Rahab** <note>the guardian angel of Egypt/Ishmael</note> and said to him: "Do you want My Torah?" 
He said to him: "What is written in it?" 
He skipped for him and said: **"Thou shalt not commit adultery."** <note>Exodus 20:14</note>
Rahab cried out: "Woe! If I inherit this, my strength will be lost!" The Holy One intended for the evil inheritance to be removed from his dominion. For his blessing was of the waters, as it is written: <insert>Genesis 1:20</insert> **"Let the waters swarm,"** and it is written **"Be fruitful and multiply,"** but of Ishmael it is written: **"He shall be a wild donkey of a man."** <note>Genesis 16:12</note>

He stood to argue before his Master and said: "Master of the Universe, two sons emerged from Abraham; let Jacob take this and let it be his portion." 
He said: "I cannot let it go without a bribe from you." 
He stood and argued, saying: "Master of the Universe, my greatness and my portion and the darkness of my inheritance—take from it and give to them." 
And so He did, as it is written: **"He shined forth from Mount Paran."** 

Why is it different for Samael and Rahab? Regarding Samael it is written **"He rose up"** <note>Zarah - like the sun</note> and regarding Rahab it is written **"He shined forth"** <note>Hofia - a lesser appearance</note>. He took that light which was covered by Samael—the power of the sword and killing—to use it for justice and to execute judgment as is fitting. This is what is written: <insert>Deuteronomy 33:2</insert> **"And He came with ten thousands of holy ones; at His right hand was a fiery law for them."** He took from the blessing that Rahab stripped off—the power of fruitfulness and multiplication. And because of this, it says **"He shined forth from Mount Paran"** and not "He rose up." Once these gifts were nullified for the nations, they were given to Israel as refined blessings and powers. He came and called them "Blessings."

<summary>This passage describes the "Pre-Sinaitic" refusal of the Torah by the guardian angels of Esau (Samael) and Ishmael (Rahab), explaining that God used their rejection to strip away their spiritual powers and transfer them to Israel as holy attributes.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the portion of Balak, specifically addressing why the nations of the world rejected the Torah and how Israel received it along with "gifts" from the celestial representatives of those nations. ## Main Text (Zohar)

As it is written: *You have ascended on high, you have led captive the captivity, you have received gifts among men* <note>Psalm 68:19</note>. This is like a king who had a precious medicine <note>The Torah is often compared to a life-giving elixir or medicine</note> that he was guarding for his son. When the time came to give that medicine to his son, the king thought: "If I give it to him now, the servants and members of the household will be jealous of him and seek to kill him." What did he do? He took a small amount of a deadly poison and placed it at the opening of the vessel. He called his servants and said to them: "Come and take from this before my son." They saw it, and when they tasted it, they almost died. They thought in their hearts: "If the king gives this to his son, he will surely die immediately." Thus, they left it for the son. They said before the king: "Master, this is not fit for anyone but your son, for it is the breath of your service; take it to him specifically." 

So it is with the Holy One, Blessed be He. He did not give the Torah to Israel until He first offered it to all the other nations. Every day they would pursue Israel and kill them, but when He offered them the Torah as a gift so they might receive it, they all refused it. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave it to Israel. Regarding this, it is written: *You have ascended on high, you have led captive the captivity...* <note>original: "עלית למרום שבית שבי"</note>. Because of this, Israel inherited the Torah without any protest or accusation from the other nations at all. Blessed be He and blessed be His name forever and ever.

Come and see: these children of Israel were like priests who had been anointed, and because of this, death and the "Other Side" <note><term>Sitra Achra</term>: the kabbalistic term for the realm of evil or impurity</note> had no power over them. Not only did they receive the Torah without protest, but they received blessings and gifts from everyone. When the nations saw what was written—*And the children of Israel took off their ornaments*—those were the gifts. 

Furthermore, it is written: *And the Canaanite, the king of Arad, heard... and he took some of them captive* <note>Numbers 21:1</note>. Despite all this, Israel is compared to a garden of lilies, and everything returns to them and is subdued by them. In the end, all will return, as it is written: *Then the Lord your God will return your captivity* <note>Deuteronomy 30:3</note>. From here onward, the king takes charge.

Another day: **When you go out** <note>original: "בצאתך"</note> from the desert, there stands against you the **Land of Rephaim** <note>The "Land of Giants"</note>. Come and see that the Land of Rephaim did not receive the Torah. Why "Rephaim"? Because they were weak <note>A wordplay on "Raphah," meaning weak or limp</note> in their actions toward the Holy One. They thought that if they received the crowns of the Torah, it would be well, but they feared it would diminish their worldly power. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, saw that all the nations refused the Torah, Israel alone remained to receive it from the surroundings of the Land of Israel. 

Because Israel accepted the Torah, they were not afraid of all the sorceries that the nations of the world could perform. For this reason, the Holy One, Blessed be He, broke before them all types of sorceries and divinations so they could not rule over them. And that fool, Balak, knew this. Immediately: *He sent messengers to Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor, which is by the river...* <note>Numbers 22:5</note>. What is the meaning of "Pethor"? It refers to a table <note>original: "פתורא" (Aramaic for table)</note> where he would arrange his divinations and seek good gifts. "By the river"—this refers to the source of his power.

Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Abba were walking to visit Rabbi Yose, the son of Rabbi Simeon ben Lakunya, the father-in-law of Rabbi Eleazar. They rose at midnight to labor in the Torah and sat down. Rabbi Eleazar said: "Now is the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, enters the Garden of Eden to delight with the righteous who are there, to hear their voices and be entertained by them." Rabbi Abba said: "This matter is hidden from us..."

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Balak**<-

A table for a prophet who does not know. He said to him: Were they like great pillars supporting a stumbling block for this world, those who did not know and did not pursue knowledge to understand upon what they stand in this world and what they would receive in that world? He opened his discourse and said: **"O Lord, You are my God; I will exalt You, I will praise Your name, for You have done wonderful things..."** (Isaiah 25:1). This verse is a secret of the faith. **"O Lord, my God"** <note>Hebrew: *YHVH Elohai*</note>. This is the supernal secret, the hidden aspect of the Supernal Point <note>The Sefirah of Chokhmah or Keter</note> which is concealed and unknown. **"My God"** is the secret of the Voice that emerges thin and delicate; it is the form established to be revealed and yet to remain hidden and unknown. He saw that he returned to it because it is hidden, secret, and stored away. **"You"** <note>Hebrew: *Atah*</note>—this is the form that stands to be shown and to be used for prophecy, and he is a priest forever. Everything is contained in **"You are a priest forever after the manner of Melchizedek"** (Psalms 110:4). However, this supernal priest is the one who stands upon the "word" <note>Hebrew: *Davar*</note> because he is male and stands only on the Right Side <note>The side of Mercy/Chesed</note>. And that male sees, and Melchizedek is his name. And why does it say **"my word"** <note>Hebrew: *Dibrati*</note>? Because below it is like David. And all the words of his praise come from that "word." Therefore, it is "my word." And in this manner, he is a priest. And we have established this regarding the "remembrance" <note>the male principle</note>, where each one is called **"You"**. **"I will exalt You"**—all as one. **"I will praise Your name"**—in the way it was, and he knew it. **"For You have done a wonder"** <note>Hebrew: *Pela*</note>—like whom and for how many to prophesy in the hidden, ancient form, in the longing of longings to be shown. Do not read it only as **"for You have done a wonder"** <note>Pela</note>, but rather "for You have made the *Aleph*." And what is the *Aleph*? We have learned: "The *Aleph* is Understanding" <note>referencing the Sefer Yetzirah</note>. Rather, the image of the *Aleph* has three sides, the secret of the supernal arm of the Primordial Man <note>Adam Kadma'ah</note>, because in the image of the *Aleph* there are two arms, one from here and one from there, and the body is in the middle, and all is one secret. And it becomes the secret of Unity, and in the manner of the *Aleph*, it is found to be One. And this is **"for You have done a wonder"** <note>Pela</note>, and the secret of faith in all is one. Thus **"for You have done a wonder"**—*Pela* is one level, and beneath it is all wisdom. And what is this? It is written: "They did not know the time," and it is a wonder. **"Counsels from afar"** <note>Isaiah 25:1</note>—this verse refers initially to Eldad and Medad. Even until the Prince of Peace and the Ancient One, you will find it taught. Rather, "counsels from afar" are two, when they were two... for all the counsel of longing comes from there. They are called "counsels from afar." **"Faithful and true"** <note>Hebrew: *Emunah Omen*</note>—these are two. Rabbi Eleazar said: He saw them all, and the one who sees killed him, and the sword killed. Rabbi Isaac said: It is the verse that is written: **"And Balaam the son of Beor, the soothsayer, they slew with the sword"** (Joshua 13:22). Rabbi Eleazar said: All this I know. Rabbi Shimon said: Eleazar, all the tools of Balaam were powerful, and the colleagues have established: **"And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses"** (Deuteronomy 34:10). In Israel, one did not arise, but among the nations of the world, one did arise—and who was it? Balaam. And we have established this matter, and all of this was in his hand, and all was powerful in the wisdom of the "stranger" <note>the "Other Side" or Sitra Achra</note>, which is good and deceptive with great strength... Therefore, they understood and killed him. But in the firstborn of the wisdom of Balaam the king, he said thus: there are three signs. A sign for transgression is paleness. A sign for the staff of words. A sign that he knows nothing of the counting, nor does he incline toward the good, as in all transgressions, all is within him. And this is written: "And he goes, and the spirit of his mouth..." Not so, but he was not worthy to be known to you, to open your mouth to speak in freedom. And to make known the words of the crown in freedom. And then the opening of your mouth will find the King and they will know what wisdom is. For there is no word in the world that they can recognize except at the time when the Holy One, Blessed Be He, opens his mouth. He saw that wicked Balaam, who watched and observed himself in everything. And because they completed their knowledge, he stood and stole away and departed with his words. With words and stirrings, he would do great things. What he said regarding those deceptive words, he would say, and he would cut off. He said of all that: he is wicked and observes himself as one. It is written that he departed with his words to all who see the cup... as it is written: **"He who hears the words of God and knows..."** (Numbers 24:16).

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Balak, specifically analyzing the boastful claims of the prophet Balaam. It transitions from discussing his spiritual level to his ultimate defeat by Phinehas.</meta>

## Balak

"One who hears the words of God" <note>original: *Shomea imrei El*</note>—who is the man in the world who would hear these words from his own mouth and not think that there was none like him in his faithful repose? And indeed, it was so; all of it was "one who hears the words of God." "And knows the knowledge of the Most High" <note>original: *Yodea da'at Elyon*</note>—it was truly so. But he was a wicked man with "open eyes" <note>referring to Numbers 24:3</note> regarding the lower levels. "One who hears the words of God" is a living matter of high ascent, and thus he said "Hearer of the words of *El*" written with an *Aleph*, referring to the God whose way is perfect <note>Psalm 18:31</note>; he spoke of the God of all things, so that he would not be mistaken for a "foreign god." "One who hears the words of God" is a small matter, yet he cast it out to show that he did not know it was great and supreme.

"And knows the knowledge of the Most High"—this refers to all the levels he observed, those that cover the path of the sea and the storm in forty directions. Among them is a great overseer through whom all are guided, and he is "Most High" over them all. It was to this level that the wicked one attached himself, claiming he "knew the knowledge of the Most High," referring to the level that is supreme over all those others. Who else was so defiled in the way that they did not stumble in their knowledge? There was no one like him in the world's history except for that wicked man who, by his own strength, spoke words of truth and prophesied the knowledge of the world's end.

"Who sees the vision of the Almighty" <note>original: *Machazeh Shaddai*</note>—the things he heard he did not value as much as seeing what others in the world did not see. The "Vision of the Almighty" refers to the holy crown from those branches that emerge from the name *Shaddai* and are made above; they are called the "Vision of the Bride" and the "Constellation of the Vision." It is the branch from which those visions of **Aza and Azael** emerge, for they are doubled, "fallen yet with open eyes." And the "Vision of the Almighty" is what he saw, "fallen yet with open eyes." Where was Balaam at that time? If you say he was there, it is written:

> "And now, behold, I go unto my people" (Numbers 24:14)

If his strength was there, they gave it to him. When that wicked man saw that the rain was doubled <note>a metaphor for divine influence or judgment</note>, he delayed there and sought to prepare himself to remain below with the great ones he worshipped. When he saw his soul flying like a serpent, his two sons were with him, **Jannes and Jambres**. And if you ask how they did not act as they did with the Golden Calf, it was certainly so, for it is written "he fell and is falling" when he took the form of **illusory transformations** <note>original: *chalfei chayim*, referring to magical shapeshifting</note>. He knew and witnessed this, and his spirit was stirred as one who calculates distant, supreme, and great gates. He knew how to see them, and here he took the form of illusory transformations. These were the sons of Balaam, **Jannes and Jambres**, who were skilled in the likeness of these transformations. Indeed, that wicked man knew all the sorceries of the world and the nullification of the ranks of men who were accustomed to them, until he was removed.

**Phinehas** struck him, for he was a man who possessed his own weaponry <note>mystical armor</note> and ascended into the air. A voice called out to the righteous sons: "Is there anyone who knows how to bind his companion, that wicked one?" For Balaam was seen **praying** <note>original: *tzaleia*</note> in the heights of the clouds, and he took the authority that rules over sorcery and flew and ascended. When he struck him, that wicked man made another path in the air and broke through five atmospheres in that path. At that moment, the wisdom of the ancients was used against him, and he was like a youth who did not know what he was doing. Phinehas threw his spear at him, and the shadow of the clouds turned against every vision like a serpent. Immediately he knew and revealed that path and came toward him; immediately they were both revealed before Phinehas. Come and see, it is written of that wicked man:

> "And he went to a high place" <note>Numbers 23:3; original: *shefi*, often translated as 'solitary' or 'a bare height'</note>

This was the highest of his levels, the male serpent. He was like two, male and female, and through this he ruled over them, because the image that ruled over them was nullified and subdued before him. This was the "Typhon" <note>a chaotic force</note> of the sun over that destruction which the wicked man wrought, as it is written:

> "Dan shall be a serpent by the way" (Genesis 49:17)

This is the Satan, the "Typhon" over the sun.

> "That bites the horse's heels" (Genesis 49:17)

This is the awakening of the serpent clearly in that generation. He came from Dan, and his structure depended on his firstborn in that generation, as it is written: "And the generation uprooted all the chariots."
