## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Balak**<-

The horse and its rider fell backward—this refers to the remnant that is destined to come like that bird <note>original: *matosa*, likely referring to a mystical bird or omen</note> to the ruins and the strongholds. They found that they were prepared and hurried to perform sorceries and divinations among the rest of the nations. And all this will be shattered; then they found the redemption of Israel, as it is written: >I wait for Your salvation, O Lord< <note>Genesis 49:18</note>. And he intended to establish them to strike the baldness <note>original: *kerach*, perhaps a play on the name Korah or a reference to a spiritual void</note> for every clarification of the matter, as it was said and as they established it. And he went down below to the ice and to the serpent. Once he descended, the horse trembled before Phinehas <note>original: *Sanhas*, a variant or scribal error for Phinehas</note> and went down. **He saw him** <note>The phrase "He saw him" (*chama leh*) repeats as a rhythmic refrain in this section</note>, the wicked one, evil revolutions passing over the holy people. **He saw him**, the serpent, come and slaughter him, and he went as those who are sealed, swimming to sustain upon him a praise, so that his divination would not go out and be included among the holy levels, and so that the evil he spoke would be fulfilled: >Let me die the death of the righteous< <note>Numbers 23:10</note>. He crushed him at that hour, doing to him as one does—for is death not awakened like the dripping of a branch that was strong (another version: mighty) over the waters of the side? And he washes away the rain. **He saw him**, Phinehas, like a vessel he took him and like a vessel he shall die; then he killed him and overcame him, for such are the mercies of the horse-side, seeing that he deserved to be crowned. Thus he died, and thus his divination went out, and thus it was included. And the Canaanite died and they judged him with thrones like the washing of the world, and he was never buried. And all his bones were crushed and made into what they were, melting from the sparks of the rest. Then they thought of the ribs that were for the children of the shield, they were supported. We found in the **Book of Wisdom** that was given to Solomon <note>A legendary mystical text often cited in the Zohar</note> an ointment: that anyone who wished to perform powerful, hidden sorceries of the left, he would know the enclosure of the vault there where Balaam is, and he found the savings seen from the bones of that wicked one. He would kill the lowliness of his head, and perform joyful sorceries like his falling—sorceries upon sorceries. There are three types of sorceries in each and every one. It went and rested thus below toward the name, the laughter of words that she bore to the world; she fermented the bone of the wood of three sorceries as we have written. Immediately, there was no wood for anyone in the world from the king who did not tell you. They hurried and circled over this, and a voice and a deviation were found for your palate. And you could not nullify even one of the lowly ones. What did he answer her? Words that were sustained thus, he informed her, as it is written: >And he told now all your heart.< Those deviations, all the people of the world cannot overcome them, all the speech of the **Holy Spirit** <term>Ruach HaKodesh: Divine inspiration or the prophetic voice</term>. And he strikes the haste of the covering of the seed, and you might say: who is able? Be silent, like the claim of that covering seed, let every man go out in repentance; he brought it out to the master of that wood according to the mind of repentance. When their daughter went out, they nullified it immediately like a single sustenance, and that sustenance they threw toward the water. Immediately his head bowed and they caught it as one catches a domestic rooster. And in all the battles of the world, they shall sleep as one lowly person; no, they cannot overcome him. A man in the world needs to strike the battle, and not from her is the digging, and he does not need to guard himself from the lowliness, for they are all subdued toward it. Then those words were crushed and laughed according to their strength, and his tent was for the height. Then he did what he did in that darkness, and these hidden secrets were not permitted to be revealed to all, so that others who dwell there should not know the hidden paths of the world. I have revealed to you that they are like hidden treasures in the world, and in their lowliness they do not know, and they are hidden elevations for you alone, and the supernal ones are bad upon it. For he throws baldness to him, and silence that he gave. And they are strong, and a pocket of truth is upon them, as it is written: >Surely the righteous shall give thanks unto Your name, etc.< <note>Psalm 140:14</note>.

->**And Now**<-
>And now, I pray You, let the power of the Lord be great, according as You have spoken, saying, etc.< <note>Numbers 14:17</note>. Rabbi Shabba opened: >A prayer of the afflicted, when he faints, etc.< <note>Psalm 102:1</note>. There are three of whom it is written "A Prayer," and let us establish this matter. But one was Moses, and one was David, and one was the poor man <note>The Zohar often compares the prayers of Moses (the prophet), David (the king), and the Poor Man (the humble/brokenhearted)</note>, who are subdued in them and joined in them. And you might say, behold it is written: >A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet<—behold there are four! But as for Habakkuk, it was not for the sake of prayer, but he saw it, as it is written in his regard...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on Parashat Balak. The previous section likely discussed the power of prayer in general; here, the text focuses specifically on the hierarchy of prayers, elevating the "Prayer of the Poor" above even those of Moses and David.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **195a Balak** <-

Through it, prayer is accepted and he is forgiven, and it is accepted by Him without anything being too much for Him, and He acts with him [the penitent] unlike with strangers who are not children of the faith. But there are three [notable] prayers: "A Prayer of Moses, the man of God," "A Prayer of David," and it is also said, "A Prayer of David" <note>The text notes the repetition of David's prayers</note>. This prayer is a prayer like no other before the King. 

"A Prayer of the Poor." Among these three prayers, which is the most significant of them all? One must say: the Prayer of the Poor. This prayer precedes all others; it precedes the prayer of David and precedes all other prayers in the world. Why? Because the poor man is <term>broken-hearted</term> <note>original: "tevir libba"</note>. And it is written <note>Psalms 34:19</note> > "The Lord is close to the broken-hearted, etc." 

The poor man is constantly making a "quarrel" <note>an urgent, desperate plea</note> with the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, listens and hears his words. As soon as he prays his prayer, he opens all the windows of the firmaments, and all the other prayers that ascend on high are pushed aside by that poor man who is <term>broken-hearted</term>. As it is written <note>Psalms 102:1</note> > "A prayer of the poor man when he faints <note>or "wraps himself"</note>." 

It should have said "when he will faint" <note>future tense</note>. What is the meaning of "when he faints" <note>present/active</note>? It means he creates a "wrapping" <note>a covering or delay</note> for all the prayers in the world, and they do not enter until his own prayer has entered. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, says: "Let all the prayers be wrapped up [delayed], and let this prayer enter before Me." I do not require a court of law here to judge between us; let his complaints be before Me, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, receives both of them alone <note>the man and his prayer</note> as a heat of complaints in that prayer, as it is written > "and before the Lord he pours out his speech." 

"Before the Lord" specifically. All the hidden things are before Him. In what does he wrap himself? In what do they [the angels] exert themselves? They say: he is unified in desire with his "vessels" <note>his broken state</note>. They do not know what he accomplishes with that prayer of the poor and all those complaints of his, for there is no desire for the poor man except when he pours out his tears in complaint before the Holy King. And there is no desire for the Holy One, Blessed be He, except when He receives them and takes his kindness. This is the prayer that creates a wrapping for all the prayers in the world. 

Moses prayed his prayer and it was delayed for many days. David saw that all the windows and all the gates of heaven were prepared to be opened for the poor man, and that among all the prayers in the world, none receives merit immediately like the prayer of the poor. When he saw this, he made himself poor and destitute; he stripped off his royal garments and sat on the ground like a pauper. He said "A Prayer of David" <note>Psalms 86:1</note> > "A Prayer of David: Incline Your ear, O Lord, answer me." 

And if you ask why? Because > "I am poor and needy." 
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "David, you are a king! You are a ruler over powerful kings! And yet you make yourself poor and needy?" Immediately, he changed his prayer to the aspect of a field <note>a metaphor for the Shekhinah</note> and an elder who is strong, and said <note>Psalms 86:2</note> > "Guard my soul, for I am pious <note>Chasid</note>." 

A person must ensure that when he prays his prayer, he should be there as a poor man, and make himself poor so that his prayer may enter among the collective of all the poor. For all the gatekeepers do not allow [prayers] to enter as they allow the poor, for they enter with permission. If a person makes himself and turns his will constantly like a poor man, his prayer ascends and meets those prayers of the poor, joins with them, and ascends with them, entering the collective and being accepted with favor before the Holy King. 

Thus King David made himself like the parched earth; he placed himself among the poor, he placed himself among the pious, he placed himself among the servants, he placed himself among those who sacrifice themselves and their souls for the sanctification of His Name. He placed himself among the poor, as it is written > "For I am poor and needy." He placed himself among the pious, as it is written > "Guard my soul, for I am pious." 

Because of this, a person must not present himself as wicked. And if you say [he should not], then he should never specify his sins? Rather, when he specifies his sins, then he is "pious," for he comes to receive repentance. He removes himself from the <term>Evil Side</term> <note>original: "sitra bisha"</note> which was his gathering place until now, and strives to cleave to the <term>Supernal Right</term> <note>the attribute of Mercy/Chesed</note> which is stretched out to receive him. And if you say that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not receive him until he specifies his sins from the day he came into the world...

-> **to account** <-

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Balak**<-

Those who become wise, even if they cannot fully grasp [the Divine], must nevertheless strive to merit the remembrance of wisdom. 
And regarding these wicked ones, through them all others are rectified, and after them, they return like living serpents <note>original: *tanninim chayin*</note> to their source. Service on high is not like service below; even when one is crushed like flowing water, one can still cling to the All, and everything is drawn after that and nullified within it. So too, the "wing of flight" <note>a metaphor for the speed and elevation of prayer</note> at the head of all gatherings does not move from a parched flight. And here, there was no "other side" behind them, as it is written: 
"The priest is with me for every expanse," for everything is here to be seen from behind in its hidden support. One does not need to wait for oneself or look here and there. So too, one does not need to specify their sins when asking from the "Abyss," for those who returned are like those below, and not those who are covered and cannot be reached, who are the upper chambers of the heights. Come and see: "The priest is with me for every expanse," and all are supported behind them. 

He placed himself <insert>King David</insert> as a poor man; he placed himself like those servants, as it is written: *Behold, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their masters.* And it is written: *Save Your servant, You are my God.* He placed himself like those who surrender their lives for the **Sanctification of His Name** <term>Kiddush HaShem: the act of self-sacrifice or martyrdom for Divine glory</term>, as it is written: *Gladden the soul of Your servant, for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul.* King David acted according to all these four "servant" roles before his Master. 

Rabbi Eleazar said: I have lifted my hands in prayer <note>original: *binlo*, a term for prayerful lifting of hands</note> before the Holy King, for the preparation of a person is to walk and confess, to send forth the word in prayer and to stir the heart, as it is written: *I have lifted up my hand to the Lord, God Most High.* We translate this as "I have lifted my hands in prayer," for our fingers contain hidden celestial mysteries. 
And the bow <note>the rainbow or the spiritual arc of prayer</note> acts in this way. I say that whoever arranges these four aspects before his Master and makes himself according to the [Divine] Will as is proper in this rectification, his prayer will not return empty. 

First, he must arrange praise before his Master and find favor before Him. This corresponds to the **Songs of Praise** <note>Pesukei D'Zimrah</note> before the main prayer. Afterward, he performs the **Standing Prayer** <term>Amidah: the central silent prayer of the Jewish liturgy</term>; he should stand as a servant to arrange the prayer of his Master. And after this, he completes all his prayer and its conclusion. 

On three occasions, he makes himself a servant in this prayer, as it is written: *Save Your servant, You are my God*; *Gladden the soul of Your servant*; and it is written: *Give Your strength to Your servant.* These three times one must place himself as a servant. Afterward, he must place himself among those who surrender their lives for the **Sanctification of His Name**, which is the unity of the **Shema Yisrael** <note>The declaration of faith: "Hear O Israel..."</note>. For anyone who directs his will according to this verse is considered as if he actually surrendered his life for the Sanctification of His Name. 

Afterward, he places himself as a servant like a beggar who enters and knocks at the gates of the highest heights when he says "True and Firm" <note>the *Emet V'Yatziv* prayer</note> and joins the theme of **Redemption to Prayer** <note>the transition between the Shema and the Amidah</note>. To show this in the Standing Prayer, he acts as one broken and poor, directing his will to be included among the poor with a broken heart and a crushed soul. 

Afterward, he places himself among the **Pious Ones** <term>Chasidim: those who act with loving-kindness beyond the letter of the law</term> at the blessing "Who hears prayer," to specify his sins. For a person must be alone when "He hears prayer," because on an ordinary day, He is ready to receive those who repent, and then he is called "Pious." These are the four aspects as they should be. Who can include all of this? He who needs to include them all and stands as a servant—this includes everything else. 

There are three "servants" corresponding to the three patriarchs, and they are all one, and their eyes are as one: *Behold, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their masters...* Once he has acted as a servant to these others—between the first servant and the second servant—he must surrender his soul for the **Unity of the Sanctification of His Name**, and regard himself as poor and destitute in the Standing Prayer, and place himself among the Pious at "Who hears prayer." He completes his prayer after he has finished and arranged everything. 

We have learned: at the moment a person arranges all these four arrangements with a willing heart, the Holy One, Blessed be He, opens [the gates] before him and spreads His "Right Hand" over him as a third servant, and calls out regarding him: *And You are My servant*, as it is written: *And He said to me: You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified.* And He pushes his prayer to—

It emphasizes that King David modeled these behaviors to achieve a direct connection with the Divine.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Balak**<-

...which he took and returned with its fragrances to the worlds. Rabbi Isaac came and kissed him. These are the general portions of all the surroundings. The third stands thus to be redeemed, as it is written: *Save Your servant, You are my God* <note>Psalm 86:2</note>. Whoever arranges this, it is known to him that the Holy One, blessed be He, is found within him, and calls out concerning him: *You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified* <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>.

Rabbi Isaac said: We have read in the Wisdom of Discipline <note>referring to ancient mystical traditions</note> and from the mouth of Rav Nachman how many ancient things—ancient words from the early generations—and when they taste them, they are unable to eat <note>meaning the depth is overwhelming</note> and it pushes them away. So it is, for the verse proves there are three "servants," yet they are one, and the Crown is one. And then, as you said, the Holy One, blessed be He, is to be crowned by him, as it is written: *For the children of Israel are servants to Me...* <note>Leviticus 25:55</note> and *they shall not be sold as a slave is sold* <note>Leviticus 25:42</note>. Because the Holy One, blessed be He, needs to be crowned by this third [level]. And "they shall not be sold" refers to the name of a [common] servant, for they belong to the Holy One, blessed be He.

Rabbi Eleazar opened and said: *Who among you fears the Lord... who obeys the voice of His servant?* <note>Isaiah 50:10</note>. What is the meaning of "who obeys the voice of His servant"? The companions have established this verse, and so it is: Whoever is accustomed to coming to the synagogue, and one time he does not come, the Holy One, blessed be He, asks about him and says: *Who among you fears the Lord, who obeys the voice of His servant, who walked in darkness and has no light?*

What is "obeying the voice of His servant"? It is as if one said the Assembly of Israel <note>the Shekhinah</note> says: Who gave, as it were, a man to the Master of the Exile, so that his prayer should be "obeying the voice," as if he were a living man in the world? Rather, that voice of the Levites' division at all times—he hears like that voice which the Holy One, blessed be He, calls to him, and is found in him, and calls him "His servant." And he shall be "obeying the voice"—like which voice? Like that which is called "His servant" plainly; a voice goes out concerning him that he is "His servant." Furthermore, that voice is heard in all those firmaments: that he is a servant of the Holy King. And this is: *Who obeys the voice of His servant, who walked in darkness and has no light.*

And is it because he did not come to the synagogue that he "walked in darkness"? Rather, for this reason, Israel gathers in the synagogues to pray to the Side <note>the holy side</note> that stands [ready], and then all the Supernal Lights <term>Nahorin Ila'in: the emanations of divine light</term> descend and spread out and hover over the worlds. And three times a day, the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra: the forces of impurity/evil</term>, male and female, roam the world. At that time, it is prepared for the exile <note>or "revelation"</note> so that there will be no accusation at all. And then it is a time for revelation, because they descend to arrange themselves in the mountains of darkness and the twilight departs. Then the power of the Supernal Lights is opened; they go out and guard the synagogues with their authority. They are like mountains over their heads.

And the Holy One, blessed be He, asks about that person who is not found there, and says: "Everything is because of so-and-so who was accustomed to being here, and now he has walked in darkness." He has moved away from the presence of the lights and ascended to the side of fear in the world, and left that wing of light which is like a wall, and he has no portion in it. "And has no light"—just as it was gathered and darkened over his companions who are there, many clouds are darkened from him, and he has no light now that he has walked in darkness. *Let him trust in the name of the Lord* <note>Isaiah 50:10</note>—this is the totality of the first "servant." *And stay upon his God*—this is the proclamation <term>Karuza</term> of the second "servant."

Rabbi Shimon said: Eleazar my son, certainly the spirit of prophecy rests upon you! Rabbi Isaac said: He is a free man who stands before them when they desire to seize prey. All the beasts of the world are strong, and the lion more than all of them. All the beasts of the world stand to take the prey from their teeth, and they have the strength to take the prey from their teeth. And they seize the prey and give it to all. "Who walked in darkness"—those who walked, they cover him. Rabbi Eleazar said: Because they are like a lamp of light to be spread out, "walked in darkness"—the dark ones to be spread out, they ascend the mountains and spread out immediately. In this manner, like a groom in the bridal chamber, including male and female. The bride goes out...

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion "Balak." The previous discourse likely touched upon the nature of sorcery and the character of Balak, the King of Moab. Here, the Zohar shifts into a deep esoteric interpretation of Balak’s lineage, specifically his father "Tzippor" (meaning "bird"), linking it to the celestial dwellings of souls.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Balak**<-

**And Balak** son of Tzippor saw what he saw. Until now, nothing has been missing from this moment. Regarding Balak, Rabbi Eleazar said: Blessed is he for what he saw. Rabbi Hiyya said: This is a hidden matter. Everything is written concerning the "bird" <note>Tzippor</note> from which he practiced divination, as it says: **"Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow <note>original: *deror*</note> a nest for herself"** <note>Psalms 84:4</note>. King David spoke these words at the gateway of the world. However, as we have learned, how many souls stand before the Holy One, blessed be He? All the souls of the world are there, but the souls of the righteous have their dwellings there in a specific order. Their dwellings are above and their dwellings are below. And so we have learned regarding the "bird" from which he divined: these are the spirits of the righteous.

We have learned that there are three rows within, and in each one, many holy spirits and souls are established from the hidden spirit of the righteous within the "Eye." No eye can know the spirits of the righteous within, for **"No eye has seen, O God, besides You..."** <note>Isaiah 64:4</note>. At certain times, there are daughters <note>perhaps referring to sparks or lower spiritual entities</note> who sit upon the throne, and at times two spirits roam and visit the place where they are needed. These times are like the roaming of birds; they are seen upon the walls of the Garden <note>Eden</note>, each one appearing like the sight of birds chirping every single morning. And their wings open to receive the exile <note>or the revelation</note> upon the waters, like a person who gazes upon it because in these days all of Israel are occupied with the commandments and the decrees of the Master of the world. Then, like the appearance of letters, birds fly and flutter over the walls of the Garden of Eden, hovering and going to protect the life of the world.

Rabbi Shimon said: Eleazar, you have certainly spoken well. Those who seek are those spirits that are there. What do you say of "and the swallow <note>*deror*</note> a nest for herself"? This "swallow" is the holy soul <term>Neshamah Kedoshah: the highest level of the human soul</term> that ascends above and rises to the hidden and concealed place that "no eye has seen, O God, besides You." 

Rabbi Shimon continued: Eleazar, you have certainly spoken well, and it is beautiful. But all of this is according to the Garden of Eden below, and so on, as you said, regarding the bird he divined with. These are the holy spirits who merited to enter and exit afterward in order to roam, and they were established thus. And these spirits—he certainly divined through them. Each one has known dwellings within, and until now they are all like a canopy for one another, since they do not yet have "freedom" <note>original: *deror*, a play on the word for swallow</note> and liberty from everything. The Holy One, blessed be He, desired for them a single hidden palace, concealed, which "no eye has seen, O God, besides You," and that palace is called "Bird" <note>Tzippor</note>. 

There, crowns upon crowns are placed... and on certain days, three times a year, the Holy One, blessed be He, desires to delight in the souls of the righteous, and He shows them that hidden, concealed palace which even the righteous who are there do not fully know or recognize. <insert>He opens the opening of his fledglings</insert>—these are the righteous who were perfected in holy ways, who merited the Written Torah and the Oral Torah in this world. They go and take two purities and are crowned before the Holy King, for the merit of their children in this world crowns them there. Who is the spirit worthy of all this? To open the fledglings to pass through to your dwellings. From here onward, come and see the King, for all is seen there like a canopy.

Rabbi Eleazar opened as before and said: The "bird" he divined with—this refers to Jethro. "And the swallow a nest for herself"—this refers to the protection that was in the Assembly of the Garden <note>Knesset HaGannit</note>... they turned like a chariot, all of them from the preparation of the Image, and they were established there and turned in the desert. When Balak saw that he was like a palm's breadth upon the link, he shielded them from there and went to the Assembly of the Garden. "And the swallow a nest for herself"—it is all one "Bird." The swallow and the bird are all one, except for the Holy One, blessed be He. And it says, "Balak son of Tzippor." Come and see what is written: "And Balak son of Tzippor saw." Did he see through his own merit? He saw through the kingship, but Jethro below rested and passed away, and this was the remainder that was left like a sea...

And they pushed...

## Main Text (Zohar)

And they pursued after him. **Balak** was a nickname <note>original: "takhna," a title or designation</note>, and the matter was transformed into a reproach. For he saw great wisdom and great judgment among those who were before him; for Jethro and his sons had attached themselves to the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Kneset Yisrael - the spiritual personification of the Jewish people</note>, and this one [Balak] sought to strengthen himself from the hidden powers below to rule over them at that time, as it is written:
> *And Balak the son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.* (Numbers 22:4)

"At that time"—what does "king" imply? That he was not king previously <note>suggesting he was appointed specifically to deal with the perceived threat of Israel</note>. And regarding this, it is written "son of Zippor" <note>Zippor means "bird"; a reference to his use of a mystical mechanical bird for divination</note>, for he did not act below [in the physical realm] alone. *And Balak saw.* It should have said "And Balak trembled." What is the meaning of "And Balak saw"? It hints that he perceived and knew that Israel was destined to fall into his hand at first <note>referring to the sin at Shittim</note>, but afterwards they would live by the hand of Israel. *And Balak the son of Zippor saw.* Rabbi Abba opened:
> *If you know not, O most beautiful among women, go out by the footsteps of the flock.* (Song of Songs 1:8)

The **Assembly of Israel** spoke before the **Supreme King** <note>The Holy One, Blessed be He</note>. What is the Assembly of Israel? She is the **Crown** <note>Atarah</note>, the gathering of the Bride, strengthened on all sides. For she gathers all the upper aspects into herself. And who are the "colors" <note>the various divine attributes</note>? As the work is called "Assembly." And if you say she is a Crown, it is because He passes over <note>original: "avor avar," a play on the word for 'transgression' or 'passing'</note> and does not give voice or cheek. For from her great **Faith** <note>original: "meimanuta"</note>, in which no blemish is found (Page 171b), they gave her twenty-eight delays in total. And she, when she is before all the camps that she gathers, passes over and prevents [harm], so that even the drop of the hoof does not strike drop by drop. This is because no faith was found below like that which was found in her, shining on every side without hindrance. And she is before Him, and they give her many gifts and possessions, one upon the other, and they do not hinder her at all; at all the gates they hinder them [the nations], but they do not hinder her, and then she is the Crown.

He passes over and [moistens] the cheek, as it were; He gives eighty and does not exceed, and acts with heat toward those who do not know her. Thus He does for the Assembly of Israel, and she learns from the holy merit of that time when she rises to gather delights and longings. And when wisdom is found in them—in Israel below—then a drop of mustard-seed-sized light and a surplus of whiteness reaches her, and she sits upon it for designated days. Then it is known above that there is wisdom in Israel, and joy is immediately awakened, and the staff of the below is moved, and the eyes are darkened from the scents that they smell, and He pushes away all lack in the totality of mercy.

Then **Samael** <note>The primary angelic figure of the "Other Side" or evil inclination</note> is awakened with a powerful voice to mix into the whole world, and "He called Esau his great son," etc. He is "great" in relation to the aspects of the **Other Side** <note>original: "Sitra Achra," the realm of impurity</note>; he is great and leads all the swords of the sea that are stirred by an evil spirit to lead them astray in the depths of the sea, like those within the heart of the sea. And when the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, acts with mercy, then all the weapons and all the blemishes of Israel are given to him [Samael], and he casts them into the depths of the sea. All his sides are called "depths of the sea," and they are... to them, and they are diminished before all other nations.

And when the sins of Israel are [removed], your righteous ones throw them and they are divided among their branches. These are the ones who are disgraced and degraded, set above like dogs before a table. And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, cancels all their debts and throws upon them that destruction of the paths, the wealth and possessions that they wanted to give to Israel—He passes over them and takes them. And immediately they are all as one, and He throws them upon the other nations.

Come and see: the Assembly of Israel is a "freewoman" as before, a merchant, etc. And she belittles herself before the Supreme King. And then she begins to cry out and says: "Where <note>original: "Eichah," the opening word of Lamentations</note> is my soul? Where is the gate? Where are the gates?" Like those who are enclosed, like those who are parched, like those who are at the point of the sword without a gate. Like those parched in the House of Bread <note>Bethlehem</note>. "Where are the gates?" Like those parched at the House of the Sword. And twice it says "Where" <note>Eichah</note>. The gate and the gates are as one. He should have mercy. So too, in the end, she speaks concerning Israel. Rather, she speaks with her mouth: "Where is the gate for the Assembly in her **Exile** <note>original: "Galuta"</note> when they are among the other nations? Where are the gates of the enclosed?" How will the dew and water drip upon them in the heat of the sun? It is like the time when Israel cries out from their distress, and the surrounding medicines are wafting.

## Main Text (Zohar)

They are weakened and scattered by the powerful rages of Gehenna <note>The place of spiritual purification/punishment</note>. Why has a knife not been prepared for you? And you find yourselves as mere bones. And they said concerning the gate, it has twenty-five primary colors. Twenty-five fats like holy species for the flow of wealth that they knocked upon, and their flames—and you find all this, and you sit wrapped in a cloak and are unable to act for them or to grant them vengeance. He said to her: **"If you do not know, O fairest among women"** (Song of Songs 1:8). This implies: if you do not know, O fairest among women, go and see; but if you do not know how to strengthen yourself and gather the strength to rest upon this. **"Go your way by the footsteps of the flock"**—like the footsteps of whom? These are the poverty-stricken students of the sages who drip with Torah. **"And feed your kids."** These are the ancient ones of the branch who are removed from them, and the houses of the upper academy are impoverished and pressed **"beside the shepherds' tents."** Regarding the form of the shepherds' poverty, it is not written "in," but rather **"upon the shepherds' tents."** This refers to the Academy of Metatron <note>The celestial prince/scribe who oversees the lower heavens</note>, for there are all the powerful ones of the world and the leaders of the generations, all of them in the world of "lack and surplus" in everything the inhabitants of the world require, for all the "footsteps of the flock" are strengths, as we have said.

Rabbi Elazar said: "The footsteps of the flock" are the students of the Creator who come later into the world and find it a ruin like a sharp sword, with the path open. Because of this, they renew ancient words every day, and the Assembly <note>Knesset Yisrael/The Shekhinah</note> is comforted by them, and she comes to learn from them, just as it says: "Arise, O Assembly of Israel..." <note>original: "ויקם כ"י" - likely referring to the personified Shekhinah rising from the dust</note> and she is comforted. Rabbi Abba said: It is certainly so. And it is all one matter. For when it says **"If you do not know for yourself"** <note>original: "לך" - literally 'to you' or 'for yourself'</note>—why "for yourself"? Rather, in every place where Israel is in exile, I <note>The Divine</note> will be with them in exile. And regarding this, it is written **"for yourself."** "In all their affliction, He was afflicted" (Isaiah 63:9). **"Go forth for yourself, O fairest among women."** "You are beautiful, my love." "The fairest"—she said that wisdom is established entirely in this way. And they said to her, "Fair is her departure." "The fairest in the assembly"—"You are beautiful, my love." This "fairest" is the Assembly of Israel, for the kindness she performed for the Assembly was like a kindness done for His sake, and He was zealous for your sake. Everything you did for the Assembly as a kindness was for My sake, and I was zealous over this, even though the deeds were hidden.

Rabbi Elazar said: We must wonder at the stoning <note>The legal punishment</note> as it is written:
> **"If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son... then his father and his mother shall lay hold of him..."** (Deuteronomy 21:18-19)

And we have learned in their houses that the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses: Moses said to Him, "Master of the World, is there anyone here who would do such a thing to a prophet?" And the staff was distant before me in wisdom—everything the Holy One, Blessed be He, does for the Assembly of Israel from the beginning of the world is a good thing. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him, "Moses, my beloved, write what you write and receive your reward." You know, and your wisdom knows even more, what is before us regarding that deed of the secret of Korah and the molten image. In that hour, He signaled to Yofill <note>The Angel of Torah; original: "יופיל"ל"</note>, the Great Prince of Torah. Moses said: "I have seen the head of this Korah." It is written: **"If a man has"**—this refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: **"The Lord is a man of war."** **"A son who will not listen. Stubborn and rebellious"**—as it is written:
> **"For Israel is stubborn like a stubborn heifer"** (Hosea 4:16)

They are blind to the Voice, and their heart is against the voice of his mother, and they chasten him: this refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the Assembly of Israel <note>The Divine Father and Mother</note>. **"And they call him"**—as it is written: **"And the Lord warned Israel and Judah by the hand of every prophet and every seer..."** but he did not listen to them. As it is written: **"And they did not listen to Me..."** **"Then his father and his mother shall lay hold of him"**—with one mind and one wisdom. **"And bring him out to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place."** **"The elders of his city"**—the elders of the city strike him. They hit him and said "to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place." "The elders of his city" refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and "the gate of his place" refers to the Assembly of Israel. "The elders of his city" are the Ancient Days, the days of old, for they are all the "gate of his place"—this is the Additional Service of the Sabbath <note>Musaf</note>. And he acts even though they all know the merit above; it is because he is pure to show that they are close to Israel and rejoice in them, and any relative does not reject the pure one for the relative, and he is exempt for the pure one. In the introductions, what is written? "To the elders of his city and to the gate of his place." What is written? "And they shall say to the elders of his city" alone.

## Main Text (Zohar)

To return and stir up his place is not written, but rather "they shall not rise up to inherit the city" <note>referring to the spiritual displacement of the nations</note>. As it were, certainly, and where are the rest of the nations?
They are rebellious and defiant, a band of thieves who strike with a voice. For at first it was not written except "and a booth" <note>referring to a temporary shelter or protection</note>. And who caused them to be rebellious and defiant toward the Fathers in Heaven? It is because they were among the rest of the nations, as it is written: "But they mingled with the nations and learned their works" <note>Psalm 106:35</note>. And it is written: "The people ate and prostrated themselves to the calf." This established their entire path—all their actions were like those of the other nations. This caused them to be rebellious and defiant toward the Fathers in Heaven. And their laws, all those sorcerers of the city, all those other nations who were skilled in wisdom and twisted crowns and built towers—from this, we understand why this section was written. And come and see: all this is found in the gathering of the world. "If you do not know, O fairest among women, go out by the footsteps of the flock" <note>Song of Solomon 1:8</note>—we have established that these are the **synagogues** and **study halls**. "And graze your little goats"—these are the **schoolchildren** <note>original: "Yanuqei de-bei Rav"</note> who have not tasted the taste of sin in the world. "By the shepherds' dwellings"—these are the **teachers of children** and the **heads of academies**. For "by the shepherds' dwellings" refers to those who are protected from the evil kings of the Amorites, from whom Israel took their land to graze their cattle; and in the place of pasture, Israel took this land. Then Balak heard that the land which was considered significant—all that Israel did in this battle—they destroyed it until they made it a place of pasture. Then he strove with all his effort and went directly to Balaam.

"And Balak saw..." Rabbi Hezekiah opened: "**Thus says the Lord**: Keep justice and do righteousness, for My salvation is near to come..." <note>Isaiah 56:1</note>. How beloved are Israel before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>The standard Rabbinic title for God</note>, for even though they sinned before Him and provoked Him at every time, He creates merits for them like a shield.
Rabbi Hamnuna the Elder said: The Sages established three "Gates" of laws in the orders of the Mishnah. The first order is the **Four Principal Causes of Damage** <note>original: "Arba'ah Avot Nezikin"</note>: the Ox, etc. The second is the "Pit" and the "Tooth" that are found. Come and see: there are three partners, and this is the secret of the "Lost Object." Why is this? Because the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> always performs merits for Israel. And those who are in the order of the Mishnah, which are three "Gates," they arranged them thus: "Man" who strikes, as it is written: "For every matter of transgression" <note>Exodus 22:8</note>—and this transgression is theirs entirely. And they established them: "for an ox, for a donkey, for a sheep."
<term>Bava Kamma</term> <note>The "First Gate" of the Talmudic order of Damages</note> deals with these matters.
<term>Bava Metzia</term> <note>The "Middle Gate"</note> deals with "every lost object."
<term>Bava Batra</term> <note>The "Last Gate"</note>—this is where "Man" is called regarding damages. For when one reaches the Middle Gate, the end of the beginning is said; this Last Gate, why? Since the verse is found, it certainly says that this is the law to be derived from the power of the Sages. "Thus says the Lord"—behold, in every place in the Scriptures where it is written "Thus says the Lord," it is not written so regarding Moses. Rather, because Moses was a prophet who looked through the <term>Luminous Mirror</term> <note>original: "Aspaklaria de-Nahara" - a metaphor for clear, direct prophecy</note> of above, "Thus" <note>original: "Koh"</note> is not written regarding him. But the other prophets saw through the <term>Non-Luminous Mirror</term> <note>original: "Aspaklaria de-la Nahara" - indirect or veiled prophecy</note>.

> **"And now,** come please, curse this people for me..." <note>Numbers 22:6</note>

"And now"—Rabbi Eleazar says: Certainly the hour stood ready for him to do what they said was needed. At first, and not at first, it was fitting.
At first, how many of Israel fell by his hand? A small moment. He said: Certainly the time stands ready, and you did not say it correctly. "Come please" <note>original: "Lekha"</note>—it should have said "To you" <note>original: "Lakh"</note>. What is "Lekha"? He said: Everything was caused by that which his name "Koh" <note>Thus/So</note> was cast upon. "And now, come please <note>Lekha</note>"—come and wage war with that "Koh." "And now, come please"—as it says, "And now to profane the offering."
He said: Until now there was no one in the world who could prevail over them because they were in a place that had no opening. But now that the hour stands ready for you, go and wage war. And all the counsel of that wicked one <note>Balaam</note> was "Lekha," as it is written: "And perhaps I will happen upon 'Koh'" <note>Numbers 23:3</note>. I will uproot that "Koh" from its end. And both of them were in evil counsel without success, and he went and did not know that "Koh" stands behind them to uproot them from the world. "For they are too mighty for me"—for until now, at what time did they wage war with him? And they prophesied to him: in what place did they join the way for them? And they were men like men.

# Balak

The actions below are their strength. What is the meaning of **"For he is too mighty for me"**? <note>Numbers 22:6</note> Rather, that wicked man <note>Balak</note> was wise and saw into the distant future. He saw that King David, who would descend from Ruth the Moabitess, would be a mighty warrior like a beast, barking in the powerful wars of the King. Because their hope was lost at his feet, Balak said, "He is mighty," for one of their own kings would inherit that strength and emerge from the "crawlers" of Moab. **"Perhaps I shall be able to defeat him"** <note>Numbers 22:6</note>—the verse should have said "perhaps we shall defeat him" or "perhaps I shall defeat them." However, that wicked man was a wise sorcerer. He said: "From within, I know that one 'Lamed' <note>The letter Lamed, symbolizing a goad or power</note> is a mighty ruin, spreading his hands to consume your people." For it is written of both of them that they joined together, and we bring from that spirit a hand—no, no—and there shall be a remnant of the King for the world, and Moab shall not be broken beneath him.

He said to him: "What is this sword?" Rabbi Isaac said: That wicked man spoke to Balaam in two tongues. One was to benefit me, and one was to benefit me <note>meaning, for his own selfish ends</note>. What is the difference between them? He said to him: "One is for counsels and sorceries that are cast down, and they are many in the pot of sorcery." Since he saw that he would give birth to more than the mouth below, he said, "Cut off strength for me." And that wicked man, who did not leave any sorcery behind, gathered all kinds of counsels and swift, cast-down sorceries, and the pot of sorcery was nullified. They sought the hope of the earth, but it passed and turned away; they saw heat and it prophesied to him at the end. When David came, he cut off the bread; it passed and turned away, heat passed over, it passed and turned away, heat passed over, and he brought forth water from the deep and silver upon the altar. At that time, Abba Chasai said: That "pot" is the brain. **"Moab is my washpot"** <note>Psalm 60:10; original: *Sir rachtzi*</note>. "Moab is my washpot," and I will cast my shoe over Edom. 

But this also looked to the distant future, as it is written: "And Esau said to Jacob, **'Please let me swallow some of this red, red pottage, for I am exhausted'**" <note>Genesis 25:30</note>. "Let me swallow" <note>original: *hal'iteini*</note> means literal swallowing—opening the mouth and throat to consume. David said: "Let me swallow wisdom," and he cast upon him... to close his throat. **"Over Philistia I will shout in triumph"** <note>Psalm 60:10</note>. This too looked to the distance; he saw the "Evil Side" <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of spiritual impurity</term>, and the Philistines are from there. Why is a "shout" <note>Teruah - a broken trumpet blast</note> needed? To break their wall and their strength. Therefore, "Over Philistia I will shout," and I will return to see them.

**"Come now, therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me"** <note>Numbers 22:6</note>. Rabbi Hezekiah opened his discourse: **"And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins, and faithfulness the girdle of his reins"** <note>Isaiah 11:5</note>. This entire verse consists of words of holiness below, to make it known that "Righteousness" <term>Tzedek: often associated with the feminine aspect of the Divine, Malchut</term> is like a dedication, and "Faithfulness" <term>Emunah</term> is Righteousness. "The girdle of his loins"—we do not find a verse like this where Righteousness and Faithfulness are addressed as one. Why? Because all is one and they are of the same degree. 

However, at the time when she <note>the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> stands in her image and receives from the side of the "Distributors," she is then called "Righteousness" <note>Tzedek</note>, which is actual Judgment. This is the meaning of **"For when Your judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness"** <note>Isaiah 26:9</note>, for the level of "Judgment" <note>Mishpat</note> is Mercy. When Judgment is brought close to Righteousness, then everything is sweetened, and the inhabitants of the world can endure the judgment of Righteousness. Therefore, Righteousness is like a dedication. "Faithfulness" <note>Emunah</note> is the name used at the time when she is united as one, and all faces are shining; then she is called Faithfulness. Then there is a relaxation for all. When souls ascend, they are laughed at for many debts and sins, but since they were deposited <note>at night</note>, He precedes them with His mercies. Then she is called Faithfulness, and Faithfulness is entirely one. 

Now, "girdle of his loins" and "girdle of his reins"—why are they called "girdles" here, and why "loins" and "reins"? Even though they are one, they are two levels: one above and one below. Above, in the narrow part, they are called "loins" <note>matnayim</note>; below, at the end, they are called "reins/hips" <note>chalatzayim</note>, as it says, **"and gird your loins"**. At the end, at the top of the thighs, all the lower parts are stirred; they are detached from the heights and the thighs, and they give birth. This is what is written about them. Therefore, for might and for war, "Righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins," and thus it is necessary for the Merciful and Good One that "Faithfulness be the girdle of his reins." In one degree, He judges the world on two sides—one degree for Israel.

## Balak

->Balak<-

May He be blessed, and the name of His name is deep. He is "Perfect Righteousness" <note>Hebrew: *Tzedek*</note> so that He may be firm in His Foundation <note>The sefirah of *Yesod*</note>. For it is written: **"In righteousness shall you judge your neighbor"** <note>Leviticus 19:15</note>, and **"Righteousness, righteousness shall you pursue"** <note>Deuteronomy 16:20</note>. How many such instances are there? And this is so because in "Righteousness" <note>*Tzedek*, referring here to the attribute of strict Justice</note> there is no leniency at all. One who owes a debt to his fellow should not expect any leniency from the law, but rather strict justice where no favoritism is found. From within this, everything is weighed, and it leans to this side and that side to see who is the giver and who is the receiver. Because of this, one level is divided into two sides, and boundaries are established: one for the decree of the nations and one for Israel. At the hour when Israel went out of Egypt, these boundaries were surrounded—one for war and one for the general collective—and everything was done through Righteousness.

When Balak took counsel, he said: "Let them be weakened by curses." The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "The level that he seeks to diminish through curses and to strike—he knows that he is punished by Me." And as for striking, who can stand against Israel? For the power of their "Tongue" <note>Prayer and Torah study</note> is stronger than his. And because he sought to weaken them through curses and to strike them from that side, he thought: "If I can weaken them, I can do all my will." What is the matter of the "Tongue"? It is according to one's mouth and one's actions. [God says:] "Your mouth spoke, but the action is Mine."

**"For I know that he whom you bless is blessed, etc."** <note>Numbers 22:6</note>. Now, who knew this? His wisdom spoke. Regarding what was written previously, he [Balaam] created them like one who performs sorcery and divination: **"And he took all his land from his hand"** <note>Numbers 21:26</note> and four for a day, etc. But "For I know"—he certainly knew, and he knew through his own wisdom. **"He whom you bless is blessed"**—it is clear that a blessing was needed here, for he was going for the sake of a curse. It was not merely a matter of divination <term>Kosem: a practitioner of forbidden mantic arts</term> from Balaam; at first, it was a curse. Regarding the words **"He whom you bless is blessed,"** who spoke this? [Balak believed] that if he could strike the source of their blessing, he could overcome them. Rabbi Eleazar said: It was certainly necessary to say "That which [you bless]," as in **"His praise is in my mouth at all times"** <note>Psalms 34:2</note>. And it is written **"He whom you bless is blessed,"** for he needed a blessing from below. He spoke below like a serpent, like a viper. And David, who knew this, said "to bless *Et*" <note>The particle *Et* often signifies the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note>.

That wicked man [Balak] said: "That level of the 'Tongue' takes hold of them because of their blessings, for they bless Him every day. You must bless that level so it may be uprooted from its place." **"For I know that he whom you bless is blessed."** And when he is in that level, he will be cursed like a viper. Because of this, he sinned and searched for a way to uproot it from its place so it would not take hold of them. Immediately: **"And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went with the charms of divination in their hands"** <note>Numbers 22:7</note>, so that their wicked one [Balaam] would not see that they were carrying these sorceries, lest he be delayed by them.

He opened and said: **"And you, do not fear, My servant Jacob, and do not be dismayed, O Israel, for behold, I will save you from afar, etc."** <note>Jeremiah 30:10</note>. The verse stands and speaks, and they were awakened by it. But until now, there is a need to awaken further below. What is the secret of the "Covenant of the Tongue" that did not spare the level of the profane in exile? The holy people are like a garden. When the time came to seek mercy for Israel, what is written? "Spare the silver that you made for me as an offering," etc. They called out and He loved them. But he [the enemy] said: "What is this one level that You have raised for me?" It is called "You" <note>*Atem*</note> because it has no spreading out from the Name, so that it should not take hold of Israel. He prepared them from the world. Behold, the Name of this secret is to take hold of them, and it shall pass from its dwelling. He sought to uproot the Name, the root of the blood, until the end. **"And what will You do for Your great Name?"** <note>Joshua 7:9</note>, for the striking of my name is the root and foundation of everything. "You" are the Lord, and he damages it... he knew that it hangs there... and he restrained himself. **"Do not fear, My servant Jacob, etc."** <note>Jeremiah 46:28</note>—it is all one. **"For I am with you."** We have established: it does not say "For I have come with you," but **"For I am with you."** **"For I will make a full end of all the nations, etc."** <note>ibid.</note>. Among all the nations, I will make a full end. Rav Hamnuna the Elder said: The pressure and distress of Israel—how much good and wisdom and benefit it causes for them! The laxity of the other nations—how much shame it causes them! The pressure and distress of Israel causes them to be good and beneficial, and He strikes them...

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Balak** <-

A portion of the bride <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> is pressed and weakened toward the side of the nations, and their persecution and sweetness are all a "consumption" <note>Hebrew: *Kallah*, a play on the word for Bride</note> and an end below for them. For all the weakness and pressure they experienced in this world causes them weakness after the total consumption. Consumption, for it is a total end, and like the ground that misleads when you occupy yourself with consumption. Consumption is like the weakness of the burden of the pressure they had, and the consumption laughed, and the consumption shall pass away, their destruction is seen. These are Israel, who live through the destructions of this "Bride" <note>The Shekhinah in exile</note>. And the secret is that they shall have pressure and laughter to fulfill the **Assembly of David that is fallen, a Sukkah of Peace** <note>Amos 9:11; referring to the restoration of the fallen Divine Kingdom</note> toward the side of the nations who had weakness. The female, when she went out as a bride in weakness as they had at first, tells that **"Though I make a full end of all nations... yet I will not make a full end of thee"** <note>Jeremiah 30:11</note>. For she shall not be seen by you. For you were pressed at first many times like the pressure of the constant exile, and the pressure shall be suspended <note>variant: <term>the destruction is triple</term></note>, **"but I will correct thee in measure."** The verse calls out thus to provoke him: "I will correct thee in judgment," for My wrath and so on is held in the claim of judgment against them. Rather, "I will correct thee for judgment," but it is written: **"The Lord will enter into judgment with the ancients of His people"** <note>Isaiah 3:14</note>. And it is pleasing to the Holy One, blessed be He, to justify Israel before they enter into judgment, so that they can fulfill "for she rested," to be justified in every single claim. The Holy One, blessed be He, gives sufferings to Israel, and a city and a watch <note>troubles and vigilance</note> at every single time and in every single generation, so that when they enter the Great Day of Judgment, they will survive the judgment and the judgment will not rule over them. And it goes out, not engraved—what does this mean? Rather, when He corrects them alone and they do not enter into judgment with the rest of the nations, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings them within the tradition of judgment and He atones for them. And at the time when He executes judgment on the rest of the nations, what does He do? The Holy One, blessed be He, knows that they fear their own record-books <note>Greek: *chartis*, meaning a legal document or ledger</note>, and He gives a reminder of the sins of Israel and gathers them all to Him for the Day of Judgment. He precedes them to justify them, and for every single sin He strikes them with sufferings and city upon city. And the female was not in sufferings, and because of this, in the judgment of truth, He did not engrave from the world the reward of the folly of sufferings and city and watch; He did not engrave it for them so as not to block their sins, but to be avenged of the kings, city by city, so that you may be righteous for the Great Day of Judgment. When judgment appears below, He brings out many notes <note>Latin: *pittacia*, meaning slips of parchment or legal decrees</note> against them. And the Holy One, blessed be He, brings out the notes of the sufferings that Israel received for every single sin, and like the blemish of all their sins, and He did not make for them any justification at all; then he [the accuser] is confused in his life and dreams and cannot prevail over them. And King David said: **"For, lo, the wicked bend their bow, they make ready [their arrow upon the string]"** <note>Psalms 11:2</note>. And the mockery of this verse, they have established it as referring to Sennacherib and the appointed host of decrees and seals for every side. The verse refers to Samael <note>The Archangel of Evil</note> and his company, to say that all his works and counsels against Israel are all Balak and Balaam. That sorcerer felt a hard thing, and this is to say they worked for an evil sunrise. They said: Amalek—*Am Lak* <note>A people that licks</note>, *Ammakh Lakah* <note>Your people was struck</note>, they took for them the hint of this star, Lilith, this is an extra stone. Balak—*B. Lak* <note>In him is licking/striking</note>. He came to strike them according to his will. Balaam—*Bala Am* <note>Swallow the people</note>. There is no people, the exile of the shepherd is our name, he grinds to destroy them and uproot them from the world. But the Holy One, blessed be He, thought otherwise because they lived as a whole, all like Balaam, all of them, all of them—what letters to storm the nations? The depth of their thought has no dominion in the world. Rabbi Shimeon said: Eleazar, and you saw the donkey for all of Balak, he seized his height in the gathering. And Balaam, there his bones and his height were poured out. And such was the evil counsel they planned on the table. Upon the hardness of the difficulty to uproot and they sealed to labor evilly to devastate <note>Hebrew: *L'valek*, a pun on Balak's name</note> according to the mouth and according to the deed. That wicked one said: I preceded to mock and to laugh, the Generation of Separation <note>The builders of the Tower of Babel</note> strived and could not. They did a deed and the mouth was lacking from their tongue to return everything and they could not, and no wisdom remains for you, and your tongue is prepared on two sides; if you strike, your passing will break you, and you will see more lack. That side that does not desire to devastate according to your mouth and your tongue to be strangled, and the side is before you and all of it thus hangs thin...

To establish it for the Other Side, and thus it was necessary for that side.

**And he said** to them: "Lodge here tonight." Regarding them it is written, "And they spoke to him." And regarding them it is written that they waited for the understanding of "Lodge here tonight." Because at that time, after it was established, his sorceries were like the hour when the hidden mountain peaks are found and covered by a cloud like a crown; and the word of the Lord Almighty <note>original: *Shaddai*</note>—take His merit, for he defiled himself like a drug of the Lord. In these two things they showed love, and it was brought to them. From before and after. And because of these, they were explicitly released and went on their own. "And the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam" did not apply to the children of Midian, for such was the will of the tongue. But the merit of those of Moab staying caused them good, because below there they were sold, while those of Midian caused them evil. What is the reason? Because they sinned against the honor of the word of the Holy One, Blessed be He, while the others did not sin at all, and they were behind them according to the reason that the wicked one said. And I will merit you with the matter of the sin of the Lord. Immediately He informed those of Moab of this, and they stayed there. <meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Balak, specifically contrasting the prophetic experiences of the wicked Balaam and the holy Moses through a royal parable. It also transitions into a narrative involving Rabbi Phineas ben Jair and the hidden miracles performed by the Divine.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Balak<-

It is written: **"And God came to Balaam"** (Numbers 22:9). <note>The Zohar is troubled by the fact that God "comes" to a wicked person like Balaam.</note> A parable: To what is this comparable? To a king who sits in his palace upon his throne, and a certain **guard** <term>santar: a low-level official or gatekeeper</term> stands at his gate. The king said, "Who is that knocking at the gate?" They said, "It is such-and-such a guard." The king said, "Let him enter here so he does not defile the palace <note>original: *heikhala*</note>, for his mind is coarse and repulsive." The king said to him, "Do not move from here, so that my son may go and come near directly. But you, I will go down and be constrained within the **image** <term>dyokna: form or likeness</term> of a donkey, burdened by his son, so that he will not be afraid of him." The king went ahead and constrained himself and came to the prophet <note>Balaam</note>. And he said to him, "Guard, why are your feet in heat because of my son who went there? Behold, they are returning and doing business in my wrappings." For he saw that the king called to the law.

The king said, "Who is it?" They said, "Your beloved, so-and-so." He said, "The beloved of my soul! Let no other disgrace be called upon him, but rather say: 'The beauty of the king.'" And he said, "So-and-so, so-and-so, enter, beloved of my soul, my friend! I have prepared all the palaces for the king with you."

So it was with Balaam: he is a **guard** far from the Throne <note>original: *karsaya*</note> who knocked and called at the gate of the King. The King heard and said, "An impure guard shall not enter and shall not defile my palace. Rather, I must go out to his lodging so that he does not approach the gate of my son <note>Israel</note> and so he does not frighten him." He said to him, "Guard, guard, **'You shall not go with them; you shall not curse the people, for they are blessed'** (Numbers 22:12). Do not approach my children, for they are good for the house of the Master in everything."

But regarding Moses, as it is written: **"And He called to Moses"** (Leviticus 1:1)—the voice of the King and no other messenger. From the Tent of Meeting, from the holy palace, from the prepared palace, from the precious palace upon which the upper and lower worlds depend, He called to the prophet, and others could not approach the prophet.

**And Balaam said** to God, **"Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab"** (Numbers 22:10). And he said "king of Moab," implying such-and-such an important king, and see: "king of Moab." See the arrogance of that wicked man <note>Balaam</note>, for even Balak was of no account to him, as it is written "king" and he did not say "king *of* Moab," implying he was not fit to be king and was not made king. Regarding the first Moab, what is written of him? **"And he fought against the first king of Moab"** (Numbers 21:26)—a king son of a king, an important man son of an important man. But here, "king to Moab" is written; the verse is lacking "king of Moab." And come and see that he intended his arrogance toward the House of the Great, for all the kings of the world rule over their youths and are ashamed before their prophets.

Rabbi Phineas was going to see his daughter, the wife of Rabbi Eleazar, who was in labor <note>literally: "in the womb"</note>, and he was riding in haste. Until finally, as he went in haste, he arrived between two mountains. He said to them, "Like this staff, has a voice been awakened from the days of the world?" They said to him, "From the days of the world we do not know. From our own days we know, for one day there were those who strayed, highwaymen passing through this field, and they encountered those paths and cheapened them. And there was heard in this field a voice that said to her: 'Spark, strike and live!' And our God came to strike with that voice and burned them, and those children were saved." He said to them, "Mountains, mountains! By this sign that you have told me, may you be protected this day from the swords that are hidden for you."

Rabbi Phineas wept and said, "Master of the Universe, You have performed a hidden mercy for Your children, and those travelers were saved and I did not know it." He opened his discourse and said: **"To Him who alone does great wonders, for His mercy endures forever"** (Psalms 136:4). How much goodness <note>original: *tibu*</note> does **the Holy One, Blessed Be He** <term>Kudsha Brich Hu</term> perform for human beings, and no one knows it but He alone! A person rises in the morning and sees his foot upon the head of a **serpent** <term>chivya</term> that came to kill him, and as he moves his foot, he crushes its head and kills it, yet he does not know it—only the Holy One, Blessed Be He, alone knows. Thus: "To Him who alone does great wonders." A person walks on the road and hidden attackers lie in wait to kill him, and another comes to be given as a ransom in his place, and he is saved and does not know the goodness the Holy One, Blessed Be He, did for him. And as much as the person thinks he is alone, "To Him who alone does great wonders." He alone does it, and the other does not know. Afterward, a herald proclaims...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (Rashbi) and his companions as they travel. It focuses on the hidden meanings of Psalm 98 and the nature of divine "Song."</meta>

What was hidden from me has been revealed to those who constantly gaze upon the fields of the living—the voice of the companions who are invited to labor in the Torah. Hear this: Rabbi Shimon, his son Rabbi Elazar, and the rest of the companions were walking ahead, and they did not know who was following them. I knew it was the voice of Rabbi Shimon, and the fields and mountains bowed down; they revealed to me what I did not know. While those followers were walking and reached the prophet, they said to him: "Here you have been a merchant for us from the days of old, yet you have not provided for us by your hand." This bread is a struggle over the Torah. I saw a vision: they were sitting under a canopy, and a single branch shielded them, and from it birds gathered and chirped voices, hovering over their heads. These and those sat, merit not departing from their heads. That Elder raised his voice over them, and they heard. He said: "Because of this, we have traveled." Followers, followers, prepare yourselves, and the way shall not be prepared before you except for as much as you labor. You said two things: one like this, and one "One" <note>referring to the unity of God</note>. Look closely, companions: that place where Rabbi Shimon is hidden, how do we know it? He said to them: "Look at the footprints of the cattle, for that is the level they stepped." At the time when they <note>the cattle carrying the Ark</note> were not carrying wine, they were grinding wheat from the path—two things—and they went there, turning like this three times. Just as Rabbi Phinehas said to the companions: "Prepare to receive the reward of the 'Face of the Days' of the Woman." And they went out, swaying on their shoulders, kneeling and standing in a trance. Rabbi Shimon, like the braying of a donkey, said to the companions: "Behold, this is a voice of joy!" For they say that here a prohibition was awakened. Rabbi Shimon stood up, and the companions stood up.

Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse and said:

> **A Psalm. Sing to the Lord a new song, for He has done wonders.** <note>Psalm 98:1</note>

And so on. "A Psalm" (*Mizmor*)—the musical accent is raised upward. We read this as a "pruning" <note>The word *Mizmor* shares a root with "pruning" or "cutting," implying the removal of harsh judgments</note>, but it is a drop of the flavor of "this," for that Psalm comes to be crowned as a supernal crown high above the heads. And it is taught: "Lift up the stone, seal the song." Those cows, all of them were lowing as they went. The fruits are the radiance of Kindness (*Chesed*), the fortune of the "One." They were saying: "Sing to all that is good," to the many appointees, to the many levels that were coming there and went out to receive Him on the road plainly. And they were saying: "Sing to Him a new song"—this is the <term>Male (Dechar)</term> aspect. What is the reason? "Song" (*Shir*) is masculine, whereas "A Song" (*Shirah*) is <term>Female (Nukba)</term>. Even there, on the lower path, this [song] went out from the exile, and nothing more; therefore, it says "this song" (*ha-shirah ha-zot*) in the feminine. But here, it is the [higher] path, and that which was hidden in the treasury was revealed. And because of that which was hidden within it, it is called a "New Song" (*Shir Chadash*) in the masculine. "For He has done wonders"—just as He did among the Philistines and what He did to their idols. **His right hand and His holy arm have gained Him the victory.** Who is "Himself"? That very Psalm, the essence of the Holy Supernal Spirit that is hidden within it. "His Right Hand"—that is the inheritance of this vision. His Right Hand was strengthened by that Psalm, and He did not grant it to any other. Here it must be revealed: as long as the Right Hand stands, it dances, just as it was strengthened by this Psalm which He placed before Him, so that His Right Hand would be strengthened. Like a man who stands before his son and says, "Who shall draw near to my son?" But when he turns away, he shows his hands over his shoulders and behind him, and he turns away with a hand of foolishness, as it were. At first it is written:

> **Your right hand, O Lord, is glorious in power.** <note>Exodus 15:6</note>

Like the power that is supported above in its arrangements. They call his garments "Male," like that power. That Right Hand is glorious and strengthened like power. He will draw near to His son. But afterward, what is written?

> **He has drawn back His right hand from before the enemy.** <note>Lamentations 2:3</note>

He placed His right hand on His shoulder and pushed him away with a hand of foolishness as before. His right hand was before Him in joy, but afterward it was behind Him on His shoulders to push him away. Here, "His right hand and His holy arm have gained Him the victory"—these are the <term>Two Arms (Trin Dru'in)</term> <note>referring to the sefirot of Chesed and Gevurah</note>. Behold, those cows did not grow angry at the covering of God, even though there was an idol among them; they sang this song. Like the braying of a donkey, which is usually forbidden, they broke out in song. Companions, you might say that a donkey does not have a soul, yet it recognized the Master of the World. Go and see the donkey of Balaam, which stood to lower his path entirely.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Balak<-

Deeply hidden and unique is this matter. Furthermore, we have seen that when Balaam looked from above, a powerful and sealed matter came upon him regarding the "mouth of his donkey." Regarding the ten things created at twilight <note>The Mishnah in Pirkei Avot 5:6 lists ten miraculous items created at the very end of the six days of creation, including the mouth of the donkey</note>, do you think a physical opening was opened in that place? Behold, the condition was set below by the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu"</note>, and the spirit of everything was not handed over to the external forces, nor do they praise the form of the Blessed One. For the "mouth of the donkey" is a lower level, belonging to the side of the Female <note>The feminine aspect of the divine emanations, often associated with the physical manifestation of miracles</note>. It was hidden and flowed upon that vision, and when the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> desired to reveal the level of the "mouth of the donkey," He unsealed it like the opening of the Great Abyss, which had been wise/hidden until that time. When that time arrived, that opening opened and labored over it, a matter similar to: **"And the earth opened its mouth"** <note>Numbers 16:32</note>. 

One must look at what was prepared there in the earth. "The mouth of the donkey" is to be looked at as the spirit that resides in the mouth of the donkey. The "Mouth of the Crown" <note>referring to a higher spiritual source</note> is in this likeness; for the "Mouth of the Crown" is that level which is appointed over it below. These are the secrets of the letter *Vav* <note>The sixth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing a connecting channel</note>, and they were the seekers of water. Three "mouths" were created at twilight as the day was being sanctified: the mouth appointed over all other mouths, which shows the beauty of the day as it ascends and is sanctified. That which is called the "Mouth of the *Vav*" at twilight joined the other mouths. To sanctify the day, the mouth of the hidden one rose above all—the "Mouth of the *Vav*." 

They saw Rabbi Phineas who was coming toward them. Rabbi Phineas saw and looked upon Rabbi Shimon. He said: The "Mouth of <term>the Lord</term>" <note>original: "YHVH"</note> has opened, which is not sweetened by his copper divinations <note>A reference to Balaam’s sorcery vs. Rabbi Shimon’s divine inspiration</note>. They rejoiced together and sat down. As soon as they sat, all those birds that were providing shade for them flew away and scattered. Rabbi Shimon turned his head and signaled to them with sounds, saying: "Birds of the sky! Do you not perceive the glory of your Master who stands here?" They stood still and did not move from their places, but they did not draw near to them. 

Rabbi Phineas said: Let them go on their way, and tell the one appointed over them that previously they were under his authority, but now they are not under his authority. All of this is a wonder for the day of hope, when the cloud rises between strong peaks and is not scattered. Those birds scattered and stayed. Behold, three of your forces spread out into the branches on three sides, and there is something like a likeness before them. All the companions rejoiced, and Rabbi Phineas and Rabbi Shimon were honored. Rabbi Phineas said: There is great sorrow for those birds; we do not wish to burden living creatures, for it is written: **"And His mercy is over all His works"** <note>Psalms 145:9</note>. Rabbi Shimon said: I did not intend to trouble them at all, but the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> has mercy on us to be wise and to complete the rejection of His gifts. 

They sat under that tree and drank from the water and were refreshed there. Rabbi Phineas opened his discourse and said: **"A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and flowing streams from Lebanon"** <note>Song of Songs 4:15</note>. "A fountain of gardens"—is there no fountain except that of gardens? Behold, how many beautiful and precious fountains are there in the world! Rather, not all springs are equal. There is a fountain that comes out in the desert, in a dry place; that one is for the grace of the one who returns. But a "fountain of gardens"—how good and precious is that fountain for the sake of the goodness of the grapes and the beloved ones! Whoever draws near to it is entirely sweetened. Why? Because of the roses and the essence of the scent surrounding it. Like a rose is that fountain, and it surrounds other fountains. "A well of living waters"—so we have established that this refers to the Assembly of Israel <note>The Sefirah of Malkhut</note>. It is called a "fountain of gardens." What are these "gardens"? The <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> has five gardens in which He delights and takes pleasure with the souls of the humble, who hold them and keep their secrets hidden and concealed. All of them produce fruit and beloved things. Below them, there is a descent, and that descent guards the surroundings from all sides of the world. Beneath that descent, there is a hidden place for the destroyed ones, which produces debts for the righteous <note>likely referring to the testing of the righteous</note>. And this descent is bound and becomes a fountain that waters them. "A well of living waters"—when it is needed, it is a fountain, and when it is needed, it is a well. What is the difference between this and that? It is not seen when it is measured...
