<meta>This page continues the Zoharic commentary on the Torah portion Balak. The previous section likely discussed the spiritual nature of the soul and its connection to divine sources. Here, the text transitions into an allegorical interpretation of the laws of warfare, specifically the prohibition against destroying fruit trees during a siege, applying it to Torah scholars during times of divine judgment.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...death from its fullness. When the waters ascend to their fields and jugs <note>original: "kaduzis," likely a corruption of the Greek 'kados' for jar/pitcher</note> from the hidden side. What are these jugs? These are the colors arranged to plant all merits in the pools of water, and the jugs drip above, one after the other, sweet waters of the soul that follow after them. So these are the sources that emerge from the hidden side above and become jugs in all the springs. Thus, the secret is hinted to us in the hidden place, that one who does not draw near to this spring is called by this name. Come, open and see, as it says: **"When you besiege a city for many days, to wage war against it to seize it, etc."** <note>Deuteronomy 20:19</note>. "When you besiege" <note>The Hebrew root T-Z-R can mean to besiege or to form/fashion</note>—just as there are many layers of merit in every single word, there are many counsels, many good things for the heart, many pearls that shine to every side. There is not a single word in the Torah that does not have many colors shining to every side. This verse follows its literal meaning, yet it contains sixty methods of midrashic interpretation, and it contains sublime wisdom to rebuke those who need it. Happy is the portion of one who strives in the Torah constantly.

Regarding one who strives in it, what is written? **"But his desire is in the Torah of the Lord, and in His Torah he meditates day and night"** <note>Psalms 1:2</note>. **"And he shall be like a tree"** <note>Psalms 1:3</note>—why is this verse placed immediately after? Rather, one who strives in the Torah day and night will not be like a withered tree, but rather established "like a tree planted by streams of water." Just as a tree has leaves, bark, sap <note>literally: "brain" or "marrow"</note>, branches, and joints, and it has a life-force that ascends seven times to ten, ten for planting; so too the words of Torah have the literal meaning of the verse, the homiletical interpretation, the hint <note>alluding to the Pardes system of interpretation</note>, wisdom, <term>Gematria</term> <note>numerical values of letters</note>, hidden secrets, and most hidden secrets, one above the other. There is the parable and its solution, the impure and the pure, the forbidden and the permitted. From these, branches spread out to every side, "and he shall be like a tree." And he is not separate from all wisdom.

Come and see how beloved are those who strive in the Torah before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>The standard Rabbinic title for God</note>. For even at a time when judgment hangs over the world and permission is given to the Destroyer to perish, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> commands him concerning those who strive in the Torah. And thus the Holy One, Blessed be He, says to him: "When you besiege a city" because of their sins, to wage war against the former ones who were established in judgment for "many days." What is meant by "many"? Three days, one after the other, are called "many days." So too here, "when you besiege a city for many days"—three days, one after the other, to make known that there is a plague in the city. From here we learn that "many days" refers to three days, as it is written: "And if a woman has a discharge of her blood for many days" <note>Leviticus 15:25</note>. Are these truly "many days"? Rather, three days one after the other are called "many days." So too here: **"When you besiege a city for many days"**—three days one after the other to make known that there is a plague in the city.

Come, and I shall command you concerning all the members of My house: **"You shall not destroy its trees"**—this refers to the Torah scholar in the city, who is the "tree of life." And if there is one who gives merit, who has the counsel for the city to repent from judgment and teaches them the path in which they should go—concerning this, **"you shall not destroy its trees by wielding an axe against them."** Do not execute judgment upon him, and do not cast upon him the burning pledge, that skin-garment <note>referring to the physical body or the forces of mortality</note> that kills the rest of the people of the world. **"For you may eat from it"**—and does that Destroyer eat from any of it? Indeed, **"for you may eat from it"**—this "eating" is a powerful one for all the mighty holy spirits that emerge from him. For there is no merit or repentance for the Holy Spirit in that essence except for the Torah that he testifies to, and everything, as it were, He sustains and gives him food in that essence more than all the sacrifices of the world. Regarding a sacrifice, what is written? "I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey," as it is written, "Eat, friends" <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>. And the food that is drawn from the Holy Temple and through His sacrifices belongs to the Holy One, Blessed be He. But those words of Torah, and the Torah that one strives with in his mouth, are likewise **"for you may eat from it."** There is no food in that essence except "from him" and those who intend and understand that "from him you shall eat," and He sustains it. **"You shall not cut it down"**—wait, be careful with him, do not approach him, for man is a tree...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on Parashat Balak, specifically focusing on the spiritual battle between the "Open Eye" of Divine Providence and the "Evil Eye" of the sorcerer Balaam. ## Balak

->Balak<-

The Open Eye <note>original: "Ayin Pekicha" - refers to the ever-watchful, merciful gaze of God</note> which is not called a root, for it is not known above or below. Until that great and mighty tree, which is the root of the side of blessing, etc., for those who are not always known to that root lean upon it. Before you, all things are a matter of order, as it is written: "You shall not afflict his eye" <note>A mystical interpretation of protecting the spiritual vision</note>; it is their head and counsel, and it is not prepared to be given before you. Just as He gives them counsel to be established and to dwell in the proper measure, and to establish for them kingship and various kinds of sparks and scribes. To all who glorify. What is "to all before you"? To all that is in front and to ascend before you, from that which is yours, like a light in the Crown <term>Keter: the highest Sephirah or Divine emanation</term> of the worlds; and the lower beings are not able to enter there. And who is the level that merits to enter there? It is the inner part, for it is a light more powerful and of mighty strength. And since this counsel is given, then sin is atoned for their inner being, and they are accepted with favor before Him.

And all this **the Holy One, blessed be He**, commanded to those who labor in the Torah, as mentioned above. Worthy are those who labor in the Torah! Those who labor in the Torah are the great trees in all the worlds. See what **the Holy One, blessed be He**, did: He planted trees upon trees, and He planted this new thing. And not just one tree, but three great trees spreading branches to every side. **The Holy One, blessed be He**, made them and gave permission before Him so that these trees would never be destroyed. And this is a sealed fountain; and until this day they stand there and testify from the altar of water, and they call them "sons," just as Phinehas acted according to his manner.

Rabbi Eleazar said: It is written, "And she took for him also..." and "she bore a son and called his name Gad," etc. And Joseph took for his house... and Rachel was before him. Rather, everything was done by the son of the world's testing. When Joseph saw the eye of that wicked one <note>referring to Esau in the historical context, or Balaam in the spiritual context</note> looking at his mother, he was afraid for her. He went out from the shoulders <insert>of his mother</insert> and spread his arms and his body and covered her, so that the wicked one would not cast his eye upon her.

In this same manner: "And Balaam saw Israel." "His eye" is written <note>The Hebrew text uses a singular form "eye" to imply the Evil Eye</note>—that is the Evil Eye. "And he saw Israel dwelling tribe by tribe"—he wanted to gaze upon them with malice. What is "dwelling tribe by tribe"? It means the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine immanence of God</term> of Joseph was there, and the Divine Presence of Benjamin. Regarding the Divine Presence of Joseph, the Evil Eye has no power over it, as it is written:
> **Joseph is a fruitful bough** (Genesis 49:22)
What is "a fruitful bough" <note>Hebrew: "Ben Porat"</note>? It means he increased his stature to cover his mother. "A fruitful bough by a well" <note>Hebrew: "Alei Ayin," literally "above the eye"</note>—meaning the Evil Eye has no power over him. Regarding the Divine Presence of Benjamin, it is written:
> **And He dwells between his shoulders** (Deuteronomy 33:12)
And it is written, "He shall dwell in safety." What is "in safety"? That he does not fear the Evil Eye and does not fear evil encounters.

That wicked one <note>Balaam</note> said: "Worthy is this servant-wall that is established!" But he looked as was fitting. Rachel was there beneath the eye of that wicked one, protected and praised. What did she do? She went out and spread her wings over them, beneath the eye. Therefore: "And Balaam lifted his eyes and saw Israel"—he saw the **Holy Spirit** <note>Ruach HaKodesh</note> spreading over the protective covering. And the Spirit of God rested—upon whom? Upon Israel, for He spread His wings and protected them. Immediately, that wicked one turned backward. At first, he saw the mouth, and then he saw the sea beneath the eye. **The Holy One, blessed be He**, said: "At the hour Joseph saw his mother Rachel, so that the eye of that wicked one should not rule over her, by your life! At the time when another Evil Eye comes to look upon your children and your mother's children, she shall cover them. You covered your mother; your mother shall cover you."

"And he lifted his eyes and saw the Assembly." A voice called out in the spirit of wisdom that speaks in the seas to the flesh of the world's children who stand in the image before **the Holy One, blessed be He**, to atone for their sins. And that Accuser <term>Satan/The Prosecuting Angel</term> stands over them, intending to rebuke them for their sins. What is that image? It is as it is written:
> **To appease his face with the tribute that goes before me** (Genesis 32:21)
After he receives the gift, that Accuser lifts his eyes and sees Israel afflicted in fasting, and he covers his feet. He sees them there, going out in their fasts, standing in that manner...

It emphasizes that those who study Torah and practice self-affliction (fasting) are shielded by Divine wings.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

In a lamentation for his weeping, he said: "Who has power over you, Holy Name? Who has power over you to forgive his sins?" And he said: **"The children whom God has graciously given your servant"** <note>Genesis 33:5</note> etc. They did not begin to prophesy at all. However, once they received that light to be transformed for them, he lifted his eyes and saw Israel in this manner. It is written that because they are His, they stand thus. He forgives his sins and says, "Who has power over you?" and mentions the children. What is the meaning of "Who has power over you"? Rather, he said: "Supplication and grace you shall seek before the King." Woe to those living infants who stand thus!

"Who has power over you?" And he mentioned the children. The Holy Spirit <note>original: Ruach HaKodesh</note> spoke, and upon it, the cantillation mark is raised like a hidden mountain. **"The children whom God has graciously given your servant."** Rather, the Holy Spirit said: These are the infants who have not tasted milk nor tasted the taste of sin, and the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: HaKadosh Baruch Hu</note>, gave them the power of that "angel" <note>original: Mamka - likely referring to the celestial prosecutor or the power of Esau/Samael</note> of yours, and he subdues them all with rebuke. And immediately, "from the hand of their oppressors there was power" <note>Ecclesiastes 4:1</note>, and this is "your servant."

As soon as he heard your camp of infants, he immediately ascended to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and said: "Master of the Universe, all Your earth is truth in judgment, and this living oppression rests upon Israel because of their sins. Their infants, who have not sinned before You, are being handed over to this 'angel' to kill them all with rebuke." And the Holy One, Blessed be He, took his words to heart and had mercy on them. That reason was not to be closed off like infants. And that Accuser took his resentment from that "angel" who descended to destroy. To me, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave those who prophesy like calves and wise ones, and to that "angel" of mine, He delivered infants with total rebuke, though they had not tasted the taste of rebuke. Immediately, he went to remove them from under his hand, but he could not prevail over them.

And regarding this, he preceded him and said to him: **"The children whom God has graciously given your servant."** To that servant of yours, there is total rebuke and total sin. And so that there would not be a reason for my "angel" to wait any longer, he sought to remove them from his hands. When the prayers of Israel ascend in this manner before the Holy One, Blessed be He, what is written? **"And he passed before them"** <note>Genesis 33:3</note>. This is the Holy Spirit who passes before them all. "And their King shall pass before them" <note>Micah 2:13</note>. And he pushed and passed before them and settled into the level of **"seven times"** <note>Genesis 33:3</note>. He turned himself toward the seven supernal levels that are above him, and gathered himself to include them with him, every single one. **"Until he came near to his brother"**—to that level of Mercy, for "son" and "daughter" are "Israel, My firstborn son." As it is said:

The Holy Spirit prepared to rouse itself until he drew near. Once he reached him, he sought their camp and showed him the youth of the children below and the two supernal ones for the hidden palace. The Prophet of Yom Kippur <note>The High Priest or the spiritual essence of the Day of Atonement</note> saw them and sought mercy for Israel to atone for them. Then it is written:
> "For on this day He shall atone for you, to cleanse you" <note>Leviticus 16:30</note>
etc. It does not say "to atone you," but "He shall atone **over** you" <note>The Hebrew 'Aleichem' implies a covering or a supernal protection</note>. And the teacher taught: "The children"—these are the ones who are here. The Holy One, Blessed be He, gave them to be crowned with them, and to look upon them; the Evil Eye shall not rule over them because of the Good Eye. The Holy Spirit spreads its wings over them.

Rabbi Pinhas opened and said: "It has been fulfilled. I did not come on this path except to hear these words which are mine. Blessed is this path that I came to you, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, is here to be found with you. And not just one portion, but three. All who perceive this supernal image <note>original: diyukna</note> look toward that hidden and concealed arrangement." These three portions are three arms that investigate the secrets of Lebanon. And they are the image of three portions between Spirit and Wisdom, and the entire portion is covered. At that hour, these three [lights] rested: one on the head of Rabbi Shimon, one on the head of Rabbi Pinhas, and one on the head of Rabbi Eleazar. And branches spread to every side over the heads of the companions <note>original: chavrayya</note>.

Rabbi Pinhas wept and said: "Blessed is my portion, and my eyes have merited to see thus. And not over your way and mine do I rejoice alone, but over Rabbi Eleazar, a holy voice that is beloved before the Holy King like one of us." He stood and kissed him. Rabbi Eleazar said: "Sit in your standing, and let them live before me and your life is mine." Rabbi Eleazar stood.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the portion of Balak, focusing on the spiritual confrontation between the forces of Balak/Balaam and the protection of the Holy One. ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Balak**<-

**He opened** his discourse and said: *O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, etc.* <note>Micah 6:5</note>. My people, how much is the path of the Holy One, blessed be He, merciful toward His children! Even when they pressed to depart from the Kingdom, He gathered all words together for the evil prophet <note>Balaam</note>. When a son comes to his father, he shares with him all that troubles him, yet the father did not turn back his desire; He focused on him with words but he did not receive them. The Father said: "Is it for my children to do to my son as you have done until this day?" At that hour, He placed strength in His anger, all that he had learned from Me. And He did not cease to look upon his neck to see what he would do, but rather He became white <note>merciful</note> and appeared to the prophet and spoke soft words to him so that he would not intermingle at all with those forces. The Holy One, blessed be He, is the trust of those who fear Him, to give them their portion, yet they did not receive it. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "I have seen among my children those who receive the lashings of the harvest for their lives; they sinned with their heads." Woe, for because of all this they were struck by sin here, as it is written of every daughter... <note>The text here contains difficult Rashi script ligatures regarding the "image" or "form" of the sinners</note>... their image was found among them, as it is written: *Your sin is searched out* <note>Psalm 10:15, interpretive</note>... Woe, when I looked upon them and they were not recognized. Now the vision is prepared for the prophet, if they would only become wise. *My people, what have I done to you? and wherein have I wearied you?* My son and my beloved who trusts in Me, what have I done to you? I gave you dominion over all the members of the Palace, I gave you dominion over all the kings of the world, and I performed wondrous deeds for you. How much more so should you be wise! For *My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him.* Remember this, let it be remembered by you, what he consulted. Now we must look into what was the counsel of Balak against the holy people, for the Torah does not return to it for nothing, as it is written: *A wandering Aramean was my father* <note>Deuteronomy 26:5</note>... and the image of the waste was truly in him. And from that time, he was like a parched grain from his side below, and he extended his step further... this is the image of the youth to show from him. Since he was like a parched grain, the threads of his step were stretched out, and in this manner it was. And *from the hills* <note>Numbers 23:9</note> to change, like the Academy of the world, the hill of lovingkindness and mercy which established the world of all. Like the Academy and the oaths in one, they go to two sides: one, that this "Hill" shall never be separated from her son forever, and she never leaves him. And we have learned: she is hidden like the hidden things of the world. And the other, that this "Hill" is the son below, who is perfected in her to be dwelt in for the time to come, when the King Messiah shall come to deliver him. The "Hill" ascends and brings him within the wings in order to strengthen him and establish him in eternal life, and from her he shall go forth with the testimony of the day, the goodness for David. And this spirit is the scroll of the *statute* <term>Chok: a decree beyond human reason</term>, as it says: *The Lord hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee* <note>Psalm 2:7</note>. And from this wisdom, one speaks to this place called "Statute" and to the crown. He said to me: *Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.* On that very day, He brings him out from under her wings with many living beings, with many crowns, with many blessings, as is fitting. And the side of the "Statute" does not remain alone. And there shall be included in him the anointing of the search, the Son of Joseph <note>Messiah son of Joseph</note>, and there he shall be strengthened, and not like failing wine. And because she is the Lower Hill, in which there is no life, this Messiah shall die and be killed, and he shall be dead and crushed until he gathers life from this Hill and arises. And likewise, like the Academy of the Firmament, and from the Hill they are sweetened as one on these two sides. It is written: *Behold, a people that dwelleth alone* <note>Numbers 23:9</note>, in unity, without the mixture of the "other side." All unity is sweetened here, the life of *The Lord our God, the Lord is One*, for His spirit hovers like a living creature, and he is honored in the joy of his planting... the Lord is the burden below. And because of this, he is not unified in unity as is fitting. And because there is a burden below, he requires the spirit of the furnace in the two Academies, and thus the portion of the place of high words that rules below, according to the measure of the extension of this "treasure" upon the healing and the inner soul.

## Main Text (Zohar)

And he took and turned, but they were not found to be as firm as him. And concerning the lower firmness from the hair of the moon <note>referring to the "shaggy" or outer spiritual forces</note> of the nine sides, it finishes below with this sign. And in every place, at times, as is fitting. And within, it is not seen, and no writing or language could sustain them. And in every sign, they are able to look at the exact form and shape as is fitting. And there is no structure made that the spirit resting upon it is not seen, because they have no writing, and it does not bring them to look and to know anything, for behold:
> **They are vanity, a work of delusion.** <note>Jeremiah 10:15. The Zohar uses this to describe the empty nature of idolatry or sorcery compared to Divine reality.</note>

And the pure spirit is not seen in their thought or in their observation, and these have writing, and all of them are living and hidden.
> **Who has counted the dust of Jacob, and the number of the fourth part of Israel?** <note>Numbers 23:10. This is part of Balaam's blessing/prophecy.</note>

"Who" <note>original: *Mi* (מ"י)</note> is that supernal point, the beginning and the end, and understanding <note>Binah</note> in its hiddenness, and it does not stand to be revealed to all. Everything in their error is to be nullified, and to make a palace by His will. And they called "Who" to go around to find His image from "What" <note>original: *Mah* (מ"ה)</note>. He brought forth his female in the lower image... <note>The text here uses highly dense symbolic language regarding the union of the Sefirot and the emergence of the soul</note> ...and this is what brought Israel out to life. Just as He brought forth his female as one, a vision for the prophet. From her is the Bride, and from them the King and His fullness. He gave him strikes like a great and precious building, and brought him out like this spark in that expansion... He brought them both out as one, in the likeness of one expanding here and there; He brought them out according to the law and the covenant in a single moment... and they were created as one. And "the number of the fourth part of Israel"—the "fourth" <note>original: *Rova*</note> that was spoken of in your understanding is this spirit; merit is his portion... the fourth of Israel is the will from the love of Israel... but from the foundation of the body to the "fourth" in will, it is in his protection... and their will is in the measure of the body, "Who" brought it all out.

Rabbi Eleazar opened and said:
> **O Lord, in the morning You shall hear my voice...** <note>Psalms 5:4</note>

"O Lord, in the morning"—this refers to the "Morning of Abraham" <note>The Patriarch Abraham is kabbalistically associated with the Sefirah of Chesed (Lovingkindness) and the morning time</note> which is awakened in the world, as it is written:
> **And Abraham rose early in the morning.** <note>Genesis 22:3</note>

For when the morning comes, that "Morning" is awakened in the world, and it is a time of favor for all, to perform goodness for the entire world. Blessed are those who prepare the time of prayer to stand before the Holy King. And until the hour when the morning comes, all those who are the King's pious ones <note>Chassidim</note> merit the right hand <note>Chesed</note> at the time of prayer. He has decreed upon them, and all those who return in repentance and seek their requests before the Holy King, because at this hour a certain appointee <note>an Angelic force</note> goes out to the side of the **South** <note>The direction of Chesed/Mercy</note>, and all kinds of **healings** are in his hand. And from the side of the South, a certain spirit and appointee goes out, and that healing supports the one who is brought low by death. And when the prayer reaches before **the Holy One, Blessed Be He** <term>HaKadosh Baruch Hu: The standard rabbinic name for God</term>, He commands His spirit that they should not open a hindrance, because they are all life to the Holy One, Blessed Be He... it is a time of favor. When the Holy One, Blessed Be He, seeks the merit of that person, if he is found with merit and a proper appearance, He does good for him... and has pity on him... as it is written: "He who spares his rod hates his son." And those... are found before the Holy One, Blessed Be He, and that sickness that goes around and is awakened in the world, and it says:
> **How great is Your goodness, which You have hidden for those who fear You...** <note>Psalms 31:20</note>

Then that appointee goes out and does all that he was commanded. And if you say that the kinds of healing are in his hand as we said—it is not quite so, for the joy that is seen is the sickness in the hand of the Holy King <note>meaning God holds the ultimate power to transform illness to joy</note>. But at the hour when the Holy One, Blessed Be He, commands joy for that person, a protection goes out, and all those accusers who at times are over evil diseases are pushed away from him. Then that spirit which is taken from the side of the South, which illuminates that man, and the joy below is in the hands of the Holy One, Blessed Be He. And it is written: **"O Lord, in the morning You shall hear my voice."** It does not say "O Lord, in the morning *hear* my voice" <note>imperative</note>, but rather refers to the Morning of Abraham. "In the morning I will set [it] before You and I will look out"—this is the Morning of Abraham and the Morning of Jacob, as it is written:
> **The morning was light.** <note>Genesis 44:3</note>

And we translate this as: "The morning shone."

<summary>This page explores the mystical significance of the morning hours, linking them to the Patriarch Abraham and the attribute of Mercy (Chesed). It describes how prayers offered at dawn trigger angelic forces of healing from the "South" to descend and protect the sick.</summary>
<keywords>Morning, Abraham, Chesed, Healing, South, Prayer, Repentance, Sefirot, Jacob, Divine Favor</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical narrative from the Zohar Chadash on the Torah portion Balak. It focuses on the "Yanuqa" (the Wonder-Child) and his interactions with Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Abba, specifically regarding the death of a scholar named Rabbi Yose and the secrets of the "Morning of Joseph" and the "Bird's Nest."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Balak**<-

A bright and ready book I shall prepare for you, and it shall spread out before you. What do you lack? For at the time it is prepared for your ear to cling to the whole, I have arranged for you to bathe. And regarding the **Morning of Joseph** <note>Hebrew: *Boker de-Yosef*; a kabbalistic term referring to the light of Yesod (the foundational emanation) which brings sustenance and revelation</note>, it is said that it is the half-merit of Levi that stands. 

And it "spreads out"—what does this mean? For all the people of the world are but a drop of vinegar. This matter was established, and thus they said: I saw a true word that comes from afar, like that first covenant of the Holy Covenant <note>The *Brit Kodesh* or circumcision, representing the sefirah of Yesod</note> which was bright before the worlds existed. The worlds could not endure it until the Holy One, Blessed be He, made a garment to clothe one within the other, and so on through all the surrounding layers, until all the worlds were established in their existence and were able to endure. And in all of them, the levels spread out and were clothed in this, and they are called the **Higher Wings**, until they reach this "Morning of Joseph." And I saw like a shadow of all the higher lights, and all the higher lights depend upon it. Its radiance rises from the ends of the upper world to the ends of the lower worlds, and they cannot endure it. David came and prepared a place for this "Morning of Joseph" to increase and sustain the worlds like a mountain of merit, as it is written:
> In the morning I will arrange [my prayer] for You, and I will look out. (Psalms 5:4)

Everything spread out and was pure. And since that merit of David depends upon it, he said: "Press me to the beauty of the place for this morning." Rabbi Abba came and kissed him. He said: "The left is not as wise as this; let us not hear from him, for it is not enough." While they were walking, a certain child <note>The *Yanuqa*, a recurring figure in the Zohar who possesses supernatural wisdom despite his youth</note> reached Rabbi Eleazar at the start of the path, and it spread out before him. Rabbi Eleazar said: "Child, you have always been like a cradle in your exile. Go and see him, for the companions are coming to you and you are with them." A cup was shaken for him for three days, and he could not overcome the fear, for they were walking toward him. The holy sage answered and said: "Do not fear him." Like the heat in the clouds of the bush, for one who is full of sleep was placed beneath him, and the days of his name passed, for he was a child before him. And those companions went. Rabbi Abba said to Rabbi Eleazar: "What is this great wonder that we have seen?" He said to him: "This child is beneath me in the exile of the paths of my life; he lives like a sick man, and I know what youth is beneath him." And he breathed a sigh over it and went up. 

While they were walking, a raven called out before them, crying out and flapping its wings greatly. Rabbi Eleazar said: "Fortunate are you, for you are standing and prepared for this! For I know a measure of the companions like him." And at the time of Kindness <note>Chesed</note> for the sleeper who was full of everything, and **Rabbi Yose** was his name, whose life had expired, for he had departed from this vessel, and there was no one worthy to attend to him. And I saw them near us; they strayed from the path and saw there. When all the people of the town saw them, they went out toward them and entered there. And Rabbi Yose, over whom the companions had expired, went and fled, and he slaughtered a market for Rabbi Yose, and he did not leave any man to reach the bed of the gathering after he died. 

He opened and said: "Divinity was supporting him," and he wept over him, his mouth clinging to his mouth. That child opened and saw the sickness of the world. It is written in the Torah:
> If a bird’s nest chances to be before you... you shall surely let the mother go... (Deuteronomy 22:6-7) <note>The commandment of *Shiluach HaKen*, which Kabbalah links to the exile of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) and the awakening of mercy</note>

That child groaned and wept and said: "Master of the Universe, the fulfillment of this matter is for freedom!" Two sons—where is the destruction? He sees all and seals and serves. It is destined for You to take us and to fulfill the word for freedom. And see now, Master of the Universe, as it is written:
> But the Lord your God would not listen... (Deuteronomy 23:6)

The mother died and lay over the children; the hiddenness of everything that was covering us and lying over the children. This is the place for freedom! Rabbi Eleazar and the companions wept for his children. And that child opened, and Rabbi Eleazar said: "Water for the spirit and earth for the depth..." until Rabbi Eleazar said this verse. A pillar of fire went out between them and went up, and his kiss was clinging to the mouth of the companion, and they did not separate. Rabbi Eleazar said to him: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to distance the cup; he desires to pray, and let no other man interfere with him." All were upon that child, and all were receiving words until they were silent. They heard a voice that was saying...

<summary>This page recounts a mystical journey where Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Abba encounter a "Yanuqa" (Wonder-Child) and witness the death of Rabbi Yose. The child offers a profound, tearful discourse on the commandment of the bird's nest, linking it to the exile of the Shekhinah and the hope for ultimate freedom.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the narrative of the "Yenuka" (the Child Prodigy) from the Zohar, Parashat Balak. It follows the dramatic scene where Rabbi Yossi has fallen into a death-like state or severe illness, and the young child’s prayers and Torah insights intervene with the Heavenly Court to restore his life.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Balak** / **205** <-

He said: When Rabbi Eleazar saw that the words of this small child <note>Aramaic: *Yenuka*</note> and his tears ascended before the Throne of the Holy King and were remembered there. And thirteen "molars" <note>A symbolic reference to the thirteen attributes of mercy or specific spiritual barriers broken</note> were knocked out from before the Angel of Death because of you. And behold, crowns and two years <note>The text uses *sakin* (years/times) as a reprieve of life</note> were added to you until you can teach Torah to this forgiven child, who is wise before the Holy One, blessed be He. Rabbi Eleazar and his companions stood up and did not allow any man to remain in the house. Immediately, they saw a pillar of fire ascending, and Rabbi Yossi opened his eyes, and that child had his mouth pressed against his [Rabbi Yossi's] mouth. Rabbi Eleazar said: "Fortunate is the portion of the wise!" We call a prophet "one with a clear eye," and that child was nursing with life as if he had just touched this world. They returned and said: "Fortunate is your portion, Rabbi Yossi, and blessed is the Merciful One who had compassion for you." For the child's soul cried out and his possessions <note>His spiritual merits</note> pressed with beautiful words at the gates of heaven like a full vessel. And when his tears reached there, they established life for all of them through that child; they raised him up and showed him great honor. They took him to another room and he drank there, and they did not inform him of what happened immediately afterward. They rejoiced there for three days and renewed many insights in the Torah through Rabbi Yossi. Rabbi Yossi said to them: "My friends, I was not given permission to reveal what I saw in that world until after twelve years. But three hundred and seventy tears that the child shed entered into the scales before the Holy King. And I invite you, friends, to hear how the prayer he opened with that verse and with visions of words shook three hundred thousand benches in the Heavenly Academy <note>Aramaic: *Metivta de-Rakia*</note>. All of them stood before the Holy King and sought mercy for me and acted as my guarantors. And the Holy One, blessed be He, was filled with mercy for me and recounted before your eyes these words and how my soul was restored to me. And one Advocate <note>Greek/Aramaic: *Patropos/Epitropos*</note> stood before Him and said: 'Forgive the world, for it is written:

> Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings You have established strength, because of Your adversaries, to silence the enemy and the avenger. <note>Psalm 8:3</note>

May it be His will that the merit of the Torah and the merit of that 'rider' <note>Likely referring to the soul or a celestial guide</note> who gave his soul for the merit of the harsh judgment should go before you." Then the Holy One, blessed be He, called to the Angel of Death and commanded him to have pity and give life, just as He gave him thirteen "molars" to be knocked out, and to return the crowns and the two years that were a pledge before him, so that he should not return him to the hands of the "Matrons" <note>Forces of judgment</note> who held him. Now, I will explain for the sake of the bread of truth that the righteous see, which I have sought before your eyes. Rabbi Yossi opened and said:

> The Lord kills and brings to life; He brings down to the grave <note>Hebrew: *Sheol*</note> and raises up. <note>1 Samuel 2:6</note>

This verse must be looked into... "The Lord kills"—but is His Name not associated with life for all? This matter is not easily dismissed, for in every place His Name gives life to all the world. How then can it say "The Lord kills"? You find that when a person is in distress, it kills them; but "The Lord kills" is certainly true. If you say it is because He departs from a person—for as long as the Divine Presence is upon him, all the accusers of the world cannot harm him, but the moment it departs, all the accusers can overcome him and he dies immediately—it is not so. Rather, "The Lord kills" literally refers to that "Grip" of the Other Side <note>Aramaic: *Sitra Achra*, the side of impurity/evil</note>. When that grip of the Evil Side sees the precious radiance of the Holy One, blessed be He, it immediately dies and has no existence for even a single moment. Once that grip of the Other Side dies and is removed from the world, He immediately "brings to life." Whom does He bring to life? That grip of the Holy Spirit that comes from the side of Holiness; He brings it to life and establishes it in perfect existence. Thus the Holy One, blessed be He, acts at once. And as for what it says, "He brings down to the grave and raises up," He brings down that holy spirit to the grave to perform a "dipping" <note>A spiritual immersion or purification</note> there, and immediately raises it up and enters it into the place it needs to be. For behold, friends, at that hour when I departed from the world, my spirit slept immediately until the hour the Holy One, blessed be He, revived me and breathed into it. It died the moment my son opened with those words; then his soul flew and awakened my soul. He was more perceptive than the wise, and he entered the place he entered, and there judgment was not executed, and I was given crowns and two years of life because of the tears that ascended."

<summary>Rabbi Yossi describes his near-death experience and miraculous resuscitation, credited to the powerful prayers and Torah insights of a young child (the Yenuka). The text explains the theological paradox of God "killing and bringing to life" as the destruction of evil forces to allow the holy spirit to flourish.</summary>
<keywords>Yenuka, Rabbi Yossi, Angel of Death, Resurrection, Heavenly Academy, Sitra Achra, Tears of Prayer, Psalm 8:3</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discourse of the "Yenuka" (the Holy Child) from the Zohar, Parashat Balak. The previous context involves the child astounding Rabbi Eleazar and the companions with his profound mystical insights. This section focuses on the death of Zelophehad and the humility of Moses.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Balak**<-

And words of truth from here and for that time were not found like the words spoken by the world <note>referring to the mundane speech of people</note>. Since we have seen what we have seen, and the Holy One, blessed be He, desires that nothing from here be lost, he opened and said:
> The Lord has disciplined me severely, but He has not given me over to death. (Psalms 118:18)

King David said this regarding everything the Holy One, blessed be He, did in the world. He spoke of the "lodging" <note>original: *akhsanot*, referring to the soul's temporary stay in the body</note> that he had in this world, regarding all that the world does to him, for the Throne spreads over the filth of sin and the way of the "pepper" <note>likely a metaphor for sharp or stinging judgments</note>. From here, the Holy One, blessed be He, is found for him and does not give him up to death. Regarding the lodging of that world, David said: "I live here, here before the Holy One, blessed be He." Here is for the knocking <note>repentance/affliction</note>, and I have brought my actions close, and He purified me from all that I sinned, and He did not leave my actions for that world after death. For "The Lord has disciplined me severely" in this world in order to cleanse me, "but He has not given me over to death" to take vengeance from me there. And here, the Holy One, blessed be He, disciplined him one time here in this lodging so that he would not be in shame in the World to Come. That *Chesed* <note><term>Chesed</term>: The Divine attribute of Loving-kindness</note> opened and said:
> Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not among the company, etc. (Numbers 27:3)

"Our father"—this reason is scorched from above and drawn from the life of the holy pious ones. How many died like a youth <note>or "shook like a youth"</note> when calling "Our father"? There is no knowledge and no clearing of the spirit and soul except when they are bald <note>pure/exposed</note> like this. "Our father" is like the clearing of the King. **"Died in the wilderness"**—and did others not die in the wilderness? For here it is hinted at, and it says "Our father died in the wilderness." How many members of the group were naked without a foundation? They say of that "cut off" one <note>Zelophehad</note> that he was forced, as it is written:
> For he died in his own sin. (Numbers 27:3)

And from here they said it, and from here they said thus. Rather, this is the exchange of the sea, for here, like all the people of the plague, is this exchange. And I have seen that my father commanded me regarding the hidden treasure. But there were many who died, and not because of the sin of Korah, nor because of the sin of the spies when the decree was decreed, but before the giving of the Torah and after the Calf that they made—those were the few of the world and those who were found in their crowns. But the reason they were burdened is like the children who died in the wilderness. And we learn from the Great Master, Joseph, and who was it that did not know the "nets" of the Torah <note>the intricacies of Law</note> as is fitting? This was the end and this was the crown of the mouth. And words and God to the Holy One, blessed be He, who descended and ascended, as it is written:
> And much people of Israel died. (Numbers 21:6)

A man who does not know the Torah is not a "Great One" <note>original: *Rav*</note> out of doubt. The greatness of the seed of Joseph is from here. And such a case in the wilderness is considered like actual *Mazal* <note><term>Mazal</term>: Constellation or destiny/flow from above</note>, for the slanderer was like a stranger with the sin of Eleazar and all the companions and all the heads here. And they did not complain with sin except before them, as if they received the Holy One, blessed be He, from him. From here, whoever is nourished from <term>Din</term> <note>Divine Judgment</note> should bring others close and hate strangers, so that the image of Simeon will be here and he will be directed accurately and will not judge except as is fitting, and the living shall not be pushed away from judgment. And they did not know this of Moses:
> Now the man Moses was very humble, more than all the men who were on the face of the earth. (Numbers 12:3)

And they did not know that Moses was not so <note>i.e., not acting out of ego</note>. Since they stood as a staff, he said: "I have seen that the whole assembly of great men of Israel, and all the leaders of the congregation, approached." Immediately, Moses separated himself from the judgment, as it says:
> And Moses brought their cause before the Lord. (Numbers 27:5)

Moses said: "This judgment is not fitting for me." The humility of Moses was to "bring their cause before the Lord." And those others did not take this path, for the assembly of the "children of the Most High" are those called "brazen-faced"—they have no humility like Moses at all, and all the portions of the staff. Rabbi Eleazar and the companions rejoiced. That Child said: "I will return to the previous words." **"Our father died in the wilderness"**—"Our father," this reason that comes to the sign hangs upon his predecessor, and he melts and is extinguished by his mouth, like the reason that you said about him above, "died in the wilderness," like the *Mazal* of his mouth. That Child looked at him and took hold of his father's neck and wept, and he was beloved to him, for this opening was like *Mazal*—he died, and the love of the elder was arranged like *Mazal* for this world. His father turned and kissed him.

<summary>The "Yenuka" (Holy Child) provides a mystical interpretation of Zelophehad's death and Moses's humility, explaining that Moses deferred the case of Zelophehad's daughters to God out of extreme self-effacement. The passage concludes with an emotional moment between the child and his father, emphasizing the divine inspiration (Mazal) of the child's words.</summary>
<keywords>Yenuka, Zelophehad, Moses, Humility, Judgment (Din), Mazal, Zohar, Balak, King David, Wilderness</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

to him and he departed <note>The child passed away</note>. Rabbi Elazar and all the companions wept, and they went and wept as they walked. They lifted him up with their words <note>eulogized him</note> upon his head and his eyes, and they wept with him. Rabbi Elazar said: "By the strength and the wine of the King, this one has been taken from me in silence and is dead." That child said: "Father, father, follow the King!" They were greatly distressed on that day, for that serpent is coiled with its tail above, tasting sweetness. At what time? This serpent [strikes] because of the sin of that [original] serpent, and not because of the sin of Adam; and his sicknesses are the speech of his mouth, for **he died in his own sin** <note>original: "כי בחטאו מת" - Numbers 27:3</note>. Rabbi Elazar said to Rabbi Abba: "Stay here for seven days in order to settle him, for all seven days that the soul departs from the body, it goes to its bed and to its grave, returning until it is settled in its place after seven days."

Rabbi Abba said: It is written, **"You shall surely open your hand to your brother, to your poor, and to your needy"** <note>Deuteronomy 15:11</note>. This verse has been established: a person should not cease from study and strength for his Master. Behold, Rabbi Yose, I see you weeping in your sickness today, and the cancellation of kindness with him. He said: "Certainly it is so." And after they buried him in the mountain, they wept all the time as they walked on the path, so that the Angel of Death would not descend. They supported that youth <note>likely referring to a different attendant or the memory of the child</note>, blessed him, and went on. Rabbi Elazar said: "I wonder at the youngsters of this generation, how powerful is their strength! They are the meritorious children of the Kings." He said: "Father, blessed is the portion of the elders of the generation. For in his days, the Holy One, blessed be He, desires to establish His two academies and to make for them a time of blessing and entry, as is fitting. This is the merit of this generation until the King Messiah comes."

They went on as they were walking. Rabbi Abba said: "Behold, we have learned that for eleven things, plagues <note>leprosy</note> come upon human beings. And these are: for [wasting] seed, for cursing the Name [of God], for forbidden sexual relations, for theft, for an evil tongue <note><term>Lashon Hara</term>: derogatory speech or gossip</note>, for false testimony, for a judge who corrupts justice, for a vain oath, for one who enters the boundary of his fellow, for one who thinks evil thoughts, and for one who sacrifices an offering [improperly]... and some say also for idolaters. All of these we have learned in our Mishnah."

Regarding [the sin of] the Golden Calf, it is written: **"And Moses saw the people, that they were exposed (parua), for Aaron had exposed them"** <note>Exodus 32:25</note>. What is the meaning of "exposed"? That they were struck with leprosy. It is written here **"exposed"** (*parua*), and it is written there [regarding the leper]: **"And the leper in whom the plague is... his head shall be exposed"** (*parua*) <note>Leviticus 13:45</note>. And regarding cursing the Name, it is written: **"This day the Lord will deliver you (yisgar'cha) into my hand"** <note>1 Samuel 17:46</note>, and it is written [regarding the leper]: **"And the priest shall shut him up (v'hisgiro)"** <note>Leviticus 13:5</note>. Rabbi Abba said: "This matter is not yet settled and needs to be looked into further." Rabbi Elazar said: "It is certainly so. This Philistine <note>Goliath</note> was close to the lineage of that generation, and he was the son of Orpah, and he was a hater, as it is written: 'from the ranks (*ma'archot*) of the Philistines.' Do not read it as 'from the ranks' (*ma'archot*) but 'from the narrowness' (*mimitzrot*) of the Philistines... and since it is written: **'And the Philistine cursed David by his gods,'** David looked at him with an **Evil Eye** <note><term>Ayin Hara</term>: a harmful spiritual gaze</note>. And in every place where David looked with an Evil Eye, all types of leprosy were drawn from his eyes. And so it was here: once David looked at him with an Evil Eye, what is written? **'There shall not fail from the house of Joab one that hath an issue, or that is a leper'** <note>2 Samuel 3:29</note>. And regarding this Philistine, since he cursed the Name, David looked at him with an Evil Eye, and he was struck in his place so that he became a leper immediately. **'And the stone sank into his forehead'**—the leprosy became attached to his forehead. And the entire evil appearance of leprosy was poured into his forehead, and it was poured out here; from his forehead, he was certainly a leper. That wicked sinner, Balaam..."

## Main Text (Zohar)

Balaam’s eyes were open from the "eye below." The <term>Eye of Splendor</term><note>original: "Eina de-Hod," referring to a specific mystical emanation or spiritual perception</note> was raised above all radiance of colors. There was no eye in the world as beautiful to behold as the eye of David. All the colors of the world are seen within it, and all creatures see in it the likeness of the world below, as it is written: *Peace, peace to him that is far off* <note>Is. 57:19</note> and its meaning. When those three saw us, all those living creatures were terrified before them. For all of Balaam’s eyes, he would strike them all with his gaze; wherever he looked with his "reverse gaze," it was a great evil for him, for there is an **Evil Eye** <term>Eina Bisha</term> in the world at the time when that evil one is in opposition to the eyes of David. Regarding forbidden sexual relations, it is written: *The Lord will smite with a scab* <note>Is. 3:17</note>, a precise term for a blemish, and it is written: *and for a scab* <note>Lev. 14:56</note>, a scab upon the carcass, as it is written: *your burning with the fire of the Lord was restrained* etc. <note>referring to the fires of lust or judgment</note>. Regarding the "Evil Eye," as it has been stated, all these traits were present in that wicked Balaam. Pethor <note>Balaam's home</note> is lacking, a hidden strike upon the hidden. For the Evil Eye was directed at that River that stands at the entrance of the Crown, as it is written:

> Behold, I will extend peace to her like a river <note>Is. 66:12</note>

And this one [Balaam] came to that Pethor and incited them. Rabbi Abba said: All these things were certainly in Balaam. Regarding all forbidden sexual relations, it is written:

> Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam <note>Num. 31:16</note>

to commit a trespass against the Lord. Here we see it was regarding forbidden sexual relations. Regarding the "closed eye," it is written: **He who knows the knowledge of the Most High** <note>Num. 24:16</note>, yet he did not even know the mind of his own animal! **Who sees the vision of the Almighty** <note>Num. 24:16</note>. His own corruption is written: *Come, and I will advise you*, for he stood with a joyful heart, and the evil one spoke to look upon them and strike from his own side, with evil intentions against them. He went up into the depths to practice sorcery, as it is written: *And he prepared a bull and a ram on every altar*, and it is written: *I have prepared the seven altars*. Regarding the sowing of discord between brothers—between Israel and their Father in Heaven—there was no slanderer in the world like him, for he cursed them generally, and all these evils were in him. The Evil Eye, as was said, was directed at that River of Israel, setting his eye to strike it. *The land of the children of his people* etc. If I only knew the land of the children of his people. A spirit of impurity attached itself to all the children of his people, as has been said.

etc. This refers to Balaam, who "blessed" Israel [insincerely]. *Neither desire thou his dainties*, for the Holy One, blessed be He, has no portion in those who are not rectified before Him. And that one [Balaam] knew how to harm; he knew the <term>lower crowns</term><note>the external or "unholy" spiritual forces</note>, and such impurity was not found even in the camp below.

And this is the "Ox and the Donkey." Until now, since he knew how to bind other sorceries, [God] said to him: *But only the word...* He weakened him and his glory was immediately removed from looking into his sorceries, and he did not think he would be in his own authority. "Wicked man! You prepare and gird your weapons to depart from My authority. See that you and your donkey shall be under My authority." He went, and the Angel of the Lord <note>original: "Malakh YHVH"</note> stood in the way and set for you a snare like a trap and a voice of shame from one of His walls that burned. He was an Angel of Mercy <note>The name YHVH is associated with the attribute of Mercy (Chesed) in Kabbalah</note>, and this is what Rabbi Shimon said: "The wicked turn Mercy into Judgment <note>Din</note>." He arranged below, etc., "to be an adversary <note>Satan</note> to him." And "to stand as an adversary" on every path, he was an adversary to him.

Come and see how wise Balaam was in his sorceries above all the people of the world, for with dark knowledge he strove to depart from the authority of the Holy One, blessed be He, from that matter which is written: **And he went with the princes of Moab** <note>Numbers 22:21</note>, etc. — to look into his sorceries. Once he prepared to be guilty and girded himself with his preparations of sorcery on the side of the spirit to curse Israel, the Holy One, blessed be He, sent the Angel of Mercy ahead against him, and from the side of Mercy, in order to frustrate his wisdom and to confuse him from below through that sorcery, as it is written: **And the donkey turned aside from the way** <note>Numbers 22:23</note>. **From the way** specifically. And because of this, it is not written "and an Angel of Elohim <note>The name associated with Judgment</note> stood," but "the Angel of the Lord <note>YHVH</note>," who is of Mercy. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "You have come to load your donkey with your sorcery in many sides of Judgment; against My [will] I shall make your burden, and this way shall be overturned." Immediately, the Angel of Mercy went ahead as an adversary to him; "to him" specifically, as has been said.

**And she saw** — she saw the Angel, etc. Rabbi Isaac said: "Was it for a donkey to see, while Balaam, who was so wise, did not see?" <meta>This page continues the discussion of the biblical figure Balaam from the previous section of Parashat Balak. It focuses on the mystical source of his prophetic and magical powers, specifically his connection to the fallen angels Aza and Azael.</meta>

# Balak

"What is man that You are mindful of him?" <note>Psalm 8:5</note> What is the nature of this human being? The Holy One, blessed be He, said to the angels: "A man who stands before you to know—his wisdom shall be higher than your wisdom." Once Adam was created and stood up, and the first beings bowed before him, the angels came and went. They said before Him: "You have given a mouth to a human to perform service before You." He said to them: "If only you were present among them..." <note>The text refers to the angelic protest against the creation of humanity.</note> What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He cast them down from their holy degree from heaven.

Rabbi Shimon said: Now you have the answer to your question regarding Balaam, who said of himself: "Falling and having eyes revealed" <note>Numbers 24:4</note>. Or, since it was not truly so, and he was merely looking at himself, how could the Holy One, blessed be He, write a false word in the Torah? For the word of the Torah is truth! How could that wicked man be found in a degree higher than all the faithful prophets? Furthermore, the Holy Presence <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence</term> does not dwell above except in a place that is fitting for it.

Now to return to the first matter: After the Holy One, blessed be He, cast them <note>the angels Aza and Azael</note> down from their holy place from heaven, they wandered in the world. Here we must look: is it not written, "He makes His angels spirits..." <note>Psalm 104:4</note>? And yet these were angels! But come and see: all those angels above cannot exist or endure except through the Supernal Light that shines for them and sustains them. If that Supernal Light is cut off from them, they cannot endure—certainly not these whom the Holy One, blessed be He, cast down and cut off from that Supernal Light. Their radiance was changed when they appeared in the world, and the air of the world dominated them, and they were changed into another degree.

Come and see: from the power that the Manna had when it descended for Israel as a blessing—that power was from the dew above that descended from the "Ancient Hidden One" <term>Atika Kadisha: the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</term>, the most hidden of all. And when it descended, a light shone in all the worlds, and from it came the letters of the alphabet <note>referring to the mystical formation of the Manna</note> received by the lower beings and the high angels. But when it descended below and the air of the world dominated it, its radiance was hidden and adjusted, and its radiance was only as it is written: "And it was like coriander seed..." <note>Exodus 16:31 / Numbers 11:7</note> and no more.

Certainly, it is the same with the angels: once they descended and the air dominated them, they were changed from that first degree they held. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He saw that they were leading the world astray. He bound them in chains of iron in the Mountains of Darkness <term>Turei DeChashokha: a legendary mystical location of exile for fallen beings</term>. In that place, they dwell in the depths of the mountains. He bound Aza and cast darkness into his eyes because that error <note>or "rebellion"</note> for which the Holy One, blessed be He, bound them grew strong and provoked the One Above. So the Holy One, blessed be He, cast him into the depth up to his neck and threw darkness into his eyes. Azael, however, did not grow as strong; he was covered and bound by darkness.

The people of the world who know this come to them and they teach them sorcery, enchantments, and divinations. And those Mountains of Darkness are called "Mountains of the East" <note>Numbers 23:7</note>. Why? Because darkness preceded the light, and therefore the Mountains of Darkness are called the Mountains of the East <note>The Hebrew word 'Kedem' means both 'East' and 'Ancient/Preceding'</note>. And from them, Balaam learned his sorcery. This is what Balaam meant when he said: "From Aram Balak has brought me, the king of Moab, from the mountains of the east..." <note>Numbers 23:7</note>.

Balaam was looking at himself from this place and saw everything: "Who hears the words of God..." <note>Numbers 24:4</note>. Because Aza and Azael told of the visions of the world. They were angels, Aza and Azael, at first above, and their time was from the holy world where they were. It is written "Who hears the words of God"—it does not say "the voice of God," but "the words of God." These are the utterances that they said from the things that come from the divisions <note>of the celestial realms</note> and the matters that depend on them.

He said from below: "Who hears the words of God and knows the knowledge of the Most High." For he knew the hour when anger hangs over the world, and he would calculate that hour in his charms. "Who sees the vision of the Almighty <term>Shaddai</term>..." What is the "vision of Shaddai"? These are the "Falling" and "Revealed of Eyes." Between these two, Aza and Azael: "Falling" refers to Aza, because the Holy One, blessed be He, deepened him into the depth of darkness, and he sits in the depth up to his neck as we said, and he is covered and darkness is cast into his eyes; therefore he is called "Falling," for he fell into the depth of darkness. Azael is "Revealed of Eyes," for darkness was not cast upon him in the same way, as he did not grow as strong or provoke as much as the one above him.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Balak<-

Through higher wisdom <note>Aramaic: *Chokhmata Ila'ah*</note>. Or, it was entirely a higher spirit, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired it all in order to humble them—those of that "Other Side"—so they would not have dominion over the various evil species, because they [Israel] are the portion of the Holy One, Blessed be He. **And the angel of the Lord stood, etc.** <note>Numbers 22:22</note>. Each and every color is kindled three times toward the side of the twelve engraved boundaries and counsels. They are included in twelve others in the spirit of the crown. That brain is divided into four divisions, and it stands so that the lower part shall not be moved. ## Main Text (Zohar)

A thin, foolish [spirit] from which a portion is drawn down to those below, and from there it branches out into several sides. And this we call <term>Nechashit</term> <note>original: "נחשית" - a feminine form of the word for serpent, referring to a specific impure spiritual shell or "Klippah"</note> which is bent from the side of the holy heights. Because of this, the entire world is conducted, both above and below. The master of sorcery arose, and we have established this blessing; both above and below, all those other idolatrous nations <note>original: "עכו"ם" - worshippers of stars and constellations</note> below are from that second "donkey-like" level. Do not say they are alone, for even those lower crowns are from that second impurity. This is like the parable of the vineyards that surround the other nations who are blessed by it. When the kingdom of the accuser saw that Balaam was turning his donkey toward that path, as it is written: *to turn her aside from the road* <note>Numbers 22:23</note>, immediately **the Angel of the Lord stood** like a vineyard fence to block the way around, so that those other idolatrous nations and those lower crowns would not be assisted by him. Furthermore, as Rabbi Isaac said, it is written: *stayed by the wall* etc., to fence in and surround the other nations in exile, while Israel is like "my own vineyard" etc., because they are in exile and are not blessed as is fitting. <note>Numbers 22:24</note> **A fence on this side and a fence on that side.** Rabbi Abba said: How could that Angel block that path? It was because his appointed time for the end had come, involving the numerical value of 151 <note>original: "קנ"א" - likely a Gematria reference</note> and the Assembly of Israel. Rabbi Judah said: The "white" <note>the side of mercy</note> assisted him, as it is written *from this side and from that side*—it was written at that moment. What is written? <note>Numbers 22:28</note> **And the donkey pressed** etc., **and she pressed against the wall.** What is "pressed against the wall"? Everything was bound to the wall, a wall of judgment that ruled over them. *And she pressed Balaam’s foot against the wall*—she gave him no assistance at all. And in her distress, she diminished <margin>Other versions: "removed"</margin> him toward that wall. And a hint was standing there, and then *he continued to strike her* on this side.

->**And he continued**<- <note>Numbers 22:26</note> **The Angel of the Lord went further and stood in a narrow place** etc. At that moment, all openings and all assistances were closed to her, so that no help was found for her from any side of the world. Then *the donkey saw the Angel of the Lord* and she opened etc. <note>Numbers 22:28</note> **And the Lord opened the mouth of the donkey** etc. This was one of those things created on the eve of the Sabbath at twilight. Rabbi Isaac said: What did Balaam see? Did he go to the donkey or to this side? Rabbi Yose said: He was selling himself to those princes who were with him. When they reached Balak, they said to him: "Is it to this side that you have arranged your encounter? You will find no substance in him, only in his words and in the speech of the lower things found in his glory." Rabbi Hezekiah said: If the donkey had not spoken, Balaam would not have been surrounded by his own testimony; through what was found, his strength was known and broken. Rabbi Abba raised a difficulty: It is written *and the donkey opened* etc., and it is written *and the Lord opened the mouth* etc. Why is it not written "And the Lord opened the mouth of the donkey" in the first instance? Rather, there, from the side of fire upon the mouth, it opened and performed the command that arrived. It is not fitting for the Holy One, Blessed Be He, to perform commands directly where a decree is already declared and abandoned, as when *the earth opened its mouth*. And the decree was carried out as his command, as it is written: *and the earth opened its mouth*. But here, no one was found to decree except the will of the Holy One, Blessed Be He, and it was His will; thus it is written: *And the Lord opened the mouth of the donkey*. From Him came the word, and from the cup it was agreed. Rabbi Judah said: This was to reveal the shame of that man, and these words show that their words are foul. Since it is written *And the Lord opened the mouth of the donkey*, do they wish to place these words as mere images? They are words of wisdom! Just as they were awakened by the blessing of the serpent, it was found that his end was in a storm. And she spoke a second time: "Turn away from me, for I have learned from here." He should have understood, but she said: *What have I done to you* etc. Thus they said: The Holy One, Blessed Be He, took the trouble to open the mouth of this power. Rabbi Abba said: Certainly, from these words we learn the mind of Balaam—that he was not worthy for the Holy Spirit to speak with him, and we learn that he had no power in his donkey to prevail or to be found.

## Main Text (Zohar)

...to be considered. And we have learned a matter that was taught: there is no word or speech in a beast that allows a flawed consciousness <note>original: *da'ata pagim*</note> to rest upon them.

Come and see: Balaam was defiled, and there is no consciousness more flawed than his; he was unable to stand within the Supernal Knowledge <note>The divine wisdom of the side of holiness</note> above him. *And the donkey said to Balaam: "What have I done to you..."* [Numbers 22:28]. It was her will to do both good and bad. Not that she intended this from the beginning, but rather because they [the sorcerers] are hateful. And even though in the assembly of the Sages, in the deep matters <note>Reference to another section: Folio 189b</note>, it was more within his power, for he had burdened her with his sorceries and she stood under his authority. *And Balaam said to the donkey: "Because you have mocked me"* [Numbers 22:29]. It was a disgrace for him to be rebuked, and she answered him with the foolishness of the matter; then they [the onlookers] pitied him, and he was disgraced in their eyes, and they knew that they were deviants. And as for what he said:

> "Because you have mocked me; if only there were a sword in my hand" <note>Numbers 22:29</note>

They said: "This deviant! If he is a master of serpents with his mouth, how is it he cannot slaughter a female donkey and requires a sword?" And we have learned that there is no speech in a beast to allow another spirit to rest upon them, so that people would not say: "Woe to him! Beasts speak!" For if they had such flawed consciousness, they would weep forever.

And learn the matter that was taught: for <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> <note>original: *HaKadosh Baruch Hu*</note> opened the mouth of the donkey. My rest is within her when the Ancient One is before Him.

> "And it was in the morning, and Balak took Balaam..." <note>Numbers 22:41</note>

Rabbi Isaac said: Balak was wiser in sorceries than Balaam, except that he could not calculate the precise moment for evil... and so on. Thus, *Balak took Balaam*—he prepared him and showed him everything. *And he brought him up to the high places of Baal.* What is the meaning of *he brought him up to the high places of Baal*? Rather, he tasted through his sorceries the "Masters of the Side" <note>Demonic forces</note> and joined with them, and it was found that they were destined and corrupted to make high places and to divide portions for Baal, as it is written: *And they went after the Baal.* *And he saw from there the end of the people*—meaning he spoke of their path and their kings who would worship him, as it is written: *And they called on the name of Baal*, and it is written: *The <term>Lord</term> <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note> is the God.* Once Balaam saw that Israel was destined to take hold of the truth:

> "And Balaam said to Balak: Build for me here seven altars" <note>Numbers 23:1</note>

It is written with a missing letter. Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Judah disagreed. One said: Corresponding to the altars of the ancients <note>The Patriarchs</note>, he offered these seven altars. And the other said: He did everything with [unholy] wisdom, for it is found that the ascensions of Israel are bound in seven levels <note>The seven lower Sefirot or spiritual emanations</note>. Because of this, he arranged seven altars outside of her [the Shekhinah/Divine Presence], for there was a love that had left him, and they were all afraid to strike at him because of that Beloved One who was destined to come below—another man—and they wanted to mingle with the Holy.

He said: "Whatever he does, he awakens a strike here." The Beloved below is a son of holiness, and I cannot prevail. What did he do? He arranged a gift <note>a sacrifice</note> to nullify that Mercy. <term>The Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> said: "His mercy... is a snare for this man." Regarding those who act for that son of the Beloved, he said: "Let this gift stand and let it be removed." It was a time for the governor to consume it. Thus Balaam came to stir up a strike against Israel, but he saw he could not because of that Beloved of theirs, as it says: *Your friend and your father's friend...* [Proverbs 27:10]. He went around to prepare a gift before Him. <term>The Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> said: "You have tasted, and it shall be a barking for you; you have cooked a gift in weeping, behold your gift is ready for the dogs." Come and see what is written:

"And God happened <note>original: *Vayikar*</note> upon Balaam." And Rabbi Shimon said: This is the language of *Keri* <note>accidental impurity/nocturnal emission</note> and defilement. Your gift is cast out and shall not enter before Me. Rabbi Judah said: *Vayikar* implies a chance occurrence—who can stand before our city? He was ready with a gift from his "Side" to prevail over Israel. Heaven forbid! It is written *Vayikar Elohim*—He made Himself a "chance occurrence" <note>diminishing His presence</note> away from that which Balaam esteemed. *And God happened*—as it was said below, it was from the side of impurity. Rabbi Eleazar said: Balaam thought that with that gift he would enter to weaken Israel, but <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> uprooted Balaam from before that gift, and uprooted Balaam from his defilement, and uprooted him from the spirit of Kindness and Glory <note>original: *Yakar*</note>. All glories were arranged in Him. He said to him: "Wicked one! You are not worthy to be bound with Me or to know..."

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Balak<-

Like a gift given to a dog to keep it from biting, so it was found here. Rabbi Shimon said: Come and see, this wicked man <note>Balaam</note> was taken for everything, for it is not found in this entire portion that "The Lord said to Balaam" or "The Lord spoke to Balaam." Rather, what is written? *And the Lord put a word in his mouth* <note>Numbers 23:5</note>. This is like a man who places a bit in the mouth of a donkey so that it will not stray here or there. So too, *the Lord put a word in the mouth of Balaam*. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: "Wicked one! Do you think it is in your hands, and that your blessings or curses will be fulfilled as you wish? You are needed for them <note>Israel</note> just as people say to a thorn..." <note>A folk idiom suggesting even a nuisance has a purpose</note>. Balak said: "Open your mouth to curse." But is it in your power? It does not depend on your mouth, but rather *thus you shall speak*—it is prepared to bless them. When you speak, you will speak words that will be fulfilled against your will, for these words are not yours. Come and see the order: when he came to Balak, and Balak heard all those words, he was distressed, for Balaam's words were being snatched away. Balak tried to use sorcery to bind the speech, so that Balaam would not be able to say what he was saying. He gathered magicians to uproot the words from his mouth. What is written? *Stand here by your burnt offering* <note>Numbers 23:15</note>. With these sorceries, he tried to delay the speech so it would not come out, but he could not uproot the words. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: "Wicked one! Do you think you can uproot them?" What is written in response? *And God met Balaam* <note>Numbers 23:4</note>, and He showed him that his sorcery was for naught. As it is written, Balak said "Good," but God said *thus you shall speak*—"thus" specifically. Come and see: at first it is not written *Stand here by your burnt offering*, but rather *Stand by your burnt offering and I will go, perhaps the Lord will come to meet me* <note>Numbers 23:3</note>. Once he saw that all those blessings were coming, then he said *Stand here by your burnt offering*, trying to use the word "here" <note>Hebrew: *koh*</note> for sorcery. "Come, curse Jacob for me"—meaning, gather their sins. He said: "I will diminish them from that level where they stand." But God said to him: "Can you diminish that level? For because of it, they are never uprooted from the world." *And come, doom Israel*—Israel is the one for whom anger is turned away, and who stands firm.

**For** from the top of the rocks I see him... <note>Numbers 23:9</note> Rabbi Yitzhak said: *From the top of the rocks*—these are the Patriarchs, as it is written:
> Look to the rock from which you were hewn
<note>Isaiah 51:1</note>
*And from the hills I behold him*—these are the Matriarchs. Once he saw the protection from this side and that side, he saw they could not be cursed. Rabbi Abba said: *For from the top of the rocks*—these are words spoken regarding Israel, for their strength begins from the head of all "rocks." And who are these rocks? They are the *Gevurot* <term>Gevurot: Divine Strengths or Judgments</term>, for all the judgments of the world emerge from those *Gevurot*, and for those below, they are hidden. *And from the hills I behold him*—these are the other "Crowns" <term>Crowns: Sefirot or spiritual emanations</term> that are below them. *Lo, it is a people that shall dwell alone*—as it is said, *The Lord alone did lead him*. *Who can count the dust of Jacob?* He raised two levels for them: Jacob and Israel. First Jacob, and later Israel. And he saw that they are all one, yet two levels. For the level of Israel is high, but *Who can count the dust...*? Below them is the "Dust" <note>A mystical reference to the Shekhinah or Malchut in its lowest state</note>. Rabbi Shimon said: It is written, *He shall give his seed like dust*. What is this "Dust"? It is well known, as it is written:
> The sword of the Lord is filled with blood... with dust
<note>Isaiah 34:6; the Zohar links dust to the site of divine judgment and creation</note>
"Dust" is that place from which the world was fashioned, as it is written:
> And the Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground
<note>Genesis 2:7</note>
And from that "Dust," how many hosts and how many camps emerge! How many officers, how many guardians of the law, how many arrows, how many catapults, how many spears and swords and weapons are found in that "Dust"! Who can count them all? They are without number. *And the number of the fourth part of Israel*—the "fourth part" <note>Hebrew: *rova*, also meaning "crouching" or "mating"</note> of Israel is a single matter; it refers to the "fourth leg" of the Divine Throne, the perfection of the Bed of Solomon. *Rova* is like a "fourth part" of water. Below, this "fourth" is called the "Strap of the Throne." Another interpretation: *Who can count the dust of Jacob*—these are all those who are attached to the "Dust" as we have established. *And the number of the fourth part of Israel*—as it is written, there is no number to his troops, the "fourth part" of Israel, as we have explained.
