## Main Text (Zohar)

To show [mercy], He turned Him back, and then He judged for the righteous and executed judgment. He judged for the righteous, for all their kind and the sign they received for their sake, etc. And He executed judgment, as it is written: ->"And he pierced both of them..."<- <note>Numbers 25:8</note>. Regarding this it is written, "He turned back My wrath," and it is written elsewhere, "He turned back His right hand from before the enemy" <note>Psalm 74:11</note>. Just as there it refers to turning back, so too here it refers to turning back. Because of this, the letter *Yud* in the name of Pinchas is small <note>In the Torah scroll, the Yud in Pinchas is written smaller than usual</note>; it is removed from its base and flies away. For whoever is "face to face" with Him—since the Covenant was upon the heads of Israel—He shows them His wrath. It was like a shadow in the sky, and it was not in the "right hand" of the Angel of Death, who needs to be subdued under his foot, and there is no letter *Tav*.

What did Pinchas do? That which was burning within him, he then took that letter *Het* and *Mem* <note>Together spelling "Ham," meaning heat or wrath</note> and snatched it, holding it openly. Since the wrath of the Angel of Death was snatched by Pinchas—taking that *Mem* as a deposit—he immediately turned back. *Het-Tet* <note>Sin</note>, because everyone who is zealous with a flame, Pinchas was inflamed within and rose to stand in the addition of *Resh-Het* <note>208</note>, and with the *Yud* <note>10</note> his name rises to *Resh-Het* <note>218? The text explores the gematria/numerical value of the spear</note>. And so it rises and descends. When he saw the *Het-Mem* <note>Wrath</note> as a shadow in the sky, he snatched it and joined it openly, and it immediately became *ReMaCh* <note>248, the word for Spear</note>.

This is what is written: ->"And he took a spear [Remach] in his hand"<- <note>Numbers 25:7</note>. For the letters *Het-Mem* were the first sign for Adam the first man to bring death upon the world. For this *Het* was a shadow over the head of Adam, as it is written: "And she took of its fruit [*M'priyo*]"—the letter *Mem* of *Priyo* <note>Fruit</note>—and it was a destroyer. And the letter *Tav* was added at the time it is written, "And she ate, and she gave... and they were opened," then death was prepared for the world.

Pinchas saw that there, that *Het* was shadowing the heads of Israel, and he laughed. He saw the *Mem* was open from within. When he saw it, he said: "This is surely the sign of the Angel of Death who always snatches the male." He spread his name and went down and took the *Het* to himself. That which was *Resh-Het* became joined as *ReMaCh* <note>Spear</note>. Then, "He took a spear in his hand." Regarding this it is written, "from its base it flies," "in his being zealous for My zeal," for he was zealous for the Holy Opening <note>The Covenant of Circumcision</note> which they were joining to a "foreign domain."

"In the midst" <note>Numbers 25:8, *be-tokhas*</note>—he showed "in the midst" because there was strength. Because of this, his base has many diagonals and many cities. He delivered himself to death in his time. For every "in the midst," it is like a razor in the hand of the *Mem*. Like the "midst" of the *Mem* was that zealotry he performed. Why the *Mem*? So it would be a sign of death... <note>The text here engages in complex letter permutations involving the letters Lamed, Mem, and Het</note>.

And this is what Pinchas took, and he stood "in the midst" of the *Mem*. Regarding this: ->"And I did not consume the children of Israel in My jealousy"<- <note>Numbers 25:11</note>. Did Pinchas then [stop] the wrath of the Holy One, Blessed be He? But is it not written: ->"And those that died in the plague were..."<- <note>Numbers 25:9</note>. [The answer is] he improved His wrath. For since all those deaths occurred, "He turned back My wrath and I did not consume the children of Israel." This means the "clear" ones were not lost.

Woe to the man who turns his face away! Woe to him who does not guard his seed! When he descends... he covers one side. The *Het* [was among] the tribe of Simeon. When the Mixed Multitude <term>Erev Rav</term> <note>The non-Israelites who left Egypt with the Jews and were often blamed for instigating sins</note> mixed with the women of the tribe of Simeon, after they were aroused and bore children, some of them died by the blow and some died by the plague.

And others died... all those were to be turned around against "And those that died in the plague." It is missing [the letter Vav]... those who died were from the beginning. But the children of Israel who remained were all the Holy Seed who were hidden, for not even one of them was missing. Regarding this it is written: "And I did not consume the children of Israel," implying that *others* were consumed. And so it is written: "My wrath from upon the children of Israel"—it does not say "from upon the others." Because of this, the verse is precise: "from upon the children of Israel." Because of this, the children of Israel were seen as they were at first, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, accepted them openly. This is like the incident of the [Golden] Calf, where it is written: ->"And there fell of the people..."<- <note>Exodus 32:28</note>. All those were from the Mixed Multitude, and not one of the children of Israel was missing. What is written afterward? ->"And Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel"<- <note>Exodus 35:1</note>.

## Main Text (Zohar)

### Right Column (Pinhas)

->**Pinhas**<-

**Take from among you an offering** <note>Exodus 35:5</note> • Come and see: at first it is written that beneath every sinner, they shall all be bent low. Since the Mixed Multitude <note>original: "Erev Rav"; the non-Israelites who left Egypt with Moses</note> committed this act <note>the sin of Baal Peor</note> and died because of it, they died in the sin against the Holy One, Blessed be He. To be reconciled with Israel, He said to them: "Gather all of you together." Once the "all" departed, "Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel" <note>Exodus 35:1</note>. According to their teachings, He said to them: "In you, the righteous, according to your worthiness, shall be My dwelling." And regarding this, it says: **Take from among you an offering**—from *you* and not from another. Not through the deeds of those below who joined with others among you. And because of this, they were all brought down. Even here, were they not from a wicked branch? And so "those who died" <note>Numbers 25:9</note>—the dead were not truly "dead" <note>spiritually</note> and were not from Israel. And because of this, He struck them, as it is written:
> **Take the sum of the heads of the children of Israel** <note>Numbers 1:2; "Take the sum" literally means "Lift the head"</note>
Lift them up, exalt them! Said Rabbi Eleazar: Furthermore, how appropriate it was here; we have not found a dispute regarding this. Rather, when he saw, he said to him: It is written,
> **And Israel joined himself unto Baal Peor** <note>Numbers 25:3</note>
They returned to join together like a man joins with his companion; thus Israel joined to Baal Peor. He said to him: Eleazar, it is so, "And Israel joined himself unto Baal Peor," but here it does not mean they were purified from that sin, but rather they were purified from death, so that death would not rule over them. He said to him: But it is written,
> **Take all the heads of the people and hang them up** <note>Numbers 25:4</note>
This was surely an act of wrath and not of mercy toward Israel. From the term "The People" <note>Ha-Am</note> we must learn: it is written here "The People," and it is written there: **The people complained**, **The people gathered**, **There fell of the people**. Come and see: **And Israel joined himself unto Baal Peor**—they did not actually worship it, but the end of the verse proves it, as it is written:
> **And the people ate and bowed down** <note>Numbers 25:2</note>
It does not say "And *Israel* ate and bowed down." Rather, it says "The People." Since it is written "And Israel joined," he was struck, but "The People" ate. Rather, "The People" were the evil desire, and he was worthy to say: what is it?

### Left Column (The Faithful Shepherd)

->**The Faithful Shepherd**<-

And what is written? **Take from among you an offering to the Lord**—and not from the Mixed Multitude, so that they do not become a harsh burden. And not only that, but the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "I desire to dwell with you," for is it not written:

And furthermore, all the children of Israel are called "Higher Ones" <note>spiritual beings</note>, while the Mixed Multitude are cast down. And because of these groups and burdens, we cry:

Arise, Holy Star, and bring forth the words of the Tabernacle <note>Sukkoth</note> for the Holy Merit, and for the Master in the first group who spoke thus: Come and see, Pinhas was zealous with a powerful zeal to establish the covenant, as it is written:

Because he took pity on Israel, and because of this, he is included with them. And this is like the Altar; Pinhas is like Isaac, and the Elder blessed the Higher Ones.

He opened and said: **Elijah, the Shepherd of the Supreme King**, a star from the work of the world. He desired the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> with the head of laughter <note>Isaac/Yitzhak means "he will laugh"</note> and the pious Pinhas. ## Pinhas

->Pinhas<-

When he completes his people, and all of them are the portion of those who merit the World to Come, they will be told in their canopy over you: this is by your will, and he gives them life. **Rabbi Pinhas ben Yair**, that great one, cast his eyes upon **the Rabbi** <note>Referring to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> and asked: Did the Holy One, Blessed be He, not know his will to give him life? He said to him: Heaven forbid! It is revealed and known to the later generations, and because of this, "Therefore say..." <note>Numbers 25:12</note>. A *Michtam* of David <note>original: *Michtam le-David*</note>. *Michtam* refers to David being "marked" <note>A play on the word *Michtam* as *mach* (lowly) and *tam* (perfect/complete)</note> in every gate, and a child was born to man, as it is written: **A Michtam of David: Guard me, O God, for I have taken refuge in You.** <note>Psalms 16:1</note>. The **Faithful Shepherd** <note>The soul of Moses</note> said: This commandment of testimony is a witness of the hidden path, which is the "Satan" <note>the adversary</note> of the testimony of faith to stand over us. And You commanded us before the King and the holy upper levels, the lights of the rose, for those companions over Israel—for those companions whose mouth is sealed over them. And there shall be assistance to be said of it and for the people of the mouth. A holy company and a holy branch, of which it is said: It is taught that it assists you to give your strength and joy in the rock. Thus, "Enduring is your dwelling place, and set in the rock is your nest" <note>Numbers 24:21</note>. It is taught: a small vessel of blue for the world and the vision of the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note>, and it rises to be said like a crown and a city.

Nestled upon its treasures and spiced for those secrets of the Laws and the Mishnahs. And every single male that comes out of his mouth, he brings into it the Name <note>the Tetragrammaton</note>, whether in sickness, or in exile, or in blessing, or in every single commandment. What is written of him? "He shall spread his palms, he shall leap and rejoice over his companion." What is "over his companion"? Over the difficulty of the secret of the "Two Faces" <note>the dual aspect of the Divine</note> from Him. The Name shall be called for all, and the Divine Presence. And because of this, they shall rejoice over his companion, as in: "May the Lord lift up His face to you and give you peace." And "set in the rock is your nest." Rather, David said of it: **The Lord is my rock and my fortress.** <note>Psalms 18:3</note>. So too we have learned: the Holy One, Blessed be He, pressed into it, strong as a rock, so that no face can open against any small thing in the world; in the strength of the pressing, it is established like a rock. And all the serpents and its difficult investigations are hers.

And because of this: **If a bird’s nest chances before you** <note>Deuteronomy 22:6</note> to open in the secular world, a "chance" and a branch of man and additions and wisdom for the portion of the people. A company of the children of insolence, and they have no depth to them to provide greenness <note>vitality</note> for the Divine Presence. This is what is written: "And the children of Israel sought the Passover..." etc. For their generations <note>original: *le-dorotam*</note>—the word "generations" is written defectively <note>missing a letter</note>, implying a lack of the tongue of greenness, and there is no protection of the Torah over it for their appointed times, for the Divine Presence did not dwell with them all their days. But for these, "If a bird’s nest chances," to bring out the secret of the Divine Presence in the secular world, a "chance," and wings spread over them, and she is found with them. And sometimes she is invited to be found with them, and the spirit of the matter is ready to be found with them. Rather, **you shall surely send away the mother.** To spread for them praised words, for them "children," masters of the Scripture.

All of them who do not acquire their learning, rather "you shall surely send away the mother." But for those who know their learning, **you shall not take the mother with the children.** And there are no words of Law <note>Halakhot</note> that are compared to the stars. These are the stars of which it is said "and all like milk," but rather for those stars of the World to Come, for those who stand forever and ever. And this is: **Let us make man in our image, after our likeness.** <note>Genesis 1:26</note>. And the Rabbis established: "the mother with the children"—everything. And to give rest to my flock, rather: "You are the Lord, you are Man," and not the idol-worshipping nations. And because of this, "Israel shall rejoice in its Maker." The **Holy Lamp** <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> said: and let the stone be for a crown in this way, this which is written of it to give and add.

For in it is the Ancient One <note>the level of Keter</note>, the Law to awaken in it, the Law to measure the amulets of pressure to spread over the dragon, hinting to the straight and remembering them in the sickness like a people who go to the field to be gathered at night, and atonement for all the stars and constellations. The Holy One, Blessed be He, created him, as it is written: **And God created man in His own image.** <note>Genesis 1:27</note>. He said to him: If so, go out...

## Main Text (The Faithful Shepherd)

And for Him, His sovereignty shall not depart from the hand of all His divisions, and He is not enslaved to the language of the profane <note>original: *chola*</note> in your statutes of the King in His forms, according to His likeness and His appearance, all of them. And because the Cause above all is not found in the upper and lower worlds to be vacant of Him, even in the smallest of all statutes, to call for sustenance and prey, and He looks with knowledge upon them all. To say this: that He does not give all wealth to be handed over to the rest of the nations. God is honored by Him from the world; rather, He spread the worlds, the Cause above all, and upon Him hang the branches. Not to a prophet, nor to an angel or a seraph, and not like the throne of the world. Immediately upon hearing these words, the Faithful Shepherd <note>Moses</note> and all his companions were shaken by the holy splendor, and they surrounded him and said: "Faithful Shepherd, if a man were not in the world except to hear this, it would be enough!" He is the one to be received in exile, in distress, to be enslaved, to be found to honor Him in all the commandments, and to be diminished in possessions as pressures require, to say that he causes pressure for all.

"And he shall lie with his fathers" <note>Deuteronomy 31:16</note>—the voice of the letters of the **Shekhinah** <term>The Divine Presence, often associated with the feminine aspect of God</term> ascended there. **Wisdom** <note>The Sefirah of *Chokhmah*</note> is there, and "possessions" was said to receive it for the elders of Israel. And things were said about it in the refined measure, giving birth to offspring in it, and seventy faces to the Torah. And in it, in all their desires, a staff "to mention My name." "You shall mention My name"—it is required of him, not in life, refined "to mention My name" in the field, refined for all, "and I will bless you."

->**By the Mouth of**<-

**The lot shall their inheritance be divided.** <note>Numbers 26:56</note> When Rabbi Yehuda arrived, he opened and said: *"I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever; nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it..."* <note>Ecclesiastes 3:14</note> King Solomon, whose wisdom was greater than all the people of the world—did he not know that whatever God does shall be forever? And the statute is matter, and "I knew" is for what a man does not know. Even so, King Solomon's wisdom rose above all the people of the world, and what he knew, all the rest of the people of the world did not know. Come and see: a craftsman of the world, when he performs a work to be placed in it and to be looked at, he exerts strength once or twice and makes it, and afterward he adds to it or subtracts from it. But the Holy One is not so. He brought forth His work in perfection, such that there is no authority in it at all, and it is truly a statute to be established as is fitting, and it does not need addition or subtraction from it. Because of this, it is written: "And God did it so that they should fear before Him," and this is better than anything. Furthermore, "whatever God does" for the repair of the world, "it shall be forever." Rabbi Yitzhak said: If so, what is "and God did it so that they should fear before Him"? Rather, the verse should have said: "For all that God has done shall be forever." What is "all"? It includes everything. Rather, the scripture says, as it is written: *"Eye has not seen, O God, besides You, what He will do for him who waits for Him."* <note>Isaiah 64:3</note> You have made from His failures a rope to say of it that He moves and covers, and His stars are all on every side, and the researchers of the world, everything. And from here a power goes out to be called...

## Main Text (Zohar)

To be found and to be established; and this **Upper and Precious Tree** <note>original: *ilana ala’ah ve-yakira*; referring to the Sefirah of Tiferet or the collective structure of the divine world</note> is above all other trees. This has been established: that hidden world which is concealed, bends toward and prepares this Tree constantly, to establish it and rectify it through its work. It crowns it with crowns so that its springs never cease from it, forever and ever. Like that Tree, the **Tree of Faith** <note>The Sefirah of Malchut or the totality of the divine system</note> dwells within it, apart from all other trees, for they all stand within it. And concerning this, it is written:
> **“Whatever God [Elohim] does, it shall be forever; nothing can be added to it, and nothing can be taken from it.”**
<note>Ecclesiastes 3:14</note>
Behold, "nothing can be added to it and nothing can be taken from it," and regarding this, it is written in the Torah: "You shall not add to it, nor shall you take away from it," for it is the Torah itself. And it was said that this is constantly called **Elohim**. "Elohim" alone refers to **Gevurah** <note>The attribute of Judgment or Strength</note>; it establishes the body and life, searching out all life, searching for its characteristics—whether peace or not peace. And regarding this, He "constantly does" <note>original: *ya’aseh* (future/continuous tense)</note> like a spring whose waters never fail for generations upon generations. Because of this, it is written that He "made" <note>original: *asah* (past tense)</note> both of them before Him. To establish this Tree in a perfect arrangement that takes hold of every side, above and below, so that his inheritance is before Him and they shall not exchange it for another side for generations upon generations. Rabbi Zakkai said: Certainly, you have spoken well. But we must further look first at "He shall do" [*ya’aseh*] and later "He made" [*asah*]—what is the difference between this and that? The Eternal God certainly "shall do" and establish this Tree so that its waters never fail for generations, and later "He made." What is "God made"? It is another Tree below it. And this "He shall do" refers to how this Lower Tree acts and prepares it, and whoever enters the upper path must, even against his will, praise the Lower Tree and fear to diminish it, but rather [honor it] as is fitting. Come and see: it is like a mountain at the entrance, and therefore they are called the **Guardians of Israel**. This is the Tree below, and its gifts are from the strength above. Therefore, it is not written "He shall do" but "He made," protecting them before Him like the world, so that those who appear to draw near shall not approach it, and no "other" shall be enticed. They are protected by the many "bans" <note>original: *chermei*; restrictions or excommunications</note> of the Torah, so they do not seek to slaughter or gaze [at forbidden mysteries]. Come [and see] regarding this Tree, in which all sustenance dwells, it says:
> **“You support my lot.”**
<note>Psalms 16:5</note>
What is **"my lot"** [*gorali*]? This is the delight which King David took hold of. Even "the lot" is written, and so it is with the letter *Yod*. It is written "according to the lot," and all of them are the portions of those who labor in the Torah day and night, who know its restrictions and the wisdom included at all times. The Upper Altar, as is said, is "perfect in wisdom," for this Upper Torah is a sign for this one below, and it is said of them here: "my servants and my portion." Rabbi Abba opened and said:
> **“And there was a voice from above the firmament.”**
<note>Ezekiel 1:25</note>
This is the Voice that takes hold of this **Firmament** [*Raki'a*] and joins with it. And this is **"He has made a memorial for His wonders."** The secret of the firmament stands over them, over those living beings. This is what they say: "to divide between water and water." It has been established that He sank the firmaments higher and higher, and they push and provide nourishment. For it has nothing of its own, except what they give to it and what covers it. Its beginning is the mystery of what is written: **“In my poverty, I have prepared for the house of my God.”** <note>1 Chronicles 22:14</note> This brings in fruit and produces arrangements, for from its exhaustion it brings out words to all sides. It flies over their portions, the hosts and the commanders. In the morning, He gathers them all and brings them into their chambers, and they have no dominion, for in the morning all are included, as it says: "To declare Your lovingkindness in the morning, and Your faithfulness in the nights." It has been established that there is a Voice over this firmament from which we learn. And this firmament, through the movement of this Voice, awakens all the hosts; they do not remain idle and have no sign except to stand in their places and be called by their portions. They look to that center which moves that firmament, and they are blessed because of it. Therefore, it is "above the firmament which is over their heads." Come and see: the firmament is over those [beings], "the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone." This refers to the Wisdom of Israel, and this is the mystery of what is written:
> **“And they saw the God of Israel, and under His feet was like a work of paved sapphire.”**
<note>Exodus 24:10</note>
When Israel sought to inherit the land, it was written regarding it "by lot" [*goral*]. Some say this for a division and that for a division, and this is from beneath the **Throne** [*Kursayya*].

## Main Text (Zohar - Portion of Pinhas)

In the likeness of the King below, and this is the staff of the tribes of Israel. It is written: *And Benjamin* <note>referring to the tribal territory</note>, so it was by the lot, certainly the portion of his inheritance. **Rabbi Isaac and Rabbi Judah** were traveling on the road to greet the Holy Face <note>a respectful term for a great sage</note>, Rabbi Eleazar, who was behind them. They saw him certainly running after the *Shekhinah* <note>the Divine Presence, often depicted as a traveling companion for the righteous</note>. When they reached him, they saw his garments were in order and almost appeared new. He opened his discourse and said:
> "Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the Lord..." (Isaiah 51:1)

"Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness"—these are the ones who follow after faith and take hold of the "Life of Righteousness." Do not look at it as a mere point like the merchants of the world do, who cause death to themselves because they did not eat well, but rather consumed fire and darkness and went about with the merchant's grievances.

## Main Text (Zohar - Portion of Tzav / The Faithful Shepherd)

-> **Command** <-
the children of Israel and say to them: "My offering, My bread..." It is written:
> "Does the Lord delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obeying the voice of the Lord?" (1 Samuel 15:22)

The will of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not in the sacrifice itself, for one brings a sacrifice because of a sin. Rather, a sacrifice that is a "vessel of guilt" is one thing, but there is the "Peace Offering" and the "Inquiry of Peace Offerings," and the "Continual Offering"—these are what atone for sins. **Rabbi Abba** opened:
> "The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit..." (Psalms 51:19)

This verse has been established: that the will of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not in the twelve types of animal sacrifice when a man sins, but rather in a "broken spirit." Because of this, my earlier words were not known. And so I heard from the *Holy Lamp* <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> that in every place where a man is found in his sin, he draws upon himself an "impure spirit" <term>Ruach Mesava: a spiritual defilement</term> from the side of impurity, which leads the man and rules over him according to its will. That impure side grows strong within him and overpowers him. A man must always strive to rule over it and purify himself. In the time when the Holy Temple stood, he would bring his sacrifice, and his entire atonement depended on it until he repented and broke that spirit through his humility and erased it. This is the "breaking" of that level of impurity. When that impure spirit is broken and he brings his sacrifice, this is "drawing near" <note>the word for sacrifice, *Korban*, comes from the root "to draw near"</note> with proper will. But if he does not break that spirit, his sacrifice is nothing. Therefore, it was handed down that this sacrifice is not for the "voice" <note>external prayer</note> to sustain. Thus, "the sacrifices of God" are properly a "broken spirit," so that the impure spirit shall be broken and not rule. Regarding one who breaks it properly, it is written: "A spirit that passes and does not return." Let that man stand in his wisdom so that it <note>the impurity</note> never returns to him before the Holy One, Blessed be He. "A broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise"—this is a delight like the delights of God; "God will not despise" because it is precious to Him.

"**Command** (*Tzav*) the children of Israel." What is the meaning of **Command**? This refers to "Idolatry" <note>based on a Talmudic tradition that the word *Tzav* implies a warning against idol worship</note>. This is so he does not cause himself to be defiled by the impure spirit, which is actual idolatry. **Rabbi Eleazar** opened:
> "I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride..." (Song of Songs 5:1)

This verse was established regarding all the hidden animals of the sacrifice. Everything was said, but it is proper that they "scratched the salt" and the "living opening." He said: because salt was found in the atonement of Enoch, and I have learned it. He said: it is not so, for that is the salt that kills.

It explains how sin draws an impure spirit onto a person and how the act of sacrifice (Korban) is intended to break that impurity and draw the soul back to the Divine.</summary>

And it is understood that he said everything is one word. And until now I have not heard, my son Eleazar, what you were saying." For every spirit of the sacrifices has many secrets there, and they were not handed over to the exile except to you, the masters of truth, for the spirit of their words is not hidden from them. The secret of these sacrifices is the "Last Living Creature" <note>Chaya</note> of those holy kings. And this spirit, "and let fowl fly," refers to two spirits. And because of this, it spreads and crowns from below, and it is hidden. And the sacrifice of birds from every side that is in it is not brought... and he merited and inherited those which are like truth for their union from all.

# Pinchas

And each and every one, both among the upper levels <note>Sefirot</note> and the lower levels, according to their likeness, approach and travel, this side toward that side, to the secret of the sacrifice as is fitting. Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Abba and the rest of the companions came and prostrated themselves before him <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note>. Rabbi Eleazar said: At this time, the Torah was spoken as if at Mount Sinai, for the Holy One, blessed be He, has not rejoiced in it so much in all His days, and the two judgments of "Woe" are removed from the world. Woe, when you depart from the world! Who will then nullify the [harsh] intentions against the Torah? Everything will be darkened from that side, and for whoever walks upon the path of the King, there will be no <term>Mezuzah</term> <note>a protective scroll; here used metaphorically for protection</note>. May there not be a generation like this generation of Rabbi Shimon, the master of the garden!

Rabbi Shimon said regarding this secret: In the end, you must not taste anything until the King has eaten. And I—what shall be for the "leftovers"? The leftover has already come in this manner previously. The engraved likenesses <note>celestial forms</note> are invited to the Supernal Throne, and then their spirits spread over the bodies and desire the sacrifice, according to the secret of their levels. The foundation in this world is weakened and nourished—**"How manifold are Your works, O Lord!"** <note>Psalm 104:24</note>. This is when they appear in the sacrifice, for their spirit spreads over them, and the likenesses are bound and invited over these creatures. This is what they say: "And the <term>Ofanim</term> and the <term>Hayyot HaKodesh</term>" <note>classes of angels: "Wheels" and "Holy Living Creatures"</note> and all those other hosts that spread out from their places.

Afterward, the High Priest, from another secret of the unique holiness—this is the "Assembly of the World," our flame, etc.—the unification that is unified is: **"Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One."** <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note>. And afterward, the Levites who awaken the melody—this is "May His Great Name," etc. "Be careful for yourselves lest [your heart] be enticed," etc. This is in the manner of the Levites, in order to hide the side <margin>Another version: to storm the side</margin> of this in this sacrifice. And afterward, he shall scratch <note>a ritual mark</note> that which is not truth, and merit and merits shall scratch the end that stands over the sacrifice <margin>Another version: the sacrifice of this world, the levels</margin> of the living creatures, the upper levels, the innermost of all that stands upon the table.

But there is no permission for any of them to eat or to stretch out a hand to the sacrifice until the Supernal King eats—and these are the Three First [Sefirot] and the Three Last [Sefirot]. Once He has eaten, He gives permission to all the likenesses and all those sides that branch out from their places to eat. Then "Man," who is the likeness that includes every side, rules and falls upon his face and surrenders himself and his likeness to the "Man" who is engraved upon those likenesses, so that his prayer may be mingled as is fitting. And this is: **"To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul."** <note>Psalm 25:1</note>. Three other likenesses and all those who spread out from their places [recite] "A Psalm of David," and this is: they shall look, they shall bow, they shall be agitated, they shall speak—all of them eat and are satisfied, each one as is fitting for him. From here on, there is no man who walks and learns in it <margin>Another version: to his path</margin> vanity and cloud, and the Lord is like a day of healing... <note>The text here uses obscure Aramaic idioms regarding spiritual blindness and judgment</note> to turn all the "rich-in-light" <note>Aramaic: *Saginorin*, a euphemism for the blind</note> against the man. Concerning this it is written: **"Happy is the people for whom it is so..."** <note>Psalm 144:15</note>.

---

Rabbi Shimon was going to Tiberias when Elijah encountered him. He said to him: "Peace be upon you, my Master. In what is the Holy One, blessed be He, currently occupied?" He replied: "In the deep [mysteries] of the sacrifice." And he said new words of support. "Fortunate are you! And I have come to establish for you a new basket and screen <note>metaphors for new revelations</note>. I wish to receive from you wisdom from the Heavenly Academy. This question: they have said that in the World to Come there is no eating and drinking, yet it is written: **'I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey...'** <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note> etc. If there is no eating and drinking, why does He say 'I have eaten' and 'I have drunk my wine with my milk'?"

Rabbi Shimon said: "And what did the Holy One, blessed be He, answer them?" He replied: "The Holy One, blessed be He, said [to ask] all his days and his masters, and I have come to receive it from you." Rabbi Shimon said: "How much the Holy One, blessed be He, cherished the Assembly of Israel! Because of the greatness of the love He has for her, His actions exceed what He usually does. Even though it is not His way to eat and drink, because of love He ate and drank, and lowered Himself and drank for her, to do her will. A bride enters the bridal canopy, and now to eat—is it not right that she should eat? A gift given plainly—it is not His way to act so. He returned: **'I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride... eat, friends; drink, and be drunk with love.'** <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note> Since she came to the canopy, I have eaten."

It also features a dialogue between Rabbi Shimon and Elijah regarding the metaphorical "eating" of God in the Song of Songs as an expression of love for Israel.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the sacrificial offerings (Korbanot) from the portion of Pinchas, focusing on the mystical union between the Divine and the community of Israel through the metaphor of a royal banquet.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

"I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey" <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>. We learn from David, who invited the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note>—for the exchange of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is the Holy One, Blessed be He—and He accepted and performed His will. He invited the King and the Queen <note>Matronita</note> together, as it is before the Lord <term>for your offering</term> <note>original: "le-minchatecha"</note>, a place where the King and Queen are together so as not to separate them. They are the kings and the appointed ones of the King, as it is written: <quote>"Let Your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let Your pious ones sing for joy; for the sake of David..."</quote> <note>Psalms 132:9-10</note>. "Let Your priests be clothed with righteousness"—to adorn them, for "Righteousness" <note>Tzedek</note> comes from the side of the Left, yet is given to the Priest <note>who is usually Right/Chesed</note>. "And let Your pious ones sing for joy"—to adorn them with singing, for song and music are all expressions of the Moon <note>the Shekhinah</note>, while "Your pious ones" <note>Chasidim</note> come from the side of the Right, <term>Chesed</term> <note>Loving-kindness</note> of the Holy One, Blessed be He. For David, this was not his usual way. David said: <quote>"For the sake of David Your servant, turn not away the face of Your anointed."</quote> The preparation of the palate is through the blasts <note>of the Shofar</note>; do not turn him away. David waited, and it was pleasant for him to do Your will and to see my desire.

And we learn from the way of the world: when a person invites a friend, that friend is obligated to do his will, even if it is not his usual custom. So too, <quote>"And he took of his fat and of his..."</quote> <note>referring to Abel's offering in Genesis 4:4</note>. A groom waits for the bride, and even if it is not his custom to dwell except in palaces and canopies, he gives her a place to dwell, and the bride accepts according to the will of the groom. This is what is written: "And he dwelt in that place," for the sake of the bride, even if it was not his usual way. So too here: "I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey," even if it was not His usual way, for the sake of the bride's pleasure; He made a home for the bride and not in another place. In His own place, He does not eat or drink. In her place, He eats and drinks, as it is written: "My bride is with me." The fats arranged by the Holy One, Blessed be He, for Abraham—they did not eat or drink in their own place, but for the sake of Abraham, they ate and drank. Rabbi Hiyya was concerned by this matter; the Holy One, Blessed be He, wished to speak, and so as not to diminish the goodness He showed to the Assembly of Israel, He directed the word to Himself. You are meritorious in the world, for such a thing is found for a master, and of you it is written: <quote>"The righteous rules through the fear of God"</quote> <note>2 Samuel 23:3</note>.

**"My offering, My bread for My fire..."** <note>Numbers 28:2</note>. Rabbi Yehuda said: In the offering there is smoke, there is spirit, and there is a pleasing aroma. The smoke represents the matters of anger, as it is written: "For a fire is kindled in My anger"; these are rectified by the smoke that settles the anger within the five senses. The "aroma" refers to those called "apples." Rabbi Isaac said: Regarding the apples, it is written: <quote>"And the scent of your nose is like apples"</quote> <note>Song of Songs 7:9</note>.

**The** first lamb you shall offer in the morning. What is "in the morning"? This is the morning of Abraham, as it is written: <quote>"And Abraham rose early in the morning"</quote> <note>Genesis 22:3</note>. How do we know this "morning" refers to Abraham? Rabbi Eleazar said: From here—"in the morning," another morning is not written, but **the morning**, the first light that the Holy One, Blessed be He, remembered from the Work of Creation. Therefore it says "in the morning, in the morning" to make known that He accepted the morning for Abraham to bring the offering. The afternoon offering <note>Bein ha-Arbayim</note> corresponds to Isaac, to correspond to the evening pressure. How do we know? As it is written: <quote>"And Isaac went out to meditate in the field toward evening"</quote> <note>Genesis 24:63</note>. Thus, the evening belongs to Isaac, as we have established.

## Commentary
### The Faithful Shepherd (Raya Mehemna)

**This commandment** is to offer the daily portion (and to offer to the Sun and the Star, and the additional offering <note>Musaf</note> on the Holy New Moon). The holy portions every day are "Blessed forever and ever" to the King in the palace of the Queen. If there is a special permission in the world, an addition is required, such as the Musaf on Sabbath, on the Holy New Moon, and the Musaf for all appointed times. Their matter stands before Him at night, and the Central Column <note>the Sefirah of Tiferet</note> is the master of this will. Jacob established the evening prayer <note>Arvit</note> to uphold his level, the Central Column. Because of this, they established that the burnt offerings are consumed on the altar all night, corresponding to the exile which is likened to night, where the "other side" rules. And all the punishments of the kingdoms are there, but merit remains in the exile with Israel. One can approach the Master: <quote>"In the morning, O Lord, You hear my voice; in the morning I lay my requests before You and wait in expectation"</quote> <note>Psalms 5:4</note>. And because of this, "And he was saddened in the morning"—there is no encounter except for Pinchas, as in "Do not entreat <note>tifge'i</note> me," for he stopped him and did not merit... for the sake of the world's correction... this is the Shekhinah.

It uses the metaphor of a royal banquet to describe the union between God and the Shekhinah facilitated by human prayer and sacrifice.</summary>

## Pinhas

-> Pinhas <-

The **Shekhinah** <note>The feminine aspect of the Divine</note> in exile is found in her fullness, hidden from the world. And what is written? *“And He gave His strength into captivity, and His glory into the hand of the foe”* <note>Psalm 78:61</note> to let it be known that there in exile, He is with the Shekhinah. And if you say to Isaac <note>representing the attribute of Judgment/Gevurah</note>, provide for her a sapphire radiance, because they arise in every night—which is the time of exile—to the throne of her Husband. They established the **Evening Prayer** as optional <note>original: *tefillat arvit reshut*</note>. And we have explained that for the sacrifice, they wait there to consume, just as in the first matters. Like these changes, they are gathered and plucked before Him, and they testify to the King, and they bind her with many knots of various kinds to awaken and signal to her. And they raise her toward the Fellowship to be partnered with her.

**The Faithful Shepherd** <note>A title for Moses, who reveals secrets in this section of the Zohar</note> said: O Holy Priest, because of this, according to the secret of the engravings, the side of death was cast upon them to go toward the **Tzadik** <note>The Righteous One, referring to the Sefirah of Yesod</note>, the Life of the Worlds, who examines every support engraved for prayer, waiting like a body in all its movements. And upon what does she lean? Upon **Yesod** <note>Foundation</note>, like a right arm. May the Lord help me until the morning. When the time for the **Mincha** <note>Afternoon</note> prayer arrives in the evening, she stands as a vessel and finds the Levite <note>representing the left side/judgment</note> at the time of evening, because the prayer was delayed. She stands to be judged by the measure of the exile of Esau, and there is also the voice of the Hassidim. And upon the windows, the divisions of judgment, which are the judgment of all the moons. And Joseph <note>the Tzadik</note> did not examine there, for he is the one who examines in every shade. For he is destined to break through the thick clouds to spread out, and in the assembly, he offers incense and stands before the Lady. And there is our protection, and there is your peace and your prostration to my sheaf. And like the Tzadik, everyone who bows, bows at the "Tzadik" <note>referring to the liturgical practice of bowing at certain points in prayer</note>.

The Holy Priest, the **Faithful Shepherd**, said: Thus it is said,
> *And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him* <note>Exodus 13:19</note>
Because the body and the Covenant <note>the sign of circumcision, linked to Yesod/Joseph</note> are together. And regarding you, it is said: *“And behold, my sheaf arose and also stood upright”* <note>Genesis 37:7</note>, for thus is the falling from a standing position, and so all the straightening and rising. And in everything, everyone who bows, bows at "Blessed" <note>Baruch</note>, and this is "and they prostrated to my sheaf" to the flame of desire in the right and left, the body and the Covenant. And afterwards, she ascends upon them to the heart to open the mouth with these sections, bowing to the light of the Litra to establish at your right hand those who stand, refined like maidens.

And because of this, the exile of the Morning is the strength of the Evening. In the Evening, he says: May we merit to be placed between the arms of the King. In exile, when the Passover comes, he will spread his voice in the right to all, and in the left arm, the judgment will go out and the voice will be refined. And there is their shepherd, and he will be proven from the exile. And because the deeds of Isaac <note>Judgment</note> did not go out, he placed his hands and moved the mountain in your right hand with joy. And because of this, the Lord said to my Lady: Sit at my right hand, waiting to receive the son of Joseph. And he said to him: Sit at my right hand until I make the enemies in the exile of Israel a footstool for your feet. At that voice, an **Extra Spirit** <note>Ruach Yeteira</note> will be awakened and will overflow upon Israel, for He has hidden His face from every side. And He will place at the right for Israel those who are worthy of the world.

And when the guilty are present, like the rest of the Sabbath <note>Erev Shabbat</note>, an **Extra Soul** <note>Nefesh Yeteira</note> is added on the Sabbath, and they have no power like on a weekday. An Extra Soul they do not have on a weekday to live by, but only the soul of the male. And all of Israel are worthy of the Extra Soul on the Sabbath, each according to his deeds. And it is ready to rest upon all of Israel at all times, even on weekdays, for they are all prepared to receive the Lord. For in every sacrifice, the name of the Lord is crowned upon them, as the priests who are the crown upon Him.

And there is an **Extra Soul** for all of Israel on the Sabbath and Good Festivals <note>Yom Tov</note>. And because of this, we established at all times when the hand reaches to provide for all blessings for sustenance, and we do not say "Musaf" <note>the additional prayer</note> except for the Crown <note>**Keter**</note>. And on the Sabbath, we established to say, like Joseph, the Crown: *“They shall give to You, O Lord our God...”* <note>The Kedushah of Musaf</note>. However, for every person of Israel, there is an Extra Soul according to his own level. If he is a man of Kindness <note>**Chesed**</note>, they give him an Extra Soul from the attribute of Kindness. If he is a Mighty man <note>**Gevurah**</note>, they give him an Extra Soul from the attribute of Strength. If he is a man of Torah, they give him an Extra Soul from the attribute of Truth <note>Tiferet</note>. And this Extra Soul is the inclusion of the Sefirot, according to the King's word.

If the people of Israel are prepared, whether from the beginning or the end, it is said of them that they dwell and go in the halls of the King, and they give him an Extra Soul which is called the **Crown of Kingship** <note>Keter Malkhut</note>. And if he is worthy to establish the wisdom of all, as it is said:
> *In wisdom You have made them all* <note>Psalm 104:24</note>
Then they give him an Extra Soul from below. And if he is prepared for all, they give him an Extra Soul from the Understanding <note>**Binah**</note>. And if he is prepared in prophecy and visions, they give him an Extra Soul from **Netzach** and **Hod**. And if he is a perfect Tzadik from the Crown, the secret of the Covenant, the sign of the Good Festivals, the sign of the Tefillin, they give him an Extra Soul of the **Tzadik**. And in every place, the Extra Soul is from above. And if he is a son of man who receives from every kind, they give him the Crown of the Soul, the strength of our God.

## Main Text (Zohar)

Our God, whenever we call to Him <note>Deuteronomy 4:7</note> there is none holy like the Lord <note>1 Samuel 2:2</note> for all are His likeness. The **Beauty** <note>The Sephirah of Tiferet</note> of the King is crowned with the **Supreme Crown** <note>Keter Elyon</note>, through which He strengthens His **Divine Presence** <note>Shekhinah</note> to give life to the "extra soul." This is the foundation of the spirit, to fulfill the verse: *“I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh”* <note>Joel 3:1</note>. Within Him, all is included and explained from above to below in this manner: the letter *Yod* is **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note>, the letter *Heh* is **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, and the letter *Vav* includes the six hidden Sephirot down to the **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note>. The final *Heh* is **Kingdom** <note>Malkhut</note>. From the unity of "Our God," the **Crown** <note>term: Keter; the highest emanation, representing Divine Will</note> is upon His head, washing Him with the taste of strength on the Sabbath day. Because He is the Cause of Causes, hidden within this Crown, He emerges to illuminate. On Sabbaths and Festivals, the "Other Side" <note>the forces of spiritual impurity</note> has no dominion to test or examine; therefore, its dominion over the stars and the "salty sea" is removed. All are crowned before the Matron <note>The Shekhinah, depicted as a Queen</note> of the King, just as lights are bound in the world; when the end is revealed, the light will break through like caves of miners and the clefts of rocks.

**146.** Eighty-eight and two: Faithful Shepherd, you are appointed over all Israel to say of Him: *“There is none holy like the Lord our God.”* To place a Crown upon every single one, providing them with existence through the Crown. When you are thin <note>humble/nullified</note>, the Crown is upon you—not as one who is "wise," "understanding," "pious," "mighty," "a seeker," "a miracle-worker," "righteous," or "king" <note>meaning: the Crown transcends all specific attributes</note>. One must look at the image of the Nest <note>the Divine source</note> without looking at the image of the children of Israel, of whom it is said there are five commandments of their Master that heal you, so there shall be no defect in him. His Divine Presence is above and below in the Supreme Crown, filling every place.

**He opened** and said: Be prepared and girded, Rabbi Shimon and all the companions—even Shimon is included with them. He said to them: Do not let yourselves be found according to their judgments. Worthy are the children of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; no one can find [fault] with you except the princes of the world. For even the whole Torah was hanging over the Reed Sea in this manner, as it is said: *“The measure thereof is longer than the earth and broader than the sea”* <note>Job 11:9</note>. Your elders, may everything be fulfilled in you that was fulfilled in the Torah. For the sake of the soul that is established in the "heart of heaven," His greatness and strength are in the holes and standing places. They prepare and arrange all the Additional Prayers <note>Musaf</note> of Sabbaths and Festivals. Every Musaf prayer in which we say "Crown" <note>Keter; the opening of the Kedushah in Musaf</note> is designated to make [the Divine] known. All the prayers of Israel are like a merchant's ship in the "Book of Days," where all souls of good life are protected from all kinds of destruction. For on Good Days <note>Festivals</note>, they rise to the holiness of the Merchant <note>the Divine provider</note>, and the wisdom of the wicked is green with envy. He speaks with the field <note>the Shekhinah</note> and opens with her a discourse that does not cease until life comes. For everyone who cries out for learning and laments over the exile in the writing of the Matron—they are beloved, and the depths of the Torah are handed over to those who enter. Thus, the people and the long portion that ascends is hidden in the Matron. Those who merit the Torah have brains <note>intellectual/spiritual lights</note> upon her. This is the "Exile of the Evening," which we established through Jacob, who came and acquired: *“And behold, the angels of God were ascending and descending on it”* <note>Genesis 28:12</note>. These are the ones who raise the "brains" and bring them down. When they descend, the "brains" are beneath them, and they care for them in many battles. Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—the Holy One, blessed be He, brings peace and the spirit of the Lord to the building of the Torah. He calls the "Battle of the Building" the Evening Prayer <note>Arvit</note> until the rise of dawn. Rabban Gamliel established it until the rise of dawn, for its commandment lasts all night, but the Sages made a fence until midnight. He has mercy on His people until the rise of dawn. One who speaks of the "Exile of the Evening" refers to the closure until the morning of Abraham, who sought the four hours, as it says: *“And Abraham rose early in the morning”* <note>Genesis 19:27</note>. This is the place of which you said "Dawn," which is in the name of Isaac, for there it is: *“To the Chief Musician; upon the hind of the morning”* <note>Psalm 22:1</note>. After all of them, to humble your enemy, is Jacob, of whom it is said "Light"; of him it is said: *“In the morning he shall devour the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil”* <note>Genesis 49:27</note>. He wraps himself in Beauty <note>Tiferet</note>, the Holy Temple, the Sacrifice, and Jacob.

**Rabbi Shimon said:** Faithful Shepherd, through him this was opened. From your gathering, you speak. The years of the Sabbath lead to the right side, which is **Victory** <note>Netzach</note>, the head of those who say the song: *“To the Chief Musician; upon the hind of the morning”* <note>Psalm 22:1</note>. Through him, he shall come upon it like a priest of the calling. Because he is a priest, and there are two songs, we established in the Mishnah: "From what time do we read the Shema in the morning?" It does not say "in the morning-light" but "at the dawns"—two. Two times shall be awakened for the prophecy of Messiah son of David, to receive the morning and to be bound in the bond of the Holy One, blessed be He, with a pleasant voice on the Right.

## Pinchas

->**Pinchas**<-

Come and see the secret of David’s harp <note>The "harp of David" is a classic Kabbalistic metaphor for the Shekhinah being awakened by the "north wind" or divine spirit</note>, which plays music to separate the profane from the "Middle Daughter" <note>The Shekhinah</note> via the North Wind, which comes from the side of the Central Column <note>The Sefirah of Tiferet</note> and the Foundation of the Living Worlds <note>The Sefirah of Yesod</note>. When he plays the harp—which is the Shekhinah, the vision of the Sages of Understanding—the "children of the conductor upon the stringed instruments" <note>A reference to Psalm 6</note> hear it. And the Foundation of the Living Worlds, when it plays <note>The text here appears repetitive or a variant version</note>, calls out to gather the Shekhinah to the River, to the Righteous One <note>Yesod</note> who is called the **Covenant of the Rainbow**. This is the sign of the Sabbath, the sign of the letter *Yod*, the sign of the Tefillin, and the sign of the Covenant of Circumcision. Corresponding to these words is the secret of the signs of the Name: "Y-H-V-H is in peace," "To the Lord in Kindness," and so on. These are the ten of the Central Column that incline toward **Kindness** (*Chesed*) for the perfectly righteous to sustain them—these are the houses of blessing for the exiles—and incline toward the wicked to judge them in Gehenna according to their deeds. And in the Central Column, He crowns the intermediate ones. Like the power of water, the three colors of the rainbow are the sign of the Covenant of the Rainbow, the Only Daughter, the **Sabbath Queen**.

The sign of the letter *Yod* has six levels under its authority. Regarding the Sabbath, we have heard that all are protected, as it is said of them: "Sabbath and Festivals are a cloak for every Only Daughter." The Sabbath, which is the Crown, the Daughter of the Queen, shall be called "Sabbath" below. **Metatron** <note>The highest angel, often described as the heavenly steward</note> is her servant at this time, and his sign is the number sixty, representing his perfection. Thus, for every side that brings death, they are removed... they are the "waters of sin" that cloud the worlds.

From the Western side, the Name *Yod-He-Vav* is present. With Metatron, there is sixty in **Might** (*Gevurah*) and six in **Beauty** (*Tiferet*). When he rules over the fifty gates, the Kingship of one Kindness is established. You are entrusted with the "Limbs of the King" <note>The Sefirot</note> to receive the Sabbath, which rules over them. Ten kingships for Kindness, ten for Strength, ten for Wisdom, and nine for the Gate. For this reason, the "Mixed Multitude" <note>Erev Rav; spiritual antagonists</note> do not have power on the Sabbath. The "Dew of Light" is like the dew of Metatron... **Old Man, Old Man!** <note>A common Zoharic exclamation when a deep secret is revealed</note> The Shekhinah is called the Ark. From the side of Kindness, she is called "Water"; from the side of Might, she is called "Fire"; and from the side of the Central Column, she is called "Air."

Because of the great desire to be cloaked in the Shekhinah—who is the Sabbath Queen below—her Kingship rules over all: over the earth, the angels, the prophets, and the wise. Because there is no "striking" on the Sabbath, and the "Extra Soul" of the community is present, there is no day like it on earth. Because the Higher Shekhinah does not spread over the earth below except on the Holy Sabbath, the "yoke" of the mundane does not rise upon it. The Lower Shekhinah is a portion for the recipient from the side of Might; she is "perfect" from the side of Kindness, as it is said: *Walk before Me and be perfect.*

From the side of the Central Column, "Kindness did not ascend," meaning the "yoke" of the **Other Side** (*Sitra Achra*) has no permission to rule—neither the Destroyer, nor the Angel of Death. During the weekdays, the Lower Shekhinah is clothed in the "Husks" (*Kelipot*) <note>The shells of impurity that conceal divine light</note> which resemble the mundane. But now, she is divested of them. At this time, it is like the day of the Wedding Canopy. Wherever Israel is found, they are protected. One must not allow the profane to touch the Holy Land, which is the Shekhinah. One should not look at the "children of the earth" <note>The unrefined or external forces</note> on the Sabbath.

The Shekhinah is called **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*), as it is written: *In wisdom He founded the earth.* Through the Central Column, the foundation of the children has existence in the world. One must increase acts of Kindness. Therefore, it is said: **"The Children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, to observe the Sabbath throughout their generations as an eternal covenant."** Blessed is He who made her dwell with them, so they do not go out from the Private Domain <note>The realm of holiness/God</note> to the Public Domain <note>The realm of multiplicity/the Other Side</note>.

It emphasizes the Sabbath as a time of "Covenant" where the forces of judgment and death have no authority over Israel.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the spiritual mechanics of the Tabernacle and the sacrificial system, specifically focusing on the balance between the divine attributes and the protection of the Shekhinah from external forces.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Four living creatures <note>The *Chayot*, the angelic beings of the Divine Chariot</note> provide sustenance to the living, and Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note> emanates to them. These are Samael and the Serpent who entwine around Israel to nullify them, so that they may not enter the Palace of the Divine Presence <note>The Shekhinah</note>. This is to prevent the domain of Samael from prevailing—he who divides the authority of the celestial princes. He opens and bends, dividing the law; such is the entire domain of Samael and the Serpent, and the scepters of the nations' rulers.

**He opened** his discourse and said: "My beloved has gone down to his garden..." <note>Song of Songs 6:2</note> until "the kings of the east," as printed in the portion of *Vayikra*, page 3, side b. **And in the first assembly**, they ascended: "I have gathered my myrrh with my spice" <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note> to the desire of the Right Arm <note>Chesed/Mercy</note> and the blessing of the Left. "I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey"—this refers to Jacob and Rachel. "I have drunk my wine with my milk"—the Right Arm and the Left Arm. The Right is the arm of the Left in the blessing of the Left. These three are united: Jacob with Rachel, the Middle Pillar <note>Tiferet</note> within the Kingdom <note>Malkhut</note>. The Left Arm is the blessing of the Right, Power <note>Gevurah</note> within the Assembly of Israel. Many of His attributes ascend in this manner. Rather, the secret of it is that in every generation, these masters of judgment, Justice and Your Kindnesses, shall soften. One must awaken the ancient ones and your Levites; he should have said "Holiness is Kindness to them," a call to merit upon him. But in the midst of merit, it is for me to do Your will, even when the Master of the House changes His mind. Even if they fall before the King, he must do my will. Because of this, the sages taught: "Whatever the Master of the House tells you, do—except for 'leave'" <note>A Talmudic maxim regarding hospitality and humility</note>. And despite all this, the secret is not fully revealed, as it is written: "For You, O Lord, I have not hoped." In all sacrifices, it is not written in such a way, but rather to vow to You, to be able to show my sorrow for my grain, for the goodness of the sacrifice. But I have chosen my myrrh—myrrh and aloes—with the spices of the world's incense. "I have eaten my honeycomb"—the taste of Israel—"with my honey"—Blessed be the Name of His glorious Kingdom forever and ever. "I have drunk my wine"—and he was silent until he heard His name, and he said "with my milk." From here we learn: "Eat, friends; drink, and be drunk with love" <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>. Three for the lower ones and three for the upper ones. Take and be drunk with the beloveds, for the blessings of the exile are many. And in the first assembly, a parable was given for the sacrifice: bulls, rams, and he-goats. These are the Face of the Ox and the Face of the Eagle. There are two Torahs; look because of this, and we must fly toward the Ox of strength to be bound in the smoke. The Eagle refers to the secret of Jacob. Because of this wisdom, the Kingdom is established. Scribes for Jacob, scribes for the first strength. Words are cast to be divided, to be called "Israel," as it is written:
> Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel <note>Genesis 32:29</note>
And the support of the letter *Samekh* is for the end of Israel, the root that distinguishes between them.

## The Faithful Shepherd (Ra'aya Meheimna)

**And a tenth** of a thousand for the blow. The Faithful Shepherd <note>Moses</note> said: The matter of the Constellation <note>Mazal</note> of Atonement <note>Kippurim</note> is the dough-offering <note>Challah</note>, a tenth of silver. He throws them below so as not to entangle the Canopy. I have pushed a tenth to the levels that end all elders for the burnt offering of the Atonements of the iniquity, to be forgiven. It must be given between the two arms, and he throws them when he seeks to investigate the hidden things. All is a narrow path, like the words "and my palate." And because of the distress, he did not tread upon them, but threw them in silver. Or like the sun, do not be appointed over the bread for the seven palates. Every man's grace is opened to him in the cup and the miracle. These are the distress, the storm, and the whirlwind, etc. The one appointed over the Constellation of Atonement for the other side, the buyers of the life of the world. One does not hate the transaction over them, but 123... and he repeats the words to awaken upon them all the providence in the bush alone. And because of this, from the Constellation comes a thousand, like the spirit from the other side. They awaken the ancient ones and he throws it like the sun, a chased woman to the crowns. He awakens the deed with love, or it is called the laws of taste. And one appointee is in charge of this, and the pursuit is hidden from the eyes of all living things, he who rules above for his crown to give him a woman, and he shall not go out from the tribe of evil. He was silent and bent to the strength of the world until it was needed for the creatures. And about this it is written: "A loaf of bread," and they have no other space. And there is no "loaf" except for the "Tower of Strength," the living God. All is foundation and honor from the shadow of the King. The Faithful Shepherd concludes: from all the holiness of my teacher, to the place of the narrow path below, and she has no kid—the secret of the loins of the Atonements...

...extended in order to diminish. <meta>This page continues the enumeration of the 613 commandments (mitzvot) from the perspective of the "Faithful Shepherd" (Ra'aya Meheimna). It follows the previous discussion of the first five commandments, now detailing the sixth through the tenth, focusing on spiritual attachment, blessings, and ritual purity.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> Pinhas <-

**The Sixth** commandment is to cleave to Him <note>God</note> with moderation of the heart and the will of the heart. This is the very foundation and existence of all sacred work. **The Sixth** corresponds to peace and blessing, and all the tables of the world correspond to them, modeled after the patterns Above. It is necessary to say that this commandment is to cleave to Him and not to the "other side" <note>the Sitra Achra or forces of evil</note>. Furthermore, one must bring forth words of the heart to Him without any defect or attachment to impurity. One must bring them forth with the consent of the "perfect ones" and not in a tangled or circular fashion; moreover, this is because of the danger that a penalty or accuser might precede the prayer.

**The Seventh** commandment is to say the Grace after Meals <note>Birkat HaMazon</note> to satisfaction, in order to merit and sanctify the mind and to touch the sparks of holiness. With the first waters <note>Mayim Rishonim; washing before a meal</note>, one must fill them to satisfaction so that they do not become diminished, finding their mouths and thoughts empty. The Sages said that the nations of the world are not found at the mouth of the well <note>a metaphor for spiritual sustenance</note>, for these commandments are praised. The masters of these matters explained them as great foundations, and these words were said concerning them according to the Torah: "And you shall sanctify yourselves, and you shall be holy" <note>Leviticus 11:44</note>. "And you shall sanctify yourselves"—these are the **first waters**. "And you shall be holy"—these are the **final waters** <note>Mayim Acharonim; washing after a meal</note>, for "holy" refers to the fragrant oil used after the meal. Rabbi Yose blessed this practice. And one who touches between one washing and the other <note>during the meal</note> must do so because of "And you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I am the Lord your God." Blessed is the people who fulfill these; it shall be a garment for them. Furthermore, "And you shall sanctify yourselves" refers to the time of marital intimacy. The first waters are required for every person to sanctify the mind; the first touches and the strengthening of the limbs, as it is written: "You have fashioned me behind and before" <note>Psalm 139:5</note>. This refers to the waters between the washings, about which it is said: "He poured water on my hands."

**The Eighth** commandment is to perform acts of kindness <note>Chesed</note>. With words of the tongue, one sends the beauty of holiness upward to be established. Because of this, for fewer than three people, a cup of blessing is not required. But they said that for a company of three, a cup is required, for there the "Amen" of holiness is found. Furthermore, in the Torah, we do not find fewer than ten: Priests, Levites, Israelites, the Covenant, the Torah, the Holy Throne, the Cup of Holiness, and this is Understanding <note>Binah</note>. And concerning this, it was said that there were three crowns: the fourth is Kingship <note>Malchut</note>. It is said there are four watches of the night, and some say three branches corresponding to the three watches, and some say four branches corresponding to the four watches.

**The Ninth** commandment is to circumcise the foreskin and to perform the uncovering <note>Pri'ah</note> of the child, corresponding to the fourth letter 'He' of the Name Y-H-V-D <note>The Tetragrammaton</note>.

**The Tenth** commandment is the redemption of the firstborn son <note>Pidyon HaBen</note>, who goes out to freedom. This is the sign of the fourth establishment and the fourth action of the Name Y-H-V-D. The "Tenth" refers to the ten Sephirot <note>divine emanations</note> which are the secret of the Name. How much must a person nullify his own body so as not to be burned by the coals of the words of the Crown <note>Keter</note>, so that he is not consumed like a burning coal. If one opens the door to the Torah but causes damage to the Shekhinah <note>the Divine Presence</note>, it is said of him: "This is the table that is before the Lord."

---

**Three** types of things cause harm to a person; two of them in this world and one in the world to come. These are: One who curses himself. We have learned that a specific appointee <note>an angel</note> is stationed before a person, and at the moment he curses himself, that appointee takes the word, and the sharp swords of those appointed under him all take up the matter and say "Amen." They carry it upward and record it, and it pursues him because of what he did to himself, and his sin is established by that word.

One who throws bread or crumbs of food as if they were nothing, and treats them with contempt; as it is said, these affect him in two worlds.

And one in this world who wastes his seed <note>the sin of Onanism/wasted seed</note> before the holiness of Israel has reached him. This is because he profanes the Sabbath and causes the exile of the Shekhinah, preventing her from being united with her Husband.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar, specifically the section known as Ra’aya Meheimna (The Faithful Shepherd). It focuses on the spiritual mechanics of the Priestly Blessing and the messianic redemption involving the defeat of the "husks" (Klippot) represented by Ishmael and Esau.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Sometimes: when the male is in desire toward the female, it is from three sides. Once he rises to the gate before his time has arrived, every appointee is in desire like a body. When the male rises as at first to that place and says, "This is the place of so-and-so," all the guilty of Gehenna <note>Hell/Purgatory</note> cry out to rise to that place. That appointee is disgraced and it is said: *Behold, the Lord will cast you out with a mighty captivity, and He will surely wrap you up* <note>Isaiah 22:17</note>. The guilty of Gehenna say: *Like a ball He will toss you into a wide land; there you shall die* <note>Isaiah 22:18</note>, because he caused them to be called before their time arrived. Behold, there are three who cause a pocket <note>loss/shame</note> for themselves as has been stated.

-> **The Faithful Shepherd** <-

**The Faithful Shepherd** said: "It is in desire, etc., until 'upon its pedestals.'" As printed in Leviticus, page 11, side b.
**Another interpretation:** And he praised, and thus the Faithful Shepherd praised regarding all the letters: "Thus you act to strengthen yourself over all creatures in order to prepare to reach their image." For the Lord is cleaved to him for life. For at first, we were like a horse and for the cheapness that I strengthened; and a woman with thirteen attributes of mercy, which is "One" <note>Hebrew: Echad (13)</note>. Now prepare the general rule of the palace, and it shall be for two supports. They called to the One God in mercy. And these three days shall be fulfilled in you: *He shall be exalted and extolled* <note>Isaiah 52:13</note>. And a thief... [the text here uses complex letter permutations and gematria <note>numerical values of letters</note> relating to the Priestly Blessing].

The letters emerge: *Aleph, Koph, Peh, Lamed, Samekh*... *He shall be exalted*... and your heart shall dwell... *The Lord lift up His countenance upon you and give you peace* <note>Numbers 6:26</note>. The fourth dwells at its time for the service upon the Children of Israel, *and I will bless them* <note>Numbers 6:27</note>.

From the side of the Right, she is called "Stone," and how many stones are divided? They call to be gathered from the pocket of the wise. The waters of the Torah emerge, and of their prophets it was said: Rabbi Akiva said to his students upon their entry: "When you reach the place of pure marble stones, do not say 'Water, water!'" <note>A famous Talmudic warning regarding mystical ascent</note> for you will be found as one who departs; do not say to the ears "Water."

Water from whom? Even a horse for the male... shall be before my eyes. Cursed are the waters that are not the lower Torah... And because these are like a horse <note>Hebrew: Sus</note>... they are forced for the water... they shall not be established... and from the side of Samael <note>the Accuser</note>... called "Inheritance" and "Timnah"... like a bride tied in inheritance, and she has three colors...

The hand is red like Samael. The Middle Pillar <note>The central sefirah, Tiferet</note> opens its bosom... and because the bosom of Metatron is to the right and Metatron is to the left, the inheritance is included in it... their depths are Samael and the Serpent. Samael corresponds to that which is hindered from love... hindered from inheriting her... on the right, in the right, to clear the level of **Kindness** <note>Chesed</note>. He removes the star from Ishmael and his camp. And from the side of the North, for the level of **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note>, he removes the star from Esau and his camp. On the two wings of the bosom: one from the right is the Righteous One, son of David <note>Messiah ben David</note>, and one from the left is Messiah son of Joseph.

And in the exile, the desire for water... to suffer his hands as it is written. Blessed to be filled. Take the right of Ishmael, so that his fall shall be his strength. Jacob is found with the holy on the left of Esau, and the plant of holiness with the right of the impure Ishmael, until Shiloh comes. The Faithful Shepherd is at the level of the **Beauty of Israel** <note>Tiferet Yisrael</note>. He removes the star of the "Evening Wolf" <note>referring to the nations</note> in these three levels. He shall visit the nations and the Israelites at the end of the exile.

And it is certain he removes the star and the "Evening Wolf" as a likeness to the "Evening Wolf" mixed in Esau and Ishmael. Thus Jacob is wrapped in Abraham and Isaac, a mixture of both. And thus Shiloh is mixed with Messiah ben David and Messiah ben Joseph... to the voice of Balaam... for thus the two Messiahs shall be bound to the Faithful Shepherd in three ways in the final exile.

**He opened and said:**
> He has not beheld iniquity in Jacob, neither has He seen perverseness in Israel; the Lord his God is with him, and the shout of a King is among them.
<note>Numbers 23:21</note>
And all of them to establish the voice... they break the *Klippah* <note>the "husk" or shell of evil</note>... to reveal Wisdom... from the three colors which are the "Segulah" <note>the chosen/vowel point</note> of which it was said: *And he traveled like the banners*... as the fourth to the fourth wisdom.

It emerges...
