<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the "Faithful Shepherd" (Ra'aya Meheimna) within the section of Pinchas. It focuses on the nature of Divine Names and the relationship between the Infinite (Ein Sof) and the created world through the lens of the 613 commandments.</meta>

## Pinchas

-> Pinchas <-

The essence of the matter and the awe [of God] is achieved through them <note>the commandments</note> for their Master. This includes the secret of King David, of whom it is said <margin>Psalms 145:14</margin> *The Lord upholds all who fall.* **The twelfth commandment** is to be called away from the claims of hidden times and from the danger on the side of the "tongue" <note>referring to the power of speech or judgment</note>. The judgment of the kingdom does not depart from him, for the "Living Being of Mercy" <note>a mystical angelic rank</note> ceases at the right arm. The right hand is an oath, for we have established that she <note>the Shekhinah</note> was obligated in the desert, which is the labor upon her to turn away from the side of Severity (*Gevurah*), lest the anger of the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) be stirred.

**The thirteenth commandment** is holiness for the servant who is called "wise" in all types of understanding reaching until the **Infinite** <term>Ein Sof: The Boundless or Infinite aspect of God prior to self-manifestation</term>, and "pious" in all types of kindness (*Chesed*), and "mighty" in all types of strength (*Gevurah*), and "counselor" in all types of humility, and "generous" in all types of charity, and "king" over all waters from the Kingdom (*Malkhut*) until the Infinite, until the Crown (*Keter*). In all these levels, the Crown is called "Merciful" and Kindness is called "Judge." Thus they have established it in many levels until the Infinite. The Lord is all around; what is the difference between "Merciful" and "Judge"? "God" (*El*) was the name called before the world was created. He is in all these levels according to the names of the creatures that were destined to be created. For if there were no creatures in the world, why would He be called by the name of "Judge"? Rather, it is on account of the creatures of the worlds, etc. All names are like garments for Him, based on His actions. In this same manner, He created the soul in attachment to Him, which is named according to its actions in every single limb of the body. The body is called a "world" and a "form." The intention of the Master of the World is to be seen within all creatures, and in everything that is not perceived... for every reward that is performed through a commandment is called by the "musical accent" <note>Ta'am: literally 'taste' or 'musical trope'</note> that rises and ascends here in His mercy. And that reward for one who commits a transgression is called by the accent that "bites" <note>referring to the 'Negina' or musical notes that dictate the flow of the text</note>. There is a reason for everything in the body... Just as the Master of the World, before any of His creatures were made, was called "Merciful" and "Healer of the Sick." However, all His names are hidden, and no "mouth" <note>expression</note> was called by them until the creatures of the world existed. Because all the masters of the generation are guilty... a person is judged according to his own measure... even a known name is like the pattern of a Sefirah <note>Divine attribute</note>, for every Sefirah has a known name, a limit, and a boundary.

And because the Masters made it for Him, it is for the soul to walk in them, to be called by them, and to be hidden in them. Everything in the soul is relative to the back of the body. But regarding the Master of all Worlds, He has no known name or known place in any side of His wisdom. Likewise, the soul has no known name or known place in the whole body, even in every place of its dominion, and no place is empty of it. For this reason, the soul has no single place; if it did not spread its dominion through the rest of the limbs, it would not be called by a single name... Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), Understanding (*Binah*), and the beginning of Knowledge (*Da'at*), and no more. For if it were more than this, the name would be lacking. So it is with the Master of the World, who has no known place, nor can He be called by names or be used... because of the level of the "Chariot" (*Merkavah*) below. In it, they "triple" the "Holy" <note>referring to the 'Kadosh, Kadosh, Kadosh' prayer</note>, for all the levels of the worlds are hidden in them. They are tripled... the Kingdom (*Malkhut*), they are the Chariot, which are the likeness of the Lion, the Ox, and the Eagle—the living beings of the Chariot for God to rest upon. And the likeness of their faces is the face of a Man. From the side of the stars, they rule over... to establish a Chariot for them.

And because of this, it is possible to say "They triple 'Holy' unto You." And so it is with the letters that are the secret of the likeness that rules in this manner: **Yod-He-Vav-He** <term>The Tetragrammaton: The four-letter essential Name of God</term>. The "Holy" is tripled to grasp the worlds, to complete the name of the Lord in them. For the Master of all has no dominion over Him through musical accents or through vowels, but He is called by every accent and has no known name. Every name that shines upon Him is to judge all the worlds... there is a man who inherits three brains... according to his level which is called "Yesh" <note>Substance/Existence</note> but not the "Supernal Wisdom." And there is a man who inherits only one world according to his level, as they have established: "Every righteous person has a world for himself." Thus every man of Israel inherits worlds according to his level. But the Master of the World has no worlds according to time, but rather He is the Lord of all worlds. The three "Holies" shine upon Him... He was before all beings, and He is within all beings... He was, He is, and He will be. The name of the Lord shines upon the Master of all, for no name has power over Him...

<summary>This page discusses the 12th and 13th commandments, focusing on the mystical nature of Divine Names and how God (the Infinite) relates to the world through the Sefirot and the human soul. ...strength, and the letters <term>Mantzapakh</term><note>The five Hebrew letters that have a different form at the end of a word: Mem, Nun, Tzadi, Pe, Khaf. The voice ascends upon it, for when it was said above: "Let it stand in its rectifications and not spread further." And the end of the mothers and the spirit is Leah, and the end of all secrets is the secret of the testimony. And what do they testify about Him? That when He was alone before creating the world, why did He need to be called by these names, or by descriptions such as "Merciful and Gracious, Long-suffering," etc. <note>Exodus 34:6</note>, "Judge," "Faithful," "Mighty," and the like? In every rectification, they were made to be called by the name of all worlds and creatures, so that they would come to know His sovereignty over them. And so it is here, at this time, the sovereignty of all limbs of the body is to receive it upon themselves. It is not to make Him known as a body that He created, for there is no void above Him that could contain Him. Furthermore, at times there are many changes and occurrences <note>referring to human perceptions of the Divine</note>, and they are called by what is not truly so for the Master of All, because he is likened to Him in his sovereignty over all the members of the body, but not in a complete sense.

Furthermore, **Hear O Israel** <note>The Shema prayer</note>: the large letter *Ayin* [of *Shema*] and the *Dalet* of *Echad* [One] <note>Together these form the word 'Ed' (Witness)</note>. This is the connection between the name from *Shema* and the *Et* from *Echad* regarding the Lord our God, and regarding all that is appointed to unite them in the world. Therefore David said: "Prepare me in the Lord," the name from *Shema* and the *Et* from *Echad* which equals 365. Furthermore, the large *Dalet* refers to the four houses <note>compartments</note> of the **Head Tefillin**, which belong to Her <note>the Shekhinah</note>, and He is crowned with them and places "beauty" [Pe'er] upon His head. All these are not for the heavens themselves, but for the **righteous and the merit-worthy**, whose "crowns are on their heads."

And the Daughter is the commandment of the **Hand Tefillin**, in the name of the letter *Yod*, the knot that draws down the letter *He*. The world is like the Head Tefillin upon the head of **Beauty** [*Tiferet*]. The Head Tefillin are like the full Name <term>YHVH</term><note>The Tetragrammaton</note>, and your sign is "To the Lord, Hear," and the end is "There is One." These belong to the Head, which is **Crown** [*Keter*]—"There is none holy as the Lord, for there is none beside Thee."

The four [sections] are with the four companions of the four houses. And for the knot of the Tefillin at the back, it is a double *Dalet*, the *Yod* is its knot. <meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Pinchas, specifically analyzing the sacrificial offerings for the festivals of Passover, Rosh Hashanah, and Sukkot. It explores the linguistic nuances of the biblical text to explain how these offerings interact with the divine attributes of Mercy (Chesed) and Judgment (Din).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Pinchas**<-

<note>The opening lines contain fragmented Aramaic phrases regarding the "bending" or "subjugation" of forces and the "infinite" (Ein Sof) nature of the Crown (Keter).</note>

**"And you shall offer** a burnt offering to the Lord..." <note>Numbers 28:19</note> Come and see: regarding the Passover sacrifice, it is written, "And you shall offer a *fire-offering* <term>Isheh: a sacrifice consumed by fire, often associated with the 'feeding' of spiritual forces</term>, a burnt offering to the Lord." But here <note>referring to a specific transition in the text</note> it does not say "fire-offering." On the day of Passover—a day of Kindness <term>Chesed: the divine attribute of expansive love</term>—nothing is lacking. Rather, it is written: "And you shall offer a burnt offering." Why? Because this day is a day of the "Ascending Offering" <note>original: Olah, which means both 'burnt offering' and 'ascent'</note>. Just as a bride enters the canopy, she emerges from all sides of the house and is crowned on that day. And this spirit, the King of all, tastes the ascent. It does not say "fire-offering" because He does not draw near to the "poor place" <note>a reference to the lower, harsher spiritual realms</note>; rather, He is distanced from there. Therefore, "fire-offering" is not written, as it is not needed here. Israel is distanced from the "Evil Side" <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of impurity</term>, and from here they are purified through days and weeks until they are included and enter into the days of purity. Rabbi Abba said: These are necessary for this "opening," to open the secret of the raising of hands to the One who remembers the world. We find in the ancient books that "fire-offering" sometimes appears without a partner <note>referring to the union of divine attributes</note>, to bring it to this side or that side. They clung to the path of the "Knowledge of Good and Evil"—to cling to the Evil or to cling to the Good. On other days, it is included in the "fire-offering," and thus it is written of them: "a fire-offering, a burnt offering." But on this day, where there is no "Other Side" standing to accuse, there is no need for the "fire-offering" to appease it. This day is a day that moves within the "Life of Lives" and not within the "Knowledge of Good and Evil." Therefore: "And you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord," and not "a fire-offering to the Lord." It is an ascent, an ascent to the highest level.

**"And in the seventh** month..." <note>Numbers 28:1</note> Just as below, this is the Day of Judgment <note>Rosh Hashanah</note>, the judgment of the whole world. A strong spirit and a weak judgment. It should have said "And you shall offer a burnt offering" as it does for all other days. However, on this day, it is written: "And you shall make for me savory foods" <note>referring to Genesis 27:4, where Isaac asks Esau for food; here applied mystically to the "tastes" of the sacrifice</note>. How many "savory foods" and cooked dishes did Israel prepare on this day! For the Accuser <note>Satan/The Prosecuting Angel</note> is empowered to chatter about the sins of the world. Therefore, it is written "And you shall prepare" <note>Ve-asitem</note> rather than "And you shall offer" <note>Ve-hikravtem</note>, and it says "a burnt offering" but not "a fire-offering." On all these days of the sacrifices, "fire-offering" is not written because the "Other Side" has no portion in them. On the days when you prepare "savory foods" and dishes without the knowledge of the "Other Side," the day reminds the Creator of the binding of Isaac <term>Akedah: the merit of Isaac's sacrifice is invoked on Rosh Hashanah</term> to bring the world to weeping and repentance. And while those forces of the "Other Side" spread out, you perform all your services and prayers. The days of Sukkot are difficult for the Accuser because Mercy is awakened. We have established the meaning of "And he brought him wine and he drank" <note>Genesis 27:25</note>—this removes the judgment from the place of the "Ancient and Hidden One" <term>Atika Kadisha: the most hidden, merciful aspect of the Divine</term>. These "tastes" and blessings pass over his sins. What is written? "And it came to pass, as soon as Jacob had gone out..." <note>Genesis 27:30</note>. Taste the Wisdom! We have already established this matter. Therefore, on the Days of Judgment, the sacrifice is called an "ascent" <note>Olah</note> so that Kindness <note>Chesed</note> may exist through the power of Isaac. And the "goat for a sin offering" is intended to subdue the Accuser in his own home. On this day, when he sees that his will is not being done, he is pushed aside, as is the case on Yom Kippur.

**"And on the fifteenth** day..." <note>Numbers 29:12</note> Rabbi Abba opened: "And the ark rested in the seventh month..." <note>Genesis 8:4</note> Come and see: on all these days, the "Doe of the Dawn" <note>a metaphor for the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> is covered so that the "Other Side" shall not rule over her. Because the Sukkah protects them, they are shielded in the "Shadow of the Ancient Sea" <note>the Supernal Mother/Binah</note>. And the Ark rested—He commanded Israel to make a feast for the camps of the surrounding nations <note>the 70 bulls of Sukkot offered for the 70 nations</note>, while the third portion is arranged for the joy of Israel, to find forgiveness and to stand before the mountains of Ararat <note>interpreted here as the "mountains of curse" or "mountains of rebellion" that are overcome</note>.

<summary>This page provides a Kabbalistic interpretation of the festival sacrifices, explaining that the omission of the word "fire-offering" (Isheh) signifies the exclusion of the "Other Side" from the divine union. It specifically links the rituals of Rosh Hashanah and Sukkot to the subduing of judgment through the merit of the Patriarchs and the protective "shadow" of the Sukkah.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the mystical secrets of the holiday of Sukkot, specifically focusing on the sacrificial offerings of bulls and the water libation ceremony. It connects the decreasing number of sacrifices to the diminishing power of the seventy nations compared to the eternal nature of Israel.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Rabbi Elazar said: On the first day of the festival <note>Sukkot</note>, the "other side" <note>the forces of impurity or the seventy nations</note> does not rule over them, nor on the second day. But from the third day onward, for the wise, the count begins to diminish for them above and increases below. The sacrifices diminish, as it is written regarding the bulls: "thirteen... twelve..." and so on. This visible reduction occurs because the first and second days are so holy that they distribute holiness to all, but from the third day onward, when the "other side" begins to seek its portion, what is written? *And on the third day, eleven bulls* <note>Numbers 29:20</note>. With each passing day, the number drops, and as they decrease, so too does their bounty <note>the spiritual energy allotted to the seventy nations</note> diminish.

Rabbi Elazar said: Come and see, from the second holy day to the third day, once the water libation <note>the ceremony of pouring water on the Altar</note> is sent forth from the third day, a spirit of bitterness <note>judgment</note> rests upon them. Those waters were not known in their totality <note>page 263</note>. To what does this allude? That the goodness of Israel is not found in a place of lack, but in a place of abundance. And because these waters alluded to here are diminished, the Scripture comes to inform us of what is written: *And water*—these are the waters that flow on the days of the festival. They are alluded to within the sacrifices, which are like "mountains of curses" <note>referring to the spiritual source of the nations</note> that were *continually diminishing* <note>Genesis 8:5</note>. Their goodness decreases so as to gather against them a state of constant lack. Because their waters were not unified below, their goodness does not join together except in small, scattered amounts. But for Israel, who are from the Holy One, Blessed be He, what is written?
> *But those who seek the Lord shall not lack any good thing.* (Psalms 34:11)

The beginning of that verse says:
> *The young lions do lack and suffer hunger.* (Psalms 34:11)

These "young lions" are the appointed ministers of the rest of the nations. But "those who seek the Lord"—these are Israel, who "shall not lack any good thing." These nations are eventually severed and have no root above, and therefore their goodness, which is symbolized by water, was *continually diminishing until the tenth month* <note>Genesis 8:5</note>. This refers to the "Sabbath," for then the days of evil were present, and that evil was awakened and strengthened. The Holy One does not testify from within impurity. At that time, all the mercies of the Holy One are hidden. These are the "Eastern Mountains," the mountains of curses below, which strengthen and do evil in the world during these days.

Five-fold burnt offerings are brought, for then all are gathered. Seven bulls—these correspond to the seventy appointed ministers who are set over the seventy nations. They rise up on the first day, and on each subsequent day they are like "goring bulls" in their time. However, they are handed over to the "Rider" <note>a metaphor for Divine control</note>, and the signs of 4 and 7 <note>mystical numerology</note> rule over them, two on each day. The elders said: Who brings them in? And if you say: "Are they then of an 'evil eye' toward the prophets?" See that it is written: *For she has dealt bountifully with them.* Eat and be satisfied! But our joy is not like their joy; holiness comes through all the days. And because we are kind to them, and through the holiness of knowledge, the streams turn upon their banks like glowing coals. Our joy makes them... <unclear>illegible</unclear>... and thus they rise like their altar. Who can offer sacrifices for them? They do not want this joy, but there is a joy for all those ministers. For all those bulls, they praise and say: "This is the hour of Israel, and such are their feasts!"

Despite all this, everything is offered only to the Holy One, Blessed be He, through His study. They bring them near, and He divides them. Regarding this it is written: *The heart of the wicked is of little worth* <note>Proverbs 10:20</note>, for these are the sacrifices of the festival. And although they are given water to drink—alluded to here on the second, third, and seventh days of the festival—the sign is "Vav, Vav, Lamed" <note>a scribal/mystical code for the variations in the Torah text regarding the libations</note>. Water alludes to:
> *Many waters cannot quench love.* (Song of Songs 8:7)

These are the waters that come from the power of the spread of the festival, through the greatness of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: *And your garment is like water.* In joy, nothing is found except those mountains of balsam, where all are purified and sanctified as in the beginning. For:
> *If a man would give all the substance of his house for love, he would be utterly contemned.* (Song of Songs 8:7)

In joy, this is the one who forgives with a flame.

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Torah portion "Va'etchanan" (Deuteronomy 3:23). ## The Book of "These are the Words" (Deuteronomy)
## Portion of Va'etchanan (And I Besought)

**"And I besought** the Lord at that time, saying..." <note>Deuteronomy 3:23</note> Rabbi Hezekiah said: "One beloved" <note>original: "chad yedid"</note> below in the exile, to the path, "Give Your servant..." and so on. <note>A reference to Psalms 86:16: "Give Your strength to Your servant."</note> Rabbi Yose opened his discourse with the verse: "Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord." <note>Isaiah 38:2</note> Come and see how powerful is the strength of prayer, and how it is superior to everything. For anyone who exerts himself in his prayer does not fear those above or those below, nor does he fear the evil occurrences of the world. This is because prayer is like the power of life; it is as if it has the power of everything every day. For prayer goes up before the Holy One, Blessed be He, like a sharp sword <note>A common Zoharic metaphor for prayer's ability to cut through spiritual barriers</note>. It cuts through and tears away the harsh decrees, for even if death was decreed upon a person, it is all canceled and removed from him. The "shadow" of a person of this world does not rest upon him <note>referring to the protection of the Divine shadow</note> to be saved by day and night, and the verse "you shall meditate on it day and night" shall not depart from him. And if he departs from this study, he is separated from Life itself.

Come and see: when a man goes up to his bed at night, he must take upon himself the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven with a perfect heart, and intend to entrust his soul to Him as a deposit <term>Deposit: The Kabbalistic idea that the soul leaves the body during sleep and is "deposited" with God for safekeeping</term>. And the masters have established this because the whole world tastes the taste of death <note>Sleep is considered 1/60th of death in Jewish tradition</note>, for the Tree of Death dwells in the world. All the spirits of human beings go out and ascend and are guarded by Him, and because they are like a deposit, they all return to their places.

Come and see: when the North Wind awakens at midnight <note>original: "palgut leilya"</note>, a herald goes forth and the Holy One, Blessed be He, awakens in the Garden of Eden to delight with the spirits of the righteous. Then all the "Sons of the Matron" <note>original: "Matronit," referring to the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> and all the "Sons of the Palace" gather to praise the Holy King. At that time, all those deposits of spirits that were guarded in His hand all return to their masters, and the spirits of the people of the world awaken at the end of that hour. And behold, their deposits are all with them. Those who have subdued everything stand and awaken and are added to the living until the day begins, and they join with the Assembly of Israel. Then, when the "Male" <note>The masculine aspect of the Divine</note> comes, he and all the Sons of the King's Palace all come before the Holy King. They are called the "Sons of the King's Palace" because of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the Torah. When one comes, he should prepare himself entirely to provide sustenance and to exert himself with the Holy King. For just as at night he exerted himself with the Matron <note>The Shekhinah</note>, now he comes with the Matron to unite her with the King.

He comes to the synagogue, purifies himself with the offerings, and waits for the additions of King David <note>The "Pesukei D'Zimrah" or Verses of Praise in the morning liturgy</note>, saying praises and blessings. He merits to say "A Psalm of David" at the beginning and end, which the masters established as the "vessels of exile" before their Master. In the exile, one must stand in the likeness of the Supernal King to be joined in righteousness. These are called "those who stand," as it is written: "And I will give you a place to walk among these who stand." <note>Zechariah 3:7</note> He directs his will before his Master and requests his needs.

Come and see: at the hour when a man stands in the night prayer, distressing himself to exert himself in the Torah, a herald calls out concerning him and says: "Behold, bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord, who stand in the house of the Lord by night." <note>Psalms 134:1</note> Now, when he stands in prayer before his Master, that herald calls out over him and says: "And I will give you a place to walk among these who stand." After he finishes his prayer with favor (and praise on high) before his Master, it has been established that he must hand over his soul as a deposit with the will of the heart, to reach the place that is necessary. And how many paths are there for a man, all of them in awe...

<meta>This page begins the commentary on the Torah portion Va’etchanan (Deuteronomy 3:23). It establishes the mystical framework for prayer, focusing on Moses’ supplication as the archetype for how a human being should approach the Divine. It connects the act of prayer to the construction of a celestial crown for the King.</meta>

# And I Besought

At the time when prayer stands <note>original: "sh'ata d'tzalota," the designated time for prayer</note> (from the beginning of the day), all those words that a person brings forth from their mouth all ascend upward and pierce the firmaments until they reach the place they reach, and they are crowned upon the head of the King, and He makes from them a **crown**. And come and see: the prayer that a person needs to offer with intention <term>Kavanah: focused spiritual direction</term> must be a prayer of "supplications" <note>Hebrew: Tachanunim</note> above all else, as it is written: *And I besought the Lord* <note>Deut. 3:23</note>—this shall be an excellent prayer.

Come and see: before prayer, one must direct their feet and their wisdom, and one must lower their head like one sitting before the King. One must direct their eyes so as not to gaze at the **Shekhinah** <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</term>. In the book of Rav Hamnuna the Elder, he said: anyone who opens his eyes during the time of prayer, or does not lower his eyes toward the earth, the Angel of Death precedes him, and when his soul departs, he will not behold the light of the Shekhinah, nor will he die with the "Kiss" <note>A mystical death reserved for the righteous, where the soul is drawn out gently by God</note>. One who treats the Shekhinah with disrespect is himself disrespected; in that hour, he is not worthy of Grace, for it is written: *For those who honor Me I will honor, and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed* <note>1 Samuel 2:30</note>.

Come and see: one who prays should pray as one standing between life and death. And how can he look upon the Shekhinah? Rather, he should know that certainly the Shekhinah stands before him, as it is written: *I have set the Lord always before me* <note>Psalm 16:8</note>. We testify that the Shekhinah is present; therefore, there should be no "insolence" <note>meaning a physical or spiritual barrier</note> between me and the wall. And the sages established: one who offers praise in his prayer must first fear before his Master, and afterward request his needs. For behold, Moses spoke thus: first, *You have begun [to show Your servant...]* and finally, *Let me cross over, I pray You...* Rabbi Yehuda said: how great is it here, for it is written that he first purified himself with the Name of the Lord, and finally [attained] the beloved state... <unclear>Possible variation in divine names</unclear>... This is the way from below to above, to include the attribute of Day in the Night, and the attribute of Night in the Day, and to illuminate everything as one, as is fitting.

->**You**<- have begun to show Your servant. What is the "beginning of all"? Certainly, Moses was the beginning in the world to be perfected in all. And if you say Jacob was perfect and saw all, he ascended below in the likeness of above; however, that which belonged to Moses did not belong to any other man, for he was crowned with a greater engraving... <note>The text here becomes highly cryptic, referencing Metatron and various angelic appointments</note>... they were appointed over them, who are like the body of Samael <note>The Accuser/Satan</note>. They are sometimes lacking... and their intentions went astray. Because of this, do not lower your fence... *And Your mighty hand*—this was sent forth, not like a vision. And come and see: Tamar. Because of this, Moses was the beginning in the world. And if you say, who was the sustenance? For Moses was the beginning and the sustenance of the King Messiah, for then perfection will be found in the world. That which was not so for generations upon generations; in that time, perfection will be found above and below, and all worlds will be in a single union. Then it is written: *In that day the Lord shall be one and His name one* <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>.

->**And the Lord said**<- to me: "It is enough for you; speak no more [to Me of this matter]." Rabbi Hiyya said: ... "It is enough for you" refers to the joy of the Shekhinah above all, and "speak no more" [regarding the war]. Rabbi Isaac said: "It is enough for you" refers to the journey to the end... for the time of the Moon <note>symbolizing the leadership of Joshua or the Shekhinah</note> has arrived, and the Moon cannot be hidden until the gathering... *But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him*...

->**But you**<- who did cleave unto the Lord your God [are alive every one of you this day]. Rabbi Yose said: ... <note>Deut. 4:4</note> ... My people who cleave... a crown... above all the nations of idolatry. He raised them to His lot and blessed them with His blessing... *The Lord bless you*—the Lord Himself. Come and see: the rest of the nations of the world, the Holy One, blessed be He, gave them to appointed ministers who rule over them; but Israel alone, the Holy One, blessed be He, took for His own portion to honor and sanctify them... and He gave them the Holy Torah in order to be purified before Him.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**261**<- ->**Va’etchanan**<-

**And the Lord spoke** to you out of the midst of the fire; you heard the sound of words, etc. <note>Deuteronomy 4:12</note> Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse and said: *As the deer longs for the water brooks...* <note>Psalms 42:2</note> The "sound of words" is the Voice that is called "Speech," for every spoken word depends upon it. Regarding this, it is written: *And God spoke all these words, saying...* <note>Exodus 20:1</note> This is the Voice called "the sound of words which you heard," and "you saw no form, only a voice." This is because hearing depends upon speech, and therefore "you heard." The colleagues established this as a sensory experience. Because the "faces" of both are called "Hearing" and "the Voice of Speech" and "the Voice of Hearing." "The sound of words you heard, but you saw no form." What is meant by "form"? As we have said: *And he beholds the form of the Lord.* <note>Numbers 12:8</note> Another explanation: "Form" refers to the Inner Voice <note>The hidden, spiritual source of sound</note> which was not visible at all. We have learned: "Voice" is the Inner Voice that is eternal. Why is "Form" called "Ancient"? Because the entire structure of the "Body" <note>The Sefirot or divine emanations</note> emerges from it. And if you ask why it is called so, it is because that "Seal" <note>The imprint of divinity</note> of the lower structure emerges from it. For this reason, there is the Upper *He* and the Lower *He* <note>The letters of the Divine Name YHWH</note>. The Upper *He* is the "Great Voice that did not cease," which commands the structures, and all those voices were found there when the Torah was given to Israel. They all emerge from that Inner Voice upon which everything depends.

Regarding that which is called the "Repetition of the Torah" <note>The Book of Deuteronomy</note>, what did the ancestors say? They already established this matter: why is it so? Rather, "Higher Wisdom" is what the whole Torah is called, and it all emerges from that Inner Voice which is related to the *Keter* <term>Crown: the highest of the divine emanations</term>. It is unified in the *Keter* which is called the "Tree of Life," and everything depends on it, specifically the Written Torah. In general, it is called "Torah," and the "Repetition of the Torah" is like the first, but from the side of *Gevurah* <term>Strength/Judgment</term> where it paused, and they are all found as one. Therefore, everything is within it, all the mysteries: *You shall not murder, you shall not steal, you shall not bear false witness, you shall not covet, you shall not desire.* These have been explained. Rabbi Yose said: Why is "You shall not desire" written when it already says "You shall not covet"? Surely that would be enough? He said to him: All of them are a single matter, a heavy burden for the feet. There are three levels called by this name. From the level where one contemplates the strength to increase his own, because of that "coveting" he takes the strength to perform the action. It depends on them in this way, for even if he does not take the object... <note>The text here discusses the psychological stages of desire versus the physical act of taking</note> as the colleagues established. Rabbi Yose said to him: Why is "You shall not murder" not written with a connecting "and" <note>The Hebrew letter Vav</note> like the others? It is because the level of "Remember" <note>The Sabbath</note> depends on *Gevurah* and not on the *Keter* of the firmament... <note>A technical discussion on the Hebrew grammar of the Commandments</note>. He said: A sharp fire! No one can stand before them. Who can stand before Him and be meritorious in the world? Happy is the portion of the righteous! Happy is my portion in this world and the world to come, for I have merited this! Regarding this, it is written: *The righteous shall rejoice and prostrate themselves.* Rabbi Eleazar opened and said:

**Draw near** you, and hear all that the Lord our God shall say; and you speak to us all that the Lord our God shall speak to us, and we will hear it and do it. <note>Deuteronomy 5:24</note> Come and see: at the time the Torah was given to Israel, all the voices were present. The Holy One sat upon His throne... out of this, they opened and spoke... and this is the "Spirit" <note>Ruach/Breath</note> of which it is written: *By the breath of His mouth all their host.* <note>Psalms 33:6</note> The word of the Lord made the heavens; it went out and spoke from the midst of the fire and the flame... the voice of fire, spirit, and water from the midst of the Shofar, which includes everything. The Israelites moved away from this level and said [to Moses], "And you speak to us"—not like the Higher Rebuke from above, but from the place of the "Female" <note>The Sefirah of Malchut/Kingship, which is more accessible to humans</note> and no more. "And you speak to us," etc. Moses said: My own self shall be judged by my words... for the people of Israel did not move away, nor did they reveal...

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the commentary on the Torah portion Va'etchanan. It follows the conclusion of the previous portion, continuing the Zohar's mystical exploration of the soul's elevation and the transition from primordial light to physical existence.</meta>

## Va’etchanan
->**(And I Besought)**<-

In the beginning, the world was unable to endure that word. Later, and at various times, generations stood before it, but at the start, they died. <note>This refers to the "Kings of Edom" or primordial worlds that collapsed because they lacked balance.</note> This was necessary because the Tree of Death caused it. Afterward, they lived and were protected, seeking to enter the Tree of Life which stands over that Tree of Death, so that they might exist forever. Once they were established in this manner, the power of death over them was weakened, and the "Other Side" <note>The Sitra Achra, or forces of spiritual impurity</note> was weakened. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "It is my desire to establish you in a high place and to have you cleave to life," for they had sought the place of the "Fresh Female." <note>A reference to the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence, in her receptive state.</note>

"Go say to them..." etc. With the letter *Lamed*, He established His stars and placed them within it. Despite all this, since Israel only acted as was fitting for the world they were in, it was only said of them that they should live... <note>The text here alludes to the temporary nature of life in the physical realm compared to the eternal life intended for them.</note> Whoever performs a deed and his heart and will are not directed toward this side—even if he fulfills the statutes—punishment rests upon him. He is not like another man, for the Holy One, blessed be He, does not judge him for evil.

**"But as for thee,** stand thou here by Me." <note>Deuteronomy 5:28</note> He [Moses] ascended and separated himself entirely from everything beneath him; he cleaved and ascended to the place symbolized by the Male, and not like the Female. <note>In Kabbalistic thought, Moses reached the level of Tiferet (the Male principle), transcending the physical and even the standard prophetic level of Malchut (the Female principle).</note>

Happy is the portion of Moses, the faithful shepherd, who merited higher rungs that no other human ever merited. Regarding this it is written: *He who is good before God shall escape from her.* <note>Ecclesiastes 7:26</note> What is "good"? It is as it is written: *that he was a goodly child.* <note>Exodus 2:2, referring to Moses' birth.</note> Because he was "good," he ascended to another, higher rung. And regarding this it is written: *for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.* <note>Exodus 3:5</note> "Whereon thou standest" is precise, because he is "good," and "good" refers to the Male. It is said of Judah and David that they were "of good appearance." Why was it not more than "good appearance"? Because "good appearance" means they were fit to be looked upon. So too, David was "goodly to look at," meaning he was pleasant for those who saw him. And it is written: *better is a neighbor that is near.* <note>Proverbs 27:10</note> Everything is "good appearance." Yet, in both of them, there was a fear of this. The staff of the Crown <note>Keter</note> which is at the end of "good" ascends to become the breath of life.

Rabbi Judah said: In all his deeds, a man must be mindful of the Holy One, blessed be He. We have established this word: Rabbi Judah followed his own reasoning, for he said that Judah... who walks on the way. Since three words ascend from here and above, the exile is greater than all. When two or three words of Torah are spoken, one need not fear, for the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence</note> is below. As it happened when Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Hiyya were walking on the way, Rabbi Eleazar said: It is written:
> And the Lord God made for Adam and for his wife garments of skin, and clothed them.
<note>Genesis 3:21; original: "Ketonot Or" (עור - skin)</note>

Were they simply made of skin from a living animal? Rather, they were garments of honor. Rabbi Hiyya said to him: If so, they were not "repaired" [rectified]. If you say these were their garments, it was only after they sinned that it is written: *And the Lord God made for Adam and for his wife garments of skin.* He said to him: It is certainly so. At first, they were in the upper gardens, stripped of the lower body, and there was a secret of the upper world upon them. But after they sinned, they lacked the treasures of eternal life, and their upper bodies were darkened. What is written? *And the Lord God made for Adam and for his wife garments of skin and clothed them,* and we see they were for the life of the worlds. It is written elsewhere regarding the priestly garments: *and you shall bring them near and clothe them in tunics.* There, it is like the pattern above; here, it is like the pattern below. There, the tunics were of fine linen; here, they were garments of skin. <note>The Zohar is contrasting the "Garments of Light" (Ohr with an Aleph) Adam had before the fall with the "Garments of Skin" (Ohr with an Ayin) he received after. The priestly garments represent a return to that higher state.</note> And even though they were such, the light of their lives surpassed everything. Their eyes were opened to the light of the world, which was not the case before when they were in the garden and their eyes were opened to be sent out. It is written: *And I will lead the blind in a way that they knew not.* <note>Isaiah 42:16</note> The Holy One, blessed be He, intends to open the eyes of those who are not wise, so they may gaze upon Wisdom.

In the Higher Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>, they are attached in a way that they were not attached in this world, so that they might be known to the sharp-witted. Blessed are those who merit that wisdom, for they possess wisdom within that wisdom, and they have knowledge within that knowledge, and attachment within that attachment. Until they were, and were not, they were alone, and He was with them to enlighten them. <term>Rabbi Elazar</term> looked at them and two beasts fell and were killed. The Higher Brain is the second compartment: **And it shall be when the Lord your God brings you**. Judah said: The brain of the Will, from which fifty gates emerge. And we have learned in the <term>Book of Rav Hamnuna the Elder</term>, who said: Many gates above and below were broken by <term>The Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, which had been closed and tied with chains, in order to bring Israel out. For behold, the gates of that brain open and all these gates are tied together. And if those gates of this brain had not been broken and opened, those others would not have opened to perform judgment and to bring Israel out from their servitude. And all is written in this: the Higher Spirit strikes to awaken the power for the Lower Awe. And what is it that is written: *Thus says the Lord*—do not read "to say" <note>le-emor</note> but "to the Mother" <note>la-ima</note>, for the Holy One was not found by the Assembly of Israel until He called her from there. And what emerges from that Higher One at the end of the second compartment is called the letter *He* of the Holy Name, which opens into fifty gates and guards the spirit for the one female of the wall's partition. And we have learned that all who emerge through it act like this brain below for those fifty years of the Jubilee. Deuteronomy 26:18</note> **the service, etc.** And because of this, the letter *He* is in the day of the spirit, to bring out the spirit to light. Come and see: from the side of Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note> emerges Kindness <note>Chesed</note>, and from the side of Understanding <note>Binah</note> emerges Strength <note>Gevurah</note>, and all is for the sake of the Holy One, Blessed be He, who is crowned with them for life.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Va'etchanan**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, meaning "And I pleaded."</note>

**The third** section is "Hear, O Israel" <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note> and the order of praise "And you shall love the Lord your God." This third section is a mystery encompassing all, for Israel to be crowned with the crown of the King. The masters who stand in the synagogues and study halls are crowned with the holy crown, and the masters of the mystery have taught: "And you shall love" is because of the love of the Holy One, Blessed be He; for a king performs more goodness and **Chesed** <term>Loving-kindness/Grace</term> with everyone. The most precious Grace of all is called the "Grace of Abraham," for everyone desires to rise toward it because of the King's love, for He loved him exceedingly. In the King's love, Grace is suspended, until he is called "Abraham my friend" <note>Isaiah 41:8</note>. And because he pressed Grace further into the world, therefore "And you shall love" corresponds to the third love, which is Grace, and this is the third group.

**The fourth** section is "And it shall come to pass, if you continually obey" <note>Deuteronomy 11:13</note>. This verse resides in powerful **Gevurah** <term>Might/Severity</term> and harsh judgment. It emerges from the side of the Supernal Spirit. Even though there is spirit from this side, it bends judgment, for the Supernal Might bends. And if you say, "And it shall come to pass if you obey" implies there is judgment within it—there is no crown among the King's crowns that does not include both good and evil, certainly so with Might, which includes both good and evil. These four sections are written for Him <note>God</note> and for us to be crowned with them, and these are the Tefillin of the Master, the Holy One, Blessed be He. We have learned: these ascend to be crowned with His crowns, the joy of His "Father" and "Mother" <note>Mystical archetypes of Wisdom and Understanding</note>. He is crowned with them all, becoming one and unified. The hearing of all above and below is to show the Wisdom that stands on all sides.

Come and see what is written: "Only in your forefathers did the Lord delight" <note>Deuteronomy 10:15</note>. Rabbi Shimon said: The Forefathers are the "Holy Supernal Chariot" <term>Merkavah; the divine vehicle of manifestation</term>. And it is written, "The Lord delighted in them." Come and see: just as there is a holy chariot below, so there is a holy chariot above. And who are they? As we have said, the holy chariot is all of them together, called to be bound one to another to become one. "Only in your forefathers"—that is three; and the Chariot is four. From here it is written, "And He chose their seed after them." What does this mean? To include **King David**, who is the fourth, to be bound to the holy chariot of the preparation of powerful Wisdom and the perfection of all. The "Body" <note>The central sefirah, Tiferet</note> looks to them and is established. And in all his preparations below, King David includes them all; he was established and breathed into, and his ladder is in her.

Rabbi Isaac said: Just as the Forefathers merited to be crowned in the holy chariot, so did David merit to be established in the fourth wisdom of the chariot. Rabbi Yehuda said: It is written of David that he was "of beautiful eyes and goodly appearance" <note>1 Samuel 16:12</note>. Why was he called "ruddy"? Because the side he was drawn from caused it <note>The side of Gevurah/Judgment</note>. "Ruddy" implies blood, yet "beautiful eyes" implies mercy, as it is written, "The sure mercies of David" <note>Isaiah 55:3</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: The mercies of David are established, but he was ruddy as we said. "With beautiful eyes" refers to the grace of Wisdom. Come and see: Jerusalem and Zion are judgment and mercy, and even so it is written, "The city of David, which is Zion." And it is written, "The Holy One is in your midst, and I will not come into the city" <note>Hosea 11:9</note>—the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: I will not enter the Jerusalem above until the Kingdom of the House of David is arranged below. Rabbi Isaac said:

It resembles four knots below, hinting at the four. The three we mentioned, and the fourth to make the holy chariot as one. This is the entirety of the supernal arrangement. They are greatly distinguished and established below in their paths, like the branches that hang from the hair of the arm, and from them all those "Graces" are established until they are bound in their places. We have learned that these are the Tefillin of the Master, the Holy One, Blessed be He. Therefore, a man must glorify himself with them, for of him it is written: "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you" <note>Deuteronomy 28:10</note>. And these are the Tefillin of the arm. The Tefillin of the arm is the left side, which is called "Strength" and "Mercy," and the Grace and the moon are upon them all, and they shall all be for a standing. Blessed is the portion of Israel.

## Main Text (Zohar)

...of the Foundation <note>Hebrew: *Yesod*</note>, and because of this, the final letter *He* <note>The last letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> is included within the Head-Tefillin. ->**And I Besought (Va'etchanan)**<-

And when these spirits of the **Head Tephillin** <note>Hebrew: *Tefillin de-Reisha*; representing the higher intellectual Sefirot</note> circulate, a herald praises this unification. This unification consists of three supreme Names, because there are four parchment sections. The first is the **Supreme Point** <note>Hebrew: *Nekudah Ila'ah*; referring to the hidden source of wisdom</note> which is the vision of all. And for the fourth, the spirit of the **World to Come** <note>The Sefirah of Binah/Understanding</note>, the Lord is their crown, included and hidden together in one collective. These are the **Head Tephillin**, and this is the primary unification.

The **Arm Tephillin** <note>Hebrew: *Tefillin de-Daru'a*; representing the Sefirah of Malkhut/Kingship</note> are included within the Head Tephillin, all standing as one. And this is the spirit of: **Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever** <note>Hebrew: *Barukh Shem Kevod Malkhuto Le'olam Va'ed*; the "Lower Unification"</note>. Here is the inclusion of those Head Tephillin as they are integrated into the Arm Tephillin. This spirit of "Blessed" (*Barukh*) is the vitality of the spirit of the Supreme Point, for it is "Blessed" because all blessings spring from there. 

Now, you might say the World to Come is called "Blessed"—but it is not quite so. For the Supreme Point is the **Male** aspect, while the World to Come is the **Female** aspect. "Blessed" (*Barukh*) is the Male, and "Blessing" (*Berakhah*) is the Female. And the Supreme Point is the source of "Blessed." 

"Name" (*Shem*) refers to the World to Come, which is the "Great Name" of all, as in the verse: *And what will You do for Your great Name?* <note>Joshua 7:9</note>. "Glory" (*Kevod*) refers to the Higher Glory, which encompasses Right and Left. "His Kingdom" (*Malkhuto*) refers to the **Hand Prayer** <note>The Arm Tephillin</note>, which sustains and provides for all as needed. 

This is the unification of the Head Tephillin and the Arm Tephillin. Just as the spirit of unification exists in the Tephillin, so is the unification of all things. This is the secret of the "What" (*Mah*) <note>A divine name associated with the human form and Malkhut</note>. Take this order of unification before your holy intention. All the colors of the order of unification are found here, and this is the certainty of them all. This spirit of unification applies to every dwelling-place of the Tephillin; it is the Supreme Unification.

Since the Right and Left of below are included as one, it is necessary afterward to bring them out as a single unification of all—a unification in the presence of the Holy One. This is to establish "The Lord is One" in the Head Tephillin and "His Name is One" in the Arm Tephillin, so they all become one. Once the unification is arranged from the head of the Supreme Point, it is then necessary to awaken it from the head of the **Holy Throne**, which is the head of all. <insert>Until here.</insert>

He engraved and established all the letters in the spirit that emerges from the unification, as it is written: **Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One** <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note>. These are twenty-two engraved letters, carved in the supernal mystery. Jacob desired to establish the "Lower Unification" below, and he established it with the letters of: **Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever**. 

When the Tabernacle <note>Hebrew: *Mishkan*; also implying the indwelling Presence</note> was completed and perfected in this mystery, it was called "Throne" (*Kes*) in the days of its completion. As it is written: *And Your pious ones shall bless You* <note>Psalm 145:10</note>—this refers to the completion of the Tabernacle and its repair. This corresponds to the twenty-two letters of the Torah.

Echad*</note> and the twenty-four letters of *Barukh Shem...*. # Va'etchanan

**Rabbi** Abba opened and said, Rabbi Shimeon said to him: This which we have established regarding the "Tefillin of the Master of the Universe" <note>A Talmudic concept that God also "wears" Tefillin, representing His connection to Israel</note>, they are the holiness of the knot. It is sufficient that regarding the Tefillin and those straps, one must call upon holiness to be found therein. He opened for him: *And the Lord God answered* <note>original: "ויען יהוה אלהים" - cf. Jonah 4:6/Job 38:1</note> and so on. The name *Elohim* <note>God/Judgment</note> is pushed aside and specifically refers to the "Woman" <note>The Shekhinah, the feminine aspect of the Divine</note>, and because we have established that "he who covers a matter is a fool," these are the arm and the arm—perhaps as they have established it. <margin>Tosefta 39, the living creatures of the Mishnah in the Book of Creation</margin> That arm is the "Samael" <note>The left side/Judgment</note> of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and it is called *Gevurah* <term>Strength/Judgment: the fifth Sefirah, associated with the left arm</term>. Thus, they are not found in the spirit except as three, yet they are four holy diagonals. And the companions have said well, as mentioned above: this one is bound to the heart, and this one is bound to the brain. The heart and the brain are bound one to the other, and they have a single union. And the end shall be "upon your hand" as it was said, and they are called nothing but "Living Creatures" <note>Chayot - the holy angels carrying the Divine Throne</note>.

Rabbi Shimeon said: Like the claim of a man who sanctifies his wings <note>his prayer shawl/Tallit</note> and places Tefillin on his head and Tefillin on his arm—he is sanctified in his arm and wraps himself in the wrapping of a garment. When he comes to exit the gate of his house, the Mezuzah <note>The scroll on the doorpost</note> is hinted at, for the holy Name is at the gate of his house. Four holy angels join with him and go out with him from the gate of his house, and they accompany him to the synagogue. They proclaim before him: "Give honor to the image of the Holy King! Give honor to the herald of the King! Give honor to the face of the King!" The Holy Spirit rests upon him to crown him and to protect Israel. When he departs, then that holy spirit ascends above and testifies about him before the Holy King. Then the Supernal King commands to write before Him all those members of the Palace, all those who are recognized before Him. This is what is written:
> *Then a book of remembrance was written before Him for those who fear the Lord and for those who meditate on His name.* <note>Malachi 3:16</note>

And so on, "and for those who meditate on His name," as it says regarding the "thought" <note>Choshev</note> of the Ephod <note>The High Priest's breastplate</note>. These are those who act for His name and His merit in all the craftsmanship of the Tefillin: in their housings, in their straps, and in the writing they are written with—the craftsmanship of His signs, their coverings in the "brain" of blue wool. The craftsmanship of the brain—these are the "meditators on His name." And it is written, "and the thinkers of thoughts." Not only that, but the Holy One, Blessed be He, gazes at him and proclaims over him to all the worlds: "See what a creature I have made in My world!" But one who enters before Him into the synagogue while bowed and loathsome, without Tefillin on his spirit and without assistance in his garment, and says he will "bow toward Your holy temple in fear of You"—the Holy One, Blessed be He, says: "Where is the fear of Me?" <note>original: "הל"ס סוד סודותי' דסקרח'" - This refers to the secret of secrets of the gaze</note>.

Rabbi Isaac said: Blessed is the portion of one who merits this. He said "Our God" to Rabbi Isaac, a higher level that is bound to the secret of the faithful. And Rabbi Shimeon said: If human beings only knew the words of the Torah, they would know that there is no end to a word in the Torah; rather, there is nothing in the Torah that does not contain supernal and precious secrets. Come and see what is written:
> *And these... and God answered him with a voice.* <note>Exodus 19:19</note>

And we have learned: what is "with a voice"? With the voice of Moses. And it is well said, "with his voice" specifically below, with that voice which he grasped above all, as it were. And the appointed ones are placed over all. And because he was to be grasped above all in the Voice—the Voice was a supernal level. He said to Israel: "The Lord your God," which is the level that searches the Shekhinah <term>The Divine Presence</term> within them. And such was his portion.

And Rabbi Shimeon said: We have learned that the voices written [in the Torah]—some were said "from the mouth of the *Gevurah*" <note>Directly from God's Power</note> and some were said by "the Torah of Moses from his own mouth." What is "from his own mouth"? Would it enter your mind, Heaven forbid, that he changed anything in the Torah or spoke from himself? Rather, this is a fine secret: "from himself" we did not learn, but "from his own mouth." He is the secret of the "Voice" <note>The Sefirah of Tiferet</note> to which he was bound. Therefore, these were not just from the mouth of Power and those from his own mouth, but from that level to which he was bound in the secret of the faithful. And therefore, in every place it says "Your God" and "Our God." Come and see: by day, human beings must guard their holiness so that they may be arranged in the service of their Master and merit eternal life. Beneath the Throne of the Holy King there are supernal dwellings, and in this place of the Throne, the preparation is bound to be found by many masters and meritorious ones who are destined...

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Va'etchanan, focusing on the mystical protection of the home and the elevation of prayer. It transitions from general commandments to the specific power of the Mezuzah and the "Song of Ascents" (Psalms).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Va'etchanan**<-
<note>Hebrew: "And I pleaded" — the opening word of the Torah portion in Deuteronomy 3:23.</note>

...which are destined to awaken within human beings in this world. In this same manner, the Holy One, blessed be He, acted toward Israel and gave them the commandments of the Torah so that they might look into them and be saved in this world from many strikes of judgment and from many accusers who confront human beings every day. Rabbi Hiyya said: Who is he that wishes to be guarded in his path and not pass by the strikes of the "flaming ones" <note>referring to destructive spiritual forces or angels of judgment</note> before his doorway? For there dwells a pure and great one <note>a guardian angel or spiritual presence</note> between the two posts of the doorway, and the wise look toward the doorway and observe all that they do in the house. A person should not wish to stray from the path of the gates. Rabbi Isaac said: From the day a person departs [from the right path], we have no concern for him, provided he does not add a sword of disgrace to them. What is the reason? Because [the accuser] has permission to cause damage, and furthermore, he even turns his head toward the house. In everything that one strives to trample, there are three lashings and deviations, and he strikes with an accounting, and death is brought by the one who rules over them; and they all go out with a person when he exits the gate of his house.

And Rabbi Elazar returned [to the subject]: The Holy One, blessed be He, desires all of this to protect Israel and to establish a holy hiddenness above. The Torah is pressed, and the Torah is entirely a hidden, holy thing; and whoever strives in the Torah strives in His Name. Come and see: a person is required to mark the Holy Name upon the doorway of his house for the strength of the faith of all. For in every place where the Holy Name is found, evil species <note>demonic forces or "Sitra Achra"</note> are not found there, and they are unable to accuse the person, as it is written:
> No evil shall befall you, nor shall any plague come near your dwelling. (Psalms 91:10)

The *Mezuzah* <term>Mezuzah: a parchment scroll inscribed with Torah verses, placed on doorposts</term> is the name for the place of the doorway of the house, rising in the likeness of the Supernal [realm]. The place of the doorway of the Upper House <note>the spiritual realm of Binah or Malchut</note> is where the *Mezuzah* dwells, for it is the rectification of the house. From this doorway, from this *Mezuzah*, the "hidden ones" of judgment flee, and they are not found before it. This commandment below—when a person fixes a *Mezuzah* to the doorway of his house with the vision of the Holy Name engraved in the seal—this person is crowned with the crowns of his Master, and evil species do not approach the doorway of his house and are not found there.

Rabbi Abba was coming along the road to see Rabbi Shimon. Rabbi Isaac met him and said to him: Are we not coming to follow the light? This man [Rabbi Shimon] is settled like a fire that consumes every day; a deep storehouse dwells here. He said to him: We have learned that the life of a person depends on receiving the face of the *Shekhinah* <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</term> at every moment and breath, and then they go out. And who are those within it? All who are aged like him, the ascents of holiness, for all the people of the world need to receive his face. Rabbi Isaac said: I will walk with you to receive the face of the *Shekhinah*, and to taste the sweetness of the supernal words that you have tasted before him.

Rabbi Abba opened and said:
> A Song of Ascents. To You I lift up my eyes, O You who dwell in the heavens. (Psalms 123:1)

Regarding this "Song," it is not written who said it. Rather, as in every place where it is left anonymous, the Holy Spirit said it concerning Israel in exile. "O You who dwell [*ha-yoshevi*] in the heavens"—it should have said "He who dwells" [*ha-yoshev*]. Why "the dwellers" <note>the original Hebrew suffix *-i* implies a plural or a specific mystical connection</note>? Rather, we have established that whoever wishes to direct his prayer before the Holy King must beg from the depths of the heart to bring forth the Will below, as it is written:
> A Song of Ascents. Out of the depths I have called to You, O Lord. (Psalms 130:1)

And see, the most "depth" of all is that place which needs to be brought forth with Will to the place called "Heavens," so that everything may rest from it; and regarding this, it says "the dwellers in the heavens." In the actual heavens, for when they are in the Will that is hidden and drawn from that deepest place of all, and we gather it to the place called Heavens, then by that Will, [blessings] are found above it and below it.
> Behold, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their masters... (Psalms 123:2)

"Our eyes are as servants"—these are the other great nations who have no physical devotion to the study that Israel is settled in. And when Israel takes with Will from that place, they are all blessed from the *Yesod* <term>Yesod: the "Foundation," the ninth Sefirah, representing the channel of blessing</term>.
> ...as the eyes of a maidservant to the hand of her mistress. (Psalms 123:2)

This "maidservant" refers to the [nations] whom the Holy One, blessed be He, established to serve His word like a master. For she has no power of her own except when it is drawn from the eight [levels] that sustain the Land of Israel. And the Land of Israel is her mistress.

<summary>This text explains the mystical protection provided by the Mezuzah against spiritual accusers and discusses the "Song of Ascents," emphasizing that prayer must emerge from the "depths" of the heart to draw divine Will from the heavens down to the Land of Israel.</summary>
<keywords>Mezuzah, protection, Shekhinah, Song of Ascents, Psalms, prayer, Land of Israel, Yesod, spiritual judgment</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the spiritual protection of Israel, specifically focusing on the Mezuzah and the physical signs that distinguish the children of the King from the "Other Side."</meta>

## Va'etchanan

Regarding the blessing we recite over the Life of Worlds, it is written: *under the ladder of the feet of Haran.* What is Haran? This is the Land of Israel, as it is said: >The eyes of the Lord your God are always upon it< <note>Deuteronomy 11:12</note>. Those deeds we mentioned—all those authorities—each one of them is not He, as it is written: >Who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage< <note>Exodus 20:2</note>. >For a handmaid when she displaces her mistress< <note>Proverbs 30:23</note>—what is this "handmaid" that we mentioned? Come and see: from the side of this handmaid emerge many "shining guards" <note>destructive angels or accusers</note> who oppose Israel to prosecute them.

But the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>The standard Rabbinic name for God, often abbreviated as Hakadosh Baruch Hu</note> provides protection for Israel, like a father who desires to guard everything. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel: "Since so many accusers are ready to oppose you, occupy yourselves with My service, and I shall be your guardian outside. You shall be prepared within your houses, and even when you are in your beds, I shall be the guardian at your doorway to protect you."

And come and see: at the moment those evil species approach a person's doorway, they raise their heads and look at the holy mark below. When they behold the name <term>Shaddai</term> <note>A Divine Name often associated with protection and boundaries; it is traditionally written on the outside of the Mezuzah scroll</note>, which is crowned with the crowns of the Master of All, they are all humbled; they fear and flee, and do not approach the person's doorway.

Rabbi Isaac said to him: "If so, let a person simply record this Name on the doorway of his house and not be required to write the entire passage <note>The Shema and Vehaya passages contained in the Mezuzah</note>."

He replied to him: "That is not sufficient, for this Name is only crowned when all those letters are inscribed with the King's inscription. When the entire passage is written, then this Name is crowned with its crowns, and the King goes forth with all His hosts; then they fear Him and flee from before Him."

Come and see: the Holy Name is arranged from below to above, and therefore "Shaddai" is inscribed on the outside corresponding to this Name. It is within, and "Shaddai" is without, so that it may be a guard from all sides, within and without. How so? At that moment when a person places a <term>Mezuzah</term> <note>A parchment scroll placed on doorposts containing the Shema prayer</note> on his gate, many holy hosts are ready, and they all proclaim and say: >This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter through it< <note>Psalms 118:20</note>.

Happy is the portion of Israel! For then Israel are recognized as the children of the Holy King. For they are marked everywhere: they are marked in their bodies with the holy sign <note>Circumcision</note>; they are marked in their garments with the wraps of the commandment <note>Tzitzit/Tallit</note>; they are marked on their heads with <term>Tefillin</term> <note>Phylacteries worn during prayer</note>, the anointing of the King; they are marked on their hands with the holy straps; they are marked in their shoes; they are marked outside on the arm. They are marked in their houses, in everything. They are marked like the children of the High King—happy is their portion!

As they were walking, Rabbi Abba said: "What is the meaning of that which is written: *And I saw his eye, a source of living water, flowing from Lebanon etc.*? 'I saw his eye' refers to one who gazes upon the sign of the holy mark. And how many gaze upon them <note>the nations</note> to bring them into the 'other domain,' to dig broken cisterns? For the idol-worshipping nations dig broken cisterns, but Israel digs a well of springing water, which emerges and flows from it, as you say: >And flowing streams from Lebanon< <note>Song of Songs 4:15</note>, and >Flowing water from the midst of your well< <note>Proverbs 5:15</note>. And it is written: >A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters< <note>Song of Songs 4:15</note>.

'Whose waters do not fail'—this refers to that River that flows and goes out to the Garden, to every garden, watering every single place, as we have established, until it reaches that place where they dig the <term>Well of Living Waters</term>. From there, the upper and lower beings are sustained, as it is said: >And from there it divided< <note>Genesis 2:10</note>. But all those crowns of the Left Side are not watered by that flow of springing waters, because they are from the side of the 'other nations.'

But one who gazes upon the holy sign is attached to that side: >Like palm-groves that stretch out< <note>Numbers 24:6</note>. 'Whose waters do not fail' and do not deceive there. And he is worthy of being guarded by it, and to be sustained by that flow, and he enjoys this world and the World to Come. This is what is written: >And you shall be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters do not fail< <note>Isaiah 58:11</note>. And he is worthy to be filled from that Supernal Well, to draw down blessings above and below. Woe to one who damages the holy sign, for he damages the gateway...

<summary>This page explains the mystical protection afforded by the Mezuzah, noting that the name 'Shaddai' only gains its full power when accompanied by the complete scriptural text. It further describes how the various physical commandments (Tefillin, Tzitzit, Circumcision) mark the Jewish people as children of the Divine King, protecting them from the 'Other Side.'</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the portion of Va'etchanan, specifically focusing on the esoteric meanings of the "Shema Yisrael" and the spiritual mechanics of the future redemption. It connects the gathering of the exiles to the unification of Divine attributes.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

**Hear, O Israel** <note>original: "Shema Yisrael"</note>. Furthermore, because of this, after they were no longer found, we read concerning it that He delivered a "bad horse" <note>a play on words or mystical reference to dark forces</note> over the Assembly of Israel. Specifically the "Assembly of Israel" <note>Knesseth Yisrael; the mystical personification of the Jewish people and the Divine Presence</note>. Rabbi Shimon established in the Composition (another book: in the *Idra* <note>The "Assembly" or "Threshing Floor," a core section of the Zohar</note>) that these words were powerful regarding her former sister, and He brought out a horse against her, just as He brought out above, as it is written: >*For You ride upon Your horses*< [Habakkuk 3:8], a "bad horse" over the Assembly of Israel. And is it not so?

For behold, Rabbi Hiyya said that Rabbi Yose said: The time will come when the blessing will be found in nature, because the Assembly of Israel inherits seven blessings. For this reason, she is called "Bathsheba" <note>literally "Daughter of Seven"</note>, but below she lacked her own blessing, the blessing they desired. The secret of the whole matter is: >*And all the people who were in the gate and the elders said, "We are witnesses; may the Lord make the woman..."*< [Ruth 4:11]. For this Assembly of Israel was not found and was not blessed therein. Once they arrived in the field of one of their constellations and their strength returned, Rabbi Abba said: Behold, this is the image of what is written regarding the destruction.

He opened and said: >*And it shall come to pass on that day, that a great Shofar shall be blown; and those who were lost in the land of Assyria and those who were dispersed in the land of Egypt shall come...*< [Isaiah 27:13]. "And it shall come to pass on that day"—who is "on that day"? It is that day that is known to the Holy One, blessed be He: >*And it shall be one day which shall be known to the Lord*< [Zechariah 14:7]. Furthermore, "on that day" means everything is in the "day" when the pair <note>the masculine and feminine aspects of the Divine</note> is upon the land of Israel. "And a great Shofar shall be blown"—what does it matter to us if it is great or small? Rather, it is that Upper Shofar <note>symbolizing the attribute of Binah/Understanding</note> through which servants always go out to freedom; it stands as the mercy and the power of the Upper Power, and it is blessed. And when this is awakened, all the freedoms of the worlds are awakened through it, and that is called the "Great Shofar."

"And those who were lost in the land of Assyria shall come." It should have said "the lost ones"—what is the meaning of "those who were lost"? They are literally lost because they are under "other authority" <note>the Sitra Achra or "Other Side," the realm of impurity</note> on this side and that side. Since they are from the "other authority" and none of them dwell in faith, for that reason they are called "lost"—they are lost on all sides. When Israel dwells in the Holy Land, then they are always meritorious, all of them meritorious above and below.

Truly, who are "those who were lost"? These are the <term>Tzaddik</term> <note>The Righteous One; the masculine Divine attribute of Yesod</note> and the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>The feminine Divine attribute of Malchut</note>. They are called "lost" from here. Regarding the Assembly of Israel, it is written: >*Why is the land lost?*< [Jeremiah 9:11]. If it does not say "Assembly of Israel" but rather "the land is lost," this refers to the Assembly of Israel. Regarding the *Tzaddik*, it is written: >*The righteous one is lost*< [Isaiah 57:1]. It does not say "desired by him as kindness," but simply "is lost," as they have established.

And if you say, "And they shall come"—from what place do these "lost ones" come? Rather, the Assembly of Israel comes from the <term>Exile</term> <note>Galuta</note>. The *Tzaddik*, as they have established, as it is written: >*And the Lord [guarded] the Sabbath*<—since he returns to his place and comes to be found within the Assembly of Israel. And regarding this: "And those who were lost in the land of Assyria shall come." And if you say, "And we shall open to the Holy Jerusalem"—what is spoken of in Jerusalem? Rather, this matter is like Abraham from Haran; as it were, Israel shall not go out from exile except with the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence</note>, as they have established. And they are like those who hope for the Lord.

Furthermore, Rabbi Abba said: It is written, >*The Lord shall guard your going out and your coming in from this time forth and forever*< [Psalms 121:8]. "The Lord shall guard your going out" is understandable. But what is "your coming in"? For one who enters his house is not afraid. Rather, it is like this: when there is holy love for his house, like words of upper praise, this is to be protected from everything. When he goes out, he who is joined to the door of his house stands tall and sees the holy love and looks (another version: because) at his openings. When he goes out, he sees the one who joins him, and when he sees him, everyone who enters his house bows before him, honoring the image of the Holy King. And all this is because that holy love is found at his door. And it is not enough for him to be protected outside, but as it is written: "The Lord shall guard your going out and your coming in from this time forth and forever." The Holy One, blessed be He, guards him when he enters and when he goes out. Worthy are Israel in this world and in the world to come. Come and see, the spirit on the following day...

<summary>This text provides a mystical interpretation of the ingathering of exiles, explaining that the "lost" ones are actually the Divine attributes of the Tzaddik and the Assembly of Israel (Shekhinah) returning from exile. It also discusses the spiritual protection afforded by the Mezuzah on a person's doorway, symbolizing Divine guardianship over one's "going and coming."</summary>
<keywords>Shema, Knesseth Yisrael, Tzaddik, Shofar Gadol, Exile, Shekhinah, Redemption, Mezuzah, Divine Protection</keywords>
