## Main Text (Zohar)

...since the gates [of the heart] are opened. Woe to the person who does not know how to be on guard against him <note>The "him" refers to the Evil Inclination or the Accuser</note> and does not run to the door of his Master. The Holy One, Blessed be He, opens [the way] for him, for he has three hundred and sixty-five evil supports—accusers, each one corresponding to a day [of the solar year]. All of them watch him throughout all the days of the year and accuse him above and below. They all watch him by day and by night; at the time of accusation at night, they seek to consume him from the worlds. When he <note>the accuser</note> goes out to prosecute him, as he enters, they place their hands upon his shoulders and say: "Woe to this person who has left the authority of his Master! Woe to this person in this world and in the world to come!" Because of this, the children of faith must be mindful of all the signs and the secrets of their Master, to be guarded on all sides from evil species, so they may be protected in this world and in the world to come. Fortunate is the portion of Israel, of whom it is written: > And your people shall all be righteous; they shall inherit the land forever < <note>Isaiah 60:21</note> and so on.

**And you shall love** the Lord your God. Rabbi Yose opened [the discussion]: > And now, what does the Lord your God ask of you, but to fear the Lord your God < <note>Deuteronomy 10:12</note> and so on. Come and see the love of the Holy One, Blessed be He, for Israel! Because of their [sinful] companions, they caused love to be withdrawn and were scattered among the nations; He demands their grievance. And come and see: when Israel dwelt in their land, the Holy One, Blessed be He, delighted in the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> for the sake of Israel, and He tasted their praises and was found among them. Once their sins caused it and Israel was exiled from the land, the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not enter the Assembly of Israel and did not delight in her, except at the time they are summoned. And see: > And now, what does the Lord your God ask of you, but to fear the Lord your God < and so on, for He took my people for nothing, as it is said: > You were sold for nothing < <note>Isaiah 52:3</note>. And from the time that Israel was revealed to be exiled from their land, joy has not been found before the Holy One, Blessed be He. Come and see: > I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth their covering < <note>Isaiah 50:3</note>. And all this is because of His love for them, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, loves them, as it is said: > I have loved you, says the Lord < <note>Malachi 1:2</note>. And regarding this: "And you shall love the Lord your God." <term>And you shall love</term> <note>Hebrew: Ve-ahavta</note> means that a person must bind himself to Him in love, for of all the supernal service that a person must perform for the Holy One, Blessed be He, in love, there is no service like the love of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

Rabbi Abba said: All the words of the Torah are here included, for they crown the path to the Torah, as the companions have established. And come, you have no matter as beloved before the Holy One, Blessed be He, as when one loves Him as is fitting. And what is that? As it is written: > With all your heart < <note>Deuteronomy 6:5</note>. What does "with all" refer to? It should have said "with your heart." Why "with all"? Rather, it is to include two hearts: one good and one evil <note>The Good Inclination and the Evil Inclination</note>. > With all your soul <—even if He takes your soul. This [interpretation] did not come to us for a homily [alone]. Rabbi Eleazar said: Even if it stands as a homily, it is so. For since one gives his soul, his money is his inheritance; and from the "Other Side," since he is sparing [with money], it provides him relief, and regarding this it is written: > With all your might < <note>meaning with all your wealth</note>.

Rabbi Abba said to direct the verse: "And you shall love" is a matter that runs to the Holy One, Blessed be He, to be crowned with <term>Chesed</term> <note>Loving-kindness, the fourth Sefirah</note> from all sides, and He performs kindness with all. And this is why he is sparing with his body and his money. From where do we know this? From <term>Abraham</term>, as it was said, for he did not spare [anything] in his love for his Master—not his heart (which is his inclination), nor his soul, nor his money. Regarding his heart: he did not look at his own will because of the love of his Master. Regarding his soul: [he risked it] for his son and his wife because of the love of his Master. Regarding his money: for he left his possessions and the crossroads, and prepared food for the whole world. Because of this, he was crowned with the crown of Kindness, as it is written: > Kindness to Abraham < <note>Micah 7:20</note>. And whoever binds himself to the love of his Master merits this, and not only that, but all the worlds are blessed because of him. This is what is written: > And I will bless those who bless you, and him who curses you I will curse; and in you shall all be blessed < <note>Genesis 12:3</note>.

And come and see, said Rabbi Yose: Rabbi Abba, Rabbi Yehuda, and Rabbi Isaac were above them. They saw him <note>likely Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> as he was falling on his face and weeping. And after he awoke, they saw that his face was smiling. Rabbi Abba said to him: You have let us hear a new word...

<summary>This passage explores the spiritual necessity of loving God with all aspects of one's being—heart, soul, and wealth—using Abraham as the ultimate model of the attribute of Chesed (Kindness). It also describes the cosmic mourning of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) during the exile of Israel.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Va'etchanan, focusing on the mystical union of the Divine Name and the transformation of the human inclination during the resurrection of the dead.</meta>

## Va'etchanan

->**Va'etchanan**<-
<note>Hebrew: "And I besought," the opening word of Deuteronomy 3:23</note>

He went and ran to the open and hidden gate, the precious one of kings. See that his appearance is like the Holy One of your King, upon whom rest thirteen mountains of pure balsam <note>original: "d'afarsamona dachya," a Zoharic metaphor for divine emanations of grace</note>. And the Holy One, blessed be He, delights in them. See what they did not give me permission to speak, and I asked them: "Where does the glory of the King dwell?" They said to me: "See that the love of your King is like the side of the world, and from what you have seen at the gates and the running, it shall be clarified." And regarding this, wisdom is for the guilty. Rabbi Abba said to him: "Fortunate is your portion! For every joint of yours, His kindness is a throne," as it is written:

> No eye has seen a God besides You, who acts for those who wait for Him. <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>

Rabbi Yehuda said to him: "Behold, we see, friends, that it is written 'He acts' <note>Hebrew: ya'aseh</note>, but it should have said 'You will act' <note>Hebrew: ta'aseh</note>." He replied to him: "This has been explained regarding every spirit of the word; this is what is written: 'To behold the graciousness of the Lord and to visit His temple' <note>Psalm 27:4</note>, as they have established it. This 'graciousness of the Lord' comes from the Ancient Holy One <note>term: Atika Kadisha - the most hidden, primordial level of the Divine</note>, in which the Holy One, blessed be He, delights. For that graciousness emerges from the Ancient One. So too here: 'No eye has seen a God besides You, He acts'—He is the Ancient One, the most hidden of all, for everything depends on Him." He said to him: "And it is truly so! Fortunate is the portion of the wise, for the love of your King clings to them, and these have no side to their portion in that world." Rabbi Isaac said: "How many dwellings upon dwellings do the righteous have in that world! And the highest dwelling of all is that of the love of your King which is bound to them, for their dwelling is bound to all and rises above all." See, because the Holy One, blessed be He, is crowned with all, He is called 'Love' <note>Hebrew: Ahava</note>. And because of love, everything exists, as it is written:

> Many waters cannot quench love. <note>Song of Songs 8:7</note>

And everything stands through love, for the Holy Name is found thus. As they have established: the Holy One, blessed be He, is never separated from the letter *Yod* <note>The first letter of the Tetragrammaton</note>, for love rests upon it and it is never separated from it. The letter *Heh*—they have established that it is not separated from the whole, and it is found in a bond of affection; they do not separate one from the other, *Yod* and *Heh*. And thus it is sealed, as it is written: 'And a river went out of Eden' <note>Genesis 2:10</note>. And behold, they are forever in affection, clinging to one another, and the dwelling is constant. All of them are in love and affection: *Yod* makes *Heh*, *Heh* makes *Vav*, and *Vav* makes *Heh*. Everything is called 'Love,' and then it is bound in affection. And whoever loves the King is bound in that love, and because of this: 'And you shall love the Lord your God' <note>Deuteronomy 6:5</note>."

**And it shall be** when these words... Rabbi Isaac opened: "Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity and passes over transgression..." <note>Micah 7:18</note>. These degraded ones seek the holiness that David spoke of through the Holy Spirit: "Who pardons iniquity," etc. Why do we offer the love of the wine of song? Rather, these verses refer to the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to revive the dead. When the Holy One, blessed be He, is seen strengthening the bones and bringing each one to their place, as it is written:

> And He will strengthen your bones. <note>Isaiah 58:11</note>

Then they are destined to sing a song. What song do they say? "Lord, who is like You?" They place the Name first in the song. Why is this superior to what they said and sang at the Sea? For there, they did not mention the Holy Name until after three words, as it is written: "Who is like You among the mighty, O Lord?" <note>Exodus 15:11</note>. But here, they put the Holy Name first, as it is written: "Lord, who is like You?" He removes the degraded people and wipes away the guilt. This is the "Good Memory" over the "Evil Side," because the Evil Inclination <note>term: Yetzer Hara - the human drive toward selfishness or sin</note> is as strong as wisdom, as it is written:

> And I will remove the heart of stone. <note>Ezekiel 36:26</note>

And the Good Inclination <note>term: Yetzer Tov</note> is like dew, as it is written: "And I will give you a heart of flesh." Come and see: what is the Evil Inclination like? It is like a traveler who comes to lodge with a man. At first, he is like a servant, until they bring him in to stay. After he is gathered in to dwell, he becomes like a fire. Rabbi Hiyya said: "When the Evil Inclination comes to lodge with a person, it is like a person who stands at the door. He sees that there is no one to strike his hand, so he enters the house and becomes a guest. He sees there is no one to strike his hand, and he goes to take possession. Since he approached the door and there was no one to strike his hand, he is found over them and becomes the master of the house."

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the portion "Va'etchanan" (Deuteronomy 3:23–7:11), specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the "Shema" prayer and the psychological struggle between the two human inclinations.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

When the whole house is found to be holy through its attachment <note>to the Divine</note>, what is the meaning of the verse "dripping from the locks of David"? <note>original: *azlufim miparshata ledavid* - a poetic reference to divine flow</note>
What is written? "And the King came to his house." <note>2 Samuel 15:16</note> He went because he was close to his entrance, and they did not want to be found there except for one whose way it is to be there. So it is with the **Evil Inclination** <term>Yetzer Hara: the drive toward selfish or physical desires</term>; as much as it approaches his house, it approaches a person to stir him up. At first, it is weak like a passerby, for such is the way of the uncircumcised. When it sees there is no one to strike its hand, what is written? "To make a way." Here, it seeks to find a path to be a guest in his house. It stirs against him like a guest and strikes once or twice, and is invited like a traveler who is hosted in the house. It strikes again and again, invited to be a guest. Once it sees there is no one to strike its hand, what is written? "And he made for the man." Here, it becomes the master of the house, as it is said: "Like a secular man of the land" or "The husband of Naomi." Thus the **Evil Inclination** acts toward a person until it becomes the "Master of the House," and the person is bound in its service, and it does its will with him. And when a person desires to remove it from his path, it stands against him so that he cannot recognize his own way. Therefore, a person must provoke the **Evil Inclination** <note>to overcome it</note>, and regarding this it is written: "And these words... shall be upon your heart" <note>Deuteronomy 6:6</note>—meaning upon your *two* inclinations <note>The Hebrew word for heart, *Levavcha*, is written with two 'bets', which the Sages interpret as the Good and Evil inclinations working together</note>. The **Good Inclination** <term>Yetzer Hatov: the drive toward morality and divine service</term> should be stirred, and the **Evil Inclination** should be humbled before its fellow. And what does the **Good Inclination** require for its path? The **Good Inclination** says to him: "Do not be stirred by them." For when the **Evil Inclination** sees that a person does not desire to labor in the **Torah** <term>Oraita: Divine Law and Wisdom</term>, it immediately ascends above and complains about him. A voice says: "The fool inherits disgrace." When the poor man comes... this portion hints at how many things must be established. "And these words shall be..."—this is the general rule of the ten times <note>referring to the ten commandments or specific utterances</note>, and there are commandments here corresponding to the commandments of the **Torah**, and these words are: "And you shall teach them diligently to your children, and you shall speak of them..."

> "And you shall teach them diligently to your children, and you shall speak of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up." <note>Deuteronomy 6:7</note>

"And you shall bind them for a sign upon your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes. And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your house and upon your gates." These six <note>instructions</note> correspond to six utterances. Regarding these portions, they are a great principle in the **Torah**, and their entire ascent is to cast <note>holiness</note> upon him every day, twice a day, so that his mouth may be sanctified with a proper holiness. **Rabbi Isaac** was standing with **Rabbi Eleazar** at a certain place after midnight, and they were laboring in the **Torah**. **Rabbi Eleazar** opened <note>his discourse</note> and said: "For she is your life and the length of your days..." <note>Proverbs 4:13/Deuteronomy 30:20</note> Come and see: of all the ornaments of the Holy One, blessed be He, when they come to the Land of Israel, the lightning-flash of the **Torah** is the greatest. Why? Because the **Shekhinah** <term>The Divine Presence, often viewed as feminine</term> does not dwell in the world except through the **Torah**, and she does not dwell above except through the **Torah**. For thus said **Rabbi Shimon**: "Everything is the Oral Torah, which is only known because of the Written Torah." The **Shekhinah** does not dwell above or below except with the **Torah**. For one who has the **Torah** found with him, he is able to exist in the world. Is it not written: "For she is your life and the length of your days," to merit the land? Regarding this, I was born... and life is not... It is written "by mouth" regarding the writing of the land. And it is written: "And the Lord said: Because they have forsaken My Torah." While they were sitting, **Rabbi Eleazar** held his head and sighed. He said: "This is certainly the secret found in the **Book of Rav Hamnuna Sava** <note>The Elder; a legendary figure in Zohar literature</note>." The verse is engraved like the secret of the **Congregation of Israel** <term>Knesset Yisrael: a mystical representation of the Jewish people and the Shekhinah</term>, as it is written: "Her food, her clothing, and her conjugal rights he shall not diminish." <note>Exodus 21:10</note> And if you do not withhold from her, what is written? "A wise son brings joy..." just as it says, "a bill of divorcement" to the wise one whom I sent. And it is written: "For nothing you were sold, and not with money shall you be redeemed." One who withholds the **Torah** from himself is like one who diminishes <note>the rights of</note> his wife and withholds from her. For she labored like a widow, yet she is not a widow, as it is written: "She has become like a widow," but not a widow. And they studied and occupied themselves with the **Torah** until the day shone. Once the day shone, they rose and went on their way. While they were walking, they saw a man who was walking in weariness, his garment wrapped around him, and a burden was signaled upon his shoulders.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Va’etchanan**<-
<note>Hebrew: "And I pleaded" — the opening word of the Torah portion.</note>

...with your lips and I did not return anything to them. <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> <note>Son of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the primary figure of the Zohar.</note> said: Certainly the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu" — the standard Aramaic name for God.</note> and the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael" — the mystical personification of the Jewish people, often identified with the Shekhinah or Divine Presence.</note> sit in a measured state, and four see the exile. The commandment prevailed in its standing like another place. After they finished the exile, we saw with mercy that the man who was heard from among them prevailed. <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> said: This verse is not foolish; grace and mercy are not guarded. He said: When you occupy yourself with the <term>Torah</term> <note>original: "Oraita" — the Aramaic term for Torah, encompassing both law and mystical wisdom.</note>, that is the reason. <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> opened and said:
> The wise shall inherit honor, but fools carry away shame. (Proverbs 3:35)

"The wise shall inherit honor" — these are the meritorious ones who occupy themselves with the <term>Torah</term>. Before he opened the matter, that man drew near to them. <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> said: We must not cease from words of <term>Torah</term>, for anyone who strives in the <term>Torah</term> merits to inherit an inheritance found above in the glory of the Holy High King, and merits to inherit an inheritance found in this world. And what is it? That which is called "honor," etc., which never ceases from among them forever. This is what is written: "The wise shall inherit honor." And that which is called "honor" [contrasts with] "but fools carry away shame." Who is he? Come and see: every man who follows the difficult, light <term>Evil Inclination</term> <note>original: "Ha-Yetzer" — the internal drive toward selfishness or sin.</note> and [yet] strives in the <term>Torah</term>, behold, he inherits that honor. And how many guardians are found above him, and all of them pass over him, and all are before the Holy King. But if a man does not strive in the <term>Torah</term> and does not walk in the path of the <term>Torah</term>, he creates an accuser against himself. And that accuser rules in that world and goes with him and does not ascend above, for the man sits liable because this man repented before him and did not want to strive in the <term>Torah</term>; then he ascends above and brings guilt upon him. This is what is written: "but fools carry away shame" — he ascends above and creates an accusation. He opened and said:
> And if the family of Egypt go not up, and come not, it shall not be upon them; there shall be the plague, etc. (Zechariah 14:18)

How is Egypt different here from all other nations? For regarding all of them it is written, "upon them there shall be no rain," but here it is not. Rather, the companions have established it: the land of Egypt does not need rain <note>Because it relies on the flooding of the Nile.</note>, and because of this, all those who would withhold rain from all those [others], the judgment is said to be removed from them; and they have said well. Come and see, it is written:
> For the land, whither thou goest in to possess it, is not as the land of Egypt, from whence ye came out, where thou sowedst thy seed, etc. (Deuteronomy 11:10)

For that [Egypt] ascends and the tax sustains the land for all, but here "it drinketh water of the rain of heaven," for the Holy Land is watered from heaven constantly. And when Israel occupied themselves with the <term>Torah</term>, it was watered as is fitting. And whoever withholds from the <term>Torah</term> is as if he withheld good from the whole world. Because of this, we stayed in a certain cave that was in that place; that man went up with them and they sat. That man opened and said: "And the Lord spoke to Moses <term>face to face</term> <note>original: "Panim el Panim" — a level of direct prophecy unique to Moses.</note> as a man speaks, etc." This verse comes as a hint, the end but not the end, the beginning but not the word, all of it is His command. "And the Lord [spoke]" — the letter *Vav* — "to Moses face to face" is well, and in a good place to the moderate one for his taking. Joshua the son of Nun, a youth. Who? <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> said: Certainly the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> desired your honor, for our time has appeared and we have merited it; let it be removed from us, whoever opened the opening of a single word. He opened and said: "And the Lord spoke to Moses face to face" — how many high and precious levels were spread from his side, and his standing was above all other prophets of the world. For all of them compared to him were like a thorn before other men. The other prophets looked through a <term>dim mirror</term> <note>original: "Aspaklaria de-la Nahara" — a cloudy lens; indirect or hazy prophecy.</note>, and even so they did not lift their faces upward, for they were not able, but as it is written:
> And their faces shall look one to another. (Exodus 25:20)

And furthermore, the words were not with them like a woman to her husband. But Moses, the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> is thus, for he looked through a <term>clear mirror</term> <note>original: "Aspaklaria de-Nahara" — a bright or translucent lens; direct, clear prophecy.</note> and drew near to it in his days. And not only that, but he lifted his head to look, like one who says to his friend: "Turn, turn, and let your face look into my face." Because you acted thus from the side of "face to face," he stood at the head without fear, his face and our faces and surroundings.

[to his] sons

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the portion of Va'etchanan, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of prophecy and the practical application of the Shema's commandments (teaching children and wearing Tefillin). It contrasts the unique level of Moses's prophecy with that of his successors.</meta>

Because the Supernal Voice <note>The divine source of prophecy</note> is not found within human understanding, and its transitions are like a shadow, whenever they [the other prophets] stood facing it to gaze upon it, they would lose their own authority and their senses. They would be changed and frightened, knowing nothing of this world. But with Moses, it was not so. Moses gazed from that very same high level and did not lose his authority or his senses. For at the moment he gazed upon the Supernal Splendor <note>original: *ziv yakira ala'ah*</note>, he immediately **returned to the camp** to speak with them regarding all their needs, his mind as settled as before, or even more so. This is the meaning of: **"And he would return to the camp"** (Exodus 33:11). But **"his servant Joshua the son of Nun, a young man"** (ibid.) certainly drew from that transition, gazing through the Holy Spirit <note>original: *Ruach HaKodesh*</note> accordingly, just as "the lad Samuel ministered before the Lord" (1 Samuel 2:18).

Come and see: as long as Joshua was with Moses, he would transition and become wise through the transition of the profane <note>meaning he could bridge the holy and the mundane through Moses's influence</note>. After he was separated from Moses and was alone, what is written? **"And Joshua fell on his face to the earth and prostrated himself"** (Joshua 5:14), for he could not endure [the vision]. This is like a king who entrusts his treasures of gold and precious jewels to his servants; as long as the king's ministers are with him, they handle them and look at them. Once that man [the leader] departs from his world, the king does not leave anything with the ministers, and the deposit is transferred to the one appointed. Woe, for in the days of his master, all the windows were in his hands! Thus, Joshua in the days of Moses drew every day from the "Field" <note>A Kabbalistic term for the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> and did not fear. After [Moses] passed away, **"Joshua fell on his face."** And come and see: because the wisdom he left within them allowed them to look into the matters of the Torah, he did not fear; but after he was separated from them, he could not look upon it alone. He then opened [his discourse] and said:

# **And You Shall Teach Them Diligently**
**"To your children, and you shall speak of them..."** (Deuteronomy 6:7). Just as one must train <note>original: *l'chaneka*</note> and cover [protect], a person must innovate words of Torah for his son. As it is said, Hezekiah [the King] would place crowns on his children so they would enter into the innovation of Torah, so that their hearts would not be found in foolishness. **"And you shall speak of them"**—all words of Torah, each and every person has their own specific portion in it. **"And you shall speak of them"**—you shall speak what is designated as your portion. A person must find himself within them, and find himself so that he does not stray to the right or the left.

**"When you sit in your house"**: To find oneself in one's home in the secret of the foundation and the choice of the "repair" <note>original: *tikkun*</note> that his household members learn from him; to find himself with them in tranquility and pleasantness, and not to cast excessive fear in his home. All his actions in his home should be like a renewed repair. **"And when you walk by the way"**: To find oneself in the words of Torah and to prepare oneself in them as is necessary, and to lead oneself in one's portion of the Torah. This protects him, just as Isaac [prepared] a gift to approach the exile, and the exile requires revealing its tomorrow; and above them are the words of Torah. **"And when you lie down"**: To lead oneself in the fear of his Master, in holiness and humility, so that he is not found acting brazenly toward his Master. **"And when you rise up"**: To give praise to his Master, who returns his soul <note>original: *nishmata*</note> from among the many "beasts" <note>spiritual predators encountered during sleep</note> that are found before his Master; and the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: *Kudsha Berikh Hu*</note>, performs a kindness <term>Chesed</term> with him and returns it to his body.

# **And You Shall Bind Them**
**"As a sign upon your hand"**: We have established this as "the hand of the *Koh* [the Shekhinah]." <note>The word for "your hand" in the verse is spelled *yadkhah*, which the Zohar reads as *Yad-Koh* (Hand of the Lord)</note>. The sages of the South sit with their secrets regarding the four compartments of the Tefillin in this manner:
1. **"Sanctify to Me every firstborn"** (Exodus 13:2) corresponds to the **Supernal Crown** <term>Keter</term> of all.
2. **"And it shall be when the Lord brings you"** (Exodus 13:11) corresponds to **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah</term>.
3. **"Hear O Israel"** (Deuteronomy 6:4) corresponds to **Understanding** <term>Binah</term>.
4. **"And it shall come to pass if you surely listen"** (Deuteronomy 11:13) corresponds to **Kindness** <term>Chesed</term>.
And after all of them, they are placed on the left arm to call upon it, as it is written: **"With His strong arm"** (Isaiah 62:8). There is no "strength" but Torah, and no "strength" but Tefillin. However, these matters are not settled for us because the Supernal Crown <term>Keter</term> includes everything and is not [individually] found. Furthermore, "And it shall be..."

## Va'etchanan

->**Va'etchanan**<-
<note>Deuteronomy 3:23, "And I besought [the Lord]"</note>

For it contains, in the manner that three emerge, that place below <note>referring to the Sefirah of Malchut/Kingdom</note> wherein there is joy for their actions, and because of this they are not established in their heavens. And we have learned: because of its heat, there are orders, and it is great, for the Holy One, blessed be He, takes them; and so too for the level above, four below and four after the likeness, and four after the <unclear>Sariuch</unclear>. Because this whole thing is bound together, a person must crown themselves with them for the sake of the life of the Supernal Holy Name, as it is written: *And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon thee...* <note>Deuteronomy 28:10</note>. And anyone who is crowned with this supernal holy crown is called a "king on earth," just as the Holy One, blessed be He, is King in heaven. This is "King for Kindness" <term>Chesed: the attribute of mercy</term> as we have explained; just as the Holy One, blessed be He, is King above, so too is He King below. And despite all this, *And thou shalt write them upon the doorposts of thy house* <note>Deuteronomy 6:9</note>, so that a person may be complete in everything and be found complete in the commandment of his Master—a mystery for the Name, a mystery below, and for the merit of the portion of Israel.

**Rabbi Eleazar** opened and said: Two verses are found within the whole as one, a second level to them. They are of one level. One verse writes: *Thus saith the Lord of Hosts* <note>original: "Ko amar YHVH Tzevaot"</note> and one verse writes: *Thus saith the Lord God* <note>original: "Ko amar YHVH Elohim"</note>. What is the difference between this one and that one? Rather, at the time it is written *Thus saith the Lord of Hosts*, then the word comes through Mercy <term>Rachamim</term>. And at the time it is written *Thus saith the Lord God*, then the word comes through Judgment <term>Din</term>. *Thus saith the Lord of Hosts*—because this "Thus" <note>the word "Ko"</note> is blessed from the "Righteous One" <term>Yesod</term> and from "Victory" <term>Netzach</term> and "Splendor" <term>Hod</term>, which are called "Lord of Hosts"; and then the word comes with sweetness, for it comes from that place. *Thus saith the Lord God*—then this "Thus" <note>Ko</note> sucks from the side of Judgment, from the place of Supernal Might <term>Gevurah</term>. And we have learned that the matter of Judgment is within Mercy, because it is written *Lord God* <note>YHVH Elohim</note>, for *Elohim* is Might in every place, and *Lord* <note>YHVH</note> is powerful Might in every place. And because of this, the words of a person's mouth are recognized, and ultimately he intends to say a word from its place, and then the "children of faith" <note>the initiates</note> know from which place the matter hangs.

**Rabbi Abba** opened and said: *Curse ye Meroz, said the angel of the Lord...* <note>Judges 5:23</note>. Come and see: this verse is a mystery among supernal mysteries. At the time the Holy King delivers His house into the hand of the Matron <term>The Shekhinah/Divine Presence</term>, He entrusts all His weapons, spears, and vessels of service into her hand, and all His legions of war He entrusts with her. This is [the meaning of]: *Behold, it is the litter of Solomon; threescore mighty men are about it, of the mighty men of Israel...* <note>Song of Songs 3:7</note>. And here they established it: then she wages war. And those "mighty men" we mentioned are the legions of war, and they are called "expert in war." It is written: *They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera...* <note>Judges 5:20</note>. And we learned: at that hour, Israel volunteered to draw the holy sword by themselves; then this *sword that shall execute the vengeance of the covenant* <note>Leviticus 26:25</note> gathered all its host and all weapons and all those who wage war to wage war with Sisera, and the stars poured out heat from above.

And **Rabbi Shimon** said: Every single star has its own name, and they are all called by names. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: "Be ready to seek vengeance for the children of two vengeances." Here He is destined to take retribution from a single assembly—one vengeance of six hundred <insert>chariots</insert> to strengthen him for a blessing that shines, in order to bring war upon them in Israel, as it is written: *And he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt...* <note>Exodus 14:7</note>. And one vengeance of enmity forever for them until now. And because of this, they are mentioned in two places: one in water and one in fire. In water, as it is written: *The brook Kishon swept them away* <note>Judges 5:21</note>. In fire, as it is written: *The stars in their courses [fought]* <note>Judges 5:20</note>. And among those stars, there is one star that did not come to that vengeance, and it was cursed forever; for all who dwell in that place, the other stars come and swallow it and all its company, and they all perish as one. As we have seen: *Curse ye Meroz, said the angel of the Lord...* Authority is given to this angel—if it is that angel of whom it is written: *And the angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, removed...* <note>Exodus 14:19</note>. And this is the one whose wars are all in his hand.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Book of Deuteronomy, specifically the portion of Va'etchanan. The previous sections likely dealt with the nature of prayer and the soul's longing; here, the focus shifts to the cosmic mechanics of the Exile and the eventual Redemption.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Va'etchanan**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, meaning "And I besought."</note>

For they did not come to the crown of the Lord; all the appointees of His heavens flow down to awaken the Lord. Like eagles, they are all found when they prepared for war with Sisera <note>Judges 5:19</note>. And this is a King, and all the danger, and all the kings of the King when He comes. And regarding this it is said, "The Lord is King," and this is what is written: *The great, the mighty, and the awesome God* and so on <note>Deuteronomy 10:17</note>. And He spoke His statutes, a herald. And this is destined to be upon them—a spark, not for the hidden world that is coming. And through this, all the holy ones will be gathered, and through this the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to take vengeance upon the idol-worshipping nations <note>original: עכו"ם - Akum, worshippers of stars and signs</note>. And regarding this it is written: *Thus I will magnify Myself and sanctify Myself* and so on <note>Ezekiel 38:23</note>. These continue until they reach the Prophet. When he saw them, he said: "Take blood, the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> is certainly here; therefore, one must erase the goodness before the face of the Divine Presence." He opened and said: ***Behold, the day is still great*** and so on <note>Genesis 29:7</note>.

They established this verse: that when Israel awakens in repentance <note>Teshuvah</note> before the Holy One, blessed be He, the merits of the Torah will awaken the Holy Land, and they will be gathered from the Exile <note>Galuta</note>. For behold, what light will the Exile take for Israel and no more? This is what is written: *Like a thick cloud all the day long.* And if they do not gather before the heat—*Behold, the day is still great, it is not yet time for the cattle to be gathered*—all of this refers to proper deeds. They ate the fruit, one heart they sufficed, they rested and labored in the Torah to be sustained by the days of the Torah. "And go, graze" <note>Genesis 29:7</note>—to the place of rest, to the place of return and longing to be endangered, for there is no great rock of assistance. This is the "Day of Inquiry," a day of tumult and confusion from the stars. On that day, the Sanctuary was to be approached, but Israel fell into Exile. Because of evil deeds, that day was prolonged and increased. This is what is written: ***Behold, the day is still great, it is not yet time for the cattle to be gathered***—because your sins lived on that day, they sufficed in their rest.

As it was said: through what? Through the Torah. For the stars of the Torah go out, and Israel leaves the Exile. Israel struck a portion for the Torah; they spoke not entirely of kindness, and all the flocks were shamed until all the remaining days are gathered upon them. *And they rolled the stone* <note>Genesis 29:8</note>—they shall remove that harsh judgment of that day which rules over the "mouth of the well." And they were found in that well, in Exile with her. And as long as this well is revealed, that judgment does not rule over it immediately. *And we water the sheep*—at times the Holy One, blessed be He, and at times to return Israel to the Holy Land and to gather them from Exile. And these are the "End of Days" <note>Acharit ha-Yamim</note>. Like this End of Days, Israel suffered the Exile. This is what is written: *And all these things shall find you in the end of days* <note>Deuteronomy 4:30</note>. "In the end of days" is precise—and she is the Assembly of Israel <note>Knesset Yisrael</note> in Exile. And with this "End of Days," they received punishment in Exile. And so the Holy One, blessed be He, shall pass over the heights for Israel constantly. This is what is written: *Kindness is with them*, once it is for your people in the End of Days. And in every place, this is it. And the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to return her to her place. This is what is written: *And it shall come to pass in the end of days, that the mountain of the Lord's house shall be established* etc. <note>Isaiah 2:2</note>.

And this is a day from another [source], to act on the mountains of another day, just as the time to approach the Sanctuary, which is the assembly of all for the appointed time. This is what is written: *Woe unto us! For the day declines, for the shadows of evening are stretched out* <note>Jeremiah 6:4</note>. This "day" is the end of the Exile and the awakening of this [light]. Every sign is shriveled and halved, and by the greatness of the blow, a man is remembered among men. And the male of this spirit is among the heralds, as it is written: *For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow* <note>Job 8:9</note>. "For we are but of yesterday"—in the Exile, and He did not rest. And know that all our days are upon the earth, to make them fragrant, the Holy One, blessed be He, upon the earth. And his portion is finished. He who sees it, merits a portion; he who does not see it, woe to him who is present when the Master of Blessing is sought to be joined with His female <note>the feminine aspect of God, the Shekhinah</note>. All are old at the hour they couple as one. Regarding that hour it is written: ***The lion has roared, who will not fear?*** etc. <note>Amos 3:8</note>. Come and see: at first it is written that Isaac divided [the blessing] with shame and longing, and who shall go out to meet this? Then: ***The lion has roared, who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken, who can but prophesy?*** At that hour it is written: *And the Lord God shall blow the shofar...* and He strikes. Even the Holy One, blessed be He, from the Exile, and He checks to see her as she comes.

-> # Portion of Ve-hayah Eikev <-

-> ## The Faithful Shepherd <-

**And it shall come to pass** (Eikev) because you listen to these ordinances, etc. <note>Deuteronomy 7:12</note> "And you shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless the Lord your God, etc." <note>Deuteronomy 8:10</note>
**This commandment** is to bless the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: *Kudesha Brich Hu*</note> for everything that one eats and drinks and enjoys in this world. And if one does not bless, he is called a "robber" toward the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: "He who robs his father and his mother, etc." <note>Proverbs 28:24</note> And all the gatherings bless because of the blessings that a person blesses the Holy One, Blessed be He; he comes to draw life from the Source of Life to the Holy Treasury, and to cause it to rest upon the Supernal Holy Congregation, and to give to the lower [congregation]. They come to the whole world, and then "and you shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless the Lord your God" for your length [of days].

## Main Text (Zohar)

And those blessings that a person directs to those supernal realms ascend on high, and all those levels and sources are blessed; they are filled so as to shine upon all worlds and for all to be blessed as one. For this reason, a person must pray with a will of the spirit <note>Hebrew: *re'uta de-rucha*, meaning intense mental and spiritual intention</note> to bless, so that the Father and the children <note>Metaphors for the higher and lower divine emanations (Sefirot)</note> are all blessed as one. And one who blesses the Holy One, Blessed be He, and desires to rejoice, his portion is considered first among the blessings for the whole world below. For once he tastes that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is blessed from there, it is like death and sickness [departing] from the head of his portion in the world. And this we have established as it is written:
> "In every place where I cause my name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you" (Exodus 20:21).

To remember all—He shall "remember all your meal offerings" (Psalms 20:4). Once the blessings of the Holy One, Blessed be He, ascend and rest upon his head, from there they spread through the whole world with Knowledge <note>The Sefirah of Da'at</note> to bestow blessings as crowned gifts. This [blessing] is from the Field of Holy Apples <note>A Zoharic name for the Shekhinah or the community of Israel</note>, and many levels appointed over the world encounter them and serve them, proclaiming: "This is the gift that so-and-so sent to the Holy One, Blessed be He!" Until it arrives afterward from the beginning of the matter to the Righteous One <note>The Sefirah of Yesod, the cosmic channel</note>; there they ascend and awaken for a blessing to extend from above and to be filled from above, and he prepares everything—"blessings for the head of the Righteous" (Proverbs 10:6). Once that level is filled and pours out, everything comes, and from there they flow and spread below. All blessings that ascend from below—there is no gate or opening on high that does not open; all those gates pass them through and they proclaim in all those firmaments: "This is the gift of the King that so-and-so sent!" This is the completion of the gift in its proper standing. And what is it? The blessing upon which they concluded "Amen." For every blessing sealed with "Amen" is established properly. And once the blessing comes and ascends through all the levels on high, they are all ready for that which is not great <note>A reference to the humble or the lower realm</note> in order to bless the person. And all the time that this exists in the blessing of their "salting" <note>A metaphor for the refinement of speech</note>, they bless it and crown it with holy crowns through the spirit of Amen. Amen is the secret of the knots of all unity and holiness in the secret of the King. And the blessing crowns him with the crowns of the worlds properly, and the Holy One is crowned by all those who bless Him, and there is an addition in the blessing below from the Holy One, Blessed be He; the blessing ascends and returns with the "addition" <note>A play on the name Joseph/Yosef, associated with the Sefirah of Yesod</note> that is not [merely] bright but is strengthened with great strength to ascend on high. And regarding this it is written, "For those who honor Me, I will honor" (1 Samuel 2:30)—these are those who bless the Holy One, Blessed be He. Woe to those who do not bless the Holy One, Blessed be He, and bring forth from their mouths a spirit to a spirit of distress... <note>The text here warns of the spiritual consequences of neglecting blessings, which causes a lack of flow to the Shekhinah</note> ...to shine blessings from above to below when the blessing is "mingled" <note>Hebrew: *belulah*, as in a grain offering</note> through the preparation of their "salting" from below to above and from above to below. Blessings that are not mingled ascend from below to above until they reach that connection... and they ascend to be integrated on high until they reach the Supernal Throne, the source of all waters. Then they go out and search the Supernal Source; the blessings circle and circle and are integrated into one another, and these ascend into those, and they shine and descend to the "Head of the Righteous" to shine below. And when they come to be blessed—the Father and the children and all their levels. And the secret of these blessings is to be integrated from above to below in the spirit of...

---

**Blessed** (*Baruch*): This is the secret of the Supernal Source of all, to shine and to be drawn forth and to bless all the "pools" <note>The channels of divine flow</note>. And He is "Blessed" constantly, for His waters never fail. And from there is the beginning of the inquiry of the World to Come, and it is called "Holy of Holies," for it is the Supernal Holiness, as there is no holiness like this below, and it is called the World to Come. And it is called the "End of All" <note>The goal of thought</note>. "Blessed" corresponds to that which comes to shine below and to be crowned from below to above through the blessing of the "Building" <note>The structure of the Sefirot</note>. And the first "Blessed" is called thus in the secret of Supernal Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), which is integrated below, said as one thin path to be shown therein.

---

**Are You** (*Atah*): After it begins to be revealed, for "Blessed" is hidden. And because of this, the Hidden Wisdom is called "Blessed," the Supernal Source that is not to be revealed. "You" (*Atah*) is the beginning of that which is revealed outwardly, and therefore it is called *Et* <note>The Hebrew word 'Atah' contains 'Et', the marker of a direct object, often signifying the Shekhinah</note>. And who is this? This is the secret of "Where" (*Ayeka*), and he is called "Priest" (*Kohen*) in relation to that place. And the secret of this is "You are a priest forever" (Psalms 110:4)... to show from above to below. And this is the supernal presence that is below to be revealed.

---

**The Lord** (*Y-H-V-H*): [The Name] to be crowned. This is for faith on all sides.

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **And it shall come to pass, because [Ekev]** <-

To cleave to the Letter H <note>The final 'He' of the Tetragrammaton, representing the Shekhinah</note> and one must know that all His ways are beautiful. And there must be support, as we have established that **Chesed** <note>Loving-kindness</note> learns to bless alone. And on Shabbat, in everything above, one must extend the holy over the profane, whether in speech, in writing, or in garments. And all these sanctifications and preparations cause the **Evil Maidservant** <note>The Sitra Achra or "Other Side"</note> to be removed, as mentioned in the thought of the washing. According to the law. In their hearts, they add the profane to the holy. For if this is the King, this is the sword.

The **Holy Matron** <note>The Shekhinah</note>, the Kingdom of Holiness, is better for joy on Shabbat. She is crowned with the **ten Sefirot** <note>The ten divine emanations</note>. She is adorned on Shabbat with drops held in the channels. With many chariots of living beings. And with many hosts and camps, and the King goes out to meet her with many crowns, and the "Evil Son" is removed as mentioned, the Evil Maidservant according to her way, all in the void. Without the Kingdom and the window to awaken upon them for those who draw and those who tie knots to the Queen of morsels, and from the births of rain it does not descend, Heaven forbid, to the field, and the Evil Maidservant to rule on Friday nights and the needs of Wednesday nights. What did they do? They would take garments and the wise and the poor of the atonements. And they make a lamentation on Shabbat nights so as not to be found in Sodom like those covered in filth, for "God has made one opposite the other" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14</note>. After they ate and drank and the Sanctuary was blessed, it was said in the weeping of the holy covering: "How does the city sit solitary, that was full of people! She is become as a widow" <note>Lamentations 1:1</note>. And he intends that on the 9th of Av there are afflictions and sides, and they make the lamentation, sitting in mourning to be found in weeping as in distress. Because their strength is that "all the voice of our grace." The cup of blessing is removed. Spread out to groan upon the table, to sigh. An oath to scorch upon the table because the poor sit upon the table.

Support is like **washing the hands** with the "final waters" <note>Mayim Acharonim</note>. The hammer is the **Grace after Meals**. The crown is the **Cup of Blessing**, and one must be concerned for them and prepare them with the Holy Spirit that covers the crown of the Sefirot, and the table shall be for the Holy One, Blessed Be He <term>Kudsha Brich Hu</term>, the table of the Creator. And because of this, our Rabbis established "the wings." First, like the washing of the hands, for so the Rabbis of the Mishnah established: "Soiled hands are disqualified from blessing," because the Shekhinah of merit should not be pushed to the side of the stomach, to the side of the vision, when they are elevated and when they are pure, the Shekhinah of the blessing of the word does not dwell except upon purity. Just as they pushed it, for the pure one, **Chesed** dwells upon him, the holy blessing, as it is written: "It is like the precious oil upon the head..." <note>Psalms 133:2</note>. And because of this: "Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying: 'Thus you shall bless the children of Israel...'" <note>Numbers 6:23</note>. And we have established: "Every Priest who blesses is himself blessed," and he who blesses is among the blessed. And we have established the words of the Mishnah: "Any blessing that does not contain the Mention [of the Name] and Kingship is not called a blessing." Kingship certainly. And furthermore, washing of the hands—one must wash them up to the joint <note>the wrist</note> to dwell upon the joints. In that hour, the hand of the Lord is upon him, and let the hand be for a blessing from the side of **Chesed** <note>Mercy</note>, his heart is open in his right hand. And see the hand for holiness from the side of **Gevurah** <note>Strength/Judgment</note>, and it dwells in the cleansing for the hand of the image from the side below to dwell in the hand of the joints for the body... ten joints, crowns for the arms and two legs and two wings and the covenant. And three flows... the hand... hint: "May He bless you," "May He keep you," "The Lord," "The Lord," "The Lord"... these are hinted at for the King of Kings, and the awakening of the children upon them... the Palace of the Lord... and this is like a shadow in the hand to be prepared... all the document from the 3rd to the palm of Sivan... all of them require the covering of a wise man.

## And it shall come to pass, because...

-> **And it shall come to pass, because** <-
<note>original: "והיה עקב" (Ve-hayah Ekev) - Deuteronomy 7:12</note>

The Life of the Worlds is in the likeness of the letters Y-H-W <note>The first three letters of the Tetragrammaton</note>. Because of this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, needs the world to be with Him, for those who exert themselves in the matters of the Torah. **The Seventh** requirement is to be generous at the table <note>original: פתורא (ptora)</note> for the sake of the poor. Because of this, "anyone who prolongs their stay at their table, their days and years are prolonged." Because of this, death is checked and kept away from him. He performs kindness, and just as he sustains the poor, so too the Holy One, Blessed be He, sustains him. Furthermore, he brings out the hungry soul for all the poor from the lower side. So too in the time of need. And there are those who need to be blessed through it. Everything is to sanctify the days over the food. Because of this, one must be generous at the table to give life to all of them. For the "children of the table" <note>guests/dependents</note> are for the sake of the glory of He who is Blessed, to bless at the table for the sake of the poor. Because of it, He established a "gate for righteousness." The Holy One, Blessed be He, is a beautiful measure for Israel and not below in the measure of poverty, in order to establish the first ones and those below it. As we have learned: there are types of deaths that are like the rebukes of the poor. And they were delivered into the hand of Samael <term>Samael: the primary angel of severity and accuser in Jewish mysticism</term>, the collector of them all. And immediately when he strikes you, there is no praising him as a "beautiful measure" as it is said. This is because all the people and languages... when He desires and is sanctified and receives in the Kingdom <note>Malkhut</note> and in sweetness, and it ceases above for all Israel, they stand to receive as a holiness and not to be diminished. And in this measure they are appointed...

...of the poor, for even if a man has wealth, if his lap is filled with illnesses and plagues until he is called "living" only through the precision of his care, and they wake him every day—as long as he is empty of it, his table goes to another. Furthermore, there is a "poor man" who is removed from the Ancient One <note>Atika/Keter</note> because of a debt below... so too, he heals the Shekhinah <note>the Divine Presence</note> to empty the cup for the lower one who is with him, to draw down the glory of Knowledge <note>Da'at</note>. And he gathers the "thorns" in the field of the sea. Furthermore, regarding the "pity" that immediately includes the 613 commandments, it is written: *This is my name forever* <note>Exodus 3:15</note>... A righteous man with mercy. And because of this, to establish it... from the Torah and from the strikes that are hidden...

**The Eighth** requirement is the "Final Waters" <note>Mayim Acharonim: the ritual washing of fingers after a meal</note> which were established for us. The first matter: it dissolves the teeth <note>removes salt</note>, for "the salt of Sodom" <note>a dangerous salt mentioned in the Talmud</note> is found there, a deadly poison that rests on filthy hands. One cannot perform a blessing with them. And regarding the cup over which one blesses: without purity, it is called "impure." Just as a cup is rinsed inside and out to be pure for the blessing, how much more so the hands. Because of this, "Final Waters are an obligation." And the spirit above: *And you shall sanctify yourselves*—these are the First Waters <note>before the meal</note>. *And you shall be holy*—these are the Final Waters. For "Holy" refers to the fragrant oil <note>sometimes used after the meal</note> corresponding to the "Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord of Hosts." Because of this, *And you shall sanctify yourselves etc.* is to be sanctified below for the sake of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: *On this day you are to the Lord your God.*

**The Ninth** requirement is the Cup of Blessing. The masters of the Mishnah established: Ten things were said regarding the Cup of Blessing, and these are they: **Crowning, Wrapping, Rinsing, Washing, Raw (undiluted), Full, Receiving it with both hands, Lifting it a handbreadth from the ground, Placing one's eyes upon it, and Sending it as a gift to the members of one's household.** In all of these, there is a secret... Rinsing and Washing... and "Full" corresponds to Mercy <note>Hesed</note>. "Raw" <note>undiluted wine</note> is from the spear... **The Cup** <note>Hebrew: כוס (Kos)</note> according to the way of Wisdom is full... without the letter *Vav* it is like a blemish or lack... it rises to the count of "throne" <note>Gematria: Kos (86) = Elohim (86)</note>. And because of the ten things corresponding to the Ten Sefirot: **Crowning** is like the Crown <note>Atarah/Malkhut</note>, the Crown of Beauty <note>Tiferet</note>. **Wrapping**: *A prayer of the poor man when he wraps himself* <note>Psalms 102:1</note>. For all blessings and prayers involve "wrapping" until the prayer of the poor man ascends. **Rinsing and Washing** are like "purify and sanctify." Purity is from the side of Mercy <note>Hesed</note>, and Sanctity is from the left side of Strength <note>Gevurah</note>. The Cup of Blessing is the Kingdom <note>Malkhut</note>... **Raw** is from the side of the Foundation <note>Yesod</note>... **Full**... **Receiving it with both hands**: the first [hand] for Mercy, the second for Strength. **Lifting it a handbreadth from the ground** corresponds to the [letter] Yod... **Placing one's eyes upon it**: for the eyes of the Lord illuminate the pupil... and **Sending it as a gift to the members of one's household.**

# And it shall come to pass (Ekev)

The eye is the letter *Vav* <note>The sixth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often representing a connecting force</note>, the voice of the eye of which it was said: "and the taste thereof was as the taste of manna, a gift of God." A tenth is connected to the decrees of the Rabbis, for immediately "Blessed be He" and the spirit that speaks because of the pressure and the cause of your skulls... <note>This introductory section contains dense, fragmented mystical shorthand regarding the Hebrew letters and divine emanations</note>.

**Rabbi** Hezekiah opened with the verse: "Do not give..." etc. until "it is written: standing before me." As printed in the portion *Kedoshim*, page 83, side b.

**Only** in your fathers did He take delight... etc. until "you shall lodge," as it is written. As printed in the portion *Vayechi*, page 242, side b.

**For** the Lord your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords, the great God, etc. <note>Deuteronomy 10:17</note>. We have learned: "And the likeness of their faces was the face of a man" <note>Ezekiel 1:10</note>. These are the Cherubim. The Cherubim are the "great faces" and the Cherubim are the "small faces" <note>A distinction in Kabbalah between different levels of divine manifestation</note> within the secret of the "face of a man," for all forms are included within them. Because they are the great faces, engraved forms shine within them upon the <term>Ginuphi</term> <note>A canopy or ornamental border of the Divine Throne</note> which is explained as the four sides: East, West, North, and South. Michael, Raphael, and Gabriel are to the South side, etc.

And the faces look toward the **face of a man**, the **face of a lion**, the **face of an eagle**, and the **face of an ox**. "Man" is male and female, and is not called "Man" unless they are joined as one. The conclusion of the form to the left side is the **Ox**, which includes all forms. When the **Lion** is present, this is "Man" in extension, included as one—a herald of male and female. All of them learn and ride; all of them emerge from this secret here. From these forms, each one spreads to its sides as we have said. These are the ones that ascend as one and are included as one, to show that each is included in its fellow.

The **Ox**, like the **Lion** and the **Man**, is carried by the spirit of the four engraved Names that ascend to be crowned and to gaze. The **Ox** ascends to the face of the **Man**. Another canopy is crowned, engraved in a spirit of two colors, and it is "Mighty" <note>Hebrew: *Gibbor*, associated with the attribute of Judgment</note>; then it returns to its place. The Throne carves and engraves it, and it returns to be spoken of in the spirit of this canopy.

The **Eagle** ascends to shine and to gaze at the face of the **Man**. Another canopy is crowned, acting as a priest in a spirit of two faces like colors, to shine and to gaze. It ascends for crowning and it is "Great" <note>Hebrew: *Gadol*, associated with the attribute of Mercy</note>; then it returns to its place. The Throne carves and engraves it, and it returns to shine in the spirit of this canopy.

The **Lion** ascends to shine and to gaze at the face of the **Man**. Another canopy is crowned, engraved in a spirit of two faces and colors, to be strengthened and bound in its strength, and it is "Mighty"; then it returns to its place. The Throne carves and engraves it, and it returns to shine in the spirit of this canopy.

**Man** gazes at all of them, and all of them gaze at him like a collection. Then all of them are formed in their canopies in this manner, by the spirit of the one canopy that searches the power. And then it is written of them: *And the likeness of their faces was the face of a man* <note>Ezekiel 1:10</note>. All are included in this right and left; the Form includes them. And regarding this secret, He is called Holy: **The Great, The Mighty, and The Awesome God**, for they are covered and engraved above in the spirit of the supernal blue, included in the four letters of the Name **Y-H-V-H**, which is the canopy that includes all these forms. They are carved and engraved in the Throne. Then the engraving is embroidered upon them: one to the right, one to the left, one in front, and one behind, surrounding the four sides of the world. When the Throne ascends, it is marked by these four forms. Four Names support this Throne, and the Throne is included in them until it is bound and flickers. Those eyes and longings descend, full like a blue ointment that fills branches to every side, a salty vision. When it descends, those thirty forms emerge, shining in their colors, their bodies covered in their purity, flickering; and they are the "will" and the "noise" unto the world.

**Rabbi** Yose was walking on the way... etc. until "to bring." As printed in the portion *Kedoshim*, page 80, side b.

# Judges / Portion of Judges and Officers

-> **Portion of Judges and Officers** <-

-> **The Faithful Shepherd** <-

### Judges
**"Judges and officers you shall appoint for yourselves in all your gates, which the Lord your God gives you..."** <note>Deuteronomy 16:18</note>.
This commandment is to appoint judges and officers. Furthermore, "For God is the judge" <note>Psalm 75:8</note>, for the seventy <note>original: ע'</note> heavens [surrounding the world] are known to the Lord <note>original: יוד"ל, a cipher for the Tetragrammaton</note> to show that the Crown <term>Keter: the highest Sefirah, representing Divine Will</term> is above them all, for "God is the judge; He brings one down [and exalts another]."

**The commandment to judge** — After this, these are the trials <note>The text transitions into a dense mystical analysis of legal procedures</note>. Just as it is said above and below, "For Jonathan saw the kings." <note>The transcription here contains several highly cryptic or corrupted abbreviations typical of early Zohar printings</note>. Justice, justice you shall pursue. We derive two types of judgment from the mouth of the All-High above, and a pure judgment from the mouth of the All below. Through his intellect, a person becomes known... no authority is granted from below until they receive permission from above, like a knot tied to the heart. There, the pure judgment is written... the "Righteous One" <term>Tzadik: the Sefirah of Yesod, the foundation</term> is the life of the worlds, containing the living blessings of the King. "My lips shall open and my mouth [shall declare Your praise]" <note>Psalm 51:17</note>; the King is in the chamber, and the King's time is established, and beneath them are the fruits...

**To judge by strangulation** <term>Chenek: one of the four capital punishments</term> — There the Name <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> is blessed in it, and the Name is spread out to strike the face below. They shall be removed with a pole... so that the wicked one shall not be struck... forty [lashes] correspond to the upper nest and the lower nest, which are the seven... and they shall be carried on a pole... without the letter *Chet* <note>original: ח'</note> in the middle... to protect the soul...

**To judge by stoning** <term>Sekilah</term> — This is compared to the Priest <term>Kohen: representing the Sefirah of Chesed/Kindness</term> who is the Lord, the Righteous One... which are the letter *He* <note>original: ה'</note>, and it is written that the curse is the letter *Vav* <note>original: ו'</note>, and the two letters *He* are written, and he throws it... the taste of the dust...

**To judge by burning** <term>Serefah</term> — To bring the poor man to the portion of the Priest... the Shekhinah <term>The Divine Presence</term> above, which is Beauty <term>Tiferet</term>. And regarding every matter of the sacrifices... the Holy One, the Dove of the Ancient One... and he called out regarding the small one... anyone who is compassionate in the desert... the commandments are all grasped in Him, both of them, and they are established... a bush burning with fire... and all his money... to burn it... Holy to the Lord... Israel is the poor man, covered by the Torah... for the commoner... as our Sages of blessed memory said... the Tree of Life and rest... for I am with you.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion of Shoftim (Judges). It focuses on the spiritual nature of testimony and the internal "witnesses" that observe a person's conduct. It connects the legal requirements of witnesses to the anatomy of the soul and the celestial court.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Shoftim (Judges)** <-

31 | "A single witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, etc. By the mouth of two witnesses or by the mouth of three witnesses shall a matter be established." This is a **commandment** to give testimony in all matters so that one's fellow is not disqualified <note>original: *m'tufsa*, likely referring to legal standing or form</note>. If there is holiness but no testimony, the congregation is established by the mouth of two witnesses, etc. "The one who is to die shall be put to death... he shall not be put to death by the mouth of one witness." And because of this, the masters of the Mishnah established: Who testifies against a person? The walls of his house. And not only that, but the members of his household testify against him. What are the "walls of his house"? These are the walls of his heart. "And Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord" <note>Isaiah 38:2</note>—to pray from the engravings of the walls of his heart. Why? Because of the twenty-two letters <note>The 22 letters of the Hebrew alphabet, seen as the building blocks of creation</note> within him, as the masters of the Mishnah established: He planted his eyes engraved upon his bones, and thus he examines, and his intentions are engraved upon his bones. And who testifies against a person? The walls of his house—these are the bones covering the "brain" of the heart <note>The mystical center of consciousness</note>, and upon them is the voice of "Who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters" <note>Psalms 104:3</note>. "Lays the beams" (*ha-mekareh*) is the language of "walls" (*korot*). And these bones are more than the flesh, tendons, and skin, because the bones are white. And it is written of Wisdom that it is not recognized except through the white, like the white of the eye <note>A mystical comparison between the physical eye and the "eye" of wisdom</note>. Furthermore, the body is destined to rise upon the bones. Because of this, merits and visions are engraved upon his bones; if he is worthy, his soul will rise upon his bones and live. If not, he will not rise and will not merit the Resurrection of the Dead. Furthermore, there are two witnesses over a person: an eye that sees and an ear that hears. And every scribe and judge sees. And not only that, but Samael <note>The accuser/adversary</note> and Michael <note>The protector/advocate</note> are witnesses over every person, as they established: "Blow the shofar at the new moon, at the concealed time (*ba-keseh*) for our feast day" <note>Psalms 81:4</note>. On that day, there are judges, witnesses, and a voice, and the deep side <note>The forces of judgment</note> gains merit. The moon goes and is hidden... for it is said: "Do not seek out what is hidden from you." This refers to the shell (*kelipah*) that covers the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*). And in that concealment, the "End" <note>The appointed time of judgment or redemption</note> must judge. Regarding the revealed things a person does below: "He who conceals his sins will not prosper" <note>Proverbs 28:13</note>, for the Shekhinah hides the crown... The masters of the Mishnah said a person must be careful at that time. Everything is for the wicked... and the two witnesses testify to all his actions... The "plotting witness" (*Ed Zomem*)—the voice is said of him, and he is lashed... And furthermore, the "Central Pillar" <note>A Kabbalistic term for the balanced middle path of the Divine attributes</note> witnesses and examines and sees... "Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever." "By the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses shall the one who is to die be put to death"—this refers to one who is uprooted from his source... as it is written, "he shall not be put to death by the mouth of one witness," for he shall have no rising at all.

**This commandment** follows that one, corresponding to the Great Court <note>The Sanhedrin</note>, which are the "eyes" of the community, originating from the side of Strength <note>original: *Gevurah*; the Sefirah associated with judgment and discipline</note>. They are called the Levites of the Great Court who examine and judge, mirroring the pattern below. "You shall surely set a king over you" <note>Deuteronomy 17:15</note>—the word "set" <note>original: *som*</note> emerges above and "you shall set" <note>original: *tasim*</note> below. This corresponds to the Court that includes the half that the Lesser Court took upon itself. The Lesser Court is a court of three, from the side of the Lower Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note>. When it enters the company of the Levites, it becomes the Great Sanhedrin. It is said among the holy ones that there were sixty members of the Great Sanhedrin. The sum of the Court includes them all, and regarding it, it is said: "Every great matter they shall bring to you, but every small matter they themselves shall judge" <note>Exodus 18:22</note>. "The lesser light to rule the night"—and in the night, the song of my life is with me, belonging to the Levites, and it shall not depart. He who established the world prepared thirteen types of joy; blessed is the light, the lesser light, which is the Divine Presence, established from the Left side. Up to here.

## The Faithful Shepherd (Ra'aya Meheimna)

**And they shall fine** him one hundred pieces of silver, etc. This commandment is to judge the law of one who brings out an evil name <note>defamation of a bride's virginity</note>. These [hundred pieces] correspond to the "signs of virginity," to teach her... <note>The text here uses dense metaphorical language regarding the spiritual state of the soul</note> and not just any evil name. We have learned that the Torah is a stringency... the teacher of Good and Evil. It is not the way of the King and the Queen to ride upon a donkey, but rather upon His horses, as it is written: <term>The Secret of the Lord (Sod Hashem)</term> "That You ride upon Your horses, Your chariots of salvation" <note>Habakkuk 3:8</note>. It is a disgrace in the Kingdom for the Queen to ride upon a donkey; no, the King does not do this. This is the "holy donkey," the servant who was prepared to ride upon the donkey, as it is written of the Messiah: "Humble, and riding [upon a donkey]" <note>Zechariah 9:9</note>.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Torah portion Ki Tisa, specifically addressing the spiritual hierarchy of the Sefirot and the cosmic struggle between the holy nation of Israel and the "Mixed Multitude" (Erev Rav). ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Ki Tisa**<-
<note>Exodus 30:12, "When you take [the census]"</note>

When the merits and virtues ascend, and when their image is refined below, the worthy ones ascend with them. The masters of the Mishnah <note>The sages of oral tradition</note> have established that they are many, and their greatness is vast. But concerning those whose likeness is like a cursed donkey lying with any beast, they are the fools below, from the side of impurity, who are guilty before the King. The masters of the Mishnah established this: regarding a living human being, he shall be like a living creature <note>original: *chayah*</note>, and through the moisture of the Torah, they shall be nursed and drawn out. And "living" belongs to the Lord. There is no other side among these who open the gates for the living creatures.

And they tremble like red ones from the side of the Holy Indignation, which is not included in the **Ten Sefirot** <term>The ten divine emanations or attributes through which the Infinite interacts with the world</term> for the one who inherits it and merits it. It is sufficient to guard the Sefirot so that they do not spread to ten or nine. For if they were to diminish the unified Kingdom <note>Malchut</note>, the nine would be left in a state of separation. Therefore, the Master of the *Book of Formation* <note>Sefer Yetzirah</note> established: "Ten and not nine." And if you say that it ascends above ten, more than ten, it is not so. For that which is honored as a throne does not ascend above ten. And because of this, it is the secret of all things that were before.

The palm-breadth of the **Matronita** <term>The Matron/Queen, a title for the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</term> is included in the mystery of the flesh of the "Other Side." **Samael** <note>The primary archangel of the "Other Side" or evil</note> was prepared to seize the daughter of the King. But the Kingdom <note>Malchut</note> is not merited by one who is not worthy of the King's throne. He shall be called **"Israel is My firstborn son"** from the side of the Father. He is called the "Vision of Israel" because the Holy One, Blessed be He, is Kindness <note>Chesed</note>... and the Kingdom belongs to the Bride. One must receive the Kingdom in spirit, for the Kingdom of the angels is in spirit. The throne of the Matronita is surrounded by judgments, and she is the image of Her Might <note>Gevurah</note>.

Is it possible to be included among the images of the world? Every kingdom that belongs to the Holy One, Blessed be He, is said to be thus: "I am the Lord, that is My name; and My glory I will not give to another, nor My praise to graven images" <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>. This refers to those who profane the Sabbaths and the festivals, and those who distress the Son of the King <note>Israel</note>. They fulfill the Torah with coldness and without love, doing everything only to receive a reward. They are like those who push away the Mezuzah to follow the desires of the world. It is said: "Honor your father and your mother." "Your father" is the Holy One, Blessed be He, and "your mother" is the **Shekhinah** <term>The Divine Presence dwelling among humanity</term>.

And despite all this, whoever profanes himself in the evening of the world with impurity, it is as if he profanes his own Matronita. They went down to attach themselves to them and did their will. Therefore, idols and foreign worship will be removed, and He will strike them from the world. But the Holy One, Blessed be He, will remove them from the world, as it is written: **"I will remove the spirit of impurity from the land"** <note>Zechariah 13:2</note>.

Because there is no one in His image, all the masters of the Mishnah must support your words: **"O God, do not keep silent"** <note>Psalm 83:2</note>.

## Main Text (Zohar)

And their youth belonged to the Lord, and all their distress was for this reason; therefore, one must give to gladden those below before [the blessing] arrives. For everything that is established for the Holy One, blessed be He, is not His own <note>meaning, the physical sacrifice is for the sake of the lower worlds</note>, as it is written: *and he shall drink the blood of the slain* <note>Numbers 23:24</note>, but before Him, it does not say "His fat," but rather *he drank the wine* alone. Because of this, they are not fit to be alone except in the body and the commandment. And one who does not sleep [on a debt] is examined, and regarding this, he shall be "expert" (*baki*) in his house. "Expert" does not mean he should toil in worldly matters specifically, but rather have the will to gladden Him. "Expert" implies: expert toward the poor, and regarding calculations and cycles. Expert so that he does not bring forth pressure to strike his sacrifice, lest a blemish be found above and below, so that the Holy One may be stirred above. These are the holy people whose King is holy within them, and they all find mercy in this world and merit the World to Come.

**On his day** you shall give him his wage, etc. <note>Deuteronomy 24:15</note>. The Faithful Shepherd <note>A title for Moses in the Zohar</note> opened: This commandment is to give the wage of a hired worker on his day. Regarding this, "on his day you shall give his wage and the sun shall not set upon him." Masters of the Academy, above and below, hear! Metatron <note>The supreme angel/heavenly scribe</note>, these are the "wages of the hired worker"—what are they? The worlds go to receive from him the living blessings of the exile every day, three times. And because of this, "on his day you shall give his wage"—this refers to the final exile.
