If a servant finishes his day, the blessings are nullified, "for he is poor"—this certainly refers to the *Tzaddik* <note>The Righteous One, a mystical grade of the Divine</note> in exile; he has nothing of his own except what they give him in exile. And because of this, "A prayer of the poor man." *A prayer of the poor man when he is faint* <note>Psalm 102:1</note>—wrapped in the *Tzitzit* <note>ritual fringes</note>, his prayer is established. And these were "gnawing at his money"—this is the Evening Prayer, which is darkness. And the Garden of Mountains is for the daily sacrifices, and they are for the sake of the "individual grape," the "severed branch," and the "corner of your field" <note>agricultural gifts for the poor</note> which are left for the morrow... they hold back the punishment. *For the poor and the stranger you shall leave them* <note>Leviticus 19:10</note>—this refers to the Middle Pillar <note>the central balance of the Sephirot</note> when the Hidden Lamp ascends. As it is written: *I have been a stranger in a foreign land* <note>Exodus 2:22</note>... in the fourth exile, in foreignness.

And if the Masters of the Academy and the Faithful Shepherd were to fulfill this commandment in the Land of Israel or not? Children, to stir mercy upon those who are purified... the flow to draw near... their nakedness is the source of the world, and their children come to this world... like a shofar blast... he does not go out for immersion... so it is for him below, the Lord strikes the man. Just as the repair of mercy is in the action of his word... the World to Come... and all that is the Crown in this world until the completion of days... to repair and to enjoy it until it returns to its source. And one who returns in repentance is like one who returns to receive, and his Indwelling Presence (*Shekhinah*) is repaired. And this is the spirit of redemption, which is placed in the voice. Hear! The Masters of the Academy, of the Upper and Lower Academies, said: Faithful Shepherd, indeed the dew of the Master of the World has clarified, and all are the portion that the Penitent merits... songs for Israel, and the glory returns to the Holy One, blessed be He, and His *Shekhinah* to draw near above and below. And because of you, Israel shall be redeemed and [suffering] shall depart... and there is no power to fly to redeem Israel except through you. And because of you, mercies are made... these are the precious ones of whom it was said: *In the Sanctuary...*

And in the middle, like a servant who asks for a gift from his master. And at the end, like a servant who takes a gift from his master and it is pleasing to him. And because of this, a servant of the throne... mercy... the Holy One, blessed be He, and Metatron ascended... because of poverty, mercy is greater for the Prophet... perhaps the law will not be to go... that is to say, perhaps the exile does not desire to go to the Crown. Of the servant it is said: *He will not be corrected by words* <note>Proverbs 29:19</note>, but rather they strike and cut from him many sections and collections. But my Rock is the **King’s Daughter** <term>Barta de-Malka: a title for the Shekhinah/Malchut</term>. And because you struck her with a blow, death was decreed upon you. ## Main Text (Zohar)

For all three sides are directed toward the letter *He* [the Shechinah] and enter into the *He*. And if you say we require the teaching of "Now this was the custom in former times in Israel concerning redeeming" <note>Ruth 4:7</note> (see Zohar on Ruth, page 70a) "and concerning exchanging, to confirm all things"—all of this hints at the merit of the Name. They did not perform all these acts—"this was the custom in former times in Israel"—merely for the merit of a physical place, but to prepare a place for His glory, to sanctify His hands for Him, for He has no need for a physical location. It refers to the change in the actions of God, for He has no change. The unity of both is found in the Bride [the Shechinah]. "And this was the testimony in Israel"—regarding the "testimony," it is said that "testimony" stated plainly refers to Him alone; He is the "plain" or "hidden" one upon whom the world stands, which is concealed, and the "earth" [the Shechinah] refers to the "Exchange," the Lower Presence. Within them, He comes to the <term>Matronita</term> <note>The Divine Matron or Queen; a title for the Shechinah</note> in her world through <term>Metatron</term> <note>The highest Archangel, often acting as the intermediary between the divine and physical realms</note>, and she dwells there as a Tabernacle and a throne, as it is said of <term>Tiferet</term> <note>The Sefirah of Beauty/Harmony, associated with the "King"</note>: "A man to dwell in a house" <note>Isaiah 44:13</note>, the Tabernacle of His face and His praise.

And because of this, the masters of the Mishnah established: not according to the written form, but according to the reading. In this world, the written form denotes Unity, but the reading denotes "God" [Elohim]. For is it not written, "I am the Lord, I do not change" <note>Malachi 3:6; original: *Ani Hashem lo shaniti*</note>? In the writing, I do not change; in the reading, I change. For the writing, which represents the mysteries, does not change; but in the reading, which is external to others, it changes. "Behold, I send an angel... pay heed to him and obey his voice; do not rebel against him" <note>Exodus 23:21</note>. Because his name is hinted at in the name of the <term>Matronita</term>, and the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> changes within him, because he is a "Youth" <note>A title for Metatron</note>, and in him is hinted the secret of the "days of youth."

But the Shechinah, in all her Name, does not change, and the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> in relation to her does not change. Everything is "I am the Lord, I do not change." For in the Shechinah, the Lord is the Central Pillar; the letter *Aleph* is not found in this world. Everything follows the General Rule; He is with the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, and therefore regarding the Shechinah, every opening is like this—from the fruit, He is the body for the dwelling, and the <term>Kingdom</term> [Malchut] is the body for the Shechinah, which is the "walking."

->**And he shall draw near**<-
> "My sister-in-law refuses to perform the levirate marriage for me in the presence of the elders... and she shall remove his shoe from his foot..." <note>Deuteronomy 25:9, describing the ceremony of Halitzah where a widow is released from the obligation to marry her deceased husband's brother</note>

You shall see this commandment: and this is the movement of the spirit from the body of the children of love with Him, in the name and the commandment of the incense. Their spirit goes with their Father, shining from the source, and the testimony of the spirit goes so far. And as long as it goes, the "iron" [the harsh forces] burns them. Woe to the one who is not wise enough to redeem Him!

And he, and the Rabbis, and the masters of the Mishnah—everything hints to them: "A prisoner cannot free himself from the prison house" <note>Talmudic maxim</note>. He is bound by the knot of the <term>Tefillin</term> <note>Phylacteries worn during prayer</note>. To bind the <term>Tefillin</term> of the head—if he has no way to redeem Him from the side above through the commandment of incense, and he is bound so that he cannot redeem himself, for he is "himself"—except through the "musical notes of the Torah" <note>Ta'amei HaMikra</note> which call to him regarding the "skull" of the <term>Tefillin</term> of the head. Rather, they strive in Torah for their own lack, in shame. Regarding <term>deeds of loving-kindness</term>, they did not establish it correctly, for "there is no 'pious one' [Chassid] except one who acts with kindness [Mitchased] toward his Creator" <note>A Zoharic principle</note>. Whoever performs kindness with your Creator, performs it with His Shechinah. For among all of Israel, it is difficult; he wants to say to them: "The Mother [the Shechinah] was weakened because of you, because you went out to evil culture." What does the King do? He leaves the King's palace and the <term>Matronita</term>. And He is merciful, but He calls the holy ones to return the <term>Matronita</term> to her place. And whoever returns in repentance and performs kindness with the Shechinah and with all the Torah and its commandments—and his intent is only to redeem the Shechinah—this person performs kindness with his Creator, and it is as if he redeemed Him, His Shechinah, and His children.

The <term>Faithful Shepherd</term> <note>Ra'aya Meheimna; usually identified as the soul of Moses</note> said: He is a wise man, the person who turns away from the world and the <term>Matronita</term> to your striving toward the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>. Not like a gift-giver who performs kindness with his Creator, but like a son who joins himself to his own pair and his own rectification to redeem his Father. And he hands himself over to death for Him. And the "holiness of Man" for them is the King's son. A servant is not with the Queen, but the <term>Matronita</term> stands in pain to be strengthened by the one who performs kindness with his Creator.

The <term>Faithful Shepherd</term> stood and joined himself before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> and wept. Therefore, he chastised his will to be like a son whose deeds are for the sake of the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> and His Shechinah. They should be to him like a son striving for them out of love and mercy—mercy greater than for his own body, his soul, his spirit, and all the worlds. He considers them as nothing in order to act...

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Metatron <note>The supreme angel and heavenly scribe</note> is the angel of the King of the worlds, acting as the patron of life through the divine name *Shaddai* <note>Almighty</note>, which corresponds to the foundation <term>Yesod: the ninth Sephirah, representing the generative and grounding force</term>. For this reason, he acts to benefit the heavens, and his heart is full of merits. He grants the reward of prayer from the foundation to the body and the covenant. They are joined together to provide life to the Central Column <term>Tiferet: the balance between mercy and severity</term> and the Righteous One <note>the Tzadik</note>, just like the Head-Tefillin <note>phylacteries</note> which draw life from Understanding <term>Binah: the third Sephirah, the Divine Mother</term>. These are placed upon the Tefillin of the King, who gives life to the Kingdom <term>Malchut: the tenth Sephirah, representing the physical world and the Shekhinah</term. The Kingdom is the Tefillin of King David, modeled after the life of Understanding. Metatron serves the Matron <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> in the world of her house. The Head-Tefillin of Metatron correspond to his Hand-Tefillin, as we have learned.

And he was like wine in his strength upon the Throne of Glory, the high dominion over every patron of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. Through the incense of the Tefillin, the excess of evil is bound, and the preciousness of the good is warmed, like the action of a mother-in-law <note>original: "chamot"</note> filled with zeal for the Matron. This occurs through the voice of prayer and the sound of the Shofar. However, this sound is hidden; it is not merely the sound of the Shofar, but the voice of the Central Column, whose mouth includes fire, wind, and water. These three correspond to the letters *Heh-Vav-Heh* <note>parts of the Tetragrammaton</note> written between them. In every place, the *Heh* rules over the *Yod*... <note>The text here uses complex letter permutations to describe the flow of divine energy</note>.

The *Vav* is the sign of Jacob, and this is the secret of the Spirit of the Scribe <note>Metatron</note> and the Shekhinah. From the Scribe and the Scribal Arts <note>Sefirot</note>, the vowel points *Kamatz*, *Kof*, and *Ketz* are clothed in the end of the letters *Heh*, *Yod*, and *Vav*. All letters come to be in dominion, beloved and beautified. The *Teruah* <note>the broken Shofar blast</note> completes the life-force. These are like the arrangements of the scribes... and the voice sings over the divisions or over the gathering. This is the sign of the sending away <note>referring to the "Sending of the Nest" commandment in Ki Tetze</note>, where they are redeemed from many dispersions in exile.

What do the people of Israel do? They bring baskets for the splendor of the life of the Shekhinah in their walk, binding her with the incense of the Tefillin. Every station of the High Priest is for her sake... "Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One" <note>The Shema prayer</note>. This is the voice that reaches Simeon. There are fifty gates <note>of Understanding</note> tied to it. Everything is sealed with the seal of life, just as it is on the Festivals. Sometimes for Passover, sometimes for the weeks of Sukkot. On the seventh day, you take the Lulav, the Etrog, three Myrtle branches, and two Willow branches <term>The Four Species: used on the holiday of Sukkot to represent different types of people and divine attributes</term>.

The four species represent the secret of the right hand... the seven days of Passover, the eight days of Sukkot, and the seven days of the Lulav, which are complete with the Myrtles and Willows. All of these are the "Bride." This is the mystery of *Shaddai* as a dwelling place. We are blessed to recite the Hallel <note>psalms of praise</note> over them, to praise the "Skull" <note>Keter, the highest crown</note>. See, his hands and arms are grasped in the thought of the four species forever, as it is written:

> I said, I will climb the palm tree (Song of Songs 7:9)

The branches rise for the *Teruah* blast—the Willow, the Lulav, and the thought of the heart. This corresponds to the thirty-two paths of wisdom. One must take the Lulav and engage in the study of the Torah. The seven correspond to the hand of the High Priest, with the sound of the Shofar and the scribal arts established above. The Shekhinah, the hand of royalty, is Metatron... Metatron is for the prophets, hearing the Torah from the side of the Central Column. The numerical value rises to forty-five, corresponding to the name of God <note>the name Mah: Yod-Heh-Aleph-Heh</note>.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the transition of leadership from Moses to Joshua. It focuses on the symbolic shift from the "Sun" (Moses) to the "Moon" (Joshua) and the role of the "Right Arm" (Aaron/Chesed) in protecting Israel.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Holy males <note>referring to the righteous or the patriarchs</note> are those with whom, as it were, the Divine Presence descends to dwell in this time when the Sanctuary was found in their midst. He desired to establish them in the likeness of the Supernal realm, and He revealed to them the reason: that the glory of His Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence</note> goes before them. This is what is written:

> **"And the Lord went before them by day"** (Exodus 13:21)

There are three holy periods corresponding to their days, and who are they? Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. In their merit, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave them supernal gifts. It has been stated that all the days of Aaron, the Glory <note>the protective clouds of glory</note> did not depart from Israel. This was established because Aaron is the "Right Arm" <term>Chesed: the Sefirah of Loving-kindness</term> of Israel. This is what is written:

> **"And the Canaanite, the king of Arad... heard that Israel came by the way of the Atharim..."** (Numbers 21:1)

This is like a person who walks without an arm and must lean his body on every place. Then, **"he fought against Israel, and took some of them prisoner"** (ibid.), because they were without the Right Arm <note>Aaron had died, removing the protective merit of Chesed</note>. Because of this, Israel needed to vow a vow, as it is written:

> **"And Israel vowed a vow unto the Lord, and said: 'If You will indeed deliver...'"** (Numbers 21:2)

Come and see: Aaron was the Right Arm of the body. Therefore it is written: **"Who caused His glorious arm to go at the right hand of Moses"** (Isaiah 63:12). And what is the "lap" of Aaron? "And Moses went" <note>referring to the parashah title, Vayelech</note>—my brother, he "went" <note>meaning he passed away</note>, for he walked but did not "go" <note>a mystical distinction in movement</note> like a body without an arm. All of them **"are gone without strength before the pursuer"** (Lamentations 1:6), for their Right Arm died and the body sought to depart. All the days of Moses, he shone upon the world. All the days of Moses, Israel ate "bread from heaven" <note>Manna</note>. Once Joshua descended <note>took leadership</note>, what is written?

> **"And the manna ceased on the morrow... neither had the children of Israel manna any more; but they did eat of the fruit of the land of Canaan"** (Joshua 5:12)

What is the difference between this and that? This [Manna] is from above, and that [fruit] is from below. From here we learn: wherever Moses is found, the "Body of the Sun" <note>The Sefirah of Tiferet</note> rises and shines upon the world. Once Moses departed, the Body of the Sun was gathered in, and the "Body of the Moon" <note>The Sefirah of Malchut, represented by Joshua</note> emerged. It is written: **"If Your presence go not with me, carry us not up hence"** (Exodus 33:15). We have learned: when the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses, **"Behold, My angel shall go before thee"** (Exodus 32:34), Moses said: "If the 'Sun-Lens' <note>The clear prophecy of Moses</note> is to be gathered in and the 'Moon-Body' <note>The reflected prophecy of Joshua/the Angel</note> is to lead, I do not want it." **"If Your presence go not"**—I desire the Body of the Sun. Then the Body of the Sun shone, and Moses was made in the likeness of the Body of the Sun before Israel. Once Moses was gathered in, the Sun was gathered in and the Moon shone; Joshua then made use of the "Moon of the Moon." Woe to that shame! <note>A reference to the diminished light of prophecy after Moses</note>

->**And he said**<-

**"I am a hundred and twenty years old this day..."** (Deuteronomy 31:2). This is what Rabbi Eleazar said: for forty years the Sun commanded the lesser [the Moon], and it was gathered in at the end of forty years, and the Moon shone. Rabbi Simeon said: this is what is written, "And he was like Moses without judgment" <note>referring to a soul transition</note>. The companions have awakened this discussion, and we shall establish the verse. Alas for what the companions have awakened! It is all necessary for the world to reveal this: that the West <note>the Shekhinah</note> gathers a man in before his days have arrived. Come and see: all spirits that go out from above go out as male and female and are then separated. Sometimes the female soul goes out before the male soul, who is her partner. If the time of the male has not yet arrived to join as one with his female, he comes down and is gathered into that [state]. When the time arrives for the union to stand, when Justice <note>Tzedek/Malchut</note> is aroused in the world to punish the sins of the world, He gathers in this "branch" that was written in the soul, and another comes and takes her. Regarding this, cases come before the Holy One, Blessed be He. All this is because the master of the male [soul] and his deeds—come and see—if his heart did not stray in his deeds, he is gathered in at that time before his days are reached so that he does not eat [suffer]. So it was with Moses, and of him it is written: "And he was like Moses without judgment." It is a tempest, for in Justice is the wisdom, because the time of another has arrived, as it is written: **"it was broken to pieces together"** (Daniel 2:35). Rabbi Eleazar said to him: "And why does the Holy One, Blessed be He, separate them and let another come and give to him?" He replied: "This is for the benefit of the man and the merit He performs for him, so that he does not reach [that time] below like the other." Come and see this...

# Vayelech
## Page 284

It is not like the actions of Aaron; even though that place where he was created was cursed, he did not resemble another from the beginning. 
Come and see: the kingdom of Saul was a kingdom that was a structure that had not yet arrived <note>referring to the temporary nature of Saul's kingship compared to the eternal Davidic line</note>. And since David was her soulmate—for the kingdom belonged to David—Saul did not rest. And when he left him, once the time arrived for David to inherit his own, then the Upper Kingdom was awakened and gathered Saul to his ancestors. The vessels of the generation were transformed and became subordinate to David, and he took what was his and it was revealed to him. For this reason, no kingdom stood or will stand except with an eye toward the Sabbath. <term>The Holy One, blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> was with him, gathering him into the kingdom so that his servant would not see himself ruling over him, but rather taking what was his as at first.
So it is seen; because of this, a person must seek mercy before <term>the Holy One, blessed be He</term> so that when he is joined to Him, he may be purified from his previous staff <note>or "tribe/inclination"</note>. It is written: *And the Lord said to me, "Let it suffice you; speak no more to Me of this matter"* <note>Deuteronomy 3:26</note>. And we have established this: 
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: "Why do you seek another <insert>variant: for wisdom</insert> world that has been dead from the day it was decreed upon it to say, *Behold, your days approach [to die]*? You shall not know the Moon <note>Joshua/Malkhut</note> from the side of the dead that stands." Rather, *Behold, your days approach to die; call Joshua* <note>Deuteronomy 31:14</note>. The Sun <note>Moses</note> shall be gathered in, and the <term>Moon</term> <note>original: "Sihara," referring to Joshua's leadership</note> shall shine. And not only that, but if you were to enter the Land, the Moon would be gathered in before you and would not rule; your authority would push aside the authority of the Moon, and it would not be seen as long as you remain in the world.

**Call** *Joshua... and present yourselves in the Tent of Meeting, that I may commission him* <note>Deuteronomy 31:14</note>—together with your <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>the Divine Presence</note>. *And this people will rise up...* <note>Deuteronomy 31:16</note>. And behold, it is included that the Holy One commanded Joshua, but rather to bring him to dwell. 
All these things that are written: *And they will forsake Me and break My covenant... and My anger shall be kindled against them on that day... Now therefore, write this song for yourselves and teach it to the children of Israel; put it in their mouths* <note>Deuteronomy 31:16-19</note>. And which one is it? It is "Ha'azinu" <note>the Song of Moses in Deut. 32</note>. Rather, the verse says: 
The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "With your <term>Shekhinah</term>." He said to him before he came: "Even though you are gathered in with your Shekhinah, for you stand to constantly illuminate the Moon just as the Sun—even though it is gathered in <note>sets</note>, it is only gathered in to illuminate the Moon." And by this, the Moon is covered when it is gathered. And regarding this: *Behold, you are about to sleep*—to illuminate. And this is: *And they will forsake Me.* And by this, Joshua is bound to illuminate. And regarding this it is written: *Behold, you are about to sleep with your fathers* <note>Deuteronomy 31:16</note>... and for Joshua to illuminate.

**And He commissioned** *Joshua... for you shall bring* <note>Deuteronomy 31:23</note>—and not "you shall come." What is the difference between this and that? One "you shall come" is to bring him news that he will enter the Land and endure in it. And one "you shall come" is to bring him news of the authority over Israel. And he was girded for the endurance of himself, and he was girded for the authority over Israel. 
**Rabbi [Simeon]** opened: *From the wing of the earth we have heard songs, "Glory to the Righteous One"* <note>Isaiah 24:16</note>. Woe to the children of men who do not notice and do not look upon the glory of their Master! They do not look upon the Supernal Holiness to be sanctified in this world, so as to be holy in the World to Come. 
"From the wing of the earth"—this is the holy <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael," the community of souls/Shekhinah</note>. "We have heard songs"—all those many songs in the night; the songs of praise of the Assembly of Israel before <term>the Holy One, blessed be He</term> in the exile <note>original: "Galuta"</note>. This is like a canopy <insert>variant: to be united with the Shekhinah</insert> and a merit to praise the Holy One, blessed be He. This is like that <term>Union</term> <note>original: "Izduvaga," the mystical coupling of divine attributes</note>, and He delights with the righteous in the Garden of Eden from <term>midnight</term> <note>original: "Palgut Leilya"</term> onwards. And then there are songs in the night, praises and songs, all of which you shall not finish. And it is written: *And who is broken and passed away?* To uproot their tunnels, all those powerful ones. For when night enters, many terrifying ones and hidden troops are found in the world, and they go and wander through the world to prosecute. From midnight onwards, a single spirit is awakened and uproots all of them from their tunnels and removes them so they shall not rule. "We have heard songs"—the praises of the Assembly of Israel in the night. And for what reason? "Glory <term>to the Righteous One</term>" <note>original: "La-Tzaddik," referring to the divine attribute of Yesod</note>—to be united in a single union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and be sanctified.

Rather, this is the spirit of the matter: from the side <note>original: *mi-sitra*</note> of himself he did not say this, but rather to Israel. "This song," and "now the song." And because of this, he said "Song," because the words are known as one, so that there should be a place for them, as it is written:
> **"And now, this song shall be before him"** <note>Deuteronomy 31:19</note>
And why? Because it is written: "For I know his inclination," and it is written: "For I know that after my death," etc. And when you do this, "And now this song shall be before him forever." Come and see, it is written: "They shall answer His name," they answered and no more; their portion is established for Him in this place, to be fixed for whoever is fixed. It is written:
> **"And David spoke to the Lord the words of this song"** <note>2 Samuel 22:1</note>
The opening of David's praise was because he said the song from below to above, and he merited this. And he did not say this except at the end of his days, for he was more clothed than this, as it is written: "Do not believe in yourself until the day of your death" <note>Ethics of the Fathers 2:4</note>. And he merited to see, and David merited to say the song from below to above at the end of his days, which was a gathering from all his sides, as it is written: "On the day that the Lord delivered him from the hand of all his enemies." A person's song is the most excellent of all; it is alive, as we have learned in the spirit of our Mishnah, in words and in action. So it is from below to above and from above to below, and afterwards to gather as one and to tie everything into one knot. From here it is implied, as it is written first:
> **"When I call out the name of the Lord"** <note>Deuteronomy 32:3</note>
How is the calling out? As it is written: "And He called to Moses"—this is the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence</note>.
> **"Ascribe greatness to our God"** <note>Deuteronomy 32:3</note>
This is the **Supernal King**. Afterwards, he descends through his degrees until here below, as it is written:
> **"He is righteous and upright"** <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>
Afterwards, he ties the **Knot of Faith** <note>original: *kitra de-meimanuta*; the unification of the Divine attributes</note> and says "He," and this is the knot of everything. Because of this, a person needs to order the praise of his Master in this manner: from below to above, to raise the glory of his Master to the place that is commanded, the depth of all that moves and goes out. And afterwards, it flows to be found from above to below, from that hidden depth to every single degree, until the final degree, so that blessings are found for all from above to below. Afterwards, he needs to tie the knot like the whole, the Knot of Faith, and this is when he honors the name of his Holy Master. And regarding this, it is written:
> **"For those who honor Me, I will honor"** <note>1 Samuel 2:30</note>
"For those who honor Me"—this is above. "I will honor"—in the world to come.
> **"And those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed"** <note>1 Samuel 2:30</note>
How are those who despise Me lightly esteemed? This is one who does not know how to unify the Holy Name and to tie the Knot of Faith, so that blessings may be found in the place where they are needed, and to honor the name of his Master. It is possible that for one who does not know how to honor the name of his Master, it would have been better for him not to have been created. Rabbi Judah said: "And those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed"—this is one who does not know how to honor his Master, nor to focus on those words: "Greater is the one who answers **Amen** than the one who blesses" <note>Talmud Berakhot 53b</note>. And we have established this before Rabbi Shimon: that "Amen" draws blessings to the King, and from the King to the Matronita, which is the **Assembly of Israel** <note>original: *Knesset Yisrael*</note>. And all of them are drawn; Rabbi Eleazar teaches them and learns from them. Once the blessings reach you, from there they move and go out.

# And He Went (Vayelech)

And blessings go forth above and below, and everything is sweetened. A humble voice prepares the pure arrangements that bring forth so-and-so, the servant of the Holy King. When one arranges [prayer] below, they must arrange the conclusion with "Amen" and direct their intention toward everything as is required. How many great gates are opened for him above! How many good things are found within those worlds! What joy! Everything strikes a note of joy for this member of Israel who causes joy. Let there be joy in this world and in the world to come. In this world, at the time they rise to guard him—and from where do we know that his prayer stands before their Master? A voice proclaims in all the worlds: "Open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faithfulness may enter" <note>Isaiah 26:2</note>. Do not read "faithfulness" (*emunim*), but rather "Amens" (*amenim*). Open the gates! Just as the gates and blessings are opened for them, so "Open the gates" that their prayers may be accepted. Happy are those who merit them in life in this world and in the world to come. Happy are their companions! For when a person departs from this world, if he was a "shomer" <note>literally "guard" or "observer"</note> who concluded with "Amen," he is called a "shomer"—meaning he guarded that blessing which the one blessing said, and he waited for it to conclude with "Amen" as is required in its proper measure. It ascends, and they proclaim before him: "Open the gates before him!" Just as he was joyful and opened gates every day when he was a "keeper of faithfulness."

Rabbi Yose said: Rabbi Yehuda [taught] "Happy is the one who says Amen." Rabbi Abba said: Behold, they have already established it; everything is called "Amen." It is the vessel that contains everything; it is called "Amen," as it is written: "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from world to world" <note>Psalms 106:48</note>. For all of them, all <margin>Another version: the shadow</margin> that is contained and goes forth is called "Amen." For we have learned: "From world to world"—a world above and a world below. The law of all is "Amen and Amen." It gazes above and it gazes below.

And finally, we have established "Amen" as the life of the letters. This one said: It stands in place of the deep male principle, where all blessings are gathered, go forth, and are found. An **Open Mem** (מ) is like the vessel that contains and brings forth, and it is called "Mem." And that is the secret we learned: an **Open Mem** and a **Closed Mem** (ם), as we established regarding the verse "For the increase of the realm" <note>Isaiah 9:6 - This verse is famous in Kabbalah because it contains a closed Mem in the middle of a word, which is grammatically irregular</note>. For example, the "straight" form is the totality of two "Khaf"s; a "bent" Khaf (כ) is the totality of life and death, the totality of a bent Khaf <margin>Another version: an Open Mem is the totality</margin> of two "Khaf"s—a straight Khaf (ך) and a bent Khaf (כ). A straight Khaf is the totality of life and death. Because of this, the whole is called "Life" and "End," and all of them are in the Mishnah thus: Three Vavs (ו)—the male; a straight Vav is the totality of male and female; a bent Khaf is the totality of that which is straight.

And in the book of Rav Hamnuna the Elder: The "Mem" here is a <term>notarikon</term> <note>an ancient system of shorthand or acronyms where letters of a word represent other words</note> for "King" (*Melekh*), and that is "Amen." "Amen" is a <term>notarikon</term> for **God, Faithful King** <note>original: "El Melekh Ne'eman"</note>. This is the totality of everything, and it is beautiful.

And it is said regarding the conclusion: anyone who hears a blessing from the mouth of the one blessing and does not intend "Amen" upon it—that is to say, to intend and let the voice complete it—all the priests [above] turn away from him. And at the time he needs it, his deeds strike him. Just as he did not open blessings above, so they do not open for him. And not only that, but when he departs from this world, they proclaim before him: "Turn away! Shut the gates before so-and-so! Let him not enter, and do not accept him!" Woe to him, woe to his soul!

Regarding the conclusion: the wicked of Gehenna <note>the place of spiritual purification or punishment</note> all ascend in known dwellings. And how many gates does Gehenna have? They are all open corresponding to the gates of the Garden of Eden. And at the time they go forth to the life of the wicked who receive their deeds, those gates are open and they lead <margin>Another version: and they ascend</margin> them outside. And all the gates are named and investigated corresponding to the gates of the Garden of Eden. And each and every gate is called a "name" corresponding to that gate of Gehenna. And the gates are recognized corresponding to them—those are the gates of the Garden of Eden.

In Gehenna, there is a dwelling at the very bottom of everything. And that dwelling is a dwelling upon a dwelling, and it is called "The Land of Gloom" (*Eifatah*). What is *Eifatah*? It is like the other thing: "It shall be square, doubled" <note>Exodus 28:16</note>, which we translate [into Aramaic] as "square and doubled" (*ka'if*). Here, *Eifatah* means "doubled." And that is called the "Lowest Depths" (*Sheol Tachtit*). *Sheol* is one dwelling; *Tachtit* is the bottom-most dwelling. And in the scripture, it is called "The Land of Gloom, the Lowest," and it is called "Destruction" (*Abaddon*). And it is written: "Sheol and Abaddon." And all the dwellings are not doubled, and all are not "gloomy" (*eifin*) except for this one. And at the conclusion, the windows that diminish toward Destruction are called—

<meta>This page concludes the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Vayelech and begins the portion of Ha’azinu. It continues the Zoharic exploration of the soul's descent and the power of sacred song to unify the divine realms.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

That which is called the "lowest depths" <note>Hebrew: *Sheol Tachtit*</note> never ascends. Regarding that place, it is said that those who are sealed there are cut off from all worlds; destruction reigns in that place, and forces of judgment are built there. They are left to be consumed by that which they did not value—the spiritual nourishment of their children—and they remain in that lower dwelling which has no opening, remaining in darkness and never ascending. Concerning this, it is written:
> As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave <note>original: *Sheol*</note> shall come up no more. <note>Job 7:9</note>

Yet, is it not also written:
> Out of the belly of hell <note>original: *Sheol*</note> cried I, and thou heardest my voice. <note>Jonah 2:2</note>

And it is written:
> The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave <note>original: *Sheol*</note>, and bringeth up. <note>1 Samuel 2:6</note>

Rather, here we speak of the **lowest** depths, and we have established that one who is gripped by it does not return. Rabbi Eleazar once saw that it is written:
> For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water. <note>Jeremiah 2:13</note>

"They have forsaken me, the fountain of living waters"—this refers to the source that never ceases, flowing from the Ancient of Days <note>original: *Dikna*, literally "the Beard," a Kabbalistic term for the flow of divine mercy</note> through the letters of praise. It is written, "to hew for themselves broken cisterns," for they trust in their own vanities which lead them down degree after degree until they descend to the deficiency called the "lowest depths." But the one who sanctifies the Holy Name as is fitting ascends degree after degree to delight in the Supernal Source, which flows constantly and never stops. This vision is before the Lord, spreading over the engraved wings below, drawing blessings from above to below until blessings are found in all worlds. Rabbi Eleazar said: Worthy are those who offer praise by saying a "perfect song," a song that includes all other songs. This is what is meant by "and you shall say on that day":
> Praise the Lord, call upon his name, declare his doings among the people. <note>Isaiah 12:4</note>

Rabbi Eleazar said: There are times when praise and song rise from below to above and descend from above to below to bind the **knot of faith** <note>original: *Kitra de-Meimanuta*, the mystical unification of the Divine attributes</note>, as it is written:
> The scepter shall not depart from Judah... <note>Genesis 49:10</note>

And they praised "this song" to the Lord. It does not say "sang" or "spoke," but "the scepter shall not depart," and in this manner, "this song" rises from below to above.
> Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it. <note>Numbers 21:17</note>

"Spring up"—meaning, rise to your heights to be united with your Husband <note>the Divine King</note>, for until now you have been found with us in exile. Afterwards, it explains that "the princes digged the well"—this refers to Wisdom and Understanding above. A herald calls out with strength: These are for those called the "purified of the nations." Blessed is the place where the King joins in blessings. And how great is the nourishment, like the longing of "Remember" <note>the masculine principle</note>. This is the meaning of the "Daughter," and this secret flows from above to below. It is led from below and finds pleasure like a laboring woman, yet it is a perfect knot, the knot of faith, the enduring knot in which everything is contained. At that time it is written:
> And the Lord shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one Lord, and his name one. <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>

And it is written:
> Then was our mouth filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing: then said they among the heathen, The Lord hath done great things for them. <note>Psalms 126:2</note>

All were found worthy.

**Give ear**, O ye heavens, and I will speak; and hear, O earth, the words of my mouth. Rabbi Judah opened his discourse:

I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer. What is written previously?

"I" refers to the **Assembly of Israel** <note>original: *Knesset Yisrael*, the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note>. "I sleep" regarding the commandments of the Torah, like one who is weary. "The voice of my beloved knocketh"—this is Moses, who rebuked Israel with many arguments.

...like many connections, as it is written there: "to His word," etc. <note>original: "לדברו"</note> "You have been rebellious," etc. "And at Horeb you provoked [the Lord] to wrath," etc. That one <note>Moses</note> knocks [at the door], and as a servant of Moses, he rebuked Israel with love. -># The Holy Small Assembly<-
<note>original: "Idra Zuta Kadisha." This is one of the most famous sections of the Zohar, describing the death and final revelations of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai.</note>

**It was taught:** On that day when the companions gathered at the house of Rabbi Shimon, he decreed the arrangement of his words to depart from the world. Present before him were Rabbi Eleazar his son, Rabbi Abba, and the rest of the companions, and the house was full. Rabbi Shimon lifted his eyes and saw that the house was filled. Rabbi Shimon wept and said: "When I was in my sickbed previously, Rabbi Phinehas ben Yair was before me, and until I chose my place, they have granted me life until now. And when I returned, the fire never ceased from before me, and never has it been interrupted; rather, it was like a throne and a covering of joy that was released, and the house was filled with fragrance." While they were sitting, Rabbi Shimon opened his eyes and saw what he saw, and fire surrounded the house. All the others left, and only Rabbi Eleazar his son, Rabbi Abba, and the rest of the companions remained and sat, ten in total. He said to Rabbi Eleazar his son: "Go out and see if Rabbi Isaac is here, for I have acted as a guarantor for his life to arrange these words, and let him sit by me." Rabbi Isaac stood up, smiled, and rejoiced. He saw those companions who had gathered and entered, and they sat before him. Rabbi Shimon raised his hands and prayed his prayer. He rejoiced and saw those companions who had gathered, the members of the Assembly <note>the "Idra"</note> who were invited here. All the others left, and there remained Rabbi Eleazar his son, Rabbi Abba, Rabbi Judah, Rabbi Jose, Rabbi Isaac, and Rabbi Hiyya. Meanwhile, Rabbi Isaac entered. Rabbi Shimon said to him: "How fitting is your portion! How much joy is destined to be added to you this day!" Rabbi Abba sat behind his shoulders and Rabbi Eleazar in front of him. He said: "Behold, this hour is an hour of favor <note>original: "Sha'ata de-Re'uta," a time when the Divine is most accessible</note>, and I desire to enter without shame into the World to Come. And behold, holy words that have not been revealed until now, I desire to reveal before the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note>, so they shall not say that I departed from the world in deficiency, Heaven forbid. Until now they were hidden in my heart to enter with them into the World to Come. And thus I shall arrange you: Rabbi Abba shall write, Rabbi Eleazar my son shall repeat the words, and the rest of the companions shall meditate in their hearts." Rabbi Abba rose from behind his shoulders and Rabbi Eleazar his son sat. He said to him: "Rise, my son, for another sits in that place." Rabbi Eleazar rose. Rabbi Shimon wrapped himself [in his cloak] and sat. He said: "The dead do not praise God, nor those who go down into silence" <note>Psalm 115:17</note>. "The dead do not praise"—this is certainly so, for those called 'dead' are not so, for <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu," the masculine aspect of the Divine</note> is living and enduring, and He dwells among those called 'living' and not with those called 'dead.' And the end of the verse says: >"nor any who go down into silence"< <note>Psalm 115:17</note>—all those who descend to the silence of the grave and their opening. But beloved are those called 'living,' for the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires their honor. He said: "How meritorious is this hour!"

This [gathering] is adorned for a new chamber. The Holy One, blessed be He, is here, and now I am here with Him, and with those righteous ones in the Garden of Eden who have never before met as one. The Holy One, blessed be He, desires the honor of the righteous more than His own honor. As it is written regarding Jeroboam, who offered incense and worshipped idols, the Holy One, blessed be He, was patient with him. And now, the Holy One, blessed be He, desires our honor, and all [the heavenly hosts] come with Him. The companions who were there were shaken; they stood up and sat at the lower edges of the house. Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Abba remained before him. For He and all His holy assembly have come to hear with joy the hidden words and the praise of the **Ancient Holy One**, the most hidden of all hidden things. He is set apart and distinguished more than all, yet not set apart, for all is attached to Him and the end is attached to all; He is everything. The **Ancient Holy One**, the most ancient of all ancients, the most hidden of all hidden things, is configured and yet not configured. He is configured in order to sustain all, and not configured because He is not [physically] found. When He is configured, He brings forth nine lights from Himself in His configuration, and those lights blaze and travel and spread out in every direction, like a supreme lamp from which lights spread in every direction. And those lights that spread out, when one approaches to know them, they are not found—only the single lamp alone. So it is with the <term>Ancient Holy One</term> <note>Aramaic: Atika Kadisha; the highest, most primordial manifestation of the Divine</note>; He is like a supreme lamp, the most hidden of all hidden things, and nothing is found except those lights that spread out, which are revealed and concealed. And they are called the Holy Names. And because of all this, this is the Name of the One. In the ancient books, for those who revealed [the secrets] to be gathered into the **Ancient Holy One**, He is revealed in them. And in every joy, those configurations of the **Ancient Holy One** fly. To them, even until now, these words—for I have seen them as one, holy and joyful, in a way I never knew before. And I kept it in my heart: why? And now, they are all here to gaze before the Holy King. How fortunate is my portion of truth, that I have come to hear these words!

<margin>**The Skull**</margin> The whiteness of the head is the beginning and the end of everything. A cluster of His power spreads out and shines, and from this, the righteous shall inherit four hundred worlds of longing in the world to come. And by it, the dead are destined to be revived in the time to come, as it is written: <note>Genesis 27:28</note> *May God give you of the dew of heaven.* His head is filled, and all the "field of apples" drips from that dew. This **Ancient Holy One** is concealed and hidden, and the <term>Hidden Wisdom</term> <note>Aramaic: Chokmta Setima'ah; the primordial, non-conceptual wisdom</note> is found within that Skull, yet not found. Certainly, in this Ancient One, nothing is revealed except the Head alone, because it is the Head of all heads. And the spirit of that Supreme Wisdom is hidden within Him, and the investigation of the Supreme Brain—the hidden brain—lies quiet and calm, and no one knows it but He. Three heads are engraved, one within the other, and one above the other. One head is the **Hidden Wisdom**, which is covered and not opened; and this hidden wisdom is the head of all heads of the other wisdoms. The Supreme Head is the **Ancient Holy One**, the most hidden of all hidden things, the Head of every head.

<meta>This page continues the discourse of the Idra Zuta (The Lesser Assembly), where Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai reveals the deepest mysteries of the Divine before his passing. It focuses on the highest configurations of the Divine Personification.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Give Ear<-
<note>original: "Ha'azinu" - the name of the Torah portion and this section of the Zohar.</note>

The Head that is not known <note>The highest level of the Divine, "Reisha d'Lo Ityada," which is beyond human or even angelic comprehension</note> does not know and is not known, for what is in this Head is not grasped by wisdom or by understanding. Therefore, it is called "Nothingness" <note>original: "Ayin"</note>—for your place is not known. And this is the mystery of "Goodness." Because of this, the Holy Ancient One <note>original: "Atika Kadisha," the most primordial manifestation of God</note> is called **Nothingness**, for within it hangs the "Nothingness" from which all those hidden things that emerge from the Hidden Brain hang. They are all spread out <note>variant: more so</note> on the side, and the back is not seen. All is within this Holy Ancient One; all is as one in joy, and it never moves from mercy. Thirteen measures of mercy are found there, because this Hidden Wisdom within it is divided three times into four, and the Ancient One includes them and rules over them all. One mercy shines in its mouth, emerging from the brain; it is the mercy in which the righteous shine in the World to Come, as it is written: "And the path of the righteous is like a shining light..." <note>Proverbs 4:18</note>. And regarding this it is written: "Then you shall delight in the Lord" <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>. From this mercy, all other mercies shine that hang from the "Mountain of Faces" <note>The Divine Countenance</note>. This Ancient One is the highest of all, the Supreme Crown <note><term>Keter: The highest of the ten Sefirot or divine emanations</term></note> above, in which all crowns and diadems are crowned. Sparks flash from it, igniting and shining, and it is the Supreme Lamp, hidden and unknown. All other lamps are ignited and shine from it. This Holy Ancient One is found in three heads, yet they are included in one Head. It is the Supreme Head, above and beyond. And because the Holy Ancient One is marked by three, all other lamps that shine are included in three. Furthermore, the Holy Ancient One is marked by two; everything in the Ancient One is in two—it is the Supreme Crown of all supreme things, the Head of all heads. And that which is above this is not known. Thus, all other lamps stand in two. Furthermore, the Holy Ancient One is marked and written as one, and it is one, and all is one. All other lamps are sanctified and attached to the One, and they are one, and all is He.

The **Forehead** <note>original: "Metzcha"</note> of the vision of the Holy Ancient One is called **Will** <note>original: "Ra'on" or "Ratzon"</note>. For this Supreme Will, which is never diminished above and is not known, extends a single branch to the whole stature that is included in the Brain. And because it is the "Will of all Wills," it is established in the Brain that is revealed with intention <note>variant: revealed in the division</note>. When this is revealed, the "Will of all Wills" is found in all worlds, and all prayers from below are accepted. The face of the Small Presence <note><term>Zeir Anpin: The more accessible, "human-like" aspect of the Divine in Kabbalah</term></note> shines, and everything is found in mercy. Because of this, all judgments are hidden and subdued. At the time of the Afternoon Prayer <note>Mincha</note>, which is the time when all judgments are normally aroused, this Forehead is revealed, and all judgments are subdued and mercies are found. Because of this, the Sabbath is found to be entirely without judgment, neither above nor below; even the fire of Gehenna <note>Purgatory/Hell</note> is silenced in its place, and the wicked find rest. Therefore, an additional soul of joy is added to the soul, and a person must rejoice in the **three Sabbath meals**, for all of faith and the totality of faith is found therein. A person must set the table and eat the three meals of faith and rejoice in them. Master Rabbi Shimon said: I testify concerning myself that regarding all these things of the Sabbath, from my days I have never missed these three meals, and because of them, I have not needed to fast on the Sabbath, and even on other days I have not needed it so much. For whoever merits them, merits perfect faith. One meal is for the Matron <note>The Shekhinah/Divine Feminine</note>, one meal is for the King <note>The Holy One, Blessed be He</note>, and one meal is for the Holy Ancient One, the most hidden of all hidden things. In this world, he shall merit them above. When this Will is revealed, all judgments shine and are subdued from their intensity. The configuration of the Holy Ancient One is established in one configuration that includes all configurations: it is the Hidden Supreme Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>, the whole of all the rest, called the Supreme Eden, the most hidden of all hidden things. It is the Brain of the Holy Ancient One. This Brain spreads to every side; from it, it spreads to the Eden that is called [the Garden], and from this Eden, it flows and is the Head...

It explains how the Divine "Forehead" reveals a Will that subdues judgment, allowing for the three Sabbath meals to connect a person to the different levels of the Godhead.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the "Idra Zuta" (The Lesser Assembly), where Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai reveals the deepest mysteries of the Divine Countenance before his passing. It focuses on the "Ancient Holy One" (Atika Kadisha), the highest manifestation of the Divine, and how its features—eyes, nose, and beard—influence the lower realm of "The Small Face" (Zeir Anpin).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The hidden head of the **Ancient Holy One** is unknown. When a single surrounding circle <note>original: *socharna*; variant reading: *gvana* (color/aspect)</note> extends to illuminate, several brains are formed within it. It is revealed and shines with many lights, emerging and becoming solid and refined <note>original: *chaltis ve-chasof*; variant reading: *kadmis*</note>. This is within the lower brain, which is placed as a single treasury. The "Hollows of Will" and "Openings of Will" extend downward in an image until they reach the place where they are repeated in the image of the "Hollows of Supreme Loving-kindness." In this Will, when it is revealed, the "Masters of Judgment" gaze upon it and are subdued. The eyes of the head of the **Ancient Holy One** are two-as-one, always open and never sleeping, as it is written:
> Behold, He who guards Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.
(Psalms 121:4)

**Holy Israel**, for this reason, there are no eyebrows over the eye, nor any covering. This brain is engraved and shines in three supernal colors. From the whiteness of this eye, the eyes of the **Small Face** <term>Zeir Anpin: the more accessible, emotive aspect of God</term> are watered, as it is written:
> Washed with milk, fitly set.
(Song of Songs 5:12)

For that is the primary whiteness, and the other whites are below it, shining to the other reservoirs. The brain is called "Prophecy," for when it flows, all blessings are found from it. And because this brain glows in the colors of the eye, it is called "He who has a bountiful eye shall be blessed" <note>Proverbs 22:9</note>; for the blessing dwells within it, as the supernal whiteness is revealed in the brain. The openings of the eye, when they gaze upon the **Small Face**, all worlds exist in joy. This eye is the brain of the eyes below. And the brain and the eyes are two-within-two colors in a gathering that flies with the teaching: for the upper *Yod* is the lower *Yod*; the upper *He* is the lower *He*; the upper *Vav* is the lower *Vav* <note>These are the letters of the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter Name of God</note>. All those upper ones are suspended in the **Ancient One**, and the lower ones in the **Small Face** are not merely suspended from them, but are them exactly. Yet they all depend on the **Ancient Holy One**, for the "Hiddenness of the Ancient One" is found in everything, yet not found by all those who depend on the Ancient One. In order for them all to be sustained below, He pushes them so they will not be [overwhelmed], and therefore the "Holy Hiddenness" is both concealed and revealed. This is what is written regarding the **Ancient Holy One**, the concealment of all. And regarding what is suspended because of Him <note>variant reading: "for the pearls of speech..."</note> in the **Small Face**, all blessings, hidden and revealed, are those that hang hidden in the **Ancient Holy One**, and they take hold to sustain the lower *Yod*. <note>variant reading: "And this is the light, just as the eyes are suspended, why is the Yod suspended for the lower Yod?"</note>

**The Nose.** Like this brain in the "nostril of the flute" <note>the nasal cavity</note>, in which the path of the "Breath of Life" flows to the **Small Face**. And like this nostril of the nose, like the nostril of the flute, the *Aleph* is suspended to sustain the other lower *He*. And the breath is not bent from the hidden brain, but the "Hollows of the Breath of Life" are prepared to know wisdom in the time of the **King Messiah**, as it is written:
> And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding...
(Isaiah 11:2)

This nose is life from all sides; joy rises from the breath of the nose. The nose of the **Small Face** is as we have established, as it is written:
> Smoke rose up in His nostrils...
(Psalms 18:9)

And it is written:
> And for My praise, I will refrain <note>literally: "muzzle my nose"</note> for you.
(Isaiah 48:9)

In the *Book of Aggadah* of the school of Rav Yeba the Elder, it is engraved: the *He* is in power, and the *He* here is not sustained thus, nor joined <note>variant: "needed"</note>, except that it rises to the **Crown** <term>Keter: the highest Sephirah</term>. But when there is a "pleasing aroma," judgment is suspended in the nose, as it is written: "Smoke rose up in His nostrils." And regarding this, it is written: "And fire from His mouth devoured." The root of anger is suspended in the nose. All the "Repairs" <term>Tikunim: the features of the Divine Face</term> of the **Ancient Holy One** are established as a silent and hidden wall. But all the repairs of the **Small Face** are established through "Lower Wisdom," as it is written:
> In wisdom You have made them all.
(Psalms 104:24)

And He is the sum of all. And one might ask: what is the difference between the [upper] *He* and the [lower] *He*? For judgment is awakened from one, but here it is "Mercy within Mercy."

**The Beard** of the **Ancient Holy One** is where all the preciousness of all hangs. It is called the **"Source"** <term>Mazal: literally 'constellation' or 'flow'</term> of all. From the end of the beard, the *Mazal* and the preciousness of all precious things flow. The upper and lower beings all gaze toward this *Mazal*. Upon this *Mazal* depends the life of all. Upon this *Mazal* depend the heavens and the earth, the rains of Eden, and the nourishment of all. From this *Mazal* comes the outflow for all. Upon this *Mazal* depend all living beings, upper and lower.

<summary>This page describes the mystical anatomy of the Ancient Holy One (Atika Kadisha), explaining how the Divine Will, Eyes, Nose, and Beard act as conduits for mercy and life-force to the lower worlds. It emphasizes that while the Small Face (Zeir Anpin) can express anger or judgment, the Ancient One is pure mercy and the ultimate source of all blessing.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discourse of the Idra Zuta (The Small Assembly) from the Zohar, specifically within the portion of Ha'azinu. It focuses on the macrocosmic structures of the Divine, describing how the highest, most hidden lights of the "Holy Ancient One" descend through the "Beard" to nourish the lower spiritual worlds.</meta>

# The Small Assembly: The Flow of Divine Wisdom

Thirteen fountains of the oil of magnificent greatness hang within the Beard of this precious <term>Mazal</term> <note>original: "Mazla" - literally "luck" or "constellation," but here referring to the specific channels of the Divine Beard that "drip" influence</note>, and all of them flow out to the <term>Lesser Countenance</term> <note>original: "Ze'ir Anpin" - the emotional attributes of the Divine</note>. Do not say "all of them," but rather nine of them are found there to subdue the judgments. And when this <term>Mazal</term>, which is clothed in the Beard, reaches down to the navel, all the "Holy of Holies" that are sanctified within it hang from this <term>Mazal</term>. It extends with the extension of the Supernal Binding. That "Head" is the Head of all heads, which is not known and not recognized, and is not known by those above or those below. Because of this, all things are suspended from this <term>Mazal</term>. In this Beard, the three Supernal Heads extend, and they all connect within this <term>Mazal</term> and are found within it. And because of this, the preciousness of the preciousness of this <term>Mazal</term> is that those who hang from this <term>Ancient One</term> <note>original: "Atika" - the highest aspect of the Crown</note> all hang from this Beard and connect to this <term>Mazal</term>. They hang from it to sustain other "letters" <note>spiritual building blocks</note> below; if these letters did not rise to the Ancient One, the others would not be sustained. And because of this, Moses said: *The Lord, the Lord, [long-suffering and abundant in] all Your kindness* <note>Numbers 14:18</note>, mentioning the Name twice with a cantillation mark separating them. For behold, like their <term>Mazal</term>, all things—above and below—long for this <term>Mazal</term> and are subdued before it. Happy is the portion of one who merits this.

This <term>Holy Ancient One</term>, the most hidden of all hidden things, is neither mentioned nor found. And because there is no "Head" higher than all heights, He is mentioned only as a "Head" alone, for the rest of the "Body" is not known. He is concealed and hidden. And because of the sustenance of the rectifications that were established by way of the <term>Hidden Brain</term> <note>original: "Mocha Stima'ah"</note>, which belongs to all of them, it extends and is rectified. It brings forth Supernal Kindness, and that Supernal Kindness extends and is rectified, and all things are included in the Hidden Brain. This Brain is covered; it strikes words that strike within this Brain so that it may be illuminated. And light from the precious <term>Mazal</term>—which is the "Brain of the Brain"—extends into thirty-two paths. When it is illuminated by this precious <term>Mazal</term>, the three Supernal Heads are illuminated twice, and one includes them. They hang in the <term>Mazal</term> and are included in it. From them all, they surround to illuminate the preciousness of the Beard, the whisper of the hidden <term>Mazal</term>. They are rectified just as the Holy Ancient One is; three Heads are crowned in Him, and so all are in three Heads. All that are crowned hang one from the other in three Heads: two from two sides, and one that includes them. You might ask: who is the Holy Ancient One?

Come and see: Above, there is that which is not known, not recognized, and not marked, and He includes all. Two Heads are included (another version: "hang") within Him, and then all others are thus rectified. And that light is among them, but not in a general way and not in thought, but only in the "Will of the Heart." Concerning this it is said: ->*I said, I will guard my ways, that I sin not with my tongue*<- <note>Psalms 39:2</note>. He said: Four forms are found from the Ancient One, which are nourished from the Brain. It is the light of <term>Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Chokhmah"</note> that extends into thirty-two directions and goes out from that Hidden Brain, from the covering that is upon it. And that which the Holy Ancient One illuminated at first (another version: "in Wisdom") is the "planting" from which they were illuminated and became three Heads, and one Head includes them. These three extend to the <term>Lesser Countenance</term>, and from their words, all things shine. This Wisdom was struck and brought forth a river that flows and goes out to water the Garden <note>referring to the flow of divine energy into the lower realms</note>. It enters the head of the <term>Lesser Countenance</term> and becomes another brain. From there, it is drawn and flows through the whole body and waters all those "plantings." This is what is written: ->*And a river went out of Eden to water the garden...*<- <note>Genesis 2:10</note>. This Wisdom was struck and extended and entered the head of the <term>Lesser Countenance</term> and became another brain. That other light is found from the two hidden ones that were engraved and connected into one Head of the "Deep Male," as it is written: ->*By His knowledge the depths were broken up*<- <note>Proverbs 3:20</note>. It enters the head of the <term>Lesser Countenance</term> and becomes another brain, and from there it is drawn and enters into the interior of the body, filling all those chambers and halls of the body. This is what is written: ->*And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled*<- <note>Proverbs 24:4</note>. And these shine from the covering of that Hidden Brain which shines within the Brain of the Holy Ancient One. All of them hang one from the other and are tied one to the other, until it is known that all is One, and all is the Ancient One, etc.

<summary>This passage describes the mystical flow of Divine Wisdom (Chokhmah) from the most hidden "Holy Ancient One" through the symbolic "Beard" and "Mazal" into the lower manifestation of the Divine, the Ze'ir Anpin. It emphasizes the unity of the Divine emanations, explaining how the "Hidden Brain" provides the spiritual energy that sustains all existence.</summary>

# Ha’azinu

And it was not spread out because of them all. These three lights shine to three others which are called "Kindnesses" <note>Hebrew: *Chasadim*</note>, and these Kindnesses shine to all, and all are weighed as one. When this Ancient One, the Will of all Wills, is revealed, all is in light and all is found in the joy of perfection. This Eden <note>A metaphor for the source of divine pleasure</note> is drawn from the Supernal Eden, the Hidden of all Hidden, and from this Eden it is called "The Beginning," yet it is not called "Beginning" or "End." And because there is no beginning or end in it, it is not called a "Place," because it is concealed and not revealed, and it is called **He** <note>The third-person pronoun "He" (*Hu*) refers to the most hidden, impersonal aspect of God</note>. And from the place where the conclusion is found, it is called **You** <note>The second-person "You" (*Attah*) refers to a more revealed, relatable aspect</note>, and it is called **Father**, as it is written:
> For **You** are our **Father** <note>Isaiah 63:16</note>

In the tradition of the school of the Elder Rav Yiba, all of the "Small Face" <note>The *Zeir Anpin*, the emotional attributes of God</note> is called **You**, and the Ancient Holy One, who is hidden, is called **He**. And it is well-explained: from the place where the "Beginning" is found—the eye that is concealed from it—there is the beginning, and it is called **You**. And He is the Father to Wisdom <note>*Chokhmah*</note>, and from this Father, [Wisdom] emerges from the Ancient Holy One, as it is written:
> And Wisdom, from where <note>Hebrew: *Me-Ayin*, literally "from Nothingness"</note> shall it be found? <note>Job 28:12</note>

And it flows but is not known. Come and see: these levels are renewed from the very heart of all; "He knows its place" <note>Job 28:23</note>—its literal place—and all its ways. Hidden Wisdom is within it like the Ancient Holy One. This Wisdom is the beginning of all; from it spread thirty-two paths—paths, and not ways. And its way is perfected within it through twenty-two letters and ten utterances <note>The 32 paths of wisdom mentioned in the *Sefer Yetzirah*</note>. This Wisdom is the Father to [all] wisdom, and in this Wisdom, beginning and end are found. And because of the Supernal Wisdom, there is a Lower Wisdom. When Wisdom spreads out to be called "Father to Wisdom," all is not diminished or cut off (for when they all spread out, they are called "Wisdoms" and are called "Father to Wisdom," yet all is not perfected or cut off), as it is written:
> You have made them all with Wisdom <note>Psalm 104:24</note>

He raised his hands and said: Behold, surely this is Eden, and everything is needed for this reason. Come [and see]: by the reason of the Ancient Holy One, the Hidden of all Hidden, when He desired to be established, He established everything in the likeness of **Male and Female**. The Crown <note>*Keter*</note> was perfected as Male and Female; they could not endure in any other way except as Male and Female. And this Wisdom, which is the soul of all, when it emerged and shone from the Ancient Holy One, it only shone as Male and Female. This Wisdom spread out and was found to be Male and Female: Wisdom is the **Father**, Understanding <note>*Binah*</note> is the **Mother**. Wisdom and Understanding are weighed as one; Male and Female were not established [separately], and between them, all is established in Male and Female—for if not for this, they would not endure. This "Beginning" is the Father of all, the Father to his children, and they are joined one to another and shine one into another: Wisdom is Father, Understanding is Mother, and it is written:
> For if you call out to Understanding <note>Proverbs 2:3</note>

When they joined, they gave birth and spread out the [world of] Faith. In the tradition of the school of the Elder Rav Yiba, they taught: What is "Understanding" <note>*Bi-Nah*</note>? It is when these join together, the letter *Yod* with the letter *He*, they are perfected and bring forth a **Son** <note>The Hebrew word *Binah* is playfully read as *Ben-Yah*, the Son of God</note> and give birth. And because of Understanding, he is called "Son." The letters *Yod-He* and *Yod-He* are the perfection of all; both are found to be joined. And so in the [divine] union, all things in their arrangements are found to be the perfection of all: Father and Mother, Son and Daughter. These matters were not given except to the "Holy Supernal Ones" who have entered and exited and know the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, and do not stray to the right or the left, as it is written:
> For the ways of the Lord are straight; the righteous walk in them... <note>Hosea 14:10</note>

And all is the portion of the one who merits to know His ways and does not stray or err in them. For these matters are hidden and the Holy Supernal Ones shine in them truly, shining from the light of the Lamp <note>A reference to Rabbi Shimon himself</note>. These words were not handed over except to one who has "entered and exited" <note>An idiom for one initiated into mystical experience</note>; for one who has not entered and exited, it would be better had he not been created. For behold, it is revealed before the Ancient Holy One, the Hidden of all Hidden, that these words shine in my heart in the perfection of love and the fear of the Holy One, blessed be He. And these "sons" who are here, their knowledge is in them, for they have entered and exited these words—though not all of them—and I open and they are illuminated in perfection, the opening that is required. And may my portion be with them in that world. Rabbi Shimon said: All that I have said of the Ancient Holy One, and all that I have said of the Small Face, all is one; it is all He, all is one, the matter is not divided.

<summary>Rabbi Shimon explains the emanation of Wisdom (Abba/Father) and Understanding (Imma/Mother) from the hidden source, emphasizing that the divine must manifest as male and female to endure. He concludes by asserting the absolute unity of all divine levels.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Ha’azinu**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, meaning "Give Ear."</note>

Separation depends on Him; blessed is He and blessed is His Name forever and for all eternity. <term>Come and see</term> <note>original: "Ta Chazi," a standard Zoharic opening</note> the conclusion of that which is not extinguished.
<term>Wisdom and Understanding</term> <note>original: "ChaB," Chochma and Binah</note> are included in the letter *Yod* <note>The smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing the concentrated point of Divine Wisdom</note> which hangs from the Holy Brain. From it, the hidden *Yod* emerges to all other letters. <term>Israel the Elder</term> <note>A specific mystical configuration of the Sefirot</note> and <term>Understanding</term> <note>Binah</note> are the source of everything. That river which flows and emerges is called the "World to Come"; it is constant and never ceases. It provides a vision of delight for the righteous, to merit that World to Come which constantly waters the Garden of Eden and never stops. Concerning this, it is added: **"Its waters shall not fail"** (Isaiah 58:11). And that World to Come proclaims and says: **"A river went out of Eden to water the garden"** (Genesis 2:10).

It includes two letters as one, for in it rests the "Enlightenment" <note>original: "Hanoch," likely referring to the illumination of the mind</note> for the brain. The thirty paths are included in the *Yod*, but in the drop that truly emerges, it is called the letter *Vav*. There is another garden which is the letter *Dalet*, and the "brain" and the *Vav* are found to be four <note>The numerical value of Dalet is 4</note>, and this is what is written: **"A river went out of Eden."** What is this "Eden"? This is the Supreme <term>Wisdom</term> <note>Chochma</note>, and the *Yod* is not there to water the garden—that was the *Vav*. It spreads and stands at four heads, which is the *Dalet*. Everything is included in the *Yod*. Because of this, <term>Wisdom and Understanding</term> are called the "House of All." From this *Yod* begins the "Day of All," as it is written: **"In wisdom You have made them all"** (Psalms 104:24). In its crown, it is not revealed and not known until it joins with another letter <note>Reference to another folio: (page 146)</note> in Wisdom.

Because of this, everything is known and hinted at; the beginning and the end of all is called <term>Wisdom</term>, and in it, everything is hidden. The "Holy Brain" reaches the "Opening of the Brain," and all those days were not found until they were engraved on the thirty sides included in this Wisdom. This *Dalet* is the woman <note>The feminine aspect</note> and we call her <term>Understanding</term> <note>Binah</note>. These two are like priests who are crowned with the Challah-offering. We have learned that everything is included in the *Yod* which joins with Wisdom, and they bring forth a "Son" (*Ben*), which is "Understanding" (*Bin-ah*). "Father and Mother" <note>Abba and Imma</note> are the *Yod* and *He*, and the "Son" is their building.

There is <term>Understanding</term> <note>Binah</note> and it is called <term>Reason</term> <note>Tevunah</note>. Why is it called *Tevunah* and not *Binah*? It is called *Tevunah* because it provides nourishment to two children, the "Son" and the "Daughter," which are the letters *Vav* and *He*. That aspect is called <term>Tevunah</term> because everything is included in these letters—Son and Daughter—and they are *Vav* and *He*, and all is one, and they established *Tevunah*.

In the book of Rav Hamnuna the Elder, he said that King Solomon’s first arrangement that he revealed and said: **"Behold, you are beautiful, my love"** (Song of Songs 1:15) was from this level. The second arrangement is called the <term>Bride</term>, which is the <term>Feminine</term> <note>Nukva</note> of the lower realm. Some say both refer to this lower Feminine, but it is not so. The first is not called "Bride," but the latter is called "Bride" because at known times they rest; for there are times between them when the Male does not join with her and withdraws from her. At that time it is written: **"And to a woman in her menstrual uncleanness you shall not approach"** (Leviticus 18:19). When the Female is found and the Male desires to join with her, then she is called "Bride."

Everything comes from the One; the desire of both never ceases, and they emerge as one and are bound as one. This one does not cease from that one, and this one does not withdraw from that one. And in the Prophet it is written: **"A river went out of Eden"** to rest and to live... **"its waters shall not fail."** Because of this, it is written "my desire," for in this desire they are all bound in primordial perfection. Here she is called "Bride," for when he comes to join with her, she was a "Bride," for she is a Bride in essence. Therefore, Solomon spread two arrangements for the Female: the first arrangement is hidden because she is hidden, and the second arrangement he spread more openly and not hidden. Afterward, all good depends on that which is above, as it is written: **"My dove, my perfect one, is unique; she is the only one of her mother"** (Song of Songs 6:9). Because she is the woman crowned with the crown of all, and her desire never ceases, all the light that the masters of all perform is given to her, for all those who stand for the whole, as it is written: **"For on this day He shall atone for you"** (Leviticus 16:30). And it is written: **"And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year; it is a Jubilee"** (Leviticus 25:10). Whenever it says <term>Jubilee</term> <note>Yovel</note>, it refers to the inner voice from the end of that river that comes and flows and emerges constantly and never ceases. It is written...
