<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on Parashat Ha’azinu (Deuteronomy 32). The previous discourse likely touched upon the perfection of God’s work, and here the text transitions into how human sin affects the Divine Name and the Shekhinah (the Divine Presence).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Give Ear (Ha’azinu)**<-

Their blemish—why are all these rectifications not found properly with Him? It is written <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note> **"The Rock, His work is perfect,"** and it is written <note>Isaiah 59:17</note> **"He put on righteousness as a coat of mail, etc."** and it is written of kindness and grace, **"and He put on garments of vengeance for clothing."** Rabbi Elazar said: It is taught that "He put on righteousness" at a time when Israel is worthy; when they are not worthy, "He put on garments of vengeance, etc." Rabbi Yose said: What is the inner meaning? As we have learned, here they are not satisfied <note>original: *mistafeqin*, implying a lack of flow or nourishment</note>—she is not blessed from that Source of All because of everything. **"This"** <note>original: *Zot*, referring to the Shekhinah</note> is His, but "not His children" is their blemish. He showed him "to Him" <note>Hebrew: *Lo*</note> and "to Her" <note>Hebrew: *Lah*</note>, two; yet it is only one above and one below. And this is what he said to him: whenever the guilty increase in the world, as it were, the Holy Name is not blessed in the world. And whenever the guilty do not increase in the world, the Holy Name is blessed in the world. This is what is written <note>Psalms 104:35</note> **"Let sinners be consumed from the earth, and let the wicked be no more. Bless the Lord, O my soul. Hallelujah."**

Rabbi Yehuda said: This verse here is exactly as it is written <note>Deuteronomy 32:5</note> **"Is 'This' His? No, His children's is the blemish."** <note>The Zohar re-reads the verse to suggest that the blemish of the children affects "Zot" (This/Shekhinah) which belongs to Him.</note> What caused the destruction of this "crooked and perverse generation"? Because we see... <unclear>mi-vei ve-raha</unclear>... it was found thus behind the Crown <term>Keter: the highest Sephirah or emanation of God</term>, for all the voices did not reach it. And the sinner [affects] the Holy Name; properly by Himself, "He is righteous and upright." But through their conspiracy, it fell upon "Is 'This' His? No, His children's is the blemish." Why so? Because they are a "crooked and perverse generation." Rabbi Yehuda said: "To Him" <note>Lo</note> is nothing; they act for themselves, for they are the perverse ones who cause blessings to be withdrawn from the world.

Rabbi Chakka said: "To Him" <note>Lo</note> is not like this, as we have established, and so it is. What is written after it? <note>Deuteronomy 32:6</note> **"Do you thus requite the Lord, O 'This' people, vile and unwise?"** <note>The Zohar reads "Zot" (This) as the Shekhinah being "with" the people.</note> For all those good things He did for you and does for your sake. Rabbi Elazar opened and said: "This" <note>Zot</note> was like a burning wrath to Him, etc. Happy are Israel above all the nations who worship idols; for even though they sinned before their Master, the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not wish to abandon them. For in every place they were exiled among the nations, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is with them in exile. This is what is written <note>Leviticus 26:44</note> **"And yet for all 'This' (Zot), when they are in the land of their enemies, etc."**

Rabbi Chakka said: "And yet for all 'This' (Zot) being with them." Come and see how great is the love of the Holy One, Blessed be He, for the Assembly of Israel. For even though they caused themselves to be exiled among the nations, the Shekhinah <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</term> did not depart from them forever. Do not say that they alone are found in exile; rather, "And yet for all 'This' (Zot)"—she is found with them. This is what is written: **"And yet for all 'This' (Zot), when they are in the land of their enemies..."**

It is like a King who was angry with his son and decreed a punishment upon him to be distanced from his house and go to a far-off land. The Matron <term>Matronita: the Queen/Shekhinah</term> heard and said: "Since my son is going to a far-off land and the King has cast him out of his palace, I will not leave him." Grace and space <note>original: *chen ve-ravcha*</note>—they both sat as one in the King's palace, and they both sat as one in the other land. Sometimes the King sought the Matron and she was not found, for she had gone with her son. He said: "Since the Matron is there, let them both dwell there." And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, remembers the Matron as before, He also remembers His children. This is what is written <note>Exodus 2:24</note> **"And God heard the groaning of the children of Israel, etc."** What caused this? "I have heard their distress"—as it were, the Matron who was with them. Then, **"and He remembered His covenant."** And it is written <note>Exodus 2:24</note> **"And God remembered His covenant."** And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, shall return Israel from exile, what is written? <note>Leviticus 26:42</note> **"Then I will remember My covenant,"** and this "covenant" is the Matron. And further it is written <note>Psalms 85:2</note> **"Lord, You have been favorable to Your land; You have brought back the captivity of Jacob."**

Rabbi Yehuda said: **"Do you thus requite the Lord, 'This' (Zot)?"** Because the crooked and perverse generation sinned, you caused "This" (the Shekhinah) to go into exile. "Do you thus requite the Lord, 'This'?"—is this the reward for what He did with you at all times, in the days of Egypt, in all those visions that were seen, that He did for you? Is this the end of the reward you give to the worlds for this? What caused this for you? Because they are a "vile and unwise people," and they were not perfected by all those good things He has done for you until now. **"Do you thus requite the Lord, 'This' (Zot)"**—this is the Shekhinah, and this we have established from what we learned <term>K.V.A.</term> <note>Abbreviation for *Kudsha [Brich Hu] ve-Ayelet [HaShachar]* or similar mystical configuration</note>... Rabbi Yehuda said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, is in every place, the Holy One, Blessed be He, and He is called "Grace" and "Two Worlds," as it is written **"from world to world,"** <note>Psalms 106:48</note> and He... in the secret of Korah... It is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says, in how many ways were they perfected for the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His existence never departs.

<summary>This page explores the mystical relationship between Israel's conduct and the Shekhinah (the Divine Presence), explaining that when Israel sins, they cause the Shekhinah to go into exile with them. Using the parable of a Queen following her exiled son, the text emphasizes that God's presence remains with the Jewish people even in their darkest times.</summary>
<keywords>Shekhinah, Matronita, Exile, Ha'azinu, Divine Name, Zot, Covenant, Repentance, Mercy</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the portion of Ha'azinu, focusing on the mystical relationship between the Creator and the Congregation of Israel during their exile, and the symbolic creation of the worlds through the Hebrew letters.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Ha'azinu** <-
<note>Listen/Give Ear - the name of the Torah portion</note>

The love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel is present in every place where they are; the Holy One, blessed be He, is among them, as it is written: <note>Leviticus 26:44</note> *I will not reject them, nor will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly and to break My covenant with them.* This indicates that His Presence remains among them, as it is written that He shall never remove His dwelling from them.
Rabbi Isaac was walking on the road and met Rabbi Chiya. He said to him: I see by your saddle that you are coming from the dwelling of Sukkot. When did you arrive? Let us sharpen our ears with words of Torah. One must sharpen oneself and be alert from the very beginning. We saw that when Jacob went on his way and sought to eat, immediately the Holy One, blessed be He, was among them to provide for them and to help them endure the exile; as if to say, *I am with him in distress; I will rescue him and honor him* <note>Psalms 91:15</note>. He said to him: Certainly, in every place where Israel wanders, the Holy One, blessed be He, is among them. And in every place where the wise of the generation go, the Holy One, blessed be He, goes with them, as it is written: <note>Psalms 91:11</note> *For He will give His angels charge over you...* How do we know this? As it is written: <note>Genesis 32:2</note> *And Jacob went on his way... and when Jacob saw them, he said, "This is God’s camp."* This refers to the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence</note> that accompanies a person on the road and in the journey on the way. For I know that we are going to one place to receive the face of the Shekhinah.
He said to him: Certainly. Rabbi Isaac taught: The God of our fathers is with us, neither in their going nor in their returning <note>meaning God's presence is constant</note>. Therefore, we go to appear before the Holy One, blessed be He, and not just for our own return. While they were walking, he said to him: Have you seen what is written? <note>Genesis 2:4</note> *These are the generations of the heavens and the earth.* "The Heavens" includes the Holy One, blessed be He. "The Earth" includes the Congregation of Israel. And all that is below are called the "generations of the heavens" from their dwelling. He said to him: If so, what is the meaning of the word *be-hibbare’am* <note>original: "when they were created"</note>? It is written <term>be-He bera’am</term> <note>He created them with the letter He</note>. He said to him: It is all one matter; when they were joined together, <term>with the letter He</term> He brought forth generations, and these are called the generations of heaven and earth.
He said to him: If so, why did you establish that <term>be-He bera’am</term> refers to Abraham <note>The Hebrew letters of "be-hibbare’am" are an anagram for "be-Abraham"</note>? He said to him: It is all one matter; the word "Abraham" is "The Heavens," for from there they began to spread out. "With the letter He He created them" is "The Earth," and they are all one word.
He said to him: Certainly it is so, for we have learned that it is written: *These are the generations of the heavens and the earth.* And we have taught: This world was created with the letter <term>He</term>, as it is written "with He He created them." And the World to Come was created with the letter <term>Yod</term>, as it is written: <note>Isaiah 26:4</note> *For in Yah [Yod-He] the Lord is an everlasting Rock.* And a river already flows out of Eden to water the garden—to include the Heavens. "To water the garden" includes the Earth. And you have established what is written: <note>Song of Songs 4:15</note> *A fountain of gardens,* which is the Heavens; *a well of living waters,* as it is written regarding the memory of the servant Isaac, "a well," as it is written: <note>Genesis 26:22</note> *And he moved from there and dug another well...* *And flowing streams from Lebanon,* for they are crowned above and rise with the scent of the King, as it is written: <note>Psalms 108:5</note> *For Your mercy is great above the heavens.* From Lebanon they go forth to the Bride. And with joy it is drawn to all corners until those springs flow and descend to be prophesied in the place called the <term>Great Day</term>, as it is written: <note>Ecclesiastes 1:7</note> *All the rivers run into the sea...* And it is written: <note>Isaiah 51:1</note> *Look to the rock from which you were hewn...* And afterwards it is written: <note>Song of Songs 4:12</note> *A garden locked is my sister, my bride...* And from here generations went forth to the Bride, as it is written "when they were created," "with He He created them," from the essence of Abraham. Rabbi Isaac said: And even literally in Jacob, and they are all one word. Rabbi Isaac said: All the time they sat before him, all this was said before him openly, and we did not need all these [explanations]. He said to them: This is the permission of the children of the building, for all of them are before Him together, prophets before Moses.
While they were walking, Rabbi Chiya said: It is written: <note>Isaiah 49:15</note> *Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb?* This verse was established, and the Elder explained what it speaks of. Rabbi Isaac said: If in the connection of their children, like a cluster, one should not look away, then what shall we say? He said to him: This is the nest of the heights. One day, while he was walking on the road and did not know the way and did not know the word—and come and see, it happened that I was walking until I had tasted nothing, and now I am going to that holy society to tell me if the bucket is lacking. He said to him: On that day when <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> was going to the house of his father-in-law, and on that day I was walking with him and he spoke words of comfort.
Rather, come and see: Rabbi Eleazar said in the name of his father: Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He, concerning the nourishment that fell in the exile, that He left them in the exile, and we see that it returns and is said: <note>Isaiah 49:14</note> *But Zion said, "The Lord has forsaken me, and my Lord has forgotten me."* The Shekhinah replied: *Can a woman forget her nursing child...* Israel, who are called "children," as it is said: <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note> *You are children to the Lord your God.* "From the womb, the son of her belly..."

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Song of Moses (Ha'azinu) from the Zohar. It focuses on the intimate relationship between the Creator and Israel, interpreting the verses through the lens of the Sefirot (Divine emanations).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Listen<-

For your sake, the Bride <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> and the sages of your planting are entirely purified and prepared below. "Even these may forget" <note>Isaiah 49:15</note>. As it is written <note>Genesis 2:4</note>: "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth." "But I will not forget you." From here we learn that the Holy One, Blessed be He, loves Israel eternally. Furthermore, it says <note>Isaiah 49:15</note>: "Can a woman forget her nursing child, or have no compassion on the son of her womb?" This is the lower secret <note>original: *raza d'letata*</note>, which is the Holy One, Blessed be He—these words are in the heavens. See how beloved the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is, for He is everything; so too He loves and cherishes Israel, for they are beloved in heaven. [The text here describes a gathering of sages including Rabbi Pinhas and a vision regarding the cave of Rabbi Eleazar]. He read over him the three lines of the verse: "Then you shall call... and you shall delight... and you shall delight yourself in the Lord" <note>Isaiah 58:9-14</note>.

**Remember** the days of old, consider the years of many generations, etc. <note>Deuteronomy 32:7</note>. "Remember the days of old"—Rabbi Hezekiah said: What are the "days of old"? These are the seven lower days <note>The seven lower Sefirot or divine attributes</note> through which the Holy One, Blessed be He, made the world, as it is written <note>Exodus 20:11</note>: "For in six days the Lord made [the heavens and the earth]." It says "six days" and not "in six days" <note>A common Zoharic distinction implying the days *are* the building blocks of creation, not just the timeframe</note>, and this we have established. "Consider the years of many generations"—meaning, those "days of old" should be known and recognized by all the elders and every single generation, until this generation that stands here. Open your palate and it will tell you, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, is the strength of your palate, and He will reveal the depths of wisdom. For each of these seven days comprises the world... but for your sake, the wisdom of freedom was given. For we have learned: everything the Holy One, Blessed be He, created was made on a condition—that when Israel comes, they will receive the Torah and live; and if not, the world would return to chaos and void <note>original: *tohu va-vohu*</note>. And because of those "days of old," they knew and recognized the King. And these branches are united in our portion. This we have established: then the Holy One, Blessed be He, chose them as His inheritance. What is written? "For the Lord’s portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance" <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>. This He gave to them as a blessing; a portion for the King and not for any appointed minister. The Holy One, Blessed be He, took Israel as His own portion, as it is written <note>Deuteronomy 32:10</note>: "He found him in a desert land, and in the waste, a howling wilderness," etc. From here we see He remembers Israel in every generation and never separates from them, remembering them with mercy, "Like an eagle that stirs up its nest," etc.

**Like an eagle** stirs up its nest <note>Deuteronomy 32:11</note>. Rabbi Yose said: We have not found a guardian who stands over his children like this eagle. And come and see, we have learned: it is written "the face of an eagle" <note>Ezekiel 1:10</note> is toward the right side, and the face of the ox is to the left. The eagle is the synthesis of all, for it is written "like an eagle," which balances everything. The way of the eagle is to hover over that very place out of mercy for its children. So too is the Holy One, Blessed be He, toward His children, like an eagle. What is written? "The Lord alone did lead him, and there was no strange god with him" <note>Deuteronomy 32:12</note>. He alone, as it is written: "And the Lord went before them." "No strange god with him"—meaning He did not lead Israel via an angel or any other appointed power, for they are the portion of the Lord alone. This is the vitality... "If Your presence does not go with us, do not bring us up from here." The Lord alone leads them. He alone, and no strange god with Him. Worthy is the portion of Israel that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is with them. Thus it is written of them <note>Psalms 135:4</note>: "For the Lord has chosen Jacob for Himself, Israel for His peculiar treasure." And it is written <note>Psalms 94:14</note>: "For the Lord will not cast off His people." Because they are attached to Him. And for this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will rejoice in them... as we have established.

<margin>36</margin> The sages will recognize, and you, Rabbi Yose, all these verses here... are for the benefit of Israel... Rabbi Hezekiah said: even when Israel is in debt [sin], the holiness does not depart... the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is entirely freedom... and they shall know them. All is for the sake of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Ha'azinu (Deuteronomy 32). The previous context likely dealt with the warnings given to Israel regarding their conduct and the consequences of straying from the path of the commandments.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

For the Holy One, blessed be He, hinted in this entire portion to warn us about this. And here it is written: *If they were wise, they would understand this* <note>Deuteronomy 32:29</note>. 
"This" <note>Hebrew: *Zot*</note> is certainly significant. We have established in several places that this refers to the fact that if Israel does not know "This," they are liable. For "This" is the aspect used to exact punishment from the guilty, and it requires contemplation and attachment to repeat it, as it is written: *This is the law of the guilt offering* <note>Leviticus 7:1</note>.
*If they were wise, they would understand this*—meaning they would be bound to it, for Israel, when they observe the commandments of the Torah, dwell with Him as His portion. They would then know that the assistance of "This" is with them to take vengeance on their enemies. Even when Israel is scattered among the nations, they would know how *one could chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight* <note>Deuteronomy 32:30</note>. And what causes this for them? It is "This" which was with them as their portion when they performed the commandments of the Torah; it will never depart from them to maintain their existence.

**If** *not that their Rock had sold them, and the Lord had given them up* <note>Deuteronomy 32:30</note>. Heaven forbid [that He would abandon them], but *their Rock had sold them* because of the generations. It is taught in the *Tikunim* <note>The Tikunei HaZohar, a foundational kabbalistic text</note> that the repairs do not ascend when they are in their distress. Rabbi Judah said: This "Rock" refers to **Wisdom** <note>The Sephirah of Chokhmah</note>, as we have established, for through Wisdom, Israel will be sustained in exile and will not perish because of it. For there are two strengths in exile, and even in Gehenna <note>Purgatory/Hell</note> Israel shall not be consumed. The Holy One, blessed be He, looks upon their hands; whenever the image of Israel falls into exile and their enemies enslave them, it is because *their Rock sold them* and *the Lord gave them up*.

He looked upon his hands. It was taught by Rabbi Judah: What is the reason He gave them wisdom? They sinned with this form. Thus, when they were destined to enter the Land and their inclination misled them, the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah</note> rebuked them for this. Rabbi Isaac said: In two places the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to rebuke Israel and the nations of the world. One is where it is written: *The Lord has a dispute with Judah, and will punish Jacob according to his ways* <note>Hosea 12:3</note>. The nations of the world argue: "They have become defiled and hated by the world." When the Holy One, blessed be He, sees that they [the nations] are rejoicing, what is written afterward? *Like a horse's heel...* <note>referencing the downfall of the oppressor</note>. When they argue, this is the response to the wrath: a mother who had a quarrel with her son went to complain about him, but when she saw him being brought to judgment, her soul was moved to quiet her heart and she burned with mercy. What should she do for the son? When the judgment is strict, she says, "Woe is me, what have I done to you? I have brought this complaint against you."

**And many** *evils and troubles shall befall them* <note>Deuteronomy 31:17</note>. It is written that afterward He will make all those *shells* <note><term>Kelipot</term>: the spiritual husks or forces of evil that conceal the divine light</note> be enslaved to him. Until now it was written in the Book of the Crown <note>possibly a reference to a specific mystical volume</note> regarding this verse: all protection is to guard you, to act toward the sick, as it is written: *the children of the sick*. It is a lack for the King to serve his fellow in the world. For when the healer goes to him, they exchange words of remembrance and writing. And if the sickness prevails over him, it is considered a lack for the King. He calls out and visits him to open for him [a way of healing]. For when Israel is in distress, it is like a sickness. He gives blessings to the one who exerts himself. Those "evils" will be transformed into another memory. It is written: *and they shall be placed*, for those sicknesses that were prepared for him were meant to guard him and to make him humble. He will look and understand that sickness, from what it arose, so that it should not increase upon him.

Afterward, he will be corrected by those "eyes" so that he may be properly bound. And "This" is their strength that rises in those healers to guard him, so he does not stray from his path. Even if he strays by one small word, it is accounted to that healer as if he spilled blood and killed him. For the Holy One, blessed be He, desires the life of that person. He is a son of the King, and one who exerts himself for him must be careful to bring him out of his deficiency. So it is with the Holy One, blessed be He: He judges these judgments for the world, whether for life or 
->for death<-

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the intersection of physical illness, spiritual judgment, and the hidden remedies found within the Torah. It specifically addresses the "Book of Remedies" (Sifra de-Asvuta) and the ethical boundaries of using divine secrets for physical healing.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Give Ear**<-
<note>original: "Ha'azinu" - the title of the Torah portion, meaning "Listen" or "Give Ear."</note>

To the masters of judgment, there are those who uproot the nest to perform many matters below, to punish with property. One falls into his **sickbed** <note>original: "be mar'ei"</note> and does not know until all that was decreed upon him is judged. Once he is punished in his money and gives all that was decreed upon him, he is saved and ceases from the **house of lack** <note>original: "be chasira" - a term for prison or a place of deprivation</note>, and there is no need to exert further judgment upon him. And a word goes out from below to the betrothed; they seize him and place him in the house of lack <note>The "house of lack" refers to both physical prison and the spiritual state of illness.</note> so that he will strive from here on to look upon the beauty of grace from their house. Afterwards, they release him from the house of lack. Regarding matters below that lead to death, it is such that even if he gives all the ransom and all the money in the world, he will not be saved and will not be restored. For this reason, one must have mercy from the house to strive for him—if he can give him **healing** <note>original: "asvuta"</note> for the body and life; and if not, let him give healing to his **soul** <note>original: "nishmata"</note>. One should strive for the healing of the soul, for this is the healing of the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, who strives for him in this world and in the world to come.

One should not awaken until this portion of the teaching is opened and explained, except for one who is meritorious. For we have seen a certain **merchant** <note>original: "Tayya'a" - often a disguised sage or celestial messenger in Zohar narratives.</note>, a master of hearing for the wise of the depths. There was one in his days who would look with all his strength; when he saw a person in his sickbed, he would say: "This one will live," or "This one will die." And from his days, the donkey-drivers <note>original: "chamrin"</note> said he was a man of truth who feared sin. And all things that he could not grasp of what was needed, he would purchase and give from his own. The donkey-drivers said there was no one as wise in the world as he. He did more than what was done in those times.

And when this was revealed to us, that pious one said: That merchant certainly spoke correctly, for he inherits from the angels of destruction. And all the vessels of the Voice of Atonement were all established upon the **secrets of the Torah** <note>original: "razin d'Oraita"</note> and hidden secrets to gaze upon. And the matters of healing were his burdens. He said that it is not proper to perform them except for a pious man who fears sin. The wise men, from what he did, examined that he was a garment for the sin against the Master, and he would say with his mouth and prepare the measure. And they all searched through that book and said: "This is a deficiency" and "This is a surplus" for one who fears sin. For instance, regarding specific illnesses, he said they depend on their wisdom in the burning of the mouth, and they are from the side of the **Serpent** <note>original: "Nachash"</note> and the adversary from the side of the "Kest" <note>likely a reference to a specific spiritual impurity or demonic force</note>. And so, those who lack should say with the mouth and lack in action. He would say until they were found for known illnesses that it was necessary to say thus, and to perform such actions and charms upon that illness, and he would be restored.

The companions were happy to the point of measure. If that book is with us, as we have said here, it is like a wine that was handed over in order to take the holy writing. And we have learned: **Rabbi Eleazar** said, "That book was in my hands for twelve months, and I found in it celestial and precious arrangements. When I reached those secrets that were swallowed in wonder—and who can rejoice to sit with one crown?—they were coming, rising, and hiding until I saw in amazement, and it was shown to me: 'What is it to you to enter into depths that are not yours? It is not necessary for you to involve yourself and to press forward upon the hidden secrets that were there.'" I arranged that book and another one, and one day Bar Yehuda leaned and I gave him the book. And then understanding was found from those sparks that lick, which arranged for him a portion. But they were not arranged according to their proper repairs as is fitting for every person who merits the healing found therein, which is repaired through other repairs and its hidden secrets. And he would unify them in their lack and completion and in prayers to the Holy One, Blessed be He. And he lived from what he did to heal through the verses of the Torah or the secrets of the Torah. Furthermore, he said to say the secrets of the Torah, and upon that spirit, he brought out secrets of healing that are not found in this manner. Blessed be the Merciful One who spared us in this wisdom of the tongue. And your life! These matters were swallowed; I leaned and saw in it that there was no one in the world as wise as he. Blessed be the Merciful One, that in every ascent they tremble, so that human beings do not err after the path of the Holy One, Blessed be He. And the chest of money... until here. May the Lord be with them all.

Rabbi Eleazar recounts his possession of the book and a divine warning against delving into secrets not meant for him, emphasizing that true healing comes through Torah and the fear of sin.</summary>

<meta>This page is the introductory preface titled "Orah" (Light) for an early printed edition of the Zohar. It establishes the editorial principles used to compile the text, specifically addressing the reconciliation of various manuscript traditions and the correction of scribal errors.</meta>

## Main Text (Preface)

-> **Light** <-
<note>Original: "Orah." This title likely refers to the illumination the editors hope to provide through this corrected edition.</note>

And let his proverb be according to my hand, and in correspondence to this path they shall no longer lack; and for the sake of my standing and my wisdom in the way, to set our tongue in its place as desired and with ultimate agreement. And although our eyes have also become accustomed to the strength of the orders and the divisions, sometimes without the pen's seal of vision and the fullness of these [matters]. One who labors in great works alone with the tip of the brush, and every wing-span of your activity and exaltation, for [they are] garments; and upon inspection to strengthen weak hands and stumbling knees. And he added a constant ferment in my heart because he brought me to the house of spiritual delight from the printing of this wondrous book from beginning to end; and the hidden sword is not needed upon those who knock for favor from the rotation of the primordial thought. May the Lord be the support of those who hold fast to it and its supporters, and may they walk in goodness and integrity among the pleasant ones, going from strength to strength and exulting in joy.

**And behold**, that which we have concluded in speech before him with great toil and heavy labor regarding its examination for its own sake, which was always for me a savior that tests day and night to refine types of silver, to remove the dross and the errors, and to arrange the letters in their order with refinement and exactitude, with great exhaustion and study, and to whiten and clarify everything well with a few <term>manuscripts</term><note>Original: "ha'atakot" - literally "transcriptions" or "copies."</note> from the hands of a scribe, according to what the hand of my limited understanding reached, and with the yoke of the sickness of those who caused me to tremble to add a vessel for its work and to prepare my hand in seeking the flow, and specifically from the manuscript of **Leviticus** and its surroundings.

**Also**, I was not wise enough to omit remnants from my own mind, nor did my heart's messengers dare to do what many wise and discerning men who preceded me did not do, whose eyes watched over me. However, since there were portions in the **Book of Deuteronomy** in which I did not find discourses from the *Book of the Zohar*, I also printed the **Faithful Shepherd** <note>The "Raya Mehemna," a later layer of the Zoharic literature focusing on the commandments.</note>. And what they found in their time to say regarding every holy portion of **Deuteronomy**, that the discourses are all from the "Faithful Shepherd," I printed them among the discourses in the portion of **Balak**, for there the "Faithful Shepherd" and the generalities were given for the benefit of whoever has a brain in his skull. And in the printing of **Leviticus**, I printed at its beginning a discourse which was not found in the old manuscripts <unclear>from the Master of his life</unclear>, every one of his sparks in the Torah and in every intellectual and scientific matter <unclear>like a full deep [well]</unclear> and from its flames. Also in the portion of **Phinehas**, a companion said that it is not found in most manuscripts, and in their scarcity they were not found in any manuscript except in one book purchased from the plague of the Holy City, the city called **Zippori** <note>Sepphoris</note> and above; and the general matter is called "And Light" <note>Orah</note> of the ancients.

**Also** this I found: all other discourses that I found doubled, I omitted every discourse from the second place where it was repeated, and I marked in its place between the page and the column the first location where it is written, so that every student may find it easily, and so it should not enter one's mind that the omitted discourse is missing from the book. This and one more thing it is proper to know and to make known: that the <term>Saba</term> <note>The "Old Man" - a famous section of the Zohar.</note> in the portion of **Mishpatim** was entirely mistaken in all the manuscripts and full of many corruptions, except in a manuscript that was perfect and complete, refined sevenfold, which came into our hands—a transcription for the light of the physicians <note>Possibly a reference to a specific family or guild of scholars.</note> as a herald of change, and they brought it from **Egypt**, a great city full of Torah and the waters of wisdom.

**And because** the proximity of the narrowness and the extension of the body, which is natural in its material ways from the day of its birth, covers the intellect from seeing every path clearly, and it is impossible, despite all the heights of diligent and pouring study, not to stumble in the physical understanding and error and the exchange of letters and words out of their order, or in the skipping of some line, word, or letter. Whether due to the blow of the man who perceives and his wandering eye, or the blow of the printers who do the work—for so it is attributed to all that is covered in its entirety—in this book there are some well-known errors. I will mention some of them from all that I have grasped, even the last one as I passed over it to copy the omissions:
* In the portion of **Kedoshim**, page 80, column 1: [the word] *Hivtimu* instead of *Hivtimu* <note>The editor is noting a specific spelling or vocalization correction.</note>.
* In the portion of **Emor**, page 88, column 1 & 2: the word *Nosefet* [added] three times instead of *Nosefet*.
* In the portion of **Bamidbar Sinai**, page 110, column 1: "And a wise man shall be able and keep silent" — every wise man is born and shall keep silent with the addition of the letter *Vav*.
* And regarding what is written in the portion of **Balak**, page 154, column 2, the verse says: "And the King said to say, and he feared the children of..." — so I found in all the manuscripts, but I checked in **Kings** and **Chronicles** and the scripture is written: "And Moab was sore afraid of the people..." <note>The editor is correcting a misquoted biblical verse within the Zoharic text.</note>

-> **More** <-

<meta>This page serves as the colophon for the second volume of the Zohar, printed in Mantua between 1558 and 1560. It marks the completion of this portion of the landmark first printing of the Zohar in Italy.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

An additional portion of the first part of Volume II of this Zohar was printed in its entirety to supplement what was missing <note>The printer is explaining that they added extra material to ensure the text was complete and robust</note>. For he has merit, since a word was being lost; therefore he said that they made a wide throne for them, weary and faint, go back and do for that one who delays, etc.

->**And Now**<-

I have humbled my supplication before every wise-hearted person who studies this holy book: if he finds in it errors, substitutions, exchanges, or accidental corruptions—for behold, "the crooked cannot be made straight" <note>A reference to Ecclesiastes 1:15</note> and the lack of what is missing is well known—may he receive a reward from the Lord for correcting it. My heart's vision and my hope is that I did not involve myself in this precious and honored work—a work of Heaven and holiness—to draw it out from the darkness <note>original: "Tzalmon," a poetic term for deep shadow or the underworld</note> with immense toil and great expense for the building and restoration of the "House of my Life" <note>A metaphor for the soul or the study of Torah</note> and to reach the final day to complete his obligation in "emptiness and desolation" <note>original: "buka u-mebuka," a phrase from Nahum 2:11 denoting total exhaustion or ruin</note>. Rather, the beginning of the thought and the end of the deed was to bring merit to the masses and to bring the Torah of Truth to light, so that they may labor in the land to know the Lord. The paths were beloved, to set a level way from the depths, to walk in the brightness of the world's darkness and its doubt. 

And beyond the general effort to complete the matters where the transcribers stumbled, to sweeten what was hidden in the depths, I sat as much as possible to clear away the thorns, to understand and to gain insight from the bounty of His holy Torah which restores the soul. The deep, inner meanings of its teachings are more precious than fine gold and sweeter than honey, all contained in this Divine book for whoever knows and desires to see by the light of the living, existing in pleasure and pleasantness, and to delight in the radiance of His glory—for this is the whole of man. And it shall be proven to be found in the numbered count, to understand His unity and the secret of His Name written in the foundations, to grant those who love Him an inheritance of "Substance" <note>original: "Yesh," often used in Kabbalah to refer to the 310 worlds of reward</note> and I will fill their treasuries. "No eye has seen, O God, beside You, what He acts for him who waits for Him" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>. May the Lord also grant the general good we hope for; in our days may Judah be saved and Israel dwell securely in the faith of perfection and praises forever and ever, Amen Selah, for all living.

I have been strengthened and encouraged and have paved the way through the labor, a decision for every wise person who seeks God. **Abraham** (may his Rock and Redeemer protect him), son of the honorable **Meshullam** (of blessed memory), of **Modena**. Here in **Mantua**, for the honor of the Lord, according to the weekly portion: *“In wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge.”* <note>Exodus 31:3; this serves as a chronogram for the year of printing</note>

---

By the partners, all of them: the distinguished **Meir Isaac**, son of the honorable **Ephraim** (of blessed memory) of **Padua**;
and **Jacob**, son of the honorable **Naphtali ha-Kohen** (of blessed memory) of **Gazzuolo**, the youngest of the printers.

---

| | | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **The Zohar is finished** | **Light of the world** | **Every hidden secret** | **Mighty in power** |
| **Tree of Life** | **Radiance of faces** | **The Heavens** | **To soar on wings** |
| **In the year 320** <note>5320 / 1560 CE</note> | **Hand in hand** | **I bow before** | **The One who forgives sin** |
| **To God ascend** | **Song and praises** | **Among congregations** | **And on every side** |
| **He worked wonders** | **Clothed in His majesty** | **Redeemed His servant** | **Who hoped in Him** |
| **Return, my soul** | **To your rest** | **For the Lord is great** | **Over every tragedy** |
| **Awake, awake** | **Arise and shine** | **For your light has come** | **And glory is joined** |
| **Behold, all these** | **God shall perform** | **Two or three times** | **With a man** |

<note>The final line of the poem is a variation of Job 33:29: "Lo, all these things God works, twice, thrice, with a man."</note>

It marks the completion of the second volume and reflects the printers' religious devotion and the immense effort required to publish this foundational Kabbalistic text.</summary>
